It mandates that when an algorithm has a significant impact on the rights and interests of users the provider 'shall give an explanation'. This gives individuals the right to understand why a decision was made.

items.title: AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0 (China)
items.justification: The framework addresses transparency by stressing the need for robust risk management practices and requiring organizations to conduct thorough impact assessments of AI systems. The document seeks to mitigate 'unexpected untruthful and inaccurate outputs' (p.53) and calls for establishing traceability and explainability systems to identify the origins of AI-generated information (p.67-68). It also advocates for the disclosure of AI technologies' principles capabilities and safety risks (p.51) regular disclosure of information on the auditing and anomaly (p.65) and disclosure of functional objectives logic usage and data sources (p.77).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of clarity regarding how AI systems operate including their purpose data sources and decision-making logic to foster public trust
thematicElements.justification: The framework emphasizes transparency as a key principle. It states that organizations should disclose key information of AI systems including 'functional objectives operational logic model usage data sources and the rationale behind decision-making' to build public trust (appendix 2 4 p.77).

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to provide meaningful explanations of their systems' outputs especially in high-stakes contexts like hiring or loan applications
thematicElements.justification: The framework includes a principle of full lifecycle safety and comprehensive governance measures for all entities including developers service providers and users (p.56). It also has 'ethical risks' (p.47) as a key area encouraging organizations to prioritize public welfare and minimize harm. However it does not specifically mention high-stakes scenarios like hiring or loan applications.

thematicElements.text: The establishment of rights for individuals to receive an explanation for a decision made by an AI system that affects them and to understand the key factors that led to that outcome

(p.33). It did not address tertiary education.

items.title: Hong Kong Generative Artificial Intelligence Technical and Application Guideline
items.justification: To promote the effective and beneficial use of generative AI this Guideline introduces a governance framework based on five dimensions including crime prevention. With reference to P.19 it is elaborated that generative AI is increasingly used to create deceptive material to spread misinformation manipulate public opinion and impersonate individuals in communications and electronic transactions for fraudulent purpose. As such when developing generative AI the guideline calls for the use of a holistic approach which incorporates ethical considerations social implications public acceptance and community response (p.19).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI tools from being used to create amplify or disseminate misinformation and hate speech or to facilitate harassment and violence
thematicElements.justification: The guideline introduces service-derived issues these include content safety ( which encompasses the dissemination of hate speech) (p.12). To counter such issues the guideline includes several recommendations for different stakeholders. For technology developers operational principles should be established to enable AI systems to provide transparent explanations for outputs and incorporate mechanisms for source verification fact-checking and validation (p.26). Risk assessment should also be conducted to analyse service deficiencies such as misinformation and negative impacts on user experience (p.29).

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to platforms and AI developers to implement robust content moderation policies and to be transparent about how their systems handle harmful content
thematicElements.justification: The guideline introduces technical limitations of generative AI applications specifically the generation of harmful content as a result of model hallucination model bias black box problems ( p.910). To address these concerns organisations could implement comprehensive data governance practices including using validation techniques version control and regular audits (p.910). The guideline also assigns responsibilities to technology developers service providers and end users in relation to misinformation and violence such as content governance and verification ethical usage community protection awareness and control (p.24)

thematicElements.text: The establishment of rights for individuals and groups targeted by misinformation or tech-facilitated violence to receive protection and to seek redress against the perpetrators and the platforms that enabled the harm
thematicElements.justification: Service Providers should strive to enhance the transparency of generative AI services provide insights into the decision-making process and establish feedback channels to promote an inclusive and responsible generative AI service process using clear and understandable language thereby improving the user experience (p.29). However the section does not specify that these measures are required to be established to protect individuals and groups against misinformation or tech-facilitated violence.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the use of AI tools to facilitate gender-based harassment and violence
thematicElements.justification: Under the fairness principle during model training and content generationscientific algorithms and rigorous review mechanisms should be employed to prevent the generation of biased or discriminatory content targeting factors such as gender (p.23)

items.title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence Framework (Hong Kong)
items.justification: The Ethical Artificial Intelligence Framework establishes a common approach and structure to govern the development and deployment of AI applications. It consists of an assessment template to assess the implications of AI applications. Under the assessment template organisations are recommended to consider whether AI applications are being used in new domains which may have impact on vulnerable groups including children(3-25 and appendix 6-7).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The protection of children's personal data and privacy when they interact with AI systems
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 3-25 the guideline recommends organisations to consider various risk factors when using AI. These risks include risks to the population making up the data subjects (including children)the ethical (permissible) basis for the collection and use of thepersonal data and provisions to protect the privacy of individuals involved in the project. However these considerations did not explicitly mention the protection of children's personal data and privacy

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the use of AI to exploit manipulate or harm children including through targeted advertising or inappropriate content
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 3-25 the framework recommends organisations to conduct ethics legalrisk/benefits assessment for AI projects. The risk criteria include assessing the risks  to the population making up the data subjects including children. When the AI project is applied in new domain organisations should also consider risks and ethical issues relation to care and safety ( appendix 6-7). However the framework did not explicitly prevent the use of AI to manipulate harm or exploit children through targeted advertising or inappropriate content.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers of AI to design systems that are safe age-appropriate and beneficial for children
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 6-7 the AI application impact assessment template recommends organisations to assess the impact of AI applications based on various risk gating criteria. These include whether such applications are covering new domains which may have an impact on vulnerable groups including children. If so the IT Board/ CIO should review the assessment and the application before commencing IT projects which involve the use of such applications. Additionally 3-25 also recommends organisations to establish Ethical AI Committee to review the risks of AI projects to data subjects including children.

items.title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence Framework (Hong Kong)
items.justification: The Framework sets out 12 ethical AI principles which includes Fairness. Under the fairness principle on 3-8recommendations and results from AI applications should treat individuals within similar groups in a fair manner without favouritism or discrimination and without causing or resulting in harm. This entails maintaining respect for the individuals behind the data and refraining from using datasets that contain discriminatory biases. The principle forms the basis of practices that organisations can follow throughout he various stages of AI Lifecycle when developing or deploying AI applications.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of the development of AI systems that are representative of and responsive to a wide range of cultures and languages
thematicElements.justification: Diversity and Inclusion is included as one of the 12 AI ethical principles. With reference to 3-17 the principle recommends organisations to involve the largest possible number of AI users representing the broadest variety of cultures interests lifestyles and disciplines.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the development of AI tools that perpetuate cultural stereotypes erase linguistic diversity or favor dominant cultures
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 3-16 under the fairness principle recommendation/result from the AI applications should treat individuals within similar groups in a fair manner without favouritism or discrimination and without causing or resulting in harm. An example provided under the fairness principle on 3-16 elaborates that training data should be free from biased characteristics such as sample size disparity selection bias and bias stemming from model design model use and feedback.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to ensure their systems are trained on diverse datasets and are adaptable to various cultural and linguistic contexts
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 3-16 under the fairness principle result from the AI applications should treat individuals within similar groups in a fair manner without favouritism or discrimination and without causing or resulting in harm. An example provided under the fairness principle on 3-16 elaborates that training data should be free from biased characteristics such as sample size disparity selection bias and model design model use and feedback bias. Based on this Section 4 of the Framework provides various recommendations to maintain fairness throughout the AI lifecycle. For exampleon 4-28 the Practice Guide recommends organisations to use several sampling techniques to include data from minority class to balance training datasets.

thematicElements.text: The promotion of fair and equitable outcomes from AI systems ensuring they don't produce biased results that disproportionately affect certain groups
thematicElements.justification: With reference to page 1-4 one of the 12 ethical principles in the framework is fairness. The principle elaborated that recommendations/results from the AI applications should treat individuals within similar groups in a fair manner without favouritism or discrimination and without causing or resulting in harm. This entails maintaining respect for the individuals behind the data and refraining from using datasets that contain discriminatory biases. page 3-17 also stated that the integrity of source data should be ensured to guarantee fair outcomes from AI applications.Data which are invalid or inaccurate when used to train an AI model will lead to biased decisions and discrimination against affected users due to dataset flaws.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI systems from perpetuating or amplifying existing societal biases and discrimination based on race ethnicity gender religion age or other protected characteristics
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 3-16 detailed elaboration is provided in relation to the definition of discrimination under the fairness principle. Under the principle discrimination is defined as adverse unfair or detrimental treatmentpreference exclusion or distinction of a person because of the person’s race colour sexsexual orientation age physical or mental disability marital status family or carer’sresponsibilities pregnancy religion political opinion national extraction or social origin. Based on this the framework recommends organisation to design AI applications that mitigate perceived unfairness through eliminating bias through training data and ensuring the integrity of source data to ensure fair outcome.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers to proactively identify measure and mitigate sources of bias throughout the AI lifecycle from data collection to deployment
thematicElements.justification: In the data extraction stage (page 4-244-25) organisations are recommended to perform data validation and obtain assurance for the provenance of data from public or third-party sources to ensure that fair recommendations and results can be generated. In the pre-processing stage (page 4-28) organisations are encouraged to define and test for fairness and bias and fix unbalanced class problems to identify and mitigate sources of bias. Page 3-17 also stated that the integrity of source data should be ensured to guarantee fair outcomes from AI applications.Data which are invalid or inaccurate when used to train an AI model will lead to biased decisions and discrimination against affected users due to dataset flaws.

items.title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence Framework (Hong Kong)
items.justification: Human oversight is one of the 12 ethical AI principles under the framework. It refers to the degree of human intervention required as part of AI application’s decision-making or operations dictated by the level of the perceived severity of ethical issues. It is determined based on different factors such as the benefits and risks of the AI application impacts of the AI decision operational cost and evolving societal norms and values. Human oversight should also be used as a form of control to intervene/ auto-shut AI applications or systems in case of system failure (3-17). The guideline recommends three different approaches for oversight which include humans in the loop humans out of the loop and humans in command (4-21).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of meaningful human control over AI systems ensuring that AI remains a tool to assist humans rather than replacing human judgment particularly in critical areas where AI-enabled decisions or actions can have broad and systemic implications
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 4-21 22 human oversight is recommended in the solution design phase within the AI lifecycle. Organisations are encouraged to determine the level of human intervention based on several factos such as benefits risks operational cost legal implications social norms and values and the probability of the AI application causing harms to human. Based on these considerations organisation can decide whether to introduce humans in the loop humans in command or humans out of the loop. For situations that have broad economicsocial or legal impacts human-in-command is recommended to be adopted.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of full automation in sensitive sectors where human intervention and ethical judgment are necessary such as in law enforcement or medicine
thematicElements.justification: The framework does not explicitly mention the full prohibition of automation in sensitive sectors. However it recommends different degrees of human intervention  ( humans out of the loophumans in the loop humans in command 4-21)based on the perceived severity of ethical issues that can be brought about by AI systems/ models (3-8). Therefore it covers aspects of the statement partially.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities using AI to designate responsible individuals who can oversee intervene in and ultimately be accountable for the decisions made by the system
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 4-21 22 project managers and end users involve in the solution design phase should determine the degree of human intervention based on various factors including benefits risks operational cost legal implications social norms and values and the probability of the AI application causing harms to humans. Though the framework recommended several approach ( humans-out-of-the-loop humans-in-the-loop and humans-in-command) it does not make explicit the individuals/ stakeholders who can oversee intervene in or be accountable for decisions made by the system.

items.title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence Framework (Hong Kong)
items.justification: The framework includes a section on AI Assessment (5-2 to 6-2). Specifically it includes an assessment template for organisations to assess the benefits impact and risks of AI applications to ensure that the impact across the AI Lifecycle is managed and that related Ethical AI Principles have been considered.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of a culture of proactive risk management by requiring that the potential societal ethical and environmental impacts of AI systems are evaluated before their deployment
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 5-3 the AI Application Impact Assessment consists of several component. The first component is the risk gating criteria where organisations are recommended to review the risk level of the AI project before its commencement. Thereafter organisations are encouraged to complement the AI Application Impact Assessment which includes questions related to benefits risks the effects on individuals’ rights and the balancing of different interests. The assessment is meant to be a live document for capturing risks and mitigations that contribute to the project.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and users of AI to conduct comprehensive Impact Assessments that identify and mitigate potential risks to individuals and society
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 5-6 to 5-7 the Project Team within an organisation should complete an AI Application Impact Assessment template starting from the planning phase of the project. A detailed review of the full assessment and a collaborative review of the I'Impact” sectionshould be completed by the Project Team. Results of the AI Application Impact Assessment should be reviewed and approved by the Project Steering Committee (PSC)/ Project Assurance Team (PAT). The PSC/PAT should review the business cases potential impacts and plan to address if the project is to proceed. The IT Board/CIO and the Maintenance Board are responsible for handling escalations and monitoring high-risk projects.

thematicElements.text: The establishment of rights for the public to access the findings of these assessments ensuring that they can hold organizations accountable for the impacts of their AI systems
thematicElements.justification: The AI Impact Assessment procedures and template ((5-2 to 6-2)did not include any recommendations for publishing the results of the assessment. However in the transition and execution stage of the Ai lifecycle (4-43) organisations are encouraged to prepare a diclosure  document that could be made available to endusers or the public (e.g. on a website) as applicable.  The document should outline the details on the AI application’s operation and intended use;data used and processed model training procedures;testing procedures;performance metrics; and checks performed to evaluate the application of Ethical AI Principles.

items.title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence Framework (Hong Kong)
items.justification: The framework includes 'reliability robustness and security' as one of the 12 ethical principles. This is also introduced as 'performance principles' which are fundamental principles that need to be achieved to create a foundation for the execution of other ethical principles(P.1-4). The principle states that AI applications should be developed such that they will operate reliably over long periods of time using the right models and datasets while ensuring they are both robust (i.e. providing consistent results and capable to handle errors) and remain secure against cyber-attacks as required by the relevant legal and industry frameworks(P.3-8).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The establishment of performance thresholds or quality benchmarks to ensure AI systems operate reliably and accurately under stated conditions
thematicElements.justification: At the project strategy phase (4-5) organisations are recommended to quantifiable or qualitative metrics to measure the impact of the AI applications. For organisations using advanced AI applications metrics should be established to measure feedback and performance Examples of metrics include inspecting the success and failure of predictions to verify that the AI application is performing in an acceptable manner. Additionally organisations should assess applications against industry standards or regulations and embed standards/ regulations in the organisational strategy for all AI projects (4-6).

thematicElements.text: The implementation of safeguards fallback procedures or emergency protocols to mitigate harm in case of AI system failure or unexpected behavior
thematicElements.justification: In the system deployment phase (1-9 4-42) multiple layers of mitigations should be established to prevent system failures or errors at different levels or modules of AI application. These include  incorporating defense or controls at the beginning or end of each solution steps setting controls in place that allow for human intervention or auto-shutdown in the event of system failure establishing business continuity plans to identify processes that should take place when the model fails needs to be taken offline or decommissioned.

thematicElements.text: The requirement for pre-deployment testing validation or documentation to ensure technical robustness throughout the AI system lifecycle
thematicElements.justification: Prior to system deployment (4-39) formal and robust testing requirements for AI applications should be initiated to validate they are appropriate for production. These tests include regression testing in the AI to identify model error standardising testing benchmarks or metrics for comparing candidate models or evaluating readiness for deployment and involving end users in the testing process to ensure AI applications can produce meaningful results.

thematicElements.text: The introduction of security obligations to protect AI systems against cyberattacks manipulation or adversarial interference
thematicElements.justification: In the model building phase (1-9) organisations should aim at mitigating common AI application errors such as inaccurate modelassumptions input variable selection model overfitting and adversarial attacks.Data scientists and project managers are recommended to perform adversarial training and dimension reduction to prevent adversarial attacks.

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence Framework (Hong Kong)
items.justification: The framework includes transparency and interpretability as one of the 12 ethical principles. Under the principle organisations should be able to explain decision-making processes of the AI applications to humans in a comprehensible manner (3-8). The framework provides further guidance on how Explainability Transparency and Provability can be materialised (3-10 to 3-12). Regarding explainability the guideline recommends built-in and post-hoc interpretations. Regarding transparency the guideline outlines Transparency as Traceability Transparency as Verifiability Transparency as Non-deception and Honest Design and transparency and personal privacy. Provability refers to mathematical certainty behind AI models' decisions.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of clarity regarding how AI systems operate including their purpose data sources and decision-making logic to foster public trust
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 3-10 organisations are recommended to incorporate explainability based on the data algorithms and configurations of the model. Two suggested approaches are built-in interpretation and post-hoc interpretation to explain model behaviour. Some recommended practices include performing integration system decision and user acceptance testing to improve transparency and explainability (4-39) and defining requirements for transparency and intrepretability of AI models through creating a communications plan on AI model interpretability (4-22) and providing examples to explain the AI decision-making process innarrative terms or graphics to non-technical audeince (4-22).

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to provide meaningful explanations of their systems' outputs especially in high-stakes contexts like hiring or loan applications
The establishment of rights for individuals to receive an explanation for a decision made by an AI system that affects them and to understand the key factors that led to that outcome
thematicElements.justification: With reference to 4-22 in the solution design phase project managers are recommended to create a communications plan on AI model interpretability to achieve transparency and interpretability to impacted stakeholders for exhibiting the relative importance of each variable to explain predictions. The plan should include examples to explain the AI decision-making process and explain the different factors and data which determine the outcomes and conclusions of their AI models. However the framework does not mention that individuals have the right to receive an explanation for a decision made by an AI system which affects them.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy (CONPES 4144) (2025)(Colombia)
items.justification: The document addresses AI Literacy under the Section 5.3.4 Digital Talent and Capacity Development (pp.93–96). It emphasizes developing competencies in the education system for ethical and responsible AI use (p.94) the training of teacher and student and the integration of AI in curricula (p.94) AI literacy and digital skills programmes for the population (p.95) knowledge appropriation and public awareness strategies (pp.95–96).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Ministry of Information Technology and Communications Ministry of National Education Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation Ministry of Labour National Learning Service Colombian Institute for the Evaluation of Education and the National Planning Department

thematicElements.text: Curriculum reforms including at primary secondary tertiary levels
thematicElements.justification: CONPES 4144 (DNP 2025) mentions the need to integrate AI into educational processes and strengthen digital skills but does not establish comprehensive curriculum reforms at all levels. Actions 4.3 and 4.4 (Appendix A) propose strategies for incorporating the pedagogical and ethical use of AI and designing a Mission for the Digital Transformation of Education which implies curricular adjustments. However it does not detail specific changes in primary secondary and tertiary curricula.

thematicElements.text: Establishment of educational institutions or programs offering AI-related courses within the formal education system
Provision of teacher training and resources for AI education

items.title: Law 2502 of 2025 - (through which an aggravating circumstance is modified and established in article 296 of Law 599 of 2000 Colombian Penal Code and other provisions are issued) (The Congress of Colombia)
items.justification: Law 2502 of 2025 addresses AI-facilitated violence and disinformation by classifying AI impersonation as an aggravating factor in the crime of personal misrepresentation (Article 3). It defines DeepFake and establishes a public policy to prevent the use of AI for deception or harm including guidelines on ethics algorithmic transparency deepfake detection and rapid response protocols (Article 4). It also mandates judicial traceability of AI-related cases (Article 5).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: The National government the Attorney Generals Office the National Police and the Ministry of Information and Communications Technology

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI tools from being used to create amplify or disseminate misinformation and hate speech or to facilitate harassment and violence
thematicElements.justification: Law 2502 of 2025 seeks to prevent the misuse of AI for identity theft and the creation of deepfakes (Articles 3 and 4) addressing the generation and dissemination of misleading content. However it does not explicitly mention the prevention of hate speech harassment or violence.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to platforms and AI developers to implement robust content moderation policies and to be transparent about how their systems handle harmful content

The establishment of rights for individuals and groups targeted by misinformation or tech-facilitated violence to receive protection and to seek redress against the perpetrators and the platforms that enabled the harm
The prevention of the use of AI tools to facilitate gender-based harassment and violence

items.title: Bill 043 of 2025 'Through which artificial intelligence is regulated in Colombia'
items.justification: Bill 043 of 2025S addresses access to redress and remedy through Articles 14 and 30–36 establishing civil administrative and criminal liability for AI-related harm. It mandates human oversight impact assessments and sanctions for violations. It also outlines procedures for complaints corrective measures and guarantees due process and protection of fundamental rights.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The establishment or reinforcement of judicial mechanisms that allow individuals or groups to seek remedy for harms caused by AI systems
thematicElements.justification: Bill 043 of 2025S includes provisions for civil (Articles 13.1 and 14) administrative (Articles 31–34) and criminal liability (Article 30) for harms caused by AI and outlines procedures for investigation and sanctions. However it does not establish or reinforce specialized judicial mechanisms (e.g. courts or panels) for AI-related harm. Instead it relies on existing legal frameworks and administrative procedures such as those in Law 1437 of 2011 (Article 33).

thematicElements.text: The creation or use of state-based non-judicial complaint mechanisms (e.g. ombuds institutions regulators tribunals or consumer bodies) to handle AI-related grievances
thematicElements.justification: Bill 043 of 2025S assigns oversight roles to administrative bodies like the Superintendency of Industry and Commerce (Article 35) which may handle AI-related grievances through inspection control and consumer protection. It also outlines non-judicial procedures for administrative sanctions (Article 33) but does not create a dedicated ombuds institution or tribunal for AI complaints.

thematicElements.text: Requirements or incentives for companies or developers to establish accessible grievance or complaints mechanisms for individuals harmed by AI systems

items.title: National Consensus on Digital Care - Colombian Communications Regulatory Commission (2025)
items.justification: The document (CRC 2025) highlights that AI shapes children's emotional cognitive and social development (p.9). It calls for ethically designed AI systems prioritizing inclusion privacy and security with age-appropriate adaptations (pp.6 15 17). Human oversight is essential for automated decisions affecting minors (p.18). The consensus recommends impact assessments before deploying new technologies to identify biases (p.18). It also emphasizes restrictions on the commercial use of sensitive data from minors requiring age verification and parental consent (pp.4 7 15 19). Educational campaigns on privacy and technology use are advocated (p.17).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: National Committee for Safe Digital Environments

thematicElements.text: The protection of children's personal data and privacy when they interact with AI systems
thematicElements.justification: The document includes specific recommendations such as requiring platforms to set high default privacy levels limit the collection of sensitive data and avoid the use of persuasive design (CRC 2025 p.19). It proposes moving toward a regulatory framework that includes age verification verifiable parental consent and clear limits on the commercial use of personal data (p.19). It warns that AI collects data on minors' use and that this can lead to commercial exploitation if not properly regulated (pp. 4 and 15).

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the use of AI to exploit manipulate or harm children including through targeted advertising or inappropriate content
thematicElements.justification: The document proposes default security settings restrictions on the use of personal data and impact assessments to prevent abusive practices such as targeted advertising or persuasive design (CRC 2025 pp.15-19). It also calls for a manual on ethics and transparency for the design and use of AI with a focus on child protection (p.7).

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers of AI to design systems that are safe age-appropriate and beneficial for children
thematicElements.justification: The document assigns explicit obligations to those who design and operate AI systems. AI systems must be designed from the outset with accessibility ethics inclusion privacy and security criteria as default settings respecting the diversity and age of children and adolescents (CRC 2025 p.6). It also establishes that digital platforms applications online services and AI systems must incorporate age-specific protection measures in their design development and use (p.15).

items.title: Bill 043 of 2025 'Through which artificial intelligence is regulated in Colombia'
items.justification: Bill 043 of 2025S addresses cultural and linguistic diversity in the development of artificial intelligence through guiding principles such as diversity inclusion and a differential approach that urges respect for ethnic cultural and territorial plurality (Article 3.2). It promotes the participation of historically excluded communities and the use of ancestral and community knowledge (Article 3.15). In the field of education it establishes the incorporation of intercultural and territorial content in AI training programs (Articles 21 and 23) ensuring a critical digital citizenship that respects the country's cultural diversity.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of the development of AI systems that are representative of and responsive to a wide range of cultures and languages
thematicElements.justification: Partially because Bill 043 of 2025S includes provisions that promote the development of AI systems that are representative and sensitive to cultural diversity but it does not use those exact words or address linguistic sensitivity. In Article 3.2 it establishes principles of diversity and inclusion advocating for respect for ethnic and cultural plurality and the participation of historically excluded groups. Article 3.15 highlights the importance of local and ancestral knowledge promoting AI systems that reflect local identities. Although it does not explicitly mention multiple languages the territorial and intercultural approach suggests an inclusive intention.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the development of AI tools that perpetuate cultural stereotypes erase linguistic diversity or favor dominant cultures
thematicElements.justification: Partially because although Bill 043 of 2025S includes measures to prevent the perpetuation of cultural stereotypes and the elimination of linguistic diversity it does not do so literally. Article 3.2 establishes principles of diversity and inclusion requiring AI to respect ethnic and cultural plurality and prohibiting discriminatory practices. Article 3.4 promotes ethics and sustainability for non-discrimination and respect for human rights which may include the protection of cultural identities. Article 3.9 requires developers to ensure the protection of fundamental rights. In addition Article 19 requires authorization for the use of voices and images which in a way protects linguistic representation.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to ensure their systems are trained on diverse datasets and are adaptable to various cultural and linguistic contexts
thematicElements.justification: Bill 043 of 2025S establishes obligations for entities that develop and use AI promoting diverse systems that are adaptable to different cultural contexts although it does not explicitly mention linguistic diversity. Article 4.9 assigns the developer the responsibility of ensuring technical quality bias mitigation and transparency which implies avoiding cultural biases and using representative data. Article 6 requires an analysis of data quality and representativeness in high-risk systems with a focus on diversity. In addition Article 3.2 promotes the participation of historically excluded groups ensuring that systems are inclusive and adapted to diverse cultural realities.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy (CONPES 4144) (2025)(Colombia)
items.justification: Document CONPES 4144 (National Planning Department 2025) initially addresses the environmental impact of AI highlighting its intensive energy and water consumption in data centers the generation of electronic waste and the carbon footprint of the technology's life cycle (pp.71-72). It points out the lack of measurement tools in Colombia and proposes continuously evaluating the social economic and environmental effects of AI to ensure its sustainability.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: The Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development in coordination with the Ministry of Information and Communications Technology the National Environmental Licensing Authority DANE the Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation and DNP

thematicElements.text: The prevention of resource-intensive AI development and deployment that contributes to excessive energy consumption and e-waste
thematicElements.justification: Document CONPES 4144 (National Planning Department 2025) acknowledges the environmental impact of AI including excessive energy consumption and the generation of electronic waste (pp.71-72). Furthermore in line of action 5.6 (pp.99-100) it proposes the development of a technical document between 2025 and 2026 to mitigate the environmental impact of energy consumption derived from the use of AI systems. However the document does not include specific measures to prevent the development of resource-intensive AI nor does it directly address the prevention of e-waste.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers to measure and report on the energy usage and environmental impact of their AI models

The promotion of efforts to improve the energy efficiency of data centers including the use of renewable energy sources advanced cooling technologies and optimized hardware to reduce their significant carbon footprint and water consumption

items.title: Standards on Algorithmic Transparency for the Algorithmic Systems used by the state (Office of the Attorney General of Colombia and Office of the Ombudsman of Colombia)
items.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 addresses fairness and non-discrimination by establishing the principle of 'primacy of fundamental rights' (Article 5a) requiring prior analysis of algorithmic systems' impacts on equality and non-discrimination. It mandates justification for affirmative actions (Article 13 Par.2) and demands algorithmic impact analysis to identify and mitigate risks of differentiated biases or affectations (Article 13c). These measures aim to ensure equitable treatment especially for vulnerable populations.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: Among the considerations it is established that Article 24 of Law 1755 of 2015 indicates that confidential information and documents include those related to national defense or security among others (Joint Directive 007 2025 p.3). This implies that algorithmic systems related to national defense and security are explicitly excluded from the scope of the Directive by virtue of legal exceptions to access to public information.

body.name: The Public Prosecutors Office

thematicElements.text: The promotion of fair and equitable outcomes from AI systems ensuring they don't produce biased results that disproportionately affect certain groups
thematicElements.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 promotes fair and equitable outcomes in AI systems under the following terms. It establishes in Article 5 the principle of 'primacy of fundamental rights' which requires analyzing the impact of algorithmic systems on equality and non-discrimination prior to their implementation. Article 13 requires the publication of algorithmic impact analyses and the identification of biases or differential effects. Article 13 paragraph 2 also requires justification for affirmative action aimed at promoting equity for vulnerable groups. However the framework only addresses the public sector

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI systems from perpetuating or amplifying existing societal biases and discrimination based on race ethnicity gender religion age or other protected characteristics
thematicElements.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 also includes measures to prevent AI systems from perpetuating social biases. In the same way as in the previous question Article 5 requires prior analysis of the impact of algorithms on fundamental rights such as equality and non-discrimination. Article 13 mandates the publication of algorithmic impact analyses that identify biases and differential effects. In addition Article 13 Paragraph 2 requires justification for affirmative actions that promote equity avoiding discrimination based on protected characteristics.However the framework only addresses the public sector

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers to proactively identify measure and mitigate sources of bias throughout the AI lifecycle from data collection to deployment
thematicElements.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 assigns clear obligations to prevent bias at all stages of the life cycle of algorithmic systems but only for public sector. Article 5 requires prior analysis of impacts on equality and non-discrimination. Article 13 mandates the publication of algorithmic impact analysis results including biases and differentiated effects. Article 14 establishes mitigation measures such as human review and audits. In addition Article 23 requires contracts to include clauses obliging suppliers to adopt good ethical and technical practices and Article 22 imposes continuous updating in the event of relevant changes in the algorithmic systems used by the State.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy (CONPES 4144) (2025)(Colombia)
items.justification: Document CONPES 4144 (National Planning Department of Colombia -NDP- 2025) addresses gender equality in AI by proposing strategies against gender-based violence in digital environments such as deepfakes and warning about algorithmic biases (p. 99). It promotes a differential and intersectional approach to the data life cycle and is aligned with the Public Policy on Gender Equality (CONPES 4080 of 2022 p.30). It indicates that these actions seek to ensure ethical inclusive and equitable AI with the active participation of women in its development and application.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Communications Regulation Commission the National Planning Department and the Ministry of Equality and Equity

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the development and use of AI systems and tools that perpetuate gender discrimination and bias
thematicElements.justification: CONPES 4144 (DNP 2025) includes provisions related to preventing gender discrimination and violence in AI-powered digital environments but lacks comprehensive technical or regulatory measures to mitigate gender biases in AI system development. Action 5.5 focuses on equity inclusion and environmental sustainability stating it will promote actions to prevent AI from exacerbating inequalities (p.99). The document acknowledges AI’s potential to increase social inequalities and biases (p.33). However while it recognizes risks and suggests related actions it does not include robust measures like gender-focused algorithm audits or bias detection tools. Thus the framework addresses the issue only partially.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations and responsibilities to entities developing and using AI systems to ensure Gender Equality and prevent discrimination
thematicElements.justification: The document partially assigns responsibilities to entities for ensuring gender equality and preventing discrimination in AI systems. Action 5.18 explicitly designates the CRC Ministry of Equality and Equity and DNP to design and implement a strategy addressing gender-based violence in digital environments involving AI. This includes diagnostics awareness campaigns and training for authorities and civil society (DNP 2025 Appendix A). However the framework does not establish comprehensive or binding obligations for all AI developers and users to ensure gender equality or prevent discrimination across AI systems.

thematicElements.text: Initiatives to increase women representation in the AI industry workforce

items.title: Roadmap for the Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence in Colombia (Ministry of Science of Colombia)
items.justification: The Roadmap (Ministry of Science 2024) addresses human oversight and determination in AI mainly in the sections on Ethics in Artificial Intelligence (p.21) and Colombia and its Framework for AI (pp.49-52). The document defines Human-in-the-loop models as total human control over decision-making and Human-over-the-loop as a transition towards greater autonomy of the algorithmic system (p.51) promotes human intervention in automated decisions (p.51) and establishes principles such as transparency explainability accountability (pp.50-54) and citizen participation (p.76) as mechanisms for inclusive oversight and guaranteeing human agency.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of meaningful human control over AI systems ensuring that AI remains a tool to assist humans rather than replacing human judgment particularly in critical areas where AI-enabled decisions or actions can have broad and systemic implications
thematicElements.justification: The Roadmap (Ministry of Science 2024) defines the Human-in-the-loop and Human-over-the-loop models (p.51) establishing that systems should not interact with citizens without human supervision. Furthermore human intervention is required in automated decisions especially in high-risk contexts. Pages 50 to 54 reinforce principles such as transparency explainability and accountability ensuring that AI functions as a support tool and not as a replacement for human judgment.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of full automation in sensitive sectors where human intervention and ethical judgment are necessary such as in law enforcement or medicine
thematicElements.justification: The Roadmap (Ministry of Science 2024) includes explicit measures to prevent total automation in medicine and security. Returning to what has been said it establishes that AI systems must maintain meaningful human control especially in high-risk applications (p.51). The Human-in-the-loop and Human-over-the-loop models are defined which guarantee human intervention in automated decisions. Furthermore on page 52 it is stated that critical decisions in sectors such as health and national security must be made by humans using AI as a support not as a substitute for ethical judgment.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities using AI to designate responsible individuals who can oversee intervene in and ultimately be accountable for the decisions made by the system
thematicElements.justification: The Roadmap (Ministry of Science 2024) assigns obligations to entities that use AI. For example it proposes the creation of a “national entity or committee to support issues related to ethical auditing in AI” responsible for evaluating ethical compliance (p.76). In addition it establishes that systems must allow for human intervention in automated decisions especially in high-risk contexts (p.51). It also promotes demonstrated responsibility (p.74) requiring that actors involved in the design and implementation of AI be accountable for their decisions.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy (CONPES 4144) (2025)(Colombia)
items.justification: Document CONPES 4144 (National Planning Department 2025) addresses AI impact assessments mainly in the strategic area of Risk Mitigation. On page 96 line of action 5.1 is proposed which seeks to promote knowledge and reduce vulnerabilities related to AI. In addition line of action 5.2 (p.98) proposes monitoring the impact on employment and 5.3 (p.98) addresses privacy protection. These actions reflect an ex-ante and ex-post approach to identifying and mitigating social ethical and environmental risks.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: National Planning Department

thematicElements.text: The promotion of a culture of proactive risk management by requiring that the potential societal ethical and environmental impacts of AI systems are evaluated before their deployment
thematicElements.justification: Document CONPES 4144 (National Planning Department 2025) promotes proactive risk management in AI but does not require formal assessments prior to deployment. Action line 5.1 (p.96) proposes strengthening capacities to identify ethical and social risks. Action line 5.2 (p.98) also addresses impacts on employment and action line 5.3 (p.98) addresses privacy and intimacy but no mandatory ex-ante assessment requirement is established. Thus aspects of awareness and monitoring are covered but not all elements of the indicator.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and users of AI to conduct comprehensive Impact Assessments that identify and mitigate potential risks to individuals and society
The establishment of rights for the public to access the findings of these assessments ensuring that they can hold organizations accountable for the impacts of their AI systems

items.title: Law 2466 of 2025 - (through which labor regulations are partially modified and a Labor Reform for decent and dignified work in Colombia is adopted) (The Congress of Colombia)
items.justification: Law 2466 of 2025 addresses labour protections in the context of AI specifically for digital delivery platforms. Articles 29 and 30 require transparency regarding automated monitoring and decision-making systems that affect access to orders income security and contractual status. They also guarantee the right to human review of automated decisions and prohibit unjustified suspensions (pp.9–10). These provisions aim to prevent discrimination and strengthen labour rights within algorithmic management ensuring fair treatment of workers in the digital economy.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Ministry of Labour

thematicElements.text: The protection of workers from AI-driven discrimination in hiring promotion and termination decisions — including those who  lack an employment contract but are subject to algorithmic management systems
thematicElements.justification: Law 2466 of 2025 addresses some aspects of protection against algorithmic discrimination but not all. Articles 29 and 30 require transparency regarding automated systems on digital platforms and guarantee the right to human review of decisions affecting working conditions preventing unjustified suspensions. However it does not explicitly regulate hiring promotion or dismissal processes in other sectors or for workers without contracts outside of platforms.

thematicElements.text: Requirements for transparency in the management process including obligations to explain how AI systems are used to monitor performance make employment-related decisions and interact with or affect workers’ right to access workplace benefits
thematicElements.justification: Law 2466 of 2025 establishes transparency requirements regarding the use of automated systems in labour management. Articles 29 and 30 require digital platforms to inform workers about the automated systems used for monitoring and decision-making that affect working conditions income access to orders and contractual status. It also guarantees the right to human review and prohibits discriminatory decisions in such processes.

thematicElements.text: The reinforcement of workers' rights to organise and collectively bargain in the context of AI-driven changes in the workplace including in sectors dominated by gig work

items.title: Standards on Algorithmic Transparency for the Algorithmic Systems used by the state (Office of the Attorney General of Colombia and Office of the Ombudsman of Colombia)
items.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 establishes active disclosure obligations regarding algorithmic systems (Art. 8-9) requiring minimum public content such as purpose data used and developer. It also regulates enhanced transparency for high-impact systems (Art. 13) algorithmic impact analysis (Art. 14) and access to source code or meaningful explanation (Art. 17) which consolidates public disclosure mechanisms.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: Among the considerations it is established that Article 24 of Law 1755 of 2015 indicates that confidential information and documents include those related to national defense or security among others (Joint Directive 007 2025 p.3). This implies that algorithmic systems related to national defense and security are explicitly excluded from the scope of the Directive by virtue of legal exceptions to access to public information.

body.name: The Public Prosecutors Office

thematicElements.text: The establishment of a public registry or inventory of all AI systems used by the government including their purpose a general description of their function and the agency responsible for their operation
The requirement to disclose key information about high-risk systems such as the data used for training the rationale for their use and the results of any impact assessments
thematicElements.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 requires enhanced disclosure for high-impact systems (Art. 13) including data used and its origin through training information (Art. 13.f) reasonableness and justification for the use of the system (Art. 13. b) and publication of algorithmic impact analysis biases and risks (Arts. 13.c and 14).

thematicElements.text: Clear guidelines on what information is subject to public disclosure versus what must be protected for reasons of national security or individual privacy
thematicElements.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 establishes clear limits on public disclosure as it refers to the grounds for confidentiality in Law 1712 of 2014 and requires a harm test to be applied before denying information (Art. 19). It also protects personal data by requiring compliance with current regulations (Art. 5.g). In this way it defines what can be disclosed and what must be withheld for security or privacy reasons.

thematicElements.text: The provision of a clear and accessible explanation for the public on how an AI system works and how it might affect them avoiding technical jargon
thematicElements.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 requires that information on algorithmic systems be presented in clear understandable language that is accessible to the public (Art. 5.d). It also mandates that meaningful explanations be provided on how a system works and how it produces decisions (Art. 17) as well as detailing decision criteria and effects in high-impact cases (Art. 13).

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy (CONPES 4144) (2025)(Colombia)
items.justification: CONPES 4144 Document (DNP 2025) addresses public procurement of AI in the Action Plan specifically in Objective 5.3.6 (pp.101-103). It establishes guidelines for incorporating AI systems as an attribute in technological solutions acquired through public procurement mechanisms for reducing digital security risks and technical support strategies for public entities.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: National Public Procurement Agency (Colombia Compra Eficiente) MinTIC and DNP

thematicElements.text: The establishment of AI-specific procurement guidelines that go beyond traditional IT procurement to include ethical social and technical considerations
thematicElements.justification: CONPES 4144 Document (DNP 2025) includes the structuring and dissemination of legal guidelines for the incorporation of AI systems in public procurement (objective 5.3.6 pp.101-103 and Annex A actions 6.1 and 6.2) which cover technical and digital security aspects. However it does not detail a comprehensive framework that explicitly integrates all ethical social and technical dimensions into the procurement guidelines but rather focuses more on legal guidelines and technical support.

thematicElements.text: The requirement for vendors to demonstrate that their AI systems have undergone thorough testing for bias fairness and safety
The assignment of a mandate to require transparency from vendors regarding the data and models used in their products to prevent 'black box' systems
Procurement mechanisms that include elements or conditions for prioritising local AI developments as a strategy for enhancing AI sovereignty
thematicElements.justification: CONPES 4144 Document (DNP 2025) includes recommendations to strengthen technological sovereignty by promoting the adoption and development of AI systems in Colombia with an emphasis on supporting local innovation and capacity building (Objective 5.3.6 p.101). In addition it mentions technical support for public entities and the promotion of AI projects with a territorial and social focus. However it does not specify public procurement mechanisms that explicitly prioritise local developments as a formal strategy for AI sovereignty.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy (CONPES 4144) (2025)(Colombia)
items.justification: CONPES 4144 (DNP 2025) addresses the indicator in the context of AI mainly under Objective 4 and its actions (pp.93-95). It proposes strategies to overcome technological barriers in education (Line of action 4.1 p.93) develop competencies for ethical and responsible AI use (line of action 4.2 pp.93-94) strengthen human capital for AI-related roles (Line of action 4.3 pp.94-95) promote social appropriation of AI knowledge (Line of action 4.4 p.95) and addresses labor reconversion to mitigate job displacement (Line of action 5.2 p.98).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Ministry of Information Technology and Communications Ministry of National Education Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation Ministry of Labour National Learning Service Colombian Institute for the Evaluation of Education and the National Planning Department

thematicElements.text: The establishment of government-funded or subsidized reskilling and upskilling programs to help workers adapt to new job market demands created by AI
thematicElements.justification: CONPES 4144 (DNP 2025) includes provisions and measures related to government-funded retraining and skills improvement programmes. For example it promotes training capacity building and digital skills development programmes led by MinTIC SENA and MinTrabajo (pp.93-95). In addition line of action 5.2 (p.98) includes strategies for job retraining and worker protection in the face of automation. However it does not detail a single explicit national retraining programme or direct subsidies to third parties for workers.

thematicElements.text: The provision of financial support or incentives for workers who participate in reskilling programs
Requirements for companies to invest in the training and development of their existing workforce to mitigate job displacement caused by automation

items.title: Guidelines on the Processing of Personal Data in Artificial Intelligence Systems (Superintendency of Industry and Commerce of Colombia) (2024)
items.justification: External Circular 002 of 2024 mentions the principle of security as part of the design of AI projects (p.3). A privacy impact assessment is required prior to the development of AI including security measures and risk assessment (p.6). Technological human and administrative measures are detailed to prevent unauthorized access manipulation or destruction of data (p.7). These provisions seek to ensure the protection of personal data in AI systems.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The establishment of performance thresholds or quality benchmarks to ensure AI systems operate reliably and accurately under stated conditions
The implementation of safeguards fallback procedures or emergency protocols to mitigate harm in case of AI system failure or unexpected behavior
The requirement for pre-deployment testing validation or documentation to ensure technical robustness throughout the AI system lifecycle
thematicElements.justification: External Circular 002 of 2024 mandates a privacy impact assessment prior to the design and development of AI systems requiring documentation of processing operations risk assessment and the implementation of technical software and security measures for data protection (p. 6). However it does not specify requirements for technical tests validations or pre-deployment testing to ensure technical robustness throughout the AI system lifecycle. Thus while it establishes a framework for prior planning and documentation it only partially fulfills the requirement for thorough technical robustness as explicit validation measures are not included.

thematicElements.text: The introduction of security obligations to protect AI systems against cyberattacks manipulation or adversarial interference
thematicElements.justification: External Circular 002 of 2024 establishes security measures to protect AI systems against unauthorized access manipulation and destruction of personal data (p.7). It mandates the adoption of technological human administrative physical and contractual measures which must also be auditable by authorities. However while it addresses data security risks it does not include specific obligations related to protecting AI systems from cyberattacks or adversarial interference. Therefore while the document covers some aspects of security obligations it only partially meets the requirement for comprehensive protection against all potential threats.

items.title: Roadmap for the Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence in Colombia (Ministry of Science of Colombia)
items.justification: The Roadmap (Ministry of Science 2024) defines algorithmic transparency as the availability of clear and understandable information about AI systems including active and passive practices to inform citizens (p.48). It highlights the importance of explainability so that people understand how systems work and how decisions are made even in complex or ‘black box’ systems (pp. 48-49). In addition it promotes mechanisms for ethical auditing citizen participation education in AI ethics and continuous evaluation to strengthen trust and accountability (pp. 81-82).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of clarity regarding how AI systems operate including their purpose data sources and decision-making logic to foster public trust
thematicElements.justification: The Roadmap (Ministry of Science 2024) addresses the promotion of clarity on how AI systems operate including their purpose data sources and decision-making logic primarily through the principle of algorithmic transparency (pp.48-49). It details transparency in data use algorithm objectives and decision explanations including for 'Black Box' systems. It also emphasizes public participation and accessible information (pp.75-77).

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to provide meaningful explanations of their systems' outputs especially in high-stakes contexts like hiring or loan applications
thematicElements.justification: The Roadmap (Ministry of Science 2024) recommends that entities developing and using AI provide meaningful explanations of their systems' outputs emphasising transparency and explainability even for complex 'black box' systems (pp.48–51). It highlights the need to tailor explanations to different audiences and contexts ensuring understanding and accountability (pp.49-55). Although the framework covers the principle in general terms it lacks detailed provisions for specific high-risk use cases.

thematicElements.text: The establishment of rights for individuals to receive an explanation for a decision made by an AI system that affects them and to understand the key factors that led to that outcome
thematicElements.justification: The Roadmap (Ministry of Science 2024) establishes the right of individuals to receive meaningful explanations about AI decisions affecting them emphasizing transparency and explanation as ethical principles (pp.49-51). It highlights the need to provide comprehensible information on system design decision logic and impact especially in high-risk contexts adapting explanations to diverse audiences (pp.50-51). The framework also promotes accountability and continuous evaluation of AI systems (pp.49-55). However it does not explicitly detail enforcement mechanisms or specific rights in all contexts so the coverage is partial.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2027 (Costa Rica)
items.justification: The ENIA 2024-2027 establishes education & training as a cross-cutting principle explicitly committing to the integration of AI education into school technical & university curricula to ensure that all individuals have the necessary skills to use and benefit from AI (p.35). The Strategy further specifies that AI education should begin in the early stages of the educational system (p.55) a commitment aligned with the National Science Technology and Innovation Plan (NPSTI) (p.61). These provisions address curriculum reform across primary secondary vocational & tertiary levels of formal education.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Ministry of Science Innovation Technology and Telecommunications

thematicElements.text: Curriculum reforms including at primary secondary tertiary levels
thematicElements.justification: Although the Strategy does not describe specific curriculum reforms it explicitly states the need to integrate AI education into school technical and university curricula to ensure that all individuals have the necessary skills to use and benefit from AI (p.35) and specifies that AI education should begin in the early stages of the educational system (p.55).

thematicElements.text: Establishment of educational institutions or programs offering AI-related courses within the formal education system
thematicElements.justification: The Strategy does not itself establish educational institutions or programmes offering AI-related courses but recognises the need to prioritise STEAM competencies from early education through university (p.61) referencing the National Science Technology and Innovation Plan (NPSTI) as the framework under which AI integration in the education system is being pursued.

thematicElements.text: Provision of teacher training and resources for AI education
thematicElements.justification: The Strategy assigns the Ministry of Public Education (MEP) responsibility for leading the integration of AI tools into the educational system and for training teaching staff to acquire the necessary skills to maximise the use of these technologies. This includes equipping educators to identify mitigate and manage misuse or inappropriate application of AI by students (p.26).

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2027 (Costa Rica)
items.justification: The ENIA 2024-2027 addresses this indicator narrowly through its respective section (p.26). The strategy recognises that children & adolescents are particularly vulnerable to data manipulation exposure to inappropriate content & the exploitation of sensitive data for commercial purposes. To mitigate these risks the strategy states that it is essential to establish robust ethical safeguards including data anonymisation limitations on the collection & use of personal information & the implementation of effective parental controls. These provisions address the protection of children's personal data and the prevention of exploitative uses of AI directed at children.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Ministry of Science Innovation Technology and Telecommunications

thematicElements.text: The protection of children's personal data and privacy when they interact with AI systems
thematicElements.justification: The strategy states that children and adolescents are particularly vulnerable to mitigate these risks it is essential to establish robust ethical safeguards including data anonymization limitations on the collection and use of personal information and the implementation of effective parental controls (p.26).

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the use of AI to exploit manipulate or harm children including through targeted advertising or inappropriate content
thematicElements.justification: In p.26 the strategy recognises that children are vulnerable to data manipulation exposure to inappropriate content and commercial exploitation of their sensitive data through digital platforms and calls for the establishment of robust ethical safeguards to mitigate these risks. This partially addresses prevention of exploitative and harmful uses of AI directed at children. However it doesn't prescribe specific prohibitions concrete preventive mechanisms or binding restrictions on targeted advertising or harmful content directed at minors.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers of AI to design systems that are safe age-appropriate and beneficial for children

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2027 (Costa Rica)
items.justification: Through two guiding principles which constitute the operative basis it addresses this indicator. The Equity & Non-discrimination principle (p.32) which says AI systems be accessible to all sectors of society respecting differences in age ethnicity gender religion economic capacity & educational level & that systems be adapted to be culturally & linguistically appropriate. The Inclusion & Accessibility principle (p.34) which requires that AI be culturally & linguistically appropriate. The strategy also notes in p.20 that Costa Rica can advocate internationally for an inclusive approach respecting cultural & linguistic diversity & identifies cultural bias and contextual misinterpretation as key risks associated with AI (pp.39 41).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Ministry of Science Innovation Technology and Telecommunications

thematicElements.text: The promotion of the development of AI systems that are representative of and responsive to a wide range of cultures and languages
thematicElements.justification: The Equity and non-discrimination principle (p.32) says that AI should be accessible to all sectors of society respecting differences in age ethnicity gender religion economic capacity and educational level while adapting systems to be culturally and linguistically appropriate.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the development of AI tools that perpetuate cultural stereotypes erase linguistic diversity or favor dominant cultures
The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to ensure their systems are trained on diverse datasets and are adaptable to various cultural and linguistic contexts

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2027 (Costa Rica)
items.justification: The Strategy mentions that non-discrimination is a central concern in AI applications if not carefully designed and monitored AI systems can replicate and amplify biases (p.23). To ensure equity and non-discrimination it is essential to create opportunities for training and skills development in emerging technologies for everyone (p.32). That is necessary to analyze the training data and algorithms to identify and mitigate potential biases that could result in discrimination (p.42). And that technical regulations and ethical guidelines will ensure that AI does not perpetuate discrimination (p.55).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Ministry of Science Innovation Technology and Telecommunications

thematicElements.text: The promotion of fair and equitable outcomes from AI systems ensuring they don't produce biased results that disproportionately affect certain groups
thematicElements.justification: The Reference Framework for Costa Rica section (p.42) states that is necessary to analyze the training data and algorithms to identify and mitigate potential biases that could result in discrimination. And the Regulatory Instruments as Enabling Instruments section (p.55) states that technical regulations and ethical guidelines will ensure that AI does not perpetuate discrimination.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI systems from perpetuating or amplifying existing societal biases and discrimination based on race ethnicity gender religion age or other protected characteristics
thematicElements.justification: The Equity and Non-discrimination section (p.32) requires conducting continuous audits and tests to identify and correct any potential biases in AI systems. Furthermore it states that policies and procedures must be implemented to promote diversity and inclusion at all stages of the AI system lifecycle. The Reference Framework for Costa Rica section (p.42) states that is necessary to analyze the training data and algorithms to identify and mitigate potential biases that could result in discrimination. And the Regulatory Instruments as Enabling Instruments section (p.55) states that technical regulations and ethical guidelines will ensure that AI does not perpetuate discrimination.
