thematicElements.text: The establishment of a government-wide strategy for upskilling and reskilling public servants and members of the judiciary to build a foundational understanding of AI its applications and its risks
thematicElements.justification: The Law establishes a government-coordinated approach to AI capacity building through the National Digital Talent Platform under which the SGTD coordinates with public administration entities civil society academia and the private sector to provide courses programs workshops and other training modalities (Art. 13.1). It also contains an explicit sector-specific upskilling mandate: the Ministry of Defense is required to promote capacity building on AI within its sector coordinated with the SGTD academia and private sector companies (Art. 13.4). However the Law does not clearly establish an overarching government-wide strategy covering all public servants across the state.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of dedicated roles and teams within government to act as AI champions providing expert guidance and fostering a culture of responsible AI innovation
The requirement for ongoing professional development and training to keep pace with the rapid evolution of AI technology
thematicElements.justification: he Law defines digital literacy as a continuous process of acquiring and developing digital skills (Art. 6) and it establishes institutional mechanisms for training through the National Digital Talent Platform where the SGTD coordinates courses programs workshops and other training modalities to build AI capabilities (Art. 13.1). This supports an ongoing approach to skills development. However the Law does not clearly frame ongoing professional development as a binding requirement for individuals or institutions specifically to keep pace with the rapid evolution of AI; it is presented more as a promoted and coordinated policy objective than as a strict obligation.

items.title: Supreme Decree 115-2025-PCM (Peru)
items.justification: The law has a section dedicated to establishing obligations for public entities regarding 'AI knowledge and skills training.' Some of these obligations are relatively generic such as the obligation to 'promote the identification and provision of courses programs workshops and other training modalities to build AI capabilities through the National Digital Talent Platform.' More specific is the obligation for the National Authority to coordinate the implementation of study programs aimed at developing AI competencies especially in STEM-related programs (Article 13).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: Yes Article 4 of the law expressly states that the provisions do not apply to the use of Artificial Intelligence-based systems for national defense and security.

body.name: Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (SGTD)

thematicElements.text: The establishment of government-funded or subsidized reskilling and upskilling programs to help workers adapt to new job market demands created by AI
The provision of financial support or incentives for workers who participate in reskilling programs
Requirements for companies to invest in the training and development of their existing workforce to mitigate job displacement caused by automation

items.title: Supreme Decree 115-2025-PCM (Peru)
items.justification: Article 7 of the law establishes various guiding principles being two of them: 'Security proportionality and reliability' and 'Risk-based security standards'. These principles are subsequently developed in greater detail including obligations related to security in the development and use of AI-based systems.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: Article 4 of the law expressly states that the provisions do not apply to the use of Artificial Intelligence-based systems for national defense and security.

body.name: Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (SGTD)

thematicElements.text: The establishment of performance thresholds or quality benchmarks to ensure AI systems operate reliably and accurately under stated conditions
The implementation of safeguards fallback procedures or emergency protocols to mitigate harm in case of AI system failure or unexpected behavior
thematicElements.justification: The principles of article 7 related to Safety and Security are subsequently developed in greater detail including obligations related to safety in the development and use of AI-based systems. Article 29 states that all developers of AI-based systems must implement at least four security measures: 1. Risk management which includes assessing and adopting measures to address risks including data encryption anomaly detection model robustness etc.; 2. Privacy by design; 3. Security audits: to identify and correct vulnerabilities and biases; and 4. Incident management through the implementation of an Information Security Management System.

thematicElements.text: The requirement for pre-deployment testing validation or documentation to ensure technical robustness throughout the AI system lifecycle
thematicElements.justification: Article 29 states that all developers of AI-based systems must implement at least four security measures. One of them is 'Security audits' which is an obligation that consists on conducting periodic digital security audits to identify and correct vulnerabilities and biases in the AI-based system; such audits are mandatory prior to system implementation and throughout its operation. However the way those audits are to be performed are not explained in detail (so we don't know if validation and documentation practices are included).

thematicElements.text: The introduction of security obligations to protect AI systems against cyberattacks manipulation or adversarial interference

items.title: Supreme Decree 115-2025-PCM (Peru)
items.justification: AI-based systems must be clear explainable and accessible ensuring that processes algorithms and decisions are understandable to users implementers and authorities. This includes providing information about their operation the data used decision criteria and potential biases promoting accountability and public trust.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: Yes Article 4 of the law ('Exceptions to the scope of application') expressly states that the provisions do not apply to the use of Artificial Intelligence-based systems for national defense and security.

body.name: Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (SGTD)

thematicElements.text: The promotion of clarity regarding how AI systems operate including their purpose data sources and decision-making logic to foster public trust
thematicElements.justification: Article 7 of the law establishes various guiding principles one of which is “Transparency.” This principle is defined as the obligation that 'AI-based systems must be clear explainable and accessible ensuring that processes algorithms and decisions are understandable to users implementers and authorities.' The law also includes specific obligations in article 25 such as the obligation for those who develop or use AI-based systems considered “high risk” to “inform the user in advance clearly and simply about the purpose or use of the AI-based system its main functionalities and the type of decisions it can make.”

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to provide meaningful explanations of their systems' outputs especially in high-stakes contexts like hiring or loan applications
thematicElements.justification: The law includes a specific obligation in article 25 for those who develop or use AI-based systems considered “high risk” to “inform the user in advance clearly and simply about the purpose or use of the AI-based system its main functionalities and the type of decisions it can make.”

thematicElements.text: The establishment of rights for individuals to receive an explanation for a decision made by an AI system that affects them and to understand the key factors that led to that outcome
thematicElements.justification: The law includes a specific obligation in article 25 for those who develop or use AI-based systems considered “high risk” to “inform the user in advance clearly and simply about the purpose or use of the AI-based system its main functionalities and the type of decisions it can make.” Also in that same article 25.3 it is stated that users may request to receive explanation on the results of such systems in the event that they make decisions that impact human rights. However since this 'right' has not been developed properly it can only be inferred that users can demand compliance with the obligation to be informed through indirect means.

items.title: House Bill No. 1699 or the 'National Digital Skills and AI Readiness Act' (Philippines)
items.justification: 'Sec. 5 of HB 1699 states: “Digital Curriculum Reform in Higher Education - The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) shall revise the existing educational curricula in tertiary education by requiring SUCs to offer at least one Al-related subject across non-tech courses including but not limited to Business Education and Agriculture as may be determined by the CHED.” Sec. 6 states: “The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) shall establish Future Skills Centers to offer free training programs in digital coding digital marketing data science cloud computing and AI tools as well as government-subsidized certification programs on global technology platforms...'' (p. 4)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: Curriculum reforms including at primary secondary tertiary levels
thematicElements.justification: One of the objectives of HB 1699 is 'integrating digital skills and AI education across all levels of formal education' (Sec. 3) implementing 'digital curriculum reform' in basic education (Sec. 4) higher education (Sec. 5) and establishing future skills center (Sec. 6). (pp. 3-4). The reforms will be done to 'equip the youth and workforce with future-proof skills such as digital literacy coding data analytics and artificial intelligence.' (Sec. 2) (p. 3)

thematicElements.text: Establishment of educational institutions or programs offering AI-related courses within the formal education system
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 5 mandates the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) to 'revise the existing educational curricula in tertiary education by requiring the State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) to offer at least one AI-related subject across non-tech courses including but not limited to Business Education and Agriculture as may be determined by the CHED.' (p. 4) It mentions AI-related subjects only not 'AI-related courses.'

thematicElements.text: Provision of teacher training and resources for AI education
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 4 mandates the Department of Education (DepEd) to revise the existing educational curricula to '(c) ensure teachers receive upskilling and certification in digital teaching methods.' However it does not explicitly mention that the training covers 'AI education' only. (p. 4)

items.title: House Bill No. 3823 or the 'Deepfake Accountability and Transparency Act' (Philippines)
items.justification: Sec. 3 of HB 3823 defines (b) Harmful Deepfake as 'a deepfake created or distributed with the intent to deceive defraud or harm an individual or the public.' Sec. 4 makes public disclosure of deepfakes mandatory. Sec 5 states it is 'unlawful to: (a) create or distribute a harmful deepfake without proper disclosure; (b) remove alter or tamper with required disclosures; (c) use deepfake technology to defame deceive commit fraud or incite violence; and (d) obtain consent through coercion deception or misrepresentation for creating a deepfake.' (pp. 3-4)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI tools from being used to create amplify or disseminate misinformation and hate speech or to facilitate harassment and violence
thematicElements.justification: ec. 5 prohibits “the use of deepfake technology to defame deceive commit fraud or incite violence” (p. 4) directly addressing the misuse of AI tools to spread deceptive content and facilitate violence. Sec. 3 also defines “harmful deepfake” as media created or distributed with the intent to deceive or harm individuals or the public (p. 3).

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to platforms and AI developers to implement robust content moderation policies and to be transparent about how their systems handle harmful content

The establishment of rights for individuals and groups targeted by misinformation or tech-facilitated violence to receive protection and to seek redress against the perpetrators and the platforms that enabled the harm
thematicElements.justification: The bill establishes penalties for individuals who create or distribute harmful deepfakes. Sec. 5 prohibits the use of deepfake technology to deceive defame commit fraud or incite violence while Sec. 7 provides fines and imprisonment for violations (pp. 4–5). These provisions offer legal protection and accountability against perpetrators. However the document does not establish specific redress mechanisms for victims or assign liability to platforms that enabled the harm.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the use of AI tools to facilitate gender-based harassment and violence
thematicElements.justification: The bill prohibits harmful uses of deepfake technology that can facilitate harassment or violence. Sec. 5 makes it unlawful to use deepfakes to defame deceive commit fraud or incite violence (p. 4). The explanatory note also highlights harms such as blackmail and non-consensual sharing of intimate images including revenge pornography which are commonly linked to gender-based harassment and abuse.

items.title: House Bill No. 13 or the 'Artificial Intelligence Development and Regulation Act' (Philippines)
items.justification: The draft bill directly addresses AI governance and related accountability and redress mechanisms (p.5 Right to remedy): establishes a right to remedy including the right to opt out of AI systems to obtain timely human review and to appeal and contest AI-driven decisions.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The establishment or reinforcement of judicial mechanisms that allow individuals or groups to seek remedy for harms caused by AI systems
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 5. (e) says 'the development application and use of AI systems shall be guided by the...' the Right to Remedy where 'every [person] shall be given an opportunity to opt out from AI systems in favor of a human alternative' '...shall have access to timely human consideration and remedy through a fallback and escalation process if an automated system fails or produces an error.' The right to appeal or contest AI's impacts on every person shall not be denied. (pp. 4-5) Sec. 9 (b and c) mandate the AI Board 'to investigate motu proprio... or initiate the necessary criminal case against the responsible persons for any violation of this Act'; and ''to issue subpoena and subpoena duces tecum in relation to its investigation...' (p. 9)

thematicElements.text: The creation or use of state-based non-judicial complaint mechanisms (e.g. ombuds institutions regulators tribunals or consumer bodies) to handle AI-related grievances
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 9 mandate the AI Board (b) 'to investigate motu proprio or upon report of any person impose and collect fines and penalties initiate and resolve the necessary administrative action or initiate the necessary criminal case against the responsible persons for any violation of this Act' (p. 9) which includes the development application and use of AI taking into consideration the right to redress by every Filipino.

thematicElements.text: Requirements or incentives for companies or developers to establish accessible grievance or complaints mechanisms for individuals harmed by AI systems
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 5 (e) requires the development application and use of AI systems to be guided by... the Right to Remedy which states that 'every [person] shall be given an opportunity to opt out from AI systems in favor of a human alternative where appropriate. They shall have access to timely human consideration and remedy through a fallback and escalation process if an automated system fails or produces an error. The right to appeal or contest AI's impacts on every person shall not be denied. Human consideration and fallback shall at all times be accessible equitable effective maintained and shall not impose an unreasonable burden to the public.' (pp. 4-5)

items.title: House Bill No. 807 or the 'Take It Down Act of 2025' (Philippines)
items.justification: Sec. 2 of HB 807 provides that it 'is the policy of the State to protect individuals especially women and children from the harms arising from the non-consensual creation possession and dissemination of sexually explicit materials including those produced through artificial intelligence deepfake or any other digital manipulation.' Sec. 3 defines a 'take down request' as a formal verified notification submitted by an affected individual or in the case of minors... seeking removal or disabling of access to content that is alleged to be non-consensual sexually explicit or otherwise prohibited under this Act.'
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The protection of children's personal data and privacy when they interact with AI systems
The prevention of the use of AI to exploit manipulate or harm children including through targeted advertising or inappropriate content
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 2 of HB 807 says it is the policy of the State 'to protect individuals especially women and children from the harms arising from non-consensual creation possession and dissemination of sexually-explicit materials including those produced through artificial intelligence deepfake or any other digital manipulation.' (p. 3) ' Sec. 4  provides that it shall be unlawful to knowingly 'produce or distribute' 'non-consensual sexually explicit material' using 'deepfake AI or other digital manipulation tools.' (p. 4) Sec. 8 (A) (3) says that if the victim is a minor the penalty is higher (Reclusion Temporal). (p. 6)

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers of AI to design systems that are safe age-appropriate and beneficial for children

items.title: House Bill No. 57 or the 'National Artificial Intelligence Code of the Philippines'
items.justification: Sec. 14 of HB 57 promotes Fairness and Non-Discrimination where AI systems shall not result in unjust or disproportionate discrimination based on race... ethnicity religion... (p. 7). Sec. 39 provides support for domestic AI model development and the State's promotion for locally built AI systems and language models particularly those tailored to Philippine languages cultural contexts and institutional needs (p. 14). Sec. 72 tackles the functions of the National Panel of Experts on AI which includes conducting 'emerging risk foresight by identifying analyzing and publicly reporting on speculative or long-term risks associated with AI including potential societal economic and cultural disruptions (p. 20).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of the development of AI systems that are representative of and responsive to a wide range of cultures and languages
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 39 of HB 57 provides that the 'State shall promote the development of locally built AI systems and language models particularly those tailored to Philippine languages cultural contexts and institutional needs.' (p. 14)

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the development of AI tools that perpetuate cultural stereotypes erase linguistic diversity or favor dominant cultures
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 14 of HB 57 promotes Fairness and Non-Discrimination where 'AI systems shall not result in unjust or disproportionate discrimination based on race... ethnicity religion...or other protected characteristics (p. 7). Sec. 72 tackles the functions of the National Panel of Experts on AI which includes conducting 'emerging risk foresight by identifying analyzing and publicly reporting on speculative or long-term risks associated with AI including potential societal economic and cultural disruptions. It also provides that one representative to the National Panel will be a sociologist anthropologist or public interest technologist (p. 20).

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to ensure their systems are trained on diverse datasets and are adaptable to various cultural and linguistic contexts
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 14 of HB 57 promotes Fairness and Non-Discrimination where 'AI systems shall not result in unjust or disproportionate discrimination based on race... ethnicity religion...or other protected characteristics (p. 7). Sec. 72 tackles the functions of the National Panel of Experts on AI which includes conducting 'emerging risk foresight by identifying analyzing and publicly reporting on speculative or long-term risks associated with AI including potential societal economic and cultural disruptions. It also provides that one representative to the National Panel will be a sociologist anthropologist or public interest technologist; also from Visayas or Mindanao (p. 20)

items.title: Senate Bill No. 25 – Artificial Intelligence Regulation Act (AIRA) (Philippines)
items.justification: Sec. 3 (h) of SB No. 25 provides as one of its objectives  'Ensure that policies of both the national and local governments on AI are driven by futures thinking strategic foresight and proactive risk management and are governed by principles of transparency accountability and sustainability.' (p. 2) Sec. 9 (j) states that the National AI Commission shall 'prioritize AI systems that promote the use of AI in agriculture health 31 education disaster risk reduction governance environmental sustainability renewable energy agriculture and biodiversity and other sectors. (p. 6); (k) Issue advisory opinions on AI systems that pose unacceptable risks to human rights... or environmental sustainability. (p. 7)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The prevention of resource-intensive AI development and deployment that contributes to excessive energy consumption and e-waste
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 9 (e) states that the National AI Commission shall 'undertake ethical and sustainability reviews of AI systems in coordination with sectoral regulators and ensure that systems align with social environmental and intergenerational goals' (p. 6) and '(k) issue advisory opinions on AI systems that pose unacceptable risks to human rights public safety democratic integrity or environmental sustainability' (p. 6). The provisions address the prevention of resource-intensive AI as they point to sustainability but does not mention excessive energy consumption.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers to measure and report on the energy usage and environmental impact of their AI models

The promotion of efforts to improve the energy efficiency of data centers including the use of renewable energy sources advanced cooling technologies and optimized hardware to reduce their significant carbon footprint and water consumption

items.title: National Privacy Commission Advisory No. 2024-04 or the Guidelines on the Application of Republic Act No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (DPA) Its Implementing Rules and Regulations and the Issuances of the Commission to Artificial Intelligence Systems Processing Personal Data
items.justification: Section 2 provides that Personal Information Controllers (PICs) ensure that personal data is processed in a manner that is neither manipulative nor unduly oppressive to data subjects... PICs shall implement mechanisms to identify and monitor biases in the AI systems and to limit such biases and their impact on the data subjects. PICs must consider systemic bias human bias and statistical bias when assessing or auditing their AI systems... PICs shall not utilize AI Washing... PICs must maintain the accuracy of personal data to ensure the fairness of the output of the AI systems. PICs shall implement appropriate measures to ensure that personal data utilized in the AI systems is correct and kept up to date. (p. 3)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of fair and equitable outcomes from AI systems ensuring they don't produce biased results that disproportionately affect certain groups
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 2 C of the Advisory states that PICs 'shall implement mechanisms to identify and monitor biases in the AI systems and to limit such biases and their impact on the data subjects. PICs must consider systemic bias human bias and statistical bias when assessing or auditing their AI systems.' (p. 3)

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI systems from perpetuating or amplifying existing societal biases and discrimination based on race ethnicity gender religion age or other protected characteristics
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 2 C of the Advisory states that PICs 'shall implement mechanisms to identify and monitor biases in the AI systems and to limit such biases and their impact on the data subjects. PICs must consider systemic bias human bias and statistical bias when assessing or auditing their AI systems.' (p. 3)

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers to proactively identify measure and mitigate sources of bias throughout the AI lifecycle from data collection to deployment
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 2 C of the Advisory states that PICs 'shall implement mechanisms to identify and monitor biases in the AI systems and to limit such biases and their impact on the data subjects. PICs must consider systemic bias human bias and statistical bias when assessing or auditing their AI systems.' (p. 3)

items.title: Updated Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment (GEWE) Plan 2019-2025 (Philippines)
items.justification: The Plan talks about how due to 'restricted access to education and training structural barriers and social norms' 'low-skilled and routine manufacturing jobs are predominantly held by women.' (p. 34) The plan discusses how to 'proactively prepare to address the potential job losses” caused by AI and other emerging technologies.” (p. 24) The Plan thinks it is 'imperative that policy responses and investments are appropriately targeted both accelerating technological trends as well as deeply-rooted management practices in global value chains to avoid further deepening of the existing inequalities between men and women in the production sectors of the economy.' (p. 34)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Philippine Commission on Women (PWE)

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the development and use of AI systems and tools that perpetuate gender discrimination and bias
The assignment of obligations and responsibilities to entities developing and using AI systems to ensure Gender Equality and prevent discrimination
Initiatives to increase women representation in the AI industry workforce
thematicElements.justification: The Plan mentions 'a program with support from the ILO called Women in STEM Workforce Readiness and Development which provides women with critical soft and technical STEM-related skills employability and leadership training coupled with targeted mentorship to help women gain quality employment and advancement opportunities in STEM-related jobs.' (p. 75) The Plan also mentions creating opportunities to encourage entry of women in the S&T and ICT workforce.' (p. 175)

items.title: House Bill 02323 or the 'Artificial Intelligence Act' of 2025 (Philipines)
items.justification: The bill provides that it shall be the policy of the State to 'incorporate a gender-sensitive pro-children and pro-poor perspective' in all AI efforts plans and programs.' (p. 5) Sec. 12 provides for the 'identification of differential impact of AI on local sectors and distinct populations including the labor sector women...' (p. 12) Sec. 13 mandates government institutions 'related to the welfare of women children... to examine current biases and discriminatory practices in AI technologies and work the council to create troubleshooting strategies to address these discriminatory practices.' (p. 14)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the development and use of AI systems and tools that perpetuate gender discrimination and bias
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 2 provides that the State shall 'emphasize the protection of all citizens from discrimination and shall endeavor to protect its citizens from vulnerabilities related to bias and discriminatory AI systems and models resulting from potential data poisoning of AI models.' It also provides that the State shall 'take measures to limit biases in AI models' in recognition of the vulnerabilities of special populations (p. 5). Sec. 13 also mandates government agencies to examine current biases and discriminatory practices in AI technologies and work with the council to create troubleshooting strategies to address these discriminatory practices.' (p. 14)

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations and responsibilities to entities developing and using AI systems to ensure Gender Equality and prevent discrimination
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 2 provides that the State shall 'take measures to limit biases in AI models' in recognition of the vulnerabilities of special populations (p. 5) including the labor sector women children.. and other populations vulnerable to discriminatory practices... (p. 12)

thematicElements.text: Initiatives to increase women representation in the AI industry workforce
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 12 states that the '(c) Identification of differential impacts of artificial intelligence on local sectors and distinct populations including the labor sector women children elderly and other populations vulnerable to discriminatory practices' shall be a major component of the national AI action plan. (p. 12) This can constitute increasing representation in the AI workforce.

items.title: House Bill No. 57 or the 'National Artificial Intelligence Code of the Philippines'
items.justification: Sec. 4.j. 'Human oversight' means the presence of operational procedures and technical mechanisms allowing humans to understand intervene in suspend or override an AI system's behavior where necessary for safety legality or accountability. (p. 2). Sec. 5.a. says 'every individual shall have the right to meaningful human oversight in decisions that affect their rights freedoms opportunities or safety. No AI system shall have final authority over such decisions without a mechanism for human review correction or override. (p. 4) Sec. 8 The Bureau of Artificial Intelligence Systems shall... (b) The Division on Ethical Risk and Human Oversight responsible for enforcing ethical safeguards and human fallback mechanisms... (p. 6).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of meaningful human control over AI systems ensuring that AI remains a tool to assist humans rather than replacing human judgment particularly in critical areas where AI-enabled decisions or actions can have broad and systemic implications
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 15 of HB 57 provides that for High-Risk AI Systems the Bureau of Artificial Intelligence Systems (BAIS) shall classify certain AI systems as high-risk based on the following factors: (c) Degree of autonomy and lack of meaningful human oversight; SEC. 16. Right to Human Review. - Any person affected by a decision recommendation classification or denial made primarily by an AI system shall have the right to request human intervention review or override of that decision by a competent and authorized officer. (p. 8)

thematicElements.text: The prevention of full automation in sensitive sectors where human intervention and ethical judgment are necessary such as in law enforcement or medicine
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 23 of HB 47 provides that for AI in Healthcare and Medical Decision-Making 'no AI system shall be deployed for diagnostic triage treatment or prioritization without: (b) Continuous human oversight by a licensed health professional' (pp. 9-10)

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities using AI to designate responsible individuals who can oversee intervene in and ultimately be accountable for the decisions made by the system
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 4.j. 'Human oversight' means the presence of operational procedures and technical mechanisms allowing humans to understand intervene in suspend or override an AI system's behavior where necessary... (p. 2). Sec. 14 provides for clearly identifiable human or institutional actor legally and operationally responsible for the outcomes of an AI system. (p. 7). Sec. 16. states that 'any person affected by a decision recommendation classification or denial made primarily by an AI system shall have the right to request human intervention...' (p. 8) Sec. 20 prohibits 'the deployment of autonomous Al systems in contexts where there is no effective mechanism for human intervention such as law enforcement use of lethal force.' (p. 9).

items.title: House Bill No. 13 or the 'Artificial Intelligence Development and Regulation Act' (Philippines)
items.justification: Sec 5 of HB 13 provides that the development application and use of AI systems shall be guided by certain rights of every Filipino including the Right Against Algorithmic Discrimination. To protect equal rights it is required to institute 'proactive equity assessments as part of the system design... pre-deployment and ongoing disparity testing and mitigation and clear organizational oversight.' 'Independent evaluation and plain language reporting in the form of an algorithmic impact assessment including disparity testing results and mitigation; information shall be performed and made public whenever possible to confirm these protections' (p.4)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The promotion of a culture of proactive risk management by requiring that the potential societal ethical and environmental impacts of AI systems are evaluated before their deployment
thematicElements.justification: Sec 5 protects the rights of Filipinos against (a) unsafe and ineffective AI systems and (b) algorithmic discrimination. Systems shall undergo 'pre-deployment testing risk identification and mitigation and ongoing monitoring that they are safe and effective based on intended use.' AI system designers developers and deployers shall take pro-active and continuous measures to protect individuals and communities from algorithmic discrimination.' Independent evaluation and plain language reporting (algorithmic impact assessment) including disparity testing results and mitigation information shall be performed.' (p.  4) The bill establishes the Philippine Council on AI to conduct an evaluation on the impact of AI systems... (p. 6)

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and users of AI to conduct comprehensive Impact Assessments that identify and mitigate potential risks to individuals and society
thematicElements.justification: Sec 5 of HB 13 requires AI systems tools and technologies to be developed with consultation from diverse communities stakeholders and domain experts to identify concerns risks and potential impacts of the system; and  undergo pre-deployment testing risk identification and mitigation and ongoing monitoring that demonstrate they are safe and effective based on their intended use mitigation of unsafe outcomes including those beyond the intended use and adherence to domain-specific standards. The bill assigns obligation to AI systems designers developers and deployers to proactively and continuously take measures to protect individuals and communities from algorithmic discrimination and shall use and design systems equitably. (p. 4)

thematicElements.text: The establishment of rights for the public to access the findings of these assessments ensuring that they can hold organizations accountable for the impacts of their AI systems
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 5 provides for 'Independent evaluation and plain language reporting in the form of an algorithmic impact assessment including disparity testing results and mitigation information shall be performed and made public whenever possible to confirm these protections.' (p.  4) Sec. 5 (e) includes access to remedy through a fallback and escalation process if an automated system fails or produces an error. The right to appeal or contest AI's impacts on every person shall not be denied. (p. 5)

items.title: House Bill No. 9448 or the “Protection of Labor Against AI Automation Act”
items.justification: Sec. 5 (a) prohibits employers and recruitment entities from using AI as their sole or primary basis in the hiring and termination of employees. Human evaluation discretion and judgment shall always be a significant factor or part in the process. Any use of Al shall be directly supervised and complemented by human oversight. Sec. 5(b) prohibits the use of AI to replace human workers resulting in displacement loss of security of tenure diminution of existing salaries or benefits or unemployment' 'unless an equivalent alternative employment opportunity for affected human workers are available.” Sec. 6 allows the use of AI... in case of 'valid retrenchment' subject to Department of Labor approval.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The protection of workers from AI-driven discrimination in hiring promotion and termination decisions — including those who  lack an employment contract but are subject to algorithmic management systems
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 5 prohibits 'employers and recruitment entities... from using AI or automated systems as their sole or primary basis in the hiring and termination of employees. Human evaluation discretion and judgment shall always be a significant factor or part in the hiring and termination process. Any use of Al and automated systems during the said processes shall be directly supervised and complemented by human oversight.' (p. 4) This provision does not include AI-driven discrimination in promotion decisions.

thematicElements.text: Requirements for transparency in the management process including obligations to explain how AI systems are used to monitor performance make employment-related decisions and interact with or affect workers’ right to access workplace benefits
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 10 states that employers shall 'maintain transparency in the use of AI systems in employee evaluations provided that employees are informed prior to the evaluation that AI technology will be used in assessing their performance with the right to request for further detailed regarding the evaluation process.' (p. 6) There are no provisions that tackle how AI systems are used to 'interact with or affect workers’ right to access workplace benefits.'

thematicElements.text: The reinforcement of workers' rights to organise and collectively bargain in the context of AI-driven changes in the workplace including in sectors dominated by gig work

items.title: DBM-DICT-DEPDev Joint Resolution No. 2025-05 Prescribing the Implementing Rules and Guidelines on the Adoption of Standards-based Approach to Information System Strategic Plan Compliance (Philippines)
items.justification: Sec. 5 provides the Policy for Responsible and Acceptable Use of AI and Machine Learning (AIML) in Government which shall: (1) 'Establish clear guidelines and safeguards for the development training procurement deployment and evaluation of AIML systems in public sector operations; and (2) Uphold the principles of Fairness Ethics Accountability and Transparency (FEAT) throughout the AIML lifecycle' (p. 3) Annex E says the document 'provides a foundational framework for the responsible development procurement and management of Al systems and services by government agencies.' (p. 34)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)

thematicElements.text: The establishment of AI-specific procurement guidelines that go beyond traditional IT procurement to include ethical social and technical considerations
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 5 provides the Policy for Responsible and Acceptable Use of AI and Machine Learning (AIML) in Government which ensures that  government is guided by ethical principles and government agencies adhere to standardized policy framework for the responsible fair and secure use of AIML-enabled capabilities solutions and platforms. The framework shall: (1) 'establish clear guidelines and safeguards for the development training procurement deployment and evaluation of AIML systems in public sector operations; and (2) uphold principles of Fairness Ethics Accountability and Transparency (FEAT) throughout the AIML lifecycle.' (p. 3). However the framework does not go beyond traditional IT procurement practices.

thematicElements.text: The requirement for vendors to demonstrate that their AI systems have undergone thorough testing for bias fairness and safety
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 5 says the policy shall be '(b) designed to complement not replace human decisionmaking—especially in sensitive use cases such as eligibility determination public safety or fiscal forecasting; and (c) Subject to risk tiering explainability testing and bias mitigation strategies;' The policy also mandates all government agencies to 'adhere to a standardized policy framework for the responsible fair and secure use of AIML-enabled capabilities solutions and platforms.' (p. 3)

thematicElements.text: The assignment of a mandate to require transparency from vendors regarding the data and models used in their products to prevent 'black box' systems
thematicElements.justification: Annex E on Policy for Responsible and Acceptable Use of AI Sec. 3.4 states that 'third-party vendors and service providers offering Al solutions to government entities' are covered by the policy. (p. 34) Sec. 6.4 provides for the principles on Transparency and Explainability which require vendors to '6.4.1 disclose Al's role in decision-making; 6.4.2 provide mechanisms for human override; and 6.4.3 'ensure explainability through interpretable models and documentation.' (p. 37). The policy does not mention the prevention of 'black box' systems.

thematicElements.text: Procurement mechanisms that include elements or conditions for prioritising local AI developments as a strategy for enhancing AI sovereignty

items.title: Senate Bill No. 79 or the 'Artificial Intelligence (AI) Training for Government Workforce Act' (Philippines)
items.justification: Sec. 3 states that the bill aims to 'harness the potential of AI as a positive and innovative approach to help the government workforce in accomplishing tasks... (pp. 1-2) Sec. 5 provides for the establishment of an AI Training Program.” (p. 2) Sec. 7 outline the topics which include: (a) the science underlying AI; (b) introductory concepts on AI systems; (c) the ways in which AI can benefit the national government; (d) the risks posed by AI including discrimination and risks to privacy; (e) ways to mitigate the risks described in subparagraph (D) including efforts to create and identify AI that is reliable safe and trustworthy; and (f) future trends in AI including trends for national security and innovation.” (p. 3)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The establishment of a government-wide strategy for upskilling and reskilling public servants and members of the judiciary to build a foundational understanding of AI its applications and its risks
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 3 states that the bill aims 'to understand the rigors of AI machine learning and associated technologies;' and 'to reskill support and develop the workforce and prepare them for the future of technology.' (p. 2) As part of the topics for the training Section 5 establishes an AI Training Program for the government workforce while Sec. 7 includes discussing 'the risks posed by AI including discrimination and risks to privacy' as well as 'ways to mitigate the risks' potentially imposed by AI. However the initiative applies to employees of government agencies (Sec. 9) and does not explicitly mention members of the judiciary

thematicElements.text: The assignment of dedicated roles and teams within government to act as AI champions providing expert guidance and fostering a culture of responsible AI innovation
The requirement for ongoing professional development and training to keep pace with the rapid evolution of AI technology
thematicElements.justification: The document requires ongoing updates to the AI Training Program to ensure that public servants keep pace with developments in AI. Section 8 states that the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) must update the AI training program not less frequently than once every two years to incorporate new information relating to AI and ensure that the program remains relevant (Sec. 8).

items.title: House Bill No. 1699 or the 'National Digital Skills and AI Readiness Act' (Philippines)
items.justification: Sec. 3 states that the bill's objectives include to 'integrate digital skills and AI education across all levels of formal government' 'establish a future skills centers to provide free training and certification' and 'facilitate public-private partnerships in upskilling programs' (p. 3) Sec. 6 requires the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) to establish regional future skills centers to offer free training programs in digital coding digital marketing data science cloud computing and AI tools and government-subsidized certification programs. (p. 4)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The establishment of government-funded or subsidized reskilling and upskilling programs to help workers adapt to new job market demands created by AI
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 6 mandates the establishment of 'regional future skills centers in every region to offer free training programs in digital coding...data science... and AI tools as well as government-subsidized certification programs on global tech platforms...' (p. 4) The bill does not mention 'reskilling and upskilling programs' specifically or 'to help workers adapt to new job market demands created by AI.'

thematicElements.text: The provision of financial support or incentives for workers who participate in reskilling programs
Requirements for companies to invest in the training and development of their existing workforce to mitigate job displacement caused by automation

items.title: Draft Department of Information and Communications Technology and Civil Service Commission Joint Memorandum Circular Series of 2024 'Principles and Guidelines for an Ethical and Trustworthy Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) In the Government' (Philippines)
items.justification: Sec. 5 (b) on Cyber Safety and Security requires protection of AI systems from cybersecurity threats and risks that cause physical and digital harm. It requires all AI systems to undergo pre-deployment testing risk identification and mitigation and monitoring and evaluation to demonstrate the safety and effectiveness based on the intended use mitigation of unsafe outcomes and adherence to internationally established standards. (pp. 4-5)
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

thematicElements.text: The establishment of performance thresholds or quality benchmarks to ensure AI systems operate reliably and accurately under stated conditions
The implementation of safeguards fallback procedures or emergency protocols to mitigate harm in case of AI system failure or unexpected behavior
The requirement for pre-deployment testing validation or documentation to ensure technical robustness throughout the AI system lifecycle
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 5 (b) requires all AI systems to 'undergo pre-deployment testing risk identification and mitigation and monitoring and evaluation (M&E) to demonstrate the safety and effectiveness based on the intended use mitigation of unsafe outcomes and adherence to internationally established standards.' (pp. 4-5) Sec. 5 (f) says 'there needs to be a tool that validates the AI model that can be used by auditors.' (pp. 5-6)

thematicElements.text: The introduction of security obligations to protect AI systems against cyberattacks manipulation or adversarial interference
thematicElements.justification: Sec. 5 (j) mandates human-centricity and requires that AI 'not be used for malicious purposes or to sway or deceive users into making decisions that are not beneficial to them or society. With this AI developers and AI deployers should also ensure that dark patterns are avoided.' (p. 7). Dark patterns refers to the use of certain design techniques to manipulate users and trick them into making decisions that they would otherwise not have made. (p. 4)

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy Roadmap (NAISR) 2.0 (Philippines)
items.justification: The National AI Strategy Roadmap 2.0 (NAISR 2.0) promotes transparency as a key AI governance principle. It states that responsible AI deployment should include regulatory frameworks that promote “transparency and accountability” (p. 26). The roadmap also highlights stakeholder engagement including civil society advocating transparency and accountability (p. 28). Under the “AI Governance and Ethics” dimension transparency is listed among core principles for responsible AI (p. 30). Additionally the proposed National AI Governance Framework identifies “transparency of policies rules and regulations governing AI systems” as indispensable (p. 39).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Department of Trade and Industry

thematicElements.text: The promotion of clarity regarding how AI systems operate including their purpose data sources and decision-making logic to foster public trust
thematicElements.justification: The roadmap states that responsible AI deployment should include regulatory frameworks that promote “transparency and accountability” (p. 26). On Establishing a National AI Governance Framework the roadmap recommends that AI should be trustworthy so that people are willing to experience whether AI systems can be operated safely reliably and consistently even under difficult (if not unexpected) conditions. (p. 39). However the document does not specify concrete details for explaining AI system operations data sources or algorithmic decision-making.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to provide meaningful explanations of their systems' outputs especially in high-stakes contexts like hiring or loan applications
The establishment of rights for individuals to receive an explanation for a decision made by an AI system that affects them and to understand the key factors that led to that outcome

items.title: Policy for Artificial Intelligence Development in Poland from 2020
items.justification: It addresses AI literacy through a multi-tiered approach targeting the general public the formal education system the existing workforce and specialized professionals. Through mass media campaigns to promote awareness of AI's societal impact and combat misinformation regarding the risks and opportunities of automation (p.26 point 3a) a key short-term objective is to educate consumers (users) of AI systems so they can understand how these systems operate (p.26 point 3e) introducing basic AI tools in primary education for developing 'computational thinking' algorithmic skills and creative problem-solving (p.52 point 1c).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: Page 3 This AI Policy does not cover state activities in the area of ??national security and defense.

body.name: Council of Ministers and Committee for Digital Affairs

thematicElements.text: Curriculum reforms including at primary secondary tertiary levels
thematicElements.justification: In executive summary on page 6 when it talks about the AI and Education chapter it says that it addresses all levels of education as well as professional skills development of adults.

thematicElements.text: Establishment of educational institutions or programs offering AI-related courses within the formal education system
thematicElements.justification: It mandates introducing classes that raise awareness of applications the use of basic AI-based tools at early education schools (p.52 1a). Policy encourages universities to create special units for artificial intelligence and related disciplines (p.46 4b).There is a program for supporting the education of the second-level and top- level professionals in artificial intelligence machine learning and cybersecurity (p. 17 second row).

thematicElements.text: Provision of teacher training and resources for AI education
thematicElements.justification: Page 52 point 1.i - it talks about developing mechanisms that support developing educational staff competences

items.title: EU Digital Services Act
items.justification: Bots fake accounts and automated conduct are mechanisms of disinformation campaigns (recital 85) and as such rules are needed to combat them (recital 9). Systemic risk assessments apply to large-scale online platforms and search engines (art. 34) and explicitly include the dissemination or amplification of misleading or fraudulent content and the negative effects on gender-based violence. This includes recommendation systems and other relevant algorithmic systems (art. 34). Mitigation measures include testing and adapting algorithmic and recommendation systems; speeding up the processing of notifications of illegal hate speech and cyber violence; and labeling content generated or manipulated by AI (art.35).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Digital Services Coordinators

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI tools from being used to create amplify or disseminate misinformation and hate speech or to facilitate harassment and violence
thematicElements.justification: The act partially establishes preventative measures requiring platforms to mitigate systemic risks (amplification) arising from the dissemination of illegal content including hate speech harassment and content that poses risks to public safety (Art. 34). Regarding dissemination platforms must adapt their content moderation processes (illegal hate speech and cyberviolence) test their algorithmic systems and apply visible labels to generated or manipulated content (Art. 35). However there are no obligations for creators of AI tools with responsibility falling on intermediaries.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to platforms and AI developers to implement robust content moderation policies and to be transparent about how their systems handle harmful content
thematicElements.justification: Intermediary service providers must publish annual transparency reports including content moderation automated means objectives accuracy indicators and error rates (Art. 15). Users must be informed when a content restriction decision is moderated by AI (Art. 17). Platforms must explain the parameters of automated recommendation systems to users. Large platforms and search engines must adapt and test their algorithmic systems to mitigate systemic risks such as illegal hate speech or cyberviolence (Art. 35) and publish risk assessments independent reports and mitigation measures (Art. 42 44). However there are no obligations for developers of AI. The measures are platform-centric.

thematicElements.text: The establishment of rights for individuals and groups targeted by misinformation or tech-facilitated violence to receive protection and to seek redress against the perpetrators and the platforms that enabled the harm
thematicElements.justification: The Act establishes a set of rights for affected users: a free electronic complaint handling system (Art. 20) access to certified extrajudicial bodies including disputes over harmful content (Art.21) as well as judicial remedies; ease of notification of illegal content with the platform required to respond promptly; a statement of reasons with all information intended for affected users (Art.17); priority notification through a specialized knowledge entity (Art. 22). However there is no liability regime for the reparation of data from victims of disinformation or violence facilitated by AI. The provider must only inform about applicable means of redress for illegal products or services (Art. 32).

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the use of AI tools to facilitate gender-based harassment and violence
thematicElements.justification: Large platforms and search engines should conduct specific risk assessments (Recital 83) covering the actual or foreseeable negative effects related to gender-based violence (Art. 34). Relevant measures include accelerating the processing of cyberviolence complaints (Art. 35) including the non-consensual sharing of intimate or manipulated material (Recital 87). However there are no measures to prevent use as the general provisions on systemic risks cyberviolence and illegal content are reactive.

items.title: EU GDPR
items.justification: The law provides a layered redress framework that applies in AI contexts whenever personal data is processed. Data subjects harmed by automated processing based on AI-driven profiling and decision-making hold the right to express their point of view and the right to contest the decision (art. 22); presenting complaints to supervisory authorities (art. 77) resorting to legal measures against gaps in the authorities (art. 78) and bringing proceedings directly against controllers or processors (art. 79). Organizations may be mandated to exercise the rights collectively on behalf of data subjects (art. 80). Supervisory authorities may impose administrative fines because of the violations of core provisions (art. 83).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: This Regulation shall not apply to the processing of personal data by Member States in the context of carrying out activities relating to the Union's common foreign and security policy (recital 16). The processing of personal data by Member States does not apply to activities related to the protection and prevention of threats to public security (Art. 2).

body.name: The law establishes the European Data Protection Board is comprised of representatives from the supervisory authority of each member states (Arts 68) acting independently (Art 69) providing guidelines recommendations and binding decisions to ensure consistence across Member States (Art 70) The Member State must to establish am independent supervisory authority responsible for monitoring and enforcing the regulation (Art 51)

thematicElements.text: The establishment or reinforcement of judicial mechanisms that allow individuals or groups to seek remedy for harms caused by AI systems
thematicElements.justification: According to the law data subjects have the right to take legal action against data controllers or processors in the courts (EU members) of the controller's country or the court of their habitual residence (art. 79). The absence of supervisory authorities within three months is under the judicial remedy (art. 78) Controllers and processors responsible for damages related to processing may be required to pay compensation for material and non-material damages (art. 82).

thematicElements.text: The creation or use of state-based non-judicial complaint mechanisms (e.g. ombuds institutions regulators tribunals or consumer bodies) to handle AI-related grievances
thematicElements.justification: It is mandatory estabilish a independente supervisory authority to receive and investigate complaints in each member state from data subjects (art.51 57). The supervisory authorities must inform the progress and outcome of their complaint incluiding a judicial review (art. 77 78) and ordering controllers to comply with data subject rights imposing processing bans and sanctioning infringements (art. 58). Organizations can represent data subjects (art. 80). The European Data Protection Board coordinates the enforcement and dispute resolution mechanisms (art. 65 70).

thematicElements.text: Requirements or incentives for companies or developers to establish accessible grievance or complaints mechanisms for individuals harmed by AI systems
thematicElements.justification: The law partially supports the rights of data subjects. Controllers are obliged to facilitate the exercise of data subjects' rights in a transparent process responding to requests promptly and free of charge (Articles 12 13 14). Data Protection Officers must be accessible to data subjects particularly regarding the processing and exercise of their rights (Articles 37 and 38). Codes of conduct may include out-of-court procedures and dispute resolution between controllers and data subjects (Art. 40). However the law stops short of mandating company-level AI-specific complaint systems.

items.title: EU Digital Services Act
items.justification: Online platform service providers must ensure the privacy security and protection of minors in their services (Art. 28) including prohibiting advertising based on profiling through the automated processing of data about children (Art. 28). Terms and conditions must be understandable to minors (Art. 14) ensuring a high level of privacy and security by default based on good practices (recitals 70 71). Large-scale online platforms and large-scale search engines systematic risk assessment applies periodically evaluating potential negative effects on minors (Art. 34). Mitigation measures are determined: age verification parental control tools abuse reporting tools and support for minors (Art. 35). Voluntary standards apply (Art. 44).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Digital Services Coordinators

thematicElements.text: The protection of children's personal data and privacy when they interact with AI systems
thematicElements.justification: The act contains substantial provisions protecting the privacy and personal data of children in digital environments (Art. 28) including profiling by algorithmic systems and safeguards for data minimization (Art. 28 (23)). Systemic risk assessments and potential foreseeable negative risks to minors are mandatory for large-scale online platforms and large-scale search engines (Art. 34). However it does not impose specific measures for the protection of minors' data and the development of AI systems. There is a partial privacy-by-default recommendation for interface design (Recital 71).

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the use of AI to exploit manipulate or harm children including through targeted advertising or inappropriate content
thematicElements.justification: Advertising based on AI systems that exploit the attention and personal data of children to generate revenue based on profiles targeting known minors (Art. 28). Trust indicators or other mechanisms may be used in relation to content harmful to vulnerable users such as minors (recital 62). There is a direct prohibition on the design of manipulative AI-based interfaces applicable to all users (Art. 25). This is relevant for very large platforms and very large search engines that intentionally or unintentionally exploit minors (Recital 81). Periodic systematic risk assessment applies including potential negative effects on minors (Art. 34) including through the design of online interfaces that encourage addictive behaviors (recital 83).

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers of AI to design systems that are safe age-appropriate and beneficial for children
thematicElements.justification: Online platforms must guarantee a high level of privacy security and protection for minors (Art. 28). Whenever an intermediary service is primarily intended for minors or used by them the service must be explained understandably as well as the restrictions (Art. 14.). Large platforms and search engines have an obligation to periodically evaluate their algorithmic systems including verifying the risks for minors (Art.34) assessing the level of understanding of how the service works (Recital 81) taking into account the best child interests when adapting their service and interface (Recital 89) incluinding age verification tools parental controls and tools for reporting abuse (art.35). Thus there is no AI developers obligation.

items.title: Policy for Artificial Intelligence Development in Poland from 2020
items.justification: The Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland (2020) promotes AI projects tailored to Polish linguistic needs including machine processing of the Polish language and translation (p.39). It supports grants for Polish-language NLP and removing legal barriers to exploring Polish text corpora (p.39). The Policy also promotes open cultural data and digital repositories (p.27 p.32) and highlights AI’s role in access to cultural heritage (p.13). However it does not establish specific obligations regarding minority languages or multicultural representation.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: Page 2 This AI Policy does not cover state activities in the area of ??national security and defense.

body.name: Council of Ministers and Committee for Digital Affairs

thematicElements.text: The promotion of the development of AI systems that are representative of and responsive to a wide range of cultures and languages
thematicElements.justification: The Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland promotes AI projects tailored to Polish linguistic needs including machine processing of the Polish language and translation (p.39) and supports grants for Polish-language NLP and access to text corpora. It also highlights AI’s role in improving access to cultural heritage (p.13) and open cultural data (pp.27 32). However it does not address representation of multiple cultures or minority languages beyond the Polish context.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of the development of AI tools that perpetuate cultural stereotypes erase linguistic diversity or favor dominant cultures
The assignment of obligations to entities developing and using AI to ensure their systems are trained on diverse datasets and are adaptable to various cultural and linguistic contexts

items.title: EU AI Act
items.justification: The law focuses on the risk classification system (Art. 6) and the requirements imposed on high-risk AI systems. It requires suppliers of high-risk AI systems to establish implement document and maintain a risk (and damage) management system throughout the system's lifecycle (Art. 9). Training validation and test datasets must conform to data governance in terms of representation error-freeness completeness contextualization and the function the system will be used for handling special personal data for monitoring purposes and detecting and correcting biases. High-risk AI systems must have consistency throughout the lifecycle by requiring appropriate levels of accuracy and robustness and reducing the risk of bias (art.15).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: Art. 2(3) states that: 'does not apply to AI systems where and in so far they are placed on the market put into service or used with or without modification exclusively for military defence or national security purposes...' and 'does not apply to AI systems which are not placed on the market or put into service in the Union where the output is used in the Union exclusively for military defence or national security purposes...' Recital 24 explains that this exclusion is due to Art. 4(2) of TEU which notes that national security remains the sole responsibility of Member States but that if a defense or security system is used outside this scope then it temporary would fall within the regulation.

body.name: AI office coordinates EU implementation (art64) European AI Board composed of one representative per Member State aims to issue guidance support consistent application and coordinate national authorities (art65 66) the national competent authorities (art70) once each country must designate at least one market surveillance authority and a notifying authority The Advisory Forum (Art 67) provides technical expertise advising the commission and council The Scientific Panel of Independent Experts (Art 68) provides support with specialized scientific and technical knowledge However neither directly participates in implementation

thematicElements.text: The promotion of fair and equitable outcomes from AI systems ensuring they don't produce biased results that disproportionately affect certain groups
thematicElements.justification: Art. 9 and 10 require a risk-management process and relevant representative data with bias detection and mitigation; Art. 15 adds that systems must be accurate and robust limiting feedback loops where biased outputs skew future inputs. However. the Act focuses on controls and process not on guaranteeing specific outcomes.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI systems from perpetuating or amplifying existing societal biases and discrimination based on race ethnicity gender religion age or other protected characteristics
thematicElements.justification: The law establishes a list of prohibited AI applications including practices related to the vulnerabilities of specific groups of people who may be marginalized or systems that infer from sensitive attributes (Art. 5). It requires that datasets for high-risk AI be examined for potential biases that could lead to discriminatory results based on geographic/contextual characteristics (Art. 10). It requires that high-risk AI systems be accompanied by instructions for use that include information about known or foreseeable biases (Art. 13). And it limits high-risk AI systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market or in service when there are biased results that influence future operations (Art. 15).

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers to proactively identify measure and mitigate sources of bias throughout the AI lifecycle from data collection to deployment
thematicElements.justification: The law requires a risk management system throughout the entire lifecycle including non-discrimination through testing to verify compliance (Art. 9). It requires robust data governance including bias analysis in training validation and test datasets allowing for the identification and correction of such discrimination before data use (Art. 10). Suppliers must produce technical documentation before placing the system on the market including risk assessment performance metrics in population subgroups and bias mitigation measures (Art. 11). Implementers specifically in the public sector must conduct Impact Assessments addressing vulnerable groups or interference with the rights to equality and non-discrimination (Art. 27).

items.title: EU AI Act
items.justification: The Act addresses gender equality through non-discrimination and fundamental rights provisions. Training datasets for high-risk AI must be representative avoiding the discriminatory outcomes and protecting attributes explicitly related to gender (Art. 10). Deployers must conduct fundamental rights impact assessments before deploying high-risk AI including gender-based discrimination (Art. 27). Equality bodies are granted market surveillance powers enabling them to investigate and sanction AI systems producing discriminatory outcomes (Art. 74).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

defenceAndSecurity.justification: Art. 2(3) states that: 'does not apply to AI systems where and in so far they are placed on the market put into service or used with or without modification exclusively for military defence or national security purposes...' and 'does not apply to AI systems which are not placed on the market or put into service in the Union where the output is used in the Union exclusively for military defence or national security purposes...' Recital 24 explains that this exclusion is due to Art. 4(2) of TEU which notes that national security remains the sole responsibility of Member States but that if a defense or security system is used outside this scope then it temporary would fall within the regulation.
