items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024 - 2026 (Zambia)
items.justification: The Strategy defines AI Literacy (Page 5) as “understanding and competence in AI enabling citizens and professionals to effectively engage with and use AI technologies.” The Executive Summary (Page 11) states that “AI literacy campaigns will be launched to raise awareness and empower citizens to participate in the AI economy.” Further Section 6 (Page 34) calls to “address the digital divide by expanding connectivity and digital literacy programs.” Together these show Zambia’s plan to promote nationwide AI awareness skills and equitable access to AI education. Overall the aim is to ensure citizens are knowledgeable in using AI and can actively benefit from opportunities in the evolving digital economy. The vision and guiding principles include capacity building investing in education and training to develop AI literacy and skills among all segments of the population. (p. 29) and education reform integrating AI and digital literacy into educational curricula at all levels from primary schools to higher education. (P. 31) as well as plan integration of AI into educational curricula in the implementation plan (p. 45).
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: National AI Council

thematicElements.text: Curriculum reforms including at primary secondary tertiary levels
thematicElements.justification: The strategy explicitly addresses curriculum reforms across all education levels. The Executive Summary (Page 11) notes that Zambia aims to integrate AI into curricula at all levels and provide professional training. Section 5.2.8 (Page 31) specifies “Education Reform: Integrate AI and digital literacy into educational curricula at all levels from primary schools to higher education.” Section 6.2 (Page 35) also highlights Human Capital Development through curriculum enhancement. The Implementation Plan (Page 45) outlines concrete steps to plan and implement AI literacy programs with relevant ministries and educational institutions.

thematicElements.text: Establishment of educational institutions or programs offering AI-related courses within the formal education system
thematicElements.justification: The strategy includes steps toward establishing AI-related programs within the formal education system. The Implementation Plan Table (Page 45 row 3) states: Initiate Capacity Building Programs: Plan integration of AI into educational curricula and Design AI literacy campaigns with responsibilities placed on Ministry of Education and Educational Institutions. This shows planning and preparatory measures but it does not yet specify the creation of dedicated AI institutions or fully developed courses.

thematicElements.text: Provision of teacher training and resources for AI education

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024 - 2026 (Zambia)
items.justification: Page 29 of the Zambia National AI Strategy under the Ethical and Responsible AI theme explicitly lists Fairness and Non-discrimination as a core principle. It emphasizes that AI systems must be designed to prevent biases ensuring equitable treatment of all individuals regardless of race gender ethnicity or socio-economic status. The Strategy on page 13 further recommends that in Preventing Bias and Discrimination Implementing measures to identify and minimise biases in AI algorithms ensuring fairness and equity in AI-driven decisions should be taken
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: National AI Council

thematicElements.text: The promotion of fair and equitable outcomes from AI systems ensuring they don't produce biased results that disproportionately affect certain groups
thematicElements.justification: The Zambia National AI Strategy partially addresses fair and equitable outcomes from AI. Section 5.2.1 (Page 29) Ethical and Responsible AI highlights the need to mitigate bias ensure inclusivity and promote transparency emphasizing risks of discrimination and diverse datasets. However the strategy does not provide detailed operational measures enforcement mechanisms or guidance for protecting specific vulnerable groups so it only partially ensures that AI outcomes are fair and unbiased.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of AI systems from perpetuating or amplifying existing societal biases and discrimination based on race ethnicity gender religion age or other protected characteristics
thematicElements.justification: The strategy includes specific provisions to prevent AI from amplifying societal biases. On page 14 it commits to: “Implementing measures to identify and minimize biases in AI algorithms Ensuring fairness and equity” and promoting inclusivity for marginalized and vulnerable groups”. These provisions address discrimination based on protected characteristics even if not all are listed explicitly. However it does not provide detailed measures or safeguards specifically targeting protected characteristics like race gender or religion nor enforcement mechanisms to prevent such harms.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and deployers to proactively identify measure and mitigate sources of bias throughout the AI lifecycle from data collection to deployment

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024 - 2026 (Zambia)
items.justification: The AI Strategy (2024–2026) promotes human oversight through its emphasis on ethical inclusive and human-centric AI as noted on section 5.2.1 “Ethical and Responsible AI” as well as pages 18–20 highlight the need for transparency accountability and fairness to ensure human control and prevent harm. It calls for governance structures like the National AI Council to oversee AI deployment and maintain human decision-making in critical areas aligning with AU and UNESCO principles on human oversight as noted on page 13-14 section 2.2 Ethical Commitment and International Alignment. Additionally page 41 on numbering 4 states under Ethical Oversight Advocate for ethical considerations and the protection of human rights in AI deployment.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: National AI Council

thematicElements.text: The promotion of meaningful human control over AI systems ensuring that AI remains a tool to assist humans rather than replacing human judgment particularly in critical areas where AI-enabled decisions or actions can have broad and systemic implications
thematicElements.justification: The Zambia National AI Strategy (2024–2026) emphasizes ethical inclusive and human-centric AI promoting human oversight and accountability but without detailing explicit mechanisms for “meaningful human control.” Section 5.2 (“Ethical and Responsible AI”) and pages 18–20 highlight transparency fairness and accountability to ensure AI supports not replaces human decision-making. However the strategy lacks concrete requirements for human authorization or control in high-risk or critical sectors.

thematicElements.text: The prevention of full automation in sensitive sectors where human intervention and ethical judgment are necessary such as in law enforcement or medicine
The assignment of obligations to entities using AI to designate responsible individuals who can oversee intervene in and ultimately be accountable for the decisions made by the system

items.title: The Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 (Zambia)
items.justification: The Act addresses Impact Assessments as they relate to AI through rules on automated processing profiling new technologies and high-risk processing. Part VIII Section 46 requires a Data Protection Impact Assessment before processing when new technologies such as AI as they pose high risk. Section 46(2)(a) explicitly covers automated processing systems including profiling which produce legal or significant effects making these AI-related activities subject to mandatory Impact Assessments.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: Data Protection Commissioner

thematicElements.text: The promotion of a culture of proactive risk management by requiring that the potential societal ethical and environmental impacts of AI systems are evaluated before their deployment
thematicElements.justification: The Act promotes proactive risk management by requiring a Data Protection Impact Assessment before high-risk processing using new technologies including AI though AI is not explicitly mentioned in (Part VIII Section 46(1)–(2).It addresses privacy and individual rights risks and mandates mitigation measures but does not explicitly cover societal ethical or environmental impacts of AI systems. Thus only some aspects of proactive risk evaluation are included.

thematicElements.text: The assignment of obligations to developers and users of AI to conduct comprehensive Impact Assessments that identify and mitigate potential risks to individuals and society
thematicElements.justification: Section 46(1)–(2) states that data controllers a term broad enough to include AI developers and users to conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment before deploying high-risk processing including automated processing and profiling. This obligation ensures identification and mitigation of potential risks to individuals prior to deployment thereby fully assigning comprehensive impact-assessment duties to AI developers and users.

thematicElements.text: The establishment of rights for the public to access the findings of these assessments ensuring that they can hold organizations accountable for the impacts of their AI systems

items.title: National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2027 (Zambia)
items.justification: The strategy highlights the goal of training 5000 ICT professionals in new and emerging technologies including artificial intelligence (AI) robotics machine learning blockchain and big data (Page 31 Row 9 in the table). This initiative aims to address the skills gap and enhance workforce readiness for the digital economy. The focus on AI and related technologies underscores the government's commitment to upskilling and reskilling programs to equip professionals with the competencies needed to drive Zambia’s digital transformation.
items.scope: Horizontal approach (the framework applies across multiple sectors or applications and is not limited to a particular domain or  AI technology type).

body.name: The Ministry of Technology and Science

thematicElements.text: The establishment of government-funded or subsidized reskilling and upskilling programs to help workers adapt to new job market demands created by AI
thematicElements.justification: The document partially addresses government-funded reskilling and upskilling programs. On Page 31 Row 9 it mentions the goal of training 5000 ICT professionals in emerging technologies like AI machine learning and blockchain which implies a focus on workforce development. However it does not explicitly mention government-funded or subsidized programs specifically for AI-related reskilling across all sectors leaving the funding aspect less clear.

thematicElements.text: The provision of financial support or incentives for workers who participate in reskilling programs
Requirements for companies to invest in the training and development of their existing workforce to mitigate job displacement caused by automation

items.title: Manastirliu 650 schools will be equipped with intelligent laboratories to increase students digital skills
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Led by the Minister of Education and Sports Ogerta Manastirliu in cooperation with the National Agency for the Information Society this initiative advances AI literacy by expanding intelligent laboratories to 650 schools nationwide. The SmartLabs infrastructure enables students starting from the first grade to develop coding cybersecurity and broader digital competencies that form the foundation for AI-related skills. By embedding technology-based learning across primary and secondary education and coupling infrastructure investment with curriculum support in STEM and digital subjects the government institutionalizes early nationwide AI readiness and digital skill development.

items.title: Preparations for the new school year Manastirliu For the first time knowledge about AI is included in the curriculum
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: This initiative lead by the ministry of education addresses AI literacy by introducing basic knowledge about artificial intelligence within the formal pre-university curriculum at an early stage of education. It supports student awareness of what AI is and how it is used and framed within digital learning objectives.

items.title: Establishment of the Special Parliamentary Committee to Coordinate and Oversee All Institutional Actions to Combat Disinformation and Other Forms of Foreign Interference in Democratic ProcessesEstablishment of the Special Parliamentary Committee to Coordinate and Oversee All Institutional Actions to Combat Disinformation and Other Forms of Foreign Interference in Democratic Processes
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The initiative addresses AI-facilitated misinformation and violence by establishing a Special Parliamentary Committee with a mandate to coordinate and oversee institutional actions against disinformation and foreign interference in democratic processes. It explicitly targets content disseminated through bots algorithmic amplification and coordinated inauthentic behavior and calls for reviewing algorithms used to display prioritize distribute or remove content. The committee is tasked with proposing administrative or legislative measures to increase platform accountability and counter hate speech and manipulation while safeguarding freedom of expression (Section II page 1).

items.title: ON THE APPROVAL OF THE METHODOLOGY DOCUMENT AND TECHNICAL STANDARDS FOR THE USE OF AI IN THE REPUBLIC OF ALBANIA
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The standards emphasize under Principle 2.4 large-scale human capacity building to prepare for AI-driven labor market transformation. It highlights the need to equip AI practitioners with advanced technical skills while also training sector-specific professionals such as doctors to effectively use AI as an augmentative tool.

items.title: Government AI Campus
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Government of Albania through the Minister of State for Public Administration and Anti-Corruption and the National Agency for Information Society (AKSHI) is implementing AI skill development in the public sector. By launching the “Government AI Campus” in partnership with the Tony Blair Institute and Apolitical it provides structured AI training (Awareness Practitioner Leadership) for civil servants and managers. The initiative equips public employees with practical AI competencies for governance constituting concrete capacity-building action.

items.title: Commissioner for the Right to Information and Protection of Personal Data
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The Commissioner for the Right to Information and Protection of Personal Data oversees compliance with Law No. 124/2024 On the Protection of Personal Data including rules on automated decision-making. Under Art. 14–15 (pg 11–13) and Art. 22 (pg 18–19) controllers must provide meaningful information about the logic involved and enable human intervention. The Commissioner investigates complaints conducts inspections and orders corrective measures ensuring AI-driven decisions affecting individuals are explainable and reviewable.

body.name: Commissioner for the Right to Information and Protection of Personal Data

items.title: Decision No 01 dated 3004-2025 On Determination of Countries Which Ensure an Adequate Level of Personal Data Protection
items.justification: Decision No. 01 (30.04.2025) operationalizes cross-border data transfer rules under Law No. 124/2024 On the Protection of Personal Data. It defines adequacy criteria including the existence of independent supervisory authorities and guarantees of transparency in personal data processing. By listing countries considered adequate it clarifies lawful international data flows supporting accountability where AI systems rely on cross-border data transfers.

body.name: Commissioner for the Right to Information and Protection of Personal Data

items.title: Algerias participation in the International Youth Robotics and AI Competition
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: National-level executive authority (Ministry of National Education) leading and representing Algeria in an international competition. This initiative supports AI literacy by exposing school-age students to core AI-related concepts such as algorithms automation robotics programming and problem-solving through a government-endorsed educational activity. By formally supporting participation in an international robotics and AI competition the Ministry of National Education promotes early understanding and practical engagement with AI technologies helping students develop foundational knowledge and skills relevant to AI in an age-appropriate applied learning context even though it remains extracurricular rather than curriculum-wide.

items.title: Skills Center
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Skills Centers initiative addresses AI reskilling and upskilling by providing government-led free and structured training in artificial intelligence and related advanced digital technologies (such as cloud computing cybersecurity and robotics). By targeting youth and future workers the initiative directly builds AI-relevant technical skills needed for an evolving labour market and supports workforce adaptation to AI-driven digital transformation even in the absence of a binding national reskilling framework.

items.title: Secretary of State defends continued investment in digital literacy in schools
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: At the 2024 Technology and Education Forum (FTE) the Secretary of State for Secondary Education emphasized the need to continue investing in digital literacy in schools including the use of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. She highlighted government efforts to equip schools with technology and improve teacher training to expand access and quality of education. The statement links digital literacy and AI skills to preparing students for Angola’s technological development.

items.title: 1st National Forum on AI FNIA25
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The 1st National Forum on Artificial Intelligence – FNIA25 organized by the Business & Innovation Forum with the support of the Institute for Administrative Modernization (IMA) and featuring the participation of the Public Financial Information and Communication Technologies Service (SETIC-FP) addressed Human Oversight and Determination by emphasizing human supervision ethical data use and responsible AI governance. The panel on AI Governance and Ethics reinforced the importance of maintaining human control and accountability in AI-driven public sector innovation. Link:https://www.setic.minfin.gov.ao/noticias/noticia/setic-fp-no-fnia-2025-a-inteligencia-artificial-como-pilar-da-inovacao-no-sector-publico

items.title: 1st National Forum on AI FNIA25
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The 1st National Artificial Intelligence Forum – FNIA25 organized by the Business & Innovation Forum with support from the Instituto de Modernização Administrativa (IMA)(Link:https://web.archive.org/web/20251109213746/https://fnia.co.ao/#elementor-action%3Aaction%3Dpopup%3Aopen%26settings%3DeyJpZCI6IjQyNiIsInRvZ2dsZSI6ZmFsc2V9) serves as a key milestone to accelerate AI adoption in Angola. It contributes to Public and Private Sector Skills Development by engaging civil servants and different stakeholders in AI governance ethics innovation and applications enhancing competencies and fostering responsible AI integration in public administration.

items.title: The White Paper on Information and Communication Technologies (2023-2027)
items.type: Policy Development — Commissioning concept notes white papers or outlines that serve as inputs for drafting.
items.justification: The White Paper on Information and Communication Technologies (2023–2027) demonstrates Angola’s commitment to developing national capacity in AI. Although the National AI Strategy has not yet been created according to the White Paper the Executive through the ENIA aims to set a policy direction to prepare the workforce for AI by prioritizing future initiatives for upskilling and reskilling. These initiatives include plans to develop AI and data skills through a National Training Plan youth talent development STEM-aligned curriculum reform and teacher training to build early AI literacy (pp. 99–101).

items.title: Partnership between Angola and the UAE to modernize AI systems support AI research and upskill the workforce by training Angolan professionals
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The initiative strengthens AI skills and workforce capacity through international cooperation and research networks. The Memorandum of Understanding with the UAE includes developing algorithms for smart public services joint research projects training Angolan public-sector professionals in AI and participation in international knowledge networks and events. Engagements with Huawei and visits to AI research centres in China further support exposure to advanced AI systems and practical applications.

items.title: Government Digital Transformation Portal
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This joint programme reduces AI-facilitated misinformation and violence by strengthening people’s ability to critically assess digital content and understand AI.Government–UNESCO Youth Media & Information Literacy Engagements explicitly aim to equip young people and persons with disabilities with MIL skills to navigate the digital information ecosystem and verify information (Framework Background Digital Transformation portal).

items.title: Antigua and Barbuda UNESCOs AI Readiness Assessment Methodology Cultural Dimension Stakeholder Consultation
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The Ministry of ICTs Utilities and Energy led national consultations on AI ethics on culture as part of the AI Readiness Assessment Methodology(https://drive.google.com/file/d/1KQCbuQ8p2ciWq8dM1RA59VokirJGCTTa/view?usp=share_link). The final Report (p.22) highlights AI’s role in preserving traditional games cultural heritage and linguistic inclusion: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VR3bltyZ0BlIkv5ZoYCcq8DctuzmdRns/view?usp=share_link

items.title: AI training cycle Teacher training in times of AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Under the Argentine Program for Innovation in Education with AI (PaideIA) the Secretariat of Education (Ministry of Human Capital) conducted the webinar series 'Teacher training in times of AI'. This initiative reached over 2500 registrants through three synchronous virtual sessions led by specialists Mario Cwi and Paola Dellepiane. The program focused on reflecting upon AI's impact on teacher training and proposing strategies to rethink teaching through this new resource. More information:https://web.archive.org/web/20260311203615/https://red.infd.edu.ar/con-una-gran-participacion-finalizo-el-webinario-sobre-inteligencia-artificial-y-formacion-docente/

items.title: Our digital world Keys to taking control of our personal data and privacy in digital environments
items.justification: The guide is directed to children and adolescents it explains how automated data processing profiling and AI-driven decisions can affect adolescents’ privacy dignity and safety (pp. 36–45). It also reinforces children's rights (pp. 21–29)  and how to contest automated decisions (pp. 59)

items.title: AI and public policies
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National Institute of Public Administration (INAP) provides training for public officials to improve how artificial intelligence is used across government. Its course on AI and public policy helps participants understand ethical and fairness standards established in Disposición 2/2023. The initiative builds awareness about algorithmic bias inclusion and responsible data use promoting fair and transparent AI practices in public administration that align with national guidelines for trustworthy AI.

items.title: Training cycle in AI and Public Policy for members of the National Public Administration
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National Institute of Public Administration (INAP) provides government staff with structured training on artificial intelligence data governance and automated systems. Specifically training activities are promoted based on an articulating axis aimed at raising awareness and strengthening the capacities of public agents in ICT with special emphasis on Artificial Intelligence. The virtual course is available to public employees with responsibilities at some stage of the process of a substantive public policy in their jurisdiction with or without personnel in charge.

items.title: AWS Entrena Argentina Developing Argentine talent and driving the digital transformation of companies through knowledge and the cloud
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: A partnership between Amazon Web Service and The Ministry of Economy provides massive free online training in cloud technologies and artificial intelligence aiming to train over 100000 people by 2025. It builds workforce capacities to manage AI-enabled systems fosters talent development for emerging AI jobs and reduces vulnerability in labor markets undergoing digital transformation.

items.title: STEPai AI educational programs will be introduced in high schools
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The Ministry of Education Science Culture and Sports of Armenia approved the “STEP.ai – Artificial Intelligence” educational program for 10th grade. Developed since 2019 by Synopsys Armenia UEICT and AGBU Armenian Virtual College with input from international experts the three-year curriculum introduces AI fundamentals to high school students (grades 10–12). Offered in hybrid and online formats it promotes AI literacy logical thinking and problem-solving through project-based learning. Supported by leading tech companies the program links education with industry needs provides internships and mentorship and aims to foster a new generation of AI specialists to drive Armenia’s digital transformation.

items.title: Approval of Signing of the Council of Europe (CoE) Framework Convention on AI Human Rights Democracy and the Rule of Law
items.justification: The Convention's Article 14 contains specific provisions on remedies. Upon signing the Convention Armenia will assume the international obligations associated with the document including the specific remedies defined under Article 14. In any case the first formal step was taken: the Government has approved the signing of the Convention.

items.title: The Council of Europe held a discussion with Parliament of Armenia on application of AI in the field of healthcare
items.justification: The Council of Europe and the National Assembly of Armenia held a discussion on AI in healthcare addressing ethical and human rights implications. The event examined amendments needed in Armenia’s legal framework human rights challenges and European standards from the CDBIO report on AI’s impact on the patient-doctor relationship. Topics included patient autonomy health data equitable access and professional standards -underscoring the importance of human oversight.

items.title: Signing of the Council of Europe (CoE) Framework Convention on AI Human Rights Democracy and the Rule of Law
items.justification: The article 16 of the Convention enshrines specific provisions on impact assessment and Armenia’s signature reflects its expressed willingness to assume binding international obligations in this domain.

items.title: Factsheet for police Non-consensual sharing of sexual material
items.justification: This factsheet explains the offences introduced by the Criminal Code Amendment (Deepfake Sexual Material) Act 2024 and clarifies that the offence applies to sexual material created or altered using digital technology including AI-generated deepfakes (pp. 1-3). It guides police on identifying investigating and prosecuting cases where AI-generated or manipulated images are shared without consent. By clarifying that such synthetic material falls within the offence the factsheet supports law-enforcement responses to AI-facilitated image-based abuse and technology-enabled violence.

body.name: Australian Federal Police (AFP) Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions (CDPP) eSafety Commissioner (referenced in aggravated offence provisions via Online Safety Act civil penalty orders)

items.title: Review of AI and the Australian Consumer Law
items.justification: The Government Treasury’s discussion paper Review of AI and the Australian Consumer Law constitutes a governmental initiative addressing access to redress and remedies by clarifying how existing ACL protections apply to AI-enabled goods and services. It discusses the remedies available to consumers in this context (p. 2) confirms that the ACL’s technology-neutral framework remains applicable without requiring reform (p. 6) and explains that consumers may be entitled to compensation where a failure to meet a consumer guarantee causes loss or damage (p. 11) while also noting that AI systems may create additional challenges for accessing remedies (p. 12).

body.name: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission

items.title: eSafety Annual Report Program Monitoring Implementation of Online Safety Frameworks
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Australian Communications and Media Authority ACMA-eSafety Annual Report 2023-24 includes performance statements regulatory outcomes and data on compliance schemes under the Online Safety Act 2021 (which underpins the Online Safety (Basic Online Safety Expectations) Amendment Determination 2024). The report provides metrics and narrative about how online service providers address harms — including through algorithmic systems age-assurance (pp. 197-198). and moderation — thus supporting children’s rights to online safety and protection from AI-enabled risks (p. 216).

body.name: eSafety Commissioner (Australian eSafety Commissioner)

items.title: AustraliaUS Joint Council Safety by Design Workshop (Dec 2024)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: A two-day Safety by Design workshop co-led by the eSafety Commissioner and U.S. DHS gathered industry and global experts to develop a toolkit ensuring child safety is embedded throughout product development including in new and emerging AI technologies. The Joint Council will build on the outputs of this workshop and continue to work with industry to develop a Safety by Design toolkit to ensure that child safety is prioritized at every stage in the development of online products and services including in new and emerging artificial intelligence technologies. The toolkit is expected to collate best practices and share innovative approaches for companies to tackle online CSEA while also exploring the challenges and limitations of adopting.

body.name: eSafety Commissioner (Australian eSafety Commissioner)

items.title: Safe and responsible AI in Australia consultation - Australian Governments interim response
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Safe and responsible AI in Australia consultation – Australian Government’s interim response by the Australian Government Department of Industry Science and Resources (p.2) notes that part of the discussion were many submissions that emphasised the importance of embedding national and cyber security measures in AI development and deployment a number of submissions called for AI development to incorporate secure-by-design practices to ensure security is a core business goal from the start of development.(p. 15) and suggests introducing obligations for accountability (for example requiring training for developers and deployers and clearer obligations to make organisations accountable and liable for AI safety risks) (p. 4).

items.title: National AI Centre
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National Artificial Intelligence Centre (NAIC) promotes inclusive and responsible AI adoption across Australia by supporting SMEs industry and government to build trustworthy AI systems. Its mandate emphasises responsible AI diversity in AI capability development and engagement across sectors and communities. Through national programs partnerships and ecosystem-building activities NAIC helps ensure AI systems reflect Australian societal values and diverse user needs including underrepresented communities.

items.title: Responsible AI Network
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: A national research and policy network advancing AI ethics diversity and transparency. Produces reports practical frameworks and sector-specific guidance to operationalise recommendations 4–5 of the Committee’s report.

items.title: Senate Select Committee Report on Adopting AI (AI)
items.justification: The report by the Senate Committee examines the environmental impacts of AI systems and infrastructure noting that AI development and deployment can significantly increase energy consumption greenhouse gas emissions water use and pressure on land and resources (Chapter 6 pp.143-165). It highlights the environmental costs of AI model training and data centre operations and discusses approaches for capturing reducing and regulating these impacts (pp. 148 to 158). The committee recommends that the Australian Government take a coordinated holistic approach to managing the growth of AI infrastructure to ensure development is environmentally sustainable (Recommendation 13 p.165).

items.title: Voluntary AI Safety Standard v2 Consultations Expression of Interest
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: These consultations address gender equality because Version 2 (V2) of the VAISS builds on the ten guardrails established in the first version (V1). One of these guardrails emphasises engaging stakeholders and evaluating their needs and circumstances with a focus on safety diversity inclusion and fairness. Through the consultation process diverse stakeholders such as civil society organisations AI companies government agencies not-for-profits (NFPs) and academia can provide input on issues related to bias and discrimination to strengthen the guardrail in the next Version of the VAISS.

items.title: Pilot AI assurance framework
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Impact assessments
items.justification: In September 2024 the Digital Transformation Agency (DTA) launched a pilot of a draft AI impact assessment tool known as the Pilot Australian Government AI assurance framework. The tool helps agencies assess potential risks and impacts of AI systems including risks of bias and discrimination. One of the key principles applied in the assessment is fairness which requires AI systems to be inclusive and accessible and not result in unfair discrimination against individuals or groups. This includes impacts on individuals with diverse genders and other protected attributes (https://web.archive.org/web/20260124113511/https://www.digital.gov.au/policy/ai/pilot-ai-assurance-framework/step-4-fairness).

items.title: Voluntary AI Safety Standard v2 Consultations Expression of Interest
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: These consultations address gender equality because Version 2 (V2) of the VAISS builds on the ten guardrails established in the first version (V1). One of these guardrails emphasises engaging stakeholders and evaluating their needs and circumstances with a focus on safety diversity inclusion and fairness which includes gender considerations and gender-related discrimination due to biased datasets. Through the consultation process diverse stakeholders such as civil society organisations AI companies government agencies not-for-profits (NFPs) and academia can provide input on issues related to bias including gender-related discrimination.

items.title: Voluntary AI Safety Standard v2 Consultations Expression of Interest
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The VAISS Version 2 (V2) consultation process supports human oversight and determination by inviting stakeholders to help refine guardrails ensuring human accountability governance and intervention mechanisms in AI systems. The consultation seeks feedback on strengthening requirements for organisations to oversee AI deployment manage risks and maintain human responsibility across the AI lifecycle. These discussions build on the existing VAISS guardrails particularly those requiring human control monitoring and accountability for AI outcomes ensuring AI systems remain tools that support human decision making rather than operating autonomously without oversight.

items.title: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) Independent Oversight of AI-related Privacy Compliance
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner OAIC as Australia’s independent privacy regulator oversees organisations’ use of commercially available AI systems and ensures compliance with privacy obligations. They published additional guidance for the public on how to assess AI's impact on privacy providing tools and steps to conduct Privacy impact assessments on their website.

items.title: Consultation on Mandatory Guardrails for High-Risk AI Systems
items.type: Policy Development — Launching consultations or stakeholder workshops to gather input for a future draft.
items.justification: The Australian Government launched a public consultation on mandatory guardrails for high-risk AI systems through the Safe and Responsible AI in Australia – Proposals Paper (2024). The consultation sought stakeholder input to inform future AI regulation. The document identifies AI in employment and workplace settings as a potential high-risk use case noting that AI used in recruitment hiring promotion pay transfers and termination decisions may significantly affect individuals’ opportunities and may produce discriminatory impacts. See discussion of employment and workplace settings (pp. 26-27) within the section on high-risk AI contexts.

items.title: Our Gen AI Transition
items.justification: The Jobs and Skills (under the Australian Government) Generative AI Capacity Study (2025) examines the potential impacts of generative AI on the Australian labour market including workforce transformation job augmentation and emerging skill demands. The report assesses how AI may change work tasks across industries and occupations and identifies implications for workforce planning and labour policy. It provides evidence to inform policy responses addressing workforce transitions and labour protections related to AI-driven changes in employment. See discussion on labour market impacts workforce transitions and occupational exposure to AI (pp. 7–15 23–30).

items.title: AI in Government Fundamentals (APS Academy)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The APS Academy’s AI in Government Fundamentals course provides APS staff with foundational skills in AI including responsible use risk awareness and human oversight. Updated in June 2025 it trains public servants on applying AI in their work directly supporting the Policy for the Responsible Use of AI in Government. The Australian Institute of Criminology mandated completion for all staff demonstrating agency-level implementation.

body.name: Digital Transformation Agency (DTA) and the Australian Public Service Academy (APS Academy)

items.title: National Skills Agreement Operational Programs
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The NSA implements several nationwide operational programs that expand reskilling and upskilling capacity in areas affected by technological change including AI. It establishes TAFE Centres of Excellence to build skills for high-technology and emerging industries (A112–A116) ensures access to digital literacy and foundation skills training (A108) and strengthens VET workforce capability (A124–A129). These programs support Australia’s transition by preparing workers with the digital and technology competencies required in an AI-enabled economy.

body.name: Skills and Workforce Ministerial Council (SWMC) which oversees stewardship national priorities reviews and decision-making (A37A39)Jobs and Skills Australia (JSA) providing labour market and skills analysis to drive implementation (A22 A41(d))National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) as data custodian supporting monitoring (A22 A134)All are operational and continue their roles under the Agreement

items.title: National Skills Agreement Operational Programs
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The NSA establishes a national M&E system to track skills outcomes essential for adapting to technological change including AI. It mandates ongoing monitoring of VET and labour-market performance (A22–A26) annual public reporting (A151–A154) and an independent review of the stewardship model (A37–A39). These mechanisms help governments assess whether training systems—including digital and technology capability initiatives—are effectively supporting reskilling and upskilling needs in an AI-driven economy.

items.title: Voluntary AI Safety Standard v2 Consultations Expression of Interest
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The VAISS Version 2 (V2) consultation process addresses AI safety and security by seeking stakeholder input to refine and strengthen the existing guardrails that manage AI risks across the system lifecycle. The consultation aims to improve practices for identifying and mitigating AI-related harms including stronger guidance for developers and deployers on secure design risk management and monitoring of AI systems. It also explores enhancements such as improved content provenance labelling or watermarking and clearer technical practices to reduce misuse and manipulation of AI systems. These updates aim to strengthen safeguards and reliability in AI deployment.

items.title: Fight Fakes
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: Fight Fakes addresses AI-facilitated misinformation and violence by educating young people to recognize AI-generated fake content such as deepfakes manipulated images or videos and fabricated news. It is designed for use in schools. The initiative enhances media literacy and critical thinking skills enabling students to resist harmful misleading or extremist narratives that can incite violence. FightFakes is implemented within Austria’s Safer Internet framework which is supported and funded by the federal government linking online safety education directly to public policy goals on digital resilience and youth protection.

It focuses on supporting learners from diverse linguistic backgrounds improving language learning across multiple languages and building teachers’ capacity to use AI in inclusive culturally sensitive ways within formal education settings.

items.title: Enlightenment 40 Human understanding of AI decision-making

The report examines the legal and practical challenges of explaining AI's impacts on individuals (pg. 7) and stresses the need to rethink explanation duties in light of increased AI-driven decision-making to protect affected individuals (pg. 11). It can also be accessed through https://web.archive.org/save/https://researchinstitute.at/en/enlightenment-4-0-project-results-published-in-english/

The program aims to train individuals and groups enabling them to use information and communication technology in teaching learning and supporting educational processes. One of the program’s main goals is the use of artificial intelligence in education; however it does not explicitly use the term “AI literacy” in its mandate.

items.title: Workshop on AI tools for professional success

items.justification: The Information and eGovernment Authority (iGA) organised a workshop titled 'AI Tools for Your Professional Success' delivered by the Innovation and Advanced Technologies Directorate team at the Bahrain Institute of Banking and Finance (BIBF) with the participation of employees from various iGA sectors and departments. This workshop fits within the scope of this indicator as it is directed towards developing AI skills for Public sector employees.

items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative is implemented by Tamkeen (Labour Fund) which is a quasi-governmental body established by the Government of Bahrain to support national workforce development and private sector competitiveness. In 2025 Tamkeen launched a national AI training initiative to train 50000 Bahrainis in AI skills by 2030. The program features three tracks: executives/leaders generalists and technical specialists. It aligns with Tamkeen's vision to enhance Bahraini competitiveness in the private sector and equip nationals with in-demand skills. Tamkeen has partnered with leading local and international training providers for this program.

items.justification: In the AI Readiness Assessment Report on page 28 the education sector’s AI integration is analyzed highlighting its early potential and room for growth. By page 32 the report dives deeper into AI literacy pinpointing gaps and readiness levels. This comprehensive analysis provides the government with a solid foundation to shape effective AI initiatives and ensure holistic progress.

items.title: Barbados AI Fraud Detection Hackathon
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The partnership between GovTech Barbados (Government agency) and Zindi is providing opportunities for the development of AI literacy among citizens. The first program took place on April 26 2025 which was a Hackathon in association with the University of the West Indies which provided youth with an opportunity to create solutions for Fraud detection whilst learning adequate skills AI literacy. These skills learnt will aid in the transition from consumers of AI to producers of AI led technologies and businesses

items.title: Govt moves to counter viral AI video launches channels to report fake news
items.justification: This initiative was created in response to deepfake videos circulating of Prime Minister Motley. In order to clamp down on these unscrupulous activities the government has created an email line that persons can report perpetrators of this deceptive act mentioned in paragraph 4. No data has been published confirming the effectiveness of this initiative. The Minister also mentioned use of social media to allow citizens to report the misuse of AI for misinformation purposes.

items.title: The Future of AI Policy Lessons for Barbados
items.type: Policy Development — Launching consultations or stakeholder workshops to gather input for a future draft.
items.justification: This lecture was facilitated by the Central Bank of Barbados Dr Videgaray a AI policy expert provided critiques of the current Public Procurement process. He also provided mechanisms that Barbados can improve their current system by for example augmenting AI knowledge and understanding in governance as well as making the necessary preparations against the varying cyber risks.

items.title: Youth Thrive Through National Transformation Initative-AI Programme
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Youth Thrive Through National Transformation Initiative-AI Programme is government led in collaboration with the Barbados Accreditation Council (BAC). The aim of the programme as underscored by BAC and National Transformation Initiative  Directors is to fill the gap for the growing demand 'for flexible high-quality training that responds to the evolving needs of the Barbadian workforce.'. In addition the programme demonstrates the importance of lifelong education the development of the workforce whilst building the competency of Barbadians for an increasingly skills-focused global economy.

items.title: INSTRUCTIONAL AND METHODOLOGICAL LETTER OF THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION OF THE REPUBLIC OF BELARUS On the activities of educational institutions implementing educational programs of general secondary education structural divisions of regional (Minsk city) executive committees city district executive committees local administrations of districts in cities exercising state powers in the field of education in the 2025/2026 academic year
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The document is an instructional and methodological letter of the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Belarus that provides guidance for organizing general secondary education in the 2025/2026 academic year. It translates legislative and regulatory requirements into practical instructions for schools covering curriculum delivery assessment safety digitalization and institutional responsibilities. The letter addresses AI literacy by referencing the AI Recommendations and outlining their key provisions explaining how AI can be used to improve the educational process and highlighting opportunities and risks of AI use in schools.Reference: Section 5. “Use of artificial intelligence in organizing the educational process” p. 6

items.title: AI & education principles of application
items.justification: The Wallonia-Brussels Federation’s “Artificial Intelligence & Teaching: Principles of Application” (August 2024) establishes a system-wide principle for the responsible use of AI across compulsory adult and higher education. It promotes understanding of AI systems awareness of risks and limitations transparency in AI-assisted work human oversight and ethical reflection (pp. 3–4; General Principles section). The framework guides institutions in integrating informed and responsible AI use into pedagogical practice.

items.title: Designation of the Belgian Institute for Postal Services and Telecommunications (BIPT) as the Digital Services Coordinator (DSC)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The BIPT's designation as the Independent Oversight Body (DSC) via the Act of April 21 2024 is the crucial implementation step for enforcing the DSA in Belgium. The DSA requires Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) to implement effective measures to mitigate systemic risks to public security and democratic processes (Art. 34) which covers algorithmic amplification of misinformation and violence. The DSC's role is to monitor investigate and sanction platforms for non-compliance with these risk mitigation duties thereby directly providing the necessary enforcement mechanism to counter AI-facilitated harms at the national level

items.title: BIPTs Operationalization of the Trusted Flaggers and Out-of-Court Dispute Settlement (ODS) Certification Mechanism
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The BIPT's operationalization of the certification mechanisms (starting in April/May 2024) is a core Multistakeholder Consultation and Capacity Building effort (Source 1.2). The DSA requires the DSC (BIPT) to certify 'Trusted Flaggers' (Art. 22) and Out-of-court Dispute Settlement (ODS) bodies (Art. 21) (Source 1.1). Trusted Flaggers are CSOs/NGOs with expertise in illegal content (like hate speech incitement to violence) whose reports must be prioritized by platforms (Source 1.7). This action directly integrates non-state expertise into the framework enabling faster more accurate identification and removal of AI-facilitated misinformation and violence and providing victims with a non-judicial redress mechanism (ODS).

items.title: VITOs use case - Living Environment
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: This is continuous Knowledge Generation through publicly-funded research. Projects within the FAIR consortium (like those at VITO) are actively working on developing 'AI Surrogate Models' which are machine learning models trained on the outputs of complex simulations (Source 1.3). These surrogates enable accurate predictions for environmental models (e.g. air quality) while significantly reducing computational cost. By accelerating scenario analysis and operational deployment while simultaneously reducing energy consumption and compute power needed this research directly generates the technical knowledge necessary to achieve the framework's goal of developing frugal and energy-efficient AI.

The four-module online training directly focused on: combating algorithm discrimination and providing 'illustrations in several areas'  By equipping public servants and regulators with the knowledge to identify and respond to discrimination risks in AI systems this training directly implements the national framework's commitment

items.justification: The 'As-is and gap analysis' report published in March 2025 provides critical information on the challenges and gaps in Belgium's current legal and institutional framework regarding AI Fairness and Non-discrimination in public administration  The report's findings directly inform and prepare government entities and Unia itself on how to better detect prevent and respond to algorithmic discrimination through strengthened legal advice policy recommendations and procedural guidance for the impending EU AI Act implementation

For example human oversight will be exercised over the results of a high-risk AI system that influences all actions and decisions every hour.

items.title: Guidelines of the Belgian Data Protection Authority on AI Systems and the GDPR
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The brochure describes the complex interaction between the General Data Protection Regulation and the Artificial Intelligence Act in the context of AI systems development. It uses 'use cases' to explain the applicability of the two frameworks. Data Protection Impact Assessments are required in some cases: they are mandatory in the processing of high-risk data or in the implementation of new technologies (p. 14); the AI Act requires a Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (p. 14-15). For high-risk systems a more thorough risk assessment is required in some cases. This analysis examines the specific risks and identifies the potential harms associated with the AI system. This obligation complements the GDPR.

body.name: Belgian Institute for Postal Services and Telecommunications

items.title: Open Market Consultation for the future Public Procurement of Innovative solutions to establish a centralised AI marketplace
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Federal Framework for AI Procurement led by FOD Beleid enOndersteuning of Belgium is an innovative initiative that aims to establish a centralized AI marketplace to simplify access to AI tools and services for federal organizations. Addressing the challenges of procurement fragmentation and limited access to suppliers this project seeks to unify and simplify AI adoption in critical federal sectors such as e-government mobility and healthcare. The marketplace will operate under a Federal Framework Agreement and a'broker-managed' model ensuring access to pre-selected AI solutions secure infrastructure customized training and regulatory compliance support. (Scope and main objectives pp. 5-6).

It speaks to ensuring that emerging technologies are used in an ethical manner to enhance rather than undermine the integrity and fairness of judicial proceedings.

items.title: Labour Inspection in the Age of AI

items.justification: The Ministry of Labour’s training “Labour Inspection in the Era of Artificial Intelligence” (Cotonou 21–25 July 2025) built capacity for labour inspectors occupational doctors and social partners to understand how AI is changing workplaces and to adapt inspection practices accordingly. It covered “artificial intelligence labour inspection and the future of work” helping enforcement actors identify and respond to AI-linked labour risks (e.g. workplace monitoring performance management and other AI-enabled employment practices) under existing labour rules.

items.title: Labour Inspection in the Age of AI

items.justification: The training on “Labor Inspection in the Age of Artificial Intelligence” constitutes public sector skill development insofar as it directly strengthens the institutional capacity of Benin’s labor administration to address AI-related transformations in the world of work. The initiative is led by the African Regional Labour Administration Center (CRADAT) in cooperation with the Ministry of Labor and Civil Service (MTFP) of Benin and is explicitly directed at public officials including Labor Inspectors and occupational physicians. By equipping these actors with knowledge on regulatory implications of AI risks of automated decision-making workplace surveillance and the integration of AI into inspection practices.

As a government-backed (Ministry of Digital Affairs and Digitalization) public event it supports the Strategy’s goal of strengthening human capabilities by creating structured opportunities for learning networking and skills development around AI and digital entrepreneurship (training-style capacity building) even though it is not a formal qualification programme.

items.title: The GovTech Action Plan- 13th FYP Goals Targets and strategies
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects

These activities aim to sensitize various stakeholders (parents educators policymakers and industry) on COP guidelines to equip them with knowledge about online threats and strategies to safeguard children.

items.title: Dzongkha Natural Language Processing (NLP) Project
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Dzongkha NLP project is an ongoing programmatic initiative led by the Department of Culture and Dzongkha Development (DCDD) and the GovTech Agency. It utilizes AI to develop Natural Language Processing tools for Bhutan's national language. The project includes AI-driven machine translation Automatic Speech Recognition and Text-to-Speech systems for Dzongkha. As mandated in the GovTech Digital Strategy 2024 (e.g. under digital service accessibility) this initiative ensures public systems and digital services are available in the local language directly leveraging AI to preserve Bhutanese linguistic heritage prevent digital language exclusion and promote cultural diversity in the technology ecosystem.

items.title: Women Digital Champions Training

items.justification: The program directly addresses gaps identified in Bhutan's 2024 AI Readiness Assessment regarding limited women's participation in AI planning and decision-making. Training content includes: AI benefits and risks from gender perspectives; technology-facilitated gender-based violence; barriers to gender-inclusive digital policies; strategies for equitable digital access; AI applications to combat online gender-based violence; and women's leadership in digital innovation. The initiative builds capacity among 30 government officials to integrate gender considerations into AI policy development and implementation ensuring women's meaningful participation in Bhutan's digital transformation and AI governance.

These were the three main conclusions of the meeting. The working group established guidelines reached after two days of deliberations among 31 delegations.
