items.justification: Free course provided by the Institute of the Federal University of Rio Grande do Norte in partnership with the Ministry of Education through the Coordination for the Improvement of Higher Education Personnel aims at Artificial Intelligence for Basic Education Educators: Digital Skills and Pedagogical Innovation. The training is aimed at teachers and undergraduate students from across the country aiming to promote education for the responsible ethical and creative use of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom. The course will cover five topics: introduction to artificial intelligence; identification and recognition of educational problems; fluency in educational data; educational problem-solving; and AI tools in education.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Ministry of Education holds a seminar on AI in basic education
items.justification: The Brazilian Ministry of Education event aims to foster dialogue between various leading institutions and academics on pedagogical practices and school management processes related to the use of AI; opportunities and challenges for the use of digital educational resources; and most importantly the paths for the ethical critical and pedagogical integration of AI in Brazilian basic education.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Public hearing on social media regulation and regular meeting
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The Social Communication Council of the National Congress held a debate on social media regulation addressing challenges related to disinformation hate speech and privacy. The goal is to gather contributions from society to balance freedom of expression and digital security. The debate supports Bill 2630/20 approved by the Senate and currently under discussion in the Chamber of Deputies which bans fake accounts and the use of bots as well as combating the spread of fake news and attacks on democracy. Due to ongoing discussions on the bill the Social Communication Council of the National Congress is still participating in the discussions.

items.title: Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship launches study on AI democracy and tackling LGBTQIA+ political violence
items.justification: The study presents diagnoses analyses and recommendations for addressing LGBTQIAphobic political violence in digital environments and promoting responsible and inclusive use of artificial intelligence reaffirming the federal government's commitment to promoting human rights and combating this type of violence. The publication brings together a set of recommendations aimed at the government technology companies and civil society. The study is available at https://web.archive.org/save/https://www.votelgbt.org/inteligencia

items.title: Hackathon Digital Rights AI Platform Regulation and Information Integrity
items.justification: The Hackathon is organized by the Coordination of Treatment Analysis and Dissemination of Scientific Information (and the Coordination of Information Technologies of the Brazilian Institute of Information in Science and Technology. It aims to propose creative and innovative solutions based on a collaborative interdisciplinary and open perspective on the following topics: Digital government and the digital transformation of the State; Ensuring privacy on digital platforms; Regulation of digital platforms; and Information integrity and the use of AI. Students will be able to develop proposals (online and in person) with experts to combat misinformation via platforms especially in the use of AI.

items.title: The Federal Government structures ANPD to assume the responsibilities of ECA Digital
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: Designation of the National Data Protection Agency as the autonomous administrative authority for the protection of children and adolescents in digital environments and establishing jurisdiction to receive court blocking orders. The court orders refer to the use of profiling techniques (based on AI) virtual augmented or extended reality for the exploitation of children and adolescents and monetization. The orders also include the possibility of disabling systems that use AI from providers of products and services in digital environments whose systems have been evaluated and found to pose a security risk or are not suitable for children and adolescents.

body.name: National Data Protection Authority

items.title: Absolute Priority Dialogues for Safe Children and Adolescents in the Digital Environment
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: A seminar hosted by the Federal Supreme Court on the protection of children and adolescents in the digital environment was held on the same day as the enactment of the Law on the Statute of Children and Adolescents in the Digital Environment which establishes protective clauses for AI-based systems and AI-based profiling for monetization. During the event the court launched the Desinfoteca—an online collection of research on digital phenomena such as disinformation and their impact on fundamental rights. The format sought to stimulate reflection on existing best practices regulatory gaps and paths for future normative innovations fostering a space for listening and inter-institutional dialogue.

body.name: National Data Protection Authority

items.title: Technical cooperation for the development of AI SoberanA - a language an LLM in Portuguese
items.justification: Agreements signed between the Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation the Government of the State of Piauí and the National Laboratory for Scientific Computing aim to promote institutional technical scientific and operational exchange and cooperation including initiatives associated with the development of generative artificial intelligence models that emphasize the use of Portuguese and the building of capabilities that promote national sovereignty.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation (include the Interministerial Committee for Digital Transformation)

items.title: The Ministry of Development Industry Commerce and Services has opened a consultation to define the list of data center equipment eligible for Redata
items.justification: This is a binding and mandatory regulatory act but it must be approved later to become a definitive law. It creates the Special Taxation Regime for Datacenter Services in Brazil Redata (art.1 pg.1 chapter I p.3-7). The act is part of the National Data center Policy (p.8). The following conditions are established (art. 11.B) for organizations that establish (or expand) data centers in the country: make available to the domestic market a percentage of processing capacity storage and data handling prohibiting its allocation for export or own use in the absence of domestic demand; meet sustainability criteria and indicators: water energy etc.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Debate on the use of AI from a gender perspective
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The National Secretary of Digital Rights representing the Ministry of Public Security and Justice participated in the Inclusive Feminist Foreign Policy Observatory such as multistakeholder consultations to explain that artificial intelligence presents technological patterns that involve political choices that can reproduce historical inequalities. The secretary highlighted the importance of a gender-sensitive approach to AI which requires conscious decisions to avoid bias and discriminatory content ensuring that technology promotes inclusion and non-violence.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Digital Future Scholarship
items.justification: A program launched by the Ministry of Science Technology and Education that supports the coordination of the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Strategy launched the scholarship program with 50% of the program's vacancies going to women as part of the commitment to inclusion and gender equality (p.3).

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Generative AI in Public Service - Definitions Uses and Best Practices
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The federal government has released a guide with recommendations and best practices for Generative Artificial Intelligence in the Public Service. The guide includes an approach to high-risk AI use and the need for human oversight (p.6). Fundamental Principles for the Use of Generative AI (p.11) were defined Risk with identification of specific vulnerabilities and implementation of mitigation measures (p.12-16) which include explainability and human supervision for high risks (p.18) risk classification (p.12-22) recommendations and practices (22-30).

items.title: The Brazilian Institute of Information in Science and Technology participates in a public hearing on the impacts of AI on the job market
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The main objective of the hearing was to analyze the transformations that the adoption of AI has brought to professional routines including the automation of tasks the reconfiguration of professions and the emergence of new roles. The event brought together representatives from public institutions unions employers' associations and academic experts. The institute believes it is necessary to rethink investment in Science and Technology adopting a stance that promotes the use of the National Fund for Scientific and Technological Development (FNDCT) to support research units and the S&T system.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Ministry discusses research on the effects of AI on the world of work
items.justification: The Minister of Labor and Employment discusses research projects analyzing the impacts of artificial intelligence on the world of work developed in several countries including Brazil with a representative of the International Observatory on Artificial Intelligence and members of the Working Group on Artificial Intelligence. The ministry's initiative aims to gather contributions to enrich the working group's discussion agenda. Research indicates that 'AI shop floor' workers face regulatory and quantitative invisibility as they are not adequately included in labor and care policies despite their high qualifications often including master's and doctoral degrees.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: A Primer on Generative AI in the Public Sector
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The Generative AI Handbook for Public Service aims to support public servants in understanding and responsibly using AI tools with practical guidance for the ethical and effective use of these tools in the Brazilian public sector. It utilizes the risk classification system from the AI regulation bill. Publicity is a fundamental principle (p. 11). The proposal is that it be continuously updated to reflect changes in regulations and technological advancements.

items.title: InovaCPIN - an online platform for public procurement for innovation
items.justification: InovaCPIN - an online platform for public procurement for innovation and is being enhanced by five government agencies with models templates and other materials that support and facilitate the procurement of innovative solutions that use AI (https://inovacpin.org/). There are multiple items on AI procurement such as terms opinions guides studies and bidding documents in the library (https://inovacpin.org/biblioteca?search=inteligencia+artificial&_embed). In total there are 9 resources and we used the date of the first one in July 2020.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: AI at Inmetro how to apply it in everyday life
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National Institute of Metrology Quality and Technology (Inmetro) held the event with the goal of presenting the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) in a practical and inspiring way to all the institution's employees. Participants attended presentations on AI trends in the public sector and practical applications of the technology in Inmetro's internal routines and those of other institutions. The event reinforces Inmetro's commitment to promoting the exchange of experiences and encouraging the conscious use of artificial intelligence in the public sector.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Labor Observatory Network - AI in Brazil Regulation and the Labor Market
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The lecture 'Artificial Intelligence in Brazil: Regulation and the Labor Market' is part of the program for the 21st Meeting of the Labor Observatory Network (formed by local centers that produce studies and analyses on the labor market). The lecture addressed the regulatory challenges of artificial intelligence in the country as well as its impacts on the labor market and public employment policies.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Escola do Trabalhador 40 launches new free courses in AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Escola do Trabalhador 4.0 has launched new free online courses in Artificial Intelligence such as - the AI learning path for NGOs and the Fluency for Students Fluency for Educators and Employability with Microsoft Copilot courses. The platform now offers 97 courses across 23 learning paths all aligned with current job market demands and trends.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Ministry of Labor and Employment establishes Working Group on AI
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The Working Group on Artificial Intelligence is responsible for conducting studies and research on the impact of AI on both the labor market and public services with a focus on identifying trends and future prospects. The group will also focus on identifying opportunities for the development of AI-based products and services that promote social inclusion and create new jobs.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: Regulatory Sandbox for AI and Data Protection
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The Regulatory Sandbox of the National Data Protection Authority constitutes a controlled testing environment that allows public and private entities to develop and test technological innovations based on artificial intelligence systems that involve the processing of personal data under structured regulatory supervision. The program is currently in its second edition.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: ANPD advocates for transparent legislation for good AI governance
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Director of the National Data Protection Authority (now transformed into an agency) he participated in the 1st Information Security Governance and Data Privacy Congress. In his lecture on 'AI Regulation in Brazil from a Governance Perspective' he addressed the principles and objectives of AI regulation which include the security transparency and explainability of systems as well as the protection of fundamental rights and algorithmic non-discrimination.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation

items.title: The Managing Authority of the Education Programme 2021 - 2027 announces a procedure for direct award Digital Transformation of School Education
items.justification: By Decision No. 413 of June 24 2022 of the Council of Ministers  on approving a draft of the Education Programme 2021-2027 a draft of it was approved. The Managing Authority of the Education Programme 2021 - 2027 (EP) announces a procedure for direct provision of grant aid 'Digital Transformation of School Education' within Priority 2 'Modernization and Quality of Education' of the programme. See Activities 2 3 6 and 7 all related to AI literacy by implementation of divergent uses of AI in the education system and teachers' training.

items.title: Program for supporting Bulgarian communities organizations and media abroad
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The program focuses on supporting projects by Bulgarian community organizations and media outlets in neighboring countries (Western Balkans) and Eastern Europe with traditional Bulgarian communities (Ukraine and Moldova) aiming to build capacity to combat disinformation and fake news improve media literacy and build public resilience against external interference and information manipulation. The program provides funding for activities related to: Fact-checking; Combating disinformation and fake news; Initiatives aimed at increasing media literacy and public resilience; Capacity building to identify and combat fake news disinformation external interference and information manipulation.

body.name: Bulgarian Communications Regulation Commission

items.title: International Conference Education 40 - AI Cybersecurity and Digital Future with Erasmus
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The event was organized by the Center for Human Resources Development. The Center is a legal entity under Article 60 of the Administration Law—a secondary budgetary expenditure authority under the Minister of Education and Science. During the event the topic of security was addressed by the Deputy Minister of the Interior who emphasized that Bulgaria is actively working to establish itself as a digital security creator in partnership with the EU and NATO. Commissioner Svetlin Lazarov (GDBOP) had a competent participation in cybersecurity issues. Together with Krasimir Kotsev (CoCyber) he conducted a demonstration on fake news and relevant digital protection strategies.

body.name: Bulgarian Communications Regulation Commission

items.title: Guidelines for using AI in the education system issued by the Ministry of Education
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative supports cultural and linguistic diversity by committing the system to monitor and evaluate AI tools to ensure their effectiveness and adequacy for diverse learning needs abilities learning styles language differences and cultural characteristics. This ensures that both students and teachers benefit from AI systems that adapt to varied linguistic and cultural contexts rather than reinforcing a single dominant model. By requiring this level of oversight the initiative helps guarantee that AI-supported resources remain equitable and accessible across different groups. In doing so it positions AI as a tool that actively reduces disparities in learning experiences for all students and teachers (pp.10-11 Principle 1).

items.title: Event Europe is with me under the motto New technologies - a look at the future organized by the Managing Board of Human Resources Development Program
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Human Resources Development Program (2021-2027) is led by Directorate General for European Funds International Programs and Projects at the Ministry of Labor and Social Policy. One of the modules of this event was 'New technologies to help people with disabilities' with priority theme 'Social Inclusion and Equal Opportunities' and different speakers including those from the Ministry discussed how AI-technologies can help people with disabilities be better integrated into the society and on equal foot by using more ways to communicate. See page 6 of the translated document.

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: Opinion of the Bulgarian Personal Data Protection Commission on the use of a video surveillance system with facial recognition functionality in retail outlets (stores)
items.justification: In this opinion the use of facial recognition video surveillance system in retail outlets for prevention of theft leading to individual’s biometric categorization is analyzed. In paragraph 4 Section 'What exactly is facial recognition?' the Commission accepts that technical inaccuracies of such AI systems may lead to biased results and discrimination. It is stated that the risk of such biased results and discrimination is of particular importance in relation to age ethnicity race gender or disability. In the last paragraph of the legal analysis section it opines the algorithms can be used in relation to different demographic groups thus the presence of bias or deviations in facial recognition can deepen prejudice in society.

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: Measure Development of Standards in the Use of AI (BG0082) as part of the Action Plan Bulgaria Action Plan 2022-2024 (December)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The measure Development of Standards in the Use of Artificial Intelligence (BG0082) was Part of Bulgaria’s Open Government Partnership Action Plan (12.2022-12.2024). It addresses human rights impact assessments safeguards for AI in public decision-making and regulatory frameworks for ethical AI use in government (see Description). E-Government Ministry led and focus areas: Automated decision-making AI ethics human rights safeguards and digital governance (see section Overview). Among others the measure consists of development of common standards in the AI use in the digitization process in order to ensure guarantees of equal access and respect for human rights (e.g. AI-based systems to be unbiased and non-discriminatory p.15 of Plan)

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: AI Readiness Index in Public Administration in the Republic of Bulgaria
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: In Section Preparation of legislation internal rules and the ethical application of AI (p.3) it is concluded that Bulgaria must update its legislation to be harmonized with the European one. In the period 2025–2027 internal mechanisms for risk assessment when using AI systems must be introduced in accordance with the risk categories defined in the regulation. In S.7.2 'What topics would you suggest for training in the field of working with AI?' the interviewed civil servants specified that they would appreciate as additional training topics impact of AI on the quality of life and society.

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: Sofia Municipality tests AI assistant for more transparent public procurement
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: One of the commitments made by Sofia Mayor Vasil Terziev is to make the public procurement process in the capital as transparent and impartial as possible. In fulfillment of this commitment the Sofia Municipality is already testing an experimental artificial intelligence assistant that assists in the verification of public procurement.

items.title: TABLE for reflecting objections and suggestions on the draft Guidelines for application under the procedureDigital Transformation of School Education created by the EXECUTIVE AGENCYPROGRAMME EDUCATION
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The table reflects the objections and suggestions submitted by different ministries on the draft Guidelines for application under the procedure: 'Digital Transformation of School Education' and was created by EXECUTIVE AGENCY “PROGRAMME EDUCATION”. The Ministry of Education stated that the requirements for use of Bulgarian AI models and use of cloud services or infrastructure outside of Bulgaria may be challenged because unclear potentially restrictive and could create legal and financial risks if applied in public procurement procedures. It noted that including such requirements in future public procurements may be challenged as discriminatory or competition-restricting especially against bidders who rely on non-BG models (proposal 4).

items.title: Public Tender Building a platform with adaptive-analytical software with the ability for self-learning data processing and analysis (AI) of the social and solidarity economy
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: The subject of the order covers the development of a comprehensive platform with adaptive-analytical software with the ability for self-learning data processing and analysis (Artificial Intelligence) of the social and solidarity economy together with the delivery of the hardware equipment necessary for its implementation. It was commissioned by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs. The focus is on a AI-driven platform to assist the social and solidarity economy. The bid explicitly mentions the delivery of the hardware equipment necessary for the implementation of the AI platform.

items.title: AI in Law Training for Appellate District Judges
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: 49 magistrates from the Veliko Tarnovo Appellate District underwent a training organized by the District Court - Ruse jointly with the National Institute of Justice. The focus of the event was 'Application of Artificial Intelligence in Law. Electronic Evidence. Evidence in Social Networks and Cryptocurrencies'. The training provided an opportunity for discussion and in-depth study in an area that is becoming increasingly important for the administration of justice in the digital age. Key aspects were examined such as: the application of artificial intelligence in the legal sphere and its potential benefits and challenges; the specifics of electronic evidence and its admissibility in the judicial process; how evidence from social networks.

items.title: AI Readiness Index in Public Administration in the Republic of Bulgaria
items.justification: This initiative supports public sector skills development by identifying knowledge gaps in AI understanding mapping priority application areas such as process automation citizen services data analysis and structuring training needs across ethics technical foundations data work practical case studies and communication ethics legal and social issues .g. legal aspects of applying AI in the public sector. By combining formal training proposals with recognition of informal learning methods like self-study peer exchange and experimentation it creates a comprehensive roadmap for building AI literacy and competence among civil servants enabling them to responsibly adopt AI improve efficiency and maintain public trust (section 7)

items.title: Annex II to the National Strategic Document Digital Transformation of Bulgaria for the Period 2024 2030 Digital Decade Programme until 2030 Roadmap of Bulgaria
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Measure 32 addresses Safety and Security in the context of AI by explicitly requiring the implementation of cybersecurity and data privacy processes in SMEs alongside the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies such as IIoT autonomous robots cloud computing and big data. Measure 37 addresses Safety and Security in the context of AI by focusing its research and innovation on digital security and adaptive software systems ensuring that AI technologies are developed with robust safeguards. Measure 41 addresses Safety and Security in the context of AI by prioritizing the development of intelligent security systems for data exchange and communications and by investing in high levels of cybersecurity as part of its digital innovation agenda.

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: Seminar of the Network of Experts in the Field of Data and AI Technologies in the Field of ESIF and EFSI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: In the period August 31 - September 5 the first of a series of events dedicated to the development of the Network of Experts in the Field of Data and AI Technologies in the Field of ESIF/EFSI was held in Albena Resort. The topics discussed during the seminar were among others cybersecurity applying artificial intelligence and data processing in the daily practice of government experts. Reps from the Institute of Public Administration (IPA) took active participation in the seminar. The IPA was established under the Civil Servant Act in 2000. It is a structure under the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Bulgaria and is the leading institution for training civil servants.

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: INSAIT and the Ministry of Defense will cooperate to implement and use AI for the countrys security
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The Institute for Computer Science Artificial Intelligence and Technology (INSAIT) at Sofia University and the Ministry of Defense will cooperate in the field of innovation computer science AI scientific research cyber security and development. This is done under a Memorandum of Cooperation. INSAIT is the first of its kind in Eastern Europe to offer world-class research facilities and conditions. INSAIT’s sole focus is on scientific excellence: conducting world-class research in AI attracting outstanding international scientists and training the next-generation of graduate students and technology leaders. For this indicator it is especially important that the cooperation will be in the field of AI cyber security and development.

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: Demystifying the process of creating digital assistants the experience of the first state institution with AI in Bulgaria
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Institute for Public Administration's (IPA) digital assistant (CHIPA chatbot) is based on GPT-4o-mini technology (p.2). All its responses come from a pre-selected verified knowledge base rather than uncontrolled internet sources (p.2). To tackle the hallucinations the chatbot is constantly monitored and adjusted and extremely strict control is exercised over the correct answers; (p.3) and verified and tested by external experts and IPA colleagues (p.4). The model is designed as a 'living' organism by continuously learning based on interactions with users. Quality is ensured by a controlled training approach where data is integrated only when verified (p.4). IPA is a structure under the Council of Ministers.

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: In-person Training on the topic AI as a Strategic Tool in the Judicial System
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National Institute of Justice (NIJ) was established by the Judicial System Act in 2003. The NIJ carries out its activities in accordance with the Judicial System Act and the principles of judicial training adopted by the EU Judicial Training Network. The NIJ held a training ' Artificial Intelligence as a Strategic Tool in the Judicial System ' in which 41 judges prosecutors and investigators participated. The lecturers provided a detailed overview of the technical aspects of AI in the courtroom. The introductory lecture was dedicated to the philosophy terminology and basic concepts of AI such as BlackBox machine learning and “deep learning”. final part presented the practical aspects of AI in criminal proceedings.

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: Opinion of the Bulgarian Personal Data Protection Commission on the use of a video surveillance system with facial recognition functionality in retail outlets (stores)
items.justification: The document enhances transparency by explicitly explaining how the facial-recognition system works including data flows human involvement and storage arrangements (p.2–4). It improves explainability by clearly identifying the categories of data processed why they qualify as biometric data and the legal bases the company claims to rely on (p.5–7). It further increases transparency by detailing risks proportionality concerns and high-risk AI implications helping the public understand both the system’s impact and the basis for regulatory conclusions (p.12–15).  The CPDP provides a step-by-step legal analysis showing why these justifications do not meet GDPR and AI Act requirements in a clear way even for non-experts (8-12).

body.name: Ombudsman Central Election Commission Commission for Protection against Discrimination Commission for Personal Data Protection Commission for Consumer Protection State Agency for Child Protection and Executive Agency General Labor Inspectorate

items.title: Khmer Digital Literacy Programme
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Khmer Digital Literacy Programme (KDLP) is led by the Ministry of Education Youth and Sport in partnership with KAPE and Meta. The initiative introduces digital literacy materials and training for students and teachers within Cambodia’s formal education system aiming to strengthen skills such as online safety responsible social media use and critical evaluation of digital information. The programme is implemented through schools and teacher support mechanisms thereby integrating digital competencies into formal education.

items.title: Creating a Safe Digital Environment for Cambodian Children (Workshop)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (MPTC)-led technical workshop addresses Children's Rights in the context of AI by prioritizing the mitigation of emerging AI-related threats. It focused on implementing the Child Online Guidelines and specifically discussed the challenges posed by generative artificial intelligence. The primary goal was to strengthen the MPTC’s regulatory role and enforce platform accountability to proactively ensure digital systems including those that use AI are designed and deployed in a manner that protects children's rights.

items.title: Cambodias AI Readiness Assessment Report
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Assessment a government-led initiative supported by UNESCO embeds cultural and linguistic diversity as a core part of its vision for ethical AI.  “Social & Cultural Dimension” (starting on p.24) assesses how AI adoption can reflect Cambodia’s social-cultural context not just technical readiness. It highlights specific inclusive tools such as the Khmer Braille project (p.13 35) which enables visually impaired students to access reading materials as an “AI for Good” initiative (p.35) showing attention to accessibility and disability. It also notes the development of Khmer-language datasets (p.10) and large language models to support Khmer and local dialects helping preserve linguistic heritage while enabling AI in Khmer.

items.title: Cambodias AI Readiness Assessment Report
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: It addresses gender equality chiefly under its “Responsible AI Inclusion and Well-being” pillar (p.49) noting persistent gender gaps in digital and STEM access in Cambodia (p.26). It observes that the gender gap in internet usage is narrowing (p.24) and highlights efforts to promote digital skills and AI opportunities for women and girls. Accordingly one of the key recommendations is to “3.1. Advance Gender Equality in the AI Ecosystem” (p.51) suggesting targeted inclusion capacity building and representation of women in AI-related education employment and governance.

items.title: Youth Digital Empowerment Workshop and Girls in ICT Day Cambodia 2025
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative led by the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (MPTC) and ITU promotes gender equality by empowering girls and young women with digital and STEM skills essential for AI careers. Session 2 of the agenda engaged participants to experience digital learning tools and applications aiming to build awareness and practical skills by introducing students and teachers to accessible digital technologies (coding AI cybersecurity).

items.title: The Regional Capacity Development Workshop under the theme AI in the Public Sector Policy Considerations and Best Practices
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This Workshop hosted by The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (MPTC) under the theme of AI in the Public Sector has brought together experts and provided an opportunity for high and mid-level public officials and practitioners to deepen their knowledge of AI so they can utilize it in their work.

body.name: The National Council for Digital Economy and Society (NC-DES)

items.title: Online Safety Forum2025 Building Trust in the Age of AI
items.justification: The Online Safety Forum 2025 led by the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications of Cambodia under the leadership of Secretary of State Chun Vat addresses safety and security in the context of AI by raising awareness of online threats associated with generative AI and promoting a coordinated multistakeholder response. The initiative emphasizes the government’s role in setting policies the responsibility of technology companies to implement technical safety guidelines and the need for users to strengthen their digital literacy and protective practices. Through public panel discussions workshops and cross sector collaboration the forum supports preventive awareness cybersecurity coordination and collective responsibility for building

items.title: Cambodias AI Readiness Assessment Report
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The report explicitly drafted in collaboration between Cambodia and UNESCO (see acknowledgements) mentions that Cambodia recognizes the need to focus on enhancing transparency (p. 19) and that procurement processes are central to several key principles in the Recommendation as they dictate requirements for elements such as transparency explainability (p. 20) as well as the need to ensure developing and deploying AI systems that are accountable transparent and explainable (p. 21).

items.title: National Strategy of AI
items.justification: The SNIA was officially launched on July 7 2025 and is merely a declarative initiative by the government. Following this statement which was not documented but only reported in the media (it can be seen in the following linkhttps://web.archive.org/save/https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/le-cameroun-developpe-une-strategie-nationale-de-l-ia-adossee-a-sept-piliers) the third pillar of this initiative focuses on a multilingual and inclusive AI through the development of a local language model – the 'GPT Cameroon' – and the promotion of national languages through linguistic research and the collection of vocal data. It is therefore at this level that we can truly acknowledge that this initiative addresses cultural and Ling

items.title: Helping Canadians identify misinformation online
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: This government-led initiative directly addresses AI-facilitated misinformation through funding and implementation of technological countermeasures. The Government of Canada via the Digital Citizen Contribution Program supports the development of an AI-powered tool by Université de Montréal to detect and mitigate misinformation across multiple formats and languages. By integrating large language models into user-facing tools such as browser extensions the initiative enhances individuals’ ability to identify false content and reduces its spread across languages modalities (text audio video images) and sources.

items.title: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC) AI Complaint Investigations
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — State-based non-judicial mechanisms
items.justification: The Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC) is an active state-based non-judicial mechanism handling AI-related grievances. During the study period the OPC launched AI-specific investigations including OpenAI/ChatGPT (April 2023 ongoing) TikTok (June 2024) and X Corp. (February 2025). In 2024–2025 the OPC received 1458 PIPEDA complaints with rising AI-related cases. The OPC investigates complaints issues findings and recommends remedies providing Canadians with a formal non-judicial channel to seek redress for AI-related privacy harms.

body.name: Treasury Board Secretariat Heads of Agents of Parliament

items.title: Grants and Contributions - The Machine-Readable Child Governance of Emotional AI used with Canadian Children
items.justification: The Grant by the Canadian government valued at $81464.10 is meant for a research project titled 'The Machine-Readable Child: Governance of Emotional AI used with Canadian Children' which will focus on evaluating PIPEDA and proposed Canadian privacy and AI legislation for their fitness to govern the use of Emotional AI used with children highlighting gaps and offering suggestions where appropriate.

items.title: Statement on AI (AI) and Children
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: This statement on AI and children is the result of a convening between Canada's Office of the Privacy Commissioner and a roundtable of G7 data protection and privacy authorities. It identifies 3 main risks of AI in the context of children's privacy and data protection: (AI-based decision-making; manipulation and deception; and training of AI models based on data-scraping) (p. 2). It also sets out several things that regulators in Canada and G7 countries may wish to regulate given these issues (p. 3).

items.title: The Government of Canada calls for stronger international cooperation on digital governance at UNESCO
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The activity led by the Government of Canada (through Canadian Heritage) as reflected in its 2025 engagement at UNESCO focuses on strengthening international cooperation on digital governance in response to the rise of digital platforms and artificial intelligence. It addresses cultural and linguistic diversity by emphasizing the protection and promotion of diverse cultural expressions in the digital environment and highlighting the importance of preserving cultural heritage and identity. It also promotes inclusive AI ecosystems.

items.title: AI integration roadmap for numerical weather and environmental predictions
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The roadmap of the Canadian Government outlines an overview of how AI can be integrated into ECCC's Research-Development-Operation (RDO) production chain for weather and environmental predictions for the future of Canada. Although the majority of it focuses on how AI can be used for the environment itself (thus outside of scope) there are also several references to reducing the impact and resource consumption of AI itself for example noting that 'current and future DA algorithms will struggle with significantly larger ensemble sizes. It is therefore essential to invest in code optimization. ' which directly affects the efficiency of the algorithm itself by paying attention to optimized codes (DA Section).

items.title: 4th review of the Directive on Automated Decision-Making
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The periodic bi-annual reviews of the Directive help ensure that the Directive is robust and meeting its goals. One of the primary goals of the Directive is to ensure fair and reasonable outcomes of automated decision-making systems. The 4th review provides for changes to the language of the Directive that ensure that a discrimination on the basis of various parts of identity is explicitly assessed (see page 11). Adding these bases of discrimination explicitly into the assessment of automated systems helps strengthen the fairness of a system's outputs.

body.name: Treasury Board Secretariat

items.title: Algorithmic Impact Assessment tool
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: Mandatory tool under Directive on Automated Decision-Making (s.6.1); gender equality link via Table 1.5 impact assessment on equality and intersectional identity factors; mandatory GBA+ engagement under subsection 6.3.8. It was approved in 2019 and last updated in 2024 https://regulations.ai/regulations/canada-2019-05-algorithmic-impact-assessment

body.name: Treasury Board Secretariat certain heads of agents of Parliament

items.title: Third Review of the Directive on Automated Decision-Making
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The third review of the Directive includes the following requirements/changes: 'Expand the scope to cover internal services'; 'Introduce measures supporting the tracing protection and lawful handling of data used and generated by a system'; 'Expand the bias testing requirement to cover models'; 'Mandate the completion of Gender Based Analysis Plus during the development or modification of a system'; 'Establish explanation criteria in support of the explanation requirement and integrate them into the Algorithmic Impact Assessment (AIA)'; 'Expand the AIA to include questions concerning an institution's reasons for pursuing automation and potential impacts on persons with disabilities'; among other requirements.

body.name: Treasury Board Secretariat Heads of Agents of Parliament

items.title: Implications of AI Technologies for the Canadian Labour Force Report of the Standing Committee on Human Resources Skills and Social Development and the Status of Persons with Disabilities
items.justification: This report is aimed at Employment and Social Development Canada and examines the impact of AI on jobs in Canada. It includes recommendations to protect workers from AI-driven discrimination in hiring promotion and termination. Specifically on pages 12-15 it addresses the risks of bias and discrimination highlighting the need for updated labour laws and ethical frameworks that ensure protections for all workers including those under algorithmic management without traditional contracts. Page 12 discusses bias risks and the exclusion of vulnerable groups while pages 14-16 recommend reviewing legislation mandating transparency by employers about AI use and ensuring diverse representation in AI oversight to address discrimination risks.

items.title: Government of Canada AI Register (Minimum Viable Product) - GC AI Register (MVP)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Open Government Portal's AIA Register requires federal departments to publicly disclose completed Algorithmic Impact Assessments prior to deploying automated decision systems (Directive on Automated Decision-Making ss.6.1.1 6.5.1–6.5.2). Each published AIA discloses the system's purpose algorithm data sources decision type impact level and mitigation measures. Multiple AIAs were published within the study period providing citizens with accessible information on how the Government of Canada uses AI in administrative decisions affecting their rights and services. This portal was operational from April 2020 and had 22+ AIAs published within the study period.

body.name: Treasury Board Secretariat Heads of Agents of Parliament

items.title: List of interested AI (AI) suppliers
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: This is a list of suppliers who can provide responsible and effective AI services solutions and products to the Government of Canada. It was compiled by Public Services and Procurement Canada as well as the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat. These pre-qualified suppliers fall into three bands which determine the maximum dollar amount that can be rewarded with Band 1 allowing work up to $1 million before taxes Band 2 allowing work up to $2 million before taxes and Band 3 allowing work up to $37.5 million before taxes. The list also shows which suppliers commit to support the Government of Canada's effort in leading the way on ethical AI. NB: The page was updated in Nov. 2025; the government considers the list a current resource.

body.name: Treasury Board Secretariat Heads of Agents of Parliament

items.title: Learning Week on AI
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Government of Canada’s Learning Week on Artificial Intelligence directly supports public sector skill development by providing federal public servants with opportunities to deepen their AI understanding and skills. Held between June 9-13 2025 this week offers flexible participation through live expert sessions self-paced learning videos job aids and discussions focused on responsible AI use. It targets all public servants from beginners to advanced users and aligns with the 2025-2027 AI Strategy priority to build talent and support ethical secure AI adoption. The initiative promotes practical learning and continuous skill development tailored to operational needs.

body.name: AI Centre of Expertise Treasury Board Secretariat

items.title: Using Generative AI in the Government of Canada (DDN321-EV)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The reoccurring course “Using Generative Artificial Intelligence in the Government of Canada (DDN321-EV)” delivered by the Canada School of Public Service (Government of Canada) constitutes a structured training initiative that supports public sector skill development. Delivered as a virtual classroom with instructor-led sessions it provides hands-on learning on the practical application of generative AI tools in government contexts. Participants are trained in core competencies such as prompt design evaluating AI outputs and applying principles of responsible and inclusive AI use.

body.name: AI Centre of Expertise Treasury Board Secretariat

items.title: Generative AI in your daily work
items.justification: The resource “Generative AI in your daily work” led by the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat (Government of Canada) constitutes a knowledge-generation output that supports public sector skill development. It provides structured evidence-informed guidance on the practical use of generative AI within government workflows translating technical and policy considerations into clear actionable insights for civil servants. The web-publication outlines core functionalities limitations and risks of generative AI alongside appropriate use cases and safeguards.

body.name: AI Centre of Expertise Treasury Board Secretariat

items.title: Securing Canadas AI Advantage
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: The budget addresses reskilling/upskilling initiatives in AI by announcing a $50 million investment over four years to provide skills training for workers in sectors disrupted by AI. It advocates supporting workers impacted by AI through targeted training programs like the Sectoral Workforce Solutions Program which will provide new skills training for workers in potentially disrupted sectors and communities such as the creative industries (p. 2).

body.name: CIFAR AI institutes (Amii Mila Vector Institute) Global Innovation Clusters the Standards Council of Canada and the Digital Research Alliance of Canada

items.title: Third Review of the Directive on Automated Decision-Making
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The recommendations from this review of the Directive include: 'Introduce measures supporting the tracing protection and lawful handling of data used and generated by a system'; 'Establish explanation criteria in support of the explanation requirement and integrate them into the Algorithmic Impact Assessment (AIA)'; and 'Expand the AIA to include questions concerning an institution's reasons for pursuing automation and potential impacts on persons with disabilities'.

body.name: Treasury Board Secretariat Heads of Agents of Parliament

items.title: Central African Republic Japan strategic partnership to train 30000 AI experts
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The aim of this training programme is to equip young central Africans with advanced digital skills in order to improve their employability and encourage the creation of local technology businesses. Participants will benefit from mentoring networking platforms and collaborative projects which will increase their chances of joining start-ups SMEs or multinationals in the technology sector.

items.title: Completion of training for 2000 young Chadians in AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This programme reflects a strong political commitment to investing in human capital by equipping young people with the AI tools. By training 2000 young people in AI and future technologies Chad is making a bold commitment to innovation job creation and digital competitiveness.

items.title: Lets Promote Education of the Future Together Initiative
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative is actively building AI literacy by training future teachers in AI. The Ministry of Science in partnership with UMCE CENIA and Kodea launched an AI course for Pedagogy students from four state universities to equip them with AI knowledge and pedagogical skills for classroom use beginning in 2025 helping them teach AI concepts responsibly to their future students. A follow-up report highlights that this “Let's Promote Education of the Future Together” initiative is being expanded to more universities and aims to certify hundreds of future teachers in AI competencies emphasising ethical critical and effective use of technology and the multiplier effect as trained teachers bring AI literacy into Chilean schools.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: Action Plan National Policy on AI (UPDATE 2024)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The action plan of Chile's National AI Policy establishes 177 cross-ministerial initiatives. A crucial component within the policy's third axis—Governance and Ethics—is the explicit mandate to study and implement measures against digital disinformation and violence. This includes measures such as ‘Impulse to multidisciplinary investigation about disinformation digital violence and mental health’ (initiative 172) but also makes explicit reference to the commission against disinformation: 'Reports from the National Disinformation Commission to issue recommendations to address the phenomenon in the digital environment' (initiative 173 p. 41).

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: Advisory Committee against Disinformation
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Advisory Committee Against Disinformation was established by the Chilean Ministry of Science in June 2023 to advise the government on analysing and countering the global phenomenon of disinformation at the local level. Comprising academic and civil society experts the Committee produced this second report with 72 specific public policy recommendations. The initiative directly tackles AI-facilitated threats in Chapter 5 and advocates for a multi-lateral governance framework. The report treats AI not merely as a tool but as a systemic actor that exacerbates misinformation and violence requiring coordinated regulatory educational and research-based responses (for example warning labels or supplementary information when AI is used).

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: Hold on check share Government Campaign
items.justification: The 'Hold on Check Share' campaign led by the Ministry General Secretariat of Government (SEGEGOB) is a direct implementation of the Advisory Committee against disinformation's public policy recommendations to build societal resilience. It specifically operationalizes the Committee's call for nationwide media and information literacy by equipping citizens with critical verification skills. This foundational behavioral intervention aims to protect the public against sophisticated AI-generated disinformation and synthetic media. By promoting a culture of verifying before sharing online the initiative directly targets the viral mechanics that amplify harmful content thereby mitigating the social impact of AI-facilitated misinformation.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: LatamGPT
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: LatamGPT led by Chile’s Centro Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (CENIA) with public funding promotes cultural and linguistic diversity in AI through the development of a large language model trained on texts from across Latin America including local and indigenous sources. The initiative draws on contributions from regional institutions universities communities and civil-society actors including Wikimedia Chile reflecting a multi-actor collaboration. In addition through CENIA Chile’s AI Action Plan supports AI tools for endangered languages such as Mapudungún and Rapa Nui contributing to the preservation and inclusion of these cultures in AI systems.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge

items.title: Action Plan National Policy on AI (UPDATE 2024)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Chilean AI Action Plan addresses Gender Equality through a dedicated strategy (Section 3.4 pages 31-33). It aims to increase women's participation in AI research development and the industry to at least OECD average levels with campaigns to showcase women leaders in tech and promote communities for women in AI implementing gender quotas fostering girls' early interest in STEM and increasing female enrollment in higher education STEM programs to 40% actions to increase women's employment in AI under decent conditions achieve 40% female participation in high-potential AI startups and close the gender employment gap.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: Cupos Ms Mujeres Cientficas (+MC) initiative
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The Cupos Más Mujeres Científicas (+MC) initiative addresses gender equality in AI-related fields by increasing female participation in STEM careers (pp. 11-12) which form the foundation for AI skills and workforce development. It provides additional university quotas exclusively for women in over 500 STEM programs across 44 universities aiming to reduce gender gaps and structural barriers in higher education. By promoting women’s entry into science technology engineering and mathematics the program strengthens gender representation in critical areas of AI development like in academic programs like Computer Science Engineering or Civil Engineering in Data Science contributing to a more inclusive and balanced future AI workforce.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: GobLab UAIs Algorithmic impact assessment
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: An initiative funded by the Chilean National Agency for Research and Development is strongly aligned with Chile’s National AI Policy whose Action Plan explicitly references the GobLab UAI ethical algorithms tools. GobLab developed three instruments for responsible AI including the Algorithmic impact assessments. This tool guides development teams in identifying risks—data bias inequity privacy cybersecurity—and defining mitigation measures before deployment. Using an 11-questions survey it strengthens transparency and accountability. More info of the tools: https://web.archive.org/web/20250909063950/https://algoritmospublicos.cl/herramientas

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: Evaluation of the Implementation of Law 21431 Which Amends The Labor Code Regulating The Contract Of Workers in Digital Platform Service Companies
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: This initiative consisted of evaluating the implementation of Law 21.431. The report combined quantitative data from the National Employment Survey qualitative findings from a FLACSO-Chile study involving participant observation and stakeholder feedback from social dialogues and lobbying meetings. It found persistent high informality (~75%) a near-total dominance of independent contractor status despite legal provisions for both categories and significant failures in achieving mandated algorithmic transparency and non-discrimination. The evaluation concluded that while the law established pioneering rights it had a limited impact on formalising labour relations or ensuring fair algorithmic management within its initial year.

body.name: Labor Directorate

items.title: Tripartite Roundtable on Digital Platforms
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: This initiative is a government-led forum for tripartite social dialogue between the government platform companies and worker unions. The initiative aims to advance and tackle the difficulties in the implementation of Law 21.431. Specific areas raised for discussion which are central to AI-driven labour protections include algorithmic bias transparency contract types and remuneration of gig work among other issues.

body.name: Labor Directorate

items.title: Chiles Department of Social Security Superintendence (SUSESO) project of implementation of procurement tool
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The WPF report shows how a specific State body the Department of Social Security Superintendence (SUSESO) is including responsible AI into public procurement through its standard bidding template for data science and AI projects which requires vendors to provide bias assessments statistical bias analyses transparency documentation data-protection measures explainability information and model governance details (pp. 1–2). It further highlights that SUSESO has two AI projects procured under this template ensuring that these systems comply with uniform ethical technical and accountability standards across public-sector AI procurement (p. 2).

items.title: Do it with AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: “Hazlo con IA” is a strong example of an AI-related upskilling initiative in Chile because it provides free large-scale accessible training in generative AI for workers SMEs and public-sector employees—groups that often face the greatest barriers to digital transformation. The program is led by CENIA and 'Futuro del Trabajo SOFOFA Capital Humano' backed by the Ministries of Economy Science and Labour 'SENCE SOFOFA' and supported by Google. Courses include IA basics prompt design responsible use and are being rolled out with specific modules for public servants across central government local administrations and autonomous bodies.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: AI enters ChileValoras catalogue of jobs
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: This initiative strengthens AI-focused reskilling and upskilling by creating five ChileValora-certified job profiles—AI Programmer Generative AI Interaction Specialist AI Ethics Auditor Applied Machine Learning Technician and Data Annotation and Labeling Specialist. Led jointly by the Ministries of Science and Labour it enables workers to certify AI skills through ChileValora the national system for labor competence certification that validates worker skills through industry-aligned standards. The effort is supported by SENCE which is offering 300 scholarships for related AI training courses.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: Do it with AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: “Hazlo con IA” is a strong example of an AI-related upskilling initiative in Chile because it provides free large-scale accessible training in generative AI for workers SMEs and public-sector employees—groups that often face the greatest barriers to digital transformation. The program is led by CENIA and 'Futuro del Trabajo SOFOFA Capital Humano' backed by the Ministries of Economy Science and Labour 'SENCE SOFOFA' and supported by Google.org. By offering thousands of no-cost course slots nationwide and partnering with both government and industry actors the program lowers financial and technical barriers while directly targeting productivity inclusion and practical AI adoption.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: Resolution on Recommendations from the Transparency Council on Algorithmic Transparency
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The initiative addresses Transparency and Explainability by requiring public bodies to disclose clear accessible information on how automated and semi-automated decision systems (ADS) operate their objectives methods or model used data sources and impacts. It mandates proactive publication of this information through “Algorithmic Transparency” items (Section 5 and 6 pp. 5–11). These measures ensure citizens understand when and how AI systems influence decisions thus promoting explainability and accountability

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: Algorithmic transparency on the Transparency portal
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: This is the Transparency Portal maintained by the Council for Transparency (CPLT) which operationalises the CPLT’s Recommendations on Algorithmic Transparency by providing a dedicated space for public institutions to disclose information on algorithmic and automated decision-making systems. However data downloaded from the portal show very limited adoption: so far only five public institutions have created algorithmic transparency pages and only one—the Social Security Institute (IPS)—has explicitly declared the use of automated decision-making systems (ADMs). IPS disclosed information on three algorithmic systems including a predictive model based on neural networks for pending pension claims.

body.name: Ministry of Science Technology Knowledge and Innovation

items.title: The issuance of Action Plan for the Adjustment and Optimization of Academic Disciplines and Majors (2025-2027)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: According to the official press release the Ministry of Education issued an action plan on reforming higher education majors. The plan implements the part of subsection (12) that calls for refining the 'structure of academic majors' to align with national strategic needs. The Ministry of Education's guidance establishes a systematic national curriculum and mandates that students receive instruction to cultivate proficiency and enhance AI Literacy from an early age.

body.name: National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) Ministry of Education (MOE)

items.title: AI curriculum for basic education
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: This initiative directly implements the requirement in subsection (12) to promote 'AI education at all academic levels' and 'general education throughout society'. The Ministry of Education mandated a nationwide rollout of AI education for primary and secondary students to cultivate a 'generation proficient in emerging technologies enhancing workforce readiness'. It transitions AI literacy from pilot projects to a systematic national curriculum.

body.name: National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) Ministry of Education (MOE)

items.title: Qinglang Campaign Rectifying Abuse of AI Technology
items.justification: The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) launched a nationwide campaign to regulate AI services and applications specifically rectifying the 'abuse of AI technology.' Key tasks include cracking down on illegal AI applications enhancing the management of AI-generated content and its labeling penalizing the use of AI to spread misinformation and urging online platforms to improve detection and verification.

items.title: Measures on the Management of Personal Information Protection Compliance Audits (with guidelines)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — State-based non-judicial mechanisms
items.justification: The system is mandated by the central regulator the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) (p.2 promulgating entity) and enforces administrative compliance. The audit is a proactive/ex-post measure where the government orders companies handling large data volumes (1million ppl for non-sensitive info; or 100k for sensitive) to audit their compliance (article 5 pp.2-3). This applies to platforms using AI that have large user base or train AI using personal data. The CAC can mandate external audits in high-risk scenarios or following significant data breaches. The audit reports outline deficiencies in areas like automated decision-making and consent mechanisms forcing the company to correct the flaws.

body.name: Cybersecurity Administration of China (CAC)

items.title: Chinas First Case on AI-Generated Voice Infringement (Beijing Internet Court 2024)
items.justification: A 2024 decision by the Beijing Internet Court addressed harms from AI-generated voice technology. The court found that defendants used a voice actor’s recordings to train and operate a text-to-speech AI system without authorization infringing her voice rights under the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Art. 1023). The court ordered the responsible companies to cease the infringement issue a public apology and pay RMB 250000 in damages. This judicial ruling demonstrates how individuals can seek legal remedy and compensation when AI systems misuse personal data or likeness.

body.name: Cybersecurity Administration of China (CAC)

items.title: Clear & Bright Summer 2025 Special Rectification of the Online Environment for Minors
items.justification: The special action is an effort by the Central Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) to enforce existing regulations like the Provisions on the Protection of Minors on the Internet. The action explicitly targets AI-related risks in its oversight scope focusing on three areas: 1. Content safety and functional regulation of children's smart devices; 2. Inappropriate application of AI functions in the field of minors; 3. Issues related to inducing addiction using AI features. The campaign aims to protect minors' rights by clearing harmful content such as network bullying explicit material self-harm inducement and content using minors' images for malicious profiteering (e.g. 'soft pornography').

items.title: China Telecom launched the Xingchen AI model for Chinese Dialects
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: China Telecom's (central state-owned enterprise a type of SOE directly supervised by the central government) Xingchen model an audio-based language model designed to understand and generate content in more than 30 Chinese dialects. The initiative directly addresses the Cultural and Linguistic Diversity indicator by developing an AI system that promotes and preserves various linguistic backgrounds. This initiative is a form of government-led initiative and also an example of capacity building and knowledge generation by a state-owned enterprise aiming to improve accessibility and cultural representation within AI technology.

items.title: Inner Mongolia Key Laboratory of Multilingual AI Technology
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The lab was founded by the regional government and its specific initiatives were largely guided and funded by the state. Initiatives related to cultural and linguistic diversity in AI include: Developing AI tools for the Mongolian language such as speech recognition and synthesis machine translation and text recognition; Creating the Beijiang Ancient Books Resource Database which is described as a comprehensive platform for the preservation and analysis of ancient Mongolian texts; Leading a National Key R&D Project to develop a bidirectional Mongolian-Chinese speech translation system. As the website only says 'June 2024' without mentioning the exact start day I put the 30th for the start day.

items.title: Green Data Center Evaluation National Index System
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The initiative is the formal implementation (June 1 2025) of the national standard Green Data Center Evaluation which provides a comprehensive technical standard for green and low-carbon data center certification. It addresses the sustainability of AI by creating mandatory auditable benchmarks for the energy-intensive infrastructure that supports AI development. The standard includes strict weighted metrics for efficient utilization of energy resources (e.g. PUE (table 1 no.1 p.1) efficiency per unit of computing power (table 1 no.16 p.2)) water utilization (table 1 no.6 p.1) and crucially Green Operation and Maintenance Level which includes requirements for the recycling and reuse of retired server equipment (pp.3-4)
