items.title: Eastern Data Western Computing Plan
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The 'East Data West Computing' project addresses the environmental impact of AI by strategically relocating data centers to leverage clean energy and natural cooling. The initiative shifts energy-intensive computing tasks from the developed eastern regions which rely heavily on fossil fuels to the western regions which have abundant renewable resources like solar wind and hydropower.

body.name: National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) National Energy Administration (NEA) National Data Administration (NDA) Ministry of Finance (MOF) Peoples Bank of China (PBC) National Administration of Financial Regulation (NAFR) State Taxation Administration (STA) State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (MARA) Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD)

items.title: Qinglang campaign Rectification of Prominent Algorithmic Problems on Internet Platforms
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The initiative enforces fairness and non-discrimination by strictly prohibiting 'Big Data Price Discrimination' where algorithms use personal data like consumption levels or device types to set higher prices for different users on the same product. It specifically protects vulnerable groups by requiring that algorithms for delivery and ride-hailing services balance platform profit with the 'legitimate rights and interests' of gig workers preventing AI from setting unrealistic safety-compromising deadlines. To ensure competitive equity the policy bars platforms from using algorithms to engage in monopolistic practices such as 'choosing one from two' (exclusive dealing) or manipulating traffic to unfairly suppress specific merchants.

body.name: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC)

items.title: The Global Digital Empowerment for Women Development Exchange and Cooperation Center
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The establishment of the Global Exchange and Cooperation Center for Digital Empowerment of Women directly addresses gender equality in the context of AI by working to close the gender digital divide. The center is a strategic initiative by the All-China Women's Federation to 'eliminate gender digital gaps' and is described as an innovative practice for promoting the international governance of digital technology.The initiative aims to boost women's digital capabilities cultivate digital talent and support research on women and digital technology. These actions are a tangible response to the ethical risks identified in AI safety governance frameworks which include the 'aggravating of social bias and widening intelligence divide'.

items.title: Statement on AI (AI) for Promoting Accessibility at UNHRC
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: China spoke on behalf of a group of countries at the 56th session of the United Nations (UN) Human Rights Council addressing the role of AI in promoting women's rights and ensuring their participation in AI governance. The joint statement initiated by China calls for upholding the principle of gender equality to ensure the 'comprehensive equal and meaningful participation of women in AI governance'. It also advocates for non-discrimination in AI systems and for enhancing ethical standards and norms for AI to advance gender equality. However I cannot find the exact speech on that day.

items.title: Generative AI Service Filing
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — AI registers
items.justification: The Generative AI Service Filing enforces determination by ensuring that any AI with 'public opinion or social mobilization capabilities' undergoes a rigorous state-led review before deployment. According to the Interim Measures (the main framework) the implementation unit (Cyberspace Administration of China) conducted assessments of relevant models and issued filing numbers. The services need to display filing numbers which also allows the government to trace the specific human entity responsible for any AI malfunction or illegal content. More info about the assessment: https://web.archive.org/web/20260127152116/https://ocpl.substack.com/p/expert-insight-chinas-ai-services

body.name: Cyberspace Administration of China

items.title: Sword-Shining Pujiang 2025
items.justification: This initiative is part of the 'Sword-Shining Pujiang' campaign by the Shanghai provincial Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC). It discovered that several platforms bypassed mandatory security assessments leading the AI to generate illegal content like 'human flesh searching' (open-boxing) money laundering and deepfakes. Despite being ordered to shut down three companies illegally restarted their services leading to formal legal prosecution. The Shanghai Cyberspace Administration (CAC) summoned the companies for a regulatory interview in accordance with the law issued a serious critique and demanded comprehensive rectification.

body.name: Cyberspace Administration of China

items.title: CAC special action of clear and bright governance of typical algorithm issues on online platforms
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: This is a time-bound joint campaign by the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) and other departments to address persistent problems in platform algorithms. It 1) highlights the need to prevent platforms from reckless profit-seeking at the expense of workers 2) mandates that platforms clearly disclose algorithm rules for time estimation fee calculation and route planning. 3) prohibits algorithms from being used to carry out monopolistic and unfair competitive practices 4) protects the legitimate rights and interests of workers 5) requires improvement of the platform's order allocation remuneration composition and payment working hours rewards and punishments and other related algorithms.

body.name: Cyberspace Administration of China

items.title: Internet Information Service Algorithm Filing System
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — AI registers
items.justification: The official Algorithm Filing system provides a public-facing database where citizens can view the provider service purpose and basic 'algorithm operating mechanism' for registered systems. During the 2024-2025 period this expanded to include AI models used by state media local government and state-owned enterprises. More information: https://archive.ph/vAahb and https://archive.ph/zKOjXl. Related measures (not explicitly to government algorithm) started on March 1 2022 so I put the date here. While the system primarily targets internet service providers some state-owned enterprises and government-affiliated entities appear in the registry offering limited public disclosure of algorithmic systems.

items.title: Politburo 20th study session on AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The 20th Politburo Study Session on AI (April 2025) is a Knowledge Generation initiative as it serves as the authoritative mechanism for synthesizing expert information and disseminating strategic knowledge across the state apparatus. The session's purpose is to allow experts to inform senior leaders enabling General Secretary Xi Jinping to officially command the bureaucracy's focus. The resulting political directive mandates strengthening AI education across all phases and enhancing public awareness. This strategic knowledge output directly implements the core goal of the 14th Five-Year Plan's talent mandate (P.58) signaling ministries to prioritize and fund the upskilling of leading cadres in AI and data competencies.

body.name: Human Resources and Social Security departments

items.title: Beijing No 1 Intermediate Peoples Court Yunti Lecture Series Specialized Training on the Challenges of Infringement Liability in the Age of AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held this training on August 27 2025 for judges and court personnel. It focused on the complex legal challenges of AI infringement liability based on specific articles of the Civil Code. This directly contributes to Public Sector Skills Development by equipping judicial officers with the specialized legal knowledge and theoretical support needed to accurately apply the law to new technologies and resolve AI infringement disputes within the existing legal framework.

body.name: Supreme Peoples Court (SPC)

items.title: Skilled Workers Training Program and Rating System Reform
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS) has recognized 72 new professions during the '14th Five-Year Plan' period (2021-2025 https://web.archive.org/web/20250826190521/https://en.ndrc.gov.cn/policies/202203/P020) including generative artificial intelligence system operator and published 328 national profession standards to improve the working environment and motivate people to explore new skills. The official state media claimed to have 44 million people gained authorized skills level qualifications since 2021 and 6000-plus have been titled senior skilled workers and chief technical engineers thanks to the optimized State-level rating system. AI-related qualifications and certificates are included in these numbers.

body.name: National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC)

items.title: China AI Development and Safety Network (CnAISDA)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The 'China AI Development and Safety Network' is the National AI Safety Network in China that is composed of research forces from various sectors including industry academia and research institutions within China. It has been set up to act like China's AI safety institution (AISI) and join international AISI events. It conducts research on frontier technologies in artificial intelligence enhancing the safety reliability controllability and fairness of AI technology.

items.title: Internet Information Service Algorithm Registration System
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: All AI models are required to register in this national system before deployment. As a set of registration processes the government also mandates providers of high-impact algorithms (including most AI models) to submit a Security Self-Assessment. This forces companies to address potential security flaws and ensures the traceability of AI models.

items.title: Frontier AI Risk Management Framework and Risk Analysis Technical Report
items.justification: Shanghai AI Laboratory a national AI lab partners with CSO Concordia to produce the Frontier AI Risk Management Framework. The framework proposes a robust set of protocols designed to empower general-purpose AI developers with comprehensive guidelines for proactively identifying assessing mitigating and governing a set of severe AI risks that pose threats to public safety and national security. Alongside the framework Shanghai AI Laboratory released a technical report that evaluated several frontier models across key areas: cyber offense biological threats large-scale persuasion and harmful manipulation and loss of control risks (executive summary p.2).

items.title: Qinglang campaign Rectification of Prominent Algorithmic Problems on Internet Platforms
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: This initiative mandates a shift from black box algorithms to verifiable accountability. It asks platforms to publicly explain the principles and intentions behind ranking search and recommendation systems in 'simple clear and understandable' terms; for gig work and e-commerce systems must disclose the specific mechanics of price calculations route planning and estimated times banning vague excuses for pricing or delays; hot-search rankings must be fully transparent with platforms maintaining logs to prove their algorithmic logic is verifiable by regulators.

body.name: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC)

items.title: Algorithm Registry System
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) created a mandatory registration system for recommendation algorithms that came into effect on March 1 2022 alongside the regulation. The registry requires companies to file detailed information about their algorithms including self-assessment reports and data on how the algorithms are trained and deployed. The CAC has released lists of algorithms that have been registered. This registry serves as a foundation for future legislation and provides a means for the government to gain insight into how algorithms function. The public can key in the name/serial number of algorithms in the search box to find information. The blue box is for AI providers to fill algorithms into the registry.

body.name: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC)

items.title: Measures for Identifying AI-Generated and Synthetic Content
items.justification: China has implemented a comprehensive AI content labeling regime that came into effect on September 1 2025. This initiative is a concrete example of implementing transparency. The regulations require all AI-generated content—including text images audio and video—to have both explicit labels (e.g. a text tag like 'AI' meaning 'AI generated') (article 3. p.1) and invisible metadata tags that are machine-readable (article 5 p.2). The regulations place the onus on internet platforms like: WeChat Weibo and Douyin to detect and label AI-generated content. Platforms must maintain compliance logs and can face penalties for non-compliance including content removal account suspension and fines.

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: AI for Science Education Funding Programme
items.justification: The funding programme support teachers in integrating AI in science teaching and learning. This funding is allocated to schools for teachers to enrol in relevant professional development courses for subject development (such as “Building PredictiveModel with the use of AI” and “Machine Learning”) and integrating AI in teaching science (p.2)

body.name: Education Bureau Steering Committee on Strategic Development of Digital Education Curriculum Development Council Standing Committee on STEAM Education Digital Education Centre of Excellence Hong Kong Education City

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Professional Development Programme
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Professional Development Programme (PDP) under the Digital Education Centre of Excellence seeks to enhance teachers' capabilities in digital education as well as promoting AI. These courses using AI to assist in teaching and learning. The CoE offers on-site support services to school on the implementation of digital education. The support services cover pedagogical technological as well as managerial issues related to the implementation of digital education e.g. artificial intelligence in education promoting Information Literacy (IL) and e-safety using innovative technologies to promote STEAM. (additional context of CoE are on P.67:https://www.legco.gov.hk/yr2025/english/panels/ed/papers/ed20250704cb3-1050-3-e.pdf ).

body.name: Education Bureau Steering Committee on Strategic Development of Digital Education Curriculum Development Council Standing Committee on STEAM Education Digital Education Centre of Excellence Hong Kong Education City

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Ethical AI Framework Quick Reference Guide
items.justification: The quick reference guide is intended to provide readers with quick reference and initial understanding of the Ethical Artificial Intelligence  Framework and procedures that should be embedded. The reference guide outlines the 12 ethical AI principles which includes Fairness. Under the fairness principle on p.5 recommendations and results from AI applications should treat individuals within similar groups in a fair manner without favouritism or discrimination and without causing or resulting in harm. This entails maintaining respect for the individuals behind the data and refraining from using datasets that contain discriminatory biases.

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Training to Equip Civil Servants to Embrace Digital Transformation of Public Services
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The legislative council press release shows that the government provides AI related training through the digital policy office and the civil service college (responses to Q6-7). According to the government's press release the digital policy office and the civil service bureau have been offering AI related training within the study timeframe(https://web.archive.org/web/20251110083647/https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202506/13/P2025061300655.htm?fontSize=1). The discussion paper also suggests that the civil service college will continue to offer AI related training(P.69:https://web.archive.org/web/20251110083929/https://www.csb.gov.hk/english/info/files/20250616_PanelPaper(IV)_e.pdf)

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Reforms of the Employees Retraining Board
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The document summarises new training courses and existing courses in the Employees Retraining Board (ERB) on technology and AI. In terms of new training courses the ERB has rolled out 22 courses covering information and technology and will continue to more courses on AI technology application and digital literacy (p.2p.3). Additionally there are also existing courses on AI already available such as AI-enhanced Social Media Content Creation in Marketing business applications of generative AI. (p.3).

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Ethical AI Framework Quick Reference Guide
items.justification: The quick reference guide is a shortened version of the ethical artificial intelligence framework. This version seeks to provide a quick guide for the public's reference. The guide includes robustness reliability and security in the 12 ethical AI principles and offers guidance on how this principle can be achieved during the AI lifecycle(p.5). For example prior to system deployment verification validation and testing should be executed to ensure AI applications perform as intended (p.11). Mitigation steps should be incorporated to minimise damages in the case of failure(p.11).

items.title: Government invests over $32 billion to integrate AI into higher education
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: This initiative seeks to integrate Artificial Intelligence into higher education through two key projects: 1) Strengthening academic communities and curricular flexibility to promote programme updating and internationalisation and 2) A national strategy for educational transformation with AI which includes diagnosis of supply advice on creating new programmes and international partnerships. Both actions promote AI skills ethical training and curriculum development at the tertiary level with a dedicated budget (COP 3.2 billion).

body.name: Ministry of Information Technology and Communications Ministry of National Education

items.title: Standards on Algorithmic Transparency used by the State - Office of the Attorney General of Colombia and Office of the Ombudsman of Colombia
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 establishes that algorithmic systems used by the State that intervene in or support processes related to the provision of services to children and adolescents must comply with additional requirements of transparency explainability and impact assessment (Article 13). These measures include analyzing the algorithmic impact prior to deploying the system taking risk mitigation measures to avoid infringing on fundamental rights establishing procedures for objections to automated decisions and clarifying the justification for affirmative action when designing systems that differentiate or prioritize vulnerable groups such as children and adolescents (Article 17).

items.title: Standards on Algorithmic Transparency used by the State - Office of the Attorney General of Colombia and Office of the Ombudsman of Colombia
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: Joint Directive 007 of 2025 addresses gender equality in AI through algorithmic impact analysis including gender-specific assessments (Article 14) and requires justification for affirmative actions that promote equity (Article 13 para. 2). It also establishes higher disclosure standards for systems that affect vulnerable populations and requires analysis of effects on rights such as equality and non-discrimination (Article 5).

body.name: Colombian National Planning Department (DNP)

items.title: Ruling T-323 of 2024 - Constitutional Court of Colombia (2024)
items.justification: Ruling T-323 of 2024 establishes guidelines for the use of AI in the judicial branch emphasizing that it should not replace human rationality and the principle of human control. The Court reaffirms that judicial decisions must be made and justified by human judges (para.219) who must verify supervise and assume responsibility for the use of AI (para.372). In addition it orders the Superior Council of the Judiciary to issue guidelines on the use of AI ensuring that human judgment prevails in all judicial proceedings (para.406). This is in line with the principles of oversight and accountability established in the Ministry of Science's Roadmap.

items.title: Ruling T-534 of 2023 - Constitutional Court of Colombia
items.justification: Ruling T-534 of 2023 addresses labour protections in AI by requiring platforms that use algorithmic or automated decisions (para.38) to respect due process guarantees for workers. The Court states that when platforms exclude users based on algorithmic evaluations they exercise normative power and must ensure legality clear reasons defense and contradiction rights and impartiality (paras.117-118).

body.name: Ministry of Labour

items.title: Court Decision T-067 of 2025 - Constitutional Court of Colombia (2025)
items.justification: Ruling T-067 of 2025 promotes the public disclosure of algorithmic systems by recognising that algorithmic transparency is part of the right of access to information (pp. 2-3 paras. 64-67 and chap. 6.1). It also orders the adoption of measures to increase the availability of information on state algorithms including the publication of source code or meaningful explanations under a principle of maximum disclosure (pp. 3-4 and chap. 6.3).

body.name: Ministry of ICT National Planning Department and Ministry of Science

items.title: The Institutional Training Plan (Colombian Civil Service 2025)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Institutional Training Plan (Colombian Civil Service 2025) strengthens public sector skills through structured training aligned with the National Training and Capacity Building Plan 2023-2030. It addresses competencies in digital transformation ethics inclusion and technical areas like AI and data analysis (See Training Plan Schedule pp. 30-34). Specifically a course on Artificial Intelligence is scheduled for the second semester (point 17 p. 33). Although this course was launched it falls outside the scope of this study (October 2025) as seen in this link: https://mintic.gov.co/portal/inicio/Sala-de-prensa/Noticias/406073:Abiertas-inscripciones-para-diplomado-gratuito-en-Inteligencia-Artificial-para-servidores-publicos

items.title: AI Course for the Administration of Justice
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The AI course for the Justice Sector developed by the Superior Council of the Judiciary of Colombia and Los Andes University is another relevant capacity-building initiative in Colombia. Launched with broad national participation it trains 1200 magistrates judges and judicial staff in responsible and ethical AI use. The program strengthens digital skills supports the justice sector’s digital transformation and promotes good practices for adopting emerging technologies.

items.title: AvanzaTEC - Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: AvanzaTEC addresses upskilling and reskilling by offering free industry-certified training in AI data analytics cybersecurity cloud services and programming to over 38000 Colombians. It enables workers to enhance current digital skills (upskilling) and supports individuals from non-tech backgrounds to transition into technology roles (reskilling) improving employability and preparing the workforce for AI-driven transformations.

body.name: Ministry of Information Technology and Communications Ministry of National Education Ministry of Science Technology and Innovation Ministry of Labour National Learning Service and National Development Department

items.title: Court Decision T-067 of 2025 - Constitutional Court of Colombia (2025)
items.justification: Court Decision T-067 of 2025 addresses the indicator by establishing the principle of algorithmic transparency as essential for the right to access public information. The Court orders maximum disclosure of algorithmic systems including publication of code or meaningful explanations and mandates clear accessible information on logic and data use (paras 57–59 and 77–81).

items.title: CARIA training platform
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Congolese government has launched  an online learning platform to teach IT and communication skills to young people. The CARIA online training platform addresses reskilling/upskilling in the context of AI by providing structured courses and practical exercises in areas such as cybersecurity AI and technological innovation that equip youth and early-career learners with AI concepts digital tools and cybersecurity skills. By targeting individuals who may lack prior AI experience the initiative enables participants to acquire new competencies or enhance existing ones making them better prepared for employment and entrepreneurial opportunities in AI-driven sectors

items.title: One thousand teachers are being trained in AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: In October 2024 the Ministry of Public Education (MEP) through its Instituto de Desarrollo Profesional (IDP) delivered the self-managed course 'The Future of Education: A Perspective from Artificial Intelligence' to 1000 teachers and administrative staff. The course aimed to develop core AI principles among educators to facilitate the design of strategies for integrating AI into teaching practices and improving educational management processes.

body.name: Ministry of Science Innovation Technology and Telecommunications

items.title: MTSS promotes occupational health in the face of the impacts of digitization and AI
items.justification: In April 2025 the Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MTSS) through the Consejo de Salud Ocupacional launched the Semana de Salud Ocupacional 2025 campaign under the theme 'The impacts of digitalization and AI on the safety and health of workers' (28 April–3 May 2025). The campaign explicitly addressed algorithmic management of work and included a dedicated session on AI cybersecurity and labour rights. It targeted employers and workers through conferences expert panels and awareness activities aiming to promote protective practices against AI-driven risks in the workplace.

items.title: High-level course on AI for the public sector with support from UNESCO and MICITT
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: In July 2025 (7–9 July) MICITT and UNESCO jointly delivered a high-level course on Artificial Intelligence for the public sector in San José as part of the implementation of Costa Rica's ENIA 2024-2027. The course received over 400 applications from public servants and provided 30 bursaries. Based on the AI4Gov programme it introduced participants to AI principles applications and governance challenges in public administration through lectures case studies and collaborative work. The Deputy Minister of Science Technology and Innovation confirmed the course as a direct ENIA implementation action.

body.name: Ministry of Science Innovation Technology and Telecommunications

items.title: Course AI Fundamentals with IBM SkillsBuild
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: MICITT through its Programa Nacional de Centros Comunitarios Inteligentes (CECI) delivers the free course 'AI Fundamentals with IBM SkillsBuild' to the general public at community centres across Costa Rica. The course covers AI fundamentals machine learning models using IBM Watson Studio AI ethics and AI labour market navigation with the explicit objective of improving participants' employability in an AI-driven economy. Multiple editions were delivered at community libraries UNED centres and municipal facilities from September 2025 onward. The initiative constitutes a public-private partnership between MICITT and IBM implemented as part of the ENIA 2024-2027.

body.name: Ministry of Science Innovation Technology and Telecommunications

items.title: Introduction of AI (AI) into the education system in Cte dIvoire in partnership with UNESCO and GPE KIX
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Ministry of National Education and Literacy in partnership with UNESCO and GPE-KIX Africa 21 Hub organised a three-day workshop in Yamoussoukro (CIV) from 15 to 17 September 2025. This event brought together decision-makers experts and education practitioners to develop an AI skills framework tailored to teachers and learners with a focus on integrating AI and digital technology into education systems. The work included the co-construction of AI skills and the translation of digital resources into national languages for inclusive accessibility. It resulted in concrete recommendations for adapting educational curricula. This is an active open-ended initiative operational as of 30 September 2025 contributing to AI literacy.

body.name: The National AI Agency (ANIA)

items.title: AI from concept to application (curriculum)
items.justification: Croatian Academic and Research Network – CARNET developed an AI curriculum for extracurricular activities for Primary Schools. Key elements of the curriculum are listed on page 6. Curriculum will 'guide students toward understanding and applying artificial intelligence and emerging technologies in various contexts'. 'Students should gain knowledge skills and attitudes related to: What artificial intelligence and emerging technologies are; The development of artificial intelligence; The use of AI-based tools especially in learning'.

items.title: Designation of authorities under Article 77 of the EU AU Act
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The Government has designated several authorities responsible for the protection of fundamental rights in accordance with Article 77 of the EU AI Act including the Ombudsperson for Gender Equality. The authority 'shall have the power to request and access any documentation created or maintained under this Regulation in accessible language and format when access to that documentation is necessary for effectively fulfilling their mandates within the limits of their jurisdiction' (Article 77(1)). The designation of these authorities represents the establishment of an institutional framework for the protection of human rights as envisioned by the AI Act.

body.name: Public Ombudsperson Ombudsperson for Children Ombudsperson for Gender Equality Ombudsperson for Persons with Disabilities Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency State Election Committee Agency for Electronic Media

items.title: Designation of authorities under Article 77 of the EU AU Act
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The Government has designated several authorities responsible for the protection of fundamental rights in accordance with Article 77 of the EU AI Act including the Ombudsperson for Gender Equality. The authority 'shall have the power to request and access any documentation created or maintained under this Regulation in accessible language and format when access to that documentation is necessary for effectively fulfilling their mandates within the limits of their jurisdiction' (Article 77(1)). Designation of the Ombudsperson for Gender Equality as one of the authorities protecting human rights is recognized as an action contributing to the implementation of the framework and also as highly relevant for the indicator Gender Equality.

items.title: Workshop on conducting fundamental rigths impact assesment
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency translated a guidebook on the methodology for conducting Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (AI Act Art.6(2)) developed by the Catalonian Data Protection Authority. The Agency held a workshop on conducting fundamental rights impact assessment which was led by the author of the guidelines.

items.title: Basics of AI Literacy - Understanding AI systems
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: State School for Public Administration introduced several AI literacy educations which are regularly implemented (four AI educations in September 2025). Description of the education module 'Understanding AI systems: 'i) basic terms risks and harms ii) problems from practice iii) ethics and principles of use legal framework and standards iv) responsible persons high-risk systems and other risk categories v) risk management system privacy policies use policies cybersecurity policies vi) personal data protection'.

items.title: Vouchers for adult education programs focused on AI skills
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) enables EU Member States to access grants and loans through their national recovery and resilience plans in order to finance reforms and investments that accelerate economic recovery and strengthen the resilience of the economy and society (Foreword p. 1). Under this framework the Government provides partial subsidies for green and digital upskilling and reskilling programmes for individuals in the labour market including AI-specific education programmes such as the application of artificial intelligence in business human resources and digital marketing as well as advanced AI specialist training. The Croatian Employment Service certifies education programs and issues vouchers.

body.name: Governing Board / the Ministry of Labour Pension System Family and Social Policy and the Croatian Employment Service

items.title: Open Book educational platform
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The MINERD Open Book platform utilizes an AI assistant to enhance AI literacy in K-12 education. Students learn to formulate questions interpret AI explanations and verify information. Teachers get AI-supported lesson ideas. This initiative promotes responsible AI use critical inquiry feedback skills and understanding AI limitations. It also expands equitable AI access aligning with ENIA's goals for curriculum integration and teacher upskilling in AI-enhanced learning.

items.title: Climate Change Monitoring in National Parks Based on Information and Communication Technologies (ICT)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: This government-led initiative utilizes an estimated US$6 million budget to enhance real-time environmental monitoring. The project leverages remote sensing CCTV mobile applications and artificial intelligence to identify wildfires monitor critical species and manage watershed and coastal ecosystems within protected areas demonstrating the application of AI in environmental protection. It matches the plan to create and open ecological/climate datasets for research and management (p 56).

items.title: SARA Automated Response and Attention System
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: SARA addresses gender equality in AI by using an AI chatbot to lower barriers for women and girls facing gender-based violence. It provides guidance on recognizing abuse shares contacts for shelters legal and psychological support and connects users to the *212 emergency line. It acts as a first discreet point of contact rather than a replacement for authorities. This government-led deployment operationalizes AI for protection and access to rights expanding timely information and referral pathways for survivors

items.title: Women in science technology and innovation key to economic empowerment and equality in Latin America and the Caribbean Panel
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Led by the Ministry of Women this initiative advances gender equality in AI by promoting women’s participation retention and leadership in science technology and innovation and by urging policies that prevent AI from reproducing inequalities. It calls for women’s inclusion in AI decision-making removal of barriers like stereotypes and discrimination and wider access to the benefits of emerging technologies. High-level engagement links these goals to concrete public agendas and investments that expand women’s pathways into AI education jobs and leadership.

items.title: Special Bill on work in digital platforms for passenger transport
items.justification: A special Bill on work in digital ride-hailing platforms is currently under review by a Senate special commission. This proposed legislation aims to establish a specific legal framework for platform drivers guaranteeing their labor and social security rights while promoting fair competition with traditional transport services. By bringing gig workers under enforceable protections the law directly addresses AI-mediated algorithmic management. The bill still under committee review reportedly includes provisions for a minimum wage mandatory enrollment in social insurance and pension contributions for drivers. These represent key labor protections for workers managed by platform algorithms.

items.title: Public Procurement Information System
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: On 18 March 2025 the Dirección General de Contrataciones Públicas (DGCP) launched a new Public Procurement Information System integrating big data and AI tools. The “ParticipaYa RD” component uses AI to generate summaries of procurement requirements while “DataCompras RD” and “Datos Abiertos” enhance transparency and access to contracts and datasets. This initiative operationalizes AI within procurement processes strengthens transparency oversight and participation and advances Objectives 2.1.4 and 2.1.7 of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Dominican Republic.

items.title: Ecuador launches 10000 AI scholarships thanks to cooperation with the United Arab Emirates
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Ecuadorian government in coordination with the Secretariat of Higher Education Science Technology and Innovation (Senescyt) the Ministry of Telecommunications and the Information Society (Mintel) and the Ministry of Education (Mineduc) launched a program offering 10000 scholarships for AI prompters. The program aims to train young Ecuadorians between the ages of 18 and 29 years and 11 months in the use of AI tools and techniques. Topics covered include AI fundamentals prompt engineering prompts for chatbots (ChatGPT Copilot Gemini; handling illusions) AI for productivity (automation in HR marketing finance and programming) and creativity with AI (art music video; DALL·E Midjourney and Runway ML).

items.title: Public Algorithms and Algorithmic Transparency in Ecuador
items.justification: In 2024 a joint study between civil society and government was conducted to highlight the transparency of algorithms in government systems that make automated decisions and their use. It was carried out by Fundapi in conjunction with the Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Society and the Ombudsman's Office. Following a conceptual introduction on page 9 the document explains the legal framework under which the Transparency Law establishes the obligation of algorithm transparency in Ecuador's public sector. Then on page 11 it presents the methodology used and from page 14 onward the results of the survey on algorithmic transparency in the public sector are presented.

items.title: Digilians Initiative
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Digilians Initiative launched by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology is a fully-funded scholarship program designed to boost Egypt’s ICT sector by equipping youth (ages 18–32) from any academic background with essential tech skills and soft skills. It partners with the Egyptian Military Academy and leading tech companies (such as Google Microsoft Cisco IBM and AWS). The initiative offers four educational tracks: a four-month Nanodegree a nine-month Specialized Diploma a 12-month Professional Master and a 24-month MSc covering areas such as AI/data science. items.title: PROVISIONS RELATING TO THE IMPLEMENTATION OF AI AND TECHNOLOGIES
items.justification: The creation of the AI National Agency (ANIA) is established in Art 7 of the Law. This Agency has issued a provision requiring systems registered with the Agency—whether voluntarily or because they operate in mandatory sectors such as health biometrics or security—to operate and incorporate bias testing and equity assessments.  According to Article 4 (Definitions) of the Law bias is defined as any systematic error in the outcomes of an AI system that disproportionately favors or disadvantages certain groups or individuals including when gender is among the relevant characteristics.  Furthermore Art 15 of the Provisions establishes that systems registered with ANIA must conduct algorithmic impact assessments that include bias impact.

Since October 2024 it has had an agreement with GBM the technology company that represents IBM in the country to offer a course on Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals with IBM through ESIT's virtual training platform. The government press release stresses that“disinformation manipulation and deepfakes” threaten security and highlights critical thinking and digital skills to resist information-influence operations. The 2024 programme includes sessions like the National Library’s “Outsmart AI” and “Stumbling over fake news”classes which teach pupils to detect AI-generated texts images and deepfakes. The Week continues in 2025 with AI-themed seminars and school activities showing it is an ongoing mechanism to build resilience to AI-mediated misinformation.

items.title: Decision No MED-2024-150 of November 15 2024 (Formal Notice to Ministry of Interior)
items.justification: This initiative constitutes a 'corrective order' where the CNIL exercised its remedial power to stop a rights violation. By issuing Decision No. MED-2024-150 the CNIL formally ordered the Ministry of the Interior to cease the illegal use of facial recognition in the BriefCam software. This serves as a direct state-based non-judicial remedy effectively halting the infringing conduct (illegal biometric surveillance) and enforcing the public's right to protection against unlawful algorithmic processing as mandated by the GDPR and the Data Protection Act.

items.title: Arcom Technical Framework on Age Verification
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Arcom 'Référentiel' (October 2024) establishes technical standards for age verification systems to protect minors from online pornography explicitly referencing the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and the 'best interests of the child' (p. 7). It specifically regulates AI-driven solutions ('machine learning' p. 12) mandating they minimize discriminatory biases to ensure equal effectiveness across all demographics (pp. 12-13). The standards also require robustness against AI-enabled circumvention risks like 'deepfakes' (p. 11) and enforcing 'double anonymity' to protect user privacy (pp. 14-18).

items.title: Designation of national competent authorities (AI Act)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: This initiative operationalises the EU AI Act by designating the national bodies responsible for its enforcement. These authorities are tasked with enforcing the Act's legally binding non-discrimination provisions. For example they will oversee high-risk AI systems used in employment (Annex III) to ensure compliance with bias mitigation rules. They will also enforce prohibition on discriminatory biometric categorisation based on sexual orientation directly addressing gender equality by providing a mechanism to protect against bias.

items.title: Designation of National Competent Authorities
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: This initiative operationalises the EU AI Act in France by designating the specific national authorities (CNIL DGCCRF DGE etc.) responsible for its enforcement. The EU AI Act framework which these bodies now oversee directly mandates human oversight measures. Specifically the Act requires that high-risk AI systems be designed and developed in a way that allows them to be effectively overseen by natural persons. This initiative thus creates the national mechanism responsible for enforcing the framework's human oversight requirements.

items.title: Designation of National Competent Authorities
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: This initiative designates the authorities (DGCCRF and CNIL) responsible for overseeing the Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments (FRIA) mandated by Article 27 of the EU AI Act. By appointing these bodies as market surveillance authorities France establishes the institutional mechanism to receive and review these assessments. Specifically deployers of high-risk AI must notify these authorities of their impact assessment results. This designation ensures that the mandatory evaluation of risks to fundamental rights is not just a paperwork exercise but is subject to official regulatory oversight and enforcement.

It ensures oversight of high-risk AI systems used for recruitment promotion termination and worker management (Annex III(4)) monitoring compliance with risk management (Art. 9) bias control (Art. 10) and human oversight (Art. 14) obligations. Additionally it enforces the ban on emotion recognition in the workplace (Art. 5(1)(f)) and ensures deployers fulfill their duty to inform workers subject to high-risk AI systems (Art. 26(11)).

items.justification: This official guide serves as the operational standard for implementing the transparency obligations of Article L. 312-1-3. It provides a step-by-step methodology for public administrations to identifying their algorithms inventory them and publish the required information. Specifically the section 'L'obligation de transparence' details the legal scope while the section 'Comment expliquer ?' provides technical and editorial guidelines for publishing source code and writing intelligible explanations to ensure effective public disclosure.

items.justification: This report constitutes a monitoring and evaluation mechanism assessing the implementation of transparency obligations (CRPA). Part III (pp. 28-39) specifically addresses 'Transparency' noting that the obligation to publish rules defining main algorithmic systems often remains a 'dead letter' (p. 37 ). It identifies failures in public disclosure (p. 37 ) and formulates recommendations to enforce these rules such as establishing a national census of compliance and introducing sanctions for administrations that fail to publish their algorithmic rules (p. 37 ).
