items.justification: This initiative addresses the procurement of Artificial Intelligence by establishing a simplified legal mechanism that allows public buyers to award contracts up to 100000 euros without advertising or competitive bidding for 'innovative works supplies or services.' The definition of innovation used explicitly covers new or significantly improved implementations which directly applies to Artificial Intelligence solutions. By removing complex administrative barriers the initiative aims to facilitate the integration of digital technologies from startups and Small and Medium-sized Enterprises into the public sector encouraging the state to act as a 'first customer' for emerging tech.

items.title: State Buyer - Key Figures 2024
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The report actively monitors 'The development of innovation procurement' (p. 5) which serves as the primary mechanism for acquiring AI solutions. It explicitly tracks expenditure on 'start-ups' (€498M across 1305 entities since 2023) and 'innovative SMEs' (9% of 2024 spend) quantifying the state's engagement with the ecosystem developing AI . Furthermore it isolates 'Information technology' as a major spending category (€4.26B) (p. 3) and identifies top digital suppliers often involved in AI services such as Capgemini Technology and Thales Digital Services (p. 4).

items.title: Innovation Rendezvous AI and Public Procurement
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative is a targeted matchmaking event organised by the State Procurement Department (DAE) to facilitate the Public Procurement of AI. Titled 'Innovation Rendezvous: Artificial Intelligence and Public Procurement' it connects government buyers with the tech ecosystem to meet 'priority procurement needs' specifically in 'artificial intelligence' [p. 2]. By focusing exclusively on AI (alongside cybersecurity and real estate) the session functions as a specialised platform for public purchasers to identify and source innovative AI solutions directly from the market [p. 2].

items.title: Public Digital Campus (Campus du Numrique Public)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative is a centralized government platform specifically designed to upskill the entire French civil service ('agents publics'). Managed by the Interministerial Directorate for Digital Affairs (DINUM) it addresses skills development by aggregating and creating digital training programs. Crucially it features a dedicated 'Data and Artificial Intelligence' category offering specific modules like 'Discover Generative AI' (co-produced with Inria Academy). This directly implements the national mandate to 'massify' AI literacy and equip state employees with the technical competencies required for public sector transformation.

body.name: Directorate General for Administration and the Civil Service (DGAFP) Interministerial Digital Directorate (DINUM)

items.title: JUST fAIr Project
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The JUST fAIr project directly addresses public sector skills development by providing a structured 24-month training program led by the National School for the Judiciary (ENM). It aims to bridge the 'digital gap' among justice professionals (magistrates clerks and lawyers) through 'acculturation' and technical training.

items.title: Compte Personnel de Formation (Personal Training Account)
items.justification: The Compte Personnel de Formation (CPF) is a government-managed financing mechanism that credits a dedicated budget (in Euros) to every active worker's account for autonomous training purchase. The platform functions as the official national marketplace enabling workers to directly search for book and pay for eligible training courses aimed at skills adaptation including digital and technical skills required for the evolving labor market.

body.name: France comptences (France Skills) Oprateurs de comptences (Skills Operators)

items.title: Comptences et Mtiers dAvenir (Skills and Jobs of the Future)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: This France 2030 initiative funds training projects to meet the skills needs of 'jobs of the future' specifically targeting the 'digital' (numérique) and 'STEM' sectors. It aims to train 400000 people per year and 1 million new graduates by 2030. The call funds 'training schemes' (dispositifs de formation) for both 'initial and continuous' training (reskilling). Crucially it mandates that projects be carried out by a 'consortium' composed of employers (enterprises) and training organizations (universities schools) ensuring partnerships to develop curricula adapted to sovereign needs.

body.name: Secrtariat gnral pour linvestissement (General Secretariat for Investment) (SGPI) Coordinateur national pour lintelligence artificielle (National AI Coordinator)

items.title: Designation of National Competent Authorities
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The designation of these national authorities is the primary mechanism for enforcing the EU AI Act in France. The AI Act itself contains core provisions on safety and security specifically requiring high-risk AI systems to be designed with appropriate levels of accuracy robustness and cybersecurity and to be resilient against errors or malicious attacks (Article 15). These designated bodies are responsible for monitoring compliance with these technical standards and taking corrective action against unsafe or unreliable AI systems thus directly implementing the framework's safety and security objectives.

items.title: Designation of National Competent Authorities
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: France designated independent authorities to enforce the AI Act under Art. 70 justifying the 'Independent' qualification. The CNIL (Data Protection Authority) oversees high-risk systems (biometrics employment) and prohibited practices leveraging its autonomous sanctioning powers. The Arcom (Audiovisual Regulator) supervises transparency for GenAI and deepfakes (Art. 50). Unlike government ministries these bodies operate with statutory independence to protect fundamental rights like privacy and freedom of communication.

body.name: Direction gnrale de la concurrence de la consommation et de la rpression des fraudes (DGCCRF) (General Directorate for Competition Policy Consumer Affairs and Fraud Control) Commission nationale de linformatique et des liberts (CNIL) (National Commission on Informatics and Liberty) Direction Gnrale des Entreprises (DGE) (Directorate General for Enterprise) Agence nationale de la scurit des systmes dinformation (ANSSI) (National Cybersecurity Agency of France) Ple dexpertise de la rgulation numrique (PEREN) (Digital Platform Expertise Hub)

items.title: Train the Trainers workshop at the University of The Gambia
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Organised by the Commonwealth Secretariat and the Commonwealth Artificial Intelligence Consortium (CAIC) (of which The Gambia is the lead for the Working Group on Research and Innovation for the CAIC) university educators were trained in Python Programming and Artificial Intelligence (AI) at the University of Gambia. Lead government agency: Ministry of Trade Regional Integration and Employment. The Minister noted that “This initiative not only empowers our educators but also ensures that our youth who are at the forefront of AI development are well-prepared for future workforce opportunities.'

body.name: The Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy (MoCDE) and the Gambia ICT Agency (GICTA)

items.title: Conference on the growing role of AI (AI) in the classroom
items.justification: The conference organized by Africa Mission Global (AMG) in partnership with the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education aimed to demystify AI for educators and equip them with basic tools to integrate it into their teaching methods. The conference was aimed at clearing up misconceptions around AI explain its uses and also talk about the risks of over-reliance on machines and the ethics of AI in youth education.

body.name: The Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy (MoCDE) and the Gambia ICT Agency (GICTA)

items.title: Nationwide campaign against misinformation and disinformation
items.justification: The Ministry of Information Media and Broadcasting Services launched a nationwide campaign against misinformation and disinformation on January 24 2025. The campaign aims to raise public awareness about the dangers of false information promote responsible consumption of media publications and equip citizens with tools to identify and counter misinformation and disinformation. The relevant Minister noted at the launch that 'it is crucial that policymakers legislators and people in all walks of life are equipped with the necessary tools and knowledge to address artificially-generated disinformation and misinformation”. The awareness tour started on the 31st of January to different areas of the Gambia and seems to be ongoing.

body.name: National Cybersecurity Coordination Directorate

items.title: Communication Commission held media literacy olympiad for the second time
items.justification: The Media Literacy Olympiad organised by gov entity - the Communications Commission is focused specifically on the theme “AI and Disinformation.

items.title: The National Bank of Georgia Launches a Pilot Project for an AI Sandbox within its Regulatory Laboratory
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The initiative does not explicitly focus on fairness and non-discrimination but aims to ensure a safe regulated and customer-centered financial ecosystem which implicitly includes these TCs as well

body.name: National Bank of Georgia

items.title: The National Bank of Georgia Launches a Pilot Project for an AI Sandbox within its Regulatory Laboratory
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The initiative does not explicitly focus on impact assessments but aims to ensure a safe regulated and customer-centered financial ecosystem which implicitly includes impact assessments as well. Under the supervision of the National Bank sandbox participants will work on the development of new ideas and initiatives. Following the preparation and analysis of proposed concepts their gradual testing will be carried out within a regulated trusted and controlled environment.

body.name: National Bank of Georgia

items.title: The National Bank of Georgia Launches a Pilot Project for an AI Sandbox within its Regulatory Laboratory
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The initiative does not explicitly focus on safety and security but aims to ensure a safe regulated and customer-centered financial ecosystem which implicitly includes safety and security as well

body.name: National Bank of Georgia

items.title: AI in vocational education
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative builds AI literacy in vocational education by offering structured AI specialist-certified training under the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) project “AI B3” responding to reported skills shortages in AI technologies (Intro). For apprentices the “Additional qualification in AI” targets foundational understanding of AI’s relevance for their professional futures across sectors (section “Trainee”). For workers “AI Specialist (IHK)” develops applied competence (data ML evaluation of use cases) including ethical questions and basic programming.

body.name: Federal Ministries for Economic Affairs Ministry (BMWK) Research (BMBF) and Labour (BMAS)

items.title: German Digital Services Coordinator (DSC/BNetzA) commissioned study Gesellschaftliche Auswirkungen systemischer Risiken (DSA systemic-risk research)
items.justification: The DSC-commissioned study treats AI as an amplifier of disinformation and violence-related harms within DSA systemic-risk work: it notes that disinformation can be produced and spread using AI especially generative AI (incl. deepfakes) increasing scale quality and personalisation (Sec 4.4 pp. 28–32 Summary p.3). It links disinformation ecosystems to digital violence threats and extremist mobilisation contributing to radicalisation and violence (pp. 39–42; p. 70).

body.name: The Federal Network Agency Federal Agency for the Protection of Children and Young Persons and Federal Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information

items.title: DSK (The German Data Protection Conference) Working Group on AI (AK KI)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The The German Data Protection Conference (DSK) formally established its dedicated Working Group on Artificial Intelligence (Arbeitskreis KI) in late 2024. This working group coordinates the legal and technical expertise of all federal and state DPAs. This initiative is a structural action to enhance the capacity of Germany’s federal and state data protection authorities to process AI-related complaints under Article 77 GDPR.

body.name: BfDI (Federal Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information) 16 Lnder data protection authorities

items.title: DSK Guidance on Technical and Organisational Measures for AI
items.justification: The DSK guidance embeds intervenability so that affected persons can seek redress. It defines intervenability as the ability of controllers to intervene across the lifecycle to implement data-subject rights and authorities’ orders (p. 7). It requires that outputs can be questioned and traced by users/human controllers with corresponding functions provided (p. 16). At deployment authorities must document human intervention options and data-subject rights (p. 19). In operation it prescribes human-control measures (pending state mandatory human confirmation periodic release) to enable timely intervention (pp. 22–23).

body.name: BfDI (Federal Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information) 16 Lnder data protection authorities

items.title: BNetzA Service Desk
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: BNetzA’s function as national market-surveillance authority enables prevention detection and sanctioning of unlawful AI that affects children. Its Single Point of Contact/Service Desk and surveillance powers provide a route for complaints and corrective action where minors could be harmed. The draft KIMUG bill BNetzA must involve the Federal Agency for Child and Youth Media Protection (BzKJ) whenever an AI system impacts minors.

body.name: Federal Network Agency State Media Authorities and Federal Data Protection Authority

items.title: The AI Language Proficiency Monitor
items.justification: The German government developed the AI Language Proficiency Monitor jointly between the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) development agency GIZ and the German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI) (p.1). The AI Language Proficiency Monitor tracks the performance of LLMs in up to 200 languages with a strong focus on low-resource languages (p.1 Abstract). Its overall aim is to help support private- and public-sector decision-making with a 'particular emphasis on underserved communities' (p.1). More information (https://slator.com/german-gov-backed-ai-benchmark-tracks-large-language-models-200-languages/)

body.name: The AI Observatory on AI in Work and Society (KI-Observatorium)

items.title: Energy Efficiency Register for Data Centers (RZReg)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: Managed by the Federal Energy Efficiency Center (BfEE) (part of Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA)) this digital register collects mandatory annual data on energy consumption power usage effectiveness (PUE) and renewable energy use from approximately 1000 data centers. The first reporting cycles were completed in 2024 and 2025.

body.name: Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA)

items.title: Official implementation support for data-centre duties (FAQ) BAFA + BMWK
items.justification: The Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK)  and Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA) creates resources such as FAQs to address environmental impact for AI by operationalising EnEfG duties for data centres which host AI compute. It explains mandatory public reporting of energy metrics via the national register under (Q “How and where… published?” p. 3) compliance with renewable electricity requirements under (Q on certificates/PPAs pp. 3–4) and the obligation to implement an energy or environmental management system (ISO 50001/EMAS) under (Q 'Is a data centre operator...' p. 4). Also federal funding programmes for energy-efficiency (p.5 from 'Are there any federal funding programs...')

body.name: Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA)

items.title: National AI Act market-surveillance authority (BNetzA)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: BNetzA serves as Germany’s central market-surveillance authority for the EU AI Act. In this role it supervises compliance with provisions that curb discriminatory outcomes including the ban on exploitative practices and the high-risk obligations on risk management data governance transparency and human oversight that apply to areas such as employment and education. BNetzA can receive complaints demand corrective measures and impose sanctions for non-compliance providing a concrete enforcement route for fairness and non-discrimination in AI.

body.name: AI Office European AI Board

items.title: AI Observatory
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The AI Observatory (BMAS 2020) conducts research and develops indicators for the Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the German Federal Government of which includes gender in AI. These studies integrate gender perspectives into monitoring and policy evidence. However the Observatory’s role remains analytical and advisory; it does not impose obligations or corrective mechanisms to address gender discrimination in AI.

body.name: EU AI Office and the BundesNetzAgentur on the national level

items.title: AI Campus AI power for women 45+
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: “AI Power for Women 45+” builds AI literacy skills and confidence among mid-career and later-career women a group underrepresented in AI and data roles. By offering accessible practice-oriented modules (e.g. understanding AI systems risks and responsible use) it lowers entry barriers to AI-related upskilling and employability broadens the talent pipeline beyond traditional STEM channels and enables informed participation in AI adoption and oversight. The course directly aims to combat age and gender discrimination.

body.name: EU AI Office and the BundesNetzAgentur on the national level

items.title: Decisions of the 34th Conference of Ministers Senatorsand Ministers for Equality and Womens Affairs of the Lnder (GMFK Resolution)
items.justification: This GFMK resolution calls on the federal government to embed gender equality into AI Act implementation. The 2024 GFMK resolution on gender-responsive digitalisation recognises that AI systems can reproduce and amplify structural gender biases through skewed data opaque algorithms and automated decision making in areas such as employment welfare and policing. The resolution calls on the federal government to embed gender equality and non-discrimination into all procedures for implementing the EU AI Act including risk assessment testing standards and an AI register for public-sector systems so that gendered harms are identified prevented and remedied.

body.name: EU AI Office and the BundesNetzAgentur on the national level

items.title: Mandated AI Regulatory Sandboxes
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Ministerial Draft Bill (Sept 2025) on p. 13 Section 4 mandates a national AI Regulatory Sandbox (KI-Reallabor). This can be considered a formal government action that commits to a programmatic structure and is a direct implementation of Article 57 of the EU AI Act. This program forces providers of high-risk AI systems to develop and test under regulatory supervision. This enforces Art. 14 of the EU AI Act for Human Oversight by ensuring systems can be stopped and its operations are fully traceable (Art. 12 logging) before being released.

body.name: AI Office European AI Board Bundesnetzagentur (BNetzA)

items.title: BMWK (Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Change) AI Regulatory Sandboxes Portal
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The BMWK's (Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Change) Regulatory Sandboxes Innovation Portal provides a controlled environment for companies to test and refine their AI systems. The section 'International Pioneers and the European Framework' states sandboxes are now 'anchored in various legal acts such as the EU AI Act.' The AI Regulatory Sandbox as established by the AI Act under Art. 57 is designed to be the practical implementation mechanism that supports the regulatory compliance obligations of the Impact Assessments in Art. 57 of the EU AI Act. The sandbox helps deployers practice and document their full EU AI Act obligations including the effective execution and reporting of their FRIA prior to market deployment.

body.name: BundesnetzAgentur (Federal Network Agency BNetzA)

items.title: AI Cockpit Project Human oversight and control of AI at work
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The AI Cockpit is financed by the BMAS (Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs) Think Tank “Digital Working Society”. Its premise is that workers and employers must be able to understand supervise and steer AI used on the job to maintain transparency and control in line with a human-in-command model. It is designed to give employees clear insight into an AI system’s outputs so they can make informed judgements on when to intervene in automated processes. Ex: Study 1 addresses the monitoring of AI in personnel selection by providing tools for HR departments and works councils to scrutinise algorithmic filtering. The software is available in 2 editions to support AI deployments that comply with the requirements of the EU AI Act.

body.name: EU AI Office Bundesnetzagentur

items.title: BAuA (Federal Institute for Occupational Safety & Health) AI Workshop 2024 Research Regulation Working World
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: A day-long workshop hosted by the Federal Institute for Occupational Safety & Health TU Dortmund University and the Lamarr Institute focused on trustworthy AI regulation and the workplace. The programme (p.5) addressed developments in AI research and the world of work like trustworthy AI systems and their integration into a human-centered work environment. Sessions such as ethical and legal challenges to align with the EU AI Act and balancing efficiency and ethics of AI in the workplace were held for the practical integration of AI into human-centered environments to tackle the legal safeguards required to protect employees' rights under the EU AI Act. (Program: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1WOWmGluHoqWCad-C9uULmz65kQAF5XMO/view).

body.name: EU AI Office Bundesnetzagentur

items.title: AI Opportunity Market (MaKI)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: Germany’s AI Opportunity Marketplace (MaKI) implements the Guidelines’ transparency principle by serving as a public AI transparency register for the federal administration offering an overview of AI systems used by authorities and their purposes. The federal IT Council formally endorsed MaKI as the central transparency register for the federal administration and the IT-Planning Council commissioned a pilot rollout to Länder and municipalities extending disclosure beyond the federal tier.

items.title: AI Opportunity Market (MaKI)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The AI Opportunity Market (MaKI) launched at www.kimarktplatz.bund.de serves as the federal administration's central marketplace and transparency database. It addresses procurement by providing a comprehensive overview of existing and planned AI systems (BMI Press Jan 2025). This initiative meets EU AI Act transparency mandates and streamlines government spending by facilitating the broader use of existing technical expertise across authorities. By acting as a pilot for state and local government inclusion in 2025 MaKI ensures that procurement is not fragmented promoting technological sovereignty and efficient resource utilisation while maintaining high ethical and transparency standards across the civil service.

body.name: Federal Ministries for Economic Affairs Ministry (BMWK) Research (BMBF) and Labour (BMAS)

items.title: AI B3 Project - AI Specialist (IHK) couse
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Funded by the Ministry of Education (BMBF) this initiative creates programs tailored to different target groups leading to 'AI Specialist' (IHK) certifications (p.4). Participants learn how processes can be improved and optimised through AI and to be able to assess the quality and benefits of different AI applications through modules on data handling data analysis basic programming knowledge machine learning and ethical challenges of AI. The project operationalises reskilling by creating certified occupation-oriented AI curricula delivered through IHK structures enabling workers to transition into AI-augmented roles.

body.name: Federal Ministries for Economic Affairs Ministry (BMWK) Research (BMBF) and Labour (BMAS)

items.title: BundesnetzAgentur (Federal Network Agency) AI Service Desk
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Federal Network Agency’s AI Service Desk acts as Germany’s single national intake and triage channel for AI-Act enquiries and complaints from providers deployers and the public. The AI Service Desk operationalises safety and security by guiding organisations on risk-based duties and routing cases into supervision. The portal explains the AI Act’s aim to safeguard health safety and fundamental rights outlines risk levels and high-risk systems and links to transparency obligations notification single point of contact and market surveillance functions. This chain operationalises risk controls testing and incident response.

body.name: Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur BNetzA)

items.title: DIN/DKE National mirror committee of CEN/CLC/JTC 21
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: DIN and DKE established a mirror committee of CEN/CLC/JTC 21 for German experts to contribute to the operationalisation of the AI Act's technical specifications including requirements in Art. 12 on explainability and Art. 13 on transparency. The development of the standard 'Record keeping:built-in logging capabilities in AI systems' defines the technical specifications and auditable log formats for tracing system operations and verifying outputs for high-risk AI systems (Art. 12). The standard 'Transparency and information to the users of AI systems' mandates technical requirements for clear Instructions for Use and detailed information disclosure about the system's capabilities limitations and expected accuracy to deployers (Art. 13).

body.name: Bundesnetzagentur (BNetzA)

items.title: Mission KI
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: A key pillar of Mission KI is to foster the development of transparent and explainable AI ensuring compatibility with the EU AI Act’s requirements for high-risk AI systems. The initiative creates assets and knowledge capacity such as the voluntary Mission KI Quality Standard and webinars on transparency in AI.

body.name: Bundesnetzagentur (BNetzA)

items.title: Public Alert on Cybersecurity Authoritys Website AI-Generated Videos (Deepfake) Promoting Fake Investments and Drugs
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This official government advisory from the Cybersecurity Authority addresses AI-facilitated misinformation through deepfake impersonation by outlining threat actor methods and providing guidance on prevention reporting and enforcement. By educating the public on recognizing and reporting deepfakes and detailing authority responses the advisory helps mitigate AI-enabled misinformation and related harms.

items.title: The Data Protection Commission Is the oversight Body
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The Data Protection Commission represents individuals in Ghana by scrutinizing organizations that hold collect and store personal data in their possession. They ensure institutions process personal data in a fair transparent secure manner and abide by the principles set out in the law to enable them to meet their accountability obligation to the public.

body.name: Data Protection Commission

items.title: Privacy awareness campaign themed Privacy is Personal
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The DPC’s public awareness campaigns promote Human Oversight and Determination by educating individuals and organisations about their rights under the Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843) including the right to human review of automated decisions. By raising awareness of these rights the campaigns enable people to intervene contest and seek human oversight of AI-driven decisions ensuring accountability and transparency.

body.name: Data Protection Commission

items.title: Enforcement Drive Against Privacy Violations
items.justification: This initiative was to clamp down on organisations misusing user data

body.name: Data Protection Commission

items.title: Readiness Assessment Measurement (RAM)- Ethical Use Of AI Launched
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Readiness Assessment Measurement (RAM) - Ethical Use of AI promotes transparency and explainability by evaluating how AI systems in Ghana align with ethical principles such as accountability fairness and openness. It guides institutions to adopt standards and self-assessment tools that ensure AI decisions are understandable and traceable.

items.title: Government of Ghana and UNDP Kicks Off Ministerial Bootcamp to strengthen AI Capacity and Advance AI-enabled Public Services
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Ministerial AI Bootcamp promotes transparency and explainability by training government leaders to understand AI systems’ design decision-making and governance processes. It builds capacity to evaluate and oversee AI use in public services ensuring responsible adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across the public sector.

items.title: Actions to Strengthen Active Citizenship - AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The Ministry of Education Religious Affairs and Sports launched the “Artificial Intelligence” program for B’ Gymnasium students. It introduces learners to AI principles through STEM methodology and hands-on workshops combining machine learning ethics and critical thinking. The program includes 7 teaching hours using the 5E model (Engage Explore Explain Elaborate Evaluate) and fosters digital literacy creativity and teamwork supporting equitable AI literacy nationwide.

body.name: Special Secretariat for AI and Data Governance

items.title: Meltemi - Open Source Bilingual Greek Large Language Model
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The 'Meltemi' initiative directly supports Cultural and Linguistic Diversity by developing an open source bilingual Greek Large Language Model that strengthens the digital representation of the Greek language and culture. Led and trained by the Institute for Language and Speech Processing of the Athena Research Center the project represents a government-backed effort to create AI tools based on Greek language datasets. By addressing linguistic gaps in global AI ecosystems dominated by English centric models Meltemi promotes inclusive access to AI technologies for Greek speaking users researchers and institutions.

body.name: Special Secretariat for AI and Data Governance

items.title: Conference AI Environment & Natural Disasters
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The conference “AI Environment & Natural Disasters” organised by the Region of Western Macedonia in cooperation with the Ministry of Digital Governance constitutes an implementation-oriented initiative aligned with the Blueprint. It operationalises the framework’s priorities on AI for climate resilience and civil protection as outlined in Chapter 6 (“AI and the State”) particularly the sections on Civil Protection and Climate Change (p. 114-118) which promote the use of AI for disaster prevention risk management and environmental protection. The event translated these strategic objectives into applied use cases knowledge exchange and public-sector dialogue supporting real-world deployment of AI for sustainability.

body.name: Special Secretariat for AI and Data Governance

items.title: Chatbot mAIgov
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The initiative introduces mAIgov the first public-sector AI “Digital Assistant” on gov.gr designed to simplify citizens’ interaction with the state by providing information on procedures and services. Public disclosure is ensured through the “Terms of use mAIgov” which explains how the system operates its Microsoft Azure OpenAI basis the use of open gov.gr data; its informational and non–decision-making nature its beta status data-protection safeguards and the Ministry of Digital Governance as the responsible operator.

body.name: High Level Advisory Committee for AI

items.title: Microsoft Civil Servants Academy
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative directly supports Public Sector Skills Development by delivering large-scale role-specific training in cloud and AI technologies for civil servants. Through the Microsoft Civil Servants Academy 2.000 public employees will be trained and certified in the period May - July 2025 covering both foundational and specialized AI skills. The partnership between the Ministry of Interior Ministry of Digital Governance EKDDA and Microsoft creates a sustainable pipeline of certified trainers within the public sector enabling ongoing upskilling and strengthening the operational readiness of public organizations.

body.name: Digital Transformation Executive Network National Coalition for Digital Skills and Jobs

items.title: PHAROS AI Factory Training Series
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The PHAROS AI Factory Training Series supports national reskilling and upskilling in AI by offering free government backed courses to professionals researchers in all fields developers AI ML & LLM experts. PHAROS AI Factory is Greece’s national initiative funded by the Ministry of Digital Governance and the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking (JU) to accelerate AI innovation and workforce readiness. The courses 'Machine Learning Fundamentals' and 'Introduction to HPC' provided practical training in data analysis model evaluation and access to EU supercomputing resources.

body.name: Special Secretariat for AI and Data Governance

items.title: Scientific Conference AI & Cybersecurity From the Present to the Future with Safety
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This scientific conference organized by the Ministry of Digital Governance the National Cybersecurity Authority and local government associations addresses AI Safety and Security by promoting awareness and capacity-building in AI risk management data protection and cyber-resilience within public administration. Sessions led by the Minister of Digital Governance and the Deputy Director of the National Cybersecurity Authority emphasized safeguards reliability and secure AI deployment in line with EU principles for trustworthy AI.

body.name: Data Protection Authority Ombudsman Authority for Communications Privacy National Human Rights Commission

items.title: Ia un atelier de formation programm en faveur des professionnels de mdias guinens
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: An AI training and awareness workshop for media professionals was organized in May 2025 focusing on the responsible use of AI tools ethical issues and best practices for digital and AI technologies. While organized by professional associations this event operates in close cooperation with national stakeholders and highlights skills building around AI understanding

items.title: ICT-Haiti-BRH Initiative Aims to Boost Human Capital
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative aimed at strengthening digital skills in the country is being carried out in partnership with several universities specializing in technology. Key areas of training include cybersecurity database analysis networking and artificial intelligence. The rationale is to meet tech demands in the financial sector and protect digital infrastructure

items.title: ICT-Haiti-BRH Initiative Aims to Boost Human Capital
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The TIC-Haïti-BRH program launched on January 24 2025 is a government-funded initiative that directly targets the broader national workforce specifically university students and youth rather than just public sector employees. The program is a partnership with four major universities (UEH-FDS ISTEAH UNITECH ESIH) designed to 'improve the employability of youth' and create a specialized talent pool for 'several sectors of the national economy' including the private sector. It addresses the indicator by providing free high-level reskilling in Artificial Intelligence and cybersecurity to the general public to bridge the national digital skills gap.  Ref press article shared above.

items.title: Teacher Training on the Use of AI in the Classroom
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This training initiative is organized by the Ministry of Education and the teachers' union Colegio de Profesores de Educación Media de Honduras. The workshop is 20 hours long and focuses on training secondary-level teachers in the use of AI for classroom management and to improve classroom learning and digital competencies. It is an entry-level training.

items.title: NAIH Data Protection Authority Procedure and Investigation Mechanisms (Complaint & Public Interest Notification Processes)
items.justification: The  National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information's complaint and investigation procedures provide state-based avenues for individuals to seek remedy for harms arising from automated or AI-driven personal data processing. Through the GDPR-aligned authority procedure for data subjects and public-interest investigation procedure for others individuals can challenge unlawful automated decisions request corrective action and trigger regulatory oversight. The initiative operationalizes GDPR rights related to transparency contestation and redress in AI contexts.

body.name: The National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information

items.title: Union Government issues advisory to social media intermediaries to identify misinformation and Deepfakes
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The advisory issued by the Union Government implements gender equality by targeting harms that disproportionately affect women notably deepfakes and explicitly anchors these obligations in the IT rules. It requires intermediaries to identify and remove such content within 36 hours reiterates legal consequences for non-compliance under the IT rules (including Rule 7) and enables affected individuals to seek remedies.

items.title: Grievance Appellate Committee Workshop
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: In January 2023 the government appointed Grievance Appellate Committee GACs and since then the GACs have received over 2300 appeals of which 2081 are resolved. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) organized a workshop on the Grievance Appellate Committee (GAC) on 7th January 2025 to discuss strengthening the grievance redressal framework under the Information Technology Act 2000. The government urged social media intermediaries to act quickly against fake content to build public trust in grievance officers. It was also emphasized that GACs must work efficiently to resolve issues promptly ensuring users can navigate the internet safely and with confidence.

items.justification: AIIS 2024 is designed as a collaborative platform for key stakeholders of the Indonesian AI ecosystem—including government industry academia media and community organizations—to showcase and exchange innovative research technological and industrial products policy perspectives and strategic insights related to artificial intelligence. AIIS 2024 explicitly supports AI Literacy by providing structured forums such as panel discussions workshops and keynote sessions that focus on increasing public and professional understanding of AI concepts ethical considerations responsible use of AI and real-world applications across sectors. These sessions are aimed not only at AI practitioners but also at policymakers educators students.

It promotes the idea of “AI for everyone” by including modules such as “Basic AI” “Generative AI” and “Responsible AI” – covering concepts like how AI works how to use AI tools to boost productivity how to craft effective prompts and how to apply AI responsibly.

items.title: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs Press Release No 150/HM-KKD/08/2025 AI Roadmap and Draft Presidential Regulation on Digital Security to Enter Public Consultation Soon
items.type: Policy Development — Launching consultations or stakeholder workshops to gather input for a future draft.
items.justification: Based on the Press Release Mr. Edwin Hidayat Abdullah Director General of Digital Ecosystems at the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs stated that the government is preparing two accompanying legal instruments under the same decree: the White Paper on the National AI Roadmap and guidelines on AI safety and security. The Concept for AI Ethical Guideline  mentioned an element of disinformation as risk (p. 9). The next process is that the government will carry out public consultations on the initial draft of the AI Roadmap then the draft that has been prepared will be sent to the Ministry of State Secretariat with 7 working groups involved and each time the discussion was followed quite enthusiastically.

items.title: AI Friend or Foe?An Analysis of How AI Could Impact Irelands Labour Market
items.justification: To establish a proactive framework for labor protection the report provides an evidentiary basis for quantifying Ireland’s significant labor market exposure to AI (63%) which exceeds the international average for advanced economies (60%) identifying a heightened potential for structural displacement. By pinpointing 'at-risk' occupations especifically the 38% of females in high-exposure low-complementarity roles and the 38% of bachelor's degree holders in vulnerable positions the analysis functions as a critical diagnostic tool for anticipating job losses and safeguarding worker security (Pg 17).

items.title: Key Principles for Evaluating AI-Driven Interventional Trials
items.justification: This mandatory guideline (Key Principles for Evaluating AI-Driven Interventional Trials) sets the standards IRBs must apply when approving research. It advances gender equality by requiring evaluation of model performance across sub-populations—including gender—to detect and mitigate bias (p. 7). Although it provides no data itself it operationalizes practices that promote gender-equal AI assessment.

items.title: National Program for AI
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Supervision & Appeal Mechanisms: Section 4.2.1 ('What is Human Involvement?') details specific oversight structures including 'Human-on-the-loop' (supervision with intervention authority) and 'Appeal' (retrospective human review of a system's decision).Automation Bias: Section 4.2 explicitly warns against 'Automation/Machine bias' and the 'computer says no' phenomenon where humans adopt system recommendations without independent judgment.Strategic Implementation: Section 4.2 states that regulators must determine 'when human involvement should be required' based on two main contexts: ethical (protecting human dignity) and utilitarian (preventing technological failures).
