items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Section 1.3 (Principles) Page 3: Human-centric approach.Section 4.1.1 (Human Oversight) Page 8: Specific oversight mechanisms.Section 5.2 (Implementation) Page 12: Professional responsibility.

items.title: Call for Proposals 20 Submission of Applications for Support in Government AI-Based Projects on the Nimbus Infrastructure
items.justification: Following the publication of the Public Sector Guide the Ministry of Innovation published an internal call for proposals to government offices for procurement. The standards of the AI Public Sector Guide were an integral part of the application.

items.title: AI Trainings Senior Staff 2025
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: This initiative addresses skills development by enforcing a mandatory strategic shift from theory to practice. Based on a Prime Minister's directive to strengthen 'human capital' the program targets senior staff with a three-part competency framework: Perceptual (mindset) Literacy (concepts) and Skill (practical implementation) .The curriculum moves beyond passive learning to include 'practical workshops' and integration into daily workflows. Execution relies on industry partnerships with AWS and Google dividing training into 'Exposure' and 'Focused Deepening' stages to ensure technical relevance .

items.title: National AI headquarters
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: This government decision provides the budget required to implement the research and implementation of the 2023 Regulation Policy Paper

items.title: The Expert Forum for National Preparedness for AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The expert forum is in charge of implementation of regulations for AI across all sectors and inter-alia is in charge of issues as transparency and explainability. Some of the members are experts in this specific field.

items.title: AI in the Classroom Scuola Futura / PNRR Digital Transition Centers
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: It's an instance of the national teacher-training initiative develops AI literacy in schools. The program is designed funded and coordinated by the Italian Ministry of Education and Merit and delivered through public Digital Transition Centers (in this case located in Tropea Center in Calabria region by the local public Institute of Higher Education). The course “Artificial Intelligence in the Classroom” offers 25 hours of structured training at national scale (10000 places) covering AI fundamentals ethical implications and pedagogical uses addressing AI basics educational applications and critical engagement with AI tools ensuring consistent state-led AI literacy development across the public education system.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: National Defence and Cybersecurity Seminar Training on Disinformation Hate Speech and Cyber Threats for Police forces
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The seminar trains military public officials and cybersecurity professionals on risks from AI-driven disinformation hate speech and deepfake-enabled cybercrime. It highlights comparative lessons (e.g. Germany’s NetzDG) and the role of national and EU cybersecurity agencies in countering online incitement and manipulation promoting resilience against AI-amplified threats (pp. 211–213)

body.name: Authority for ensuring communication

items.title: Polizia di Stato Deepfake-enabled Online Trading Scam Takedown (Feb 2024)
items.justification: During this operation 473 websites accounts and advertisements that exploited artificial intelligence (AI)-generated movies or 'deepfakes' to trick users into making fraudulent investments were found and blocked by Polizia Postale. Law enforcement directly combats the use of deepfake tech (AI systems) to propagate false claims and distort reality. It combats the spread of false information using AI advocates safeguarding citizens against fraud and harassment enabled by AI and exhibits proactive prevention measures.

body.name: Authority for ensuring communication

items.title: Data Protection Authority OpenAI data use awareness - EUR 15 million fine
items.justification: The Italian Data Protection Authority (Garante) fined OpenAI €15 million in December 2024 calculated taking into account the company’s cooperative attitude and launched a six-month national awareness campaign around ChatGPT as a result of an investigation initiated in March 2023. Access to Redress and Remedy is addressed through the administrative penalty that holds people accountable for violations of AI-related rights.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: AI in Schools Guidelines - Ministry of Education
items.justification: The guidelines by the Ministry of Education (in charge mostly of primary and secondary education) states that in order to prevent bias or discrimination in AI applications particularly for kids with special educational needs systems must promote accessibility and inclusion (Section 2 page 7). To evaluate issues like algorithmic discrimination privacy violations or manipulation the document also requires a 'Impact assessment on fundamental rights (FRIA)' for AI systems in schools (Section 4 page 20-22).

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: Minerva 7B LLM model (and the broader Minerva family)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Minerva 7B is the first LLM designed specifically for the Italian language and trained from scratch for Italian and English”. It emphasises Italian-centric vocabulary open design and aims to avoid dependence on models trained primarily on non-Italian data thus supporting the preservation of linguistic and cultural identity in AI systems.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - FAIR Foundation for research

items.title: Consip Integration of Environmental Standards (CAM) in ICT and Data Center Procurement
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: Consip (in-house company of the Ministry of Economy and Finance manages the public procurement system) from 2024 starts to systematically integrate Criteri Ambientali Minimi (CAM) into ICT procurement including data centers and cloud services. Section 11.2 of the Relazione sulla Gestione highlights CAM application to ICT tenders requiring energy-efficient server consolidation virtualization and cooling. Contracts include the “Opzione Verde” for renewable electricity in data centers and mandate supplier reporting on energy performance. These standards ensure public AI workloads run on greener more efficient infrastructures reducing their environmental impact.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy - Department for Digital Transformation -Foundation for AI

items.title: Green-aware AI Spook - FAIR Foundation
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Green-aware AI Spoke focuses on embedding environmental sustainability into AI by design. Its work packages target green-aware learning with reduced computational resources energy-efficient deep learning on IoT devices graph sparsification for disaster management to save energy and green-ML for healthcare. It also develops pilots in smart energy management renewable energy systems sustainable cities and Industry 5.0. These activities directly address the environmental impact of AI by reducing carbon footprint energy use and resource intensity.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy - Department for Digital Transformation -Foundation for AI

items.title: Decalogue for the provision of national health services through AI systems - Privacy Authority
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The Garante Decalogue establishes mandatory standards for AI in national health services focusing on justice non-discrimination openness and human-in-the-loop safeguards operationalizing GDPR (Arts. 22 35) in healthcare AI situations. It requires: (1) the principle of non-discrimination algorithmics with periodic bias checks and data rectification; (2) the principle of non-exclusivity to maintain human oversight; and (3) knowledgeability so patients understand the logic utilized (pp. 10-14 particularly Section 4).

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: Provision no 675/2024 against Foodinho srl (Glovo Group) algorithmic management of riders (Italian Data Protection Authority)
items.justification: Glovo's rider management algorithm was deemed by the Garante to be both opaque and possibly discriminatory. The decree (Provv. 675/2024) prohibits fully automated punitive decisions and mandates proportionality contestability and reasoning transparency. In order to prevent discrimination against workers guarantee meaningful human review and adhere to non-discrimination protections under the GDPR and national labor legislation it requires Foodinho to modify monitoring and scoring (pp. 2–6 12–15 of decision).

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: CONSOB SupTech AI in Market Supervision
items.justification: The CONSOB FinTech paper (pp. 41-69) describes AI proof-of-concepts for insider trading detection that are integrated into human-in-the-loop protocols. It emphasizes that AI technologies remain diagnostic with ultimate judgments kept for human officials assuring oversight fallback mechanisms and conformity with the EU AI Act.

body.name: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali AGENAS (National Agency for Health Services)

items.title: AI Impact assessment - AGID
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Impact assessments
items.justification: The AI Impact Assessment Guidelines (AgID Feb 2025) provide a structured tool for public administrations to assess AI systems before adoption. They operationalize impact assessments by requiring administrations to document scope purpose and risk level (C1) analyze effects on fundamental rights fairness and bias (C2) ensure robustness and explainability (C3) verify data governance and privacy (C4) test risk management and fallback procedures (C5) and guarantee accountability and transparency (C6). An appendix links directly to the AI Act’s risk levels ensuring compliance.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN)

items.title: Garante Privacy corrective orders against Foodinho/Glovo on algorithmic management of riders
items.justification: The Italian Data Protection Authority fined Foodinho/Glovo €5 million and €2.5 million to Deliveroo issuing corrective orders requiring fairness transparency and human contestability in algorithmic management of riders. The authority stated there can be no “incontestable” algorithm deciding working conditions. It mandated safeguards to prevent discriminatory automated decisions obligations to inform workers about algorithmic logic and rights to challenge AI-driven outcomes.Ref: Garante Doc. 9782895

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: Responsible Use of AI The Art of the Prompt National School of Administration (SNA)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This SNA course trains public administration staff in the responsible use of generative AI focusing on how to design effective prompts manage AI-assisted workflows and understand ethical and legal implications. It includes modules on AI in public powers automated administrative decision-making data analysis using AI tools and safe human-centered AI use. The 2025 editions running from January to December including one starting 30 September 2025 directly strengthen AI skills across the civil service. (pp. 1–2)

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN)

items.title: National School of Administration The Art of the Prompt course (Public Administration AI Training)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National School of Administration (SNA) delivers government-funded training for public employees on responsible and effective use of AI including generative systems and prompt design. The course builds technical and ethical competencies for integrating AI into administrative processes covering automated decision-making legal implications and practical applications. Multiple 2025 sessions including on 30/09/2025 demonstrate ongoing implementation.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: Fondo Nuove Competenze (New Skills Fund)
items.justification: Fondo Nuove Competenze is a national government program that funds company workforce training by reimbursing wage costs during participation in approved courses including AI and digital-skills reskilling paths. It operationalizes the Strategy’s commitment to “incentives for reskilling and upskilling in all production contexts” (p.30) and supports structured training aligned with technological transition priorities (F.5 pp. 33–34) enabling workers to adapt to AI-driven labour market changes.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: National Cybersecurity Agency adheres to International Guidelines on AI Safety
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: By integrating secure-by-design procedures and resilience posture into the national cybersecurity plan ACN's compliance with the International Guidelines on AI Security is a government-led initiative that operationalizes Italy's responsibilities. It exhibits acceptance and application outside of the policy wording conforming to the Safety & Security clauses.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: FAIR Spoke 3 Resilient AI
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Spoke 3 develops methodologies for robust and resilient AI in real-world and adversarial environments. It advances algorithms resistant to malicious data and attacks supports verification and validation of AI pipelines (including safety-critical sectors like automotive) and promotes strategies for unforeseen failures. It also addresses ethical/legal issues to ensure compliance with safety norms (pp. 3–6 Spoke 3 – Resilient AI).

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: AgID Public Consultation on AI Guidelines for Public Administration (Draft 2025)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The proposed Guidelines place clear transparency requirements on PA AI systems including the need for decision logic to be explicable and for users to be informed when engaging with AI. They require notice requirements disclosure procedures and communication protocols and make reference to AI Act Art. 50 transparency duties (pp. 39–41 §§7.1–7.2). These clauses seek to make AI in public services transparent responsible and reliable.

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: FAIR Spoke 1 Human-Centered AI
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Spoke 1 develops explainable and trustworthy AI through human-in-the-loop methods interpretable decision-support systems and empirical pilots (WP1.1 WP1.6 WP1.7). It focuses on explainable AI for medical and industrial case studies co-design of trustworthy-by-design systems and risk assessment of explainers ensuring users can understand evaluate and trust AI outputs (pp. 3–12 17–21).

body.name: Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) - National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) - Future AI Research Foundation (Fondazione FAIR)

items.title: Govt to implement AI workforce readiness strategy
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: In September 2025 the Government of Jamaica in partnership with the Amber Group established a National AI Lab at the University of Technology Jamaica (https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/2025/10/17/amber-group-bets-ai-robotics-next-decade/). The Lab's explicit objective is to upskill Jamaicans in AI offering advanced AI training including machine learning data science and deep learning. This constitutes a formal tertiary-level AI literacy initiative equipping students with technical competencies to understand evaluate and create AI systems. The initiative is supported by a signed MOU between UTech and the Amber Group and is operational as of September 2025.

items.title: National Child Online Protection Committee (NCOP)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: Cabinet approved the NCOP in November 2021 (1). The mandate of the committee is to develop a National Child Online Protection Strategy. While the 27-member committee has been formed and is looking at the threats and other aspects of AI as well as other dangers associated with internet use no strategies have been developed to date. In fact the committee's Chair indicated in May 2024 that they were seeking to have the strategies developed within 9 to 12 months (2). (1)https://jis.gov.jm/strategy-approved-to-protect-children-online/ (2) https://web.archive.org/web/20251102161435/https://iriefm.net/cabinet-appointed-committee-developing-strategies-to-protect-children-from-artificial-intelligence-and-other-related-threats-online/

items.title: National AI Task Force Policy Recommendations
items.type: Policy Development — Mandated bodies (commissions task forces or inter-agency working groups) to draft an AI-related framework.
items.justification: The report was the culmination of extensive research stakeholder engagement and rigorous analysis conducted by the National AI Task Force whose members represented academia industry government and civil society. Their recommendations (pp. 22 24 and 30) talk about the need for Jamaica to develop national ethical guidelines that outline core principle of responsible AI that focus on fairness transparency and accountability.

items.title: Office of the Information Commissioner (OIC)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The OIC is responsible for monitoring compliance issuing guidelines and advising the Minister on data protection matter. The DPA grants individuals the right not to be subject to decisions made solely by automated means that significantly affect them. It also gives them the right to request human review or challenge such decisions. They can do this to the data controller who has to respond within thirty days. The OIC has oversight and may order the data controller to reconsider the decision or to take a new decision that is not based solely on automated decision.

body.name: Office of the Information Commissioner (OIC)

items.title: Reskilling Upskilling and Re-skilling (RUN) Project
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Transformation Implementation Unit (TIU) of the Government of Jamaica operates the RUN (Reskilling Upskilling New-skilling) Project which provides fully funded access to over 7000 courses and certification programmes for public sector employees via Coursera and Academy+. Artificial Intelligence is explicitly listed as one of five priority skill development areas alongside Data Science Power BI Microsoft Excel and Customer Service. The programme is open to all public sector employees with selection prioritising those whose professional roles align with the subject matter.

items.title: National AI Task Force Policy Recommendations
items.type: Policy Development — Mandated bodies (commissions task forces or inter-agency working groups) to draft an AI-related framework.
items.justification: The report was the culmination of extensive research stakeholder engagement and rigorous analysis conducted by the National AI Task Force whose members represented academia industry government and civil society. Their recommendation (p. 7) talks to workforce adaptation and addressing the need for re-skilling and up-skilling to align with AI-driven economies. The government will be implementing an artificial intelligence (AI) workforce-readiness strategy (1) following these recommendations. (1) https://web.archive.org/web/20251107155741/https://jamaica-gleaner.com/article/news/20250322/govt-implement-ai-workforce-readiness-strategy

items.title: Reskilling Upskilling and Re-skilling (RUN) Project
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Reskilling Upskilling and New-Skilling (RUN) Project started in July 2024 and is a direct response to the need to equip Government of Jamaica employees with relevant skills to function in the digital age. The RUN Project is managed by the Transformation Implementation Unit. The project offers public sector employees access to over 7000 self-paced courses and certification programmes from world-class universities and companies including Google Harvard Yale and Salesforce via online portals from Coursera and Academy+. Several AI courses are included.

items.title: National AI Task Force Policy Recommendations
items.type: Policy Development — Mandated bodies (commissions task forces or inter-agency working groups) to draft an AI-related framework.
items.justification: The National AI Task Force Policy Recommendations published February 2025 (https://opm.gov.jm/national-ai-task-force-report-published/) were developed to guide Jamaica's national AI policy framework. Safety and security are explicitly prioritised (p. 3). Pages 30-31 propose developing AI standards and best practices to ensure interoperability and consistent implementation across sectors. Pages 7 and 14 address cybersecurity objectives including strengthening AI systems' resilience against cyber threats and protecting critical digital infrastructure.

items.title: Office of the Information Commissioner (OIC)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The OIC is responsible for monitoring compliance issuing guidelines and advising the Minister on data protection matter. The DPA grants individuals the right to be informed of the logic behind any automated decision-making when their personal data is processed in such a way and the right to have that decision reviewed.

body.name: Office of the Information Commissioner (OIC)

items.title: Designated school practice examples and videos - Educational practices on how to utilize generative AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Ministry of Education Culture Sports Science and Technology (MEXT) has begun publishing designated school practice case studies and teacher-facing videos on their website. One rubric is specifically called “Educational practices for utilizing generative AI” which offers practical guidance on implementing AI tools in schools covering concerns classroom ideas and effective use strategies.

items.title: Lets learn ICT literacy in five fields - How not to be deceived by fake and misinformation
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Japanese Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) launched a public education initiative to enhance Information and Communication Technology (ICT) literacy of the public. The program provides instructors with teaching materials and guidelines for courses across five thematic areas including “How not to be deceived by fake and misinformation (2nd edition).” This module specifically addresses generative AI-related misinformation such as fake images created by AI (Slide 48) and illustrates the danger by showing real-world examples that took place in Japan for instance AI-generated disaster footage that spread widely on social media and lead to panic or a fake CEO created by AI as a scam (Slides 31–32).

body.name: Japan AI Safety Institute (J-AISI)

items.title: AI Guidelines for Business APPENDIX Ver11
items.justification: While the AI Guidelines for Business lacked any mechanism for redress/remedies the Appendix deals with implementations for reference and is intended as a reference for specific actions [p.2]. Specifically for privacy violations the Appendix points out the need for follow up response including subsequent remedy from damage [pp.135 152]. It also mentions under 'Specific Methods' regarding explainabillity to 'Establish and communicate the remedial mechanism including the process by which stakeholders can lodge complaints.' [p. 146].

items.title: Leading DX School Project (FY2024 supplementary budget)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: Schools can receive funding (900.000 yen (maximum)) under the Leading DX School Project to try implementing the MEXT guidelines regarding the safe and deliberate use of generative AI in classroom settings [p.4].

items.title: MEXT Online Training Sessions on the Use of Generative AI in Schools
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: MEXT provides tutorials training videos and guides for teachers so they can properly teach students how to safely use generative AI in school settings in line with the MEXT guidelines.

items.title: Singapore AI Safety Red Teaming Challenge to accurately reflect cultural and linguistic risks in different regions
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: Singapore’s Infocomm Media Development Authority launched a Singapore AI Safety Red Teaming Challenge gathering experts in culture and language to enhance AI safety in specific regions to accurately reflect cultural and linguistic risks in different regions for AI models. Japan including experts from the Japan AI Safety Institute (AISI) and the Japan Deep Learning Association (JDLA) also participated to address this gap taking challenges on 'Multilingual Testing' and 'Cultural Manifestations of Bias.'

items.title: Establishment of the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The newly established Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board supports implementing the guidelines (in particular the evaluation viewpoints of the Guidelines among which number 11 addressed environmental concerns and energy use of AI) by understanding the procurement and utilization status of generative AI in each ministry and agency suggesting risk mitigation and best practices for the procurement and utilization of generative AI in each ministry and agency and providing advice on the effective use of generative AI in each ministry and agency to improve the functionality quality and cost-effectiveness of generative AI systems [pp.13].

items.title: Introduction to AI safety initiatives on the J-AISI Partnership
items.justification: The Partnership of the Japan AI Safety Institute (J-AISI) which is a governmental organization established within the Information-technology Promotion Agency (IPA) introduced initiatives on AI among them one from Rikagaku Kenkyujo (RIKEN) on the development and evaluation of machine guidance methods to enhance fair decision making [p.20]. Their study was aimed at publishing papers [see Type of Output p.20] regarding fair machine guidance and prompted the participants to reassess their views regarding fairness reflect on their biases and modify their decision-making criteria. The ultimate goal of the initiative is to develop AI systems able of making unbiased decisions using fairness-aware machine learning [p.20].

items.title: Case Study Collection of Womens Digital Human Resource Development Plans
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The Cabinet Office Gender Equality Bureau has compiled a collection of public and private case studies on improving women's digital talent acquisition [p.2]. The case study is meant to spread efforts to develop women's digital talent throughout Japan by suggesting to local governments companies and organizations that they will use the case study examples as a reference and proactively advance their efforts by starting new support for digital skill acquisition and employment support in the digital field for women as well as collaborating with the local governments and companies for the sake of the Initiative [p.2].

body.name: Ministry of Economy Trade and Industry (METI) Gender Equality Bureau Cabinet Office

items.title: Interim Report
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Report prepared by the AI Strategic Council under the “Integrated Innovation Strategy Promotion Council” emphasizes continuous and collaborative impact assessments throughout the AI lifecycle covering development provision and use. It calls on government and industry to analyses AI model characteristics potential risks and stakeholder impacts [p.13] urges information sharing regarding deployment [p.13] and highlights the need to ensure transparency at all stages of the AI lifecycle [p.17]. The Report also notes the importance of implementing safety evaluation systems as part of responsible deployment [p.18] and advises caution regarding outputs that may affect citizens’ rights emphasizing careful review beforehand [p.21].

body.name: AI Safety Institute (AISI)

items.title: The Employment Policy Study Group Report
items.justification: The report explains that the AI may lead to employment substitution and a reduction in jobs making it necessary to monitor labor demand and facilitate job placement to support workers who risk displacement [p.37]. It notes that tasks and roles will change and emphasizes labor–management communication to manage these transitions and prevent negative impacts on employment [p.38]. To address challenges that cannot be resolved individually the report calls for regional or industry-specific cooperation to support companies and workers who cannot adapt [p.39]. It further warns that AI systems can reproduce bias and discrimination stressing the need for considerate implementation of AI to protect workers from unfair treatment [pp. 40 57].

items.title: AI Guidelines for Business APPENDIX Ver11
items.justification: The Appendix by the Ministry of Economy Trade and Industry (METI) serves as reference to the main Guidelines. The example on p.8  proposes the typical use-case of an AI-driven applicant-screening system that supports hiring decisions by analyzing past application data and acceptance outcomes. Also the example on pp.15-16 relates to the labour and work sector because it involves AI used in human-resources processes (specifically predicting whether applicants might withdraw) and shows how inappropriate handling of personal data in recruitment led to the system being abolished. The case directly concerns job applicants’ rights transparency and personal data protection in employment contexts which are core labour-related protections.

items.title: Research on the conversion of government information into AI learning data
items.justification: The Digital Agency of Japan has under the initiative of the Cabinet Office Council for Science Technology and Innovation (CSTI) conducted a survey on the needs for Society5.0 learning data.  The purpose of the survey was to show what kind of AI should be disclosed and in what format and what people who handle it in business should be aware of in order to provide government-owned information in a form that contributes to the utilization and development of generated data in Japan based on recent technological trends. The research highlighted the importance of continuously disclosing high-priority data based on the method used in the survey.

items.title: Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board - Meeting
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board (established within the Digital Agency which is responsible for implementing policies aimed at achieving people-centred digitalisation) is mandated under the guidelines to monitor the procurement status of generative AI systems across ministries and agencies and to provide advice on related risk-mitigation measures [p.17]. In its recent meeting the Board discussed potential improvements to the Guidelines for the Procurement and Use of Generative AI to Advance and Innovate Public Administration. During the session members examined government perspectives on appropriate procurement and use of AI and exchanged views on the current status of the procurement check sheet (see slides 3 and 6).

items.title: First Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board - Meeting
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board established within the Digital Agency is mandated under the guidelines to monitor generative AI procurement across ministries and advise on risk-mitigation measures [p.17 of Guidelines]. In its recent meeting the Board examined potential updates to the Guidelines for the Procurement and Use of Generative AI and specifically emphasized the need for improving education and literacy regarding generative AI for individuals and organizations involved in the development and operation of generative AI systems among the government items (slide 2).

items.title: Report on the Development of Digitally Skilled Workforce for the Era of Society 50 For Skills-Based Workforce Development
items.justification: The Ministry of Economy (METI) has held discussions on developing a digitally skilled workforce with experts through the Study Group on the Development of Digitally Skilled Workforce for the Era of Society 5.0 and its Working Group on Skills and Learning. The research findings were then consolidated in the report and released to the public. The report highlights the growing need to utilize digital transformation and AI and developing and securing human resources with the skills necessary to promote digital transformation [p.5]. The report also outlines many reasons and strategies for AI skill upscaling; such as providing in-house AI training to equip employees with the skills to use generative AI leading to increased corporate value [p.16].

items.title: Evaluation Report of the 3rd joint test exercise Advancement of agent evaluation methods
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Japanese Institute of AI Safety (J-AISI) joined an AI safety exercise together with other AI safety-focused institutes from ten countries. The document presents their evaluation report on this exercise and its findings. Among the key questions they explored were how safe models are as agents with respect to common risk categories [p. 3]. They concluded that among the most important tasks is capturing an agent’s reasoning to identify when it displays unsafe thinking or behavior even if the eventual task outcome is not harmful [p. 4] and how to ensure agent safety across languages [p. 4].

body.name: AI Safety Institute (AISI)

items.title: Japan AI Safety Workshop
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The workshop's goal was to enable a discussion on the importance of ensuring that AI systems are designed with rigorous safety standards helps mitigate risks fosters transparency and promote responsible innovation [p.3]. It also noted that when organizations prioritize AI safety they build a foundation of trust that enables collaboration among stakeholders policymakers and the public and how a strong commitment to AI safety supports the sustainable growth of AI [p.3]. Akiko Murakami the Executive Director of the Japan AI Safety Institute (J-AISI) was also a Keynote speaker where she highlighted how innovation can only accelerate when safety is ensured [p.4] and to advance innovation and adoption of AI by integrating safety [p.5].

body.name: AI Safety Institute (AISI)

items.title: Research Report - Known Attacks and Their Impacts on AI Systems
items.justification: In order to provide an overview of security attacks specific to AI systems the Japanese AI Safety Institute (J-AISI) has compiled a list of potential attacks against AI and AI systems and their impacts that have been published as an academic paper. The document notes that AI-specific security measures are essential [p. 2] and the importance of measures against conventional cybersecurity attacks especially when system incorporates AI specifically those involve intervening in an AI model’straining or inference processes as well as exploiting or tampering with its inputsand outputs [p. 3]. Pages 10-20 then outline all of the potential attacks so users can be prepared.

body.name: AI Safety Institute (AISI)

items.title: Workshop to promote the realization of an AI-symbiotic society (3rd Meeting)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Information-Technology Promotion Agency Japan hosts a workshop to realize a society where humans and AI coexist assessing social issues that AI might cause in Japan. During the third meeting AI in the sensitive healthcare sector was discussed and in line with the framework the importance of implementing the AI system with transparency so that we can see what the software sees and what humans see was emphasized [p.12]. The expert also suggested that it is important to treat AI as merely a simple tool especially in highly specialized fields [p.12-13].

items.title: The Regulatory Framework for the Use of AI in the Jordanian Banking Sector
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The CBJ AI Framework ensures access to redress and remedy through contestation and oversight. Section 2.4 (Accountability page 13) mandates open channels for customers to submit inquiries or requests for review of AI-based decisions with an appointed AI System Owner responsible for governance and compliance. In parallel Sections 6.1–6.2 (Incident Response and Business Continuity page 20–21) require AI-specific incident protocols centralized logs and prompt reporting to FinCERT under CBJ supervision enabling investigation correction and regulatory follow-up on AI-related harms.

items.title: Organizational Strucutre MoDEE
items.justification: The National Artificial Intelligence Committee chaired by MoDEE oversees implementation of Jordan’s National AI Code of Ethics (2022) which includes fairness impartiality and equality across gender race and religion. Through its ethical oversight role the Committee ensures that AI systems developed or adopted nationally align with gender equality principles and prevent discriminatory outcomes. This link provides more information about the committee albeit not from an official site: https://web.archive.org/web/20251012190311/https://oxfordinsights.com/insights/spotlight-series-jordan/

items.title: The Regulatory Framework for the Use of AI in the Jordanian Banking Sector
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The Regulatory Framework for the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Jordanian Banking Sector (CBJ July 2025) embeds Human Oversight and Determination throughout its provisions. Pages 11 and 18–19 require integrating Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) and Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL) mechanisms in AI systems ensuring human supervision intervention and fail-safe control. Page 13 assigns accountability and mandates review channels for AI-driven decisions guaranteeing that final responsibility and decision-making remain with humans in all critical banking applications.

items.title: AI Raising Awareness for Public Employees
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The AI Capacity-Building Initiative by the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE) and JODDB directly advances Public Sector Skills Development. It trains 3000 employees from 100 government entities including leaders staff and technical experts; to integrate AI into public services enhance efficiency and foster innovation. As part of the National AI Strategy (2023–2027) it aims to equip 15000 public servants with AI skills by 2027 modernizing government performance and enabling data-driven decision-making.

body.name: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE)

items.title: AI Raising Awareness for Public Employees
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The AI Raising Awareness for Public Employees project launched in 2024 by the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE) in collaboration with the Jordan Design and Development Bureau (JODDB) directly supports the Jordan AI Strategy (2023–2027) objective to enhance national AI capacity. It trains 3000 government employees from 100 institutions including leaders specialists and staff in AI applications and technical skills aiming to build a future-ready public workforce and upskill 15000 employees by 2027.

body.name: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE) National Council for Entrepreneurship and a Steering Committee

items.title: The Regulatory Framework for the Use of AI in the Jordanian Banking Sector
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The AI Regulatory Framework for the Jordanian Banking Sector (CBJ 2024) embeds Safety and Security as core supervisory pillars (Sec. 5.1–5.3 & 6.1–6.2  pages 17 to 20). It requires banks to integrate AI into their cybersecurity business continuity and disaster recovery plans supported by regular stress tests and incident simulations. Institutions must also report AI-related incidents to FinCERT maintain an AI-incident register and implement secure data-handling and access controls. These measures ensure resilience safeguard financial systems and prevent AI-driven operational or security risks.

body.name: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship and the National Council for Entrepreneurship

items.title: KazLLM National Kazakh Large Language Model
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The KazLLM initiative directly promotes cultural and linguistic diversity by developing a national Large Language Model trained on a comprehensive Kazakh-language corpus. According to the media source over 140 researchers and 26 institutions created domain-rich Kazakh datasets across 115 scientific fields ensuring high-quality AI processing translation and analysis in the Kazakh language. This strengthens linguistic inclusion preserves cultural identity and integrates Kazakh into modern AI technologies such as chatbots assistants and translators.

items.title: #SheInnovator Project
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The #SheInnovator project was implemented by TechnoWomen with the support of the National Commission on Women Family and Demographic Policy under the President of Kazakhstan USAID and Astana Hub. According to the official summary on 10 September 2024 the project trained girls and women in digital transformation AI use e-commerce and marketplace skills through 10 regional conferences and master classes reaching over 1650 participants. TechnoWomen also joined the KazLLM Competence Center to contribute to developing a gender component in AI including gender-inclusive data and reducing algorithmic bias.

items.title: AI-Qyzmet National AI Skills Training Program for Civil Servants
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: AI-Qyzmet is a government-led national training program launched by the Agency for Civil Service Affairs and the Ministry of Digital Development to build AI competencies among public officials. The program trains civil servants to use AI tools in administrative processes planning information processing decision-making and task automation. It includes practical modules on working with modern language models and implementing domestic AI solutions. Training is delivered through the Academy of Public Administration and its regional branches using flexible formats such as short “Snack Learning” video lessons. In 2025 the program aims to train around 30000 civil servants contributing directly to public-sector skills development.

items.title: Build With AI for Public Sector 2025
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Build With AI for Public Sector 2025 is a government-supported national program launched by the Ministry of Digital Development together with Google and Apolitical to strengthen AI competencies across the civil service. It provides multi-level training covering senior leadership middle management and general staffon the responsible and effective use of AI tools in public administration. The program includes workshops applied courses and training modules based on Apolitical’s Government AI Campus - a global platform for public-sector AI governance skills. By focusing on practical AI use cases decision-making and best practices for integrating AI in government workflows the initiative directly supports public-sector skills development.

items.title: Build With AI for Public Sector 2025
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Build With AI for Public Sector 2025 is a government-supported national program launched by the Ministry of Digital Development together with Google and Apolitical to strengthen AI competencies across the civil service. It provides multi-level training covering senior leadership middle management and general staffon the responsible and effective use of AI tools in public administration. The program includes workshops applied courses and training modules based on Apolitical’s Government AI Campus a global platform for public-sector AI governance skills. By focusing on practical AI use cases decision-making and best practices for integrating AI in government workflows the initiative directly supports public-sector skills development.

items.title: The Kenya High Courts 2025 Worldcoin judgment [ Republic v Tools for Humanity Corporation (US) & 8 others Katiba Institute & 4 others (Ex parte Applicants) Data Privacy & Governance Society of Kenya ]
items.justification: The Kenya High Court’s 2025 Worldcoin judgment directly advances access to redress and remedy for AI-related grievances by applying the Data Protection Act (2019) to biometric and automated decision-making systems. The Court recognized individuals’ rights to seek judicial relief where AI-driven processing causes harm—such as exploitation or unlawful data collection.It ordered suspension of Worldcoin’s AI-powered biometric operations erasure of unlawfully obtained data and mandated the ODPC to enforce compliance showing coordination between judicial and administrative mechanisms. This creates a practical pathway for redress—victims can file complaints with the ODPC or seek court intervention when AI  systems violate their privacy.

items.title: Microsofts partnership with UAE-based AI firm to invest in a Data Center in Kenya
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The government of Kenya has publicly facilitated/endorsed major private investments in data centres that explicitly plan to use renewable energy (geothermal). These partnership announcements are real near-term steps that reduce the carbon footprint of AI infrastructure in Kenya.

body.name: Ministry of ICT and Digital Economy

items.title: KEBS_Information technology AI Code of Practice for AI Applications
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The KEBS Code of Practice for AI is a Standard developed by the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) that aims to provide guidance on responsible development testing deployment and use of AI systems in Kenya. The Code of Practice is intended to help organizations develop provide and use AI systems responsibly. The Code explicitly incorporates AI impact-assessment concepts and requirements as part of responsible AI risk governance. It embeds these concepts within risk management ethical/societal concerns and documentation practices. The Code calls for AI impact assessments to evaluate the potential consequences of AI system failures and their effects on stakeholders and integrates impact assessment into its risk-management.

items.title: Africa Center of Competence for Digital and AI Skilling
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Though the evidence leads to a UNDP website the content shows active drive by the Kenyan government in equipping civil servants with AI-relevant skills. The partnership has been done with the UNDP and Microsoft and it includes the creation of the Africa Center of Competence for Digital and Artificial Intelligence Skilling.

items.title: Kenya-UK partnership on emerging technologies
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: This is a collaboration between Kenyan and UK academic/research institutions focused on emerging technologies (including AI) which supports research innovation and potentially safety/security capacity-building.

items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Kuwait Ministry of education changed computer course curriculum for 10th grade to include AI to make students ready to the new world this was lead by government in order to promote AI literacy

items.title: Smart Energy Management and Sustainability
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: AI-driven energy systems are now being implemented to optimize power distribution reduce waste and monitor consumption patterns across residential and industrial areas.Smart grids powered by AI are capable of predicting electricity demand based on time temperature and population movement. This ensures that energy production aligns more accurately with consumption needs minimizing both shortages and excess generation

items.justification: Kuwait’s Central Agency for Information Technology (CAIT) and the Communications and Information Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA) signed a strategic partnership agreement with Microsoft Corporation marking the Kuwaiti government’s second collaboration to accelerate digital transformation and enhance artificial intelligence (AI) development across government entities. This training will be for 4500 public servant for AI and cybersecurity and they will be certified to train others

items.title: Partnership with Microsoft

items.justification: Kuwait’s Central Agency for Information Technology (CAIT) and the Communications and Information Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA) signed a strategic partnership agreement with Microsoft Corporation  signed deal with Microsoft to lunch several AI courses The partnership marks a milestone in leveraging the AI applications in Kuwait. Microsoft aims to train 4500 (( government officials ))in cybersecurity and AI along with 30000 individuals on the Copilot system

items.title: Online course on AI for teachers in Kyrgyzstan
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The online AI course for teachers launched by the Ministry of Education and Science of Kyrgyzstan directly promotes AI literacy by enhancing educators’ understanding of artificial intelligence concepts practical applications and ethical considerations. It equips teachers with the skills to integrate AI topics into classroom instruction supporting the development of students’ digital and AI competencies. This initiative operationalizes the Kyrgyzstan's Digitalisation Concept framework’s goals to build AI and digital skills across the education system.

body.name: National Council for AI Development

items.title: The creation of an interdepartmental working group on the protection of personal data
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The State Agency for Personal Data Protection under the Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic and the Ministry of Internal Affairs jointly created the Interdepartmental Working Group on the Protection of Personal Data. It enhances coordination between government bodies to address violations of personal data rights in digital environment including those resulting from AI-driven processing and automated decision-making. Its establishment strengthens mechanisms for citizens to seek redress and ensures AI-related harms are handled transparently and effectively.

body.name: The State Agency for Personal Data Protection under the Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic

items.title: Official Request to Commercial Bank Kyrgyzstan OJSC Following Large-Scale Debiting Incident
items.justification: The State Agency for Personal Data Protection issued an official request to “Commercial Bank Kyrgyzstan” OJSC on 23 January 2024 after a large-scale unauthorized debiting of citizens’ funds allegedly linked to automated banking processes and may affect the interests of citizens and violate the principles of security and confidentiality of personal data. The Agency’s intervention aimed to ensure accountability transparency and compliance with data protection and security principles. This action strengthened access to redress by compelling the bank to clarify the causes address potential AI-related data misuse and take corrective measures to protect citizens’ rights.

body.name: The State Agency for Personal Data Protection under the Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic

items.title: Access to TikTok has been blocked in Kyrgyzstan
items.justification: The TikTok blocking initiative in Kyrgyzstan aims to protect minors from harmful digital content and potential risks of exploitation or manipulation through the platform’s algorithms and AI-driven recommendations. The government justified the measure on child protection grounds (April 2024 decision) thereby prioritising the right of children to safety and privacy in the digital environment.

body.name: The Ministry of Digital Development and Innovative Technologies of the Kyrgyz Republic

items.title: Aitil
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The “Aitil” national AI platform directly addresses cultural and linguistic diversity by embedding the Kyrgyz language into modern AI applications. It enables translation between Kyrgyz and major world languages supports voice-to-text transcription and offers a chat assistant in Kyrgyz ensuring the language is represented in the digital sphere. By doing so it preserves and promotes Kyrgyz linguistic heritage prevents marginalization of minority languages in AI systems and expands access for Kyrgyz speakers to digital technologies.

body.name: The National Commission on the State Language under the President of the Kyrgyz Republic

items.title: Automated Information System Electronic Archive
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The “Electronic Archive” was launched under the Digital Transformation Concept 2024-2028 which was later formalised into binding law by the Digital Code (adopted on 31 July 2025). Implemented by the Legal Aid Service under the Ministry of Justice with support of UNDP enhances fairness and non-discrimination by ensuring equal digital access to justice services. It reduces administrative bias improves transparency in case handling and enables consistent data-driven oversight of legal aid delivery. The initiative advances the Digital Code’s principles on fairness equality and digital inclusion.

body.name: The Ministry of Digital Development and Innovative Technologies

items.title: International Womens Day About 50000 girls completed STEM learnings
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The “Girls in Science” initiative celebrated on International Women’s Day 2025 in Bishkek is a program jointly organized by the Ministry of Education and Science of the Kyrgyz Republic and UNICEF. It directly supports Gender Equality in AI by promoting STEM education for girls which includes fields critical for AI development (computer science data and technology). Since 2020 over 60000 adolescents (48000 girls) have received STEM peer-to-peer training breaking gender stereotypes and building the pipeline for women in the AI workforce.

body.name: The Ministry of Labor Social Security and Migration of the Kyrgyz Republic

items.title: The Ministry of Digital Development and Innovation Technologies developed and released for public discussion the Draft Cabinet Resolution On the Approval of Requirements for the Methodology of Hazard Assessment of AI Systems and Requirements for High-Risk AI Systems
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Ministry of Digital Development and Innovation Technologies developed and released for public discussion the Draft Cabinet Resolution “On the Approval of Requirements for the Methodology of Hazard Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Systems and Requirements for High-Risk Artificial Intelligence Systems”. It establishes a unified framework for AI hazard (impact) assessments. It requires AI system owners to evaluate and classify risks before deployment introducing a step-by-step self-assessment algorithm aligned with the Digital Code (Art. 193). The initiative promotes transparency mitigates risks to citizens’ rights and aligns with OECD and EU AI regulatory principles.

body.name: The Ministry of Digital Development and Innovative Technologies

items.title: Strengthening the Capacity of Civil Servants in Kyrgyzstan Media and Information Literacy and Digital Communication
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Government of the Kyrgyz Republic initiated the project “Strengthening the Capacity of Civil Servants in Kyrgyzstan: Media and Information Literacy and Digital Communication” with technical support from UNESCO and UNDP and supports the Concept for Digital Transformation 2024-2028 goals by enhancing civil servants’ digital and AI-related competencies. It trains public officials in digital governance data protection and interaction with artificial intelligence directly advancing the Concept’s provisions on AI skills development in the public sector.

body.name: National Council for AI Development

items.title: Programme to Enhance Digital Skills for Local Self-Government Officials
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Ministry of Digital Development and Innovation Technologies together with the Youth Development Institute Public Foundation supported by Deutscher Volkshochschul-Verband e.V. International and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe Programme Office in Bishkek launched a two-day Digital Skills Enhancement Programme for representatives of local administrations councils and community groups. The initiative focused on reskilling participants in digital and AI tools such as ChatGPT Gemini and DeepSeek enhancing their capacity to apply AI in communication data analysis and local governance and supported implementation of the Concept on Digital Transformation.

body.name: National Council for AI Development

items.title: Workshop on Strengthening Digital Leadership and Cybersecurity Capacity among Deputy Heads of State Agencies
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The workshop on strengthening digital leadership and cybersecurity capacity organized by the Ministry of Digital Development and Innovative Technologies of the Kyrgyz Republic in cooperation with the OSCE Programme Office in Bishkek addressed AI Safety and Security by training senior government officials on cybersecurity risks and responsible AI use in state institutions. The event focused on preventing misuse ensuring reliability and building institutional capacity to implement the Digital Code’s AI safety and risk management principles.

body.name: The Ministry of Digital Development and Innovative Technologies

items.title: Capacity Building Program on AI Governance
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative addresses AI Literacy by providing foundational and practical training to bridge the digital divide. Coordinated by the Ministry of Technology and Communications (MTC) and supported by UNESCO it targets the core of the educational system to ensure long-term scalability. The primary action is a UNESCO-supported program training 6200 TVET instructors in AI tools. This directly addresses AI literacy by equipping educators with practical skills enabling them to integrate AI into vocational curricula and prepare students for the digital economy. Broader efforts also include creating inclusive AI literacy programs for civil servants and journalists.

items.title: National Research Program Education project application call
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The application call for research grants by the Latvian Council of Science targets project applications on Artificial intelligence opportunities in education. The goal of the program is to promote high-quality relevant and practically applicable research in the field of education in the context of AI with a particular focus on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the learning process and on supporting educators.

body.name: AI Centre

items.title: Educational program Discover Technology
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Riga TechGirls' most popular educational program 'Discover Technology' has attracted more than 7300 interested participants this year. A total of 56 classes were held in the spring and fall sessions and more than 1800 certificates were issued for completing the course in 2025. One of the topics of the education programme is the use of artificial intelligence.

body.name: AI Centre

items.title: Guidelines for the Use of AI in Primary and Secondary Education
items.justification: Developed under the leadership of the Latvian Safer Internet Center the guidelines are designed as a practical tool that: promotes the development of critical thinking and AI literacy for all involved in the educational process; promotes the meaningful use of AI tools in education; helps prevent ethical legal and academic integrity issues.
