items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The Coordinator established a cooperation system with other Latvian administrative institutions culminating in a Memorandum of Institutional Cooperation signed on November 28 2024 by 12 authorities whose competence is related to digital services. The Memorandum established a framework for cooperation aimed at leveraging DSA opportunities effectively and enhancing the online information space. On January 28 2025 the Consumer Rights Protection Center (hereinafter – CRPC) and other institutions signed another memorandum on the effective implementation of the Digital Services Act in Latvia (hereinafter – the Memorandum).

body.name: Consumer Rights Protection Centre

items.title: Handbook against disinformation Recognise and Resist
items.justification: In July 2022 the State Chancellery published the 'Handbook Against Disinformation: Recognizing and Resisting' to arm primarily those working in public administration and indirectly any resident of Latvia with practical knowledge and recommendations so that they can engage in measures to protect and strengthen the security of the country's information space. In August 2025 the State Chancellery published a renewed and expanded edition of the “Handbook against Disinformation: Recognizing and Countering. 2nd Edition”. Compared to the first edition which the State Chancellery published in July 2022 this digital book has been expanded with several new disinformation messages and fact-based refutations ...

body.name: Consumer Rights Protection Centre

items.title: Guidelines for the Use of AI in Primary and Secondary Education
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Guidelines addresses children's rights by drawing attention to various risks for example privacy risks (the use of AI to monitor student performance can lead to privacy violations and reinforce a culture of surveillance); privacy threats (AI systems can collect and store private and sensitive data which if not properly protected can be leaked or misused) etc. Developed under the leadership of the Latvian Safer Internet Center the guidelines are designed as a practical tool that: promotes the development of critical thinking and AI literacy for all involved in the educational process; promotes the meaningful use of AI tools in education; helps prevent ethical legal and academic integrity issues.

body.name: The Ombudsmans Office

items.title: Integration of media content into the Digital cultural Heritage Platform
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Culture Information Systems Centre from August 2023 until May 2026 as a cooperation partner implements the project“Integration of media content into the Digital cultural Heritage Platform” of the “Central Platform and System of Governance” administered by the national Library of Latvia. The Centre will implement the development of a specialised media language corps within the framework of which valuable regional media records will be digitised for nearly 6000 hours. The established specialised language corps will be used for training and adapting the existing model of the Latvian State Administration Language Technology Platform Hugo.lv speech recognition solution.

body.name: AI Centre

items.title: Report AI Systems and Discrimination Aspects
items.justification: The research report was funded by the Ombudsman of the Republic of Latvia. It analyses non-discrimination law and AI regulation. The study collects and analyses examples from international practice related to discrimination caused by AI systems in four high-risk areas i.e. biometric identification education employment and access to basic services based on such 'protected characteristics' as gender disability race ethnicity social status age sexual orientation. The examples analysed reveals how the use of AI systems and algorithms can lead to discrimination.

body.name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM)

items.title: Report AI Systems and Discrimination Aspects
items.justification: The study is funded by the Ombudsman of the Republic of Latvia. It analyses non-discrimination law and AI regulation. The study collects and analyses examples from international practice related to discrimination caused by AI systems in four high-risk areas i.e. biometric identification education employment and access to basic services based on such 'protected characteristics' as gender disability race ethnicity social status age sexual orientation (p.5-10). The examples analysed from other countries reveal how the use of AI systems and algorithms can lead to gender bias discrimination and gender inequality (p.24-34). Recommendations related to these matters are provided for the implementation of the EU AI Act.

body.name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM)

items.title: Report AI Systems and Discrimination Aspects
items.justification: The study is funded by the Ombudsman of the Republic of Latvia. The study analyses non-discrimination law and AI regulation as well as collects and analyses examples from international practice related to discrimination caused by AI systems in four high-risk areas. It reveals how the use of AI systems and algorithms can lead to discrimination and violations of fundamental rights and emphases the importance of human oversight to prevent the risks AI systems raise. It provides recommendations inter alia regarding human oversight and determination (see e.g. p.56).

body.name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM)

items.title: Guidelines Data Protection Impact Assessment
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: According to the AI Act the fundamental rights impact assessment  FRIA and the Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) under the GDPR have a complementary relationship. Article 27(4) of the AI Act states that if a DPIA already covers some elements required for the FRIA the FRIA can build upon the DPIA to avoid duplication. The State Data Inspectorate provided these guidelines to serve as standards for these impact assessments.

body.name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM)

items.title: Report AI Systems and Discrimination Aspects
items.justification: The report analyses the regulatory framework for the prohibition of discrimination data protection and artificial intelligence as well as draws attention to the problems and challenges of the existing legal framework in the context of the use of algorithms and AI systems. It explores the most visible examples from international practice related to discrimination caused by AI systems in the four areas mentioned above. The report emphasises the need to carry out fundamental rights impact assessment of AI systems to prevent discrimination risks. Impact assessment is also listed as one of the essential recommendations in the conclusion (see p.57).

body.name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM)

items.title: AI and Discrimination Aspects
items.justification: The report published by the Ombudsman’s Office of the Republic of Latvia analyses the regulatory framework for the prohibition of discrimination data protection and artificial intelligence as well as draws attention to the problems and challenges of the existing legal framework in the context of the use of algorithms and AI systems. It summarises and analyses the most visible examples from international practice related to discrimination caused by AI systems in four high-risk areas. Chapter 6 of the study examines the use of AI and the associated risks in the field of labour and employment (p.37).

body.name: The State Data Inspectorate the Ombudsman VARAM

items.title: Publishing use cases of the AI systems used in Latvian public administration
items.justification: The Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development has published a list of the AI systems used in Latvian public administration. The list describes 14 use cases of AI systems in Latvia e.g. by the State Audit Office Court administration Road Traffic Safety Directorate and Municipal Police etc.

items.title: Research Towards a more efficient public administration how to harness the potential of AI?
items.justification: The study published by the Analytical Service of the Saeima of the Republic of Latvia examines the role of AI in improving the efficiency of public administration provides practical examples of the use of AI technologies for various tasks in public administration and describes the main challenges and risks associated with the implementation of AI in public administration. The insights and examples of good practice gathered in the study will contribute to the development of the Latvian AI ecosystem (p.36). This study examines the tasks functions and types of work in the public sector that could be improved by AI.

items.title: AI Centre
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Centre was established by the Artificial Intelligence Centre Law. On April 2 2025 the Artificial Intelligence Center (AIC) was officially opened at the Science and Innovation Center of Riga Technical University with the aim of developing Latvia as a leading country in the responsible use and implementation of artificial intelligence (AI). The AI Centre have several tasks including to ensure that artificial intelligence systems are used ethically responsibly and safely respecting fundamental human rights; to implement measures to mitigate the risks associated with the use of artificial intelligence.

body.name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM)

items.title: Report AI Systems and Discrimination Aspects
items.justification: The study is funded by the Ombudsman of the Republic of Latvia. The study analyses non-discrimination law and AI regulation as well as collects and analyses examples from international practice related to discrimination caused by AI systems in four high-risk areas. It reveals how the use of AI systems and algorithms can lead to discrimination and violations of fundamental rights and emphases the importance of transparency to prevent the risks AI systems raise. It provides recommendations inter alia regarding transparency and explainability (see e.g. p.56).

body.name: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM)

items.title: Community Digital Inclusion
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Community Digital Inclusion Model advances fairness & non-discrimination by opening school computer labs as community digital centres and deploying trained Digital Ambassadors to deliver basic digital-skills training in villages—prioritising women youth and rural communities. By lowering access and skills gaps (devices connectivity local training) the programme enables under-served groups to participate in the digital economy and benefit from AI on more equal terms reducing bias driven by unequal access and literacy.

items.title: New Initiative to Integrate Foresight and AI into Educational Process in Libya
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: A joint initiative was launched by ICESCO the Ministry of Education the Libyan National Commission for Education Culture and Science and the Libyan Delegation to the Organization. It included the convening of a three-day training by ICESCO’s Foresight and Artificial Intelligence Centre on strategic foresight for decision-making. This training is tailored for several officials and employees of the Libyan Ministry of Education and aims at equipping them with the necessary skills and knowledge to keep pace with educational transformation and to establish a foresight unit within the Ministry. The launch also includes the development of a system for integrating AI into the educational process.

items.title: New Initiative to Integrate Foresight and AI into Educational Process in Libya
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative launched by ICESCO the Ministry of Education the Libyan National Commission for Education Culture and Science and the Libyan Delegation to the Organization delivers structured training tailored for several officials and employees of the Libyan Ministry of Education to support integrating AI into the educational/pedagogical process building a skills pipeline and AI institutional capability. It also aimed to capacitate them to establish a foresight unit within the Ministry.

items.title: Launch of New Initiative to Integrate Foresight and AI into Educational Process in Libya in Partnership with ICESCO and Ministry of Education
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The ICESCO–Ministry of Education in Libya Initiative (launched July 2024) directly contributes to reskilling and upskilling efforts by embedding AI and foresight training into Libya’s educational ecosystem. It focuses on building teacher and institutional capacity to integrate AI into teaching and learning processes thereby equipping educators with the skills to prepare students for an AI-driven future. Through workshops digital curriculum development and training for education officials the initiative strengthens national competencies in AI literacy data management and digital transformation.

items.title: The Role of the National Authority for Information Security and Safety in Regulating Emerging Technologies
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The workshop presented the Authority’s current efforts in enhancing cybersecurity readiness and establishing technical frameworks for the governance of emerging technologies including artificial intelligence blockchain and cloud computing. Among these efforts were awareness sessions on “Information Security in the Age of Artificial Intelligence” and also plans to establish cooperation frameworks with the General Authority for Communications and Informatics (GACI) to align cybersecurity standards with Libya’s National AI Policy (2024) and Ethics Charter (2025)

items.title: Cultivating effective teams of humans and AI understanding the necessary leadership capabilities
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Training project funded by the Lithuanian Research Council Summer Internship for Students. The project aims to understand how to foster successful collaboration between humans and AI in the workplace. Given that leaders lack evidence-based solutions to deal with these unprecedented new challenges this project aims to investigate and identify the leadership competencies needed to successfully lead teams composed of humans and AI (p.3).

body.name: Ministry of Economy & Innovation and Innovation Agency

items.title: Designation/operation of the Digital Services Coordinator in Lithuania (RRT)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: As Lithuania’s Digital Services Coordinator under the DSA RRT supervises and enforces platform due-diligence duties that mitigate AI-facilitated misinformation and violence. This includes handling notices/complaints and overseeing mechanisms such as trusted flaggers and out-of-court dispute settlement and supporting the DSA risk-management obligations for VLOPs/VLOSEs (systemic risk assessment and mitigation of risks linked to recommender/algorithmic systems). These tools reduce dissemination of illegal hate speech/cyber-violence and other harmful content online

body.name: Communications Regulatory Authority (Ryiu reguliavimo tarnyba RRT) Digital Services Coordinator

items.title: SDPI 2024 Supervision Review (national M&E report)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: Non-judicial remedy: the Review explains that individuals can submit complaints to the SDPI which investigates them and may use monitoring/inspections and corrective powers (instructions reprimands fines) (pp. 43 47–48). It also notes that the SDPI adopted a recommended complaint form under PDPA amendments (p. 58). Judicial/non-judicial: violations may be defended in court or out of court by applying to the Inspector of Journalists’ Ethics (p. 77). Contact details for both bodies are provided (p. 90).

body.name: State Data Protection Inspectorate (VDAI / SDPI) national GDPR supervisory authority

items.title: VSSA model AI application policies & rules
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: VSSA’s “AI Application Policy” template addresses cultural/linguistic diversity indirectly through safeguards relevant to language bias: it lists AI use for document drafting and translation (Sec. I “AI application areas”) requires high-quality training data and risk management for high-risk AI (Sec. II 8.1.5) and sets non-discrimination and transparency/explainability principles (Sec. II 8.7.1; 8.5) to help prevent biased outcomes in public services.

items.title: AI training platform for civil servants (VSSA)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: From June–Aug 2025 Lithuania delivered large-scale training for public servants on safe and ethical AI use including bias mitigation data protection and transparency with further waves planned. This builds AI literacy so deployers can identify and reduce harms linked to language or cultural bias in public services—operationalising EU AI Act duties (risk management data quality/representativeness human oversight) during 2025.

items.title: Designation of RRT as AI Act market surveillance authority and single point of contact in Lithuania
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: Designation of RRT as Lithuania’s AI Act market-surveillance authority creates the enforcement mechanism for AI impact-assessment obligations. Under the AI Act high-risk AI systems must apply risk management and where applicable conformity assessment and technical documentation; RRT supervises compliance and acts as the national contact point for guidance/complaints

body.name: Communications Regulatory Authority (Ryiu reguliavimo tarnyba or RRT) Innovation Agency (Inovaciju agentura) Ministry of the Economy and Innovation (Ekonomikos ir inovaciju ministerija)

items.title: AI training platform for civil servants (VSSA)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative establishes an AI training platform for Lithuanian civil servants to strengthen public-sector AI skills. It offers structured learning on using AI tools in daily administrative work and stresses responsible use including compliance with legal and ethical requirements. As an operational programme run by VSSA it supports continuous capacity building for AI-enabled public service delivery

items.title: AI and the Labor MarketRelationship to Industrial Revolutions Possible Futures and Policy Choices
items.justification: Report prepared by the Research Division of the Information and Communication Department of the Chancellery of the Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania (parliament) that examines the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) applications on the global economy. The work creates 4 short scenarios of the consequences of AI: optimistic (AI as an expansion of human capabilities) pessimistic (structural unemployment and inequality) futuristic/utopian/dystopian (almost complete replacement of human labor) and realistic (skills mismatch problem). It is intended for policymakers and all those interested in future developments. The conclusions emphasize that the ultimate consequences of AI likely depend more on policy decisions than on the technology (p.3).

body.name: Ministry of Economy and Innovation

items.title: National cyber-incident reporting & statistics platform operated by NCSC
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: Lithuania maintains a national platform for cyber-incident reporting and publishes periodic statistics/analyses. AI-related events are captured where systems are network-exposed supporting continuous monitoring of safety/security risks and informing mitigation. On pages 13 and 14 the document mentions cybersecurity frauds in which the use of AI is increasing.

body.name: National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)

items.title: Administrative enforcement of security obligations by SDPI (data security) and RRT (product/network security)
items.justification: Accorindg to the Review of Personal Data Protection Supervision in Lithuania document (2024) SDPI imposes corrective orders and fines for inadequate security of processing when AI systems handle personal data. RRT conducts market-surveillance and can order withdrawal/corrective measures for insecure connected products/services covering AI-enabled devices (P.42-51)

body.name: National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)

items.title: AI Governance in the Public Sector (EIMIN 2025)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: Government M&E report mapping AI use across ministries identifying transparency/ explainability gaps and recommending actions aligned with Lithuania’s AI Governance Model. It operationalises public-sector transparency duties (e.g. regular public disclosure about AI systems and their impact) and supports implementation of Seimas Resolution No. XIV-2620 principles on transparency and responsibility (p.7 16 18 48).

body.name: EIMIN VSSA CRA

items.title: Malawi NSTIP National Stakeholder Consultative Workshop
items.type: Policy Development — Launching consultations or stakeholder workshops to gather input for a future draft.
items.justification: The Malawi NSTIP workshop addresses AI literacy through: Policy Integration incorporating AI into national frameworks aligned with African Union's Science Technology and Innovation Strategy for Africa (STISA) 2034 and African Union Development Agency (AUDA) AI roadmap (p.2); Curriculum reform integrating AI across primary secondary and tertiary education to build STEM skills (pp.8-9); Gender inclusivity addressing AI gender gaps through standardized policies and accessible infrastructure (p.11); Capacity building focusing on human capital development and teacher training (pp.28); Ethical governance establishing advisory bodies and safeguarding marginalized groups (pp.711).

items.title: MACRA Data Protection Authority (Independent Oversight Body)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: MACRA Data Protection Authority enforces human oversight through monitoring compliance with Section 25 prohibition on solely automated decisions (Act p.15). Investigating complaints about automated decision-making violations via Section 44 powers (pp.26-27). Issuing compliance orders requiring safeguards for AI systems under Section 45 (pp.27-28). Registering controllers using automated processing per Registration Regulations 2025. Imposing penalties up to K50M/2% turnover for violations (Section 43 p.25). Complaint system at dpa.mw enables individuals to challenge automated decisions lacking human review. Authority ensures AI systems processing personal data maintain meaningful human control through regulatory oversight.

body.name: The Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA)

items.title: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) System for Automated Processing
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Impact assessments
items.justification: DPIA System requires pre-deployment assessment under Section 30(2)(a) for automated processing (Act p.17). Section 30(3) mandates risk evaluation and safeguards (p.17). Section 30(4) requires Authority consultation for high-risk systems (p.18). Ensures human evaluation before AI deployment ongoing monitoring and regulatory oversight. Controllers must demonstrate human oversight measures preventing purely automated decision-making.

body.name: The Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA)

items.title: MACRA Data Protection Stakeholder Engagement and Training Program
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Government institution workshops educating MDAs on Section 25 automated decision-making prohibitions (Act p.15). Stakeholder training on DPIA requirements under Section 30 for automated processing (p.17). Public awareness campaigns on data subjects' rights to challenge automated decisions under Section 44 (pp.26-27). Registration guidance teaches controllers about safeguards required by Section 25(3) when automation is permitted (p.16). Training covers individual rights compliance obligations and human control mechanisms. Educates the public sector on preventing solely automated decisions implementing human review processes and ensuring meaningful human oversight in AI/automated systems processing personal data.

body.name: The Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA)

items.title: MACRA Regulatory Sandbox
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The MACRA Regulatory Sandbox enables innovators to test AI solutions under regulatory oversight requiring compliance with risk management security and consumer safety standards. Applicants must address data protection system reliability and protocols for AI misuse. The Sandbox sets safety benchmarks for deployments helping identify and mitigate risks before full market entry.

items.title: Reserve Bank of Malawi AI-powered Cybersecurity System
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Reserve Bank of Malawi’s AI-powered cybersecurity system is designed to counter a new generation of AI-driven cyberattacks targeting the country’s financial sector where attackers already use AI to automate reconnaissance social engineering and intrusion attempts against banks and payment systems. By deploying an AI-based tool (Darktrace) that learns normal network behaviour and autonomously detects and responds to anomalous AI-enhanced attack patterns in real time the initiative directly addresses AI-powered cyber risks rather than introducing new ones thereby helping to ensure that AI systems and tools operate safely and reliably and do not exacerbate existing harms.

items.title: AI Fluency Course
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The AI Fluency course available on advances Malaysia’s national AI literacy agenda by providing a structured accessible foundation in artificial intelligence for the general public. It introduces core AI concepts practical applications and responsible usage considerations including generative AI and its societal implications. By equipping citizens with baseline digital and AI competencies the initiative supports workforce readiness informed technology adoption and broader public understanding of AI’s role in Malaysia’s digital transformation strategy.

items.title: Guidelines for Sustainable Development of Data Centres
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The 'Guideline for Sustainable Development of Data Centre' addresses Environmental Impact by mandating the declaration of Guideline for Sustainable Development of Data Centre' and by mandating the declaration of key sustainability metrics—PUE CUE and WUE—according to international standards (ISO/IEC 30134-2 30134-8 and 30134-9 respectively) (p23) to ensure data centres focus on reducing energy consumption and carbon footprints accelerating the use of renewable or clean energy and enhancing the efficiency of water consumption that directly relates with artificial intelligence.

items.title: Garis Panduan Pengadaptasian Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) Sektor Awam (Guidelines for the Adoption of AI (AI) in the Public Sector)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The guideline issued by the Ministry of digital addresses AI impact assessment through its AI Risk Management framework (p 104-115) which requires agencies to classify AI systems by risk level and apply proportionate mitigation measures and through the Self-Assessment for Ethical AI Compliance tool (p137) which operationalises ethical and impact evaluation prior to and during deployment.

items.title: Strategic Research Fund - Request for Proposal - DEVELOPMENT OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL (LLM) IN THE HEALTH SECTOR FOR MINISTRY OF HEALTH (MOH) APPLICATION Transforming Healthcare Guided by AI (AI)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: This initiative addresses Public Procurement of AI by formally procuring an AI system (a Clinical Large Language Model) through a structured government RFP that specifies objectives scope of work compliance requirements evaluation metrics and accountability mechanisms for vendors thereby embedding AI procurement within existing public-sector funding and governance controls (p. 1). It further strengthens responsible AI procurement by requiring vendors to comply with data protection laws explainable and responsible AI principles model testing auditability ongoing improvement and staff training ensuring ethical secure and performance-based delivery throughout the AI lifecycle (p4 6 10).

items.title: AI AT WORK FOR PUBLIC SERVICES 20
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: AI at Work for Public Services 2.0 addresses Public Sector Skills Development by equipping public servants with practical AI literacy and role-specific competencies including the use of Gemini and Google Workspace for free until 2028 to support daily work decision-making and service delivery. The initiative promotes continuous learning and responsible AI use ensuring public officers can safely ethically and effectively adopt AI tools as part of modern public service operations.

items.title: PROGRAM AI UNTUK RAKYAT DI KALANGAN PENJAWAT AWAM
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This is an initiative that mandate all public sectors workers to complete the 4-hour program 'AI Untuk Rakyat' online to obtain badge 'AI Aware' and 'AI Appreciate' to ensure the readiness of all public sector workers to navigate future ai digitalisation. The letter ask all public sector workers to complete the training via this link: www.ai.gov.my. The website is not available in the English version and the letter that was originally in the Malay version has been translated to the English version.

items.title: MyMahir National AI Council for Industry (MyMahirNAICI)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The MyMahir–NAICI initiative addresses AI reskilling and upskilling by establishing a national industry-led coordination platform that aligns workforce training with real-world AI adoption using tools such as the MyMahir Impact Study AI Talent Framework AI Readiness Index (AIRI) and sector-based pilot programmes to systematically identify skills gaps retrain affected workers and prepare Malaysians for emerging AI-related roles.

body.name: Ministry of Human Resources

items.title: Impact Study of AI Digital and Green Economy on the Malaysian Workforce
items.justification: The MyMahir National AI Council for Industry(MyMahir-NAICI) conducted an Impact Study on AI and Digital. It addresses reskilling and upskilling by analysing how AI and digital technologies affect existing jobs (p.44) identifying emerging roles and future skills and using these findings to inform targeted reskilling and upskilling pathways delivered via the MyMahir platform in collaboration with training providers (p.18).

body.name: Ministry of Human Resources

items.title: NATIONAL TECHNOLOGY AND INNOVATION SANDBOX - AI
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: Under the NTIS Malaysia process the NTIS Sandbox addresses Safety and Security by operating as a ready-made centrally managed web-based platform that provides a controlled and supervised environment for testing and validating AI systems prior to real-world deployment enabling early identification and mitigation of safety security and compliance risks.This national sandbox platform remains relevant and in active use as of 30 September 2025 supporting continued risk-managed AI experimentation and regulatory alignment in Malaysia.

items.title: TEL Benchmarking reports and AI Guidelines in Higher Education
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Technology-Enabled Learning (TEL) Project has redefined the digital landscape of Mauritius' higher education sector. From foundational studies to capacity building and now to AI integration this initiative has empowered six public HEIs to embrace innovation and future-proof their academic systems. Phase 4 focuses on AI integration in the higher education sector and included capacity building for 60 staff trained in generative AI tools. These trainings were limited to staffs of public universities only.

items.title: Curricular Learning Unit Program Programming and AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: In July 2025 the Secretaría de Educación Pública (SEP) formally incorporated a Curricular Learning Unit titled 'Programación e Inteligencia Artificial' into the upper secondary education curriculum within the vocational training component. The programme covers foundational AI concepts coding and ethical dimensions of AI use aiming for students to understand AI as both a technical and social tool. This constitutes a government-led formal education initiative integrating AI literacy into the national secondary curriculum directly addressing the indicator's focus on curriculum reforms at the secondary level.

items.title: Toward a Regulatory Framework for AI (AI) in Mexico Consolidated Report of the Six Thematic Discussions 2024-2025
items.justification: The Senate AI Commission's Consolidated Report of Six Thematic Discussions 2024-2025 addresses fairness and non-discrimination through specific findings and recommendations. Premise D of the Regulatory Policy Premises section establishes the need to prevent bias and algorithmic discrimination through technical standards. The UNESCO Principles section explicitly includes inclusion and non-discrimination as a core regulatory principle. The Regulatory Mechanisms section establishes that effective regulation must embed ethical values into AI systems to prevent algorithmic bias and discrimination. These findings inform the Commission's proposed regulatory framework for Mexico's forthcoming AI legislation.

items.title: IMSS Pilot Program for Registration of Digital Platform Workers under Mandatory Social Security
items.justification: On 24 June 2025 the IMSS Consejo Técnico published in the DOF the General Rules of the Pilot Program for the incorporation of digital platform workers into the mandatory social security regime (ACDO.AS2.HCT.270525/132.P.DIR) entering into force on 1 July 2025. The program requires platforms to register as employers enrol workers earning above the minimum wage and manage social security contributions. It directly implements Articles 291-F and 291-K of Chapter IX Bis enforcing the labour rights protections for algorithmically-managed platform workers established by the framework.

body.name: Secretariat of Labour and Social Welfare (STPS)

items.title: The Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare launches the course AI for Life and Work
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Mexican Secretariat of Labour and Social Welfare (STPS) launched the free online course 'Artificial Intelligence for Life and Work' on August 27 2025 through its PROCADIST platform. The course aims to equip workers and enterprises with foundational AI competencies to prepare the workforce for technological transitions. Developed in collaboration with Microsoft and the Red for Cibersecurity) it represents a government-led capacity building initiative explicitly addressing AI-driven reskilling at the national level.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: The Mongolian AI assessment report developed jointly by the Government of Mongolia and UNDP. It highlights that while Mongolia has taken steps to improve digital literacy a broader approach is needed to equip citizens with AI-related critical thinking ethical considerations and data literacy. Specifically on page 37 Pillar 1. 2 Skills report recommends to expanding initiatives such as the E-Mongolia Academy and integrating AI literacy into public education and professional development programs those can ensure that both individuals and government officials are better prepared for AI adoption. The report contributes to knowledge generation on AI literacy by identifying policy gaps and proposing future actions.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: On page 66. Pillar 3. 4 Transparency addressed the issue as follows 'Robust AI governance frameworks should also incorporate effective mechanisms that empower individuals adversely affected by AI decisions to challenge and seek redress for such outcomes' which means that AI frameworks should allow people to challenge and ask remedy for AI errors and harms. The assessment document is initiated and requested by the Ministry of Digital Development and Communications and assessment is conducted and funded by UNDP.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: Page 34 Pillar 1 Infrastructure First recommendation says as follows: Promote the Development of Energy-Efficient Data Centers: As Mongolia advances towards the widespread adoption of AI the demand for reliable scalable and sustainable data infrastructure is expected to increase substantially. To address this growing need it is critical for the government to prioritize the development of energy-efficient data centers. Mongolia’s cold climate and abundant renewable energy resources present a strategic opportunity to establish cost effective environmentally sustainable data infrastructure. These natural advantages position the country as a competitive location for green data centers that can underpin long term digital transformation.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: The report developed jointly by the Government of Mongolia and UNDP assessed current state of Mongolian AI ecosystem and its readiness for further development in many areas of responsible AI. In relation to the Fairness and Non-discrimination dimension report explicitly recommended establishing an AI Ethics Committee that can provide oversight on risk assessment privacy protection and bias mitigation in context of AI governance in Enhance AI Governance and Regulatory Frameworks section Pillar 2 1 Technology on page 48. Also report recommended to reduce existing biases in relation to population including gender age ethnicity disability and other important factors in Pillar 3 2 Inclusivity section on page 62.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The research 'Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment of Mongolia' was initiated by Ministry of Digital development Innovation and Communications and funded and conducted by UNDP. Research revealed that there is a notable gender gap in digital competencies—favoring women. Women scored 10.9% higher than men across key digital skills which presents opportunities for Mongolia fostering a more gender inclusive AI workforce and ensuring women’s participation in AI development and deployment. Report recommended reducing economic social gender equality in the context of AI and promoting gender equality through establishing AI committees with representatives from gender equality advocates in Pillar 3.2 Inclusivity section on page 62.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: On Page 58 Pillar 3 Accountability addressed human oversight as follows: Furthermore it is required that digital systems which collect process and use data without human input should incorporate a technological solution for decisions made by algorithms to be able to be reviewed reprocessed and reviewed and confirmed by a person.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: In relation to AI Impact assessment mentioned 12 times in the document. The report developed jointly by the Government of Mongolia and UNDP discusses the need to establish AI risk categorization frameworks and algorithmic impact assessment tools at the government level. It serves as a knowledge-generation initiative that identifies policy gaps and provides recommendations for integrating impact assessment practices into Mongolia’s AI governance. For example on page 28 Pillar 3 Ethical AI 3. Safety. document mentioned 'establish an official AI ... algorithmic impact assessment tools at the government level'.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: The report developed by the Government of Mongolia and UNDP notes that while Mongolia has a strong commitment to e-governance and data protection it lacks mechanisms for algorithmic transparency. In order to improve transparency accountability and public trust in AI-driven decision-making process accountability section (p.59 Pillar 3 1) recommends enhancing transparency by establishing a public-sector AI Algorithm Registry to document and disclose key information about government-used AI systems. Report further notes that opportunities for Mongolia to enhance documentation and disclosure of AI use in the public sector remain (p. 29) and although there are strong data protection laws AI-specific guidelines need improvement (p. 41).

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: The report developed jointly by the Government of Mongolia and UNDP the assessment report provides a foundational understanding of the current state of Mongolia’s AI ecosystem and constitutes an important initial step toward identifying its strengths existing gaps and opportunities for inclusive and sustainable development. The report recommended that Mongolia should establish a Government AI Procurement Framework with standardized guidelines to enhance transparency and efficiency in Pillar 2 1 Technology on Page 48. Also report highlighted lack of adequate training programs on AI procurement among public servants and introduction of clear and standardized guidelines for AI procurement oversight and performance evaluation on page 70.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: The report developed jointly by the Government of Mongolia and UNDP the report revealed that there is significant skill gaps among civil servants both technical and non-technical as well as a lack of adequate training programs on AI procurement ethics and governance. In addition report explicitly addressed need of establishing and expanding formal training programs to build necessary knowledge and skills for AI adoption among civil servants. Moreover report provided recommendations for strengthening AI Governance Skills Across the Public Sector building Technical AI Capacity Within Government Institutions and expanding Digital Literacy and IT Skills Among Civil Servants in Pillar 2 3 skills section on page 53 in the report.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: The AI landscape assessment of Mongolia report developed jointly by the Government of Mongolia and UNDP discusses that there is currently no comprehensive policy addressing technical AI skill development in Mongolia. However report recommended to establish national AI skills framework for AI workforce training partnerships with the private sector and incentives for upskilling. On Page 53 Pillar 2 3 Skills section addresses importance of strengthening AI Governance Skills Across the Public Sector building Technical AI Capacity Within Government Institutions strengthening AI Recruitment and Talent Retention Strategies expanding Digital Literacy and IT Skills Among Civil Servants and leveraging Online and International Training.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: The report developed jointly by the Government of Mongolia and UNDP discusses that while Mongolia has existing regulations provide a foundation for assessing digital systems and ensuring data protection there are opportunities to establish an official AI risk categorization framework and algorithmic impact assessment tools at the government level. The document recommended to enhance AI safety and security in several sections specifically on page 65 Pillar 3. 3 Safety as follows: 'AI safety governance and risk assessment should go beyond a narrow focus on cybersecurity to encompass a broader range of potential harms that may affect individuals communities and society as a whole' and 'should focus on data privacy security' etc.

items.title: AI Landscape Assessment of Mongolia
items.justification: The report developed jointly by the Government of Mongolia and UNDP assessed current state of Mongolian AI ecosystem and its readiness for further development in many areas of responsible AI. The assessment was requested and initiated by the Government of Mongolia to UNDP and UNDP was funded and conducted the assessment in 2025. The report explicitly stated that there is no comprehensive AI transparency framework in current Mongolian government policies and regulations and recommended Government of Mongolia to undertake a systematic review and enhancement of AI transparency-related regulations in near future in Pillar 3 4 Transparency section on page 67.

items.title: Report on the Implementation of the Education System Digitalization Strategy 2022-2027 for the Year 2024
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The initiative reports on how AI literacy has been addressed as part of framework implementation. The implementation report documents that workshops on the ethical application of AI were organised in secondary schools with 6 workshops involving 146 students aimed at raising awareness and understanding of AI-related ethical issues (page 7).

body.name: Ministry of Education Science and Innovation

items.title: The AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024)
items.justification: In the Inclusivity chapter under Recommendations it is written that policymakers should engage Civil Society and Minority Groups in AI Policy Development: Involve representatives from civil society gender advocacy groups and minority communities in discussions about AI policy and project design. Their insights can ensure that AI policies address unique needs of underrepresented populations. Montenegro government has a role responsible for convening these stakeholders and integrating their input into national AI strategies and regulations. By leading participatory consultations and embedding diversity considerations into policy processes government ensures that AI governance reflects the cultural and linguistic diversity in Montenegro.

items.title: The AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024)
items.justification: AILA Montenegro (2024) addresses fairness/non-discrimination by highlighting bias risks and recommending measures to prevent discriminatory AI. It notes AI readiness must address risks like bias (Background note page 6). Under AI ethics it recommends a national ethics/accountability framework with standards focusing on fairness (Pillar 3 - Accountability pages 36–37) and Inclusivity framework to reduce inequalities promote representative data and bias mitigation and require gender and diversity audits of AI systems (Pillar 3 - Inclusivity pages 38–39). Strategic recommendations reiterate ethical AI standards emphasizing fairness and inclusive AI practices (page 45).

items.title: The AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024)
items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024) conducted by the Ministry of Public Administration and UNDP represents the first systematic observation and baseline assessment of AI implementation in Montenegro. Gender equality is addressed in the Inclusivity section. Page 38 highlights the need to reduce inequalities across socioeconomic and gender lines. Recommendations include mandating gender and diversity audits for AI systems incorporating gender impact metrics in AI evaluations and engaging gender advocacy groups in AI policy development (pages 38 and 39).

items.title: The AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024)
items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024) conducted by the Ministry of Public Administration and UNDP represents the first systematic baseline assessment of AI implementation in Montenegro. The report highlights the importance of accountability transparency and citizen oversight in AI governance. It recommends the establishment of a national AI coordination or oversight body and mechanisms enabling individuals to challenge AI-driven decisions in order to ensure meaningful human oversight and responsibility in AI use (Ethical AI and Governance sections pages 36–41).

items.title: The AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024)
items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment (AILA) addresses impact assessments indirectly by evaluating Montenegro’s readiness to manage AI risks. While it does not mandate formal ex-ante or post-impact assessments the report identifies the absence of systematic AI risk and impact assessment mechanisms as a governance gap. It recommends developing structured AI safety and accountability frameworks including regular risk assessments and oversight mechanisms for future AI deployments (Pillar 3: Ethical AI - Accountability (pages 36-37) and Safety (pages 40–41).

items.title: Training on AI within the General Programme for the Professional Training and Development of Civil Servants and Public Employees
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative is an official AI training for civil servants organised by the Human Resources Administration as part of the General programme for the professional training and development of civil servants and public employees. The training calendar for February-June 2025 and September-December 2025 lists the course “Vještacka inteligencija” (Artificial Intelligence) as a full-day session in Podgorica. By teaching basic AI concepts and applications to state employees it strengthens their digital and analytical skills and supports public sector capacity to work with AI systems.

items.title: AI AGE - AI Supported Identification of Novel Non-invasive Biomarkers of Aging
items.justification: The AI-AGE project proposes the use of machine learning algorithms and evaluation of AI tools to train and create prediction models to identify novel non-invasive biomarkers of aging and increased risk for development of age-related conditions. AI-AGE project is implemented through partnership between the Faculty for Information Systems and Technologies (UDG) and Faculty of Medicine (UoM). The project is funded by the Ministry of Education Science and Innovation. Through research activities training events and collaboration with Montenegrin institutions the project builds technical capacity and knowledge that can later support evidence-based policy making and research in the public sector particularly in healthcare and education.

items.title: The National conference AI in the function of innovation and services
items.justification: The National Conference “AI in the Function of Innovation and Services” was held on 22 November 2024 at the Science and Technology Park Montenegro in Podgorica organised by the Association of Managers of Montenegro (AMM). The event gathered representatives of the public sector the technology community and the business sector focusing on the potential of artificial intelligence to improve innovation public administration and services. The panel discussion featured Sava Laketic (Director of the Tax Administration) and MinasTrubljanin (General Director in the Ministry of Finance) who discussed digitalisation tax compliance and the possibility of using AI for real-time monitoring of budget spending.

items.title: NCC Montenegro - The National Competence Centre for High-Performance Computing
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National Competence Centre (NCC) Montenegro established in 2021 under the EuroCC project and coordinated by UDG in cooperation with Ministry of Education Science and Innovation provides continuous training workshops and mentoring focused on artificial intelligence data analytics and high-performance computing (HPC). Through cooperation with academia industry and public institutions the NCC enhances digital competencies reskills professionals for AI-related fields and supports workforce adaptation to AI-driven technologies in Montenegro. The NCC serves as a link between national stakeholders and European HPC resources helping businesses researchers and policymakers utilize the power of advanced computing technologies.

items.title: The AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024)
items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (UNDP 2024) analyses the country’s readiness for AI adoption. The AILA initiative addresses reskilling and upskilling by identifying significant AI-related skills gaps and recommending targeted capacity building. It highlights low technical and non-technical AI skills within government (Pillar 1 – Skills pp. 24–25) and calls for comprehensive AI training programmes. As an enabler it proposes national AI and data skills initiatives digital competency training and rural AI skills centres encourage upskilling through online and remote Learning (Pillar 2 – Skills pp. 28–29) ensuring workforce readiness for AI-driven change.

items.title: The AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024)
items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro addresses safety and security in the context of AI under Pillar 3: Ethical AI specifically the Safety chapter. The report identifies that Montenegro is at an early stage in managing AI-related risks and highlights the need to prevent malicious or unintended use of AI systems and reduce security and ethical risks (Pillar 3 – Safety pages 40–41). It recommends establishing a national AI safety framework adopting risk assessment and mitigation measures strengthening cybersecurity and aligning AI safety standards with international best practices to ensure secure and responsible AI deployment (Recommendations pages 40–41).

items.title: The AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024)
items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment (AILA) Montenegro (2024) addresses transparency and explainability in a dedicated chapter Transparency (pages 42 and 43). The report notes that transparency and explainability of AI systems are currently limited and not systematically ensured particularly in the public sector. It recommends to develop an AI Transparency Framework strengthening transparency by clearly informing users and citizens when AI systems are used improving the explainability of AI-supported decisions and defining responsibilities and procedures that allow individuals to understand monitor and challenge decisions influenced by AI.

items.title: An Engineering School Dedicated to Digital Transition and AI
items.justification: The Minister of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform signed an agreement to establish the Higher School of Engineering in Digital Transition Digital Technology and Artificial Intelligence as well as the development of specialised training programs in these fields. This initiative reflects the desire to bring training programs closer to real-world needs aligning academic pathways with the needs of local areas and the priorities of national economic and technological development as outlined by the Ministry's website.

body.name: The General Directorate for Digital Transition

items.title: Signing of an agreement for the regulation of ethical and technological uses
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data (CNDP) the Commission for the Right of Access to Information (CDAI) and the Rabat branch of the Economic Military School (EGE) signed an agreement in the field of business intelligence and the regulation of ethical and technological uses. The president of the CNDP  Mr Seghrouchni stated that this agreement aims to encourage and explain the risks of unethical use of technologies particularly with regard to 'deepfakes' and 'fake news.' This aligns with the framework's last two recommendations supporting the cross-sectoral collaboration to enhance research in this scope and raise awareness.

items.title: The National Control Commission for the Protection of Personal Data (CNDP) consults experts and institutions to regulate AI
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The National Commission for Personal Data Protection (CNDP) has initiated a consultation regarding AI and personal data protection. The goal is to ensure that citizens have access to remedies in cases of automatic decision-making. The CNDP has begun deliberations on AI data processing and has opened this consultation to experts and institutions for their input.

items.title: Human Rights in Morocco and the Challenges of Emerging Issues
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National Council of Human Rights emphasised the importance of creating a national legal framework to regulate the use of AI in line with a human rights during a workshop held on December 18 2024. They also highlighted the necessity of anticipating the risks associated with certain digital applications and their potential negative impact particularly on children and vulnerable individuals. The council underscored the need to achieve a balance between technological advancement and the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms.

items.title: National Conference on AI Summary Report
items.justification: On the sidelines of the first National Conference on Artificial Intelligence held in Rabat on July 1 and 2 2025 the Minister of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform signed a cooperation agreement with Mr. Martin Tisné 'Current AI' on the technological development of artificial intelligence in the public interest. This agreement aims to promote ethical secure and inclusive artificial intelligence by supporting pilot projects in high-impact areas such as health linguistic diversity and governance.

items.title: The 28th edition of the Fez Festival of World Spiritual Music
items.justification: The Minister of Digital Transition and Administration Reform participated in the Fez Forum in the dialogue session entitled: 'What can artificial intelligence offer to culture and heritage?' where she highlighted the vast potential offered by AI to monitor in real time the state of conservation of monuments archaeological sites and historical structures thanks to advanced and precise tools. She also emphasised that AI helps overcome linguistic and sensory barriers thanks to neural translation speech synthesis techniques and sign language recognition which ensures a wider dissemination of culture among various segments of society. She added that AI constitutes a strategic lever for promoting Amazigh heritage.

items.title: National Platform for Responsible AI
items.justification: The Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform and the National Commission for the Control of Personal Data Protection have concluded a partnership for the development of a national platform for responsible AI and a platform framework based on an LLM. The agreement concerns the establishment of a responsible AI framework that integrates the design of a national platform framework based on an LLM developed with national specificities taking into consideration the Moroccan language and culture the national legal framework and sovereign digital identity. This aligns with one of the strategic goals established at the National Conference on AI which aims to leverage AI to preserve the national cultural and linguistic heritage.

items.title: National Conference on AI Summary Report
items.type: Policy Development — Commissioning concept notes white papers or outlines that serve as inputs for drafting.
items.justification: The summary report of the National Conference on AI recapitulates the first roadmap for a National AI Strategy outlining and validating the major strategic orientations in this regard (p.7). One of the proposals aims to pinpoint strategic locations for the establishment of data centres linked to renewable energy production specifically solar and wind with a focus on southern Morocco to enhance performance sustainability and energy independence (p.18). Additionally one of the pillars for action supports the responsible investment in essential and sovereign digital infrastructures (p. 31).

items.title: Green Cloud Morocco
items.justification: Several agreements were signed during a ceremony held on the sidelines of the First National Conference on AI. One of the agreements was initialled by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform and the Founder and Secretary General of the Digital Cooperation Organization (DCO). It includes the Green Cloud Morocco initiative which will position Morocco as a regional hub for sustainable digital infrastructures. This project includes the construction of three AI factories including a green data centre enabling CO2 emissions and energy costs to be reduced by up to 70%. (Paragraphs 17-21)

items.title: National Conference on AI Summary Report
items.type: Policy Development — Commissioning concept notes white papers or outlines that serve as inputs for drafting.
items.justification: The National Conference on Artificial Intelligence outlined and validated the major strategic orientations forming the foundation of Morocco's future National AI roadmap (p.7). The summary report of the National Conference on AI recapitulates the first discussions and recommendations for a National AI Strategy. One of the strategic orientations is to produce ethical guidelines to ensure that AI prioritises fairness transparency and accountability and addresses potential risks such as discrimination and job loss p.44.

items.title: National Conference on AI Summary Report
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: On the sidelines of the first National Conference on Artificial Intelligence held in Rabat on July 1 and 2 2025 the Minister of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform signed a cooperation agreement with Mr. Martin Tisné 'Current AI' on the technological development of artificial intelligence in the public interest. This agreement aims to promote ethical secure and inclusive artificial intelligence by supporting pilot projects in high-impact areas such as health linguistic diversity and governance. This will help ensure an inclusive and fair development of AI in the Kingdom.

items.title: Women in Tech Salon Connecting Women
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: One of the projects established by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform to strengthen gender equality in AI is the 'Women in Tech Salon' training program. This program was launched by the Ministry in collaboration with a private entity with the objective of strengthening the skills of female civil servants in new information and communication technologies such as AI IoT Cloud and the metaverse. This aligns with the strategy's objective of bridging the digital divide and promoting digital inclusion for women through upskilling measures.

items.title: The 3rd Parliamentary Economic Forum
items.justification: On the sidelines of the 3rd Parliamentary Economic Forum in Marrakech the Minister Delegate for Digital Transition and Administrative Reform stressed the urgency of responsible deployment of AI based on principles of ethics transparency and trust. The minister called for the establishment of a specific legal framework. This should clarify responsibilities impose technical audits guarantee the transparency of algorithms and protect privacy. She emphasised that a draft framework law is already in preparation along with the creation of a national directorate dedicated to AI. Thus technical audits will enable human oversight when evaluating and monitoring AI technologies. Transparency requirements will also facilitate oversight.

items.title: Training of judicial staff in digitalization and AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: A partnership agreement was signed between the Ministries of Justice and Higher Education Scientific Research and Innovation focusing on training Justice Ministry staff in digitalization and AI. The Minister of Higher Education emphasized the importance of strengthening the professional and communication skills of Justice Ministry staff to address the challenges posed by AI and digitalization and to confront the growing constraints. He noted in a similar statement that this agreement will pave the way for further partnerships with universities to ensure the ongoing training of all Justice Ministry personnel and provide new training programs to meet the major challenges ahead.

items.title: The National AI Conference
items.justification: The first National Conference on Artificial Intelligence engaged multiple stakeholders in drafting the AI roadmap in Morocco. Ministers emphasized that training public and private sector stakeholders in AI is essential to fully harnessing its potential and making it a driver of sustainable growth. They highlighted AI's role in modernizing education enhancing economic competitiveness transforming the labor market and optimizing energy management. The presentations also stressed the need for a suitable legal framework the development of local skills and leveraging Morocco's strengths-digital connectivity green energy and human capital-to establish it as a regional technology hub.

body.name: General Directorate for Digital Transition

items.title: National Platform for Responsible AI
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform and the National Commission for the Control of Personal Data Protection have concluded a partnership for the development of a national platform for responsible AI and a platform framework based on an LLM. The objective is to provide citizens businesses and administrations with generative and conversational AI tools that are secure efficient and respectful of fundamental rights. This aligns with the strategic goal of establishing robust infrastructure for AI operation enabling both AI security and efficiency.

body.name: The General Directorate for Digital Transition

items.title: National Conference on AI Summary Report
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: On the sidelines of the first National Conference on AI the Minister of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform signed a cooperation agreement with Current AI to develop AI in the public interest. This agreement aims to promote ethical secure and inclusive artificial intelligence by supporting pilot projects in high-impact areas such as health linguistic diversity and governance. It aims to strengthen international cooperation around transparent responsible and beneficial AI particularly emphasising Moroccan engagement in linguistic diversity health and accountability (p. 24). The first National Conference on AI built the strategic axes of the national AI strategy(p.7) in alignment with the recommendations of the framework.

items.title: INTIC Leads Discussion on AI in Mozambican Education During Pedagogical Training Session
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative focused on training educators on the role of AI in teaching and learning. During the Matola Pedagogical Training Session INTIC officials introduced teachers to AI concepts ethical considerations risks and strategies for responsible integration in classrooms. The programme strengthened digital pedagogy and aimed to build teacher capacities to understand and guide AI use in schools.

items.title: III Seminar on CybercrimeCombating Organized Crime in the Era of AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The III Seminar on Cybercrime held by the Office of the Attorney General (PGR) with participation from INTIC and UNODC aimed to strengthen institutional capacity to prevent and combat AI-enabled cybercrime. The event addressed challenges such as AI-driven fraud organized cybercrime and threats to children and critical infrastructure. It promoted ethical AI use in the justice system enhanced interagency collaboration and supported the development of digital skills legal frameworks and technological solutions to mitigate AI-facilitated misinformation and violence. The event's objectives underscored classify the main attacks and crimes against children and adolescents facilitated by the use of AI and identify and disseminate best practices for their effective protection.

items.title: Safer Internet Month Understand How Scammers Use AI Such as Voice Cloning and Deepfakes to Commit Fraud
items.justification: During Safer Internet Month the National Institute of Information and Communication Technologies (INTIC) published an awareness article explaining how AI is used in online fraud including voice cloning and deepfakes. The initiative notes that “techniques such as voice cloning and deepfakes have become common among criminals” enabling 'misinformation manipulation and financial harm'. It provides guidance on verifying content authenticity identifying phishing and investment scams and avoiding manipulated media. The initiative addresses AI-facilitated misinformation through public education and digital literacy.

items.title: 3rd Edition of the Lusophone Internet Governance Forum Panel 2 Linguistic and Cultural Diversity on the Internet Challenges and Opportunities for the Portuguese Language in the Digital Environment
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The 3rd Lusophone Internet Governance Forum (between 22-23 of September) organized by Mozambique’s National Institute of ICT (INTIC) on 22 September 2025 in Maputo featured a panel on “Linguistic and Cultural Diversity on the Internet.” The session addressed the role of Portuguese the integration of local varieties and the lack of AI and digital tools for African Portuguese indigenous and local languages.

items.title: AI Challenges and Opportunities for Mozambique
items.justification: Artificial Intelligence: Challenges and Opportunities for Mozambique addresses AI reskilling and upskilling through a structured workforce development approach in Sections 7.3–7.8 (p.108–114). Section 7.4.1 (p.110) emphasises continuous professional development and postgraduate AI training including the UEM Master’s in AI. Sections 7.5 and 7.6 (p.112–113) propose a national human resources reference framework and map technical non-technical and transversal AI skills. Section 7.7 (p.113–114) promotes formal non-formal and continuous training pathways including bootcamps and certifications while Section 7.8 (p.114) highlights public–private partnerships internships and training programmes to support labour market insertion.

items.title: AI Challenges and Opportunities for Mozambique
items.justification: The INTIC Book Artificial Intelligence: Challenges and Opportunities for Mozambique addresses AI safety and security. Section 3.4 (Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in Mozambique) point 10 (Safety and Data Security) notes that AI in corporate and everyday applications poses significant safety and data security risks that must be managed to ensure system reliability. Cybercriminals are actively seeking to exploit AI. Section 4 emphasizes that safe AI adoption requires infrastructure human capacity and regulations. Section 11 stresses continuous updates and that safety must be considered throughout the AI project lifecycle from planning to deployment and maintenance.

items.title: International Conference on Applied Research in Education
items.justification: At the International Conference on Applied Research in Education 2025 Myanmar’s Ministry of Education highlighted the integration of artificial intelligence and language resources in education and research alongside broader themes of science and technology for sustainable development. The event emphasized the need to build future generations’ capacity through AI literacy digital education and research-driven innovation to advance national and regional progress.

items.title: AI training course under the Mekong-Korea Cooperation Project at the Industrial Technology Training Institute in Yangon
items.justification: Myanmar is listed as a participating country in the Mekong–Republic of Korea Cooperation Fund (MKCF) projects for the period 2013–2025 (see p.13 of From the Mekong–Republic of Korea Cooperation Fund (MKCF) Projects document). Within this framework on 11 November 2025 the Ministry of Science and Technology launched an AI training course under the Mekong–Republic of Korea Cooperation Project at the Industrial Technology Training Institute in Yangon.

items.title: AI (AI) Technology Training Course
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Across the five initiatives (2024–2025) government-run AI trainings focused on basic AI concepts history types of AI machine learning generative AI practical applications ethics and the use of AI tools in public administration. They aimed to build AI literacy counter misinformation and deepfakes and improve digital skills among civil servants in regions including Mandalay Ayeyarwady Lashio Yangonand Nay Pyi Taw.

items.title: Orientation Program Report on AI Cyber Security and Digital Literacy 2081 (2024/25)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The capacity development program was organized by the National Assembly (Upper House) for its members to enhance knowledge on digital technologies and get acquainted with 'AI cybersecurity and digital literacy'. 32 participants including 17 members(parliamentarians) of the Assembly and other officials took part in this training.

items.title: AI Impact Game
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The AI Impact Game supports AI Literacy by enabling educators to experience discuss and reflect on the impact of generative AI in schools building awareness of opportunities and risks and stimulating critical thinking about policies and responsible use in education. Participants explore future scenarios from different roles which helps them understand how AI could affect teaching learning and school organisation. It does this through workshops which is supported by downloadable documents to let schools run this themselves.

items.title: Digital Literacy - Illustrations of the core objectives
items.justification: The SLO (National Center of Expertise for Curriculum) has created this illustration document to provide concrete educational examples for translating the framework into classroom practice . It addresses this through :1. Foundational Knowledge: Explaining that AI learns from human-provided data and that algorithms are human-made (Section 22D p.1)2. Technical Understanding: Describing sensors Large Language Models (LLMs) and training methods like supervised learning (Section 21D p. 4).3. Practical Skills: Training AI systems to recognise images or using LLMs to structure texts (Section 21D p.4).4. Critical Evaluation: Discussing bias in datasets the ethics of AI in healthcare and the need for AI regulations (Sections 21D & 23C p.4)
