items.title: BENEDMO (Belgium-Netherlands Digital Media Observatory)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: BENEDMO identifies and analyses harmful disinformation across the the flemish and dutch regions and develops cross-border multidisciplinary tools research and fact-checking to counter it. It builds an expert network advances early detection supports policy analysis and strengthens media literacy through targeted educational programs and public initiatives. It has received supplementary grants from the Dutch government to strengthen the fact-checking network in the Netherlands (as mentioned in the framework Page 7). Publications on the provided link show that the project is still ongoing.

body.name: Autoriteit Consument & Markt and Dutch Data Protection Authority

items.title: isdatechtzonl
items.justification: IsDatEchtZo addresses AI-facilitated misinformation by explaining generative-AI deepfakes and chatbots offering practical detection tips checklists and educational materials to spot AI images/videos and misleading chatbot outputs. The project started in 2021 but is still ongoing: https://www.isdatechtzo.nl/wat-is-nepnieuws/ai-en-desinformatie/je-gelooft-je-eigen-ogen-toch-wel/. It is fully funded by BZK (Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations). see: https://www.isdatechtzo.nl/over-ons/

body.name: Autoriteit Consument & Markt and Dutch Data Protection Authority

items.title: Dealing with Misinformation for Local Authorities
items.justification: The evidence is a guidance developed by the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations addressing AI-facilitated misinformation and violence by providing local officials with legal and practical frameworks to identify and respond to synthetic threats. It explicitly defines deepfakes (audio/video) and generative AI as emerging drivers of misinformation that can confuse public debate. It offers a step-wise response plan ('Stappenplan') including platform reporting mechanisms to remove harmful AI content and legal steps for officials facing intimidation (Chapter 3 & 4).

body.name: Autoriteit Consument & Markt and Dutch Data Protection Authority

items.title: Directorate Coordination Algorithms (DCA)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The DCA strengthens access to redress by coordinating oversight of algorithmic systems across Dutch regulators ensuring complaints are effectively routed to competent authorities. It supports existing complaint desks (“loketten”) and clarifies citizens’ rights through guidance and outreach making it easier for individuals to report harms and obtain corrective measures. The DCA also facilitates enforcement actions such as warnings. corrective orders or sanctions ensuring remedies are not only available but actionable. Since it is part of the Dutch Data Protection Authority(AP) grievances can be filed through AP.

body.name: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP)

items.title: Strategy for Childrens Rights Online
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The 'Strategie kinderrechten online' or the 'Children’s Rights Online Strategy' informs the House of Representatives about the government's commitment to a safe and healthy digital living environment for children and young people. On page 6 Section 3 (“Education as a foundation for digital resilience”) it calls for “clear frameworks for the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education with due regard for autonomy privacy and equal opportunities.” The same section outlines a curriculum revision to include “digital systems media security privacy data and AI. Page 3 (Section 1) highlights risks from “harmful algorithms and addictive design techniques” which implicitly includes AI algorithms.

items.title: Child Rights Impact Assessment
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Impact assessments
items.justification: It addresses children’s rights in the context of AI by offering a structured framework to identify assess and mitigate digital service risks to children’s well-being and rights. The CRIA Manual discusses AI in Section 2.2 (p. 9) as a technology that may require a (FRAIA) alongside the CRIA when digital services use algorithmic or AI systems. It situates AI within risk-based design considerations. Section 3.5 (pp. 20–21) details risks from AI-driven systems algorithms smart toys behavioural design biometrics like profiling and manipulation. The Ministry of BZK has applied CRIA to Instagram Snapchat and TikTok https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/documenten/kamerstukken/2025/09/04/kamerbrief-bij-kinderrechten-impact-assessments

body.name: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations (BZK) plays a coordinating role monitoring progress and adjusting policy changes

items.title: Research report on the implementation of KIA
items.justification: The report addresses children’s rights in the context of AI by evaluating how digital services (like TikTok Instagram and Snapchat) affect children’s well-being and fundamental rights. It serves as a self-assessment tool to help platforms identify discuss and mitigate AI-related risks such as algorithmic profiling recommender systems and dark patterns that can influence children’s autonomy privacy and safety. For the benefit of children the report explains AI in simpler terms 'Social media apps use smart computers that work with different types of technologies. Think of AI or algorithms. These smart computers help the app show you the content in your feed.' Reference: Chapter 1.2–1.3 (pp. 7–9) and Chapter 3 (pp. 17–20)

body.name: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations (BZK) plays a coordinating role monitoring progress and adjusting policy changes

items.title: GPT-NL
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Netherlands will develop its own language model called GPT-NL. The model is being developed by research organization TNO the Netherlands Forensic Institute (NFI) and the ICT cooperative SURF under the guidance of The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy (EZK). GPT-NL promotes cultural and linguistic diversity by developing a Dutch-language large model grounded in local data culture and societal values. It addresses English dominance in AI by training on high-quality Dutch datasets from consenting providers and engaging public institutions to ensure representativeness.

items.title: ALT-EDIC
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The Alliance for Language Technologies-EDIC preserves cultural & linguistic diversity by federating language and multimodal resources for all EU national and regional languages (including low-resource languages) funding model development that supports multilingual/multimodal capabilities building bias-aware evaluation/certification and running a cultural outreach programme to involve data-producers and public administrations. The Dutch government has co-financed this programme and participates as a full member.

body.name: Algorithms Coordination Directorate (DCA) and Government AI Validation Team (Rijks Al-validatieteam)

items.title: ELSA Lab for Technical Industry
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The AiNed ELSA Labs programme explicitly lists energy & sustainability as one of its core application domains. The ELSA Lab for Technical Industry emphasises “contributions to global sustainability goals” through responsible AI deployment in industry.  This shapes the focus on reducing environmental footprint and aligning AI use with sustainable development.

body.name: Algorithms Coordination Directorate (DCA) and Government AI Validation Team (Rijks Al-validatieteam)

items.title: Generative AI and Sustainability
items.justification: This report directly addresses the environmental impact of Generative AI (GenAl) by investigating its 'sustainability costs'—specifically energy consumption CO2 emissions and water consumption (p.5-7). It then provides mitigation recommendations for government organizations and the Ministry (BZK) . Key actions include creating a sustainable digitalization strategy monitoring energy use and choosing GenAl models sustainably .(Pg-6)

body.name: Algorithms Coordination Directorate (DCA) and Government AI Validation Team (Rijks Al-validatieteam)

items.title: Algorithm Testing Framework
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Netherlands Court of Audit (NCA) addresses fairness and non-discrimination by acting as an independent watchdog. Its initiative audits government algorithms specifically for risks of bias and discrimination holding the government accountable. Through the Algorithm Testing Framework first launched in 2021 it published a report 'Understanding algorithms' followed by a 2022 audit which investigated 9 government algorithms and found 6 failed to meet basic requirements exposing 'risks of bias'. In 2024 the updated framework assessed three algorithms for objectivity security and IT management revealing deficiencies in the Royal Netherlands Marechaussee and GDPR non-compliance in Rijkswaterstaat although no bias was detected.

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP RDI Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: Non-discrimination in algorithms and data
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The RADIO (IT-AcademieOverheid) AI programme addresses fairness/non-discrimination by providing targeted learning and capacity-building. It specifically has an 'E-learning – non-discriminatie in algoritmes” module microlearnings on the ethical side of AI webinars and workshops that teach how algorithmic bias arises and how to prevent it plus it also has the Nationale AI-course covering privacy reliability and fairness concerns.

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP RDI Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: DUOs approach to fraud found to be discriminatory and illegal
items.justification: The Dutch Education Executive Agency DUO used an algorithm to check whether students were abusing the grant for students living away from home. This was found to be discriminatory and therefore unlawful by the Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) after an investigation. The algorithm used a risk profile based on 'Type of education'  'distance'  and 'age'. These factors were established based on 'experience and common sense' with no objective justification.This practice led to indirect discrimination against students with a non-European migration background. DUO was asked to suspend the use of the algorithm and the government announced refunds/compensation for affected students.

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP RDI Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: Green and Digital Jobs Action Plan
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: In the section on 'Pillar 1: Increasing intake in beta-technical education' the letter states that a key focus of the actions is on 'underrepresented groups of students' in technical subjects and career choices. The letter explicitly mentions that this includes a focus on 'more gender equality and diversity'. It is also mentioned in the government website under the Ministry of Education Culture and Science here. https://www.government.nl/topics/gender-equality/womens-labour-force-participation

body.name: NCDR (National Coordinator against discrimination and racism) and FRAIA (Impact Assessment Fundamental rights and algorithms)

items.title: Algorithm Register
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — AI registers
items.justification: The Dutch Algorithm Register addresses human oversight by mandating transparency. It requires government bodies to publicly document their algorithms using a standard template. This template explicitly asks agencies to declare their human oversight procedures in the human_intervention field (in Dutch: 'Menselijke tussenkomst')

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens or the Dutch Data Protection Authority) RDI (Rijksdienst voor Identiteitsgegevens or the Dutch National Office for Identity Data) Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: FRAIA (Fundamental Rights and Algorithms Impact Assessment)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Impact assessments
items.justification: FRAIA is a tool to identify the impact of specific algorithm on fundamental rights and was piloted at 15 dutch govt org. It addresses Human Oversight and Determination in Part 3: How? specifically in Sec 3.2: The role of humans in the decision (p 51-52). It mandates defining the precise role of humans in decision-making based on algorithmic output and ensuring they are empowered to decide responsibly. It explicitly frames this control using models such as 'human in the loop' 'human on the loop' and 'human in command'. It links oversight to organisational accountability by requiring the identification of ultimate responsibility (Part 1 p18-19) and ensuring sufficient qualified staff are in place to manage and review the system (Part 3).

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens or the Dutch Data Protection Authority) RDI (Rijksdienst voor Identiteitsgegevens or the Dutch National Office for Identity Data) Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: AI4Oversight Lab
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The AI4Oversight Lab directly addresses human oversight by designing AI as a support tool for human inspectors not a replacement. Its entire purpose is to research and build 'human-centric AI' that requires a 'meaningful interaction between computer and inspector. One of the lab's research agenda includes 'Hybrid AI' where the human (inspector) remains in the loop using their judgment and experience (determination) to make the final decision. The AI provides data-driven advice to help the inspector and the inspector's feedback improves the algorithm. This ensures the human retains control.

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens or the Dutch Data Protection Authority) RDI (Rijksdienst voor Identiteitsgegevens or the Dutch National Office for Identity Data) Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: FRAIA (Fundamental Rights and Algorithms Impact Assessment)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Impact assessments
items.justification: The FRAIA (Fundamental Rights and Algorithms Impact Assessment) structurally addresses the concept of Impact Assessments by being a multi-stage comprehensive assessment tool itself. The core of this function is embedded in Part 4: Fundamental rights (Roadmap) (Pages 66-70) which outlines a 7-step structured process to systematically evaluate and mitigate the risks posed by algorithms to fundamental rights. Furthermore FRAIA is designed as an overarching tool that integrates and complements other assessments such as the Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA).

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP RDI Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: Algorithmic management insight and workplace implications
items.justification: This publication was produced by the Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie (The Netherlands Labour Authority) which is a national government body that operates under the Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment and is responsible for monitoring and enforcing labour laws. The Labour Authority conducted a survey on the influence of Algorithmic Management (AM) at Dutch companies and commissioned literature reviews (by TNO). The stated aim was to gain insight into how AM affects managers and employees. The document identifies AI risks (e.g. declining autonomy discrimination) and asserts that existing labour laws like the Working Conditions Act and Works Councils Act apply mandating the inclusion of these risks in company risk assessments (Page 4 5)

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP RDI Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: AI register
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — AI registers
items.justification: The Dutch Algorithm Register addresses public disclosure by listing all government algorithms including their purpose general function and responsible agency. It operationalises transparency beyond the Woo by providing a centralised publicly accessible inventory. While not a law it implements government policy on algorithmic transparency.

body.name: The Advisory Board on Openness and Information Management (ACOI)

items.title: Fundamental Rights and Algorithms Impact Assessment (FRAIA)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Impact assessments
items.justification: FRAIA (fundamental rights and algorithm impact assessment) otherwise called IAMA(Impact Assessment Mensenrechten en Algoritmes) in Dutch is a discussion and decision making tool for government organisations. The tool facilitates an interdisciplinary dialogue by those responsible for the development and/or use of an algorithmic system(Page 2). It addresses disclosure by acting as the standardised 'transparency report' for high-impact algorithms. It forces agencies to document the system's inner workings before deployment creating a comprehensive public record. The FRAIA is compulsory for the Central Government when developing high-risk AI systems.(https://www.tweedekamer.nl/kamerstukken/moties/detail?id=2022Z06024&did=2022D12329)

body.name: The Advisory Board on Openness and Information Management (ACOI)

items.title: AI Procurement Clause
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: This initiative addresses public procurement of AI by providing model contractual clauses that public authorities can include in procurement contracts for AI systems. The clauses operationalise EU AI Act requirements at the purchasing stage by allocating supplier obligations on risk management (Art. 2 p 3–4) data governance (Art. 3 p 4–5) technical documentation and transparency (Arts. 4–6 p 6–7) human oversight (Art. 7 p. 7) and accuracy robustness and cybersecurity (Art. 8 p. 8). They also enable audits and compliance checks by contracting authorities (Arts. 18–19 p 11–12). The preliminary remarks clarify their specific use for public sector AI procurement especially high-risk systems (p 1–2).

items.title: Buyer Group Market Vision and purchasing strategy
items.justification: A Buyer Group brings public clients together who develop a shared market vision for a specific product category and embed into procurement practice. It strengthens AI procurement via four themes. Sec 3.1 ensures Quality through lifecycle management (p.20) and legal 'Model Provisions' (p.25). Sect 3.2 enhances Cybersecurity by mandating BIO/CSIR standards (p. 29) and requesting Software Bills of Materials (p.30). Sect 3.3 promotes Data Sharing via an 'Open unless' policy (p.36) and ARBIT/GIBIT terms (p.37)  to secure ownership. Sec 3.4 addresses Ethics by requiring AI Impact Assessments prior to tendering (p.42) and registration in the Algorithm Register (p.41). The initiative is led by the Dutch AI Coalition with PIANOo supported by BZK.

items.title: AI Factory
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: While not specific to public servants the AI Factory contributes to public-sector skills development through the establishment of a dedicated Expertise Centre scheduled to become operational by mid-2026. As articulated under Priority 3 of the Netherlands’ Digitalisation Strategy (NDS) (pp. 10 13) the initiative is explicitly aligned with the strategic objective of training attracting and retaining digital talent within government. The Expertise Centre is designed to provide the government with low-threshold access to advanced AI infrastructure and specialised skills training. By offering a secure environment for responsible experimentation the AI Factory enables public officials to develop hands-on experience with AI systems.

body.name: 1 The Netherlands Digitalisation Strategy (NDS) council 2 Administrative Consultation on Digitalisation (BDO)

items.title: AI Acceleration Team
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The AI Acceleration Team (Priority 3 of the NDS) addresses public sector skills by prioritising 'AI literacy' and the 'training and retaining of talent' (Sections: 'Framework for responsible use' and 'Strategic objectives'). Led by Larissa Zegveld the team shifts focus from policy documents to 'tangible progress' involving CIOs and directors from all government levels to ensure AI applications are practically feasible for staff (Section: 'The AI Acceleration Team'). It translates complex regulations like the AI Act into actionable procurement and deployment guidance. By fostering 'shared solutions' and active knowledge sharing the initiative builds collective expertise across the public sector to ensure AI is used responsibly.

body.name: 1 The Netherlands Digitalisation Strategy (NDS) council 2 Administrative Consultation on Digitalisation (BDO)

items.title: Congres Rechtspraak en AI (National Rechtspraak and AI Congress)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The “Jaaroverzicht 2024 AI activiteiten Rechtspraak” (2024 Overview of AI Activities in the Judiciary) is an official PDF summary of AI-related activity within the Dutch Judiciary (Rechtspraak) in 2024 which contains evidence that 'Congres Rechtspraak en AI (National 'Judiciary and AI' Congress) which had approximately 400 participants aimed at building AI capability within the judiciary. Under information and training it also mentions workshops and internal learning programmes.

body.name: The Landelijk Programma Artificile Intelligentie (National AI Programme within the Dutch judiciary)

items.title: SLIM SUBSIDY
items.justification: The SLIM (Stimuleringsregeling Leren en Ontwikkelen in MKB-ondernemingen) subsidy supports reskilling/upskilling by funding internal learning and development initiatives that organisations design for their workforce. Though it doesn't mention AI explicitly it funds planning and training structures that can include digital/AI-related learning. Secondary websites like https://amsterdamdataacademy.com/slim-budget/ confirm that SLIM budgets can be used for AI trainings by SMEs. This sectoral development plan by the government also covers ICT. https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/onderwerpen/hervormingen-arbeidsmarkt/meer-geschikt-personeel-en-blijven-ontwikkelen-tijdens-werk

body.name: Algorithms Coordination Directorate (DCA) and Government AI Validation Team (Rijks Al-validatieteam)

items.title: Human Capital Agenda ICT
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The Human Capital Agenda ICT (HCA-ICT) is a national action plan led by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate in the Netherlands. It addresses AI-related reskilling/upskilling by coordinating national efforts to train retrain and upskill ICT professionals including AI and data skills to close talent gaps in the digital economy. It supports career-switchers lifelong learning and employer-led training fostering workforce adaptability to technological change.

body.name: Algorithms Coordination Directorate (DCA) and Government AI Validation Team (Rijks Al-validatieteam)

items.title: Digital Europe Programme (DEP)
items.justification: The initiative contributes to AI security through targeted investment in cybersecurity under the EU Digital Europe Programme (2025–2027). The programme allocates €1.7 billion to support deployment of cybersecurity technologies including innovative security technologies strengthening digital reliance and protection of critical digital infrastructure. Dedicated cybersecurity calls explicitly aim to strengthen resilience reduce strategic dependencies on non-EU technologies and improve preparedness across public authorities and industry.(https://www.rvo.nl/onderwerpen/cybersecurity-funding-portal/toelichting) Complemented by €16.2 million in national co-financing these measures support the secure operation of AI and digital systems.

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP RDI Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: Security Peace and Justice (VVR) working group of the Dutch AI Coalition
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The Security Peace and Justice (VVR) working group of the Dutch AI Coalition (NLAICoalitie) addresses AI safety and security by bringing together government industry and knowledge institutions (a 'triple helix'). This work is facilitated by Security Delta (HSD) on behalf of the Ministry of Justice and Security is concentrated in a few key areas which includes building a catalogue of AI use cases privacy-proof data sharing developing solutions for cybersecurity and ensuring decision support applications are safe and reliable.

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP RDI Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: ROBUST
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The program is an initiative of the Innovation Center for Artificial Intelligence (ICAI) and is funded by the Dutch Government. It is a large-scale public-private partnership. The program ROBUST concentrates on six core dimensions: accuracy explainability reliability repeatability resilience and safety which guide the development of algorithms designed to address objectives inspired by the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

body.name: European AI Office Dutch AP RDI Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: Algorithm Register
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — AI registers
items.justification: The Dutch Algorithm Register addresses transparency by being a mandatory public database where government bodies must disclose what algorithms they use why (the purpose) what data is involved and what human oversight is in place. It tackles explainability by requiring a plain-language description of the algorithm's 'operation' and 'logic'. This provides 'societal explainability' making the 'application and outcome' of AI understandable to citizens who can then hold the government accountable for its use. While this is voluntary currently the Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) has called for the register to be mandatory.

body.name: Dutch Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens the Netherlands national Data Protection Authority RDI (Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur) Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: The DECIDE project - Democratising AI Empowering Citizens through Transparent Decision Making
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The DECIDE project (“Democratising AI: Empowering Citizens through Transparent Decision-Making”) is funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) an independent government-funded body under the Ministry of Education Culture and Science. The €6.8 million multidisciplinary project brings together nearly fifty partners including universities municipalities and civil-society organisations to co-develop AI systems with citizens. Instead of treating AI as a “black box” DECIDE prioritises transparency and explainability focusing on why decisions are made rather than just what the outcome is making AI more interpretable reliable and accountability.

body.name: Dutch Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens the Netherlands national Data Protection Authority RDI (Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur) Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: Dutch DPA imposes a fine on Clearview because of illegal data collection for facial recognition
items.justification: The Dutch DPA fined Clearview AI €30.5M for serious GDPR violations. Clearview unlawfully processed personal and biometric data of individuals in the Netherlands without a legal basis (Articles 5 6 9 GDPR). It failed to adequately inform data subjects (Articles 12 14) and did not respond to access requests or facilitate individuals’ rights (Articles 12 15) highlighting major transparency and explainability gaps. These violations demonstrate how Clearview’s practices prevented people from understanding or controlling how their data was used.

body.name: Dutch Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens the Netherlands national Data Protection Authority RDI (Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur) Netherlands Institute for Human Rights

items.title: GenAI in NCEAassessment FAQs
items.justification: The document addresses AI literacy by providing steps for schools and teachers on aspects such as acceptable use of Gen aI helping them navigate a) prevent and detect GenAI academic misconduct (see Q 3 of the doc) b) recommends students to follow school assessment policy and guidelines mentioning the GenAI tool used in assignments and explaining what the GenAI tool did/ was used for (see Q 11 of the doc) c) Show students examples of inaccuracy bias logical and stylistic problems to deter GenAI use in assessment (see Q 19 of the doc) d) Provide guidance on how to acknowledge use of GenAI (see qs 10 and 11).

items.title: Empowering Aotearoa An Inclusive Approach to AI Literacy in Tertiary Education
items.justification: The “Empowering Aotearoa: An Inclusive Approach to AI Literacy in Tertiary Education” project addresses AI literacy by co-creating resources and structured programmes to equip diverse tertiary learners and educators with critical AI knowledge ethical understanding and confidence for using AI tools in learning and assessment. It emphasizes cultural and linguistic inclusivity develops best-practice guidelines for AI integration and produces accessible materials in multiple languages and formats. The goal is to ensure equitable benefits practical skills and enhanced employability for all students with a special focus on Maori Pacific and neurodiverse learners.

items.title: Safeguarding children and young peoples privacy in New Zealand
items.type: Policy Development — Launching consultations or stakeholder workshops to gather input for a future draft.
items.justification: This report examines children and young people’s privacy in New Zealand with a focus on how well current laws regulations and guidance protect them now and into the future especially in the changing environment of children using social media & AI (Pg 3; second line). Between August- November 2023 the government sought feedback from stakeholders on these issues and published the findings in April 2024 summarising the views received. The consultations resulted in suggestions for government-led guidance on how to apply the Privacy Act and the Information Privacy Principles to help organisations and individuals understand privacy rules in specific contexts including when using technologies such as AI.

items.title: Digital Government Key Areas of Work
items.justification: Under NZ Digital govt's key areas of work the Maori-Crown Digital Partnership Programme (established in August 2025) ensures cultural diversity in New Zealand’s public sector technology by embedding Maori rights values and aspirations in digital service design and delivery. It applies Te Tiriti o Waitangi principles supports Maori data governance and fosters equal Maori-Crown partnerships including in AI. This initiative aims to uplifts staff cultural capability strengthen Maori influence on emerging technologies and promote frameworks like Mana Orite - securing Maori cultural perspectives across government digital transformation.

items.title: Maori Data and AI guidance for business
items.justification: The 'Maori Data and AI – guidance for business' guidance (although released in 2019; still holds relevance) from data.govt.nz addresses cultural diversity by outlining principles for respectful and responsible management of Maori data in AI. It urges businesses to distinguish between noa (non-sensitive) and tapu (sacred) data involve Maori in decision-making respect Maori data sovereignty and adopt culturally safe practices. The guidance encourages transparency careful use of Maori knowledge ethical data use and safeguards to minimise bias and benefit Maori communities—ensuring that Maori perspectives and values shape how AI systems incorporate and use data related to their culture.

items.title: Algorithm impact assessment user guide
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Algorithm Impact Assessment User Guide (Dec 2023) was released as part of the Algorithm Impact Assessment (AIA) process and documentation prepared by Stats NZ under the commitments of Algorithm Charter for Aotearoa New Zealand (Section: Purpose). In Section 8 namely Bias and other unfair outcomes the AIA user guide provides general guidance on bias and unfair outcomes with case studies & key considerations to mitigate the risk of bias/unfair outcomes. It also provides a brief on ways to address unwanted bias like decisions on how best to represent the training data in features interpretable by the algorithm data labelling trained and algorithms are validated before deployment. The guide is current and ongoing.

items.title: Algorithm Impact Assessment (AIA) Questionnaire
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Algorithm Impact Assessment (AIA) Questionnaire was developed as part of the one-year review of Algorithm Charter. The review noted that Public reporting of algorithms in use is fragmented and incomplete. Therefore the toolkit addresses transparency and explainability aspect under section 4 of the Questionnaire: by (4.2) Accountability: Who is responsible if things go wrong (4.5) Human review: Replace/assist decision-making; opt-out rights.4.6 Automation bias: Describe the extent to which algorithm users might rely on recommendations instead of their own judgement. How will this risk be addressed? (Pg 3-4; Governance and Human Oversight).

items.title: Ministry of Justice Charter Commitments
items.justification: As part of The Algorithm Charter a commitment by government agencies to manage their use of algorithms in a fair ethical and transparent way the Ministry of Justice published their charter commitments with practical application of impact assessment. The Ministry published a risk matrix assessment for areas of AI usage including: task generator algorithm automatic attachment orders algorithm and algorithm to identify new contact details for debtors. Please note that the Algorithm Impact Assessment (AIA) Toolkit complements the New Zealand Algorithm Charter by providing the practical operational framework for government agencies to implement the charter's high-level principles.

items.title: Inland Revenues Algorithm Charter of Aotearoa New Zealand
items.justification: Inland Revenue’s 8 May 2024 OIA response titled “Algorithm Charter of Aotearoa New Zealand” provides direct evidence of Algorithm Charter implementation by describing how IRD has set up governance groups to oversee algorithm use. The document notes that IRD’s Artificial Intelligence Oversight Group and Artificial Intelligence Working Group guide the use of algorithms and that members of these groups work in alignment with IRD’s public sector commitments to strengthen the Maori–Crown relationship. It also notes that these groups aim to integrate Te Tiriti o Waitangi and Te Ao Maori concepts and perspectives into Inland Revenue’s work linking algorithm governance explicitly to partnership and equity obligations. (Pg 3).

items.title: AI Procurement checklist
items.justification: The NZ AI procurement checklist is a guide published by MBIE to help organisations evaluate and engage AI suppliers. It outlines key factors to consider including supplier reputation legal compliance alignment with business and governance needs training data quality security performance monitoring and cost risks—when procuring AI systems. The checklist also recommends transparency from vendors about model data performance and support arrangements and encourages regular reviews and information sharing for responsible AI procurement and deployment.

items.title: AI Foundational Capability
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: AI Foundational Capability program is a part of AI Foundations Programme. It explores what is needed to enable AI in practice including change management user-centred design and the trade-offs between customising or acquiring AI tools. This learning content has been created by the Government Chief Digital Office and is envisioned to help build capability in the Public Sector and is not intended as AI policy guidance or settings. It is meant to build the confidence and capability to assess and enable AI opportunities in a safe transparent and productive way uses consistent and well-informed approaches and reflects public service values and context and is not mandatory for public servants.

items.title: Algorithm Impact Assessment (AIA) Questionnaire
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Algorithm Impact Assessment (AIA) Questionnaire was developed by Stats NZ as part of the one-year review of Algorithm Charter. The review noted that  public reporting of algorithms in use is fragmented and incomplete. Therefore the toolkit addresses transparency and explainability aspect under section 12 of the Questionnaire: a) How and why the algorithm is being used what decisions are being made by the algorithm who the algorithm will impact and how; b) What personal information is involved and how training and production data has been collected secured and stored; c) Where a user is interacting with an algorithm not a person and 12.2 Explainability: Explain how and why the algorithm produces its outputs. (Pg 10-11).

items.title: HAPDP Online Complaint Mechanism (Formulaire de plainte)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — State-based non-judicial mechanisms
items.justification: HAPDP’s online complaint form operationalises access to redress or remedy for AI-related harms where AI involves automated processing of personal data. It lets the data subject file a complaint against an organisation and document key facts (incl. dates of access requests or when the harmful practice was discovered) (Q4 lines 40–41). It captures typical rights-violations relevant to AI decisions e.g. consent collection or use third-party sharing access response delays purpose disclosure and correction (Q5 lines 42–61). It also requires prior attempt to resolve with the organisation (Q6 lines 62–67) and asks what remedy the complainant wants HAPDP to take (Q8 line 86).

body.name: High Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (HAPDP)

items.title: The 3 Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The 3 Million Technical Talent (3MTT) Program addresses AI Literacy by directly delivering AI skills training to the populace.Capacity Building: It offers structured training in high-demand technical skills specifically including AI/Machine Learning for the first phase (Cohort 1 began in December 2023).Scale and Access: The program's large scale (3 million target) and hybrid model ensure that training which is a key NAIS initiative reaches a broad diverse demographic across all regions tackling the challenge of limited access to AI knowledge.This directly implements the NAIS objective to 'Equip individuals with the skills and knowledge necessary to participate actively in the AI-driven future' (Strategic Objectives).

body.name: AI Governance Regulatory Body (Pillar 5 Objective 512 pp 4546) However in practice the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) working through the National Centre for AI and Robotics (NCAIR) is currently coordinating activities aligned with the Strategy (see ecosystem/delivery actors on p 16 and the high-level Roadmap for Implementation on p 59)

items.title: NIGERIA DATA PROTECTION ACT (NDP ACT) 2023 -GENERAL APPLICATION AND IMPLEMENTATION DIRECTIVE (GAID) 2025
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: GAID explicitly addresses automated decision-making (Art. 9) requiring data controllers to ensure the operation of human oversight mechanisms when automated systems produce decisions that affect data subjects directly operationalizing the rights to object (as per section 27 of the law). Enhanced protection obligations are established for vulnerable data subjects including the requirement for controllers to establish accessible internal procedures for handling complaints of damages arising from automated processing (Art. 6). Data subjects have the right to be informed about their rights to object to automated decisions providing practical guidance on how such disclosures should be structured (Art. 3).

body.name: Nigeria Data Protection Commission

items.title: NIGERIA DATA PROTECTION ACT (NDP ACT) 2023 -GENERAL APPLICATION AND IMPLEMENTATION DIRECTIVE (GAID) 2025
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: GAID provides technical and procedural guidance on the application of the Law's provisions including specific safeguards for the processing of children's personal data and obligations applicable to automated decision-making systems. It establishes specific safeguards for the processing of personal data of children and other vulnerable groups requiring data controllers to implement enhanced protection measures when deploying automated systems that process data of minors (Art. 6) including the mandatory assessment of risks to the rights and interests of minors before deployment. The requirement for parental consent for the processing of children's data (Section 31 Law) is extended to apply to digital services and online platforms (Art. 3).

body.name: Nigeria Data Protection Commission

items.title: N-ATLAS - Nigerias multilingual multimodal LLM
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Nigeria Multilingual Multimodal LLM (NCAIR) is a government-led development project under the oversight and direction of the Federal Ministry of Communications Innovation and Digital Economy (FMCIDE) to build a large language model covering Nigerian languages (not just English). Creating language resources and models for local tongues enables translation speech/text understanding and content generation that reflect local culture and expression. Link to the model information: https://web.archive.org/web/20250925203652/https://huggingface.co/NCAIR1/N-ATLaS

body.name: AI Governance Regulatory Body (Pillar 5 Objective 512 pp 4546) However in practice the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) working through the National Centre for AI and Robotics (NCAIR) is currently coordinating activities aligned with the Strategy (see ecosystem/delivery actors on p 16 and the high-level Roadmap for Implementation on p 59)

items.title: N-ATLAS - Nigerias multilingual multimodal LLM
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: N-ATLAS (Nigerian Atlas for Languages & AI at Scale) is a government-led programme (NITDA/NCAIR) building multilingual models and datasets for Nigerian languages (e.g. Hausa Yoruba Igbo). By expanding high-quality local-language data and benchmarks it reduces English-centric bias in NLP improves performance for under-represented groups and enables fairer access to AI services. Its open resources/tooling help developers test mitigate and monitor disparate performance—advancing NAIS goals on fairness non-discrimination and inclusion.

body.name: AI Governance regulatory body

items.title: NCAIR AI Collective
items.justification: AI Collective advances Fairness & Non-discrimination by convening open meetups/workshops where practitioners learn to detect and mitigate bias (data curation model evaluation across demographics documentation/model cards). It lowers entry barriers for under-represented groups to participate in AI building promotes use of locally relevant datasets (reducing English-centric and urban bias) and shares practical guidance/tools that developers can adopt in real projects helping Nigeria’s ecosystem design more equitable AI systems.

body.name: AI Governance regulatory body

items.title: National Centre for AI and Robotics (NCAIR) AI Collective
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The NCAIR AI Collective is a government-run platform that grows Nigeria’s AI ecosystem through open calls community meetups workshops and collaboration spaces. By lowering entry barriers spotlighting participation from under-represented groups and promoting skills-building around responsible AI (fairness/bias) it supports women’s inclusion and career pathways in AI. This advances NAIS goals on inclusive human-centred AI and helps increase women’s representation in AI practice and entrepreneurship even though it’s not a women-only program.

body.name: AI Governance Regulatory Body (Pillar 5 Objective 512 pp 45 - 46) However in practice the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) working through the National Centre for AI and Robotics (NCAIR) is currently coordinating activities aligned with the Strategy (see ecosystem/delivery actors on p 16 and the high-level Roadmap for Implementation on p 59)

items.title: DeepTech_Ready Upskilling Programme (under the 3 Million Technical Talent 3MTT Initiative)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The DeepTech_Ready (under 3MTT) is a government-led upskilling programme providing advanced Data Science and AI training to 20000 young Nigerians over successive cohorts. It uses a rigorous 6-month curriculum (self-paced and on-site supported learning) project-based immersion and job-readiness support with AI specialisations including Data Science/Machine Learning Computer Vision and Natural Language Processing. FMCIDE states it “aligns…under the National AI Strategy” showing NAIS-linked implementation.

body.name: AI Governance Regulatory Body (Pillar 5 Objective 512 pp 4546) However in practice the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) working through the National Centre for AI and Robotics (NCAIR) is currently coordinating activities aligned with the Strategy (see ecosystem/delivery actors on p 16 and the high-level Roadmap for Implementation on p 59)

items.title: NITDA Advocates AI Security Integration for Sustainable Development
items.justification: The initiative links AI deployment to “secure” innovation stressing that “innovation without security is unsustainable” and that security is needed to protect trust in a high-cybercrime environment. It promotes integrating artificial intelligence (AI) machine learning (ML) and data analytics alongside security controls and points to government mechanisms like the Computer Emergency Readiness and Response Team (CERRT) and the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA) 2023 as part of the security ecosystem supporting safe AI use.

body.name: AI Governance Regulatory Body

items.title: Teacher registration begins for training on the application ofartificial intelligence in teaching
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Hosted by the Ministry of Education and Science secondary school teachers in the country can apply for advanced training on the application of artificial intelligence in teaching. If they have a basic level of knowledge of digital tools and are actively fluent in English they can apply for the 'AI in the Classroom' training which will help them incorporate artificial intelligence into all phases of teaching from lesson preparation to assessment.

body.name: National Council for Digital Transformation and Cybersecurity was established with the aim of planning coordinating and implementing the activities required for the digitalization of processes as well as efficiently dealing with the challenges it brings (page 53)

items.title: Curriculum for elementary schools
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The Curricula is directly aimed to children enrolled in the 8-9th grades (page 1) and tackles the topics of digital literacy intellectual property risks about irresponsible and use of ICT(page2). In p.2–3 the curriculum’s Digital Literacy standards (IV-A.3 IV-A.7 IV-A.8; IV-B.3 IV-B.5) set learning objectives for safe organizing storing and sharing information and ethical critical use of digital content foundational privacy competencies for pupils; in p.14 the “Challenges related to AI” outcomes explicitly list “loss of privacy” as a risk and ask students to identify protections; in p.17 “Dangers when using AI” uses role-play scenarios (e.g. AI recommending friends) to have pupils spot risks and propose protective actions.

items.title: Personal Data Protection Impact Assessment (PDPA)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: Page 19: article 39: Data protection impact assessment and prior consultation. The document provides guidance on how to perform impact assessment for data controllers when applying the Law on Personal Data Protection. It has several sections and FAQ for each section provided with links and good examples of impact assessment.

body.name: Personal Data Protection Agency

items.title: Digitalization of work and employment A threat or opportunity for employees?
items.type: Policy Development — Launching consultations or stakeholder workshops to gather input for a future draft.
items.justification: The initiative starts with: The application of artificial intelligence in the workplace can no longer be ignored! Then it lists the risks of the AI on workplace. The initiative is implemented by the Workers Unions and calls that they must negotiate transparency in algorithms data access/deletion rights and the 'right to disconnect' to safeguard worker interests. This initiative is part of EU Funded Project and involves Macedonian Free Trade Unions (FTU) as national partner. It has goal to modernize the labour law by adding the workers right to disconnect here also from the AI systems. On page 3-4 the initiative has produced an Action plan which is available here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1DLjYqVoBejLRHrrkg6QXXeuvdF2JJfET/view?usp

items.title: AI - Framework for characterizing AI system methods and capabilities
items.type: Policy Development — Mandated bodies (commissions task forces or inter-agency working groups) to draft an AI-related framework.
items.justification: The Institute for Standardization of North Macedonia provides a standard framework of descriptors to support the consistent characterization of AI system methods and capabilities. The framework helps AI stakeholders describe AI systems and have a common understanding of them. This document applies to all types of organizations involved in any of the lifecycle stages of AI systems as well as to any AI stakeholder roles. It will then help the agencies and other public bodies to make specifications in procurement AI systems.

items.title: AI in the Classroom
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative led by the Ministry of Education and Science (MES) of North Macedonia allows secondary school teachers in North Macedonia to apply for advanced training on the application of artificial intelligence in teaching. If they have a basic level of knowledge of digital tools and are actively fluent in English they can apply for the 'AI in the Classroom' training which will help them incorporate artificial intelligence into all phases of teaching from lesson preparation to assessment.

body.name: Ministry for Digital Transformation and the National Council for Digital Transformation and Cybersecurity

items.title: AI in the Classroom
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Secondary school teachers in the country can apply for advanced training on the application of artificial intelligence in teaching. If they have a basic level of knowledge of digital tools and are actively fluent in English they can apply for the 'AI in the Classroom' training which will help them incorporate artificial intelligence into all phases of teaching from lesson preparation to assessment. The initiative is implemented through the Ministry of Education and Science

body.name: Employment Service Agency of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.title: LEGAL REGULATION OF AI IN THE EUROPEAN UNION AND THE REPUBLIC OF NORTH MACEDONIA
items.justification: The analysis is prepared within the Parliament  institute for research and information.  In the section on 'high-risk AI applications' (page 8) the analysis  explicitly states that AI systems  used in “educational or vocational training can determine access to education and the professional trajectory of someone’s life (for example exam scoring).

body.name: Employment Service Agency of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.title: Competence packages for digital competence in schools
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Norwegian Directorate for Education and Training elaborated competence packages designed to support digital competence in Norwegian schools. These packages are aimed at teachers school leaders and school owners helping them develop the skills needed to support students’ learning and meet the requirements of the Kunnskapsløftet 2020 curriculum reform. For instance one of the packages includes basic insights into AI and its relevance to the curriculum and pedagogical practice addresses challenges and opportunities with AI including teaching practices assessment privacy information security and age-appropriate use of AI tools.It also includes discussion tasks and activities to encourage reflection among teachers and school staff.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: AI and Democratic Elections International Experiences and National Recommendations Report by the Expert Group on AI and Elections
items.justification: The report is conducted by an expert group appointed by the government to assess the influence of AI deepfakes and AI-driven misinformation tools on elections and democracy. Chapter 1.5 p14 discusses genAI deepfakes dis/misinformation as a phenomena and what they entail. Chapter 3 addresses all the ways AI can be used in the context of elections. Chapter 5 assesses the current state of technology and other factors involved in elections in Norway latest changes that have already happened Lastly Chapter 6 offers conclusions and recommendations to implement to counteract the spread of deepfakes dis/misinformation and other harmful influences of AI.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: Report on quality assurance Use of AI in health and care services
items.justification: The report issued by Norwegian Directorate of Health outlines the key considerations organizations must address to assess AI systems trustworthiness (p.4). Chapter 9.3 brings up incident management and how the healthcare staff and the patients can report adverse events and file complaints related to AI. 'The organization should ensure that its internal incident reporting systems are adapted to support reporting of AI-related incidents whether clinical or technical to capture all AI relevant events. Patients can also use this to report adverse events.[..]For AI systems the organization is obligated to report serious incidents that pose a risk to the supplier without delay in accordance with Article 26(5) of the AI Act.'

body.name: The Norwegian Data Protection Authority (Datatilsynet)

items.title: Report to the St 32 (2024 2025) Safe upbringing in a digital society
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The government presented the White Paper on Safe Growth in a Digital Society with government measures to provide children with a safer digital education. The government wants to be proactive and implement a clear policy that prioritizes the safety of children and young people in their daily digital lives which includes ensuring that digital services platforms and marketing are adequately regulated and safeguard children's rights (p. 69). The government will: promote children's rights online through dialogue with platform companies and the technology industry ensure transparency about algorithms on digital platforms and how provider oversight can be carried out and prioritize work on incorporating the Digital Services Act.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom) Norwegian Media Authority the Norwegian Consumer Authority and the Norwegian Data Protection Authority

items.title: Report on large language models in Norwegian health and care services Risks and adaptations to Norwegian conditions
items.justification: Page 26 (Chapter 5): the report addresses the importance of adjusting AI tools and Large Language models used in healthcare to Norwegian realities maintaining the diversity of languages and dialects used. Page 29: 'If language models are to be used to process speech for example speech-to-text the language models should also master the dialects in use in Norway as well as other oral speech variations such as Scandinavian languages.' Page 28:'As with Sami language users efforts should be made to ensure that AI tools consider the cultural perspective in meetings between users from minority groups and society at large which will be in line with the Patient and User Rights Act.'

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: The footprint of Norwegian digital infrastructure 2024
items.justification: Report quantifies climate and environmental impacts of digital infrastructure operating in Norway in 2024.It's commissioned by the Norwegian Communications Authority(Nkom).Big part of the report evaluated the sustainability and impact of data centers. The report highlights that while the current footprint is moderate rapid growth in data center capacity and land use is expected making energy efficiency electricity sourcing and spatial planning critical for limiting future environmental impacts (p67 Conclusion). Chapter 9.6 p.90: the analysis includes serverscooling systems UPS and batteries backup generators buildings racks.This reflect awareness that embodied emissions(construction equipment manufacturing) matter as well as the whole.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: Algorithms AI and discrimination An analysis of the possibilities and limitations of the Equality and Non-Discrimination Act
items.justification: The Ombud is a government agency administratively subordinate to the Ministry of Culture. In 2024 they released a document on discrimination through algorithms and AI (linked)defining risks challenges and potential actions. The report talks about discrimination and unfairness through algorithms in the report Chapter3 outlining existing legislation that can be somewhat applicable Chapter4 defines discrimination and Chapter5 the actors in it Chapter 5 explaining consequences and repercussions.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority

items.title: Algorithms AI and discrimination An analysis of the possibilities and limitations of the Equality and Non-Discrimination Act
items.justification: The Ombud is a government agency administratively subordinate to the Ministry of Culture. In 2024 they released a document on discrimination through algorithms and AI (linked)defining risks challenges and potential actions. While Norway has an overarching Equality and Anti-Discrimination Act it can only be vaguely applied to gender and AI. The Ombud however talks about specific  gender discrimination through algorithms in the report Chapter3 outlining existing legislation that can be somewhat applicable Chapter4 defines gender discrimination and Chapter5 the actors in it Chapter 5 explaining consequences and repercussions.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority

items.title: On the way to a super-intelligent synthetic and robot-supported everyday life? A nationwide survey on the populations encounter with AI
items.justification: The report carried out by Consumption Research Norway (SIFO) analyzes a nationally representative survey on the population's encounter with artificial intelligence. The data collection was carried out in March 2025 with respondents aged 15 to 80 years. Chapter 1.7 of the report discusses human agency vs. AI agency the importance of human control and oversight. Further chapters like 2.3 report on the results of the survey which demonstrates certain skepsis towards AI influence e.g. 'hyper-personalization' that potentially decreases human agency in decision- making

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority

items.title: Report on quality assurance Use of AI in health and care services
items.justification: The report Phase 5 (Chapter 8) and Chapter 4 provides guidance and advice on risk/quality assessment when introducing new AI systems in health and care services. One can find some suggestions for assessment points (chapter 4.2) as well as pointers to some existing assessment frameworks that can be utilized e.g. Health Technology Assessment (HTA) in Chapter 5.3 and Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)/Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA) in Chapter 8.1. Overall the report serves as a valuable resource for understanding the legal ethical and practical aspects of AI impact assessment in the health sector.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: PILOT COPILOT FOR Microsoft 365 Findings report from NTNUs project in the Norwegian Data Protection Authoritys regulatory sandbox
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The report documents NTNU’s pilot and evaluation of Microsoft 365 Copilot carried out as part of Datatilsynet’s regulatory sandbox for AI and privacy-friendly innovation. One of the report’s findings (Finding 7 page18) is that Copilot has the capability to monitor and measure employees’ performance and behaviour. This is relevant from a labour-rights perspective as workplace monitoring and AI-assisted performance assessment can affect employee autonomy fairness and transparency. The use of such tools may shift power relationships in the workplace and raises important questions about how performance data are interpreted who has access to it and how decisions based on this information are made.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: AI - overview of projects in the public sector
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — AI registers
items.justification: The Directorate of Digitization together with NORA.ai initiated an overview of AI projects in the public sector. The information is collected directly by contacting the actors implementing AI systems and contains such facts as project owner ministry the project belongs to owner type short description links to the project and current status. All this information is open to the public searchable and can be created or updated by actors themselves through online forms.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: Report on quality assurance Use of AI in health and care services
items.justification: Chapter 4 of the report defines in detail the process of procuring AI systems for health and care services ensuring that selected solutions are safe effective and compliant with legal and quality requirements. The requirements to procurement; the report lists the following: p.5'General requirements may include that the supplier must address ethical and societal considerations related to the AI system. This can include requirements for safeguarding fundamental human rights such as health and safety as well as environmental and sustainability considerations. ' 'Data quality is a particularly important consideration in AI procurements' p.6 'The organization must require that the supplier has considered the special challenges and threats ass'.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: KI in the municipal sector From theory to practice
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The course by The Norwegian Association of Local and Regional Authorities contains webinars teaching how Norwegian municipalities can practically implement AI in their operations. The contents offer 'concrete examples and practical solutions that are already in use in municipalities' 'focuses on experience sharing' 'encourages copying and adapting solutions'. The course also promotes 'collaboration with various stakeholders such as authorities business academia civil society and environmental organizations' claiming that 'Artificial intelligence has the potential to contribute to major changes in municipal services'.

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: Elements of AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative is the direct execution of one of the government steps outlined in the AI Strategy (the framework defined for this indicator): 'The aim of the course is to teach as many as possible about what AI is what it can and cannot be used for and how to start using methods based on AI. The course combines theory with practical exercises and requires no prior knowledge.' The government has funded Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) (https://www.ntnu.edu/norwai/elements-of-ai) to make this AI course available for anyone in Norway who wishes to gain new knowledge and skills in AI

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: Report on quality assurance Use of AI in health and care services
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The report introduces a framework to support the quality assurance and safe use of artificial intelligence systems in Norway’s health and care services responding to the need for clearer structures to assess and manage AI technologies in the sector. Chapter 5.3 addresses assessing the security of AI system before acquiring and adopting it: 'As part of Phase 2 an overall assessment should be conducted to determine whether available AI systems on the market meet acceptable security standards. The Code of Conduct for information security and data protection (Normen) is a helpful tool for safeguarding information security and privacy in the health and care sector.'

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)

items.title: Report on large language models in Norwegian health and care services Risks and adaptations to Norwegian conditions
items.justification: The Ministry of Health and Care Services has tasked the Norwegian Directorate of Health with developing a joint AI plan for the health and care services which has resulted in this report. The report discusses the importance of transparency and explainability in AI applications in health service defining the risks and offering solutions for the future (Chapter 4 web page 12 PDF version.) While the specific case study is healthcare the definitions sources and effects described in the report can be applied in various domains and are crucial for AI in public sector especially. The report states that it 'recommends measures that should be initiated now to lay the foundation for safe and responsible use of AI going forward.'

body.name: Norwegian Communications Authority

items.title: Omani Language Model Maeen
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Omani Language Model “Maeen” an advanced AI-powered language model designed to reflect Oman’s unique cultural and linguistic characteristics. This initiative aims to enhance AI applications in various sectors by incorporating the Arabic language and Omani dialects thereby preserving and promoting the Oamn's linguistic heritage.

body.name: The Ministry of Transport Communications and Information Technology

items.title: National Committee of AI
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: This initiative addresses Fairness and Non-discrimination in the context of AI by overseeing the ethical implementation of AI policies given that a significant part of its mandate involves addressing the ethical aspects of AI and ensuring that AI systems are developed and deployed in ways that avoid bias and discrimination. It promotes inclusive representation by involving multiple stakeholders from government academia and industry supports adherence to ethical principles in AI decision-making and provides guidance to ensure that AI applications respect equality transparency and equitable treatment across all societal groups.

body.name: Ministry of Transport Communications and Information Technology

items.title: National Committee of AI
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The committee is tasked with preparing strategic roadmaps to support public-private partnerships aimed at accelerating AI adoption. Through PPPs the government can co-develop or co-procure AI systems with private firms which may reduce cost and risk and increase alignment with national priorities. The committee is tasked to monitor global AI developments to assess their impact on Oman which allows them to bring in best practices from other countries in AI procurement and adapt them to Oman’s context. The committee is well positioned to shape a responsible AI procurement ecosystem.

body.name: The Ministry of Transport Communications and Information Technology

items.title: National Committee of AI
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The committee is tasked with reviewing existing legislation and proposing updates to regulatory frameworks relating to AI systems and technologies and evaluate potential risks such as algorithmic bias and misuse of personal data to promote responsible innovation and safeguard society.

body.name: The Ministry of Transport Communications and Information Technology

items.title: Study of Revenue Documents Inheritance Laws and AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The training session for judiciary was on “Study of Revenue Documents Inheritance Laws and Artificial Intelligence”. In the session the evolving role of artificial intelligence in the justice sector was taught.

items.title: National AI Upskilling Program
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Ministry of IT & Telecom Higher Education Commission and Meta launch National AI Upskilling Program to train technical and non-technical faculty members in AI technologies. There are two tracks (1) Soft Skills Training for 1000+ non-technical faculty and (2) Hard Skills Certification for 250–500 technical members.

items.title: Workshop for State Communicators on Disinformation and AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative provided training to state communicators on the risks of disinformation amplified by digital platforms and emerging AI tools. Led by communication scholar Silvio Waisbord the workshop focused on how AI can accelerate false content distort public debate and undermine trust in institutions. It raised awareness among government information officers about synthetic media misinformation dynamics and the need for responsible communication practices. Although not a technical program it directly addresses AI-related disinformation risks.

items.title: GuaranIA Project (SPLCIDIT Agreement funded by the IDB)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The GuaranIA Project develops generative AI services in the Guarani language to promote digital inclusion among rural and vulnerable populations. The project includes dataset collection and structuring model training and the development of inclusive digital tools tailored to Guarani-speaking communities. It is currently being implemented with reported progress activities in the department of Caazapa a region with a significant Guarani-speaking population. The initiative is funded by the the IDB (IDB PR-T1373 https://www.iadb.org/es/proyecto/PR-T1373; see: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1nE7M7hOdcokLde90aHjPqQwiUDq0Vrv4/view?usp=share_link) and executed through collaboration between SPL and CIDIT.

items.title: Paraguay trains judges on the ethical use of AI in the judicial system
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative focuses on training judges on the ethical use of AI in the justice system emphasising equality in access to justice and the prevention of bias in automated decision-making systems. It aims to strengthen institutional understanding about UNESCO's tool kit on AI and the Rule of Law and public trust in fair and responsible AI not to develop new policy or regulatory instruments.

items.title: Paraguay trains judges on the ethical use of AI in the judicial system
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative is the 'AI in the Rule of Law and the Judicial System' workshop organized by the Paraguayan Judiciary and UNESCO. The event addressed ethical foundations for AI in judicial settings based on UNESCO guidelines. Although the full agenda is not public the use of the 'AI & the Rule of Law Toolkit' confirms discussions on judicial responsibility and automation limits. Specifically point 4 (p. 43) of the toolkit details the 'Human-in-the-Loop' principle emphasizing that human oversight is mandatory for judicial decisions to ensure accountability and legal integrity.

items.title: Training Programme for Judges on the Ethical Use of AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Judicial Branch of Paraguay in collaboration with UNESCO conducted a training programme for judges on the ethical and responsible use of artificial intelligence in the justice system. The initiative introduced core concepts of AI governance human rights safeguards algorithmic transparency and risks associated with automated decision-making. It strengthened judicial capacity to interpret AI-related legal issues and contributed directly to public sector skills development in AI.

items.title: She Secures Paraguay 2025
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: She Secures Paraguay 2025 is a government-led 24-hour virtual cybersecurity competition organized by MITIC through CERT-PY with OEA/CICTE support targeting women over the aged of 16 held September 19–20 2025. The initiative explicitly aims to reduce the gender gap in the technology sector by strengthening participants' technical skills including AI-related topics. It is national government-funded and operational within the study timeframe oriented to  enhancing AI skills for the workforce.

items.title: Introduction to AI Course
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This serve as evidence of a government-led initiative addressing AI transparency and explainability. The National Civil Service Secretariat (SFP) offered the online class 'Introducción a la Inteligencia Artificial' on 10 June 2025 (according to the uploaded video description https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OwGpDZODs_0) which includes a module on ethical and responsible AI use covering transparency explainability and citizens’ rights when interacting with AI systems.

items.title: Guidelines for the ethical use of AI at the National Institute for the Defense of Competition and the Protection of Intellectual Property - INDECOPI
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The initiative aims to establish the principles and directives for the ethical use of artificial intelligence (hereinafter AI) at Indecopi. Sections 6 ('General Provisions') and 7 ('Specific Provisions') clearly establish the permitted and prohibited uses of AI for the execution of public services provided by the entity. To meet these new standards it is also noted that 'the inclusion of training in the Entity's Personnel Development Plan aimed at strengthening the capabilities of employees in AI-related topics' will be implemented. (Section 5.2).

body.name: Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (SGTD)

items.title: Remote course AI for Public Management
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This course is organized by SERVIR (National Civil Service Authority of Peru) the entity responsible for building capacity among public servants and officials. It is specifically designed for public sector employees. The course aims to 'Design strategies for incorporating artificial intelligence tools into a public entity considering advancements methodologies tools and best practices in AI to improve services to citizens.'

body.name: Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (SGTD)

items.title: DepEd to revise curriculum to include responsible AI use Angara
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: According to the article Education Secretary Sonny Angara has announced that 'the agency is set to revise the national curriculum to include training on artificial intelligence use' 'to better prepare Filipino learners and educators for the fast-evolving digital landscape.'“Soon babaguhin na rin natin 'yung ating curriculum para matutong gumamit ng A.I. ang mga bata at matutong gumamit ng A.I. 'yung mga guro natin. 'Yan ang pagbabagong ina-anticipate natin sa darating na mga taon” said Angara. (trans. Soon we will revise the curriculum so that students and teachers alike can learn how to use A.I. This is a change we anticipate in the coming years.)
