items.title: Department of Education Order No 013 Series of 2025 Establishment of the Education Center for AI Research (E-CAIR)
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The Department of Education (DepEd) partnered with the Southeast Asian Ministers of Education Organization (SEAMEO) to establish the Education Center for AI Research (ECAIR). 5.d says ECAIR will “support the responsible inclusive and strategic integration of AI into the basic and secondary education system covering policy development curriculum enhancement research and capacity building.” 5.e. states that it will 'contribute to the alignment of Al curriculum integration and other related AI initiatives with the Philippine Qualifications Framework to strengthen the coherence of Al learning outcomes with national qualifications and labor market needs.' (p. 1)

items.title: Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and Meta Joint Initiative to Counter AI-Driven Scams and Online Disinformation
items.justification: The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) has coordinated with Meta to strengthen efforts to combat AI-generated scams and online disinformation. The initiative includes strategies to detect and filter AI-generated content particularly manipulated videos on social media platforms. The DICT’s Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) also works with law enforcement and private sector partners to monitor investigate and take down AI-generated scams and malicious content while assisting victims and raising public awareness about misinformation and online fraud.

items.title: Commission on Human Rights Position Paper on House Bills Promoting The Development and Regulation of and Establishing A Framework for AI
items.justification: The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) lauds the inclusion of the Bill of Rights of Filipinos in relation... AI as embodied in House Bill 7913. It cites the Right to Remedy which 'gives all persons the right to opt-out from the AI systems; all persons shall have access to human consideration and remedy when automated systems fail or commit error and the right ofpersons to appeal or contest the impact of AI will not be denied.' (p. 7) As the Bill of Rights is not present in other bills the CHR recommends 'a harmonized approach across all AI legislation' to ensure consistent rights protections. (p. 7) The paper also recommends additional measures including 'ensuring accessible information and legal protections for all...' (p. 9)

items.title: NPC Advisory No 2024 03 or the Guidelines on Child-Oriented Transparency
items.justification: The advisory contains guidelines (p. 1 Whereas clauses) on the implementation of RA No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act (DPA) which provides that Personal Information Controllers (PIC) must implement reasonable and appropriate organizational physical and technical security measures intended to protect personal data. In determining the appropriate level of security PICs must consider the risks D by the processing among other factors. The advisory covers (Sec. 1) all PICs and PIPs engaged in the processing of children’s personal data whether in a digital or physical environment. It covers products or services specifically intended for children or likely to be accessed by children. The DPA covers automated processing of personal data.

items.title: iTANONG (trans Ask)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Under the Advanced Science and Technology Institute of the Department of Science and Technology iTANONG is a 3-year project proposal which starts in 2022 with an aim to develop a natural language interface to relational databases (NLIDB). This artificial intelligence (AI) application can be accessed through a web browser or a mobile app that will enable end-users to key in questions in Filipino English or TagLish (more languages can be accommodated for later research). The answer can be derived from the connected relational database management systems (RDBMS). This linguistic interface will precisely fill the gap between the users and the RDBMS being maintained by an organization.

items.title: Policy Note on AI
items.justification: The Policy Note prepared by the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) warns that 'AI may potentially accelerate resource consumption' and that 'it can lead to overexploitation.' It notes that 'data centers use significant amounts of water to manage their temperatures' and 'are also significant sources of greenhouse gas emissions.' (p. 48) The Policy Note recommends 'adopting standards for measuring energy consumption and the carbon footprint of AI processes and applications' to mitigate their environmental impact. It also recommends encouraging the use of energy-efficient technologies to reduce energy demands and to manage e-waste to minimize the environmental footprint of AI systems. (p. 56)

items.title: Policy Note on AI
items.justification: The Policy Note on Artificial Intelligence by the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) highlights governmental efforts to promote human oversight in AI governance. It notes that the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and the Civil Service Commission drafted a Joint Memorandum Circular on the Principles and Guidelines for an Ethical and Trustworthy Use of AI in Government encouraging public institutions to adopt principles such as responsibility and accountability contestability and reasonable human control in AI use and human-centricity (p. 46). These principles aim to ensure that AI systems remain subject to human supervision and intervention.

items.title: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Project Sapiens Thematic Review of AI and Machine Learning in the Philippine Financial Services
items.justification: The Review by Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) or the Central Bank recommends that institutions must conduct a 'mandatory Privacy Impact Assessment for all AI systems that handle personal data' and a risk analysis 'to evaluate potential privacy risks to individuals arising from the system's operations.' Institutions must 'develop mitigation strategies to minimize identified risks...' The BSP suggests that 'risk-based assessment per project... through risk tiering be implemented to uniformly determine if proposed projects are within the risk appetite and tolerance of entity.' 'Identifying high-risk AI system is beneficial for prioritization and risk management.' (p. 13)

items.title: Workforce Competitiveness and AI Governance Consultation and Strategic Discussion
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The consultation focused on the responsible integration of AI in workplaces with a strong emphasis on ensuring job security fair employment practices and continuous workforce development. In his speech Department of Labor Sec. Laguesma emphasized the 'critical role of stakeholder collaboration in ensuring ethical use of AI' and that 'human accountability must remain central to decision-making.'AI must be introduced into the workplace in a way that supports and engages workers. Many employers acknowledge that AI can drive business efficiency and innovation but emphasize that its integration must be accompanied by strategic workforce planning particularly in reskilling and job transition support” the Labor Secretary said. (p. 3)

items.title: Strengthening the Philippine Workforce through Adaptive and Responsive Digital Knowledge (SPARK)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Department of ICT’s “digitaljobsPH” program was rebranded to SPARL in 2024. SPARK aligns with Republic Act No. 11927 or the Philippine Digital Workforce Competitiveness Act which created the framework to bridge the country’s digital-skills gap focusing on upskilling and reskilling the Filipino workforce to meet the demands of a rapidly evolving digital economy. DICT Secretary Ivan John Uy said 'digital literacy is our assurance of our competitiveness globally and ensuring jobs for our fellow Filipinos...[who] will benefit from acquiring skillsets that cover cybersecurity artificial intelligence... among other areas of digital technology.'

items.title: School equipment for remote learning
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: The Ministry of National Education is providing 16000 AI and STEM laboratories to primary and secondary schools under the National Recovery Plan (C13L announced 29.07.2025). These labs create dedicated infrastructure for teaching AI-related competencies enabling practical learning and supporting the integration of AI into formal education. Nationwide distribution ensures equitable access and operationalizes the AI education objectives of Poland’s AI Policy.

items.title: Position on Data Protection Impact Assessments
items.justification: The document demonstrates the practical mechanism by which an individual can enforce their rights when a powerful AI entity fails to respect them. The document highlights the specific legal power citizens have to escalate issues. The document details UODO's response which represents the state intervening to ensure the remedy is provided.

body.name: Personal Data Protection Office

items.title: Public consultations
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: These were very short consultations because the only thing being consulted was that the previous version of this regulation was time limited do Aug 2024 and the change being consulted was that it will be prolonged to Aug 2026.

body.name: President of the Office of Electronic Communications

items.title: PLLuM (Polish Large Language Model)
items.justification: Goal: To build an open sovereign Large Language Model trained primarily on high-quality Polish data (literature legal texts scientific archives) rather than translating from English concepts. The project includes the Polish Linguistic and Cultural Competency Benchmark. This is a testing framework consisting of manual questions about Polish history geography literature and traditions to evaluate any AI model's 'Polishness' ensuring it understands local context (e.g. knowing who 'Wokulski' is or the significance of the 'Warsaw Uprising' without hallucinating).

body.name: Council of Ministers Committee for Digital Affairs

items.title: AI Basics for Public Administration
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Training is aimed at local government employees who want to better understand how AI can streamline management improve communication with residents and optimize administrative processes. It is designed for public administration representatives such as city officials municipalities counties and other local government institutions who want to develop their competencies in modern technologies.

body.name: Polish Agency for Enterprise Development

items.title: Sectoral Skills Centers
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: This initiative provides free training funded by public funds at the Branzowe Centrum Umiejetnosci (Sectoral Skills Centre) in Robotics in Wodzislaw Slaski. The centre offers courses such as “Robot Operator” for adults aged 25+ aimed at helping participants acquire practical skills in robotics and industrial automation. The Branzowe Centrum Umiejetnosci (Sectoral Skills Centre) provides certified training using real industrial equipment and supports reskilling and career transitions for workers and adults. As an operational programme funded through public resources and active as of 2025 it represents a government-supported initiative implementing workforce upskilling and reskilling in advanced technologies aligned with AI and automation l

body.name: Polish Agency for Enterprise Development

items.title: Draft Act on AI Systems
items.justification: Ministry of Digital Affairs of Poland prepared and published the Draft Act on Artificial Intelligence Systems which establishes mechanisms to ensure the safety and oversight of AI systems in Poland. The draft proposes creating the the Commission for the Development and Safety of Artificial Intelligence as the market supervisory authority responsible for monitoring AI systems conducting inspections and imposing sanctions for violations. It also introduces regulatory sandboxes (Chapter 8 – Support for Innovation) enabling companies to test AI solutions under regulatory supervision and verify safety requirements before wider deployment.

items.title: Standing Subcommittee on AI and Transparency of Algorithms in Polish Parliament
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: This subcommittee actively convenes to audit how algorithms in public administration (e.g. tax social security) are being deployed.

items.title: The Forum for Digital Skills
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National Digital Strategy assigns INCoDe.2030 a central role in implementing digital-skills actions: Annex II Initiative #1 (p. 23) lists AMA (INCoDe.2030) as a responsible entity for revising curricula creating the National Index of Digital Competences and developing AI-related digital-skills measures. To operationalize these goals INCoDe.2030 created the Digital Skills Forum which included the panel “The Importance of Digital Skills in Artificial Intelligence” featuring Arlindo Oliveira Alípio Jorge Andrés Ortolá Joana Gonçalves Sá João Dias and Paulo Nuno Vicente—directly advancing national AI literacy objectives (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kHTf95FEdr5rJBO9vZl2phfY0dP7h7hU/view?usp=drive_link).

body.name: The Council for Digital in Public Administration (CDAP)

items.title: Project National Media Literacy PlanStrategy 2025-2029
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Development of the project 'National Media Literacy Plan - Strategy 2025-2029' for a robust national strategy for media literacy and the fight against disinformation. Plan developed in accordance with the regulations on Artificial Intelligence (2024) the Digital Services Act (2022) the Code of Practice on Disinformation (2021) and the European Media Freedom Act (2024). (p.4). It aims to promote media literacy among all audiences. Combat disinformation and fake news; Promote responsible and informed consumption of content; Promote a more informed and participatory citizenry. (p.3)

body.name: National Communications Authority Regulatory Authority for Social Communication and National Data Protection Commission

items.title: CNPD WARNS ABOUT THE USE OF PERSONAL DATA FOR TRAINING METAS AI
items.justification: The CNPD’s initiative warned Portuguese users about Meta’s plan to use public data for AI training explicitly urging them to exercise their rights by objecting if their data were used through the company’s online forms. This demonstrates that the CNPD is requiring an actor to change cease or remedy a non-compliant practice by enabling individuals to object to the processing of their personal data in AI-driven systems.

body.name: National Data Protection Commission (CNPD)

items.title: Unified Strategy for the Rights of Children and Young People 2025-2035
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The strategy with an action plan establishes intervention priorities. It ensures the continuity of measures implemented within the National Strategy for Children's Rights 2021-2024 and the integration of the Action Plan for Child Protection 2022-2030. TThe 7 strategic areas include security in the digital age to ensure the responsible use of artificial intelligence promote digital literacy among children and young people promote the safety and responsible use of digital technologies and promote access to digital public services for children and young people.

body.name: National Communications Authority Regulatory Entity for Social Communication National Data Protection Commission

items.title: Scientific and technical presentation of the Portuguese AI model Amlia scheduled for September 30th
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The government’s initiative to launch the AMÁLIA model through a public workshop promoting Cultural and Linguistic Diversity by developing an AI system centered on the Portuguese language and its varieties. The model was trained on Portuguese-language data and integrates multimodal elements—text speech image and video—within a Portuguese cultural context. By emphasizing European Portuguese and its cultural heritage the initiative enhances the representation of local language and culture in AI systems countering the dominance of English-based models.

body.name: Specialized Monitoring Committee

items.title: The CIG 2024 Action Plan
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The CIG 2024 Action Plan explicitly includes formal education and awareness initiatives addressing gender bias in AI. Under the section “Program of the XXIII Constitutional Government – 3rd Strategic Challenge: Inequalities” the plan sets the goal of promoting a gender perspective in R&D content activities and careers. This involves coordinating with R&D institutions and emerging technological areas aligning with public funding frameworks and developing solutions that combat gender bias in AI systems (p. 24 of the PDF).

items.title: ANACOM Conference - AI - The Challenges of Innovation and Regulation
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The conference addressed AI governance challenges in the Portuguese and European context incorporating key terms tied to Human Oversight and Determination: regulation (pp.1–7 of the pdf) oversight (pp.412 of the pdf) accountability (pp.47–8 of the pdf) innovation and trust guided by ethical values inclusion and transparency (p.2 of the pdf) fundamental and human rights (p.4 of the pdf) regulatory framework centred on human rights (p.5 of the pdf) decision-making (pp.2711 of the pdf) and people empowerment/skills (pp.1–246 of the pdf). The conference emphasized that technologies must be regulated according to these human-rights-centred principles.

items.title: AI Business School AP
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The INA Program on p.21 of the PDF includes AI Business School AP which aims to equip public-sector leaders with skills to develop strategies for leveraging Artificial Intelligence within their organizations teams and citizen-service projects. It covers data analysis data projection tools and intelligent bots. The INA website publicly promotes this formal education program and provides an active permanent registration link. This public dissemination and ongoing enrollment demonstrate that the INA training program is being implemented.

body.name: National Institute of Public Administration (INA-Portugal)

items.title: 2187 Information and communication technologies and digital transition in the judicial system
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The implementation of the Activity Plan 2024/2025 is confirmed through government-led actions publicly documented by the Center for Judicial Studies. The Superior Council of the Judiciary published Notice No. 8/2024 opening registration for several training sessions including a full module on artificial intelligence and machine learning in judicial practice covering concepts terminology applications and regulatory instruments (p. 60 of the translated version and p. 56 of the original PDF).

items.title: Training + Digital Voucher
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Training + Digital Voucher (part of the Employment + Digital 2025) offers state-funded financial reimbursement for training costs available to workers regardless of digital proficiency including: eligible specialization courses (starting before 30 September). AI Business School – Public Administration – 1 September 2025; Lean Six Sigma Master Black Belt – 9 September 2025; Machine Learning for Chemical Engineering: Basics – 11 September 2025; Machine Learning for Chemical Engineering: Advanced – 11 September 2025; DaSH – Data Science Engineering – 15 September 2025; Future Built Environment – 16 September 2025; Generative Artificial Intelligence  – 27 September 2025. It operationalizes Article 6(1)–(2) of the Labour Code.

body.name: The Ministry of Labour Solidarity and Social Security

items.title: Guide to AI (GuiA)
items.justification: The Portuguese Guide for Artificial Intelligence highlights the EU AI ACT (p.17 of the PDF) and situates robustness and security as core components of a trustworthy AI ecosystem (pp. 41-46 of the PDF). Robust AI systems must be resilient to faults errors misuse and adversarial threats and maintain reliable functioning across their lifecycle (pp. 41-42 of the PDF). Security measures (e.g. risk mitigation safeguards against cyberattacks and resilient performance) ensure systems behave predictably and safely (pp. 44-46 of the PDF).

body.name: ANACOM

items.title: National Cyber Security Agency organizes an awareness workshop on AI risks in the media sector
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The NCSA workshop “Risks of AI in the Media Sector” builds capacity to counter AI-enabled misinformation by raising awareness of AI risks in media including deepfakes and related cyber threats such as fraud data leaks and privacy breaches. It also discussed practical mitigation steps including incident response and recovery procedures helping media entities detect and respond to AI-enabled deceptive content and online harms.

items.title: Qatar GovAI Program for AI Innovation & Digital Transformation
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Qatar Government AI Program led by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) forms part of the country’s broader AI governance framework and promotes responsible AI deployment in government services. While the program primarily focuses on accelerating AI adoption across public sector entities it operates alongside Qatar’s ethical AI principles and guidelines which emphasize safeguards such as fairness transparency and the mitigation of algorithmic bias aiming to prevent discriminatory outcomes in AI systems used by government (MCIT Government AI Program).

items.title: National Cyber Security Agency NCSA Organizes a Conference on the Safe Use of AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative addresses AI Impact Assessments by presenting and operationalising the “Guidelines for Secure Adoption and Usage of Artificial Intelligence” issued by NCSA. Through sessions and workshops the conference trained participants on applying a risk based approach to AI including identification assessment documentation and mitigation of risks to individuals and society across the AI lifecycle in line with the roles responsibilities and governance/risk provisions set out in Sections 4 and 5.2 of the Guidelines (p 13–21).

items.title: GovAI Program
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The GovAI Program led by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology supports Qatari public sector entities to design and deploy AI solutions while building internal skills. It offers tailored training mentoring and hands on support for civil servants involved in AI projects helping them understand AI concepts use cases and risks in their domains. Through capacity building workshops and expert guidance it develops practical competencies to manage procure and oversee AI systems within government.

body.name: AI Committee

items.title: AI Committee
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Committee supports AI reskilling/upskilling by coordinating implementation of Qatar’s AI Strategy and formulating recommendations for plans and programmes to prepare human resources in AI applications as well as fostering the development of skilled AI professionals. The Committee also oversees AI programmes/initiatives across ministries and prepares periodic reports on implementation progress helping translate workforce skills objectives into ongoing government action (AI Committee responsibilities section on the MCIT page).https://web.archive.org/web/20251217181957/https://www.mcit.gov.qa/en/about-us/artificial-intelligence-committee/

body.name: AI?Committee

items.title: SMEs Go Digital workshop for the hotel sector
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The SMEs Go Digital workshop hosted by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) in collaboration with Qatar Tourism (Visit Qatar) addresses AI transparency and explainability by providing SMEs with practical guidance on the adoption and use of AI solutions. Through expert-led sessions participants were introduced to real-world AI applications in the tourism sector including how AI systems function how outputs are generated and how AI can be used responsibly to improve customer experience and operations. This hands-on awareness approach supports informed decision-making and helps SMEs better understand assess and explain AI-driven tools used in their business processes.

items.title: International Conference on AI and Human Rights Opportunities Risks and Visions for a Better Future
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The International Conference was led locally by the National Human Rights Committee of Qatar in collaboration with the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology and the National Cyber Security Agency. The resulting Doha Declaration advances transparency and explainability by stating in its Preamble that transparency is fundamental to the trustworthiness and legitimacy of artificial intelligence systems (p.1). The section on Transparency and Explainability calls for public disclosure of artificial intelligence use understandable explanations of artificial intelligence-driven decisions and independent review and human rights impact considerations (pp.2–3)

items.title: Quick Diagnosis of the Moldovan Public Sectors Readiness for AI
items.justification: The SCIA survey supports Fairness & Non-discrimination by baselining risks to inform bias-mitigation policies (Introduction & Methodology p.3) surfacing ethical concerns as an adoption barrier that needs policy responses (p.12) and recommending guidelines/best practices and a clear legal and ethical framework to ensure responsible non-discriminatory AI across institutions (p.18).

body.name: National Council on Digital Transformation (NCDT) Sub-Council for AI and Data Governance (SCIA)

items.title: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI Human Rights Democracy and the Rule of Law
items.justification: Via Art. 8 and 9 the Framework Convention requires Parties to adopt or maintain measures to ensure that adequate transparency and oversight requirements are in place in respect of activities within the lifecycle of artificial intelligence systems. It further mandates Parties to ensure accountability and responsibility for adverse impacts resulting from AI systems’ lifecycle activities.These provisions establish a legal basis for governments to publicly disclose AI systems oversight mechanisms and documentation.

items.title: Training for public officials in the use of AI
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: This initiative addresses Public Sector Skills Development as an operational programme that implements the objectives of the Government’s civil service professional development framework (Government Decision No. 166/2025 “Professional Development Programme for Civil Servants 2025–2027”). It delivers a centralized online AI training course to 1000+ public servants building practical skills for day-to-day use of AI: effective prompting drafting/admin automation AI-assisted correspondence and content complex data analysis and AI-supported policy work.

body.name: State Chancellery National Institute of Administration (INAMP) Cyber Security Agency

items.title: Training for public officials in the use of AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Training for public official in the use of AI initiative (June 2025) organized by the E-Governance Agency (AGE) with the Moldovan Association of ICT Companies (ATIC) and the State Chancellery directly advances reskilling and upskilling in the context of AI. Over 1000 public officials completed Google’s Experience AI course to gain skills in AI-assisted document generation data analysis policymaking and content creation. The program builds institutional capacity to integrate AI tools into public administration enhancing efficiency transparency and service quality in line with the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023–2030.

body.name: Sub-Council for AI and Data Governance (SCIA) National Council for Digital Transformation

items.title: Governmental memorandum on the establishment of a coordination committee at a national level in the field of data digital services and AI
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: On 23 April 2024 the Romanian Government approved a memorandum establishing a Coordination Committee for Data Digital Services and AI. The committee comprises nine public institutions tasked with implementing and ensuring the consistent application of the EU’s Digital Services Act and AI Act. Additionally the then Minister for Digitalisation stated that the committee would clarify responsibilities and develop practical tools to ensure that content created using generative AI (deepfakes) can only be uploaded with a clear indication of its artificial origin.

body.name: National Authority for Management and Regulation in Communications

items.title: Romanias National Cybersecurity Directorate implements EU INSPIRE project
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: Romania’s National Directorate for Cybersecurity has joined the EU-INSPIRE project coordinated by the University of Piraeus Research Centre in Greece which focuses on innovative multidisciplinary industry-oriented cybersecurity education aimed at upskilling and reskilling the EU workforce. Launched in January 2025 the project will deliver three specialised master’s programmes (MSc MBA and research-focused MSc) in cybersecurity and AI. The initiative seeks to address the cybersecurity skills gap by developing accredited training programmes and certifications centred on protecting AI-enabled systems and securing digital infrastructures.

body.name: Interministerial Commission for the Coordination of the Implementation of the National AI Strategy

items.title: National Cybersecurity Directorate participation in Innovative multi-disciplinary industry-focused cybersecurity education for upskilling and reskilling the EU workforce
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: Romania’s National Directorate for Cybersecurity has joined the EU-INSPIRE project coordinated by the University of Piraeus Research Centre in Greece which focuses on innovative multidisciplinary industry-oriented cybersecurity education aimed at upskilling and reskilling the EU workforce. Launched in January 2025 the project will deliver three specialised master’s programmes (MSc MBA and research-focused MSc) in cybersecurity and AI. The initiative seeks to address the cybersecurity skills gap by developing accredited training programmes and certifications centred on protecting AI-enabled systems and securing digital infrastructures.

items.title: AI Teacher Training Program in Rwanda
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: In July 2025 Day of AI and MIT RAISE in collaboration with the Rwanda Ministry of Education and the Rwanda Education Board (REB) launched a first-of-its-kind national initiative to bring AI literacy to every classroom in Rwanda. The program focused on equipping educators with the tools to incorporate AI into their existing ICT curriculum preparing students not only to use AI but to think critically and ethically about AI’s role in society.

body.name: The Responsible AI Office (RAIO)

items.title: Productivity Enhancement through AI Empowering Government Operations
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: A one-day training workshop entitled 'Productivity Enhancement through AI: Empowering Government Operations' was held for government employees. The workshop was 'a collaboration between Taiwan Technical Mission (TTM) and the Caribbean Digital Transformation Project (CARDTP).' CARDTP is an initiative of the Organization of Eastern Caribbean States. The Government of St. Lucia has a leading role in the CARDTP as the local initiative. The training was implemented in Saint Lucia for public officials held at the National ICT Centre in Castries with technical support from the Taiwan Technical Mission.

items.title: Saudi Arabia launches AI school curriculum
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Ministry of Education in collaboration with the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology and the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority announced this initiative to enhance educational quality through modern school infrastructure and partnerships with innovative private-sector schools. The launch of the new curriculum represents one of the largest national AI education deployments globally as Saudi Arabia integrates artificial-intelligence learning pathways from elementary through higher-education levels. While AI literacy is not always explicitly named the technology-driven design directly supports the development of AI skills and advanced digital competencies across the education system.

items.title: Report Fake News National Platform
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — State-based non-judicial mechanisms
items.justification: The National “Report Fake News” Platform enables citizens to report digital misinformation directly to authorities. Operated under the Digital Government Authority it employs artificial intelligence and machine-learning tools to swiftly detect classify and track misleading or harmful online content. This initiative demonstrates practical enforcement of the AI Ethics Principles (2023) and Generative AI Guidelines (2025) by using AI systems for content verification public protection and social stability translating ethical commitments on AI transparency safety and accountability into operational practice.

items.title: Humain
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The HUMAIN initiative addresses Cultural and Linguistic Diversity in AI by prioritizing Arabic-native large language models and culturally aligned AI systems tailored to Saudi and regional contexts. HUMAIN emphasizes Arabic language enablement and localization to reduce dependence on Western-centric AI models (HUMAIN website “About” and “What We Do”). HUMAIN was launched through a strategic partnership with the Ministry of Interior at the Absher Conference and operates within the national AI ecosystem. Moreover SDAIA is listed as a strategic ally confirming formal state backing alignment with Vision 2030 and sovereign-level coordination rather than a private or civil-society initiative.

items.title: The CST Sustainability Toolkit
items.justification: The CST Sustainability Toolkit (2024) was developed by the Communications Space & Technology Commission (CST) — the Saudi government’s national regulator for the ICT and emerging technology sectors.It demonstrates the government’s leadership in promoting environmentally sustainable AI and ICT practices providing national guidance on energy-efficient data centers renewable energy adoption and e-waste reduction.Sections 2.1 “Sustainable ICT Infrastructure” and 3.4 “Energy Efficiency and AI Operations” (pp. 10–15).This toolkit supports Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 sustainability goals and the UN SDGs (7 12 13) by aligning AI growth with environmental responsibility.

items.title: Generative AI Guidelines
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The initiative addresses Fairness and Non-discrimination by explicitly requiring government entities to identify affected groups and actively prevent bias discrimination or profiling arising from GenAI data or algorithms. It mandates careful review of AI-generated content to detect stereotypes biased associations and under-representation and stresses user awareness of intersectional biases (e.g. gender race). It also requires understanding training-data sources and applying human oversight to eliminate discriminatory outcomes before use in government contexts (Section 3.1 Fairness p.4)

items.title: AI Ethics Principles
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The AI Ethics Principles (2023) issued by SDAIA promote Gender Equality in AI through their emphasis on fairness non-discrimination and inclusiveness. The framework requires that AI systems be designed and deployed to ensure equal treatment of all individuals preventing bias or discrimination based on gender or other attributes.Principles 2 (Fairness & Non-discrimination) and 5 (Accountability).

items.title: Elevate Program
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Elevate program (launched by SDAIA with Google Cloud) directly addresses gender equality in AI by training 25000+ women in data science and machine learning aiming to close the gender gap in the AI workforce. It equips women with technical skills mentorship and career pathways to increase their representation in a male-dominated sector.

items.title: NeLC and MCIT Launched a Training Program on AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative described in the National eLearning Center (NeLC) & Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) training-programme on AI clearly relates to reskilling/upskilling in the AI context. It “targets all categories from students and professionals” and offers “a comprehensive understanding of … AI … diverse applications across healthcare learning finance and technology”. nelc.gov.sa The programme offers an accredited certificate upon completion and emphasises “continuous learning in AI … from different age groups and levels of expertise”.

body.name: Saudi Data & AI Authority (SDAIA)

items.title: SDAIAs AI Ethics Certification Program
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: SDAIA’s AI Ethics Certification Program operationalizes Principle 6 – Transparency & Explainability from the Principles of AI Ethics (pp. 23–24) by requiring certified service providers to document and disclose data sources algorithms decision logic and rationale behind AI outcomes. Certification audits verify that AI systems are traceable auditable and explainable with mechanisms for user feedback and redress. This ensures public trust through accountability and clarity in how AI decisions are generated and communicated.

items.title: The AI Adoption Framework
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The AI Adoption Framework enhances transparency and accountability by embedding continuous monitoring and evaluation mechanisms across the AI system lifecycle. It requires entities to document data flows model behavior and decision outcomes ensuring results are explainable and traceable. Sections on AI Governance and Monitoring (pp. 18–22) and Performance Management (pp. 26–28) outline periodic reviews reporting dashboards and compliance metrics to ensure AI systems remain transparent ethical and accountable over time.

items.title: National teacher training program in digital technology and AI (AI)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Senegalese Ministry of National Education (MEN) officially launched a national teacher training program in digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI) . Coupled with the distribution of computers to science students this initiative marks according to authorities the operational launch of the Digital Education Strategy 2025–2029 a 130 billion CFA franc initiative unveiled in January. The training delivered entirely online should be accessible from a computer tablet or smartphone with an internet connection.  It aims to enable teachers to adapt their teaching practices to technological advancements; to use digital resources to enrich learning; to raise students' awareness of the challenges of digital technology and AI.

body.name: Ministry of Digital Economy

items.title: Using AI to improve language learning in Senegal
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Developed with the social enterprise Kajou and the research lab Pleias this simple and sustainable platform is based on a LLaMA (Large Language Model Meta AI) language model with seven billion parameters. The Senegalese Ministry of Education has integrated a wide of variety of French text and royalty-free content into the app with the aim of developing activities that are specifically geared towards the linguistic and cultural context in Senegal.

items.title: National E-Learning Platform to Train Civil Servants in Digital Skills
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Senegalese government is actively planning a national e-learning platform aimed at training civil servants in digital skills with AI explicitly part of the agenda for modernizing public administration.This initiative emerged from high-level discussions between the Ministry of Digital Affairs and the Ministry of Civil Service and Public Service Reform focusing on strengthening digital literacy integrating AI tools into workflow and establishing mechanisms for continuous skills upgrading among government employees

items.title: National teacher training program in digital technology and AI (AI)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: While administered under the education strategy this programme operationalises AI skills development targets that the 'SNIA' (National Strategy on AI) also emphasises in its human capital orientation — since building AI competence among educators feeds into broader nationwide capacity building. It directly contributes to reskilling/upskilling by enabling educators to teach and use AI tools effectively which will in turn affect students and the wider workforce. It includes interactive content self-study modules and certification assessments. It aims to enable teachers to adapt their teaching practices to echnological advancements; to use digital resources to enrich learning; to raise students' awareness of the challenges of AI.

items.title: Council for AI in Serbia established
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The established Council for Artificial Intelligence supports AI literacy by coordinating AI-related policies standards and strategic actions in Serbia. Through its advisory role the Council can influence educational programs public engagement and awareness campaigns ensuring citizens professionals and institutions gain knowledge about AI its applications risks and ethical considerations. By shaping the AI ecosystem and promoting informed responsible use the Council contributes to building societal understanding and capacity around AI.

body.name: Council for AI

items.title: Launching AI Digital Assistant on the eUprava Portal
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The eUprava digital AI assistant (initiated by the Office for Information Technologies and eGovernment of Serbia) allows citizens to interact with public services in natural Serbian. By doing so it helps ensure that Serbian remains a living usable language in AI-powered government systems rather than being pushed aside by foreign-language defaults. In that sense the project supports the continued presence of Serbian in the country’s digital and AI ecosystem and reinforces linguistic sovereignty in the public sector.

body.name: Council for AI

items.title: Council for AI in Serbia established
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: Council for Artificial Intelligence addresses Fairness and Non-discrimination by overseeing the implementation of Serbia’s AI ethical framework ensuring that AI systems follow principles of fairness inclusion and non-discrimination. It provides guidance standards and recommendations for AI development and deployment that align with the Ethical Guidelines Sections 3.4 Fairness and 4.5 Diversity non-discrimination promoting equitable and bias-awareness AI practices across sectors.

items.title: Council for AI in Serbia established
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The Council’s mandate includes monitoring implementation of planned strategic measures and preparing recommendations on AI development and application which encompasses education and capacity building for public sector personnel. By aligning AI strategic objectives with implementation oversight the Council provides institutional leadership that supports development of AI skills and competencies among public servants and public sector stakeholders helping ensure that training curriculum reforms and workforce readiness measures in the Strategy are pursued across government.

body.name: Council for AI

items.title: Council for AI in Serbia Established
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The Council for Artificial Intelligence supports Safety and Security by overseeing implementation of Serbia’s AI strategy and Ethical Guidelines including robustness and risk-management principles. Through coordination and expert guidance it promotes compliance with Section 3.3 Prohibition to cause damage and Section 4.2 Technical Reliability and Security.

items.title: Council for AI in Serbia established
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: Council for Artificial Intelligence in Serbia promotes Transparency and Explainability by advising on responsible AI deployment monitoring compliance with the Ethical Guidelines and fostering public trust in AI systems. It guides the use of traceable explainable AI models and encourages stakeholder communication including informing users about system purposes decision logic and data sources. These actions align with the Guidelines’ Sections 3.1 and 4.4 (pp. 10 26-31) operationalizing transparency and explainability across sectors.

items.title: Sierra Leone Ministry of Technical and Higher Education and Agilix Labs MOU for Future Learning Institute (FLI)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The MoU between Sierra Leone Ministry of Education and And Agilix Labs establishes Future Learning Institute (FLI)  an AI-powered learning platform and training programs for educators. It builds AI literacy by equipping teachers with skills to use apply evaluate and integrate AI tools in classrooms and curricula. Educators gain data and algorithm literacy hands-on AI experience and awareness of ethical considerations. The MoU(link as above) outlines AI training curriculum support and capacity-building activities for formal education.

items.title: Qhala to Boost AI Adoption Across Sierra Leones Civil Service
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The MoU delivers AI-focused training workshops and masterclasses for policymakers and civil servants building both technical skills and governance capacity in AI. It directly addresses the indicator by upskilling personnel to manage deploy and oversee AI responsibly

items.title: GE2025 Public warned against irresponsible online conduct ahead of election
items.justification: It specifies criminal penalties under the Parliamentary Elections Act for publishing digitally altered election content misrepresenting candidates warns against AI-enabled harassment and advises verification of information from official sources. The initiative also references POFMA POHA and the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act (p. 3-4) establishing legal consequences for disinformation and online harassment.

body.name: Elections Department (under Elections Commission Singapore) and Singapore Police Force (SPF)

items.title: Personal Data Protection Week 2025
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Personal Data Protection Week 2025 included a PDP Summit from July 7 to July 10 which included a workshop session from 2-5pm titled 'It's Not Child's Play – Protecting Kids’ Data in a Grown-Up Digital World'. This workshop aimed at Data Protection Officers Compliance Teams Business Users and Professionals (especially from sectors that may handle children’s personal data such as retail education healthcare etc.) allows greater understanding of the regulatory expectations around children’s personal data under Singapore’s PDPA and exploration of practical strategies through scenario-based exercises to design safer and compliant digital experiences for young users.

items.title: National Multimodal LLM Programme
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The National Multimodal Large Language Model Programme (NMLP) addresses cultural and linguistic diversity by developing AI systems that understand Southeast Asia's diverse cultures and languages. The S$70 million program creates multimodal LLMs with regional context and builds upon SEA-LION (Southeast Asian Languages in One Network) which is more representative of Southeast Asia's cultural contexts and linguistic nuances supporting 13 languages including Thai Vietnamese Indonesian and managing context-switching between languages in multilingual societies (IMDA Infocomm Media Development Authority Press Release 4 Dec 2023 paragraphs 2-3).

items.title: Singapore AI Safety Red Teaming Challenge Evaluation Report (2025)
items.justification: The initiative advances cultural and linguistic diversity by designing a multicultural multilingual red-teaming exercise across 10 Asia-Pacific languages and 9 countries developing a cultural bias taxonomy and methodology tailored to local contexts and comparing exploits in English vs regional languages to reveal weaker safety guardrails outside English (69.4% vs 30.6% of successful exploits). Key discussions: Executive Summary; Cultural Bias Taxonomy (pp.14–20); Stage 4 Results Analysis – Quantitative Findings (Successful exploits across Bias Categories English vs regional) (pp.23 26–27).

items.title: Refreshed Green Mark for DCs 2024 (GMDC2024)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Refreshed Green Mark for DCs 2024 (GMDC:2024) addresses environmental impact in AI by setting strict energy efficiency (Section 1 pp. 5–8) carbon monitoring (Section 2 pp. 9–12) and renewable energy requirements for data centers which directly support AI workloads. It includes credits for energy-efficient IT equipment monitoring of greenhouse gas emissions and mandates for cooling system efficiency all critical for mitigating the environmental footprint of AI-driven data centers (Sections 1–2 pp. 5–12).

body.name: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)

items.title: AI Verify Toolkit
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The AI Verify initiative was developed by the Infocomm Media Development Authority of Singapore (IMDA) a government statutory board. Its ongoing development and adoption are supported by the AI Verify Foundation a entity wholly owned by IMDA. The AI Verify Toolkit operationalizes fairness and non-discrimination by providing a standardized process for organizations to test their AI systems for demographic bias and fairness (see SGModelAIGovFramework2.pdf pp. 55–60 Section 7.7.2). It guides organizations to use technical and process checks to detect measures and address discriminatory outcomes ensuring that AI deployments produce fair and equitable results across diverse groups.

items.title: SG Women in Tech Relaunch Programme
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Relaunch directly targets gender gaps in the tech/AI workforce by helping women who left work re-enter tech roles including AI-related jobs through training employability support and employer partnerships. The SG Women in Tech (SGWIT) platform – an IMDA initiative – positions Relaunch as part of its mission to attract and develop girls and women for the tech sector. IMDA’s press release on SGWIT’s 5th anniversary describes Relaunch as “empowering women to re-enter the tech workforce” with NTUC LearningHub as anchor partner (para. 4–7; link:https://web.archive.org/web/20260210093027/https://www.imda.gov.sg/resources/press-releases-factsheets-and-speeches/press-releases/2024/sg-women-in-tech-marks-5th-anniversary)

items.title: Testing Real World GenAI Systems
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The Global AI Assurance Sandbox implements ex-ante impact assessment mechanisms by providing a structured testing environment for organizations to evaluate potential risks and harms of generative AI applications before public deployment. Organizations partner with specialist technical testers to conduct comprehensive evaluation of hallucination undesirable content data disclosure adversarial prompt vulnerability and broader use-case risks such as safety financial impact trust regulatory compliance and human oversight. Each testing cycle produces public case studies and reports enabling ex-post documentation and learning from deployed systems.

items.title: Singapore AI Safety Red Teaming Challenge Evaluation Report (2025)
items.justification: This report operationalizes ex-ante impact assessment by developing a systematic methodology for evaluating potential harms before wider deployment. It establishes a 4-stage red teaming methodology (pages 10-23 Evaluation Report): 1. Risk Definition (pages 12-14) 2. Challenge Design (page 20) 3. Annotation (page 22) 4.Results Analysis (pages 23-27 40-42). The report directly supports the Model AI Governance Framework's Testing and Assurance dimension (Framework pages 19-20) by providing empirical evidence and benchmarking data to test LLMs for cultural bias.

items.title: TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The fact sheet describes a nationwide AI skilling effort targeting the Information & Communications workforce including roles in public institutions such as National University Health System and NTUC First Campus and is funded by public agencies (IMDA SSG WSG) to reskill 18000 tech workers over three years in AI analytics and complementary areas (Paragraphs 1–4 p.1–2; employer list p.2–3).

body.name: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)

items.title: Singapore AI Safety Institute at Digital Trust Centre
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The designation of the Digital Trust Centre (DTC) as Singapore’s AI Safety Institute (AISI) supports AI Safety and Security through research and operational activities. The institute conducts Testing and Evaluation to develop methodologies and tools for assessing AI system safety robustness and security. It also works on Safe Model Design Development and Deployment addressing vulnerabilities and integrating safeguards into AI systems. In addition Content Assurance research aims to mitigate risks such as manipulation and misinformation in AI-generated content while Governance and Policy work provides evidence-based input to AI governance

items.title: AI in education - website and a national plan (for 2025-2027)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The initiative is led by the Ministry of Education Research Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic (government). The Plan for the Responsible Use of AI in Education (2025–2027) focuses on integrating AI into the Slovak education system and strengthening AI literacy in formal education. It outlines measures to support the use and understanding of AI in schools and universities including the development of guidance for responsible AI use in education the incorporation of AI-related competencies into teaching and learning processes and support for educators and students in working with AI tools within the formal education environment.

body.name: The Office of the Deputy Prime Minister of the Slovak Republic for Investments and Informatization

items.title: Office for Personal Data Protection of the Slovak Republic
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: 18/2018 Z. z. on personal data protection regulates status activity and organisation of the Office (article1c). The Office participates in the protection of fundamental rights of natural persons in relation to processing of personal data and executes data protection supervision including imposing corrective measures and fines. https://web.archive.org/save/https://dataprotection.gov.sk/files/personal-data-sample/2019_10_03_act_18_2018_on_personal_data_protection_and_amending_and_supplementing_certain_acts.pdf?csrt=690386874085683806

body.name: Office for Personal Data Protection of the Slovak Republic

items.title: The Online Eye reporting
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Spletno oko is classified as Programmatic Implementation & Funding because it is an operational reporting service co-funded by the Ministry of Digital Transformation to remove illegal online content. As Slovenia’s national hotline it serves as a rapid response mechanism for AI-facilitated harms. The 2023–24 Annual Report (May 2025) provides evidence of its active implementation specifically addressing AI-driven threats in the “New and Growing Risks” section. It details the handling of cases involving AI-generated “deepnude” content used for extortion (p.13) and synthetic CSAM including “realistic images of non-existent children” (p.14) as well as broader pathways through which children become victims of sexual abuse videos (p.5).

body.name: Agency for Communication Networks and Services of the Republic of Slovenia (Agencija za komunikacijska omreja in storitve Republike Slovenije AKOS)

items.title: Spletno Oko Annual Report
items.justification: The Spletno oko Annual Report (2023–24) provides direct empirical evidence of AI-facilitated harms including deepfake sexual content and AI-generated child sexual abuse material (pp.5 13 14). It documents how such technologies are used for exploitation and violence offering concrete insight into emerging risks and patterns of abuse. As Slovenia’s national reporting hotline co-funded by the Ministry of Digital Transformation and the EU (p.22) Spletno oko functions as an operational mechanism to identify and respond to these harms thereby directly addressing safety and security as well as AI-facilitated violence through real-world case handling and reporting.

body.name: Agency for Communication Networks and Services of the Republic of Slovenia

items.title: Monograph Razvoj slovencine v digitalnem okolju (Development of Slovene in a Digital Environment)
items.justification: This monograph documents the outcomes of the government-funded RSDO project (2020–2023) created to prevent the 'digital extinction' of Slovenian. Chapter 2 written by researchers from the Fran Ramovš Institute for the Slovenian Language describes the essential infrastructure for AI and NLP development in the local language including speech transcription in the creation of the Artur speech database (P. 39-59). By releasing these open-access resources the initiative ensures that future AI systems can be trained on diverse high-quality Slovenian datasets preserving linguistic nuance and cultural representation

body.name: Ministry of Public Administration

items.title: The Impact of AI on the Labour Market Economic Analysis Reducing the Competence Gap and Providing Labour Law Protection (V5-2267)
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The research project “The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Labour Market: Economic Analysis Reducing the Competence Gap and Providing Labour Law Protection (V5-2267)” funded by the Slovenian Research and Innovation Agency and the Ministry of Digital Transformation (2022–2024) examines how AI technologies transform work affect labour rights and reshape employment conditions. It analyses gig-economy models legal protections and competence gaps providing policy recommendations to ensure fair labour protections in Slovenia’s AI-driven economy.

body.name: The Ministry of Digital Transformation

items.title: Public Tender Development of a unified horizontal platform for AI (JN006311/2025)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: The public tender Publication No. JN006311/2025-EUe16/01 was issued on 11 August 2025 for the development of a unified horizontal platform for artificial intelligence. The project supports the National Programme’s objective of establishing shared AI infrastructure within the public sector. Financed by European Union funds the procurement follows an Open Procedure in line with the Public Procurement Act ZJN-3. The contract is awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender reflecting an evaluation beyond price alone. Through this tender the government advances responsible AI procurement by investing in a centralized and standardized platform that enables consistent development and deployment of AI solutions.

body.name: NpAI Steering Committee

items.title: Training of Public Servants for Future Competencies project by the Public Administration Academy (Upravna akademija)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative supports public sector AI skills development through concrete publicly funded training courses delivered by the Slovenian Upravna akademija. These include “Generative Artificial Intelligence and Leadership” a 12 hour mentored programme for senior public officials focused on the safe ethical and effective use of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and Copilot through practical case work; “Using ChatGPT and Generative AI in Practice” a 5 hour course for public sector employees covering everyday AI use prompt design and security considerations see https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YRP1rMI_2tdLwFML4mvABvpctZh-AJEG/view?usp=drive_link for curriculum.

body.name: Ministry of Public Administration

items.title: EDIH DIGI-SI (European Digital Innovation Hub Slovenia)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: EDIH DIGI-SI operates as Slovenia’s central entry point for digital transformation co-funded by the Ministry for Digital Transformation and the EU. The initiative directly addresses AI reskilling through subsidised programmes such as the seminars “Demystifying Artificial Intelligence in Collaborative Robotics” “Digital Future: ChatGPT in Practice” and “Demystifying AI HPC and Big Data.” Events such as the “EU Financial Clinic” for AI-oriented companies and the “DemoFarm TechHack” for agriculture enable the practical application of advanced technologies. Through these activities EDIH DIGI-SI implements the objectives of the National AI Programme (NpAI) and equips the Slovenian workforce with competencies for an AI-driven economy.

body.name: NpAI Steering Committee

items.title: AI for the Security Operations Centre of Slovenias Energy Sector (ALiEnS-SOC Project)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The ALiEnS-SOC project (2025–2027) coordinated by ELES with partners including SI-CERT the Government Information Security Office and the Academic and Research Network of Slovenia develops an AI-based Security Operations Centre for the national energy sector. It integrates advanced cyber-defence mechanisms digital-twin testing and bias-mitigation methods to strengthen the safety accuracy and reliability of AI systems used in critical infrastructure.

body.name: The Ministry of Digital Transformation

items.title: Data Protection Authority Establishment
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The Data Protection Authority (DPA) is an independent agency. According to Article 7 the Authority shall promote the protection of personal data oversee the implementation of this Law and be responsible for its enforcement.

body.name: Data Protection Authority

items.title: Data Protection Authority Establishment
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: DPA is formally established as an independent agency under Article 6 of the 2023 Act to oversee enforcement monitor compliance and promote public awareness contributing to the implementation of the Data Protection Act (2023).

body.name: Data Protection Authority

items.title: Framework of Cooperation to work together to combat disinformation and other digital harms in South Africa
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) partnered with social media giants Google Meta and TikTok and non-profit organisation Media Monitoring Africa (MMA) to curb disinformation ahead of South Africa’s 2024 National and Provincial Elections. The parties signed a Framework of Cooperation to work together to combat disinformation and other digital harms including deepfakes. As part of the agreement the Real411 digital disinformation reporting platform created by MMA (see CSO initiatives) was implemented. While the agreement was for the 2024 election similar agreements were concluded during previous election cycles and will possibly be the same for future elections.

items.title: GUIDANCE NOTE ON THE PROCESSING OF PERSONAL INFORMATION OF VOTERS AND THE COUNTERING OF MISINFORMATION AND DISINFORMATION DURING ELECTIONS
items.justification: The South African Information Regulator (established under the Protection of Personal Information Act) issued a Guidance Note on the Processing of Personal Information of Voters and the Countering of Misinformation and Disinformation during Elections. The guidance note recognises the right to privacy and protection of personal information in cases where a person’s “voice and/or image is used without their consent to spread fake messages particularly in instances where generative artificial intelligence is used.”(pg. 18). It also provided guidance for how political parties and independent candidates can mitigate against misinformation and disinformation (pg. 18-19).

items.title: ATC250626 Report of the Portfolio Committee on Justice and Constitutional Development on Budget Vote 27 Office of the Chief Justice and the Strategic Plan for 2025 2030 and Annual Performance Plan for 2025/26 of the Office of the Chief Justice Dated 25 June 2025
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: R424.2 million has been allocated to the Information Regulator over the Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) period which covers the three-year period from 2025/26 to 2027/28. They are responsible for implementing and enforcing the POPIA which includes provisions that automated decision-making may not be based on personal information including gender sex and sexual orientation.

items.title: National School of Government AI training modules
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National School of Government (NSG) has prioritised the development of a suite of specialised digital transformation courses aimed at capacitating public servants with digital skills in Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Robotics Cybersecurity and the Internet of Things (IoT) (Pg. 15). The NSG’s online learning platform has a course on AI fluency. See: https://web.archive.org/web/20260112192927/https://study.mynsg.thensg.gov.za/digitalskills/courses

items.title: National AI Skilling Initiative
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National AI Skilling Initiative launched by Microsoft  is aimed at 'empowering one million South Africans with growing in-demand digital skills by 2026.' In line with the initiative the National School of Government and Microsoft concluded an MOU that aims to enhance the skills and capabilities of public sector employees in digital literacy artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity. The AI Fluency Programme structured into six courses provides videos covering key AI concepts. A series of sessions that emanate from this partnership include Digital Literacy AI fluency  cybersecurity tracking and reporting. AI in Leadership and AI fluency and cybersecurity training have also been given to senior officials.

items.title: Advancement Plan for Elementary and Secondary Digital Infrastructure
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Ministry of Education launched a plan to invest KRW 96.3 billion (~US$70 million) in school infrastructure for digital and AI-supported education including the deployment of 1200 “digital tutors” and 170 tech support centres in elementary and secondary schools. These initiatives show that the government is actively investing in AI literacy and education. Although they are only focused on infrastructure and textbooks rather than developing curricula or formal AI teacher-training programs.

body.name: The Ministry of Education (MOE)

items.title: National AI Committee
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The National AI Committee's strategy has as one of its 4 key policy directions the goal of “Creating a culture of inclusiveness and fairness” (goal #3). Under the section titled '3. Vision and Implementation Strategy' the initiative outlines its intent to “implement measures to prevent discrimination and privacy violations during the development and use of AI.” This objective is detailed within the 'Four Key Policy Directions'. However the initiative does not provide a clearly operationalized framework to guard against bias ensure equitable outcomes or hold AI developers/deployers legally accountable for discriminatory impacts.?

body.name: AI Safety Research Institute

items.title: APEC Members Urged to Cooperate in Fostering and Exchanging Female Talent Amid AI Leadership Gap
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The event was organized by the Korea Foundation for Women in Science Engineering and Technology (WISET) a government-affiliated organization dedicated to advancing women in STEM fields. It centered on promoting women’s participation and leadership in artificial intelligence featuring workshops networking sessions and expert exchanges designed to strengthen female talent and leadership in STEM and AI. In her opening remarks WISET Chair Moon Aeri highlighted the importance of achieving gender equality in AI leadership.

items.title: A draft of the Enforcement Decree (the Enforcement Decree)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) in South Korea has been actively working on the Enforcement Decree of the AI Basic Act which provides detailed guidelines on implementing transparency obligations including labeling requirements for generative AI outputs. This indicates the MSIT's commitment to enforcing compliance with the Act's provisions.

body.name: National AI Committee

items.title: National AI Committee
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The National AI Committee plays a strategic oversight and coordination role in implementing the AI Basic Act including its provisions on impact assessments. While the Ministry of Science and ICT remains the primary enforcement authority the Committee is tasked with reviewing national AI policies ensuring ethical and safety compliance and advising on standards and methodologies for conducting AI impact assessments.

body.name: National AI Committee

items.title: AI Support System for Labor Inspectors
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Ministry of Employment and Labor developed an AI Support System to help labor inspectors analyze workplace data such as past accidents and hazardous equipment to identify high-risk businesses and better allocate inspection resources. The system also offers 24-hour labor law consultations enables incident reporting and supports AI-human collaborative investigations to more efficiently address wage arrears and other labor disputes.

items.title: The Governments AI Transformation How Were Doing It
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The document is the plan to develop public-sector management systems that include procurement guidelines for high-impact AI (pages 2- 4). Rather than setting detailed rules it frames procurement as part of the operational infrastructure needed for safe and trustworthy public-sector AI adoption signaling that government agencies will require standardized processes when purchasing or deploying high-impact AI systems.

items.title: Implementation Plan for Projects to Accelerate AI Integration Across Daily Life Industries and the Public Sector
items.justification: The MSIT strategy outlined in the link establishes a high-level public-private governance council to oversee a KRW 710.2 billion investment aimed at accelerating AI integration across daily life industry and the public sector.

items.title: AI Star Fellowship Program
items.justification: The AI Star Fellowship Program is run by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the Institute of Information & Communications Technology Planning and Evaluation. It is an advanced AI upskilling initiative that trains top-tier researchers through funded university–industry collaborations. While not a general workforce program it strengthens Korea’s AI talent base by developing experts who lead innovation and contribute to broader national AI capability-building.

body.name: The Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT)

items.title: Establishing the National AI Committee
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: This National AI Committee is supposed to give recommendations and opinions to heads of National Institutions AI business operators and others regarding the correct use of AI implementation of AI ethics and AI technology safety and reliability. The AI Committee does not possess direct enforcement authority over AI safety. Instead its role is advisory providing strategic guidance on AI policy and safety measures. The Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) holds the primary responsibility for enforcing safety standards and regulations related to AI systems.

body.name: National AI Committee

items.title: Cdigo Escuela 40
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Código Escuela 4.0 is a project to strengthen the foundations needed to understand and use AI in formal primary and secondary schools. It focuses in developing both students’ and teachers’ computational thinking and programming skills provides teacher training including in-class support and equips public schools with the necessary resources including hardware and software. The objective is to provide hands on learning from early educational stages. This initiative was part of the Spanish National AI Strategy (p. 35).

body.name: Ministry of Science Innovation and Universities

items.title: No to unrestricted access to digital technology
items.justification: A campaign launched in conjunction with various organizations aims to recommend that families postpone giving mobile phones to their sons and daughters and instead supervise their interaction with the digital world thus preventing access to inappropriate and harmful content such as pornography or violence among others. It is essential to highlight and denounce the responsibility of large technology companies as the main disseminators of fake news polarization violence pornography and gambling.

body.name: National Commission on Markets and Competition as Digital Services Coordinator and Spanish Data Protection Agency

items.title: Court Ruling Spanish Supreme Court STS 3826/2025
