items.justification: The case in Supreme Court concerned a challenge brought by a CSO BOSCO against the use without disclosure of an automated decision-making system employed in the Spanish public sector. The claim relied on the GDPR arguing that the system involved automated profiling and that affected individuals were entitled to contest the decision and seek meaningful review. The ruling demonstrates how Articles 22 and 79 can be used to challenge decisions supported by algorithmic systems and to seek judicial review. It confirms that individuals and CSOs can rely on GDPR procedural rights to contest AI-supported decisions obtain reasoned explanations of how such systems operate and trigger independent oversight by administrative and judicial authorities.

body.name: Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD)

items.title: Children digital health and privacy Strategy and lines of action
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: In 2019 the Working Group on 'Children Digital Health and Privacy was established to study and propose initiatives and measures to protect children in the digital sphere. In 2024 the Prime Minister announced the objective to protect children and adolescents by law (p.4). Given this situation the Agency defines strategic lines with 10 action priorities and 35 measures (p.4) including: regular meetings with the providers of social networks and equivalent digital services for the implementation of effective systems for verifying age in access to content and its monitoring (p.8); promotion of codes of conduct by companies providing digital services including protection for data processing (p.9).

body.name: National Commission on Markets and Competition as Digital Services Coordinator Spanish Data Protection Agency

items.title: ILENIA
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: ILENIA (Impulso de las lenguas en IA) a project to build multilingual text and voice datasets & models in Catalan Basque Galician Valencian. Some of these models for example AINA in catalan are already available to use open-source.

body.name: Secretara de Estado de Digitalizacin e Inteligencia Artificial

items.title: LEIA
items.justification: LEIA creates open corpora tools and models for Spanish so AI systems reflect real grammar expressions and regional varieties. It includes an observatory of neologisms and variants and plans open grammar checkers and Q&A tools accessible via the RAE platform explicitly focusing on the diversity of Spanish’s geographic varieties. The project includes open release of its datasets and code.

body.name: Secretara de Estado de Digitalizacin e Inteligencia Artificial

items.title: National Plan for Green Algorithms (PNAV)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: National Plan for Green Algorithms tackles AI’s environmental impact by standardising how energy use is measured and compared across the AI lifecycle (design development training and execution) and by funding tools to help developers quantify and reduce energy consumption (page 21). It also provides research funds and the creation of two academic chairs for “Green Artificial Intelligence and Algorithms” (page 16).

body.name: Ministry for Digital Transformation

items.title: FRIA model Guide and use cases
items.justification: This is a report by the Catalan Data protection authority providing assistance to companies and public institutions testing how to conduct a Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment under art.27 of the AI Act. This is part of a larger strategic plan of 'promoting the development of training aimed at institutions.'(page 4) In this case these specific reports tries to provide assistance to companies to analyse the relevant fundamental rights for their specific deployment context and better protect the rights of citizens. (see Use cases in index p.2 ) Non-discrimination is a key fundamental right analysed in the document. In addition the goal of the FRIA is a fairer deployment of AI. (p.7 and 9-10)

body.name: AESIA - Spanish Agency for AI Supervision

items.title: Report and Initial Action Plan - State Agency for the Supervision of AI AESIA
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The State Agency for Artificial Intelligence Supervision presented an initial action plan that describes its functions and objectives (p. 10) specifically regarding supporting the development and use of artificial intelligence systems with a gender perspective incorporating equal opportunities between women and men in their design and implementation and promoting impact assessments capable of identifying potential discriminatory biases particularly those based on gender and ethnicity/racial origin and promoting equality (p. 12); fostering training in artificial intelligence to reduce and eliminate the gender digital divide (p. 21) through the Department of awareness training dissemination promotion and awareness (p. 64).

body.name: Spanish Agency for the Supervision of AI (AESIA)

items.title: Spains AI Sandbox for high-risk systems
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: Spain’s AI Sandbox for high-risk systems is a government-led initiative designed to help companies identify assess and mitigate the potential negative impacts of deploying AI in concrete scenarios. Through supervised pilot tests the Sandbox allowed real-world use cases to be analysed generating practical insights that can be reused by other actors in the sector to better understand the risks. In this way the initiative supports more informed and targeted impact assessments by deployers. Although outside GIRAI’s data collection period the Sandbox concluded in December 2025 with the publication of a series of practical guidance documents to support impact assessment practices: https://aesia.digital.gob.es/es/guias

body.name: Spanish Agency for the Supervision of AI (AESIA)

items.title: Spains AI Sandbox for high-risk systems
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: Spain’s AI Sandbox for high-risk systems explicitly included employment use cases which makes it directly relevant to labour protections under the AI Act. Among the selected participants were Adevinta Jobs with its “How You Match” tool that ranks compatibility between applicants’ CVs and vacancy requirements and Shakers Global Solutions with its “Shakers AI Matchmaker” system that uses personalised recommendations to match freelance talent with business projects. By testing these HR and labour-matching systems in a controlled regulatory setting Spain is generating practical evidence on how such systems work what risks may arise in practice and what compliance measures will be needed.

body.name: Spanish AI Supervisory authority (AESIA)

items.title: Deployment of AI in public administration
items.justification: Spain’s National Institute of Public Administration course Deployment of artificial intelligence in public administration (2.ª Ed.)” meets the criteria for a government-led Public Sector AI Skills Development initiative because it is run by a public administration training body and is explicitly targeted at public-sector staff. The course objectives include building foundational AI concepts understanding the regulatory and ethical challenges and learning practical applications of AI in public services.

body.name: Ministry for Digital Transformation

items.title: Generacin D
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Generación D is a large-scale government-led digital skills initiative that brings together public and private actors to expand digital competencies across the workforce. As part of its training ecosystem it includes programmes financed under Spain’s Recovery and Resilience Plan and its National AI Strategy that offer training and mentoring on digital transformation including artificial intelligence for employees SME managers unemployed youth and professionals helping them gain relevant skills to adapt to technological change in particular an AI shaped labour market.

body.name: Secretary of State for Digitalisation and AI

items.title: Launch of AI Clubs in Schools
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The launch of AI Clubs in schools was a collaborative initiative involving the Ministry of Technology the Ministry of Education AIClub SLASSCOM and IronOn. As part of the National AI Strategy 2024–2028 this initiative “aims to promote AI knowledge and skills preparing students for a future where AI competencies will be crucial for success.” The event was attended by multiple stakeholders from both the government and the private sector as well as 300 school students. This initiative would be implemented across 100 schools with plans for expansion to all schools islandwide. (https://web.archive.org/web/20250214221149/https://mode.gov.lk/notices/ai-clubs-in-sri-lanka-schools).

items.title: Memorandum of Understanding between Ministry of Education (MOE) and Microsoft Corporation to integrate AI (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) into Sri Lankas National School Curriculum
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: This initiative aims to formally incorporate AI literacy into Sri Lanka’s education system. Led by the MOE in partnership with Microsoft the programme commenced as a pilot to integrate AI and ML into the national school curriculum. The curriculum is being developed collaboratively by global Microsoft Education teams and the National Institute of Education (NIE) ensuring alignment with national education standards. The pilot has been rolled out across 20 selected schools in 20 districts with phased expansion planned. By following a “train-the-trainer” model the initiative seeks to empower both educators and learners equipping them with foundational skills to navigate the era of AI.

items.title: Parliamentary Debates Adjournment Motion New Legislation to Protect Society from AI-related Harmful Activities
items.justification: The adjournment motion titled “New Legislation to Protect Society from Artificial Intelligence-related Harmful Activities” was proposed to Parliament by a member of the then-ruling party. He stressed the need for new legislation to protect citizens from AI-related harms on cultural religious and societal grounds (p. 47). He also noted the growing manipulation of human images videos photographs and audio using AI and the potential negative impact on national security (pp. 48-49). While he does not specifically mention AI-facilitated misinformation and violence the motion’s broad theme encompasses it by highlighting risks from unethical AI use.

items.title: AI for Child and Women Protection
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This presentation delivered by a Sri Lankan government cybersecurity official during a training organized by the Ministry of Women and Child Affairs under the section titled “Importance of AI in Child and Women Protection” outlines potential AI applications for online safety (pp. 19–21) early detection of abuse and law enforcement support (pp. 22–25). Under “Challenges and Considerations” it also introduces high-level safeguards related to privacy bias and human oversight concerning children (pp. 31–32). While this demonstrates government awareness and capacity-building efforts it does not constitute an official policy or legal framework (https://web.archive.org/web/20250906000853/https://childwomenmin.gov.lk/feature/training/en).

items.title: Terms of Reference - Selection of a consultancy firm for the design development and implementation of an AI-enabled information platform and digital access channels for GIC including enhancements support and maintenance
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: This TOR invites qualified firms to design develop and implement an AI-enabled information platform for the existing Government Information Centre (GIC). The project is centered on a “Vetted Content Store maintained by a Proactive Data Collection system and accessed via multiple channels” (pp. 4–6) implemented in three phases. Phase 1 rolls out the Vetted Content Store which will manage English content initially and later be extended to support Sinhala and Tamil content (pp. 9–13); Phase 2 establishes an AI-powered Call Center integrating STT NLU Dialogue Management RAG and TTS components (pp. 13-15); and Phase 3 incorporates future enhancements thereby ensuring inclusive access and representation for Sri Lankan citizens (p. 15).

items.title: AI for Child and Women Protection
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This presentation delivered by a Sri Lankan government cybersecurity official at a training organized by the Ministry of Women and Child Affairs outlines potential AI uses for online safety early detection of abuse and law-enforcement support (pp. 19-20) as well as high-level safeguards related to privacy bias and human oversight in relation to women (pp. 21-25). This serves as evidence of government awareness and capacity-building but it is not an official policy or legal framework (https://web.archive.org/web/20250906000853/https://childwomenmin.gov.lk/feature/training/en).

items.title: AI for Transforming Public Service
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This workshop organised by the Ministry of Digital Economy with the support of the Presidential Secretariat served as an initial orientation for public service officials on the use of artificial intelligence in government including awareness sessions and practical demonstrations. It contributed to foundational AI capacity-building by equipping civil servants with a basic understanding of AI concepts applications and potential productivity gains in public service delivery.

items.title: The AI Aptitude Accelerator Workshop
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Information and Communication Technology Agency of Sri Lanka (ICTA) organized an initiative called the “AI Aptitude Accelerator Workshop” a series of workshops aimed at equipping students and young professionals with AI tools and digital skills to improve productivity and career readiness (https://forms.gle/fMQhGyPucRzHfR1t6). Recent workshops have been co-organised with universities such as the University of Kelaniya and the University of Colombo featuring speakers from ICTA and other organisations who provide theoretical and practical training on real-world applications of AI in professional contexts.

items.title: Drafting the Arab Charter for the Ethics of AI
items.type: Policy Development — Mandated bodies (commissions task forces or inter-agency working groups) to draft an AI-related framework.
items.justification: As an initiative by the Arab League the regional charter will be adopted by member states and it addresses children's AI rights (ex. P. 14). The Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy drafted the charter and takes part in regular meetings (latest was June 2025).

items.title: FDPIC concludes investigation into voice recognition at PostFinance
items.justification: The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) has examined whether PostFinance AG is violating data protection regulations when using voice recognition as a means of authentication. It concluded the investigation on 16 May 2025 with a ruling instructing PostFinance to obtain the express consent of the person concerned when creating voiceprints for voice recognition and to delete voice prints for which no consent has been explicitly been given. In its investigation the FDPIC found that PostFinance's processing of biometric data for authentication purposes violates the principle of proportionality. In addition voiceprints are being created without customers explicitly providing their consent.

body.name: Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC)

items.title: AI - Youth and Media
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The platform is the federal government's national platform for promoting media literacy including AI. It is intended for parents and professionals with the goal of empowering children and young people. The repository has the following content framed within the context of children and youth: Algorithms and their relationship with AI (p.2) ChatGPT and other forms of generative AI (p.3) Risks of AI (p.4) AI and youth protection (p.5) Legal (p.6) and Educational materials (p.7). There is guidance on the use of AI Chatbots in working with young people (p.6). The educational material includes access to other platforms.

items.title: Apertus a fully open transparent multilingual language model
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Switzerland's first open-source large-scale multilingual language model Apertus has had its entire development process including its architecture model weights training data and methods made open-access and fully documented. This marks a milestone in generative AI for transparency and diversity. Trained with 15 trillion tokens in over 1000 languages Apertus includes many languages that were previously underrepresented in language models such as Swiss German Romansh and many others. This initiative is led by the Swiss government which funds the project through the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre in partnership with EPFL and ETH Zurich universities. The model is being implemented by Swisscom.

items.title: AI in the Energy supply Impact on security of supply
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The Federal Office for Energy (SFOE) Geoinformation and Digital Innovation Section has conducted an analysis of potential regulations in the context of AI and security of supply in the Swiss energy sector. The report should support the necessary actions for the safe use of AI with a view to security of supply (p.5).

items.title: OFCOM Monitoring of the AI Guidelines for the Confederation 2025
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM) completed the first official monitoring cycle of the AI Guidelines for the Confederation in 2022. The second report was published in 2025 and was also the Overview of Artificial Intelligence Regulation Report to the Federal Council to provide information for the decision on Switzerland’s approach to regulating AI in the future. In the report fairness and (non-)discrimination were key terms that were mentioned. Adjustments to existing sectoral laws and the responsibility of the competent specialized authorities are necessary particularly in matters relating to discrimination and equity in various sectors (p.11).

items.title: Competence Network for AI (CNAI)
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The Competence Network for Artificial Intelligence (CNAI) addresses non-discrimination and fairness regarding AI by providing legal guidance facilitating compliance and promoting best practices to state actors who must adhere to existing law. The CNAI (Competence Network for Artificial Intelligence) facilitates active knowledge exchange through its growing Community of Practice (CoP) which is an organized group for people to share information develop know-how and broaden general AI knowledge. This includes meetings seminars and the 'Data Science and AI for the Public Good' webinar series. The network also runs an internal federal administration group the DS&AI CoP which plans to expand its reach nationally and internationally.

items.title: Swiss Federal Commission for Womens Issues
items.justification: The Swiss Federal Commission for Women's Affairs' magazine 'Women's Issues' has published articles shedding light on the current situation in Switzerland and raising social legal and political questions: What legal framework exists in Switzerland and Europe to regulate the use of these technologies? What adjustments are needed to prevent the exacerbation of existing social inequalities? For example the magazine's authors highlight a specific case of algorithmic discrimination in hiring in Switzerland and visited the Federal Parliament building to obtain information on the political stance of parliamentarians regarding the topic of AI. 'Women's Issues' is published annually on a current topic.

items.title: Factsheet on data protection impact assessment
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: With the entry into force of the revised Federal Data Protection Act there is now an obligation for federal bodies and private individuals to prepare a data protection impact assessment if the planned data processing entails a high risk for the personality or fundamental rights of the data subjects. The factsheet specifically addresses artificial intelligence respectively one of the questions asks if 'new technologies including artificial intelligence are being used'. (page 11)

items.title: Monitoring systems in the workplace
items.justification: The supervisory authority's initiative highlights that modern workplace monitoring systems (including internet/email surveillance and people analytics tools) are becoming increasingly intrusive. It emphasizes that as an independent data protection authority it oversees the lawful use of these systems ensuring the protection of employee data transparency in monitoring respect for individual freedom and compliance with data protection principles (p. 2). By applying the data protection framework to workplace monitoring (often carried out by automated or analytical systems) the initiative helps safeguard workers' rights in environments where AI/automation can drive monitoring decision-making or profiling contributing to the protection.

body.name: Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC)

items.title: CNAI - Competence Network for AI Project Database
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — AI registers
items.justification: The Competence Network for Artificial Intelligence (CNAI) takes over the role of supporting the use of and confidence in AI and in informing the public stating its project overview helps ensure transparency of ongoing AI projects of the Federal Government. The specific page for the project database shows that the CNAI maintains a list of AI-relevant projects to create an overview and transparency about AI projects providing key information such as the title institution and contact persons.

body.name: Federal Digital Transformation Council

items.title: CFC-Copilot for Staff
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The development and deployment of the 'CFC-Copilot for staff' multilingual AI chatbot. This project provides an 'innovative tool for information procurement and learning' for staff directly contributing to AI skills development by enabling on-the-job training and promoting technology use (page 5). The information about the 'CFC-Copilot for staff' project noted as contributing to AI skills development is detailed within the source context provided (page 5).

body.name: Federal Digital Transformation Council

items.title: Competence Network for AI (CNAI)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The Competence Network for Artificial Intelligence (CNAI) manages and supports Communities of Practice and Expertise within the Federal Administration. These interdisciplinary forums allow civil servants to share experiences and learn from each other on AI use. This directly implements the strategic goal for interdepartmental coordination and knowledge sharing (page 5).

body.name: Federal Digital Transformation Council

items.title: Overview of AI regulationReport to the Federal Council
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM) completed the first official monitoring cycle of the AI Guidelines for the Confederation in 2022. The second report was published in 2025 and was also the Overview of Artificial Intelligence Regulation Report to the Federal Council to provide information for the decision on Switzerland’s approach to regulating AI in the future. It is concluded that public trust in the security of useful and efficient applications is also crucial. Without public trust it is impossible to create a basis for social dialogue and the development of new emerging technologies (p. 17). Furthermore a more comprehensive implementation of regulation aims to ensure that the risk and impact assessment of AI is confirmed by

items.title: OFCOM Monitoring of the AI Guidelines for the Confederation 2025
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The report emphasizes the need for legislative action in the country. It revealed the need for adjustments regarding transparency and oversight (Article 8) safe innovation (Article 13) corrective measures (Article 14) and procedural safeguards (Article 15) (p. 8). Regarding the Convention on Artificial Intelligence regulation will be necessary in certain areas including transparency analysis of the risks and impacts of AI systems and the necessary control mechanisms (p. 17). Ensuring adequate transparency traceability and explainability of processes and decisions using AI is essential to strengthening public trust in AI (p. 19).

items.title: Competence Network for AI (CNAI)
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: CNAI fosters AI use serves as an enabler has two communities and maintains a project database for transparency about AI projects available in the Federal Administration. The database lists projects from the Federal Administration that are AI-related or based on AI technology providing key information such as the title thematic field the associated institution and relevant contact persons. Furthermore it also provides information on important aspects relating to AI such as data type and machine learning components. Tags structure the database and enable target-oriented content filtering.

items.title: AI is introduced as a specialty in 10 universities
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: It was reported that 10 universities introduced courses on AI as a part of the implementation of the strategy on development of AI. This initiative is aimed to create a new generation of AI specialists with a centralized curriculum. Introduction of the new course is coordinated by Ministry of Education and Science that is also involved among other ministries in the implementation of the strategy on development of AI. is the  The initiative has not began on 25 October. It is the date when this article was published. Considering that all study courses in Tajikistan start on 1 September there is no possibility that AI course were introduces in the middle of the semester.

body.name: Council on AI

items.title: AI for Schools (AI for Schools) Batch 5
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This government-led initiative implemented by the Institute for the Promotion of Teaching Science and Technology (IPST) invited teachers students and the public to participate in four structured online AI courses. These included Level 1: Awareness introducing AI and its role in daily life; Level 2: Components and Basic Concepts covering AI development decision models and social impacts; Level 3: Model focusing on training computers to classify data and predict outcomes; and Level 4: Integration applying AI knowledge in practical educational settings.

body.name: The Institute for the Promotion of Teaching Science and Technology (IPST)

items.title: Side Event - AI and Children Using AI for realizing the rights of children
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative promotes children’s rights in the context of AI by ensuring that AI systems integrate children’s specific rights needs and safeguards. Co-organized by UNICEF and the Thailand Safe Internet Coalition (TSIC) and led by the Ministry of Social Development and Human Security it brings together government law enforcement private sector civil society and youth stakeholders. Guided by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child especially General Comment No. 25 it advances child-centred equitable and safe AI governance while strengthening children’s access to education healthcare and protection.

items.title: Tech for Gov NextGen GovAI Training Program by Digital Government Development Agency (DGA)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Personnel from the government sector were trained in AI skills to help them formulate problems and apply AI knowledge to create innovations. They received basic training and support from expert advisors along with a team that helped turn their ideas into real solutions.

body.name: The Digital Government Development Agency (DGA)

items.title: Microsoft AI Skills for Everyone (by Department of Skill Development Ministry of Labour)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This course was initiated by the Department of Skill Development under the Ministry of Labour in cooperation with Microsoft. It targeted workers entrepreneurs students and members of the general public aged 18 and above who are interested in artificial intelligence and its practical applications in everyday life. The programme used Microsoft Copilot as the primary AI tool. Course topics included an introduction to generative AI and best practices using AI to support document preparation and create professional content designing and customising visually appealing images producing high-quality videos in a few steps and creating songs or other new forms of digital content.

body.name: The Department of Skill Development (Ministry of Labour)

items.title: Plan to bring AI into technical education (No specific name provided)
items.type: Policy Development — Mandated bodies (commissions task forces or inter-agency working groups) to draft an AI-related framework.
items.justification: The initiative advances AI literacy by institutionalising AI education within technical training targeting both learners and educators and aligning skills development with real economic and technological change.

items.title: National training program in Computer Programming AI and English
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: It is an initiative to train students at Togolese public universities in computer programming artificial intelligence (AI) and English. This program is part of the national digital transformation strategy which aims to make Togo a major technology hub in West Africa. The State provides financial logistical and academic resources to embed AI awareness and technical skills within public universities thus creating a structured implementation mechanism for AI capacity development.

items.title: National training program in Computer Programming AI and English
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Commonwealth-backed Togo Digital Training Programme (Togo First) provides reskilling and upskilling in AI by offering courses in artificial intelligence cybersecurity software development and digital transformation to students professionals and executives. It enhances digital capabilities specifically in AI and strengthens workforce readiness for AI adoption and technology-driven roles.

items.title: Government Partners with UNDP and UNESCO to Launch National Digital Initiatives Including AI Assessments
items.type: Policy Development — Mandated bodies (commissions task forces or inter-agency working groups) to draft an AI-related framework.
items.justification: Page 2 para 6 links two of the initiatives (RAM and AILA) to safety inclusiveness and impactful AI — key governance goals for preventing digital harms online violence and misinformation. Page 2 para 4 explicitly mentions ethics human rights and transparency — pillars of AI fairness and accountability that directly address misinformation and harmful AI outputs. Hence this initiative is directly related to the research area.

items.title: Anansi National AI Assistant
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Anansi addresses three key principles of Human Oversight & Determination; (1) Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL): Citizens can request human agents to intervene at any time demonstrating humans supervising the AI system's overall performance. (2)Human Determination/Agency: Citizens exercise free will by choosing between AI assistance or human agents maintaining capacity to make informed decisions and (3) Human Failsafe: Live ttconnect agents serve as the human failsafe mechanism ready to intervene when AI cannot adequately respond. This is chiefly seen in the section Ask Anansi Your Trusted Government Guide that states “And because sometimes you still need a human touch you can always ask to connect with a friendly ttconnect agent.'

items.title: The Implications of AI Considerations for the Labour Market
items.justification: This is a research paper done by the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago which is a governmental organization. Focuses on AI and labour market implications (displacement skills) .  It will translate into policy input.

items.title: Ministry of Public Administration and AITransforming public Service with the Power of AI (AI)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This is a concrete training programme for public service officers explicitly focused on AI applications and digital transformation in government i.e. direct skills-development evidence.  It is a professional government-training course (promoted by Singapore Cooperation Programme) designed to strengthen national capacity in IP management commercialization and innovation policy.

items.title: Government Partners with UNDP and UNESCO to Launch National Digital Initiatives Including AI Assessments
items.justification: The news release launches a national AI readiness assessment explicitly covering the Public Service identifying needs for AI capability and training.  PP 1-2.  The UNDP AI Landscape Assessment (AILA) serves as a diagnostic tool to evaluate Trinidad and Tobago’s readiness—both strategic and technical—for adopting AI. It will produce a national report that includes actionable recommendations data visualizations and a roadmap to facilitate AI implementation in vital sectors like health education and the Public Service.

items.title: AI in education
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The workshop is explicitly designed for teachers. According to the event page the target audience is “All Teachers (North)”. By training teachers in AI tools assessment methods and AI-enhanced teaching practices the program is upskilling the teaching workforce. This increases their digital and AI literacy enabling them to adapt their pedagogy and integrate AI into their professional practice. this is upskilling.  Through the objectives teachers gain foundational AI knowledge which is key for reskilling: even if teachers are not AI experts this training builds their capacity to work with AI.

body.name: The Ministry of Public Adminsitration and AI

items.title: The Ministry of Public Administration and AI
items.type: Policy Development — Mandated bodies (commissions task forces or inter-agency working groups) to draft an AI-related framework.
items.justification: The formation of the MPAAI establishes the institutional authority responsible for AI governance a foundational institutional step. It establishes the authority and infrastructure through which future frameworks policies or drafts on transparency and explainability in AI can be developed and implemented.  Hence its relevance. To date MPAAI-led initiatives (e.g. AILA) explicitly include transparency as a principle.  https://web.archive.org/save/https://mpaai.gov.tt/sites/default/files/2025-07/media-release-v4---government-partners-with-undp-and-unesco-to-launch-national-digital-initiatives-including-ai-assessments.pdf)

items.title: Seminar on digital culture and transformation of public administration
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: A four-day seminar focused on training civil servants in modern digital tools was organized as part of the joint project between UNDP and the Academy of Civil Service under the President of Turkmenistan with the participation of an international expert on digitalization from the Faculty of Artificial Intelligence at RUDN (Russia) University. Statedly the seminar focused on digital transformation including its social consequences including those related to changes in the labor market. Reportedly a separate block of the program was dedicated to “the study of artificial intelligence its functionality in public platforms and the role in the development of civil society”. No further details are available.

items.title: Roundtable on the topic Innovative Economy and Startup Ecosystem
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: Roundtable brought together representatives of higher and secondary professional educational institutions to discuss the development of the startup ecosystem and the innovative economy with a particular focus on the growing use of artificial intelligence in various sectors. The discussion included discussions on AI impact on labor market demands for skills and professions and including recommendations from the ILO on adapting educational systems to future labor market requirements. Statedly proposals made during the roundtable were to be incorporated in the draft Strategy for the Development of Higher Education in Turkmenistan 2026-2052.

items.title: Educational course AI for students
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The webinars provide for educative materials for students of high schools and elaborates on the key AI and digital literacy skills everyone should possess to effectively and responsibly apply AI tools. It was launched by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine with the support of the Swiss-Ukrainian Program 'Electronic Governance for Government Accountability and Community Participation' (EGAP) implemented by the Eastern Europe Foundation and funded by Switzerland in cooperation with the popular science media 'Kunsth'.

items.title: National Project on Media Literacy Filter
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The project provides for educational initiatives to counter misinformation including AI generated one and uses the Recommendations as one of the instruments to educate Ukrainian media.

items.title: Decree On the implementation of an experimental project on organizing the research of high-tech tools using the Sandbox method
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The decree provides for guidance on the mechanism for implementing a sandbox method for high-tech tools. Paragraph 14 of the Decree provides that relevant soft law is used in the process of assessing AI systems within the sandbox. Among other things what is assessed is the existence of the complaints and feedback portals as well as organisational capabilities of the developer to provide redress.

body.name: Ukrainian Parliamentary Commissioner for Human Rights (Ombudsman)

items.title: Ukrainian National LLM
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: Within the National LLM project there is an initiative to ensure that cultural linguistic and national diversity is represented in the project. For this purpose an advisory board was created by the end of September ensuring diverse representation of various communities and groups. The aim of creating the National LLM was to 'know our context dialects terms history and culture so we will be able to respond qualitatively'.

items.title: Decree On the implementation of an experimental project on organizing the research of high-tech tools using the Sandbox method
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The sandbox provides for testing of AI systems with benchmarks being built based on the soft law documents and guidelines including those requiring human oversight. 14. During the study the following is established in particular:1) compliance of the high-tech device with the requirements and norms of the legislation;2) compliance of the high-tech device with the current level of scientific and technical knowledge trends in scientific and technological progress;3) predicted scientific technical and socio-economic consequences of the further implementation of the high-tech tool;4) defects and vulnerabilities of the high-tech tool;5) risks of using the high-tech tool;...

items.title: The Ministry of Digital Transformation together with Juscutum held workshops on the HUDERIA methodology for the safe integration of AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: HUDERIA methodology as a human rights impact assessment that is designed to check AI system compliance with human rights standards was used as an instrument for pilot human rights impact assessment workshops conducted by the Ministry of Digital Transformation.

items.title: Educational course AI
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The educational course was developed to ensure that ordinary citizens can improve their AI skills and remain competitive on the market.

items.title: How public servants can make friends with AI join the presentation of recommendations from the Ministry of Digital Affairs and CDTO Campus
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Within the event organised by the Ministry for Digital Transformation such activities were organised: Panel discussions with experts already working with AI in the public sector;Speech by representatives of government agencies and technology companies;Overview of training programs and opportunities for developing digital skills. - The workshop was specifically organised to discuss the level of AI literacy in public sector and ways to improve it.

items.title: Educational Series Digitalisation of the State Sector
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: A training course improves the digital literacy (in particular AI) skills of civil servants and other representatives of state authorities. It still remains available and was updated after the Guidelines on AI for civil servants have been released. The declared aim of the course is to improve the digital skills of state sector workers.

items.title: Decree On the implementation of an experimental project on organizing the research of high-tech tools using the Sandbox method
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The sandbox addresses safety and security by requiring to consider soft law instruments when conducting testing exercises within the sandbox (Section 14 of Decree) which includes the relevant Recommendations on responsible use of AI.

items.title: Ministry Of Education Introduces AI Curriculum In Public Schools Starting From 2025-2026 Academic Year
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: The initiative addresses AI literacy by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) as an official subject from kindergarten to Grade 12 starting 2025-2026. This strategic move aims to equip students with essential knowledge and skills to understand AI concepts and apply them in everyday life. The curriculum ensures public school graduates are well-versed in AI fundamentals by covering seven key areas: foundational concepts data algorithms software use real-world applications innovation and project design and policies and community engagement. It focuses on responsible usage emphasizing ethical awareness tech ethics understanding bias and ethical AI use. Students learn digital thinking skills design and evaluate AI system.

items.title: The AI for Safer Children Initiative
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — State-based non-judicial mechanisms
items.justification: The initiative supports the state structures that handle child protection outside of formal court proceedings. The initiative is designed to support law enforcement agencies policymakers educators and technology providers in building a coordinated response. The underlying protection mechanisms in the UAE (e.g. the Child Rights Law) rely heavily on state-based non-judicial interventions by the Child Protection Specialist. These specialists handle preventative and therapeutic intervention and take necessary measures in agreement with the custodian before escalating to public prosecution or court. The AI initiative enhances the operational capability of these state mechanisms

items.title: The AI for Safer Children Initiative
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The initiative develops and deploys over 90 innovative AI tools for practical and scalable solutions to enhance children's safety and well-being. These tools contributed by more than 50 technology providers include solutions for detecting online child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and facilitating victim identification.This implementation directly secures the child's right to protection from exploitation abuse and Child Pornography which is prohibited under the law. By developing these resources the initiative ensures AI is a 'shield for the most vulnerable' fulfilling the commitment to technologically advanced child protection.

items.title: The AI for Safer Children Initiative
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: The initiative itself is a 'groundbreaking international collaboration' between the Ministry of Interior of the UAE and UNICRI.Its central mechanism for engagement is the Global Hub on AI for Safer Children which serves as a 'collaborative digital space' connecting 'child protection professionals technologists and law enforcement entities around the world'. This hub has achieved wide international reach incorporating over 1100 members from 120 countries (as of January 2025).

items.title: DIFC Data Commissioner
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The DIFC Commissioner can conduct periodic reviews of Accredited Certification Bodies (ACBs) which must submit annual reports. ACBs in turn perform ongoing monitoring and at least one compliance audit of certified AI systems during their three-year validity. System owners must also provide an annual attestation of adherence. The framework has processes for handling complaints and reviewing the regulation itself for continuous improvement

body.name: Regulation 10 Advisory Committee

items.title: DIFC Regulation 10 Advisory Committee Charter
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: the DIFC Regulation 10 Advisory Committee is to provide expert multi-stakeholder advice to the Commissioner of Data Protection on the development and implementation of Regulation 10 for high-risk AI systems [3.1.1 1878]. Its functions are purely advisory and include helping to draft guidelines developing criteria for accrediting certification bodies and advising on public policy related to the regulation [3.2.1 1878 1879].

body.name: Regulation 10 Advisory Committee

items.title: Assessment of the Impact of Personal Data Protection
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Impact assessments
items.justification: The DPIA ensures human oversight in AI by mandating pre-deployment evaluation of high-risk automated systems. Controllers must assess risks when processing involves automated profiling with legal or serious impacts ensuring human review before deployment. The DPIA requires clear explanations risk evaluations and mitigation measures coordinated with a Data Protection Officer (DPO) who provides technical oversight. Controllers must also regularly review results embedding continuous human control and accountability across the AI system’s lifecycle.

body.name: The UAE Data Bureau (Office)

items.justification: Although currently in beta mode this tool will enable AI developers and operators to evaluate their systems against the UAE’s AI Ethics Principles and Guidelines covering areas such as fairness accountability transparency and societal impact. It effectively serves as a practical form of impact assessment allowing organisations to identify and mitigate ethical and social risks during AI system design development and deployment.

items.title: AI Pioneers Program
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: While there is no clear date as to when the initiative was started (apart from 2013) this program in collaboration with the National University of Singapore is an initiative designed to equip government employees with practical skills in Artificial Intelligence enabling them to develop innovative digital services using AI technologies and tools. This program offers a comprehensive understanding of AI Principles and effective methods for its use in government work addressing administrative technical and ethical aspects.

items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Program (AIP) is a government-managed specialized training initiative by the National Program for Artificial Intelligence and the University of Birmingham. The AIP aims to upskill/reskill UAE officials and private sector employees to become AI experts and adapt to fast-paced changes. The plan includes five modules from May to September 2024 taught by faculty from Oxford Birmingham and NYU Abu Dhabi. Objectives include acquiring skills in data analysis and developing an 'action plan for the adoption of AI technology'. Evaluation requires a mandatory Capstone Project. The fee is AED 81000. Successful completion enhances career prospects and allows progression to an MSc or a Post Graduate Diploma with Saïd Busi

items.title: AI Program
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The initiative is the Artificial Intelligence Program (AIP) a specialised training program managed by the National Program for Artificial Intelligence. It directly addresses reskilling/upskilling by empowering existing government officials and private sector employees to become AI experts.The curriculum focuses on Generative AI and Machine Learning with the objective of acquiring skills in data collection interpretation and analysis. The ultimate goal is to enable participants to adapt to fast-paced changes and develop an action plan for the adoption of AI technology in their organisation. Successful completion provides Certificates that significantly enhance students’ career and educational prospects.

items.title: AI Program

items.justification: The AIP is a government-managed specialised training program designed to upskill/reskill UAE employees. Its main goal is to 'empower officials' and private sector staff to become AI experts and 'adapt to fast-paced changes'. The curriculum focuses on Generative AI and Machine Learning. Objectives include acquiring skills in data collection and analysis and learning to enhance 'strategic planning for the adoption of Generative AI and AI systems'. Crucially participants must 'develop an action plan for the adoption of AI technology' in their organisation. Successful completion results in Certificates that 'significantly enhance students’ career and educational prospects' and allows progression to an MSc or a Post Graduate Diploma.

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: National Centre for Computing Education
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The government-funded (https://teachcomputing.org/about) National Centre for Computing Education is an operational programme commissioned by the UK Department for Education and delivered through partner organisations. It represents a publicly funded implementation initiative with dedicated budget support for improving computing and AI education nationwide. The programme delivers structured courses and resources including training such as “AI in primary computing” which equips teachers to integrate AI concepts into school curricula using age-appropriate materials.

body.name: Office for AI

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

The National Centre for Computing Education's Teach Computing Curriculum includes AI content at Key Stage 3; specifically the Year 8 'Layers of computing systems' unit covers artificial intelligence and machine learning with learning objectives including defining AI/ML identifying real-world examples and describing how machines are trained. https://web.archive.org/web/20260208234520/https://teachcomputing.org/curriculum/key-stage-3/computing-systems/thinking-machines

body.name: Office for AI

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: The Office of Communicationss opening of formal enforcement programmes under the Online Safety Act
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The Ofcom Online Safety Act Roadmap to Regulation initiative supports implementation of the framework by operationalising risk management and enforcement of platform duties that directly relate to AI-facilitated misinformation and violence. It guides how the Office of Communications expects services to identify mitigate and report risks from algorithms and automated systems that amplify harmful or illegal content (including violent hateful or misleading material). The roadmap shapes how platforms should use proactive technologies transparency reporting and algorithmic risk assessments to reduce AI-driven harms which are all core to applying the Act’s requirements to real world AI misuse.

body.name: Office of Communications (Ofcom)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Horizon Scanning - AI disinformation and cyber security
items.justification: The POST briefing on AI disinformation and cyber security addresses the indicator by providing a government-led evidence-based analysis of how AI systems enable and amplify misinformation including risks of manipulation societal harm and potential links to violence. Produced by the Parliamentary Office of Science and Technology within the UK Parliament it synthesises current research policy developments and threat landscapes including issues such as  AI-deepfakes information warfare and online radicalisation. By informing legislators and supporting parliamentary scrutiny it strengthens the state’s capacity to understand and respond to AI-driven misinformation risks.

body.name: Office of Communications (Ofcom)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Information Commissioners Office (ICO) Annual Report and Performance Reporting Framework
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Information Commissioner's Office Annual Report and Performance Reporting Framework supports Access to Redress and Remedy in the AI context by documenting how individuals can seek remedies through complaints and regulatory oversight. The report explains that helping the public “resolve complaints quickly and efficiently” is a core regulatory function (p. 20) and presents detailed statistics on data protection complaints handled investigations completed and enforcement outcomes (pp. 19 34–36). It also identifies artificial intelligence and biometrics as a regulatory priority and reports on investigations and interventions addressing risks from AI use (pp. 10 15–18).

body.name: Information Commissioners Office (ICO)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Protecting children from harms online Codes of Practice (Ofcom)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Protection of Children Codes of Practice operationalise children’s rights in AI by requiring platforms to control recommender systems that could surface harmful content to minors (Section 4E pp. 47–52). They mandate highly effective age assurance (Section 4B pp. 21–28) and define “highly effective” with AI/ML-specific safeguards: reliability testing ongoing monitoring and fairness/bias checks on AI age-estimation models (Section 5 paras 5.14–5.15 pp. 87–88). Together these measures make AI systems age-appropriate and reduce algorithmic harms to children.

body.name: Ofcom (Office of Communications)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Online Safety Transparency Reporting Final Transparency Guidance (Ofcom)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Final Transparency Guidance makes children’s rights in AI measurable by requiring annual provider reports and Ofcom’s own report enabling systematic oversight of algorithmic risks to children (s.1.3 p.3; s.5 pp.20–22). It tailors notice requirements to the proportion of child users and applicable child-protection duties (ss.3.19–3.22 pp.12–13). Annex A1 lists reportable metrics on content harmful to children mitigation systems and the design/operation of algorithms affecting recommendations (Part 1 items 1–3 8–9 18; pp.27–29).

body.name: Ofcom (Office of Communications)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Ofcom Online Safety Act enforcement investigations
items.justification: Ofcom’s investigations enforce the Act’s child-safety duties that directly implicate AI systems. Services must assess and mitigate risks from “the design of functionalities algorithms and features” (s.11(6)(b) pp.11) and deploy highly effective age assurance (s.12(4–8) pp.12–13). Probing suspected breaches compels platforms to fix recommender systems moderation AI and age-checks that could expose children to harm. Ofcom’s enforcement powers (fines directions) are set out in ss.122–127 (pp.145–153). Ofcom launched nine investigations under the Online Safety Act.

body.name: Ofcom (Office of Communications)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: ICO statutory Codes of Practice (AI/ADM and EdTech)
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The initiative is the ICO's statutory duty to prioritise children's protection established under Section 91. When regulating AI systems that process children's data the Commissioner must consider that children merit specific protection as they may be less aware of risks consequences and their rights regarding personal data processing. This embeds child-focused oversight into all regulatory decisions including AI guidance enforcement actions and code development ensuring children's vulnerabilities are actively prioritized in practice.

body.name: The Information Commissioners Office (ICO)

items.justification: The UK Department for Science Innovation & Technology (DSIT) report “Safety and Security Risks of Generative Artificial Intelligence to 2025 (Annex B)” addresses children’s rights and protections by identifying the risk of AI-generated child sexual abuse material and other harmful content. It explicitly recognises that generative AI can enable and scale the creation and distribution of such material increasing the exposure of children to exploitation and abuse.

body.name: The Information Commissioners Office (ICO)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: The National Archives (Transkribus)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The initiative is a program by The National Archives that involves training automated text-recognition models (Transkribus) to decode historical documents supported by large-scale public participation via Zooniverse. It addresses Cultural and Linguistic Diversity by enabling systems to learn and accurately process distinctive historical handwriting styles and language variations thereby preserving and making accessible culturally significant archival materials that would otherwise remain unreadable (p. 9).

items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: This initiative partially addresses workforce diversity rather than cultural/linguistic diversity. The programme provides £10000 scholarships targeting underrepresented groups in AI: women (over 40% of students) Black students (25%) and disabled students (15%). Page 23 of the National AI Strategy confirms these diversity targets. While this addresses demographic representation in the AI workforce it does not specifically target cultural groups linguistic communities or indigenous representation. The programme focuses on gender racial and disability diversity rather than cultural traditions or linguistic diversity.

body.name: The Office for AI

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: AI Energy Council
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Independent oversight bodies
items.justification: The AI Energy Council addresses AI's environmental impact by overseeing energy sustainability of AI infrastructure. The United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organization dimension focuses on promoting energy efficiency of data centres including renewable energy use and reducing carbon footprints. The Council co-chaired by the Technology and Energy Secretaries convenes energy providers the Office of Gas and Electricity Markets the National Energy System Operator and AI companies to forecast AI energy demand ensure AI Growth Zones are powered by clean energy and explore low-carbon solutions like small modular reactors.

body.name: The Sovereign AI Unit

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Government Digital Sustainability Alliance (GDSA) Report on AI Data Centres Water Use
items.justification: The Government Digital Sustainability Alliance (GDSA) is a government-led alliance bringing together various actors to ensure the sustainability and green-ness of the UK government's digital services/infrastructure. It recently published this report on AI's water demands.

body.name: The Sovereign AI Unit

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: The Fairness Innovation Challenge
items.justification: The government-led activity by the Department for Science Innovation and Technology in collaboration with Innovate UK and supported by the Information Commissioner's Office and Equality and Human Rights Commission is a grant programme (Fairness Innovation Challenge 2023–March 2025). It addresses Fairness and Non-Discrimination by funding projects that develop practical tools and methods to detect assess and mitigate bias in AI systems across sectors such as healthcare finance education and recruitment promoting equitable AI outcomes.

body.name: The Information Commissioners Office

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: AI tools in recruitment Audit outcomes report (ICO)
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Algorithmic audits
items.justification: ICO’s audit initiative advances fairness and non-discrimination by requiring recruiters and AI providers to process data fairly monitor and address accuracy/bias issues and ensure any special-category data used for bias monitoring is adequate and accurate (not inferred/estimated) (pp. 6–7 “Recommendation: Fairness”). It mandates transparency/explainability—tell candidates what data is processed the logic of predictions and how data is used for training/testing (p. 6 “Transparency and explainability”)—and to complete/maintain DPIAs (p. 7). The programme issued ~300 recommendations all accepted (p. 3).

body.name: The Information Commissioners Office

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: An industry guide for addressing technology-facilitatedgender-based violence through Safety by Design
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The “Technology-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence: Safety by Design Industry Guide” led by the Australian Government’s eSafety Commissioner establishes structured design standards and risk management protocols for identifying and mitigating AI-enabled gender-based harms. It requires developers to anticipate and address risks such as harassment deepfakes and abuse that disproportionately affect women and marginalized groups (p. 4). By embedding safety-by-design impact assessments and preventative safeguards into system development it directly advances gender equality by reducing discriminatory and gendered harms in AI-driven digital environments (pp. 5 23).

body.name: AI Opportunities Unit

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: ICO Regulatory Sandbox
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Regulatory sandboxes
items.justification: The ICO Regulatory Sandbox helps organisations design AI systems that comply with UK GDPR including Article 22 on human review of automated decisions. It provides direct support for implementing human oversight explainability and risk mitigation in AI projects. Participating organisations such as Good With Onfido and Tribela worked with the ICO to embed mechanisms for human control and accountability into their AI systems.

body.name: Information Commissioners Office (ICO)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: ICO Audits and DPIA Framework
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Impact assessments
items.justification: The ICO’s audits and DPIA framework operationalises Human Oversight and Determination by requiring organisations to identify and mitigate risks from high-risk AI and automated decision-making. Under UK GDPR Art. 35 DPIAs must assess necessity proportionality safeguards and rights (including Art. 22 rights to human intervention and contestation). ICO DPIA guidance templates and audits check that AI systems include meaningful human review and fallback procedures before deployment.

body.name: Information Commissioners Office (ICO)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: AI and Data Protection Risk Toolkit
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Risk management protocols or fallback procedures
items.justification: The 'AI and data protection risk toolkit' launched by the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) helps organisations identify AI-specific risks to individuals' rights and freedoms and provides practical mitigation steps categorized as 'Must' (legal requirements) 'Should' (best practice) and 'Could' (optional measures). Organisations use the toolkit to identify AI risks and incorporate findings into their Data Protection Impact Assessment (requirement under Section 64 of the Data Protection Act 2018) documenting risk assessments and mitigation measures to demonstrate compliance.

body.name: The Information Commissioners Office

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Information Commissioners Office Regulating AI The Information Commissioners Offices Strategic Approach
items.justification: The Information Commissioner's Office published this strategic report outlining its approach to regulating AI under the UK GDPR. It demonstrates labour protections through enforcement actions including orders to Serco Leisure to cease using facial recognition and fingerprint scanning for employee attendance monitoring (page 15). The ICO applies core UK GDPR principles fairness transparency security and accountability)to workplace AI systems requiring employers to justify biometric surveillance and algorithmic management tools. The report provides guidance on automated decision-making in employment contexts supporting Article 22 protections ensuring human oversight and workers' rights to contest unfair algorithmic determinations.

body.name: The Information Commissioners Office

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Information Commissioners Office Enforcement Notice against Serco Leisure for Unlawful Biometric Monitoring of Employees
items.justification: The Information Commissioner's Office issued enforcement notices ordering Serco Leisure and seven community leisure trusts to stop using facial recognition and fingerprint scanning to monitor 2000+ employees' attendance at 38 facilities. The ICO found violations of Articles 5(1)(a) 6 and 9 of the UK GDPR ruling that biometric processing was neither necessary nor proportionate given less intrusive alternatives existed. The action enforces workers' data protection rights against algorithmic surveillance demonstrating active implementation of UK GDPR protections in employment contexts.

body.name: The Information Commissioners Office

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Algorithmic Transparency Records Repository
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The Algorithmic Transparency Records Repository is the UK's operational public registry of government algorithmic systems directly fulfilling the indicator's core requirement. Led by the Government Digital Service (GDS) within the Department for Science Innovation and Technology (DSIT) it provides public access to standardised records containing: tool name and purpose description of function responsible agency data used human oversight arrangements and risk assessments. Citizens can search records by organisation sector geography and model capability.  The repository enables proactive transparency allowing civil society and the public to scrutinise government algorithmic tool usage without requiring Freedom of Info requests.

body.name: Government Digital Service (GDS)

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Crown Commercial Service (CCS) RM6200 AI Dynamic Purchasing System (AI DPS)
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Dedicated budget lines or public tenders
items.justification: Crown Commercial Service’s RM6200 Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (AI DPS) operationalises AI procurement by giving public-sector buyers a ready route-to-market to run competitions and award contracts for AI services. The official Find a Tender notice states Crown Commercial Service “has set up a Dynamic Purchasing System for the supply of artificial intelligence services” enabling ongoing supplier participation and buyer call-offs. The Guidelines for AI procurement explicitly point buyers to specialist AI procurement routes and name the Crown Commercial Service Dynamic Purchasing System for AI (RM6200) as an example route-to-market.

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Collection AI resources for the public sector
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The UK Government’s “Artificial Intelligence resources for the public sector” is a government-led activity for civil service AI upskilling coordinated and delivered through official platforms such as Government Skills Civil Service Learning and the Government Campus. It provides structured AI training pathways guidance and learning materials tailored to public sector roles including different levels from basic awareness to more advanced application. The programme is aimed at civil servants across departments supporting consistent skill development within government.

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Civil Service Learning AI Courses
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Civil Service Learning AI Courses directly implement the AI Playbook's skills development provisions by providing free AI training to all civil servants. Launched in August 2024 by the Cabinet Office and Government Skills the initiative offers courses covering AI fundamentals ethics generative AI large language models machine learning deep learning NLP and computer vision. The courses target all five learner groups identified in the framework (from beginners to senior leaders) and are delivered in multiple formats (video interactive written). This addresses the indicator's requirements for capacity building and training programs for public servants on AI applications and risks.

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: TechFirst Programme
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: TechFirst is a £187 million government programme launched on 9 June 2025 that directly implements the AI Opportunities Action Plan's Recommendation 19 to 'ensure its lifelong skills programme is ready for AI.' It delivers AI upskilling across four strands: TechYouth (£24m) provides AI skills training to 1 million secondary students; TechGrad (£96.8m) offers scholarships in AI and computer science; TechExpert (£48.4m) funds 500 doctoral students in AI research; and TechLocal (£18m) helps SMEs adopt AI. The programme aims to 'train up people of all ages and backgrounds for the tech careers of the future.'

body.name: AI Opportunities Unit

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Government-Industry Partnership for AI Skills (75 Million Workers)
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This government-industry partnership launched on 9 June 2025 commits to upskilling 7.5 million UK workers (20% of the workforce) with essential AI skills by 2030. Major tech companies including Google Microsoft IBM Amazon BT Accenture Sage and Salesforce have pledged to make high-quality AI training materials freely available to businesses of all sizes. Training focuses on enabling workers to use AI systems such as chatbots and large language models to boost productivity with sector-specific training developed for industries including healthcare finance and manufacturing.

body.name: AI Opportunities Unit
