items.title: Implementation Guide for the AI Cyber Security Code of Practice
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Implementation Guide commissioned by The Department for Science Innovation and Technology provides practical guidance for implementing the 13 security principles across the AI lifecycle. It addresses security obligations through: threat modelling and risk management for AI-specific attacks (Principle 3); safeguards requiring systems to withstand adversarial attacks (Principle 2); incident management and recovery plans (Principle 6); pre-deployment testing procedures (Principle 9); and monitoring for anomalies and security breaches (Principle 12). The Guide offers scenario-driven implementation examples - role-specific advice and mappings to international frameworks to help achieve baseline AI cyber security compliance.

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: The UKs AI Security Institutes Research Agenda
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The UK government’s AI Security Institute research agenda constitutes a government-led operational programme for the implementation of AI safety and security. Developed by the Department for Science Innovation and Technology and executed through the AI Security Institute it sets out concrete ongoing activities to address AI-related risks. The agenda operationalises state priorities through targeted research programmes on threat identification system evaluation and alignment/control mechanisms.

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Research and analysis Safety and security risks of generative AI
items.justification: The UK Department for Science Innovation & Technology (DSIT) report “Safety and Security Risks of Generative Artificial Intelligence to 2025 (Annex B)” is a government-led research analysis focused on the safety and security of AI systems particularly in relation to cybersecurity and system vulnerabilities. It examines how generative AI can be exploited to enhance cyberattacks fraud impersonation and other malicious activities while also highlighting risks arising from the integration of AI into critical digital and physical infrastructure.

country.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard Hub
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The government-led activity by the Government Digital Service is the implementation of the Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS) introduced in 2023 and expanded through 2025. It addresses Transparency and Explainability by establishing a standard requiring public sector organisations to document how algorithmic tools function their purpose data inputs and their role in decision-making.

items.title: Information Commissioners Office (ICO) Annual Report and Performance Reporting Framework
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The ICO Annual Report and Performance Reporting Framework supports transparency and explainability in AI by publicly reporting on how the regulator handles complaints investigations and regulatory action including cases involving automated decision-making. The Annual Report’s sections on “Complaints and concerns” and “Regulating data protection” describe how individuals raise concerns about data processing and how the ICO assesses compliance including failures to explain or justify automated decisions. By publishing statistics outcomes and regulatory priorities the reporting framework makes the operation and enforcement of transparency and explainability obligations in automated decision-making visible and accountable.

body.name: Information Commission

items.justification: It's national-wide six months campaign to combat online misinformation fake news and digital fraud. The campaign seeks to raise awareness on the harms and consequences of publishing unverified news. The objective is to instil the need for people to verify information before they publish and if one cannot verify information should refrain from publish or sharing such information online.

items.title: Special training for DPOs
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The trainings promote Data Protection within institutions including the proper collection and processing of children’s personal data.

body.name: Personal Data Protection Commission

items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative built public sector AI skills by training civil servants in machine learning natural language processing and responsible AI practices. Through hands-on workshops and practical exercises participants gained both technical and ethical competencies enabling government staff to adopt AI responsibly in governance service delivery and decision-making strengthening Tanzania’s public sector capacity for digital transformation.

items.title: Proposed Priority and Definitions-Secretarys Supplemental Priority and Definitions on Advancing AI in Education
items.justification: Under the DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION it addresses AI literacy by operationalizing how schools and higher-education institutions may use existing federal grant programs to support AI-related teaching and learning. The letter explains that funds may be used for instructional materials tutoring advising and educator professional development involving AI (pp. 1–2). It emphasizes helping students and educators understand use and responsibly apply AI tools while aligning with privacy civil rights and transparency obligations (pp. 2–3). In doing so it translates the Executive Order’s AI literacy objectives into practical fundable educational activities.

items.title: United States Government Accountability Office Technology Assessment AI Generative AIs Environmental and Human Effects
items.type: Policy Development — Commissioning concept notes white papers or outlines that serve as inputs for drafting.
items.justification: The Government Accountability Office's assessment report systematically analyzing how generative AI affects energy use water consumption carbon emissions and e-waste across its full lifecycle. In Section 2 (pp.11–18) GAO documents that training and using generative AI requires substantial electricity and water while developers rarely disclose data creating major knowledge gaps. Sections 1.3–1.4 (pp.5–7) explain methods for measuring impacts including data-center efficiency (PUE/WUE) and lifecycle assessments covering hardware manufacturing use and end-of-life disposal. Section 4.1 (pp.29–30) presents policy options to mitigate impacts such as improving environmental data reporting and encouraging more resource-efficient mo

items.title: Federal AI Use Case Inventories + public posting
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: This initiative addresses fairness and non-discrimination through mandatory monitoring and evaluation (M&E) mechanisms for federal AI use. OMB Memorandum M-24-10 requires agencies to inventory AI use cases annually and publicly report which systems are “rights-impacting” including risks of inequitable or discriminatory outcomes and how they are managed (Sec. 3(a)(iv) p. 5). For such systems agencies must conduct ongoing monitoring to detect AI-enabled discrimination perform periodic human reviews and mitigate or discontinue use if discriminatory impacts cannot be addressed (Sec. 5(c)(iv)(D)–(F) pp. 19–20; Sec. 5(c)(v)(C) p. 23). These requirements institutionalize continuous oversight of bias and fairness impacts (p. 21).

items.title: Health Data Technology and Interoperability Certification Program Updates Algorithm Transparency and Information Sharing
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The HTI-1 Final Rule advances Human Oversight and Determination by regulating AI/ML-enabled Predictive Decision Support Interventions (DSIs) used in certified health IT. It requires developers to provide plain-language explanations disclose intended use limitations and risks and implement risk-management practices enabling clinicians to independently evaluate contextualize and override AI outputs rather than defer to them. The rule explicitly links transparency to preventing over-reliance and supporting informed human judgment (§170.315(b)(11) pp. 37–46; discussion on independent review and avoiding over-reliance pp. 41–45).

items.title: Health Data Technology and Interoperability Certification Program Updates Algorithm Transparency and Information Sharing
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: The HTI-1 Final Rule supports Human Oversight and Determination through ongoing monitoring and surveillance under the ONC Health IT Certification Program. Certified health IT with AI/ML-enabled Predictive Decision Support Interventions (DSIs) is subject to post-certification surveillance maintenance of certification and corrective actions ensuring systems continue to operate as decision-support tools rather than replacing human judgment. Monitoring focuses on compliance with transparency risk-management and documentation requirements enabling clinicians to reassess trust and intervene over time (§170.315(b)(11) pp. 37–46; Program surveillance and enforcement discussion pp. 240–247).

items.title: Health Data Technology and Interoperability Certification Program Updates Algorithm Transparency and Information Sharing
items.justification: The HTI-1 Final Rule reinforces Human Oversight and Determination through administrative enforcement actions that ensure AI remains a support tool subject to human judgment. Non-compliance with transparency risk-management and documentation requirements for AI/ML-enabled Predictive Decision Support Interventions can trigger information-blocking investigations and civil monetary penalties enforced by HHS Office of Inspector General (OIG). This enforcement framework incentivizes organizations to maintain conditions that enable clinicians to independently review questions and override AI outputs preserving human agency (§170.315(b)(11) pp. 37–46; Enforcement and Penalties pp. 245–247).

items.title: US Department of Justice Compliance Plan for OMBMemorandum M-24-10
items.justification: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ)’s M-24-10 compliance initiative operationalizes AI Impact Assessments by “standing up a new AI Impact Assessment process” for rights- and safety-impacting AI in “1. Strengthening AI Governance – General” (p.2) coordinated by the Office of Privacy and Civil Liberties with the ETB and CAIO (p.2). It also launches quantitative real-world evaluation of these AI uses (p.2) and updates Initial Privacy Assessment Privacy Impact Assessment and Authorization to Operate processes to integrate with AI governance (p.3).

body.name: Chief AI Officer (CAIO) AI Governance Board (agency AI governance body)

items.title: AI Use Case Inventory Office of the Assistant Secretary for Administration & Management
items.justification: The Public AI Use-Case Inventory operationalizes disclosure by requiring each agency to inventory its AI use cases and “post a public version on the agency’s website” (Appendix §3(b)(v) p.11) and to do so on a recurring cycle (see “Consolidated Table of Actions” p.25). This produces an accessible agency-run public registry describing government AI uses. Example of implementation: the U.S. Department of Labor publishes its public AI Use Case Inventory online.

body.name: Office of Management and Budget (OMB)

items.title: GSA Unveils OneGov Strategy to Transform How the Government Buys Goods and Services
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) OneGov addresses public procurement of AI by standardizing and centralizing federal acquisition of IT tools—the channel through which agencies commonly buy AI capabilities—using enterprise-wide terms/pricing and direct OEM engagement to improve transparency cybersecurity and reduce fragmentation/lock-in. It frames procurement as a “shared enterprise” and begins with easier access to IT tools on standardized deals expanding across categories. (GSA news release Apr 29 2025 esp. opening paragraphs describing “first phase… IT tools… standardized terms and pricing” and “direct engagement with OEMs”).

body.name: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP)

items.title: AI Training Series for Government Employees
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Organized through the AI Community of Practice (AI CoP) of the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) within the Technology Transformation Services (TTS) Centers of Excellence this initiative  supports Public Procurement of AI by building procurement capacity: the page’s “Acquisition Track” explicitly trains staff on AI procurement including “Buying AI: Government Contracts 101” “Risk Management & Ethics” “Developing a Long-Term AI Acquisition Strategy” (explainability/harms/compliance) “Data Privacy Considerations” and “Compliance with AI-Related Regulations” (all procurement-relevant). See “Access the 2024 Training Series Acquisition Track” (lines 68–77).

body.name: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP)

items.title: Department of Labor Compliance Plan Office of Management and Budget Memorandum M-25-21
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: DEPARTMENT OF LABORCOMPLIANCE DOL’s M-25-21 Compliance Plan (2025) advances Public Sector Skills Development by committing to continuous AI training for staff. In “AI Literacy and Engagement” it pledges regular outreach and training for “AI education upskilling and reskilling” to build an “AI-ready workforce” (p.2). In “1.3 AI Talent” it describes role-based training pathways via a learning management system and plans for certification/career tracks to strengthen AI capabilities across the Department (pp.4–5).

body.name: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Chief AI Officer (CAIO) Agency AI Governance Board

items.title: Encouraging the Use of Workforce Innovation and Opportunity ActFunding to Help Youth and Adults Develop AI Skills
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Under the U.S. DEPARTMENT OF LABOR TEGL 03-25 advances AI reskilling/upskilling by directing state/local workforce boards to use WIOA Title I (Youth Adult Dislocated Worker) funds to help participants develop AI skills via AI literacy training integrating AI learning into programs partnerships and creating AI skills programs (pp.1 Secs. 1–2). It then provides implementation guidance on delivering AI literacy through the public workforce system and links it to WIOA authorities (pp.2–4 Sec. 4(a)–4(e)).

body.name: US Department of Labor (DOL)

items.title: Supercharging Americas AI Workforce
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The initiative supports AI reskilling/upskilling by curating and connecting government-supported AI education and workforce training opportunities. Under “America needs an AI-ready workforce…” it describes DOE lab training that builds AI concepts and skills through hands-on research experiences and investments in an “AI-ready workforce” including professionals “looking to add to their skillsets.” By 2025 the education and workforce opportunities provided by the DOE and NSF pilot program will add to the national AI workforce by training more than 500 new researchers at all career stages in a variety of critical basic research and enabling technology development areas.

body.name: US Department of Labor (DOL)

items.title: Department of State Compliance Plan for OMB Memorandum M-25-21
items.justification: Agency M-25-21 Compliance Plans operationalize AI safety/security by translating “minimum risk management practices” into agency controls. Example: the HHS Compliance Plan lists “Cybersecurity” as a key domain and commits to speeding AI through the Authority to Operate (ATO) while enabling “develop test and maintain” AI with monitoring capabilities (Sec. “Removing Barriers to the Use of AI” p.4). It also requires applying minimum practices to high-impact AI and stopping non-compliant AI tying ongoing compliance to FISMA the NIST RMF and NIST SP 800-53 security/privacy controls via the ATO process (Sec. “Implementation of Risk Management Practices…” p.11).

body.name: Chief AI Officer Council (CAIOC)

items.title: Board Governance of the Federal Reserve System Compliance Plan for OMB-Memorandum M-25-21
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The Fed’s Compliance Plan for OMB M-25-21 supports transparency/explainability by committing to public-facing and internal documentation of AI use. It will report use-case practices via the annual AI Use Case Inventory (Overview p.1) and states inventories are validated for “accurate and transparent reporting” (AI Use Case Inventory p.7). It increases explainability through governance artifacts: publishing lists of approved AI environments/models/tools and licensed data inputs for GenAI (Removing Barriers—IT Infrastructure and Data p.2; Agency Policies p.6) and requiring “human-in-the-loop” review to verify outputs (Developing oversight procedures p.3).

body.name: The body unit or mechanism is namedChief AI Officer (CAIO)Chief AI Officer Council (interagency body chaired by the Office of Management and Budget)(As titled in OMB Memorandum M-25-21 Sections 3(a)(i) and 3(c)(i))

items.title: AI in Education
items.justification: The evidence is a government-commissioned research report produced by ANEP's Directorate of Educational Planning (Exp. 1-483/24). It provides an overview of AI and large language models examines AI's role in formal education and includes recommendations for how educational institutions should address AI going forward including fostering critical AI understanding among students and guidance for teachers. While advisory rather than binding it represents a formal government knowledge-generation effort to inform AI literacy policy within the formal education system.

items.title: Recommendations on algorithmic transparency
items.justification: The observatory of AI developed a document called Recommendations on algorithmic transparency. This document is Justified (Page 6) on the possible biases that AI may have. It promotes proactive identification and mitigation of bias by requiring public bodies to document datasets training processes system objectives and impacted audiences enabling traceability of discriminatory risks (pp. 14–15). It mandates audit and control mechanisms continuous evaluation of system behavior and recording of social and human rights impacts (p. 15). it incorporates impact assessment tools recommending both Impact Assessments to systematically identify risks to people and address unfair or discriminatory effects (p.19).

body.name: Public Sector Strategic Committee for AI and Data

items.title: AI Observatory
items.justification: The Observatory published & reported 3 meetings in which they addressed the issues of Impact assessments in Human Rights: https://www.gub.uy/agencia-gobierno-electronico-sociedad-informacion-conocimiento/comunicacion/publicaciones/informes-espacios-dialogo-del-observatorio-inteligencia-artificial. First meeting included the proposal to include recommendations on Human Rights as part of the work of the Observatory (p.3). Second meeting included the intention to send a clear message about which uses don't allow the application of AI in the State from the point of view of guaranteeing human rights (p.4). Meeting 3 evaluated if a human rights impact assessment was necessary for public services (p. 4).

body.name: Strategic Committee of the Public Sector for AI and Data

items.title: Decree 145/2025 which operationalises and enforces Law 20396/2025
items.justification: Decree 145/2025 operationalises Law 20.396/2025 by extending algorithmic transparency obligations beyond individual workers to trade unions incorporating a collective dimension to algorithm information access. It establishes concrete criteria for labour inspectors courts and social security authorities to assess employment dependency based on algorithmic control indicators such as scheduling and disciplinary systems. It also mandates occupational health and safety standards regardless of worker classification and requires platforms to maintain a physical national presence to ensure labour law compliance and enforcement by the General Labour Inspectorate.

body.name: The Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MTSS) / General Labour and Social Security Inspectorate

items.title: Survey of use cases of AI application in the State
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: AGESIC's AI Observatory publishes individual use-case files for each AI system in operation across public agencies disclosing the technology type training data type licence human supervision arrangements implementation stage responsible agency and key implementation challenges. As of 2024 27 active or pilot cases were documented. Files are publicly accessible via the Observatory's dedicated page. See: https://www.gub.uy/agencia-gobierno-electronico-sociedad-informacion-conocimiento/casos-de-uso-inteligencia-artificial

body.name: AI Observatory

items.title: Cybersecurity and AI course in the field of Public Administration
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The National School of Public Administration (ONSC) offers a 16-hour course on Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence for public officials last updated September 2025. Module 3 covers AI fundamentals safe use of AI applications in public administration practical exercises and ethical and legal considerations in AI. The course's specific objective includes promoting the safe use of AI applications among civil servants. See the machine-translated programme here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cJTkt-ay5KnQjQWraMFIc8qmElQWAuM6/view?usp=share_link

body.name: Strategic Committee of the Public Sector for AI and Data

items.title: Recommendations on Algorithmic Transparency
items.justification: The document promotes transparency and explainability by requiring agencies to disclose how AI systems work their data sources purposes and limitations (pp. 4–5). It clarifies that people must be informed when decisions involve AI and be given meaningful explanations of system outcomes. It also mandates proactive publication of system details—objectives processes data types and impacts—to ensure understandable and accessible information for the public (pp. 9 12–13).

body.name: Strategic Committee for AI and Data

items.title: One Million AI Leaders
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The program led by Ministry of Digital Technologies “One Million Artificial Intelligence Leaders”  the educational platforms aistudy.uz and omp.aistudy.uz have been launched. Platforms offer five free online courses aimed at training young people with modern knowledge and skills in the field of AI. The program is scheduled to run until 2027 and aims to train One million young specialists in the field of AI and more than 1000 trainers who will teach computer science teachers in schools and universities. The project will also cover schoolchildren with a national AI competition. The programme doesn’t fully cover formal curriculum reform across all levels it does contribute to labour&skills via large-scale public training.

body.name: The Ministry of Digital Technologies of the Republic of Uzbekistan

items.title: Seminar on the positive and negative aspects of AI in spreading fake information and disinformation
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Ministry of Digital Technologies held a capacity-building seminar (May 29 2024) on AI’s role in spreading fake information/disinformation training information services on risks and countermeasures. Deepfakes fabricated images and news and apps that help distinguish false reports supporting prevention and response to AI-facilitated harms were explicitly discussed during the seminar.

items.title: Development of National AI Model
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: In July 2025 Uzbekistan announced the development of a National AI Language Model emphasizing both technological and cultural localization. Officials noted that current global language models often misinterpret Uzbek names faces and cultural symbols reinforcing stereotypes. The national model aims to ensure accurate representation of Uzbek identity language history and heritage—strengthening cultural and linguistic diversity within AI systems.

body.name: The Ministry of Digital Technologies

items.title: Green Data Centers A New Infrastructure Hub
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: Government-led initiative include such examples as push for green renewable-powered data centers to support AI workloads: at ICT Week 2024 the Ministry of Digital Technologies and IT Park signed an MoU with DataVolt for a 10 MW data center powered by renewables; the government also announced plans with DataVolt for three green data centers (up to 500 MW by 2032). These actions explicitly tie AI infrastructure to lower-impact energy sources.

items.title: Women & AI Forum 2025
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Multistakeholder consultations or advisory groups
items.justification: Organized under the initiatives of GAP Women IT Union and IT Ladies with support from the IT Education Association and co-organized by the Ministry of Digital Technologies the forum served as a platform for dialogue experience exchange and presentation of success stories in the digital economy. Discussions centered on the influence of AI on education entrepreneurship and professional growth while participants showcased programs that encourage girls and women to pursue careers in technology.

items.title: Parliamentary Discussion of the Draft law On Regulating Relations Arising from the Use of AI
items.justification: The government-led draft AI bill implements Human Oversight & Determination by (1) mandating labels for AI-generated content to inform users when outputs are machine-produced and (2)it emphasizes that when making decisions regarding human rights and freedoms one cannot rely solely on the conclusions of information resources and systems created using AI. These provisions were publicly outlined by the Legislative Chamber and ministries during April–May 2025 deliberations and in later adoption reports; the full draft text is not public.

items.title: One Million AI Leaders
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: Part of the One Million AI Leaders initiative led by Ministry of Digital Technologies according to Resolution 452 directly advances reskilling and upskilling by providing nationwide government-backed AI training to prepare citizens for an AI-driven labour market. It offers free online courses on AI coding and digital skills through platforms such as AIStudy.uz and includes regional hackathons and practical learning activities. By 2030 it is planned to train 4.75 million schoolchildren and students 150000 teachers and 100000 civil servants.

body.name: Ministry of Digital Technologies of the Republic of Uzbekistan

items.title: Platform and Guide to using AI in teaching and learning
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The platform is operated by the Vietnam Institute of Educational Sciences (VNIES) under the Ministry of Education and Training and serves as a dedicated portal for AI in education. Relevant sections (as seen in the Guide) include Part I (Introduction to AI in education and AI tools) Part III (AI competency requirements and guidance for learners) and Part IV (AI competency requirements and guidance for teachers) which together aim to build foundational understanding and responsible use of AI in educational settings.

body.name: Official dispatch No 2250/BGDT-GDPT year 2025 on the implementation of the Official Instructions for AI Applications in Teaching and Learning

items.title: Vietnam Anti-fake news platform
items.type: Monitoring Evaluation & Information Systems — Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) reports or platforms
items.justification: This website is set up and managed by the Vietnamese government previously the Ministry of Information and Communications currently the Ministry of Culture Sports and Tourism under the Authority of Broadcasting and Electronic Information. This platform allows users to report cases of misinformation and violence on the digital space which covers AI-facilitated misinformation and violence. One of the news featured on the fake news website explicitly was targeted at AI violence/misinformation see link https://web.archive.org/web/20260128052015/https://tingia.gov.vn/cuc-du-lich.html

items.title: Nationwide campaign to combat exploitation of ChatGPT and AI to distort and sabotage Vietnams politics
items.justification: These series of articles have been a systematic attempt to prevent use of AI technologies in spreading misinformation to distort Vietnam's politics as part of implementation of Resolution No. 35-NQ/TW dated October 22 2018 of the Politburo on strengthening the protection of the Party's ideological foundation and combating erroneous and hostile viewpoints in the new situation. The Steering Committee 35 (SC35) - a special organization of the Communist Party of Vietnam operating from the central to local levels to protect the Party's ideological foundation and combat erroneous and hostile viewpoints especially in cyberspace - leads this nationwide campaign.

items.title: Lao Cai Provincial Police punished 3 cases of using AI images to post false information on social networks
items.justification: Lao Cai Provincial Police punished 3 cases of using AI images to post false information on social networks. After verification the Lao Cai Ward Police confirmed that this was fake information and the image was created using AI technology. The account holder N.V.T. (born in 1989 residing in Cam Duong Ward) admitted to posting the image to 'gain likes and views.' The Lao Cai Ward Police have issued a report and a decision to impose an administrative fine of 7.5 million VND on N.V.T. The Lao Cai Provincial Police said that spreading fake news and false information on the internet is particularly dangerous at a time when the locality is focusing intensely on disaster prevention and control.

items.title: The Cybersecurity Department recommends the 4T principle when allowing children to participate in the online environment and use AI tools
items.justification: At the Ministry of Information and Communications' regular November press conference the Deputy Director of the National Cybersecurity Monitoring Center (NCSC) shared some of the risks that artificial intelligence (AI) applications can pose to children: 1) access to inappropriate information; 2) leakage of private and personal information; 3) being lured or enticed into participating in dangerous challenges; 4) acting on AI advice including biased inaccurate harmful or misleading content. The Information Security Department recommends adhering to the '4T principles' which include: compliance intelligence caution and kindness.

body.name: There is no one specific body or unit It just builds on the existing mechanism of children protection across ministries and agencies

items.title: Au Lac AI Alliance
items.type: Knowledge Generation — Research centers or networks
items.justification: The Au Lac AI Alliance is to develop LLM that can process Vietnamese accurately naturally and in accordance with Vietnamese culture and identity thereby improving public knowledge and promoting national economic development. The activities of the Alliance are based on three principles: Consensus - Respect - Open Community. One of the core functions is Building AI standards and policies aiming to contribute opinions on policies standards and codes related to AI to ensure safe responsible and legally compliant products. This is a gov-led initiative because Professor Dr. Nguyen Xuan Thang Politburo member Director of Ho Chi Minh National Academy of Politics Chairman of the Central Council of Theory was one founding member.

items.title: Decision No 36/Q-TTg (11/01/2024) on the Information and Communication Infrastructure Planning for the period 2021-2030 with a vision to 2050
items.type: Policy Development — Commissioning concept notes white papers or outlines that serve as inputs for drafting.
items.justification: Decision 36/QD-TTg of the Prime Minister sets out the following development requirements for 'green' data centers by 2025: 'Data centers must meet green standards according to international standards in which the Power Efficiency Index (PUE) of newly built data centers must not exceed 1.4.' The plan also outlines: 'Forming large-scale data centers adhering to green standards closely following regional energy planning; ensuring that data centers are synchronously connected data is interoperable and has the ability to redundancy each other promoting the development of the big data industry; improving the efficiency and effective exploitation of existing data centers.'  (page 5-6 Sec II.2.b).

items.title: Directive No 32/CT-TTg issued by the Prime Minister on September 4 2024 on promoting the implementation of Government Resolution No 175/NQ-CP approving the National Data Center Project
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: Directive No. 32/CT-TTg issued by the Prime Minister on September 4 2024 on promoting the implementation of Government Resolution No. 175/NQ-CP approving the National Data Center Project assigns the Ministry of Information and Communications to develop and issue regulations on the standards and norms of data centers(Section II.2.b page 2). The standards for data centers implementing Government Resolution No. 175/NQ-CP (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mhQjpYEoqYkt1vAyNSW_-V3jyqyb2uw92ntVEr2FWbg/edit?usp=sharing) approving the National Data Center Project must meet the standards and requirements for green data centers prioritizing the use of renewable energy sources and smart solutions for energy control (Appendix IIPart I.3page33

items.title: National Standards on AI and Big Data
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: This is the National Standards on Artificial Intelligence and Big Data by which all AI systems must be evaluated before being launched into the market (mandatory for high-risk and systematic risk AI systems and recommended for low-risk AI systems. This National Standards provides a reference technical point to assess risks from AI systems which include bias assessment in page 7 - 3.3.3 (Sample Selection Bias). Components from 3.3.3.1 to 3.3.3.5 describing different types of technical bias (3.3.3.1. (sample selection bias);3.3.3.2. (missing at random); 3.3.3.3.(missing at random-class); 3.3.3.4.(missing completely at random); 3.3.3.5. (missing not at random))

items.title: National Standards on AI and Big Data
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The design of this risk management process is largely based on the well-known risk management process of ISO 31000. After identifying risks organizations then assign the likelihood of occurrence and analyze the potential negative impact of the identified risks. Here it is crucial to decide on appropriate methods to quantify different risk scenarios and define acceptable ranges for these measures. This facilitates the risk assessment of the AI model of interest against the identified risks of the risk identification phase. (Artificial Intelligence - Life Cycle Processes and Quality Requirements - Part 2:Robustness). Thus the standards indicate the process and requirements of the assessment.

items.title: Draft Law on Employment (amended)
items.justification: At parliamentary discussions on 7th May 2025 on the draft Law on Employment (amended) National Assembly deputies proposed having policies to support workers affected by the conversion of automation technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to ensure the ability to adapt and change jobs. 1) Add a separate clause 'have policies to support workers affected by the transformation of automation technology and artificial intelligence'; 2) Mandate gov agencies to update labor market data at least quarterly synthesize and publish periodic labor situation reports every 6 months. The labor market database must be synchronously connected and shared with the population tax insurance and vocational education databases.

items.title: Explanation to the public on official news outlets The process of handling traffic violations from AI camera
items.justification: The initiative led by the Traffic Police Department under Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security provides public information about the operation of an AI-based traffic monitoring and enforcement system. Through the explanation of how the system detects violations using surveillance cameras processes data and requires human verification before penalties are issued the authorities disclose key aspects of how AI is used in public service enforcement thus contributes to public disclosure of government AI use by explaining the system’s functioning and role in traffic enforcement.

items.title: The 2024 Action Plan for implementing the Strategy for the Development of AI Applications until 2030 (AI Application Strategy) was issued under Decision 2259/QD-BTTTT dated December 7 2022 by the Minister of Information and Communications
items.type: Programmatic Implementation & Funding — Operational programs plans or projects
items.justification: The 2024 Action Plan (p45) set targets that at least 100 (by 2024) and 1000 (by 2030) officials and experts in central and local government agencies and state-owned corporations and companies will receive training and knowledge enhancement in applied AI completing the applied AI training course integrated into the Project 'Raising awareness popularizing skills and developing human resources for national digital transformation until 2025 with orientation to 2030' approved by the Prime Minister of Information and Communications in Decision No. 146/QD-TTg dated January 28 2022. Ministry of Information and Communications was the leading gov actor.

items.title: Training course on digital transformation and application of AI in performing tasks and public duties at the Ministry of Home Affairs in 2025
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: From June 21 to 22 at the Ministry Headquarters the Ministry of Home Affairs organized a training course on digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI) application for civil servants leaders and managers at the Department level and equivalent at units under the Ministry. The training course is the first activity in a series of training programs for all civil servants and public employees of the Ministry of Home Affairs (the Ministry of Home Affairs organized 29 training courses including 12 digital transformation training courses and 17 training courses on AI application in performing tasks and public duties) with the goal of sharing providing and raising awareness knowledge and skills on digital transformation and AI

items.title: Vietnam AI Academy program
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Formal education initiatives
items.justification: On 21/08/2025 Deputy Prime Minister attended the launching ceremony of the “Vietnam AI Academy” program. The program is the result of cooperation between the National Innovation Center Hanoi University of Science and Technology and NVIDIA Corporation (USA) to realize the agreement signed between the Vietnamese Government and NVIDIA. For the program to be implemented effectively and sustainably the Deputy Prime Minister requested NVIDIA to continue implementing activities to train high-quality human resources research transfer knowledge and develop a team of Vietnamese AI experts that meet international standards. The gov also launched an open upskilling platform: https://web.archive.org/web/20251214140107/https://onetouch.mic.gov.vn/

items.title: National Standards on AI and Big Data
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: On pages 2 and 8 of TCVN DIN SPEC 92001-2:202x DIN SPEC proposes to distinguish between high- and low-risk AI modules related to safety security privacy and ethics. In this DIN SPEC each AI module is considered either high-risk or low-risk. AI modules related to safety security privacy and ethics are classified as high-risk (potential) modules. On December 29 2023 the Ministry of Science and Technology issued Decision No. 3298/QD-BKHCN announcing this National Standard. This decision takes effect from the date of signing. The General Department of Standards Metrology and Quality is the implementing agency. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KYcXQNZ3S5iEmTeMFQoMnzGlJTjpU8ELMopSYIQQ63s/edit?usp=sharing

items.title: National Standards on AI and Big Data
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: (P49) Regarding the scope of application: The purpose of this standard is to establish a quality assurance and transparency lifecycle for artificial intelligence (AI) modules. Key quality criteria are identified and specific AI problems are addressed. To achieve this standard a set of quality requirements is presented within a specific quality metamodel for AI. (P105) Action Recommendations of the AI Standardization Roadmap: Standards and specifications can contribute to creating a safe high-quality reliable and easily explainable AI: they form the basis of technical sovereignty promote transparency and provide direction. To unlock this potential five overarching action recommendations need to be implemented.

items.title: Zambian government trains youths on AI cybersecurity to boost employability in digital labour market
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The youth training initiative described by International Trade Centre (ITC) in partnership with Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority (ZICTA) and the Women’s Entrepreneurship Access Centre (January 30 2025) advances AI literacy by equipping 175 youth (nearly half women) in Lusaka and Livingstone with knowledge in artificial intelligence cybersecurity and social media. The program enables participants to develop practical skills over 60 created freelancer profiles and some integrated AI tools into their work thus ensuring they understand apply and evaluate AI technologies. By targeting young people and bridging regional gaps it enhances equitable access to AI literacy and aligns with Zambia’s strategy to build hum

items.title: SMART Zambia Trains Provincial Leaders in ICT to Drive Digital Governance
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: This initiative had previously been provided as implementation of the framework and has since been moved to government initiative with the justification from the researcher as provided here: The SMART Zambia Institute’s 2025 ICT training for provincial heads of departments directly advances public-sector skills development by equipping senior officials with practical digital competencies including cybersecurity e-government services and the use of AI tools in operations. This initiative strengthens digital literacy enhances service delivery promotes innovation and aligns leadership capabilities with Zambia’s Digital Government Transformation Agenda building a more skilled efficient and AI-ready civil service.

items.title: Information Session by Independent Broadcasting Authority Urging ethical use of AI
items.type: Oversight Standards & Risk Management — Standards certifications or quality labels
items.justification: The Independent Broadcasting Authority’s initiative promotes the ethical use of AI by advocating for transparency and explainability in AI operations within the broadcasting sector. It encourages clear communication about how AI systems function ensuring stakeholders understand AI decision-making processes. By urging adherence to ethical standards the initiative seeks to build public trust prevent misuse and foster accountability in AI deployment thereby supporting transparency and explainability as core principles in AI governance.

items.title: Women in ICT Conference 2025
items.justification: The conference provided a platform to deepen awareness of how gender inequalities shape women’s participation in the digital economy. Participants discussed the specific barriers women face in accessing and using digital technologies including limited access to affordable devices and connectivity lower levels of digital skills and gendered online harassment. Through the discussions on cybersecurity speakers highlighted how women and girls are disproportionately exposed to online abuse and privacy violations underscoring the need for gender-sensitive cyber safety policies complaint mechanisms and survivor-centred support services.In relation to AI entrepreneurship and innovation the conference drew attention to the risks of bias.

items.title: Digital Skills Program
items.type: Capacity Building & Public Engagement — Training courses workshops
items.justification: The Zimbabwe Ministry of ICT Postal and Courier Services  launched a Digital Skills Programme (launch April 10-11 2025) which explicitly includes AI-related training as part of its upskilling agenda. According to reports the initiative aims to train 1.5 million individuals in “Programming Fundamentals Data Science Fundamentals Android Kotlin Developer Fundamentals and AI Fundamentals.” By integrating AI fundamentals into a large­scale national training effort the project supports both reskilling for those shifting into tech roles and upskilling by building deeper competencies in AI/data science in Zimbabwe’s workforce.

items.title: “Advancing Digital Rights in Albania – ADRA” project
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Under the ADRA – Advancing Digital Rights in Albania project the Center Science and Innovation for Development (SCiDEV) an independent CSO organized a public event examining the EU AI Act’s implications for Albania (p.2). As the leading civil society actor SCiDEV raised concerns about limited transparency (p.3) lack of explainability and insufficient accountability in AI uses such as biometric surveillance and public procurement. Discussions stressed that AI remains a human-directed tool (p.3) underscoring the need for meaningful human oversight institutional review capacity and contextualized alignment with EU law to safeguard rule-of-law principles.

items.title: Open public consultation on Albania’s draft National AI Strategy 2025–2030
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: In August–September 2025 SCiDEV an Albanian civil society organization focused on digital rights monitored and reported on the government’s public consultation for the draft National AI Strategy 2025–2030. Its Digital Rights e-bulletin (Summer 2025) notes that on 14 August 2025 Albania opened the consultation and outlines priority domains including education and cultural heritage and tourism linking AI policy choices to Children’s Rights in schooling and to Cultural and Linguistic Diversity through heritage preservation and access.

items.title: QuLearnLabs and AI Albania forge new partnership to tackle Europe’s deep tech talent gap
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The initiative which is a collaboration including QuLearnLabs and the CSO Albanian Centre for Artificial Intelligence (AI Albania) strengthens workforce preparedness by delivering structured training and collaborative programmes focused on AI and deep-tech skills. Through partnerships with European talent initiatives it supports reskilling and upskilling pathways for students and professionals in Albania helping them acquire competencies needed for AI-driven labour markets. At the same time its training activities build AI literacy enabling participants to understand critically assess and responsibly use AI systems at the intersection of AI and Quantum Computing.

items.title: Inclusion of Women in the Technological Sector in Angola
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: A collaboration between TIS and CFTIA focuses on developing training programmes technical courses mentorships and career opportunities for women in programming networking cybersecurity artificial intelligence and digital entrepreneurship. The partnership includes workshops bootcamps and tech fairs for young female talents across Angola aiming to strengthen women’s skills promote innovation and foster a more inclusive and competitive technological ecosystem.

items.title: Machine Learning Bootcamp Angola – Frontier Tech Leaders
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Bootcamp de Machine Learning Angola – Frontier Tech Leaders organized by UNDP Angola in partnership with the UN Technology Bank for Least Developed Countries and the UNDP Istanbul International Center for Private Sector in Development (ICPSD) mainly contributes to Reskilling/Upskilling Initiatives. The three-month program provides practical project-based training in AI Machine Learning and Deep Learning enhancing technical competencies and innovation capacity aligned with the SDGs.

items.title: Deputies: Vía Libre participated in the meeting to analyze Artificial Intelligence regulations
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The presentation by Fundación Vía Libre before the Chamber of Deputies highlights that AI development must not cross certain normative and institutional limits implicitly reinforcing the need for human oversight in decision-making. It identifies explicability as a core ethical pillar of future AI regulation (08:35) arguing that systems must remain understandable to allow effective human control and accountability. It also raises concerns about the economic costs of deploying and maintaining AI systems (12:05) framing sustainability and resource constraints as relevant considerations for public-sector AI governance.

items.title: Guide for the use of AI in the public sector in Argentina
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The guide addresses fairness transparency and human oversight across several sections. It explicitly warns that biased data and opaque systems can reinforce existing inequalities particularly in high-inequality contexts and calls for ethical criteria and impact assessments to prevent discrimination (pages 8–9). Transparency and explainability are addressed through recommendations on algorithmic transparency traceability and citizen information stressing that AI decisions must be understandable and auditable (page 11). Human oversight is emphasised through repeated references to human-in-the-loop systems and the need to avoid uncritical automation (pages 4 and 9).

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DISABILITY: LIGHTS AND SHADOWS.DOUBTS AND OPPORTUNITIES
items.justification: The article addresses the rights of persons with disabilities by analysing how AI can both create opportunities for inclusion and reinforce existing barriers. It highlights the ethical and social implications of using AI in accessibility rehabilitation and communication while warning against bias and discrimination embedded in algorithmic systems. The piece promotes a rights-based and participatory approach to AI design urging that technologies be developed with and not merely for people with disabilities.

items.title: AI for the public sector
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The initiative addresses AI Literacy by providing public-sector workers with structured training on artificial intelligence including ethical legal and governance aspects (p. 2) and practical AI techniques and applications (p. 3). It builds competencies for using AI responsibly in public administration improving decision-making and service delivery. Through its 25-hour curriculum it strengthens workers’ digital skills provides a general presentation of AI and prepares them for evolving technological demands in government roles.

items.title: AI for the Public Sector
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: This 'Asuntos del Sur' free and open course trains public-sector actors on the ethical and responsible use of AI with a strong focus on data protection privacy and security. The programme introduces regulatory and governance aspects of AI highlights legal and ethical obligations and promotes transparent accountable and safe use of data in public institutions. It strengthens institutional skills for assessing risks ensuring responsible data handling and integrating privacy-protective practices in AI projects.

items.title: GUIDE TO INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIAL - Perspectives for Civil Society Organizations
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The guide addresses Data Protection and Privacy by warning that AI systems process large amounts of personal data and require strict privacy safeguards; this is detailed in Challenges and Considerations (p.13). It addresses Safety and Security by highlighting risks such as algorithmic bias discriminatory outputs and data-security vulnerabilities on page 13. It relates to Consumer Protection through its recommendations for responsible transparent and ethical AI use to avoid harm to beneficiaries outlined on pages 14–15.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Legal Ethics: New Challenges and Opport
items.justification: LegalTech Armenia is an initiative by the Armenian Lawyers’ Association and Iravaban.net that explores how digital technologies transform the legal field in Armenia. The series provides expert analysis on tools like AI and data science and examines the ethical questions they raise including bias transparency privacy and responsibility.

items.title: FEMINNO Conference on Female Innovation
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: During the Conference a special panel was dedicated to the topic of gender natural artificial intelligence.

items.title: Paper on AI Use in Armenian Media:Ethical Considerations
items.justification: This paper aims to outline the key ethical guidelines applicable to journalism with particular attention to the use of artificial intelligence. It emphasizes the need for journalists to uphold ethical standards when engaging with AI technologies. The final recommendations (p. 5 Recommendation 2) note the growing prevalence of AI and stress the importance of journalists acquiring both technical proficiency and a clear understanding of AI’s capabilities limitations and risks. To promote responsible use media organizations (including CSOs) should implement targeted AI training programs designed to strengthen journalists’ skills and professional competencies in the field of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Inquiry on Adopting Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Submission of the Human Rights Law Centre to the Senate Select Committee Inquiry on Adopting Artificial Intelligence urged a human-rights-based approach to AI governance by referencing the Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence as a good example to adopt into Australian policy (pp. 7 9). It recommended clear accountability frameworks transparency (p. 7) standards the importance to consider the environmental wellbeing (p. 7) and independent human oversight mechanisms in AI (pp. 5 7) to prevent discriminatory (p. 7) or opaque algorithmic decision-making in Australia’s public and private sectors.

items.title: AI and Journalism Training Program
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The AI and Journalism Training Program by the Walkley Foundation addresses transparency and explainability and aspects of human oversight. Several sessions focus on understanding how AI tools work in journalism and on verifying AI-generated content including identifying deepfakes and AI-manipulated media as well as fact-checking and verification methods. It also discusses risks and responsible use of AI tools in newsroom workflows implying that journalists should critically evaluate AI outputs before using them.

items.title: SUPERCHARGING AUSTRALIA’S RENEWABLE ROLLOUT
items.justification: The Climate Council’s 2025 report links rapid data-centre expansion—fuelled by AI demand—to rising electricity use and emissions (p. 12). It recommends accelerating renewable and storage deployment to offset AI-related energy loads highlighting AI’s environmental footprint and sustainability policy needs (pp. 4 6).

items.title: AI For All – An Equitable Regulatory Framework for Australia – Submission to the Department of Industry Science and Resources on Safe and Responsible AI in Australia
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: This initiative advances the rights of persons with disabilities by influencing the Australian Government’s AI regulatory framework to include accessibility equality and participation principles. The submission calls for mandatory accessibility requirements disability impact assessments inclusive representation in AI design and AI literacy programs for the disability community. (See pp. 12–13 “Summary of Recommendations” and pp. 28–31 “Recommendations & Conclusion” of the PWDA submission.)

items.title: Centre for Future Work – Submission to the House of Representatives Inquiry into the Digital Transformation of Workplaces (2024)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Australia Institute and The Centre for Future Work’s 2024 submission to the House of Representatives analyses how AI automation and algorithmic management affect job quality safety and workers’ rights highlighting risks of surveillance intensified work and unfair decision-making (pp. 2–6). It recommends stronger labour protections transparency obligations and worker consultation (pp. 7–10). The submission also calls for national policies on reskilling to ensure workers benefit from technological change (pp. 3 11–12).

items.title: VTHC OHS Liveshow – “The Health and Safety Impacts of AI and Workplace Surveillance”
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The VTHC OHS Liveshow provides education to health and safety representatives on potential risks on AI-enabled workplace surveillance and algorithmic management. It explains psychosocial risks privacy impacts and how AI affects safety and working conditions. The session offers practical guidance on identifying hazards enforcing workers’ rights and applying existing OHS laws.

items.title: MEAA 2025 AI Campaign on Protecting Creative Workers and Jobs
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: MEAA’s 2025 AI campaign uses public statements media releases and survey findings to raise national awareness of AI’s impacts on creative workers including job loss exploitation and unauthorised use of creative content. Key evidence includes MEAA’s July 2025 ” July 2025 release:https://web.archive.org/web/20251205073000/https://www.meaa.org/mediaroom/government-urged-to-act-on-ai-and-stop-theft-of-nations-creative-assets-as-critical-productivity-talks-approach/  August 2025 release:https://web.archive.org/web/20251205073500/https://www.meaa.org/mediaroom/productivity-commissions-shortsighted-recommendations-are-a-blueprint-for-theft-of-nations-creative-and-cultural-assets/

items.title: Centre for Future Work – Research Report on Employee Voice Union Delegates and Technology Change (2024)
items.justification: The 2024 Centre for Future Work report analyses how technological change including AI affects worker voice safety and rights (pp. 3–10). It shows that strong delegate rights improve workers’ ability to respond to AI-driven management systems and identify emerging risks. The report highlights the need for consultation transparency and safeguards around AI adoption in workplaces strengthening labour protections and supporting workers’ AI literacy.

items.title: CPSU – Artificial Intelligence in the Workplace: Draft Principles (2025)
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The CPSU’s 2025 Draft Principles set standards for the responsible use of AI in public sector workplaces. They call for transparency human oversight worker consultation protections against AI-enabled surveillance and fair processes for performance assessment (pp. 1–3). The principles require employers to provide training and support where AI changes job roles improving workers’ AI capabilities and ensuring fair reskilling pathways.

items.title: Digital Rights Watch – Submission to the Senate Select Committee on Adopting AI
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: Digital Rights Watch’s submission to the Senate Select Committee on Adopting AI addresses Trust and Safety risks by centring human rights privacy and accountability in AI governance. Section B “Placing human rights at the centre” (pp. 3–5) outlines risks of biased and discriminatory AI including facial recognition and automated decision-making harms. Section C “Data Governance” (pp. 5–8) discusses privacy data provenance secondary data use and overfitting risks calling for stronger Privacy Act protections. Section D “Key risks and harms” (pp. 9–11) addresses biometric surveillance online safety and AI-enabled deepfakes. Section E (pp. 12–13) calls for impact assessments enforceable oversight and access to redress.

items.title: Human Rights Digital Rights and AI: Children’s Online Rights
items.justification: This webinar built civil society capacity by educating educators and community organisations about AI-driven risks to children including profiling privacy violations exposure to harmful content and algorithmic amplification of misinformation. It promoted awareness of safety-by-design approaches rights-based governance and responsible data practices strengthening CSO capability to advocate for protections for children in AI-mediated environments.

items.title: Human Rights Law Centre – “Rights-First: Principles for Digital Platform Regulation”
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The HRLC report provides a human-rights framework for governing digital platforms that use AI for content recommendation moderation and data processing. It highlights privacy risks profiling safety harms misinformation amplification and the need for transparency and impact assessments. The recommendations guide civil society advocacy and regulatory reform advancing responsible AI use across major Trust and Safety domains.

items.title: Law Institute of Victoria – Ethical and Responsible Use of AI Guideline
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The LIV guideline sets best-practice standards for safe AI use in legal practice including obligations to protect client data assess AI accuracy and bias maintain transparency and ensure human oversight. It addresses privacy safeguards reliability risks and consumer protection in professional services. The guidance promotes responsible AI deployment and risk assessment across a high-stakes sector.

items.title: Equitable AI Knowledge Hub
items.justification: The Equitable AI Knowledge Hub is a free public resource created by the Equitable AI Alliance to support advocates developers researchers and practitioners working at the intersection of AI and disability inclusion. It aggregates evidence-based resources insights and strategies to shape inclusive AI policy guide technology design and promote equitable AI practices that address risks and opportunities for persons with disabilities. It contributes to knowledge generation in AI ethics inclusion and policy-making helping stakeholders make informed equitable decisions about AI development and use by centralizing curated knowledge and perspectives from global experts.

items.title: Data Science in the Humanities and Social Sciences for Women.
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: It provides structured self-paced training and career guidance designed to help women transition into data science and AI-related roles. It delivered 43 online learning modules covering data science and AI fundamentals practical tools and applied methods alongside a career guide explaining skill requirements learning pathways and job profiles. These resources build AI literacy (understanding concepts methods and applications) while directly supporting reskilling/upskilling for labour-market entry or transition into AI-enabled professions.

items.title: Femmes Digitales
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Femmes Digitales – Public Association: “Supporting Women in TECH” is a non-profit organization dedicated to eliminating the gender gap in the tech industry with a goal to get more girls and women excited about technology and IT. They organize and host several AI related workshops and trainings for women in STEM field.

items.title: Conference on “The impact of digitalization and artificial intelligence on workplaces”
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: AHIK (Azerbaijan Trade Unions Confederation) and the National Confederation of Entrepreneurs (Employers) Organizations of the Republic of Azerbaijan (ASK) jointly organized this conference. In the event AI is recognized as both a labor-protection issue (occupational safety workers’ rights) and a skills challenge. Through this initiative awareness on the risks of AI for labor and skills have been raised among unions employers and state bodies and the need for continuous upskilling in the face of AI-driven change has been stressed.

items.title: Capacity Development of trade unions with appropriate advocacy and negotiation skill for adaptation of Artificial Intelligence and Lobby for establishing AI policy in the National level
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Area: Labour protections & Reskilling/Capacity BuildingProject Summary:The project assesses automation’s impact on workers and industry readiness while enhancing trade union capacity for advocacy on AI automation and Just Transition. It supports evidence-based research for policy advocacy strengthens union leaders’ knowledge and sensitizes employers brands and government on workforce impacts promoting collaboration on skill development and social security to ensure workers’ well-being during and after the 4IR transition.

items.title: Blending Art with Artificial Intelligence in the CaribbeanKey Takeways from the A.I. Symposium on Caribbean Arts & Heritage
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The AI Symposium on Caribbean Arts & Heritage led by Barbados Museum & Historical Society (BMHS) in partnership with UNDP and regional stakeholders addresses the Ethics Equity and Human Rights indicator by embedding responsible AI principles within the Orange Economy. Under Section 2: Ethics Equity and Human Rights discussions stressed that AI use in the arts must be grounded in human dignity cultural specificity and inclusivity. Panelists highlighted risks of Western-centric biases in dominant AI systems and the region’s position as a net consumer of AI tools. The symposium emphasized anchoring AI in Caribbean values to reduce inequality mitigate bias and protect cultural diversity and creators’ rights in SIDS.

items.title: Belarusian Association of Journalists: Research (guideline/recommendations) on Artificial Intelligence in Media
items.justification: The Belarusian Association of Journalists published research/guidelines on the responsible use of AI in media. The document provides best practices regarding transparency by requiring disclosure of AI-generated content clear labeling and explanations of how AI tools influence news production it emphasises human oversight recommending editorial control verification and accountability for AI-assisted outputs it addresses fairness warning against biased datasets discriminatory outputs and the risks of misinformation supporting ethical and safe AI use in journalism (pp. 6-10 28-30).

items.title: Human Constanta: public awareness on voice deepfake fraud in Belarus
items.justification: Belarusian NGO 'Human Constanta' published an article explaining how criminals in Belarus use AI-generated voice deepfakes for fraud schemes. The article and awareness campaign explain how deep-fake voice AI is used for fraud raising awareness of the technology and its risks (which directly contributes to literacy/understanding of AI)

items.title: Belarusian Association of Journalists: Research (guideline/recommendations) on Artificial Intelligence in Media
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Belarusian Association of Journalists published research/guidelines on the responsible use of AI in media. The document raises awareness of AI technologies promotes understanding of their impacts (AI literacy - pages 7 and 10).

items.title: Development and submission of the “Model Law on Artificial Intelligence” to the Commonwealth of Independent States by the United Institute of Informatics Problems of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus (research center)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) Model Law on Artificial Intelligence was developed by the United Institute of Informatics Problems of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus adopted on April 18 2025 within the CIS sent to the parliaments of the CIS member states and was recommended for use in national legislation. It includes Data Protection and Privacy (Arts 1934) Data Sharing and Access (Arts 3132) Safety and Security (Arts 1225) Consumer Protection (Arts. 36) Access to Redress and Remedy (Arts. 3536) Impact Assessments (Arts. 1821)

items.title: Human Constanta: public awareness on voice deepfake fraud in Belarus
items.justification: Belarusian NGO 'Human Constanta' published an article explaining how criminals in Belarus use AI-generated voice deepfakes for fraud schemes. The material raises public awareness of AI-enabled deception explains the mechanism of voice-cloning attacks describes real cases reported by Belarusian residents and provides guidance on how to recognize and avoid deepfake-based scams. It has a link to a YouTube video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5i53USVKuQg) illustrating cases and a call to share the article to make the public aware of the AI-generated scams. It covers topics of consumer protection safety/security and mitigation of AI-facilitated misinformation.

items.title: Belarusian Association of Journalists: Research (guideline/recommendations) on Artificial Intelligence in Media
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Belarusian Association of Journalists published research/guidelines on the responsible use of AI in media. The document provides best practices and how to avoid risks regarding data protection and privacy deepfakes and misinformation security concerns consumer protection (pp. 6-12 18-30) as well as establishing criteria and mechanisms for assessing artificial intelligence technologies for their safety and other characteristics for placement on the market and operation (p. 28).

items.title: Transparency International Belgium: AI & Technology Conference: Using Technology and AI to Enhance Ethics and Compliance Efficiency
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Transparency International Belgium a CSO hosted this conference in Brussels. The event focused on the intersection of AI Ethics and Compliance. By bringing together experts to explore the transformative solutions offered by AI to streamline compliance and reduce risks the conference served as a Public Engagement platform. The central theme of Ethics and Compliance directly relates to Human Oversight (ensuring ethical control) and Transparency (managing regulatory risks and data protection) in AI systems

items.title: ECOS (Environmental Coalition on Standards) Joint Statement: 'Within Bounds: Limiting AI's environmental impact'
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: ECOS ECOS Environmental Coalition on Standards a Brussels-based CSO published this statement in February 2025 which functions as a set of Ethical Guidelines/Best Practices It calls for mandatory measurement and reporting of environmental impacts (including energy and water usage) across the AI lifecycle This directly promotes Environmental Impact awareness and advocates for new Transparency standards and policy implementation relevant to Belgian data center and AI policy. it was a joint CSO statement over 90 CSOs signed it.

items.title: Artificial intelligence: a useful tool for people with disabilities?
items.justification: Esenca is part of the Solidaris network of associations and represents the union of people with disabilities and carries out concrete actions to affirm the rights of these people (p. 10). In the report it explains how AI can positively influence the lives of people with disabilities (p. 4) in communication (p. 5) medical care (p. 6) training and employment (p. 6) and the challenges and ethical issues to be considered (p. 7) such as financial accessibility privacy and security (p. 8). Regarding the publication date: https://www.esenca.be/analyse-2023-intelligence-artificielle/

items.title: Future of work: rethinking workers' rights in the digital age Conference (ETUI/KU Leuven)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This conference was co-organized by the European Trade Union Institute (ETUI) and academics (KU Leuven) bringing together trade unionists policymakers and researchers. Its core aim was to 'rethink workers' rights' in the face of algorithmic management and AI. The agenda included sessions and workshops on: 'Protection of working conditions on labour platforms' and 'Algorithmic discrimination' directly addressing the need for robust Labour Protections to counter risks like discrimination precarious employment and fragmentation of work caused by AI deployment.

items.title: League for Human Rights action against Uber eats
items.justification: The Egaliberté Foundation CIEP-B and the Human Rights League filed a complaint with the Brussels Court of First Instance against Uber (EATS) to defend workers' rights regarding data and automated decision-making (p. 1). There is also a lack of transparency regarding workers' personal data collected by the Uber Eats platform (p. 1-2). Uber must provide information about the personal data processed in a format that allows for understanding the analyses performed clearly and completely informing workers about profiling methods automated decisions and any other processing (p. 2).

items.title: Ligue des Droits Humains - Campaign for a Total Ban on Biometric Surveillance and AI Rights Advocacy
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Ligue des droits humains and the Liga voor Mensenrechten advocate for a total ban on facial recognition in Belgium. The Artificial Intelligence Law prohibits the use of this technology due to the risks it poses to European citizens but also provides for exceptions. The two Leagues are appealing to Belgian authorities to approve a law that protects the rights of all (p.1).
