They warn of the abusive access to databases by the police and that these databases are shrouded in significant opacity both in terms of quantity and the information they contain (p.2). Authorities should hold a public debate on structural solutions that are adequate to the public interest and respect our fundamental rights (p.4).

items.title: Women Digital Week
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: During the 2025 edition of Women Digital Week held in Cotonou FRIARE partnered with digital entrepreneurs to promote women’s inclusion in the AI ecosystem. Through a masterclass on ChatGPT and generative AI led by Mrs Paola Dagba FRIARE empowered participants to understand and apply AI tools in entrepreneurship marketing and digital creativity. The initiative directly addressed gender inclusion by equipping women with AI literacy and advancing responsible and equitable digital innovation in Benin. Further online search describes it as a foundation focused on ethics impact assessment awareness and capacity-building around AI and therefore can be considered a CSO.

items.title: Benin Youth Internet Governance Forum 2024 (Benin Youth IGF 2024)
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Benin Youth IGF 2024 addressed AI Literacy and reskilling or upskilling by convening a youth-focused forum on AI’s impact on training and employment aiming to “prepare young people for the proper use of AI” and give them “basic knowledge” and awareness of job prospects (Objectives p.5). It further recommends investing in training Benin’s youth to use and develop AI technologies (Recommendations p.17). It also discusses that in the field of education AI facilitates learner learning by offering personalized resources tailored to the needs of each student. Self-education is also emphasized enabling students and professionals to train autonomously. In addition the integration of AI by teachers to enrich educational (p. 10).

items.title: Forum on Information & Democracy (FID) – ALCRER AI Governance and Trust & Safety Initiative (Benin)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The brochure by ALCRER (Association de Lutte contre le Racisme l’Ethnocentrisme et le Régionalisme) a CSO coordinating national contributions to the Forum on Information and Democracy (FID addresses Safety and Security Access to Redress and Remedy and AI-Facilitated Misinformation and Violence. Under “Legal and Strategic Framework for AI” and “AI Governance Framework” it calls for AI-content detection transparency risk-mitigation measures and a dedicated AI authority. Under “AI and Elections” it stresses algorithmic transparency and electoral security while “AI Governance Framework” and “AI and Journalism” establish complaint mechanisms mediation opt-out rights and compensation.

items.title: Guide to Implementing Data Protection and Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Bolivia
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: This is a guide created by the InternetBolivia Foundation for the responsible implementation of AI. It outlines several basic principles regarding transparency non-discrimination and inclusion in the development use and implementation of AI technologies by public and private entities. The document was prepared in collaboration with several specialists and local experts.

items.title: Mis datos project
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: InternetBolivia Foundation have organized several workshops during 2024 and 2025 for students companies and public servants regarding the implementation of its Guide for data protection and responsible AI. At least 400 people participated in these workshops along the last two years. Also several materials such as infographics and comics were distributed through social media.

items.title: Data Protection Implementation Guide and Responsible Use of AI
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Data Protection Implementation Guide and Responsible Use of AI directly strengthens the Trust and Safety dimension by establishing robust safeguards for privacy security and ethical AI. It adopts GDPR principles—including accountability and transparency (pp. 11–12)—and introduces mandatory risk assessments such as DPIAs for high-risk AI (pp. 18 56). The guide outlines security measures aligned with ISO 27001 (pp. 31–34) requirements for human oversight and explainability under the EU AI Act (pp. 51–55) and protections against algorithmic discrimination (p. 50). It also emphasizes continuous monitoring audits and human-rights due diligence (pp. 43–45 57–59) reinforcing public trust and AI governance

items.title: Gaborone Hub  Young AI Leaders
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Hub runs educational webinars and AI literacy sessions that break down core AI concepts for young people who haven’t had formal exposure. It also supports reskilling and upskilling through applied AI hackathons hands-on projects and mentorship opportunities that help participants develop practical workforce-relevant AI skills.

items.title: Public Consultation on Artificial Intelligence in Brazil: inclusion of promoting competitiveness
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: A group of non-governmental and civil society organizations is holding a public consultation platform: What Brazil Wants from Artificial Intelligence. The toll operates with open themes that can be proposed by anyone. Simply search within the platform. Regarding fairness: mechanisms that guarantee fair and competitive AI markets preventing excessive market concentration; transparency: the exchange of information between public and private actors must respect data protection security and privacy promoting transparency without compromising competitiveness. Specifically this statement includes: Technical note presented to the Office of Senator Eduardo Gomes rapporteur of Bill 2338/2023 completed on May 8 2024 (via the link above).

items.title: The Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan: Towards AI Sovereignty? Webinar
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The event aimed to analyze the AI for the Good of All 2024-2028 Plan which outlines a series of goals to empower the Brazilian population and consolidate a robust and innovative technological infrastructure. During the event topics such as sustainable innovation social inclusion and ethical governance were widely discussed.

items.title: Brazil wants to develop AI but faces a lack of infrastructure
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: Criticism of the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Planand issues related to national data infrastructure and data centers. It highlights that the plan failed to establish measures to attract sustainable infrastructure projects. It also criticizes other parliamentary proposals to encourage the expansion of sustainable high-capacity data centers for AI systems due to a lack of indicators and planning. This was republished in newspapers.

items.title: AI and Changes in the Brazilian Judiciary
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The report is a result of the publication of a resolution by the National Council of Justice. The principle of due process in informational matters must guarantee the inclusion of the individual in the decision-making process (p. 4). The identification of biases foresees the adoption of rigorous corrective measures (p. 5). Impact assessment involves regular audits continuous monitoring and periodic reviews (p. 7). The creation of this National Committee strengthens digital governance in the Judiciary (p. 10). Recommendations on the decentralization of governance through collaborative institutional structures to include vulnerable groups (p. 15) continuous validation of algorithmic impact (p. 15) and risk mitigation methods (p.1-2).

items.title: Contributions to the National Data Protection Authority's Subsidy Collection for the Processing of Personal Data of Children and Adolescents
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Since 2024 the National Data Protection Authority the National Council for Children and Youth and other entities have been debating the treatment of children's and adolescents' data including the collection and use of data for training AI systems. Data privacy contributed to the Authority's proposals including the AI approach. One example was Meta using personal data of children for training AI (p. 17). The entity endorses age verification methods that include the use of artificial intelligence algorithms that estimate age based on online behavior patterns or facial features. These methods need to be improved to ensure accuracy and minimize risks (p. 43).

items.title: AI in the Labor Market: Who Wins Who Loses — and Who Gets Left Behind
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The report seeks to contribute to the structuring of public policies and good corporate practices that can be adopted in Brazil to promote productive inclusion in the AI era (Chapter 1 p.9).  It is no longer just a 'debate about the future' but rather a necessary political-institutional articulation that takes into account the development and implementation of AI-based solutions in the labor market that do not deepen social exclusion. The recommendations suggest: Creating a national policy for professional retraining launching a national support program for the adoption of AI by micro and small enterprises a national observatory on AI and the labor market codes of conduct for the use of AI in the workplace etc (p.60).

items.title: AI Literacy for Educators
items.justification: The course explores the transformative impact of Generative AI on the educational environment. Designed for educators at all levels it offers a comprehensive understanding of how GenAI is reshaping teaching methodologies and student learning experiences. It emphasizes the importance of digital and AI literacy addressing ethical concerns and practical applications in various educational contexts. The association headquarters and legal domicile are in São Paulo and it aims to encourage the evangelization and education of the Brazilian business environment https://i2aiportal.blob.core.windows.net/static/content/estatuto/NOVO_ESTATUTO_SOCIAL_APROVADO_DA%20_ASSOCIAC%CC%A7A%CC%83O_INTERNACIONAL_DE_INTELIGE%CC%82NCIA_ARTIFICIAL-25.05.2022.pdf

items.title: Artificial Intelligence advances among Brazilian companies but its use exposes challenges
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Research on the rapid spread of AI in Brazilian companies presents a predominantly positive view of its impact on productivity (pp. 2-3). However it indicates that bottlenecks still exist and that policies to encourage workforce training are necessary. The study also highlights inequality in access to and use of the potential benefits of AI in the workplace. Workers with higher levels of education or income use the technology more frequently. Among companies its use is more frequent in large corporations highlighting inequality in access and potential gains in productivity and income (p. 8). Overall the study indicates the need to expand training and qualification programs both within and outside companies (p. 8).

items.title: AI in the 2024 Brazilian elections - Generative AI and the first round of the 2024 elections
items.justification: The observatory is an initiative that seeks to identify and record primarily possible cases of violation of electoral justice related to the manipulation of information with generative AI in political campaigns (p. 11). The report mapped AI use cases by campaigns and citizens in cities. AI is being used by both official campaigns and voters in various media formats (images videos and audio). Among the uses identified the following stood out: the creation of deepfakes highlighted the potential for disinformation in future elections; especially cases of deepnudes targeting female candidates in different municipalities (p. 2).

items.title: Mandatory use of consumer data for training artificial intelligence (AI) on Meta platforms
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Consumer Defense Institute has filed lawsuits and denounced to the competent authorities: lack of communication and consent from users regarding the use of Meta's publications to feed artificial intelligence models (p.2). The institute demanded from the national data authority (p.5) that in addition to the lack of information there are risks of harm to which the data subjects/consumers are subjected (p.5). It is an abusive practice based on manipulation to hinder the exercise of rights making it difficult for data subjects/consumers to access their right to object (p.14). Under penalty of violating Art. 6 of the Consumer Protection which ensures the prevention and reparation of patrimonial whether individual or collective right (p.17).

items.title: Illustrated Guide Against Deepfakes
items.justification: Data Privacy Brazil developed informational material aimed at raising public awareness about the risks and challenges related to the dissemination of deepfakes AI-generated false content that simulates unreal situations and speeches within the Supreme Federal Court's Program to Combat Disinformation (p. 17). Deepfakes can foster the belief that someone said what they would never say do or a situation that never occurred resulting in scams and fraud deception to obtain sensitive personal information or even impersonation of relatives to request loans or financial transfers (p. 9). They have been used as a political weapon creating false narratives and generating sexually explicit videos and harassment in school (p.10).

items.title: Guide for Digital Influencers in the Elections
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: InternetLab and Redes Cordiais guide has launched a guide for influencers in elections. The guide explains and offers best practices on the use of artificial intelligence (p.44 political violence (p.28) disinformation (p.56) electoral crimes (p.52) and hate speech (p. 27). It explains how being careful to check before sharing is still the best way to avoid the spread of disinformation (p. 39) and avoid dissemination (p. 39). In the case of sharing electoral propaganda with AI it is necessary to have an explicit warning to followers about the use of the tool in the content (p. 45). Be aware of practices that attack and restrict opinions or groups through silencing and threats harming their freedom of expression (p. 31).

items.title: TRUST AI – Higher Education as a Catalyst for the Trustworthy and Sustainable Use of Artificial Intelligence Project number: 2024-1-BG01-KA220-HED-000249185
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The project is implemented by collaboration of six leading partners one of which is Acta Foundation Bulgaria. Some of the main objectives are promoting AI use in accordance with the principles of ethics trust and sustainability among students in the humanities university professors higher education research and business.In January 2025 the TrustAI consortium carried out a survey across Bulgaria Malta Spain Italy and Poland and gathered insights from 175 students university lecturers and business professionals.Their input helped to pinpoint the most relevant topics on ethical and trustworthy use of AI. Part of the curriculum for humanitarian students is Ethics & Governance – Bias fairness transparency GDPR and the EU AI Act.

items.title: Training materials for the project Disrupt - Bulgarian Foundation Law and Internet
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The materials are drafted by the Bulgarian Foundation Law and Internet. Section 1.4 comments on the factors that make minors LGBTQ+ youth and other marginalized groups more vulnerable online. It specifically discusses in the table with Additional Information the collection of evidence in child trafficking cases using AI tools with minimal or no human input. It is suggested that although this practice of AI-generated evidence without human-in-the-loop is already established in some countries it is arguable how this evidence will be treated by the legislators and the courts. This category is chosen as one of Disrupt project's objectives is potential of digital evidence at national and EU level.

items.title: “JuLIA” is a European research project on Justice fundamental rights and Artificial Intelligence
items.justification: The project aims at investigating the impact of the use of AI by courts and other public and private institutions on fundamental rights such as non-discrimination (https://www.julia-project.eu/). The project worked on research and preparation of articles books and trainings on the following topics: JuLIA Handbook – AI and Public Administration: The (legal) limits of algorithmic governance. One of the project partners is the Bulgarian NGO LIBRe Foundation. E.g. as part of the implementation of the project in Bulgaria LIBRe organised 'Artificial Intelligence and Consumer Protection' Judicial Lab on 08.07.2025.

items.title: Ethical issues in the use of artificial intelligence (AI)
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The guidance on the ethical issues of use of AI is primarily addressed to students explaining in plain terms that fairness means that AI should treat everyone equally without discrimination (point 2.1) and that the transparency refers to how easily we can understand how an AI system makes decisions and how the 'black box' effect makes it difficult to trace how a given conclusion was reached (point 2.2.).

items.title: The AI Act - Gaps and Opportunities from a Human Rights Protection Point of View
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The author is a member of the Bulgarian Centre for Not-For-Profit Law In the overview of the different prohibited practices the author presents possible directions for optimizing AIA that she sees useful in view of the recommendations of international human rights organizations. Direction for improvement is given in relation to the ban on an AI system exploiting any of the vulnerabilities of individuals due to age disability or specific social/economic situation namely the collecting data on people's vulnerability regardless of the criteria should be an unacceptable practice because it creates the conditions for misuse of such information which is a direct abuse of fundamental human rights (pp.8-9). She suggests changes to AI Act.

items.title: Roundtable: Fundamental Rights Artificial Intelligence and EU Law: Safeguards and Challenges
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The roundtable was organized by NGO Centre for the Study of Democracy and different lecturers were invited (including a lecturer from the Bulgarian NGO). In one of the presentations of Katja Kolman (EU Agency for Fundamental Rights) the gender bias due to use and implementation of AI systems was discussed (see slide 15 of the presentation saved in Google Drive). The event was a roundtable that brought together experts representing national fundamental rights watchdogs public administration and civil society organisations to examine how digital rights are protected in Bulgaria and delivered detailed presentations based on their own expertise and research and it represents an educational activity for professionals and stakeholders.

items.title: The Safer Internet Center presents the updated Digital Scouts educational platform
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The educational initiative is led by the Bulgarian Safer Internet Centre with the support of one of the mobile operators in Bulgaria Yettel. The the platform turns digital safety training into an interactive adventure for children and young people and is aimed to train the children on how to be safe in the digital space. This initiative aims at protection the children  from all forms of abuse neglect and exploitation. Some of the platform components challenge children to deal with real-life situations related to the AI use safe communication in online games and recognition of various types of fraud. This can be found in the Section 'Interactive educational events' of the Article.

items.title: Young People Human Security And Media Literacy (A Handbook for Teachers and Youth Facilitators)
items.justification: The sole responsibility for the doc is of Partners Bulgaria Foundation (p.1). Its mission is to support among others child protection (p.2). The overwhelming media content exposes young people to various risks due to the growing amount of misinformation & false information thus the initiative especially the development of critical thinking/AI literacy aims at protecting children from these AI harms online thus this initiative is focused on their protection in online space by increasing AI literacy (p.3). It aims to increase digital skills and media literacy among children & young people by proposing educational tools for the development of digital citizenship and critical thinking including by research methods (pp.36 and 7).

items.title: The Artificial Intelligence Council at the Bulgarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry took part in the presentation of the Draft Law on the Use and Development of AI
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The  the Bulgarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCI) is an NGO and BCCI took part in a live event for the presentation of the Bulgarian  Draft Law on the Use and Development of Artificial Intelligence where representatives of institutions academia business and civil society attended. During the event BCCI emphasized its position on the need for systematic training and retraining programs to prepare the Bulgarian workforce for the new digital environment. BCCI considers that this is fully consistent with the priorities set out in the 2025 Plan which includes partnerships with academic institutions business organizations and the state administration.

items.title: Invitation to participate in a training program for Mentors in companies - Under the project 'AI in Mentoring' - Using artificial intelligence in mentoring practice organized by the Bulgarian Industrial Chamber ('BIC')
items.justification: BIC invites mentors and business leaders to join international program aimed at improving their skills and implementing innovative approaches in mentoring through the AI use. These prospective participants are invited to join the program (employees who work with students in dual education human resources specialists team leaders mentors of newly hired employees.). The training program is organized based on the EU project 'AI in Mentoring' and includes: development of mentoring skills AI training and its application in mentoring practical real-life cases and examples related to the daily work. Given that among the target audience are also employees working with students in dual education this underpins the AI Literacy indicator.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: trends regulations and development scenarios prepared by the NGO Bulgarian Industrial Chamber ('BIC')
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This report of NGO BIC is strong evidence for AI literacy and upskilling because it explicitly stresses that “AI implies a deep and large-scale comprehensive reform of the education system in which critical thinking and analytical abilities are basic skills” (Introduction). The Conclusions highlight that “education and labor market policies can position our country among regional leaders” requiring “significant investments in human capital” (Conclusion §14). Section 5.5.2 emphasizes that attracting retaining and training AI talent is a “fundamental priority” globally while Appendix 5 scenarios show how future workplaces demand continuous learning. Together these references directly link AI adoption to literacy and upskilling.

items.title: Digital Skills for the Future program
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The ‘Digital Skills for the Future’ program is developed and led by Partners Bulgaria Foundation.  The program is interactive and develops digital competences and literacy by providing knowledge of basic concepts looking at practical applications of artificial intelligence in life supporting the development of skills to identify fake news to tackle online hate speech and to protect personal data and privacy in a digital environment.

items.title: AI-based framework for supporting micro (and small) HSPs on the report and removaL of onLIne tErroriSt content (ALLIES)
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The ALLIES project is coordinated by Bulgarian Law and Internet Foundation and implemented with the ISF support of the EU Commission under Grant Agreement ? 101080090. The ALLIES project aims at supporting micro (and small) Hosting Server Providers in achieving compliance with new requirements under the Regulation 2021/784 of on addressing the dissemination of terrorist content online also known as the Terrorism Content Online Regulation (TCO Regulation). One of the four main approaches adopted by ALLIES is learning and awareness raising. It is stated that both the learning and awareness raising initiatives will further expand the the capacity of TCO Regulation implementation by designing a taxonomy of terrorist related behaviour online.

items.title: Young People Human Security And Media Literacy (A Handbook for Teachers and Youth Facilitators)
items.justification: This Handbook is the result of a partnership between the Partners Bulgaria Foundation and PartnersGlobal within the framework of the project Engaging Youth in Combating Disinformation and Misinformation. The sole responsibility for the content of the document lies with the Partners Bulgaria Foundation (p.1). It aims to increase digital skills and media literacy among young people by proposing educational tools for the development of digital citizenship and critical thinking including by research methods (p.3). Some of the exercises are fully focused on the widespread spread of disinformation and misinformation underlined by the use of AI tools as these are threats to human security and the well-being of communities (pp.3 5 6 and 7).

items.title: Agile Manufacturing as a Service through AI Autonomous Agents (MaaSAI)
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The Bulgarian Law and Internet Foundation is leading and one of the partners in this MaaSAI Project (Agile Manufacturing as a Service through AI Autonomous Agents) that represents a transformative initiative aimed at redefining the manufacturing ecosystem through a comprehensive digital system that automates and optimizes collaboration between manufacturing system providers and consumers. As the Security Privacy Ethics and Legal Compliance Partner the Law and Internet Foundation plays a critical role in ensuring the MaaSAI Project adheres to the highest standards of data protection ethical principles and regulatory compliance. The foundation is committed to safeguarding the trust and integrity of the MaaSAI ecosystem.

items.title: AI training for blind and visually impaired people
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The National Association of Blind and Visually Impaired Students (ANEAM) has organized an AI training for 56 Blind and Visually Impaired people. The purpose is to help them grow professionally. It is a capacity building activity that promotes persons with disabilities right to education and training. This is an initiative related to inclusion.

items.title: CITADEL research paper about automated translation models French to Mooré based on Transformers
items.justification: CITADEL is a national center that belongs to a public university. They are working on AI tools that translate words from french to a local language named 'mooré'. These research outcomes promotes preservation of local languages and their integration in AI tools. Thus it is an initiatve ensuring Diversity (of languages) in AI

items.title: AI training for communications professionals
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: An association of communication professionals has organized a training session on the topic 'AI and communication'. The objective was to give to the attendees AI skills necessary for their job.

items.title: HR annual meeting
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Network of Human Resource Management (HRM) professionals in Burkina Faso has organized its annual event on the topic : 'AI and HR function transformation'. This meeting brought together experts decision-makers and students to discuss about the challenges and opportunities presented by the AI revolution in human capital management. there were conferences and workshops. Thus it was a public engagement and awareness activity organized by a CSO

items.title: The Convention of Civil Society Organizations for Domestic Election Observation (CODEL) Burkina Faso training for Media professionals and content about fact-checking and combating hate speech
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Convention of Civil Society Organizations for Domestic Election Observation (CODEL) organized a training workshop on fact-checking and combating hate speech. The training addressed the challenges posed by fake news in Burkina Faso and offered tools to help participants learn how to better verify online information especially in a context of increasing artificial intelligence (AI). The activities in the training allowed participants to learn how to distinguish fact from fiction.

items.title: Promotion of agriculture and the food system through youth entrepreneurship and innovation for a better future.
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This initiative addresses reskilling/upskilling by providing young entrepreneurs with training in innovative agricultural practices SME management and modern agribusiness techniques. It fosters AI literacy by introducing AI-powered tools such as drones and sensors for crop monitoring irrigation and harvest forecasting equipping participants with practical AI skills applicable in agriculture.

items.title: Community of Practice on Artificial Intelligence (COPAI) - Hub 12: Integrating an Inclusive Lens into AI Innovation
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Organized and led in cooperation between ESCAP and the CSO Community of Practice on Artificial Intelligence Cambodia the session promotes inclusive AI education and opportunities for all groups bridging digital divides and supporting equitable participation. (2) The discussions stress transparent trustworthy AI with ethical design data privacy and representative datasets to build public trust.

items.title: Generative AI in higher education:The need to develop or revise academic integrity policies to ensure the ethical use of AI in Cambodia (Cambodia Development Center)
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The document published by the CSO Cambodia Development Center addresses these indicators through the lens of academic integrity policy development to ensure ethical and responsible AI use. Transparency and Explainability: Covered by the need for policies to include definitions of key terms associated with AI use/misuse (p.4)  ensuring students and faculty are well-informed (p.4). Human Oversight and Determination: Advocated through the need to establish an AI committee (p.4) or assign a competent member of an existing committee to check for potential AI use in academic writing (p.4).

items.title: Center for Buddhist AI Ethics
items.justification: The Center for Buddhist AI Ethics outlines best practices for the development and use of AI based on Buddhism. Specifically they recommend in their webinar series to be mindful of how AI systems can perpetuate bias and considering its potential consequences.

items.title: Workshop on AI for Good: AI Application for Sustainable Development
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Led by the Cambodian CSO Institute of Digital Research & Innovation (IDRI) The “AI for Good” workshop mainly promotes disability by advancing accessibility through inclusion projects like Khmer Sign Language and Braille translation systems enhancing accessibility for persons with disabilities.

items.title: Research Report: Technology-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence in Cambodia: Impact on the Civic Freedoms of Women Journalists and Human Rights Defenders (Asia Centre)
items.justification: The report summarises highlights how digital platforms are increasingly used to target women journalists and human rights defenders. These online attacks often rooted in patriarchal structures not only violate women's rights but also undermine their civic freedoms and participation in public discourse. The report emphasizes the need for comprehensive strategies to address TFGBV including legal reforms digital literacy programs and enhanced security measures to protect women in the digital space.

items.title: Training: How to Use AI for CSO’s Work
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The “raining: How to Use AI for CSO’s Work initiative by the Cambodian Institute for Democracy focuses on upskilling/reskilling CSO staff by giving them practical hands-on experience with AI tools such as ChatGPT DeepL Google Translate Canva to improve communication translation and content creation tasks. It equips participants regardless of technical background with new digital competencies and a personalised action plan to apply AI in daily work (see Learning Outcomes section).

items.title: Training Young Entrepreneurs in Artificial Intelligence by SNK Foundation
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The SNK AI Challenge 2025 initiative trains youth from Buea and other cities in practical AI skills that can boost their businesses and career opportunities. Specifically the program offers a three-day intensive workshop on AI fundamentals and applications enabling participants to apply AI to creative tasks and business processes thereby addressing the area of reskilling/upskilling for AI use in real economic contexts. This directly supports enhancing digital competence and employability among young people

items.title: Global AI Alliance for Climate Action
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This is a partnership between the Vector Institute and the Turkish Informatics Foundation. The Vector Institute engages in AI research talent building as well as collaboration with industry and partnerships to advance AI-based research in Canada while the Turkish Informatics Foundation advances and explores informatics and ICTs in society the economy and public institutions. Vector will lend its AI research community to the Turkish Informatics Foundation's Be Node platform in order to explore the possibility of using AI to address climate change issues.

items.title: The Montreal AI Ethics Institute (MAIEI) Joins the AI Alliance
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Montreal AI Ethics Institute (MAIEI) co-hosted an event at the AI Alliance launch in Toronto (June 2024) promoting responsible AI adoption safety transparency and accountability in AI development. As an independent non-profit MAIEI contributed to civil society engagement in AI ethics by fostering multi-stakeholder dialogue on transparent and accountable AI practices. The event emphasized the importance of human oversight and transparency as foundational principles for responsible AI contributing to public awareness and cross-sector collaboration on AI governance in Canada.

items.title: Submission to The Standing Committee on Industry and Technology on Bill C-27 An Act to enact the Consumer Privacy Protection Act the Personal Information and Data Protection Tribunal Act and the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act and to make consequential and related amendments to other Acts
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The submission to a public consultation urges recognizing privacy as a fundamental human right and embedding intersectionality throughout Bill C-27 Canada's previous proposed law that would have overhauled federal private-sector privacy law and that would have enacted law to govern private sector AI (p. 3). The submission calls for stronger oversight (p. 14) broader harm definitions (p. 16) and inclusive consultation with affected groups before passing the law on AI (p. 4 11 11-13). It links to disability children’s gender and cultural-linguistic rights by demanding laws that protect those most at risk of digital harms through inclusive equitable AI and privacy governance with a focus on groups with intersecting identities (p. 13).

items.title: Women in AI Canada
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Women in AI Canada launched since September 2020 has expanded across 7 major cities building a strong team of volunteers who believe in the mission of Women in AI. WAI Canada successfully operates global WaiINSPIRE programs like WaiEducate WaiResearch WaiAwards NA WaiConnect WaiTALK and  WaiTIME  to promote equal opportunities for women in early-age AI education innovation and research industry careers and entrepreneurship.? They believe in nurturing mentoring and celebrating women  to create next generation of leaders in AI.

items.title: Youth Perspectives on theUse of Artificial Intelligencein Paediatric Healthcare - A consultative report writtenby MediaSmarts
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: MediaSmarts is Canada’s not-for-profit centre for digital media literacy. Although their research report is from 2026 it notes 'Drawing on insights from youth aged 10–17 in a mixed-methods study (2021–2024) led by Dr. Melissa McCradden — including 28 interviews a youth workshop and a survey of more than 300 young people — the report and guide offer recommendations to support the responsible integration of AI in paediatric care while respecting children's digital rights.' Thus the knowledge generation took place beforehand.

items.title: Responsible AI and Children: Inisghts Implications and Best Practices
items.justification: This report explores the challenges and benefits of AI for children. It was drafted by a group of academics for CIFAR (Canadian Institute for Advanced Research) a Canadian-based international research organization. The report uses a systematic review of design research applying child-centric methods and a review of existing Canadian policy. The authors recommend a child-centric and rights-based framework regarding responsible AI and children.

items.title: Canadian Union of Public Employees: Submission to Innovation Science and Economic Development Canada for the consultation on the renewed Canadian AI strategy
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: CUPE's AI strategy submission demands worker-centred governance and regulations protecting against job loss algorithmic management and surveillance. The union advocates for public AI infrastructure over corporate subsidies mandatory workplace transparency and stronger employment insurance for displaced workers. CUPE criticizes the industry-heavy consultation process noting marginalized workers face disproportionate harms. Key recommendations: establish sectoral tables with unions and researchers invest in digital literacy training prohibit biometric surveillance require employer notification before using AI and enforce environmental standards. CUPE emphasizes workers need consultation rights and laws preventing discrimination.

items.title: Canada's First Responsible AI Literacy Initiative for Environmental Nonprofits
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Sustainability Network and Skills4Good AI launched Canada's first sector-specific Responsible AI Literacy Initiative for environmental nonprofits. The program empowers environmental leaders to use AI ethically as a force multiplier for climate action biodiversity protection and community engagement. It includes a free '7 Lessons in 7 Days' starter course (launching July 16 2025) and 15 sponsored Fast Track Memberships ($547 value) offering 3-month training with certification pathways. The initiative addresses the gap between corporate AI adoption and nonprofit capacity ensuring environmental organizations can leverage AI for grant applications data analysis advocacy campaigns while maintaining responsible practices.

items.title: OPEN LETTER to the Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation from civil society organizations and individuals opposing “National Sprint” consultation on AI strategy
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The open letter mentions labour impacts extensively documenting how AI exacerbates workplace inequality through exploitation of underpaid ghost workers algorithmic management systems that violate privacy and health rights discriminatory hiring tools invasive surveillance ('bossware') and wage theft via algorithmic discrimination. It criticizes automated welfare systems that harm vulnerable populations. While the letter doesn't specifically address 'AI literacy' it notes that students relying on LLMs show declining critical thinking skills. The letter emphasizes that workers bear AI's harms while industry dominates policy discussions arguing that marginalized communities most affected by AI lack representation in government consultations.

items.title: Gendered Disinformation: New Resources Launched to Address This Urgent Threat
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The Community Safety Knowledge Alliance (CSKA) is a non-profit applied research organization. Their initiative contributes to public policy processes in the role of an independent observer by generating research-based insights and documenting emerging risks associated with AI-facilitated misinformation and violence. Through its analytical work on gendered disinformation and its societal impacts they aim to provide evidence that can inform policymakers oversight bodies and advisory councils without being embedded within government structures.

items.title: CIFAR - RESPONSIBLE AI AND CHILDREN: INSIGHTS IMPLICATIONS AND BEST PRACTICES
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The report by CIFAR which is a Canadian-based global research organization (operating as a registered charitable organization) see https://www.unesco.org/ethics-ai/zh/civil-society-organizations/canadian-institute-advanced-research-cifar outlines best practices for AI specifically in regard to children advocating the need to protect their personal data and privacy (p. 12).

items.title: Exploring The Role Of African Civil Society In Decision-Making On Artificial Intelligence Risks Opportunities And Governance Gaps The Role Of Repongac In Ai Governance In Central Africa
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Repongac is concerned about the well-being of the region's citizens and is aware of the harmful effects AI can have on our societies. In addition to fighting for African civil society to play a role in decision-making for an inclusive equitable and responsible AI Repongac has several levers to strengthen its local capacity playing a key role in raising awareness among the population and creating a safer digital environment. It collaborates with schools universities local businesses and other civil society organisations to organise joint events share resources and create awareness campaigns produce and disseminate of educational contents volunteers to raise public awareness provide advice on AI and report incidents to authorities.

items.title: Exploring The Role Of African Civil Society In Decision-Making On Artificial Intelligence Risks Opportunities And Governance Gaps The Role Of Repongac In Ai Governance In Central Africa
items.justification: The article by REPONGAC examines risks that AI systems may reproduce or amplify existing discrimination particularly against women and marginalized groups. In the section “Risks related to AI in Central Africa” it highlights how algorithmic bias and unequal access to digital infrastructure can deepen gender inequalities and exclude ethnic minorities and rural populations from AI benefits. The document also stresses that limited access to technology and participation in AI governance may further marginalize women and other vulnerable groups advocating for more inclusive and equitable AI development.

items.title: Exploring The Role Of African Civil Society In Decision-Making On Artificial Intelligence Risks Opportunities And Governance Gaps The Role Of Repongac In Ai Governance In Central Africa
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Repongac has several levers to enable participation in decision-making on AI governance.- Capacity building- Promoting international cooperation - Creating coalitions - Collaborating with other actors - Conducting research - Promoting transparency and accountability- Public awareness and advocacy. They advocate for the integration of specialised educational programmes on emerging technologies in schools in partnership with local and international universities to prepare future generations and train experts in data science machine learning and AI ethics and successfully integrate this AI-dominated world. Encourage the creation of AI Centres of Excellence and Innovation for the development of solutions adapted to local contexts.

items.title: Legal Challenge to Google’s Cerrillos Data Center Environmental Approval
items.justification: This court ruling concerns a legal challenge to the environmental approval of Google’s Cerrillos Data Centre (~US$200M) initiated by a citizen group (MOSACAT) and the Municipality of Cerrillos (See https://web.archive.org/web/20260213210307/https://restofworld.org/2024/data-centers-environmental-issues/) and later continued by an individual claimant. The case questioned whether the environmental assessment adequately addressed water use air quality sustainability and the need for a full Environmental Impact Study. The ruling led Google to abandon the water-intensive design and relaunch the project with air-cooling significantly reducing its environmental impact.

items.title: TRAMAS - Geopolitics of the end of the world: rare earths in Penco Chile
items.justification: The TRAMAS case study on Penco in central Chile conducted by the Non-profit Instituto Latinoamericano de Terraformación addresses AI’s environmental impact by examining extractive industries linked to digital and AI technologies. The “Mineral” section explains how rare earth elements are key inputs for semiconductors and digital infrastructure that enable AI while outlining environmental risks such as impacts on water ecosystems and local communities. These issues are further framed in sections on territory environmental conflict and community resistance in Penco which situate mineral extraction within global supply chains driven by data centres and AI-intensive industries.

items.title: Datos Protegidos collaboration in capacity building
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: On behalf of Datos Protegidos Foundation and the Transdisciplinary Digital Convergence Regulation Nucleus Patricia Peña collaborated in three multi-stakeholder events on AI gender equality and human rights. Her work exemplifies collaborative capacity building: presenting the feminist chatbot Sof+IA—developed by Datos Protegidos and the Observatory of Gender Statistics and Diversity (ODEGI)—at the 'Back to School with Artificial Intelligence' teacher training initiative while her roles at the IACHR hearing (representing the Feminist AI Research Network) and Khipu 2025 demonstrate sustained collaboration to advance gender justice in AI governance.

items.title: NGO Amaranta's Fanzine on AI
items.justification: The initiative involved the publication of the fanzine “La inteligencia artificial no es tan artificial ni tan inteligente” by NGO Amaranta a Chilean organisation focused on addressing online gender-based violence digital rights and feminist education. The fanzine strengthens AI literacy by offering accessible explanations of how AI systems work and emphasising that they are human-made technologies that can reproduce social and gender biases. It explicitly links AI and gender-based violence showing how AI systems and digital platforms can reinforce discrimination harassment sexism ableism and unequal power relations in online environments.

items.title: CENIA´s LatamGPT and other language models
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: LatamGPT is a regional initiative led by the State funded CENIA in Chile that advances cultural and linguistic diversity in AI by developing a language model grounded in Latin America’s voices including Indigenous and local vernacular languages. Complementing this effort CENIA also leads the Rapa Nui Translator (https://www.traductorrapanui.cl/) created with the Academia de la Lengua Rapa Nui and UC which supports the preservation of the endangered Rapa Nui language through community-based AI tools. By countering the dominance of English-centric AI systems and fostering more inclusive and representative datasets and models LatamGPT contributes directly to the indicator on Cultural and Linguistic Diversity.

items.title: FIEL Foundation Workshop on AI and the World of Work
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: A workshop organised by Fundación Instituto de Estudios Laborales (FIEL) a non-profit created in 2005 by Chile’s main national trade union confederation the Central Unitaria de Trabajadores y Trabajadoras de Chile (CUT). It addressed labour protections through union-led adaptation to AI aiming to safeguard workers’ dignity and safety during digital transformation. It combines reskilling and upskilling efforts including analysis by CENIA on the impact of automation on occupations with a practical workshop on generative AI tools. AI literacy is further promoted through training union leaders on the challenges and opportunities of AI.

items.title: Advisory Committee against Disinformation
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The initiative developed with three civil society NGOs (Derechos Digitales Fundación Multitudes and Fundación Datos Protegidos) directly tackles AI-Facilitated Misinformation and Violence by recommending research and policies to counter threats like deepfakes particularly gendered disinformation (pp. 34-35). It addresses Data Protection and Privacy by urgently advocating for updated legislation and a supervisory agency to prevent the data exploitation that fuels disinformation campaigns (pp. 32). Furthermore it contributes to Safety and Security by proposing measures to protect critical infrastructure and coordinate institutional responses to disinformation threats during elections and public crises (example in p. 37).

items.title: AI Safety and Governance Forum at World AI Conference 2025
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: On July 27 2025 Concordia AI (a social enterprise based in Beijing) hosted a forum at the World AI Conference in Shanghai. The forum brought together a diverse group of experts to discuss AI safety and risk management. The forum includes the topic of 'transparency in technical disclosure and regulatory alignment [and] organization-level ethical governance mechanisms'. Discussions touched upon human oversight as well: they emphasized emergency shutdown systems hardware-enabled governance monitoring for deceptive behaviors and risk management frameworks (e.g. Frontier AI Risk Management Framework v1.0).

items.title: Frontier AI Risk Management Framework (v1.0)
items.justification: This is a report co-published by Concordia AI (social enterprise) and Shanghai AI lab (a state-affiliated AI lab) on AI risk. In the section on risk governance the report proposes 'Transparency and Social Oversight' as one way to govern AI risk. This includes model system card public oversight mechanisms third-party audits and supplementary liability mechanism (p.35) while Section 4.3 (p.26) addresses external communication of deployment decisions. The framework also introduces emergency control mechanisms (Section 6.4 p.35) red lines and deployment restrictions (Section 2) and lifecycle risk monitoring to ensure human oversight and prevent loss of control.

items.title: Responsible Innovation in AI x Life Science
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The report co-conducted with Concordia AI (social enterprise) promotes transparency through several recommendations :It suggests that researchers should be required to disclose the role of AI in their work and any potential biosecurity risks in research proposals and publications (6.4 p.80). It advocates for regular third-party audits of nucleic acid synthesis providers to enhance their risk controls (3.3.1 p.28). The report stresses that human oversight is crucial especially in the AI-Enabled Offense-Defense Landscape (6.3.2. p.79)

items.title: Cyber MulanAI Bean Plan
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The AI Bean Plan jointly initiated by the Zhejiang Ant Foundation (a philanthropic group established by Ant Group) and the China Women's Development Foundation addresses gender equality through digital employment focusing on the AI data annotation industry. The project empowers women in economically underdeveloped regions through a 'training-certification-incubation-order provision' model. By the end of 2024 the 'Cyber Mulan AI Bean Plan' had established 16 digital employment centers across various counties facilitating over 7500 local employment opportunities. Nearly 70% of participants were women achieving economic independence with average incomes significantly surpassing local per capita disposable incomes.

items.title: Disability-focused AI Knowledge Bases (First Batch)
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: Tencent (big tech) partners with four Beijing CSOs (New Life Elderly and Disability Service Center Love Decibel Public Welfare Foundation Fengtai District Sound Wave Disability Social Service Center Xinmeng Autism Care Center) to create AI knowledge bases for people with visual hearing physical and autistic disabilities. These knowledge bases are built on an LLM and provide scientific authoritative knowledge on topics relevant to individuals with disabilities based on authoritative sources (including national accessibility standards to make information more accessible to a wider audience. The initiative also produced four AI assistants: 'No Barrier Pass 1.0' 'Golden Blind Cane' 'Little Shell Bunny' and 'Da Fu'.

items.title: Ethical Standards Consensus for Artificial Intelligence Services to Minors
items.justification: The China Cybersecurity Association (a social organization) in coordination with research institutions internet companies and legal organizations released ethical standards for AI services to minors. The consensus addresses children's rights in AI through seven principles: health priority (assessing AI's psychological impact on youth) content assurance (screening for violent/inappropriate content) privacy protection (highest data security standards for minors) clear rules (risk awareness education) transparency (accepting supervision) collaborative governance (multi-stakeholder cooperation) and ethics-first development. This industry self-regulation initiative guides AI providers on product design content management and privacy.

items.title: Voluntary AI Safety Commitments
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The AIIA (AI industry alliance a non-profit government-sponsored industry body) drafted Voluntary AI Safety Commitments that major Chinese model developers (e.g. Baidu Alibaba) signed. These commitments pledge safety measures red teaming and data security across the AI lifecycle (commitments 1& 2 p.3). This demonstrates an industry association (a form of CSO/mediator) collaborating to set and enforce non-binding governance standards that influence regulatory expectations.

items.title: AI Safety and Governance Forum at World AI Conference 2025
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Concordia AI Safety and Governance Forum at WAIC 2025 is a high-level convening that addresses topics in AI safety. The initiative contributes to Data Protection and Privacy and Data Sharing and Access by featuring keynotes emphasizing the importance of trustworthy data sharing and privacy-preserving computation. It supports Access to Redress and Remedy by having experts recommend regulations for emergency shutdown mechanisms and defining 'red lines.' It contributes to Impact Assessments by discussing the need to mandate rigorous safety evaluations red-teaming and pre- and post-deployment monitoring. It tackled AI-facilitated misinformation with senior officials underscoring the urgency of governance over risks like 'deep fakes.'

items.title: Responsible Innovation in AI x Life Science
items.justification: The Report is co-authored by CSO Concordia AI. Data Protection and Privacy: identifying data compliance as an optimization area for government agencies and suggesting synthetic data for privacy (2.1.1 pp.17-18); Data Sharing: advocating for a international warning and detection system for bio incidents that involve sharing data (6.3.1 p.79); Access to Redress and Remedy: noting that a lack of complete operation logs and attribution mechanisms hinders accountability and tracing responsibility (3.1.3 p.27); Impact Assessments: the report itself is a comprehensive risk classification and ethical evaluation summary; AI-facilitated misinformation: p. 38 on 'Information Viruses' (misinfo on biosci) that interfere with scientific consensus.

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Girls Go Tech Programme: Empowering Girls in STEM
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Girls Go Tech Programme (GGT) launched by the Women Foundation aims to inspire and empower underserved secondary school girls in Hong Kong to pursue education and careers in STEM (Science Technology Engineering Mathematics) including AI. The programme provides self-directed courses corporate visits interschool events scholarships. The objectives of the programme are to offer new digital skills challenge gender stereotypes and inspire interest and confidence in STEM. The project is still ongoing during the project's study timeframe as per the project facebook page: https://www.facebook.com/girlsgotechtwf/

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Kids' AI Summit
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The summit aimed to provide a platform for children to participate in discussions related to AI. Around 100-200 primary and secondary school students were invited to express the opinions on various topics including AI and education AI and children's wellbeing AI and children's safety and security AI diversity and inclusion as well as AI and future career.

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: CUHK Jockey Club AI for the Future Project
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The project seeks to foster the development of AI education ecosystem through establishing the first junior secondary AI Curriculum in Hong Kong. It also organizes ranges of trainings workshops sharing sessions open classes etc to enhance teachers' knowledge and understanding in AI. The project is funded by The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust the Faculties of Engineering and Education of The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Media and Artificial Intelligence Literacy Research
items.justification: The research conducted by the Hong Kong Federation of Youth Groups (HKFYG) covers the media and AI literacy of youth. The survey found that 55.4% of the youth interviewed are concerned about personal data protection and privacy when using AI applications (p.1) where respondents shared concerns related to personal data leaks and the misuse of personal data (p.1). Additionally the survey finds that youths face increasing online risks as AI-generated images and texts can propagate false information (p.3) but they may not have the skills to discern the authenticity of information (p.1). The HKFYG is sponsored by the Community Chest and receives government funding but it is not part of the government.

items.title: Fiscal Watson: Study on the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Office of the Attorney General in Colombia - Karisma Foundation (2024)
items.justification: In its report on the Fiscal Watson tool of the Office of the Attorney General in Colombia the Karisma Foundation addresses equity and non-discrimination by warning that poor-quality data in the system for the oral accusatory criminal system can generate biased or erroneous results affecting the right to a fair trial (pp.14-15). It addresses transparency and explainability by criticising the opacity of Fiscal Watson the lack of public information about its operation and the contradictions in official responses (pp.18-20). Regarding human oversight and determination it emphasises that Watson should be a support tool whose results should be verified by prosecutors and not be definitive avoiding replacing human labour (p.16).

items.title: Digital environments for children and adolescents: what Bill 210 must not overlook - Karisma Foundation
items.justification: Karisma Foundation (2025 p.8) mentions in its comments and recommendations on the bill on safe digital environments that the “Comprehensive Monitoring and Evaluation System for the Protection of Children and Adolescents in Digital Environments” could include early detection technologies that use artificial intelligence or risk scoring systems. This could lead to mass surveillance preventive criminalization and discrimination especially toward children and adolescents who already face exclusion or stigmatization. The lack of algorithmic transparency informed consent and independent control mechanisms is highlighted which puts at risk rights such as privacy personal data protection and freedom of expression for children.

items.title: From the screen to public policy. Perspectives and challenges of cultural rights in digital environments in Colombia - Karisma Foundation (2025)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The report addresses among other things how artificial intelligence impacts cultural rights in digital environments. It analyzes the risks of algorithmic discrimination the invisibility of local cultural identities and the gender digital divide (Karisma Foundation 2025 pp. 24–25 and 45–46). It also proposes that Colombia participate in international debates on AI recommendation algorithms and platform regulation to ensure fair representation of diverse voices and protect cultural identity in the digital ecosystem (pp. 22–23 and 42–44).

items.title: Statement by the Karisma Foundation before the First Committee of the House of Representatives - Karisma Foundation (2023)
items.justification: Karisma Foundation (2023) addresses Labour Protections by warning that Colombia’s role in AI supply chains often involves precarious work like data labeling and content moderation and urges regulation of automated decision systems that affect working conditions (pp.4-5 and 7). It supports AI Literacy indirectly by calling for a broad multi-stakeholder process to design context-aware regulation and segment risks fostering informed debate and understanding of AI impacts (pp.7-8).

items.title: VIII NATIONAL CONGRESS OF THE CUT - United Workers' Union of Colombia (2024)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: During the 8th National Congress of the CUT (United Workers' Union of Colombia 2024) it was recognised that artificial intelligence and new technologies are profoundly transforming the world of work. The papers ‘Neoliberalism new technologies and the world of work’ (pp.25-27) ‘Decent work and just transition’ (pp.93-100) and ‘Working youth and trade union training’ (pp.147-152) recognised that these technologies can lead to job losses and labour flexibility with an increase in precariousness and loss of labour rights. They noted that automation and digital platforms displace workers affecting women and young people. They emphasised the need to ensure training and retraining so that workers can adapt to these changes.

items.title: How to live and survive as a journalist in Colombia - FLIP (2025)
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The FLIP (2025) report on the journalism sector addresses Labour Protections highlights precarious working conditions and recommends establishing ethical limits on the use of AI in order to protect jobs and editorial integrity (p.16). It addresses AI literacy and reveals that only 13% of journalists feel fully informed about AI calling for training in digital and AI skills (pp.10 and 16). Finally with regard to upskilling/reskilling it suggests promoting critical and strategic education on AI in order to adapt to digitalisation (p.16).

items.title: Statement by the Karisma Foundation before the First Committee of the House of Representatives - Karisma Foundation (2023)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Karisma Foundation (2023) addressed trust and safety by highlighting gaps in data protection (p.6) urging harmonization with privacy laws and copyright exceptions for data access (p.5) and warning about security risks from foreign AI systems (pp.4–5). Them statement supported impact assessments and algorithmic audits but questioned institutional capacity (p.6).

items.title: Ruling T-323 of 2024 - Constitutional Court of Colombia (2024)
items.justification: Ruling T-323 of 2024 addresses the use of generative AI in judicial proceedings and establishes guidelines for its ethical and responsible use emphasizing transparency accountability privacy non-substitution of human rationality risk prevention equality human control and ethical regulation (para. 423). Civil society including Fundación Karisma and El Veinte provided a critical analysis of the risks of bias hallucinations and lack of data updates in AI and recommended that the judiciary develop its own AI to ensure data protection and reduce risks (paras. 255 and 258). These contributions influenced the Court's recommendations and orders to guarantee fundamental rights especially due process in the use of AI in the judiciary.

items.title: Fiscal Watson: Study on the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Office of the Attorney General in Colombia - Karisma Foundation (2024)
items.justification: The report of Karisma Foundation (2024) analyzes Fiscal Watson’s use in the Office of the Attorney General in Colombia highlighting risks to privacy and data protection under Laws 1266 of 2008 and 1581 of 2012 (pp.5-7) issues of data sharing and sovereignty due to possible IBM cloud migration (pp.16–17) security measures like SPOA mirror copies (p.16). It also notes the absence of prior impact assessments and monitoring mechanisms (pp.23-24).

items.title: Women and Artificial Intelligence in the Congo
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: 'Women and Artificial Intelligence of Congo' (Fiac) is a network bringing together female entrepreneurs and students. It aims to train its members in artificial intelligence while establishing a mentoring system where each Fiac member mentors two to three students to pass on their expertise.The initiative addresses Gender Equality by increasing women’s participation and representation in artificial intelligence through targeted training mentorship networking and awareness-raising activities. FIAC empowers women and young girls to acquire AI skills access professional opportunities and engage in AI-related entrepreneurship and leadership thereby helping to reduce gender gaps in the digital and AI ecosystem in Congo-Brazzaville.

items.title: AI and youth empowerment by The Jeune Chambre Internationale (JCI-Congo)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Junior Chamber International Congo (JCI-Congo) organized a high-level webinar during which it encouraged young people to embrace Artificial Intelligence (AI) to empower themselves. The areas it mainly contributes to are: Reskilling / upskilling initiatives – by providing guidance and exposure to AI tools and skills relevant to employment and entrepreneurship. AI Literacy – by raising awareness and understanding of AI concepts among youth participants.

items.title: Public Algorithms Costa Rica
items.justification: The Citizen Center for Studies for an Open Society Association (ACCESA) created the Costa Rica Public Algorithm Repository to promote algorithmic transparency to help audit and monitor data information collected and the way in which it is processed and analyzed.

items.title: Impact of generative AI on Costa Rican jobs
items.justification: The Academia Centroamericana a Costa Rican independent think tank published a study in March 2025 examining the impact of generative AI on jobs in Costa Rica. The study finds that 19.2% of Costa Rican jobs are susceptible to enhancement by generative AI technologies with a disproportionate impact on highly skilled positions (53%). It identifies the sectors most exposed and those least affected such as agriculture and transportation. The study is explicitly directed at informing policymakers and business leaders on how to mitigate risks and maximise benefits for the workforce making it directly relevant to the labour and skills implications of AI.

items.title: AI Under the Spotlight: The Other Side of the Coin
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Privacy watchdog organization Politiscope organized an educational seminar for journalists and human rights defenders examining the societal impacts of artificial intelligence with particular emphasis on its implications for human rights and the right to non-discrimination. The event explored the often-overlooked harms of AI systems and how AI is shaping surveillance public services and policy making. It brought together several digital rights defenders who advocate and litigate to protect citizens from harms and discrimination inflicted by AI systems. The event concluded with a round table on the national implementation of the AI Act featuring digital rights activists and a representative of the Data Protection Authority.

items.title: Press release: 'Protecting children in online spaces is a shared responsibility of all those committed to the well-being of children'
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: On the occasion of the launch of the process for drafting the National Plan for the Development of Artificial Intelligence the civil society organization Pragma issued a press release calling for the introduction of new criminal offenses covering the creation possession and distribution of AI 'nudification' tools as well as the sharing or threatening to share explicit personal deepfake content. Pragma further demands that deepfake sexual abuse be formally recognized as a form of violence against children.

items.title: Media literacy workshop for journalism students
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Democracy watchdog organization Gong holds workshops on disinformation for journalism students as part of its long-standing Media Literacy programme. A workshop held in May 2024 also addressed several AI-specific topics. The workshop examined the impact of artificial intelligence on the journalistic profession but also the impact AI-generated disinformation such as deepfake videos images and audio recordings. The ability to distinguish authentic content from AI-generated material was highlighted as an essential journalistic skill. As part of the programme participating journalists took part in a quiz designed to strengthen their ability to recognize AI-generated photographs.

items.title: Interplay of GDPR and the AI Act
items.justification: The privacy watchdog organization Politiscope organized a panel discussion on 'The interplay of GDPR and the AI Act' as part of a regional Internet Governance Forum event (SEEDIG8). Representatives from the Office of the Ombudsperson Croatian Agency For Personal Data Protection and two Croatian unicorn companies Infobip and Rimac discussed key issues such as the legal basis for lawful personal data processing transparency requirements and data subject rights when personal data is processed by AI systems.

items.title: Promotion of regional cooperation and improving media standards
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The project “Encouraging Regional Cooperation and Improving Media Standards” implemented by the fact-checking organization Faktograf and funded by the National Endowment for Democracy (NED) aims to counter the misuse of new technologies that undermine democratic processes. Over a 15-month Faktograf monitors AI-generated content on online platforms. Faktograf produces investigative articles to help citizens better understand and recognise AI-generated disinformation.  The project also publishes in-depth analyses of the impact of artificial intelligence on society and democracy including its influence on elections labour and media integrity.

items.title: Advocacy for Democratic and Inclusive Governance of Information in the Democratic Republic of Congo by Kinshasa News Lab
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: It explicitly links AI-related harms to trust and safety issues in the information ecosystem in the Democratic Republic of Congo (RDC).
