It highlights algorithmic manipulation disinformation deepfakes and emerging risks to public trust in information noting that such AI-enabled distortions undermine social cohesion and institutional confidence. The initiative advocates for a policy framework on AI use in media that incorporates transparency ethics and responsibility as well as coordinated mechanisms to counter disinformation and protect journalists in digital contexts — all central elements of trust and safety governance for AI systems interacting with public information channels

items.title: 5th Global Forum @ Casa de Campo: The Future of Artificial Intelligence: Innovation Ethics and Global Challenges.
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: This forum developed by FONGLODE (a local NGO) promotes ethical and sustainable AI development prioritizing public interest and multi-stakeholder collaboration. Key principles include accountability for roles and responsibilities and transparency. The forum advocates for AI that is inclusive accessible well-governed and empowers individuals. The keynote speech connects ethical risk management with sustainability goals. Through open debate clear explanations of risks and choices and balanced regulation. The event aims to guide AI development towards fair outcomes stable institutions and lasting benefits for society particularly in the face of geopolitical competition and rapid innovation.

items.title: 5th Global Forum @ Casa de Campo: The Future of Artificial Intelligence: Innovation Ethics and Global Challenges.
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: At the 5th Global Forum Casa de Campo: The Future of Artificial Intelligence: Innovation Ethics and Global Challenges organized by Global Democracy and Development Foundation (FUNGLODE) a Dominican NGO the opening speaker urged an AI future that is inclusive sustainable and accessible governed through multi-stakeholder collaboration so it empowers people rather than excludes them. They framed inclusion as core to ethical AI called for participation from government industry academia and civil society and flagged risks such as bias and job displacement that demand balanced regulation and ongoing public dialogue across health education culture and industry.

items.title: Future of Hope
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The “Future of Hope” program created and led by Cincinnatus and Altice boosts AI literacy among underserved youth through free training. The program covers core AI concepts - critical thinking and practical coding culminating in certificates that validate participants’ new skills. By combining hands-on projects with problem-solving and collaboration it helps students understand apply and critically evaluate AI tools—essential literacies for both academic and professional paths. Delivered through a city–industry–NGO partnership the initiative expands equitable access to education beyond traditional schooling creates pathways to tech jobs and aligns with ENIA objectives such as curriculum-relevant skills and support for teachers.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Workshop
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The program's objective was to educate participants in practical AI tools that would allow them to enhance their professional careers and/or ventures as well as gain knowledge for better professional performance.

items.title: First Edition of the Egypt's AI Bill Roundtable Discussion
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: On January 14 2025 the Access to Knowledge for Development Center (A2K4D) hosted a high-level roundtable on Egypt’s draft AI Bill led by MP Sahar Al Bazar deputy chair of the Foreign Relations Committee. In collaboration with ADSERO Law Firm and APCO Worldwide the event brought together tech leaders multinational corporations entrepreneurs and academics to discuss balancing innovation with risk mitigation data governance and accountability in AI-driven decisions. The roundtable was the first in a series aiming to Charting Egypt’s Path to Responsible AI. The roundtable discussed the role of the bill in addressing the impact of AI on Fairness bias explainability human oversight and the environmental impact.

items.title: Free AI Training Program
items.justification: This program is brought by EiTESAL and Village Capital with support from Google and in partnership with MinnaLearn and the University of Helsinki. The training is composed of 4 chapters. Chapter 4 is about AI Implications. Examining the ethical social and business implications of AI implementation. Though which ethical components are tackled in the training is not clear since social implications are mentioned it contributes to fairness.

items.title: AI for People: An Event Co-organized with Kasr El-Dobara Evangelical Church (KDEC)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: On April 26th Kasr El-Dobara Evangelical Church (KDEC) organized an event exploring the risks and opportunities of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The event was part of an ongoing initiative by the church called “Khatwa”—a service launched to deliver educational sessions aimed at helping individuals make more informed decisions in various areas of life. The event was divided into two main sessions: an educational session and a practical workshop. The educational session was led by Marwa Soudi Consultant and Gender Specialist for the MENA Observatory on Responsible AI. Marwa provided an in-depth overview of AI—its definition and its potential risks including environmental impact bias issues of transparency and fairness.

items.title: An Approach to AI Governance: Essential Frameworks for Promoting Justice and Protecting Human Rights by (Masaar Technology and Law community)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Masaar platform publishes policy papers and recommendations on AI governance standards and sectoral/regulatory approaches for Egypt.“Masaar” has introduced several papers and reports on AI. In particular the Ai governance policy paper  explicitly 'addresses the foundational principles necessary for ethical AI governance. It delves into key areas such as non-discrimination fairness and inclusivity emphasizing the importance of designing AI systems that do not perpetuate bias or exclude marginalized communities. It highlights the role of data integrity transparency and accountability in fostering trust and mitigating harm. Additionally it examines the critical need for human oversight....and environmental responsibilities'

items.title: The Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World (OWSD)- Egypt Chapter has organized a workshop entitled 'Women in Science and Artificial Intelligence for Shaping the Future'
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: OWSD (Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World) Egypt Chapter held a “Women in Science and Artificial Intelligence” workshop (Nov 19 2024) an explicit civil-society event linking gender and AI inclusion. The initiative promotes gender equality by empowering women scientists and researchers to actively participate and lead in the rapidly evolving field of AI. Through workshops expert talks and networking opportunities led by female role models. Supported by institutions like UNESCO and the National Research Center it also integrates gender perspectives into scientific research and policymaking ensuring women’s voices are represented in shaping the future of AI.

items.title: Elements of AI for Business
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: EiTESAL in partnership with Village Capital supported by Google and in collaboration with MinnaLearn and the University of Helsinki launched a free one-month online course titled “Elements of AI for Business” in Egypt. The curriculum spans four chapters AI fundamentals machine learning neural networks and AI implications designed for entry-level employees fresh graduates and young professionals.  Learners gain practical digital skills real-world business applications of AI and globally recognized training at no cost.

items.title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence in Egypt: Proposed Standards and Principles by Masaar
items.justification: The policy paper issued by Masaar an Egyptian NGO working at the intersection of technology and law does not introduce sector-specific legal provisions. Rather it assesses the broader political legal and regulatory environment in Egypt in relation to artificial intelligence with a particular focus on safety security data protection misinformation and fundamental rights. The report analyzes existing laws and regulatory frameworks and proposes a set of general evaluation criteria that should guide future AI legislation and define the obligations of AI system providers especially for high-risk applications. These criteria are intended to assess how AI systems may impact safety security privacy and consumer interests.

items.title: Best practices for the regulation of artificial intelligence systems in El Salvador
items.justification: The report 'Best Practices for the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Systems in El Salvador' was prepared by the Salvadoran Foundation for Economic and Social Development in April 2025. It analyzes the legal and international frameworks for promoting AI in the region and presents recommendations for designing El Salvador's AI legal framework. On page 14 the document refers to the importance of incorporating principles as transparency and explainability Human Oversight and Determination. Fairness and Non Discrimination into the legal frameworks to be implemented in El Salvador drawing on best practices promoted by UNESCO.

items.title: Training Seminar:“AI and decision-making processes compliance with the rights of individuals
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The seminar tackles “insufficient transparency” in AI use and trains ombudspersons to understand AI fundamentals (functions types underlying logic) and EU rules—so they can demand and assess explanations documentation and evidence in administrative decisions. Its stated goal is to improve readiness to provide effective oversight of AI used by public authorities—scrutinising automatic administrative decisions for rights compliance and ensuring human-led review and redress within ombuds mandates.

items.title: Development and roll-out of AI teaching materials and teacher training 2025 Safer Internet Day campaign in Estonia
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The initiative is run by “Targalt internetis – Safer Internet Centre in Estonia” a multi-partner project coordinated by the Estonian Union for Child Welfare (NGO) together with the Education and Youth Board Tallinn University of Technology and the Estonian Social Insurance Board. Safer Internet Day 2025 (01.02–01.03.2025) was a nationwide awareness campaign on children’s digital literacy online safety and responsible use of AI and social media with school events webinars and materials on AI-related risks (misinformation design privacy).

items.title: Political demands of Estonian trade union confederation for the 2024 European Parliament elections
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The initiative is led by the Estonian Trade Union Confederation (EAKL) a national umbrella trade-union NGO representing workers. In the article EAKL hands over its political demands for the 2024 European Parliament elections to all parties and candidates. Among these are calls for a just digital transition regulation of AI based on a “human in control” principle and guaranteed access to lifelong learning for workers. Because EAKL uses these demands to shape parties’ programmes and future legislation this is coded as participation in public policy formulation.

items.title: Teachers explore possibilities of AI in teaching
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The article states that on 21 October Cooperation Chamber of Teachers' Associations in cooperation with the Estonian Informatics Teachers' Association organised a training for its members focused on the use of artificial intelligence (tehisintellekt / AI) in teaching. It is a formal workshop for working teachers helping them understand and use AI tools in their daily work – this is AI literacy and upskilling of the education workforce.

items.title: Safer Internet Day 2025
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Safer Internet Day 2025 initiative led by the Estonian Union for Child Welfare and partners invites parents teachers and children to jointly discuss safe internet and device use highlighting online risks and protection (dialogue focus). It connects this to AI by promoting webinars and materials on algorithms manipulation scams artificial intelligence and misinformation and by offering themed videos on scams misinformation cyberbullying sexual abuse and AI.

items.title: HaqCheck’s fact-checking training series
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: HaqCheck’s fact-checking training series (held across Ethiopia in Addis Ababa Dire Dawa and Arba Minch from 7 Mar–24 Apr 2024) hosted through the HaqCheck fact-checking initiative (in collaboration with Addis Ababa University and supported by the U.S. Embassy) trained journalists bloggers and other participants on digital/media literacy OSINT and verification techniques to spot and debunk AI-enabled misinformation including “deepfake/AI” manipulated audio-visual content. By strengthening early detection documentation fact-checking and public correction it helps reduce the spread of harmful narratives that can escalate tensions or trigger violence.

items.title: Legal Challenge Against the French Family Welfare Scoring Algorithm
items.justification: The legal challenge directly addresses Fairness and Non-discrimination by arguing the CNAF (Caisse Nationale des Allocations Familiales - National Family Allowance Fund) algorithm is 'discriminatory by design' targeting vulnerable groups like single mothers and disabled people equating poverty with suspicion. It addresses Transparency by demanding the algorithm's code and function be made public challenging its opacity. It also relates to Human Oversight by contesting a system that automates suspicion based on opaque scores potentially diminishing human judgment in deciding who gets investigated.

items.title: Objectif IA: Get Started with Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This free course addresses Environmental Impact in Part 2 Chapter 3 which discusses the energy consumption of data centers and the ecological footprint of training algorithms. It also targets Transparency and Explainability in Part 2 Chapter 2  which covers the challenges of explaining black-box models and ensuring safety. Fairness and Non-discrimination are also addressed in Part 2 Chapter 3 specifically through sections on detecting and reducing algorithmic bias. (Start date: https://web.archive.org/web/20260103160446/https://www.institutmontaigne.org/publications/objectif-ia)

items.title: Conference: Can AI be frugal?
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: This conference organized by the professional association NWX (Normandie Web Xperts) on Feb 15 2024 featured Thomas Solignac discussing 'frugal AI.' It aimed to raise awareness among approximately 100 attendees about AI's environmental impact including energy consumption and resource extraction. Discussions covered measuring impacts best practices (like AFNOR standards) regulation and low-tech AI directly engaging professionals on the Sustainability of AI.

items.title: At France Travail the rise of algorithmic control
items.justification: This investigative article by La Quadrature du Net published June 25 2024 reveals the use of opaque algorithms by France Travail to 'evaluate sort and classify' job seekers. It addresses Transparency by exposing these hidden systems. It tackles Human Oversight by detailing the 'dehumanization of social support' due to automation. It relates to Fairness by highlighting how these systems facilitate control and risk stigmatizing precarious individuals.

items.title: Labelia - Responsible and Trustworthy AI Certification
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: This initiative by the non-profit Labelia provides certification for 'Responsible and Trustworthy AI' described as the first of its kind in Europe. It includes a reference framework structured around 5 axes: Ethics & Societal Impact (addressing Fairness) Communication & Transparency (addressing Transparency) and Management & Governance (addressing Human Oversight). It offers an assessment platform and certification audit to help organizations demonstrate compliance and ethical practices.

items.title: Legal challenge against the CNAF's discriminatory welfare algorithm
items.justification: In October 2024 a coalition of 15 Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) led by La Quadrature du Net filed litigation before the Council of State against the CNAF (Caisse Nationale des Allocations Familiales - National Family Allowance Fund). The coalition which includes Amnesty International France challenges the CNAF's use of an algorithmic risk-scoring system to detect fraud. They argue the algorithm is discriminatory as it disproportionately targets vulnerable populations such as single mothers people with disabilities and low-income households by using socio-economic data as proxies for 'risk' (p. 1). This action addresses inclusion and diversity by seeking to protect marginalised groups from automated discrimination (p. 2).

items.title: DéClics Numériques: 20th edition focused on Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This initiative the 20th edition of 'DéClics Numériques' focused on AI  was organized by the CSO Diversidays. It addresses Cultural and Linguistic Diversity (in the broad sense of social inclusion) by promoting equal opportunities for underrepresented talents regardless of their social cultural or geographical origins to access training and jobs in the digital/AI sector. The program aims to facilitate professional retraining into AI-related careers for these diverse groups fostering a more inclusive workforce.

items.title: Participation in the LINGUATEC-IA project
items.justification: This initiative the LINGUATEC-IA project (January 1 2024 - December 31 2026) involves the CSO Lo Congrès permanent de la lenga occitana as a partner. It constitutes knowledge generation addressing Cultural and Linguistic Diversity. Its explicit goal is to advance the digitization of the POCTEFA territory languages (Aragonese Catalan Basque and Occitan) using Artificial Intelligence. The project develops AI knowledge and tools like neural language models machine translation and voice synthesis specifically tailored for these less-resourced languages thereby contributing to their digital presence and vitality.

items.title: Launch of a working group on the use of AI in child protection
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The Convention Nationale des Associations de Protection de l'Enfant (CNAPE - National Convention of Child Protection Associations) launched this working group to address AI's impact on child protection covering risks like profiling and cyber-pedocriminality. Its goals are to explore AI use cases support ethical practices respectful of children's rights and develop sector-specific recommendations for public authorities. This directly contributes to protecting the rights and fundamental needs of children in the age of AI.

items.title: Report of the Central Social and Economic Committee of July 24 2025: France Travail of the Future or the Generalisation of Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The General Confederation of Labour union within the Central Social and Economic Committee of the public agency France Travail evaluated the deployment of Artificial Intelligence tools (such as the virtual advisor NEO). The report identifies grave risks including psychosocial risks anxiety at work and loss of skills for agents. Citing an audit by the expert firm Degest the union challenges the administration's efficiency plan and explicitly demands the opening of negotiations to regulate Artificial Intelligence use to protect jobs and working conditions.

items.title: AI Initiation Workshops
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Simplon a social enterprise partnered with Meta and the Impact AI collective to launch 'AI Initiation Workshops' (Page 1). The initiative aimed to train 30000 French people in generative AI by the end of 2024 (Page 2). It specifically aimed to make digital skills accessible to all including those 'far from employment or undergoing professional retraining' (Page 2). The program includes half-day workshops in eight cities and an online MOOC to ensure broad access (Page 2) while raising awareness of ethical issues and responsible use (Page 3).

items.title: General Union of Engineers Executives and Technicians: Study Day - Artificial Intelligence: What Future for Skilled Work?
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The General Union of Engineers Executives and Technicians of the General Confederation of Labour organized a thematic study day titled 'Artificial Intelligence: What future for skilled work?' on April 26 2024 (Page 1). The event aimed to raise awareness about the impact of Artificial Intelligence on skilled jobs. The program included roundtables on topics such as 'Help my colleague is an algorithm?' and 'Trade union intelligence against the worst of Artificial Intelligence?' (Page 3) as well as a forward-looking exhibition by the Association for the Employment of Executives on the future of work (Page 3).

items.title: Charter 'Algorithms Artificial Intelligence and Recruitment'
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The association 'With Equal Skills' (À Compétence Égale) defined a charter for users of algorithmic systems in the context of identification evaluation or selection of job applicants (Page 13 source 965). The initiative aims to guarantee respect for the rights of job applicants and fight against discrimination in recruitment processes involving Artificial Intelligence (Page 13 source 964-965). This addresses Labour Protections by setting ethical standards for recruiters to prevent automated bias.

items.title: Generative AI Committee (Comité de l’intelligence artificielle générative)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: This advisory council (Sept 2023–Mar 2024) integrated civil society (e.g. CFDT Union researchers) into France's AI policy formulation. Its mandate was to define a national strategy for Generative AI to 'enlighten the Government's decisions.' The final report directly addresses Safety and Security by recommending adapted regulations to 'protect against abuses' (dérives) and Impact Assessments by evaluating the technology's consequences on labor markets culture and society. This demonstrates active CSO partnership with the state to shape governance. https://web.archive.org/web/20260115182647/https://www.info.gouv.fr/upload/media/content/0001/09/4d3cc456dd2f5b9d79ee75feea63b47f10d75158.pdf

items.title: Complaint against algorithmic video surveillance processing implemented by the police prefecture
items.justification: On July 31 2024 the CSO La Quadrature du Net filed a formal complaint with the CNIL against the Police Prefecture regarding the use of algorithmic video surveillance (VSA) for the 2024 Olympics. The initiative directly addresses Data Protection by alleging that the deployment violated the Data Protection Act (Loi Informatique et Libertés). It also addresses Access to Redress and Remedy by arguing that the late publication of authorization decrees (one day before implementation) hindered citizens' fundamental 'right to an effective remedy' (droit à un recours effectif).

items.title: Petition campaign: France must not become the champion of surveillance
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Amnesty International France launched this petition to oppose Algorithmic Video Surveillance (VSA) legalised for the 2024 Olympics. It addresses Data Protection and Privacy by criticising how VSA analyzes behavioral data in public spaces which threatens the right to anonymity. It also highlights Safety and Security implications warning that these 'exceptional' security measures risk normalising mass surveillance and discriminatory practices paving the way for facial recognition technologies that undermine civil liberties.

items.title: Operationalizing AI System Risk Management
items.justification: On July 19 2024 the non-profit association Hub France IA published a technical guide titled 'Operationalizing AI System Risk Management.' This deliverable addresses Safety and Security by providing organizations with a practical framework to map and mitigate risks associated with AI systems ensuring compliance with the upcoming EU AI Act. It specifically covers 'High-Risk AI Systems' and generative AI offering tools to evaluate technical and operational risks which directly contributes to the implementation of robust Impact Assessments in the French ecosystem.

items.title: Paris Charter on AI and Journalism
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) in partnership with 16 international CSOs launched the 'Paris Charter' in November 2023 to regulate the use of AI in media. The initiative directly addresses AI-facilitated Misinformation by establishing 10 ethical principles such as the requirement to clearly distinguish between human and AI-generated content and ensuring human oversight in editorial decisions. It serves as a 'best practice' guide for newsrooms to maintain the integrity of information and protect democratic deliberation from the risks of AI-driven disinformation.

items.title: Gambian Educators Trained on Artificial Intelligence in the Classroom
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Africa Missions Global's (AMG) Gambia chapter in partnership with the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education facilitated a training workshop for over 200 teachers administrators and principles focused on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education and preparing teachers for the future of education. The session included interactive presentations and real-life examples that helped demystify AI for educators who may have had little prior exposure. They also addressed ethical considerations in AI use and stressed the need for responsible integration in education systems.

items.title: Conference on the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on journalism
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Led by the Gambia Press Union (GPU) a journalists’ trade union and civil society organisation media professionals government officials and civil society leaders convened at the Bakadaji Hotel in Kololi to mark this year’s World Press Freedom Day. The day focused on the transformative yet perilous impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on journalism. Speakers discussed AI’s impact on journalism including job displacement and working conditions for media workers and raised public awareness of risks that automation and AI pose to media labour.

items.title: AI Week for women and girls to take place in Georgia
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The initiative aims to demolish the gender gap in technology and science by fostering a new generation of highly skilled women in the field. The goal of the project is to equip women and girls with the necessary skills to integrate contemporary technologies into everyday life. Fifteen female entrepreneurs will facilitate sessions for fifteen female students from grades 9-12. The project will be executed through a series of workshops and practical exercises over the mentioned span of five days.

items.title: AI and...  Series of Lectures
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This lecture series organised by the Georgian AI Association covers a range of topics from different fields and features discussions with experts on how AI can be integrated into their respective domains what impact it might have and related issues. The series is held on a recurring monthly basis and is open to the public. So this initiative addresses the topic of reskilling and upskilling

items.title: Advisory Board of the Digital Services Coordinator
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Advisory Board is a multi-stakeholder body composed of 16 representatives from academia private sector and civil society (e.g. AlgorithmWatch HateAid LOAD e.v. Federation of German Consumer Organisations etc.). The board advises the Digital Services Coordinator (DSC) on how to audit the recommender systems and content moderation algorithms of platforms to ensure they do not produce discriminatory outcomes or bias against specific groups. They specifically review compliance with Art. 34 of the Digital Services Act (DSA). The board facilitates Data Access Requests (Art. 40 DSA). DSC's also overlook 'trusted flaggers' -- independent experts detect and remove illegal content (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/dsa-dscs)

items.title: Let's Stop Nudification Apps Together!
items.justification: This initiative leverages the Digital Services Act (DSA) to combat systemic gender-based violence. Non-consensual AI-generated imagery ('nudification') disproportionately targets and harms women and girls reinforcing deep-seated social inequalities. By forcing platforms like X and Meta to mitigate these risks under Articles 34 and 35 AlgorithmWatch initiates lawsuits in the aim to eliminate a discriminatory 'safety gap' where gendered harassment is often less strictly moderated than other illegal content. Furthermore using Article 40 to demand data access aims to uncover algorithmic biases in how these harmful tools are promoted ensuring that marginalised groups receive equal protection from AI-facilitated abuse.

items.title: Within Bounds: Limiting AI's environmental impact: Joint statement from civil society for the AI Action Summit
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The joint statement led by the Green Screen Coalition a group coalition of funders and practitioners addresses AI’s environmental impact by demanding that computational infrastructure operates within 'planetary boundaries' (Intro). It warns that data centre electricity use may reach 1000 TWh by 2026 (Sec 1). To counter this the initiative calls for a fossil fuel phase-out and 100% renewable energy (Sec 1). Section II addresses resource exhaustion noting that data centers consume millions of liters of water daily. Finally Section 5 mandates tracking energy and water use across the AI lifecycle to ensure transparency and accountability moving beyond false 'climate solutions' to verifiable ecological limits.

items.title: Report Algorithmic Discrimination! (AlgorithmWatch)
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: This initiative led by the German CSO AlgorithmWatch directly addresses fairness and non-discrimination by creating a structured channel to identify and document cases of potential algorithmic discrimination. By inviting individuals to report suspected harms it helps uncover how algorithmic systems may produce unequal or biased outcomes in practice. The collected reports contribute to making discriminatory effects more visible and better understood thereby generating evidence on systemic fairness issues. This in turn supports AlgorithmWatch’s advocacy for stronger protections accountability and safeguards against discriminatory uses of AI reinforcing efforts to promote equitable and non-discriminatory AI.

items.title: Joint Statement: Upcoming Commission Guidelines on the AI Act Implementation: Human Rights and Justice Must Be at Their Heart
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: AlgorithmWatch (Germany-based CSO) contributes to this joint civil society statement advocating for ethical guidelines in their rights-based implementation of the EU AI Act. The document explicitly addresses fairness and non-discrimination by highlighting how AI systems (e.g. social scoring predictive policing biometric categorisation) can disproportionately harm marginalised groups including racialised communities migrants and persons with disabilities. It calls for broad interpretation of prohibited practices and safeguards against proxy discrimination (e.g. postcode data).

items.title: Hamburg Declaration on Responsible AI for the SDGs
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Concluded at the Hamburg Sustainability Conference 2025 this initiative involved CSOs working with the German government in drafting principles for 'equitable inclusive and sustainable' AI deployment. It specifically targets the integration of underrepresented languages and diverse cultural contexts into AI systems (p.2-3) and ensures the representation of individuals with disabilities (p.3) in AI ethics conferences. Signatories committed to promoting gender equality (p. 3-4) and inclusivity by ensuring that AI systems are developed through inclusive participation particularly from the Global South and marginalized communities (p. 3&5) and the underrepresentation of diverse cultural and linguistic groups in AI training data (p.4).

items.title: AI & Society Lab (Alexander von Humboldt Institute for Internet and Society (HIIG))
items.justification: The AI & Society Lab hosts workshop series on'Public Interest AI' (p.7). During the 2023–2025 period their work has directly addressed several key dimensions of inclusion. The Simba project (p. 12) is an open-source AI-powered tool that provides automated text simplification for those with disabilities and promotes inclusion of non-native German speakers. The Mapping of Public Interest AI pilot program (p.11-12) focused on linguistic diversity. The goal is to ensure models are trained in local languages to capture cultural nuances that English-only models miss. The 'Women* in Tech' project aims to strengthen the equal rights of women worldwide through networking and expertise as well as to create new opportunities (p. 6).

items.title: AI's Missing Link: The Gender Gap in the Talent Pool (Interface)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Interface published an extensive data-driven analysis of the gender gap within the global and European AI workforce. The research highlights that Germany lags significantly behind other EU nations (p.4 p.18 p.31) with women comprising only approximately 20% of AI professionals. The report argues that this homogeneity leads to AI systems that reflect and amplify societal biases (p.5). The goal of the report is to provide policymakers with the evidence needed to develop strategies for closing the gender gap emphasising that diversity is not just an equality issue but a prerequisite for 'developing AI systems that work equitably for all of society' (p.5).

items.title: Joint statement: Upcoming Commission Guidelines on the AI Act Implementation: Human Rights and Justice Must Be at Their Heart
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: AlgorithmWatch (Germany-based CSO) leads this civil society statement on the implementation of the EU AI Act advocating for ethical guidelines in their rights-based AI governance. The document explicitly addresses cultural and linguistic diversity and anti-racism by highlighting risks of AI systems reinforcing discrimination against racialised and migrant communities (e.g. social scoring predictive policing). It also covers gender equality and disability rights through its call to regulate biometric categorisation and proxy data that can infer sensitive attributes such as gender identity ethnicity or disability. By demanding broad interpretation of harms and stronger safeguards it advances inclusive AI principles

items.title: DGB (German Trade Union Confederation) position paper to the German Federal Goverment's Digital Affairs Committee on 'National leeway in implementation of European law on AI'
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The DGB (German Trade Union Confederation) was part of the public expert hearings of the German federal government's Committee on Digital Affairs (link in 'open observations'). The DGB also provided a formal written submission to the German federal government's Committee on Digital Affairs on how Germany should translate the EU AI Act into national law especially within the context of employment context – an area that the group claims the EU AI act deliberately leaves to the Member States (p. 1 para 5). The DGB paper cites Art. 2 Para. 11 of the AI Act as the primary legal gateway for national labor law (p.2) demands for a specialised employee data protection law (p.3) and demands to exclude Predictive Analytics in the workplace (p.3).

items.title: Free training for Berlin educators to learn how to open critical conversations about the impacts of AI & tech (Tactical Tech)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Tactical Tech is an international non-profit and hosted a workshop targeted specifically at Berlin-based educators. The open call page description states that the event will use a training-of-trainers format on AI misinformation and digital literacy ('What does partnership look like?') and offers funding for participants’ activities in local communities ('Goals of the training'). This initiative promotes AI literacy by equipping teachers to recognise AI-generated content explain risks and safeguards to pupils and cascade practical classroom resources.

items.title: Upcoming Commission Guidelines on the AI Act Implementation: Human Rights and Justice Must Be at Their Heart
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: AlgorithmWatch (Germany-based CSO) contributes to this joint civil society statement advocating for ethical guidelines in their rights-based implementation of the EU AI Act. The document explicitly addresses labour protections by noting AI use in employment contexts where social scoring practices are prevalent and should be prohibited

items.title: Digital Firewall (Chaos Computer Club)
items.justification: During the study period the German NGO Chaos Computer Club (CCC) actively served as an expert advisor and participated in parliamentary hearings and public consultations regarding the German Digital Violence Protection Act (Digitale-Gewalt-Schutz-Gesetz). On June 24 2024 the CCC provided formal testimony to the Committee on Internal Affairs regarding the amendment of the Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG) arguing against the legal expansion of biometric surveillance. On March 6 2025 CCC presented a 'Digital Firewall' position paper to policy-makers to ban biometric mass surveillance and automated profiling directly influencing the implementation of the EU AI Act in Germany and the data protection and privacy of German citizens.

items.title: Report Algorithmic Discrimination! (AlgorithmWatch)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The 'Report Algorithmic Discrimination!' project systematically documents suspected cases of AI bias in hiring and credit scoring to build strategic litigation. This challenges the 'black box' barrier that often prevents individuals from proving discrimination under the German General Equal Treatment Act (AGG). Furthermore it integrates with AlgorithmWatch’s Impact Assessment Tool  which provides a two-stage impact assessment procedure (Triage and Transparency Report) to help organisations identify ethically relevant risks before deployment. By exposing systematically biased 'proxy variables' the initiative holds proprietary algorithms accountable for discriminatory data assessments.

items.title: Impact Assessment Tool for Responsible AI (AlgorithmWatch)
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: AlgorithmWatch’s tool operationalises Impact Assessments through a two-stage process of Triage and Transparency Reporting. The Triage stage filters systems by risk level while the Transparency Report requires detailed documentation of goals performance metrics and accountability structures.

items.title: AI Learning for young people in Africa
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The AI Literacy initiative addresses the growing need for AI education as a core component of modern literacy. This program aims to equip children educators and communities with essential skills to navigate and thrive in an AI-driven world promoting a new era of digital inclusion and ethical AI use. Initial rollout is in select schools across GHANA Tanzania and Nigeria with plans for expansion to other African countries by 2026.

items.title: Eighth Quadrennial Delegates Conference of the Communication Workers Union Ho. Theme: 'The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Future of Work: The Role of the Union'
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The conference addressed the reskilling and upskilling indicator primarily at the agenda-setting and advocacy level.Conference discussions highlighted AI-driven automation as a risk to employment and emphasised the need for proactive worker reskilling and upskilling through education retraining and skills development. The conference framed skills transition as a shared responsibility of unions government and industry actors.While no specific reskilling programmes or training initiatives were announced the conference contributed to the reskilling and upskilling indicator by embedding workforce skills transition within union policy discourse and advocacy rather than through direct implementation and actionable measures.

items.title: Ghana Fact: Ghana's Independent Fact-checking platform
items.justification: Ghana Fact addresses AI-facilitated misinformation and violence by detecting verifying and debunking AI-generated false content such as deepfakes and manipulated media. As Ghana’s IFCN-verified fact-checking platform it counters the spread of harmful narratives that could incite hate or violence. Through media literacy campaigns and public education it strengthens citizens’ capacity to identify false information promoting safer digital spaces and reducing the societal risks of AI-driven misinformation. The evidence can be read as technical report as the link provided directs to a list of all the fact-checked cases many of them including AI deepfakes

items.title: Homo Digitalis's 4th Study on the AI ACT  - Comparative overview of the provisions on the rights of affected individuals
items.justification: The Homo Digitalis initiative '4th Study on the AI Act – Comparative overview of the provisions on the rights of affected individuals' scrutinises the right to explanation through a detailed legal comparison of Article 86 of the AI Act and Article 22 of the GDPR (p. 20–21). It analyses key legal terms and interpretive gaps and evaluates how both frameworks enable human oversight and redress. The study proposes concrete improvements: defining 'clear' and 'substantial' explanations specifying 'main elements' of decisions technical criteria and stronger supervisory mechanisms to detect bias and discrimination (p. 24).

items.title: Freedom of Information Request (FOIA) to the Greek Ministry of Education regarding the “OpenAI for Greece” Memorandum of Cooperation
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The initiative by Homo Digitalis is a legal request to the Ministry of Education regarding the 'OpenAI for Greece' program which addresses fairness transparency and human oversight by invoking Articles 4-8 of Law 4961/2022. It requests disclosure of impact assessments transparency obligations and safeguards for students’ rights in the use of AI systems in public education. Through legal advocacy it promotes accountability and compliance with human rights and data protection standards in AI deployment.

items.title: InfoLaw 2024 Conference - “Regulating Digital Innovation: Artificial Intelligence Cybersecurity and Platforms”
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The InfoLaw 2024 Conference examines the legal and social implications of AI cybersecurity and online platforms. Its first session on the AI Act discusses human oversight general purpose AI and fundamental rights impact assessments (FRIA) directly addressing transparency explainability and fairness. A workshop on “AI and Justice” further explores ethical and supervisory aspects of AI use in the legal field.

items.title: The Greek CSO Homo Digitalis participated in the AI Office’s public consultation on Prohibited Practices under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act.
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Homo Digitalis contribution to the EC consultation (Dec 2024) addresses gender equality children’s rights disability inclusion and cultural and linguistic diversity. It calls for stricter prohibitions under Article 5 of the AI Act against systems that reinforce stereotypes exploit vulnerabilities or discriminate against marginalised groups (p. 19 20 28). On p. 33 it explicitly supports a ban on emotion-recognition technologies arguing they are unreliable invasive and ignore cultural and contextual differences in emotional expression. It urges a broad ban covering proxies like “suspicious” or “untrustworthy” in contexts with power imbalances such as policing and migration.

items.title: Greek CSO SciFY’s Initiative on Disability Inclusion in AI  - “People with Disabilities (PWD) Pioneers in Artificial Intelligence”
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The SciFY “PwD Pioneers in AI” initiative promotes social inclusion and equal opportunities for persons with disabilities by integrating them into the AI development process. Through training programs participants with autism and mental health conditions learn to perform AI data annotation (text sound image) proving their ability to contribute meaningfully to AI innovation. The project challenges social and cultural stereotypes about disability and highlights how AI can serve as a tool for empowerment accessibility and inclusion rather than exclusion.

items.title: FRIA - Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment Guideline
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The FRIA template constitutes a test for a comprehensive legal compliance assessment of AI systems which is becoming necessary for many systems including those classified as high-risk before they are created or implemented in Greece. It addresses all selected areas by embedding equality accessibility and diversity checks into its framework. It includes sections for gender children disability and cultural or linguistic impacts (Part II pages 13-14 Part III pages 20-22).

items.title: GenAI Education Frontier - National Program for Educator Training in Generative Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The GenAI Education Frontier program by the Tipping Point (TTP) NGO enhances both reskilling and AI literacy by training over 1.000 educators across Greece especially in rural and island regions on the responsible and effective use of Generative AI tools in teaching. Through interactive workshops teachers gain practical digital and AI skills enabling them to integrate GenAI into curricula guide students in ethical AI use and act as local multipliers of digital transformation in their communities.

items.title: SciFY Academy event: “AI & Circular Economy”
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The “AI & Circular Economy” event by SciFY Academy promotes AI literacy and upskilling among SME professionals introducing them to the practical applications of Artificial Intelligence in sustainable business models. Experts from research NGOs and industry presented how AI tools can support the Circular Economy while participants learned about free EU-funded training programs (AI4GreenSME) to develop essential digital and green skills. The event empowers SMEs to adapt to the dual transition of AI and sustainability.

items.title: Creation of Greek Artificial Intelligence Network (GAIN) - Network for the Protection and Promotion of Human Rights Democracy and the Rule of Law during the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems in Greece
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The GAIN Declaration promotes the protection of fundamental rights in the development and use of AI systems explicitly referencing data protection consumer protection security and access to justice. It calls for a network of 17 founding organizations to ensure compliance with the Greek Constitution the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and the ECHR. It goes beyond legal compliance encouraging ethical responsibility and transparency in AI governance. The initiative is coordinated by Homo Digitalis with the support of the European Artificial Intelligence & Society Fund (EAISF) and is open to any interested organization.

items.title: Freedom of Information Request (FOIA) to the Greek Ministry of Education regarding the “OpenAI for Greece” Memorandum of Cooperation
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The initiative addresses data protection and privacy by requesting public access to the “OpenAI for Greece” Memorandum and accompanying documents to verify compliance with GDPR Law 4624/2019 and Law 4961/2022 (p. 4-5). It raises concerns over the legal basis for processing data categories collected from teachers and students storage duration and whether a Data Protection Impact Assessment was conducted ensuring transparency and accountability in the use of AI tools in education (p. 2-3).

items.title: Seminar: “Artificial Intelligence and the General Data Protection Regulation” - Hellenic Centre for European Constitutional Law
items.justification: The seminar trains legal professionals and data protection officers on how AI systems intersect with the GDPR’s core principles such as lawfulness purpose limitation data minimization accuracy transparency and accountability.

items.title: Researcher’s Night: Synthetic Content and Misinformation in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: It is a public event aimed at informing and raising awareness about misinformation and the use of artificial intelligence to address it. It functions primarily as an activity for knowledge dissemination and public engagement. The event was organized by the Centre for Research and Technology Hellas (CERTH) and the Media Analysis Verification and Retrieval group (MeVer) of the Information Technologies Institute (ITI). The MeVer group has extensive experience and expertise in the area of online disinformation with an emphasis on multimedia-mediated disinformation and has emerged as a result of research in several projects on social media mining information retrieval and multimodal Artificial Intelligence.

items.title: FRIA - Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment Guideline
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The FRIA Standard provides a structured method to assess AI impacts on fundamental rights under Art. 27 of the AI Act. It operationalizes privacy through “Privacy & data governance” checks - lawfulness user control security and governance/DPO measures (p. 23). It links FRIA to GDPR DPIA requiring FRIA to complement Art. 35 DPIAs (pp. 41 43). It embeds redress by referencing effective-remedy principles and requiring procedures to inform affected persons and complaint mechanisms (p. 11).

items.title: Fundación Terra + The Trust for the Americas (POETA DigiSpark AI Center)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Fundación Terra’s POETA DigiSpark and RDS-Honduras’ AI training for youth teachers and entrepreneurs focus on digital inclusion and AI literacy. Promotes adaptation of the workforce to technological change and bridges the AI-skills gap though it does not address collective labour rights.

items.title: “Use of AI for disinformation campaigns in Honduras”
items.justification: The initiative raises awareness about the ethical and societal risks of AI specifically its use to manipulate information ecosystems during political campaigns. It also seeks to inform and educate the public and promote accountability around AI-driven disinformation which directly affects the representation of marginalized voices and democratic discourse. It is part of a series of alerts and articles produced by C-Libre warning about AI-generated disinformation/deepfakes circulating in Honduras.

items.title: Operation Misinformation
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The investigative report “Digital Troops of Disinformation in Honduras” addresses AI-facilitated misinformation and violence by documenting and exposing the internal operation of state-linked networks. Based on interviews with current and former public employees the report analyzes how coordinated online structures use automated accounts bots and algorithmic manipulation to spread propaganda distort public debate and attack opponents on social media. While not a technical AI governance instrument it contributes to public understanding of how digital infrastructures—potentially including automated tools—facilitate misinformation and political harassment including gendered online violence.

items.title: Hungary’s new biometric surveillance laws violate the AI Act
items.justification: The Hungarian Civil Liberties Union’s legal analysis examines Hungary’s 2025 facial-recognition use. It addresses Transparency and Explainability by clarifying the operation and regulatory classification of the system. It explains in accessible terms how CCTV or protest footage is processed through automated facial comparison against a government database enabling rapid identification in infraction procedures. It also argues that the system should be treated as “real-time” remote biometric identification under the EU AI Act rather than a retrospective (“post”) system meaning stricter safeguards should apply. The post further highlights the transparency deficit of such surveillance noting that individuals may be identified without their knowledge.

items.title: Hungarian Helsinki Committee (HHC) – “Pécs Pride 2025: Q&A on AI Act & Facial Recognition”
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: THe Hungarian Helsinki Committee published an explainer on how Hungary’s planned use of facial recognition at Pride intersects with the EU AI Act informing LGBTQ+ communities and the wider public about their rights and risks tied to AI surveillance.

items.title: Legal analysis of Hungary’s biometric surveillance laws
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Társaság a Szabadságjogokért (Hungarian Civil Liberties Union HCLU) blog post is providing a legal analysis of Hungarian legislation related to AI-based biometric surveillance. The analysis examines how the law enables the identification and tracking of individuals in public spaces using biometric data such as facial recognition often without their knowledge or meaningful consent. It highlights risks related to unlawful data processing insufficient safeguards and disproportionate surveillance powers. By explaining these legal and rights-based implications in accessible language the blog post raises public awareness about privacy data protection and security risks linked to AI-driven biometric monitoring.

items.title: The Centre for Internet and Society’s comments and recommendations to the: Report on AI Governance Guidelines Development
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Centre for Internet and Society submission is a formal civil society response to the Government of India’s Report on AI Governance Guidelines Development. It addresses Human Oversight by emphasising human-in-the-loop systems and critiquing a post-facto AI incident database (Section II; IV.3 p.6). It advances Transparency through calls for an accessible incident database and third-party audits (IV.3–4 p.6) and supports Fairness by warning against exclusion and bias from poor data quality (II.A; III p.3–4).

items.title: Digital Citizen Summit Theme: Algorithm  AI  Accountability
items.justification: The 6th Digital Citizen Summit 2024 organised by CSO Digital Empowerment Foundation (DEF) and the Centre for Development Policy & Practice (CDPP) invited researchers to submit their papers reports about Algorithmic Bias and Discrimination to Ethical AI Development Data Privacy and Security Algorithms of Platform Companies & their impact on Gig Workers and AI Regulation & Implementation in an array of services. Pages 13 25 37 40 43 44 57 mention the fact that the event discussed environmental impact fairness and non-discrimination and transparency and explainability.

items.title: ParakhAI — An open-source framework for Participatory Algorithmic Auditing by CivicDataLab
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: ParakhAI developed by CivicDataLab advances Fairness Transparency and Human Oversight by providing an open-source participatory auditing framework for high-risk algorithmic decision-making systems. The framework supports public and private agencies in ensuring decisions are fair transparent and accountable. It enables active citizen involvement in design and deployment and includes participatory consultations and focus group discussions to identify and mitigate risks associated with high-risk AI systems.

items.title: Right to Information Request about FRS for public food distribution
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The Internet Freedom Foundation addresses Fairness Transparency and Human Oversight by filing an RTI on facial recognition use in the POSHAN Tracker. In “IFF’s Action” and “No FRS-specific order was shared” it highlights the absence of a clear legal mandate. Under “Data Protection Compliance” and related sections it notes missing DPIAs security audits and failure-handling SOPs warning of exclusion risks for mothers and children and demanding safeguards and alternative authentication mechanisms.

items.title: Internet Freedom Foundation's (IFF) response to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) Report 'AI Governance Guidelines Development'
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Page 9: argued against the Indian government’s proposal for a self-regulatory approach for artificial intelligence stating that such a model depends on internal accountability without any proper government oversight. As such it could exacerbate the risks posed by AI misuse such as bias. Page 12: IFF talks about the absence of a discussion on algorithmic accountability for gig workers adding that an absence of such accountability could lead to unfair treatment and job insecurity. Page 15: urged the government for a consultation in multiple languages.

items.title: Digital Empowerment foundation's Just AI initiative
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Page 63: The foundation has partnered with Dentsu India to teach rural women and youth digital skills. The project sets up 50 digital training centres in 10 Indian states giving people the tools and knowledge they need to succeed in today’s digital world. Each centre is led by a trained local woman SoochnaPreneur who teaches digital literacy soft skills storytelling and basic knowledge about Artificial Intelligence (AI)

items.title: Understanding the Implications of GenAI on Gender
items.justification: Page 14: Scope for gender specific challenges with Gen AI models Page 31: data fed into AI systems can lead to human rights risks the report found that Midjourney and Stable Diffusion contained thousands of child sexual abuse material images. Page 35: Scope for human rights and gender risks in dataset preparation. Page 39: lack of gender representation in data labour force

items.title: Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) submission on MeitY’s “AI Governance Guidelines Development”
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: On page 12 IFF talks about the absence of a discussion on algorithmic accountability for gig workers within IT Ministry’s report. It says that these workers depend on AI-based tools for job allocation payment and performance reviews adding that an absence of such accountability could lead to unfair treatment bias and job insecurity. The organisation has given specific examples of the impact of opaque algorithmics on gig workers which suggests its focus on inclusion in AI regulatory efforts. Page 18 mentions that a comprehensive consultation on AI governance should include grassroot workers.

items.title: Anudip Foundation AI Academy
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The website mentions that the AI Academy is a dedicated initiative focused on building future-ready digital skills with a strong emphasis on Artificial Intelligence particularly Generative AI (GenAI). It says that the foundation embeds AI in vocational training for job market alignment explaining that the program has had 6500 AI learners so far and equipped over 200 employees with AI.

items.title: Indian Federation of App-Based Transport Workers (IFAT) presented recommendations for algorithmic transparency in gig work
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: IFAT participated in a meeting with Secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment to discuss social security schemes for gig and platform workers. During this meeting it argued that the government should ensure that  algorithms that influence pay working hours task allocation and deactivation are fully transparent and accessible to workers. While the details of what was discussed are not publicly available IFAT spoke to a news publication linked above and mentioned algorithmic transparency as one of its demands explaining that workers should be able to understand algorithmic decisions. Its conversation with media suggests an effort to increase public awareness about AI related labor issues.

items.title: India Employment Report 2024- Institute for Human Development and International Labour Organisation (ILO)
items.justification: page 99: mentions lack of transparency in AI powered algorithmic decision-making processes and its impact on workers mentions blurring lines between employee and gig worker with the algorithmic management practices redefining the hiring monitoring evaluation and payment processes page 188 mentions disruption of outsourcing to India because of AI and opportunities that it may bring page 192 suggests need for production policies that take advantage of new technologies like AI

items.title: Digital Empowerment Foundation Just AI – Data & Algorithms for Communities
items.justification: Issued by Digital Empowerment Foundation Just AI – Data & Algorithms for Communities they focus on training. Page 2 Data Protection: Mentions efforts towards demystify AI help communities understand algorithmic systems and create awareness about the importance of data protection. Page 3 Misinformation: Mentions a project called SheCatalyst training rural women to become fact-checkers and combat misinformation including deepfakes.

items.title: The Centre for Internet and Society’s comments and recommendations to the: Report on AI Governance Guidelines Development
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Centre for Internet and Society initiative is a formal civil society submission providing comments and recommendations on the Government of India’s Report on AI Governance Guidelines Development (March 2025). It addresses Data Protection and Privacy by highlighting data quality concerns and privacy/security audits (Section II.B.3; IV.4). It supports Impact Assessments via pre-deployment risk assessment recommendations (IV.3) and advances Access to Redress and Remedy through calls for grievance redressal (IV.5).

items.title: Takshashila Institution- State of AI Governance Report 2024
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The report by Takshashila Institution cross-compares policies of India the EU US and China towards AI governance. Specific contributions are as follows: Data Protection and Pirvacy Page 8: points to societal wellbeing mentions the steps India has taken towards data protection. Safety and security: Page 10 mentions different companies' principles for mitigating AI risks. Consumer Protection/Access to redress: Page 8 mentions China's AI watermarking requirements and complaint redressal mechanisms. Also mentions that Chinese regulations mandate algorithm filing transparency security assessments and ethics reviews before AI deployment.

items.title: AI Ethics Circular seeks voluntary commitments from companies and stakeholders
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: ELSAM (Policy Research and Advocacy a human rights and civil society organization) in collaboration with the Ministry of Communication and Informatics (Kominfo) Bisnis Indonesia and Atma Jaya Institute of Public Policy organized the National AI Seminar aims to strengthen the commitment to implement the Minister of Communication and Information Technology Circular No. 9 of 2023 on Artificial Intelligence Ethics. The circular provides guidelines on ethical values that AI developers and users are to adhere to including principles of transparency environment humanity.

items.title: National Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) Position Paper for Indonesia’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Roadmap 2025
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Position Paper is intended to serve as the official strategic recommendation from the CSO Network to the National AI Roadmap Working Group under the Ministry of Digital Communications. This consolidation represents a strategic opportunity in the process leading up to the Public Consultation on the National AI Roadmap White Paper set for the final quarter of 2025 to ensure that the values of justice diversity and human rights protection are embedded in National AI policy from the earliest stages. This document maps the risks that AI could pose for women (Page 5) children (Page 6) and person with disability (page 5).

items.title: EngageMedia CSOs hold capacity-building sessions for AI governance in Indonesia
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The capacity building sessions presented risk of bias (gender) bleeding into the data set how data is identified or labelled by humans and even from historical and sociocultural assumptions and prejudice. These can then have a discriminatory impact on access to fundamental rights or public service.

items.title: The Role of Generative AI in Shaping Human Rights and Gender Equity: A Critical Analysis
items.justification: This research aims to explore the dual role of generative AI technology in supporting human rights activism and gender equality. The primary issue addressed is how AI can empower individuals and organizations in advocating for human rights while also posing risks such as the spread of misinformation and the perpetuation of bias. The conclusion emphasizes the importance of creating strategies that maximize the benefits of AI while minimizing its risks. Thus this research contributes to efforts to create an AI-driven future that not only supports human rights but also promotes gender equality and it encourages further discussions about the boundaries between humans and machines in the context of these rights (Page 9-14).

items.title: Realising AI’s Potential for Southeast Asia’s Workforce: Spotlight on Indonesia
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The event highlights the importance of inclusive skills-based approaches that align closely with civil society priorities particularly in reaching rural communities and marginalised groups often excluded from digital transformation. Through discussions on alternative education pathways such as micro-credentials bootcamps and online learning; the event reinforces the role that CSOs can play in community-level skills development lifelong learning and worker transitions in response to AI-driven labour market changes. The event creates space for civil society actors to advocate for equitable workforce policies support reskilling initiatives and ensure that AI adoption contributes to inclusive and just labour outcomes in Indonesia.

items.title: AI Ethics Circular seeks voluntary commitments from companies and stakeholders
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: ELSAM (Policy Research and Advocacy a human rights and civil society organization) in collaboration with the Ministry of Communication and Informatics Bisnis Indonesia and Atma Jaya Institute organized the National AI Seminar which aims to strengthen the commitment to implement the Minister of Communication and Information Technology Circular No. 9 of 2023 on AI Ethics. The circular provides guidelines on ethical values that AI developers and users are to adhere to including principles of data protection and security. This soft regulation is intended to serve as a guide or basis for future higher-level regulation potentially initiating the drafting of a ministerial regulation to formalize and enforce these ethical standards.

items.title: Submission to the Joint Committee on Artificial Intelligence Introduction to AI: Children and Young People
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: pg 7- Recommendation 1:All Ensure that all AI providers and deployers be required by law to ensure their systems are safe for children by design and default. They should take the views of children and young people into account and ensure that systems are transparent and accessible. Such systems should have effective child-friendly complaints and reporting systems in place.  pg 7. There must be a focus on transparency to ensure children and young people have access to adequate and accessible information so they can have a reasonable understanding of what the AI system does its impacts the measures taken to account for the capacities and needs of children and the efficacy of these measures.

items.title: AI Awareness Training (eLearning)
items.justification: Course Structure section: This AI Awareness training course is designed for volunteers staff and managers who use or intend to use AI-powered systems tools or applications in their work. some of the chapters of the course are linked to the EU AI ACT- Lesson 4: AI Regulatory Compliance: We explore the implications of the European Union AI Act 2024 and why regulatory compliance is necessary to safeguard the development of AI systems into the future.Lesson 5: Ethical AI Policy Development: In this topic we take a practical look at how managers might develop an Acceptable AI Usage Policy to help safeguard the deployment and use of AI systems tools and applications in the workplace.

items.title: Online Safety Monitor :Safeguarding Children's Rights Online
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: pg 7. No-3 Non-discrimination requires that all children regardless of their background or circumstances have equal access to opportunities and protections in the digital environment free from exclusion or bias.      pg 43- To support children’s freedom of thought the State must implement regulations that promote transparency in digital content algorithms and encourage platforms to provide a balanced range of information. These measures help safeguard children’s right to form and express their thoughts without undue influence from biased or manipulative digital content.

items.title: Postgraduate Diploma in Data Science In collaboration with the Data Science Institute
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: WaiLEARN Ireland includes a range of educational programs WaiCERT and WaiPRACTICE that support women in Ireland to build competence in Artificial Intelligence by providing access to Learning Practice and a Community for support. One of such projects is the-Postgraduate Diploma in Data Science In collaboration with the Data Science Institute

items.title: Meeting on the Ethics of AI Centre for Religion Human Valuesand International Relations
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Meeting on the Ethics of AICentre for Religion Human Valuesand International Relations 19th April 2024 pg 5 section v- AI should not reinforce inequality. Inequality refers to gender inequalities. Also pg 4- provides more insight to the meeting on 19th April where the aim was to produce a consensus-based document on the issue of AI not reinforcing gender inequality as a contribution to public debate. This document (the present document) was to be ready well in advance of the Brussels meeting on 20th November.

items.title: POLICING AND RACIAL DISCRIMINATION IN IRELAND:A Community and Rights Perspective
items.justification: page 8- recommendations to the government- no 2.
