Prohibit racial profiling in law including all forms of direct and indirect racial discrimination by Gardaí. no. 9 RECOMMENDATIONS TO AN GARDA SÍOCHÁNADevelop and deliver specific training on racial profiling that addresses unconscious bias. 9a) Cross-cultural communication and intercultural understanding;

items.title: Centre for Excellence in Universal Design
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The Centre for Excellence in Universal Design contributes to the development of ethical principles and best practices by analysing how AI systems should be designed and governed to ensure inclusion of persons with disabilities. The report identifies risks such as inaccessible system design and biased data that may reinforce exclusion and outlines the need for inclusive design approaches accessibility requirements and safeguards in AI deployment. By articulating how AI should account for disability inclusion across sectors the document provides normative guidance that functions as a set of principles and best practices for inclusive AI governance. (pp. 4 6 22 33).

items.title: Submission to the Irish Government on AI Act Implementation
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Irish Council for Civil Liberties (ICCL) participated in public policy formulation by submitting recommendations on Ireland’s implementation of the EU AI Act. The submission addresses labour protections by highlighting the role of sector-specific regulators including in the employment sector in overseeing AI systems that affect individuals’ working conditions and rights. It also addresses reskilling/upskilling by emphasising the need for technical expertise and calling for regulators and authorities to “upskill to assess the fundamental rights impacts of AI systems.” (pp. 224-226).

items.title: The Future of AI and Education
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: On September 23 2025 there was a conference exploring the future of AI and education across the post-primary and higher education sectors.Co-organised by the Royal Irish Academy the Insight Research Ireland Centre for Data Analytics and the Adapt Research Ireland Centre for AI-Driven Digital Content this conference will consider the future of AI and education in Ireland through the lens of enhancing literacy and exploring the adoption and integration of AI in teaching learning and assessment.

items.title: Accounting for Workers in the Age of AI
items.justification: The initiative led by the Financial Services Union (FSU) generates knowledge through a research report and survey examining the impact of artificial intelligence on workers in Ireland’s financial services sector. Based on a survey of over 600 workers the report analyses AI-driven job displacement workplace surveillance and changing labour conditions thereby addressing labour protections. It also identifies significant skills gaps and calls for employer and public investment in training directly addressing reskilling/upskilling initiatives. (pp. 19-22).

items.title: Roundtable Discussion: Harnessing AI in the Public Service in Ireland
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The University College Dublin(UCD) Geary Institute for Public Policy and Centre for Applied Data Analytics( CeADAR) roundtable highlighted that the challenges of implementing artificial intelligence in Ireland's public services pivot on establishing the security and safety of these systems.The third concern of the roundtable- challenges facing the responsible integration of AI into public services including cultural resistance are fundamentally linked to establishing system safety and security which demands meeting rigorous regulatory requirements and resolving critical questions of public trust and accountability.

items.title: The Irish Council for Civil Liberties (ICCL) v Microsoft (RTB Representative Action Ireland)
items.justification: The Irish Council for Civil Liberties (ICCL) led litigation by initiating a representative action against Microsoft before the Irish High Court (26 May 2025). The case challenges the use of real-time bidding (RTB) systems which rely on automated profiling and algorithmic decision-making to process personal data (e.g. IP address location browsing behaviour) and match users with targeted advertising in real time. It explicitly addresses data protection and privacy and data sharing and access as such data is allegedly broadcast to numerous third parties. Brought under Ireland’s Representative Actions Act it also supports consumer protection and constitutes access to redress and remedy through collective enforcement of digital rights.

items.title: IPPOSI launches Citizens’ Jury report on AI in Healthcare
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Citizens' Jury process was a crucial exercise in deliberative democracy that engaged citizens directly in formulating ethical policy regarding the most sensitive aspects of AI in healthcare: data protection and data sharing. Informed Deliberation on Data Ethics: The process convened 24 demographically representative citizens over 12 weeks for structured learning. They cross-examined expert witnesses with a focus on understanding the ethical issues inherent in AI's reliance on patient data. Citizen-Led Mandate for Data Governance: The final report represented a citizen-led verdict with 25 recommendations prioritizing data security transparency and interoperable digital infrastructure.

items.title: Accounting for Workers in the Age of AI
items.justification: Robustness and Cybersecurity (Page 12): The report states that systems deemed 'high risk' must comply with strict obligations before entering the market including demonstrating high levels of robustness cybersecurity and accuracy.

items.title: People Manage People Via Machines Research Project Survey Results
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: This is a research project held within the Israel Democracy Institute aimed at addressing the different challenges of using AI to govern and administrate. It includes inter alia research into the Public use of AI Transparency publications and public consultation. The project also includes workshops with the participation of government officials. See for example participation of the Head of the Privacy Authority https://shorturl.at/IY4bT (8/9/25) and post of the Head of Israel Digital Agency after participating in IDI Dec 1st event: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/shiralevami_%D7%94%D7%A9%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A2-%D7%94%D7%A9%D7%AA%D7%AA%D7%A4%D7%AA%D7%99-%D7%9B%D7%93%D7%95%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA-%D7%91%D7%9B%D7%A0%D7%A1-%D7%94%D7%97%D7%96%D7%99%D7

items.title: HCJ 4271/24 Ass'n for Civ. Rts. in Isr. v. Isr. Police (Isr. Sup. Ct. 2024)
items.justification: Fairness and non-discrimination are advanced through the critique of AI-based policing decisions that rely on opaque statistical correlations and biased datasets emphasizing the risk of profiling and unequal treatment and insisting that enforcement decisions must avoid discriminatory considerations and be based on rational individualized grounds (Sections C; E; Legal Argument – Violation of Equality). Transparency is promoted by highlighting the “black box” problem and arguing that decisions affecting liberty must be explainable reviewable and justified to both the individual and the courts as a condition for due process and accountability (Sections B; Legal Argument – Explainability and Accountability).

items.title: People Manage People Via Machines Research Project Survey Results
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: This project conducted a comprehensive survey 'People Manage People via Machines' investigating AI’s impact on human capital management. Findings were presented at the Israel Bar Association the Israeli Industrial Relations Research Association 2025 and the Privacy Protection Authority 2025 to raise awareness.The survey specifically addresses:Fairness: Identifies significant concerns regarding built-in bias in automated recruitment.Transparency: Highlights a lack of written policies for autonomous decision-making and insufficient employee training.Human Oversight: The report provides clear evidence of a 'unanimous agreement' across sectors that humans must retain the final word in AI-driven decisions to mitigate ethical risks.

items.title: People Manage People Via Machines Research Project Survey Results
items.justification: Fairness and Non-DiscriminationPage 31: 11% of lawyers reported encountering issues of 'employee or candidate discrimination' when advising clients.Page 32: 23% of lawyers identified 'fear of improper discrimination' as a legal challenge during the implementation of these technologies.Page 35: 30% of lawyers believe government regulation is specifically required for 'protection against discrimination'. Transparency and Explainability Page 19: Results show that most organizations (54%-71%) lack a written policy regarding 'decisions technologies can make independently' (explainability).Page 21: Covers transparency regarding data rights showing only 31-48% of organizations allow employees to view or correct collected data.

items.title: The Expert Forum for National Preparedness for Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: This Expert Forum established by the state of Israel - was also manned with leading members from the Civil Society. It contributes in all academic and ethical aspects for the development of AI and AI regulation in Israel.

items.title: Machines Managing People
items.justification: This initiative which houses a myriad of researches surveys and reports -  includes a specific reference to maintaining civil liberties - including gender equality inclusiveness and culture within the use of AI in the government services. For example a managerial tool for locating issues such as this: https://www.idi.org.il/articles/61529 and many other products.

items.title: Machines Managing People
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: This is a wide ranging initiative which encompasses all aspects of using AI to decide over human being. It include several researches including a book (Man-Machine-State) with chapters on biases and discrimination (chapter on biases for example at 175) on the use of AI in the workplace on surveillance. All with mentioning of the inclusivity and data of use in Israel.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Systems in the Workplace:A Comparative Perspective on Risks Opportunities Regulation and Social Partners
items.justification: The initiative protects workers by addressing discrimination surveillance privacy and weakened unions in Part A: Micro/Meso/Macro Risks and by recommending notification duties and privacy/anti-discrimination rules in Israel – Level Three. It supports reskilling through STEM and workforce training in South Korea U.S. and Israel – Level Four. AI literacy is promoted via guidance tools and training in Israel – Level Two and broader digital-literacy strategies in Nordic Countries Germany and South Korea.

items.title: National AI experts Forum
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: This expert forum advises the Ministry of Innovation and escorts the government during the AI regulation process including Trust and Safety.

items.title: Mass Surveillance and the Applicability of the Right to Privacy in the Occupied Territories: A Legal Opinion
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The legal opinion addresses Data Protection & Privacy Safety & Security and Access to Remedy by documenting invasive surveillance (“Surveillance Tools Used…”) analyzing the right to privacy under IHL and human rights law (“The Right to Privacy”; “1.1”; “2.1”) and showing how mass AI-driven monitoring violates dignity and ICCPR Art.17. It further explains the security harms created by biometric and digital surveillance (“The Violation of Human Rights”) and highlights the absence of oversight or avenues for redress within the dual legal system (“Israeli Law Applicable…”; “3.1”). This opinion was published online and included press coverage which increased public debate.

items.title: Preliminary Position Statement Regarding the Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the Work of Attorneys
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Data Protection and Privacy: The document mandates strict adherence to the Privacy Protection Law and attorney-client privilege. Attorneys are instructed to avoid inputting personal or confidential information into AI platforms to prevent data embedding and leakage.Safety and Security: It highlights security risks in both open and 'closed' systems noting that information can still leak. For internal tools firms must ensure vendors are contractually bound to confidentiality and data segregation.Consumer Protection: AI cannot replace professional judgment. Attorneys bear full liability for AI use and must verify all outputs to prevent misleading clients or courts. Explicit written consent from the client is required before using

items.title: LUMSA Foundation Summer School on Artificial intelligence ethics and human rights
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The LUMSA Human Academy Summer School is designed for university students postgraduates Ph.D. candidates professionals UN personnel and AI enthusiasts interested in exploring the intersection of AI ethics and human rights. It specifies that participants will engage with core values such as “non-discrimination transparency explainability meaningful human control”. It also highlights how issues like “algorithmic bias discrimination and inequalities in AI systems the tension between public safety and personal freedom” can be addressed.

items.title: The ethics of AI - Radio radicale symposium
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: At Italy’s Senate Radio Radicale symposium speakers from government media professions and academia framed AI as a powerful tool that must be guided not halted. Priorities outlined were: defend copyright and the sustainability of journalism; make AI-made content clearly recognizable; combat deepfakes and doppelgänger sites; and accelerate digital skills. Professionals stressed ethics-by-design human oversight and disclosure to clients when AI is used. Scholars warned of biased or opaque models global failures and energy costs. The key transparency levers mentioned were: labeling watermarking data governance auditability and public education.

items.title: Privacy Network report 2024/2025 - 'Automated administration'
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The OAA launched by Privacy Network in 2021 maps and studies algorithmic decision-making in Italy’s public administration. The 2024 Privacy Network report 2024/2025 on 'Automated administration' promotes transparency by documenting which systems are in use and requiring disclosure of objectives datasets and outputs (pp. 18–19) addresses fairness by highlighting risks of bias and discriminatory outcomes e.g. in welfare education and immigration systems (pp. 9–10; 46–47). Futhermore it calls calls for accountability impact assessments and public involvement in design (pp. 12–15; 21) ensuring citizens can contest and understand automated decisions that involve them.

items.title: For a Responsible AI – White Paper by Fondazione Bassetti
items.justification: The For a Responsible AI white paper (2024) outlines ethical rules and concepts for AI governance emphasizing justice by highlighting the potential of bias in automated choices particularly against underrepresented groups (pp. 19–23). Furthermore it encourages transparency by calling for explainable responsible AI and participatory government (pp. 24-27; 43-46) and stresses human oversight; discussing the how AI must adhere to democratic ideals rights such as habeas corpus and accountability frameworks (pp. 30–33; 48).

items.title: Participation of the Digital Human Rights Network in Italian Senate hearings on national AI legislation
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Digital Human Rights Network (Hermes Center Amnesty International Italia and other CSO) formally participated in Italian Senate hearings on the national AI law (DDL 1146) submitting a comprehensive memorandum addressing risks of algorithmic discrimination and exclusion including for persons with disabilities and marginalized groups. The memorandum recommends safeguards for digital rights and the establishment of an independent AI authority. (Memoria pages 1-14)

items.title: General Italian Labour Confederation (CGIL) Parliamentary hearing on the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and the world of work
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: In this parliamentary hearing before the XI Labour Committee CGIL provided expert testimony on AI’s impact on labour calling for protections and structured training to accompany technological change. The memorandum stresses the need to “take action on work organization production processes professionalism and training” to manage AI-driven transitions and avoid inequality. CGIL advocated for social dialogue skills development and regulation to ensure a just transition for workers in the age of AI.

items.title: NIdiL CGIL Filcams CGIL and Filt CGIL Palermo (trade union) appeal against Glovo Group
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Foodinho (Glovo) “excellence score” created indirect discrimination: riders who could not work evenings/weekends/holidays (e.g. due to care responsibilities disability age or religious reasons) received lower scores and therefore lost access to better job opportunities including the ability to book preferred work slots in advance. The Palermo Labour Court held the system “blind” to individual circumstances and ordered a remediation plan after consultation with the unions (NIdiL CGIL FILCAMS CGIL FILT CGIL).

items.title: Coding Girls - Hackathon “Rethink. Artificial intelligence & design thinking at the service of the territory”
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The initiative by Mondo Digitale Foundation a knowledge-oriented non profit organization aims to spread awareness of the opportunities offered by generative artificial intelligence and provide skills for its sustainable and inclusive use with a particular focus on women and southern Italy. The programme involved a total of over 600 students 19 schools and 15 young tutors including master's students doctoral students and PhD students from the Universities of Salerno and Cagliari.

items.title: Stati Generali dell’Innovazione – AI Conference on Work Regulation & Skills (Dec 2024)
items.justification: This national conference organized by Stati Generali dell’Innovazione on 7 December 2024 explored the implications of AI for society labour and future skills coinciding with adoption of the EU AI Act. Speakers analyzed regulation workplace impacts and the “new digital divide in the age of AI” addressing inequalities between workers and the need for awareness and adaptation in employment and education contexts.

items.title: 'Prospects on Risks Liabilities and Artificial Intelligence Empowering Robots at Workplace Level' - Brodolini Foundation Working paper
items.justification: This initiative directly advances the Labour and Skills area by examining risks and protections for workers interacting with AI-empowered robots. The paper by the Brodolini Foundation frames AI/robot systems as a “third element” in employment relations and analyzes workplace risks liability and safety duties under EU and U.S. regimes (Introduction; Sec. 1–4). It focuses on injury prevention insurance and mitigation (Sec. 3) questions adequacy of existing occupational safety systems and proposes a new “Robot Labor Law” to regulate IWRs and protect workers’ wellbeing (Sec. 5) - Link https://www.fondazionebrodolini.it/en/story

items.title: AI Governance and Consumer Protection - banking financial and insurance authorities - Consumers' Forum
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The 'Governance dell'AI e tutela degli consumatori' initiative of the Consumers' Forum. Italy's independent authorities (AGCM AGCOM Garante Privacy IVASS and Bank of Italy) convened under the title 'Il ruolo delle Autorità bancarie finanziarie e assicurative' (Rome April 2025) to evaluate the risks and protections associated with the use of AI in banking insurance and financial services. By emphasizing consumer rights openness and monitoring in algorithmic decision-making it improves consumer protection tackles privacy issues and encourages the safer application of AI in delicate economic areas.

items.title: When They See Us – Exhibition on AI and Biometric Surveillance
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The exhibition When They See Us (Bologna Sept. 2024) examined the ways in which biometric systems powered by AI track categorize and possibly discriminate against people. Interactive pieces such as Tactical Tech's visualizations revealing the collection and use of data and Dries Depoorter's facial recognition simulation installations were on display. It promoted critical public discourse on surveillance digital rights and the dangers of AI misuse in misinformation and security contexts. It was organized under Sineglossa's 'The Next Real' program (Sept. 2024–June 2025) and co-curated with The Good Lobby and Hermes Center.

items.title: IDMO (Italian Digital Media Observatory) – Monthly Report on AI-Generated Disinformation (April 2025 edition)
items.justification: The research published in April 2025 which was produced by Pagella Politica/Facta in collaboration with Bufale.net Open and other fact-checkers tracks how AI techniques increase the likelihood of false information. AI-generated misinformation in Italy quadrupled from the previous month to 11.6% of misleading reports according to the IDMO monthly report. Fake photos and videos of Pope Francis as well as misleading statements on the EU Ukraine and vaccines were among the subjects. The aim is to increase public awareness encourage fact-checking and fortify resistance against AI-driven manipulation by monitoring narratives and uncovering fake information.

items.title: WE-TALK
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The WE-Talk project a collaboration between WMW Jamaica Violence Prevention Alliance and Oxfam Canada used AI to analyze 245000 Google queries and 16000+ social media posts to gain insights into perceptions and attitudes on online gender-based violence (OGBV) in Jamaica. WMW Jamaica worked directly with Quilt AI to customise algorithms for Jamaica's cultural context including Jamaican Patois. Using these insights WE-Talk crafted targeted campaigns and workshops to tackle GBV root causes including the ongoing WE-Talk FACTSS awareness campaign (February 2024).

items.title: JCTU demands people-first policies as AI reshapes labour market
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Jamaica Confederation of Trade Unions (JCTU) has issued public statements calling for 'people-first' AI policies demanding worker consultation training and protections as AI and automation reshape the labour market. JCTU Vice President Shamir Brown speaking at the Planning Institute of Jamaica's labour market forum 'AI and Us: Navigating the New Human-Machine Partnership' (September 24 2025) stated that AI deployment must be guided by fairness equity and dignity and that workers must have a voice in how AI is introduced into their workspaces. The JCTU is calling for increased training programmes to help employees transition and remain competitive in the evolving workplace.

items.title: Initiatives for AI Ethics by JEITA Members Aiming to Promote Ethical Development and Use of AI
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Japan Electronics and Information Technology Industries Association (JEITA) a non-gov. industry association formed by merger of 2 associations (JEIDA and EIAJ) focuses on the realization of Society 5.0 and providing policy recommendations to the JP Gov. JEITA prepared a material on a network of initiatives for AI ethics being carried out by various JEITA members in a joint effort collaboration. Major private sector actors outlined in their respective document best practices of AI [pp.5-6] to reduce unwanted side-effects such as biases that might affect judgments of AI which could result in discrimination [p.2]. Many of the initiatives also emphasized the need for transparency [pp.4-5 9] in light of digital safety and accountability.

items.title: Press Conference by the Citizens' Association
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Citizens’ Association publicly raised concerns about Mitsui Fudosan’s plan to construct a 72-meter data center in Hino City. Mitsui Fudosan is a major Japanese real estate developer known for large-scale commercial/urban projects. The association held a press conference urging both the city to establish a formal consultation forum and require developers to adopt measures preventing harm to the environment and daily life. Citing unresolved concerns over groundwater local water resources shade electromagnetic waves electricity use and CO2 emissions the Citizens’ Association demanded detailed environmental disclosure to enforce environmental goals (such as reducing greenhouse gases) and ensure constructive transparent discussions.

items.title: Column: Growth of AI Will Not Negatively Impact Electricity Supply and Demand Even Help to Achieve 100% Renewable Energy
items.justification: The Renewable Energy Institute is a public interest incorporated foundation that conducts studies on electricity systems and renewable-energy policy. Their research column on AI and energy indicates that a potential rise in demand from increased AI use can be mitigated through wider adoption of renewables improved energy-management strategies and advances in semiconductor efficiency; measures that together reduce greenhouse-gas emissions and shrink AI’s environmental footprint. They also note that if a higher-demand era arrives due to AI sustainable progress of Japan will depend on supplying electricity at near-zero marginal generation cost so AI’s expansion might actually help accelerate Japan’s transition toward 100% renewable power.

items.title: B’AI Global Forum: Research on norms ethics and praxis for a truly gender equal society and a guarantee of rights for minorities in the AI age? (Beyond AI)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The B’AI Global Forum project is structured around four pillars. Pillar 1 focuses on supporting gender equality by working toward a gender-equal society researching AI-mediated discrimination and examining equality attitudes toward disabled people. Pillars 2 and 3 aim to design culturally diverse and inclusive media-expression spaces with AI and to create a global forum for collaboration. They explicitly emphasize under point 3 the creation of a global forum for collaboration between the humanities and sciences bringing together industry government academia and the private sector and fostering a broad network of research and practice across national boundaries by for example holding workshops.

items.title: International Women’s Day Special Event: Inclusion Through Innovation: Can AI Bridge the Gender Gap in Society? Hosted by The College Women’s Association of Japan (CWAJ)
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The College Women’s Association of Japan (CWAJ) invited leading researchers to discuss AI’s potential to hinder and to promote gender equality in Japanese society. The first talk on gendered innovations presented the failure of scientific research historically to serve women and minority groups. The second highlighted the potential of AI to identify and correct gender biases in hiring processes. The third discussed the broader implications of AI on social inequality noting how data biases could worsen disparities and proposing ways to make AI more inclusive and equitable for all. While the main focus was on Gender Equality the first and third talk were more broad and also touched on cultural diversity (minority groups social inequality).

items.title: National Awareness Survey on ''Generative AI and Human Rights Violations of Children'' (Child Fund Japan)
items.justification: Child Fund Japan surveyed public attitudes on how generative AI/deepfakes can potentially violate children’s rights (bullying/harassment child sexual abuse material (CSAM) privacy) and used the findings for advocacy of stronger legal protections (e.g. banning synthetic/“non-real” child sexual abuse material as well as real-child material see p. 6) plus education/self-protection measures for youth.

items.title: Recommendations for the Information and Technology Working Group of the Curriculum Planning Special Subcommittee of the Central Council for Education – Next Curriculum Guidelines
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The specified NPO (see: https://code.or.jp/news/2025) Minna no Code (Translation: Everyone’s Code) which promotes digital education for children released “Recommendations for the Curriculum Planning Special Subcommittee of the Central Council for Education - Next Curriculum Guidelines.” Drawing on research and school collaborations the proposal outlines how information education can foster creativity and technological literacy while ensuring compatibility with emerging technologies such as GenAI. It emphasizes positioning AI literacy in the curriculum [pp. 4-5] and calls for timely revisions of curriculum guidelines to respond flexibly to rapid technological advances contributing directly to Japan’s ongoing education policy discussions.

items.title: JMITU Statement on settlement of the case for unfair labor acts(misuse of artificial intelligence)
items.justification: In August 2024 the Japan Metal Manufacturing Information and Telecommunications Workers’ Union (JMITU) and IBM Japan reached a landmark settlement at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Labor Relations Commission concerning IBM’s use of its in-house AI system IBM Watson in salary assessments. JMITU had challenged IBM’s refusal to disclose how AI influenced wage decisions citing risks of bias and opacity. The agreement obliges IBM to reveal all AI-related factors explain their link to wage criteria and negotiate transparently on future concerns. This precedent enhances employee protection promoting transparency and accountability in the corporate use of AI for HR and pay evaluation.

items.title: Official launch of the 'Everyone Generates AI Course' that can be used in school classes (BETA)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Minna no Code who are a certified non-profit organization focused on digital education launched the Beta of the 'Everyone Generates AI' Course. The course targets elementary junior high and high schools across the country aiming at creating an environment where generated AI can be used safely and securely in schools and classes with practical teaching support (on-demand videos lesson examples teacher management). The course places the utmost importance on expanding students' free ideas through generative AI assuring that by allowing students to experience generated AI themselves under the appropriate guidance of a teacher they will be able to understand its characteristics including its advantages and disadvantages.

items.title: Code for Japan Summit 2024
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Code for Japan Summit is an event where speakers and participants can be inspired by keynotes learn about activity examples think through workshops and interact with each other. The event is organized by Code for Japan who are a non-profit group that brings together technologists civic activists and community members to build open-source tools support civic participation and promote digital inclusion across Japan. One of the sessions during the summit was specifically focused on the grassroots introduction of cutting-edge technologies such as metaverse generation AI in educational institutions.

items.title: AI Alignment Network - Webinar Series
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The AI Alignment Network's primary activity is to cultivate and support AI alignment research. In the face of a researcher shortage both domestically and abroad they strengthen the overall field by driving forward both education and research in the field. To this end they created a Webinar Series regularly inviting expert speakers. Many of the Webinars are focused on topics related to AI safety such as discussing Safeguards for AI (Webinar #11) and the field of general AI with safety guarantees (Webinar #3).

items.title: Progress in AI data utilization and required governance - Conference (MyData Japan)
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The conference hosted by the Japan Information Economy and Society Promotion Association tackled several topics regarding AI data utilization. Specifically the experts talked about safety management measures and security risks of AI (Section 1-2) the damage caused by AI hallucinations and false information output (Section 1-2)  privacy violations (Section 1-2) the importance of businesses responding to privacy issues and being accountable to consumers (Section 1-1) and AI governance and its relationship with privacy governance (Section 1-2).

items.title: Fact Check - White Paper
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Fact Check - White Paper  jointly created by the certified NPO Fact Check Initiative (FIJ) and Waseda University Next Generation Journalism and Media Research Institute (INGJM) addresses many of the false or misinformation incidents comprehensively describe the history current situation and challenges of fact-checking efforts in Japan. Among the discussed facts was also the case of generative AI being used to construct fake images of heavy rain disasters to gain attention on social media [p. 21]. The paper concluded that  due to the advent of generative AI it is expected that false and misinformation will be easily produced in large quantities in the future and further strengthening of fact-checking will be required [p. 100].

items.title: US-Japan NEXT Alliance Initiative - Allied on AI Assurance (Roundtable Dialogue)
items.justification: The US-Japan NEXT Alliance Initiative established by Sasakawa Peace Foundation USA with support from The Nippon Foundation is a forum for bilateral dialogue and joint policy recommendations. They held a roundtable dialogue to discuss matters of allied AI Assurance proposing best practices to move forward. They discussed and compared different approaches to AI safety [p. 6] and strategies for AI security [p. 8] but also the process of risk assessment arguing that we must anticipate future developments in the AI field and build a comprehensive understanding of its risks [p. 9] and also recommended AI assurance practices incident sharing initiatives and risk and vulnerability analysis sharing [p. 10].

items.title: Digital Shadows: The Threat of Online Violence Against Women in Jordan
items.justification: The Arab Renaissance for Democracy and Development (ARDD) published a 2024 blog and assessment project on Technology-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence (TFGBV) in Jordan analyzing how generative AI tools like deep-fakes intensify online harassment of women. Drawing on national data and testimonies ARDD links AI misuse to gender inequality urges stronger legal safeguards and localizes global TFGBV debates. The initiative advances gender equality promotes digital inclusion and raises awareness of AI-enabled gendered harms in Jordan’s digital sphere.

items.title: Phenix Center concludes training on empowering youth to work on cloud platforms.
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: In 2025 the Phenix Center for Economic Studies and Informatics a Jordanian non-profit CSO conducted a training program for 60 youth from Amman Zarqa and Balqa on essential AI and digital-work skills. Participants learned to use AI tools such as ChatGPT Copilot and Gemini and to apply them in freelancing content creation and cloud platforms like Mostaql. The program promoted AI literacy employability and digital inclusion supporting youth reskilling for the evolving labour market through practical ethical use of AI technologies.

items.title: Harnessing Technology and Artificial Intelligence: An Opportunity for Jordan to Boost Productivity
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Jordan Strategy Forum (JSF) a non-profit think tank published “Harnessing Technology and Artificial Intelligence: An Opportunity for Jordan to Boost Productivity” (March 2024) to enhance public and institutional awareness of AI’s role in national productivity. In pages 16 to 18 “Forum Recommendations” the JSF urges joint public–private–civil society efforts to launch a national awareness campaign and training workshops on AI concepts and ethical use targeting all age groups companies and public institutions. It further calls to integrate AI tools and ICT/STEM skills into education at all levels and to provide grants and specialized training to develop a skilled labor force as well as covering labor protection in Section 2 page 7

items.title: Advancing AI Governance and Security in Jordan
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Information Systems Audit and Control Association (ISACA) Amman Chapter hosted the seminar “Advancing AI Governance and Security in Jordan” on 13 February 2025 engaging 40–50 professionals in discussions on AI risk management cybersecurity and ISO 42001 (International Organization for Standardization) the international standard for AI management and governance. Through expert-led sessions by Société Générale de Surveillance (SGS) participants learned how to identify assess and mitigate AI-related risks align with ethical and security standards and strengthen compliance practices. The initiative promoted a culture of AI safety accountability and trust across Jordan’s digital ecosystem.

items.title: #SheInnovator – AI Training Program for Women and Girls (TechnoWomen)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: CSO TechnoWomen initiated and implemented the #SheInnovator program training over 1650 women across 10 regions in AI and digital transformation. The initiative directly advances Fairness and Non-Discrimination by increasing women’s participation in AI promoting gender-inclusive data practices and reducing algorithmic bias. TechnoWomen also joined the KazLLM Competence Center to develop a gender component in AI including bias detection discrimination audits and inclusive model design. '... representation of women in AI are critical to the development of inclusive and unbiased Technologies. Diversity in AI Teams leads to a wider range of perspectives and experiences which can help avoid bias in data algorithms and models (p. 3).'

items.title: The Digital Almaty 2025 Forum: Women in Tech Kazakhstan’s panel “Gender-Biased AI: Technologies for a New Era”
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The panes was organized by CSO Women in Tech Kazakhstan Chapter. This public session as part of Central Asia’s largest tech conference drew attention to systemic gender biases in AI and explored pathways toward inclusive innovation. It featured Kazakhstani and international experts highlighting issues like biased language models and the lack of women in AI while advocating solutions (from balanced datasets to institutionalizing inclusivity in upcoming AI laws). Such high-profile events in 2025 raised public awareness and spurred dialogue on ethical AI signaling strong civil society engagement.

items.title: The international forum - TECHNOWOMEN CENTRAL ASIA: AI FUTURE
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The forum is a CSO-initiated multi-stakeholder event organized by the Kazakhstani NGO TechnoWomen with support from the National Commission on Women’s Affairs ITU the Ministry of Digital Development Astana IT University and Astana Hub. TechnoWomen as the lead CSO designed and delivered the programme including AI masterclasses attended by around 300 women and showcased its IT-Ayel and TechGirls initiatives. The forum also highlighted CSO contributions through the TechnoWomen Leaders awards recognising groups such as the Kinergy Public Foundation and the National Association of Women Entrepreneurs ASMAR.

items.title: The Digital Almaty 2025 Forum: Women in Tech Kazakhstan’s panel “Gender-Biased AI: Technologies for a New Era”
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The panes was organized by CSO TechnoWomen. This public session as part of Central Asia’s largest tech conference drew attention to systemic gender biases in AI and explored pathways toward inclusive innovation. It featured Kazakhstani and international experts highlighting issues like biased language models and the lack of women in AI while advocating solutions (from balanced datasets to institutionalizing inclusivity in upcoming AI laws). Such high-profile events in 2025 raised public awareness and spurred dialogue on ethical AI signaling strong civil society engagement.

items.title: “AI for Her – Meet-up Pro” (Women in Tech Kazakhstan)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Women in Tech Kazakhstan a non-profit promoting women’s participation in STEM and AI organized the “AI for Her – Meet-up Pro” on 20 June 2025 as a follow-up event to the online course “AI Tools for Personal Effectiveness” launched earlier that month. The meet-up provided practical AI training through sessions on effective AI tools and creating landing pages using AI. It strengthens women’s employability by building hands-on AI skills digital competencies and professional networks.

items.title: Standard for the protection of workers’ rights in the Implementation of Artificial Intelligence in enterprises
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The Federation of Trade Unions of the Republic of Kazakhstan together with the Council of Trade Unions of Central Asian countries developed a Standard for the protection of workers’ rights in the implementation of AI in enterprises. The document sets out human-centred and socially just principles for workplace AI including prohibitions on algorithm-only dismissals (Section 4.1) requirements for transparency and explainability of AI decisions (Section 3.1–3.4) and mandatory social dialogue with worker representatives (Sections 1.6 2.1–2.4). It is intended as a practical model for legislation collective agreements and sectoral standards promoting retraining and decent work in AI-driven digitalisation (Sections 5.1–5.5 9.1).

items.title: FactCheck Dive Offline Training Series – MediaNet International Center for Journalism (2024–2025)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The project is implemented by MediaNet International Center for Journalism and including trainers from Factcheck.kz. The initiative strengthens resilience against AI-facilitated misinformation by training journalists students and educators to detect misinformation verify digital content and identify AI-generated text images and videos. Participants learned OSINT methods advanced search techniques and digital verification tools. The description explicitly notes sessions on “identifying AI-generated content” and fact-checking practices. The program builds national media literacy and resilience against AI-driven misinformation. The event date is given at https://web.archive.org/web/20250806083404/https://medianet.ngo/en/archives/5942

items.title: XV Central Asian Forum “Development of the Internet Sphere in Central Asia – InternetCA-2024”
items.justification: This event was organized by CSO - the International Center for Journalism MediaNet. The initiative contributes to Public Engagement & Awareness by convening journalists civil society researchers government officials and students to discuss digital rights and AI-related challenges. The forum addressed strategies to counter disinformation the impact of neural network services (AI) and approaches to regulating the internet while safeguarding rights. Sessions focused on balancing regulation with rights combating propaganda and understanding AI-driven trends in the internet sphere.

items.title: AIFC–Digital Rights Center Qazaqstan guidance on data protection & AI
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: In 2024 Digital Rights Center Qazaqstan in partnership with the Office of the Commissioner for Data Protection at the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC) co-developed and published a publicly accessible Guidance on Data Protection and the Use of Artificial Intelligence. The document gives practical recommendations to organisations on how to process personal data in AI systems including transparency security and accountability obligations and is explicitly intended as a tool to mitigate AI-related privacy and security risks in the financial sector and beyond. As co-author DRCQ contributed legal and civil-society expertise on privacy and digital rights.

items.title: Policy Brief - AI for Inclusive Development: Guiding Kenya's Policy Landscape
items.justification: This policy brief examines the challenges and solutions guiding Kenya’s policy landscape towards inclusive development and ethical AI integration for societal benefits.It provides key recommendations for forging Kenya's path towards responsible AI leadership. It recommends development of ethical AI principles for building trust in AI systems. These include among others fairness and transparency.

items.title: Media Guide on the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Kenya
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The Guide establishes that media houses and journalists must deploy AI tools while preserving human judgment and responsibility. Key ethical principles include transparency (identifying automated content) accountability (who is responsible when AI produces errors or bias) privacy and data protection (respecting personal data complying with laws like the Data Protection Act) fairness (avoiding discrimination or bias) and intellectual property rights. For sustainability it emphasizes investing in skills and capacity (talent-development) continuous performance measurement risk management and strategic implementation so media organisations can adapt and remain viable long-term.

items.title: AMNESTY INTERNATIONAL KENYA AND 5RIGHTS FOUNDATION COMMENTS THE DRAFT GUIDANCE NOTE FOR PROCESSING CHILDREN’S DATA
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: This is a Memorandum developed by Amnesty International Kenya during the public participation phase of the Draft Guidance for Processing Children's Data prepared by Kenya's Data Protection Authority (DPA). In this Memorandum Amnesty recommend that the DPA enhances the Guidance Note by clearly defining and regulating the commercial use of children’s data; strengthening provisions for children’s evolving capacities and direct participation in data rights; emphasising tech companies’ responsibility to protect children’s rights rather than relying on parental consent mechanisms; addressing the additional risks presented by AI systems; and explicitly integrating a broader human rights impact assessment framework that considers online harms.

items.title: Report: Generative AI and the Rights of Children in Kenya.
items.justification: This policy brief based on in-depth conversations with 15 children (ages 13–17) across Kenya reveals how GenAI is shaping young lives in ways that are both inspiring and alarming. It highlights the risks children experience daily which include;algorithmic bias cognitivie over-reliance privacy fears misinformation dangers and inequality. These Policy Brief provides actionable recommendations on child-centric policies for policy makers and tech companies.

items.title: Press Release by the Kenya Human Rights Commission: Why government must do more to protect dignity and human rights of digital platform workers
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: In its March 2024 press release “Taptengelei: Why Government Must Do More to Protect Dignity and Human Rights of Digital Platform Workers” the Kenya Human Rights Commission (KHRC) condemned poor working conditions in Kenya’s gig economy highlighting exploitation low pay and lack of social protection for platform workers. KHRC urged the government to regulate the sector ensure fair pay provide legal safeguards and uphold workers’ dignity and human rights within Kenya’s rapidly growing digital and platform-based labour markets. It addressed cases like Sama's subcontracting for AI labelling in Kenya

items.title: Judicial Review Application E119 of 2023
items.justification: In 2023 5 Kenyan CSOs - Katiba Institute Law Society of Kenya Kenya Human Rights Commission International Commission of Jurists-Kenya (ICJ Kenya) and the African Center for Open Governance were ex-parte applicants in a litigation that challenged World Coin Foundation's collection of Kenyans' data including biometric data through facial scans without prior consent on the basis that it breached provisions in the data privacy Act of 2019. Key breaches include consent transfer of personal data outside of Kenya collection of sensitive data data security. The case is particularly relevant to AI as it challenges data privacy issues in the context of biometric data and facial recognition system. The court ruled on the case in May 2025.

items.title: Next Gen Workforce – Open Call: Upskilling for the AI Era in Kosovo
items.justification: Women in Tech Kosovo – AI & Digital Skills Initiative: This CSO programme offers training mentorship and networking to increase women’s participation in tech and digital fields addressing gender gaps in AI-related skills. While the Facebook post does not clearly state a gender focus in the caption the organisation’s official website explicitly describes its mission to empower women through tech education and capacity building which relates to enabling women’s inclusion in the AI workforce.Official site: https://women-in-tech.org/ko/

items.title: Reshaping the Future: Women Driving Innovation in Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This research report led by the IPKO Foundation and supported by Open Data Kosovo generates evidence on women’s participation and leadership in AI and cybersecurity which is why it falls under knowledge generation. The report identifies gender gaps in digital and AI fields and highlights barriers women face in accessing skills and leadership roles (pp. 18–22). It also proposes policy and capacity-building measures to advance gender equality including training mentorship and inclusion strategies (pp. 21-22)

items.title: Gulf society issues in the age of artificial intelligence: opportunities challenges and development prospects conference
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Gulf and Arabian Peninsula Studies Center at Kuwait University in cooperation with the International Organization for Women's Empowerment host a conference related to AI challenges and opportunities . The 2nd panel talks about the rights of disabilities to reach AI with no discrimination and the challenges facing women to enter AI era and how to overcome those challenges. On the 3rd session they proposed the transition to Transition to Clean Energy in Hydrogen-Dependent Countries and how AI affects the environment (Qatar as an example who to use AI to reduce carbon emissions ). The 5th session talks about human oversight and that education shall give the people the tools needed to control AI.

items.title: Gulf society issues in the age of artificial intelligence: opportunities challenges and development prospects conference
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Kuwait University in Collaboration with the International Organization for Women Empowerment and Capacity Building (Tamkeen) and Abdullah Al-Salem University Organized the 51st International Conference Entitled 'Gulf Community Issues in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities Challenges and Prospects for Development.' there was 3 sessions related to women empowerment rights of persons with disabilities and children rights

items.title: Kuwait Lawyers Association in cooperation with the French Embassy in Kuwait held a conference on “Artificial Intelligence between Law and Technology: The Role of Lawyers in Artificial Intelligence and Data Protection.”
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The two days event is held to enhance lawyers skills; knowing the last innovations in AI lawyers industry and the impact of Ai in the industry. They agreed to establish a learning platform to enhance lawyers skills

items.title: The 51st International Conference entitled “Issues of Gulf Society in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities Challenges and Prospects for Development.”
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Gulf and Arabian Peninsula Studies Center at Kuwait University in cooperation with the International Organization for Women's Empowerment and Capacity Building (Tamkeen) and Abdullah Al-Salem University held the conference with multiple panel first panel talks about security and deepfake risks  all session talks about impact assessment over gulf region last day talk about consumer protection and data sharing and privacy from legal point of view and the conference conclude multiple recommendation related to AI and enhancing public awareness

items.title: Workshop on ‘Responsible use of data and formation of a global legal framework for Artificial Intelligence’
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Workshop was organized by the Journalists’ Public Association (a Kyrgyz CSO promoting media freedom and digital literacy see:  https://web.archive.org/save/https://journalist.kg/ru/about/) with support of UNESCO. It featured expert presentations on legal and ethical regulation of AI human rights protection and algorithmic accountability. A practical session demonstrated bias and variability in AI outputs underscoring the need for explainability and responsible human oversight.

items.title: Workshop on ‘Responsible use of data and formation of a global legal framework for Artificial Intelligence’
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The research by ISOC Kyrgyz Chapter and KG Labs Public Foundation promotes awareness on Fairness and Non-Discrimination by advocating open-source and publicly licensed AI models that ensure equal access and reduce algorithmic bias in government digital systems. It promotes awareness on Transparency and Explainability by requiring publication of AI data code and model documentation allowing external review and public understanding of AI decision-making. Human Oversight and Determination by recommending governance mechanisms and expert working groups to guide review and ethically monitor AI integration in public digital infrastructure. This initiative inform the public about responsible AI principles.

items.title: Sanarip Insan
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The “Sanarip Insan” project (launched in 2022 and ongoing see:https://web.archive.org/save/https://encouncil.org/2022/04/11/launch-of-the-sanarip-insan-project/) is implemented by the Internet Society Kyrgyzstan Chapter a CSO promoting digital inclusion. It advances children’s rights by improving youth access to digital education and safe online participation and promotes gender equality by empowering women and girls in rural areas through digital skills and mentorship. It builds awareness of AI tools and ethical digital practices fostering inclusive and responsible technology use aligned with human rights.

items.title: Turkic states AI summit
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Kyrgyz AI Community is a CSO in Kyrgyzstan that brings together researchers developers and practitioners working on AI. It organizes events conferences and trainings including mentioned initiative - participation in the Turkic States AI Summit 2024 where co-founder Timur Turatali presented on “Artificial Intelligence and National Languages: Preserving and Developing the Linguistic Heritage of the Turkic World.” The initiative explicitly connects AI with the promotion of linguistic and cultural diversity including supporting the development of Kyrgyz-language AI tools such as AkylAI.

items.title: Startup Competition “Sanarip Insan” - Empowering Youth and Young Women through Advanced Digital and AI Skills for Business Creation
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The “Sanarip Insan” Startup Project Competition enhanced AI literacy by empowering young people especially young women to apply advanced digital and AI skills in creating sustainable business projects. One of the four competition tracks explicitly focused on artificial intelligence encouraging participants to develop AI-based solutions. The initiative culminated in the final competition on 10 Nov 2023 where winning teams received sponsorship to develop their AI and digital projects. The initiative was organized by the Kyrgyz Chapter of the Internet Society (ISOC Kyrgyz Chapter) and the European Neighborhood Council with support from the European Union.

items.title: Trainings on Internet and Artificial Intelligence Governance for civil society
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The 2 day training on Internet and AI Governance conducted by Aziz Soltobaev founder of KGLabs Foundation. KGLabs Foundation organized this event in partnership with the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law to enhance participants’ AI literacy and helped participants upskill and reskill by providing them with practical knowledge and new competencies in AI governance ethics and policy-making.The event raised public visibility by informing participants about AI risks rights and responsibilities and fostering open societal dialogue on these issues. It equipped civil society representatives with knowledge of AI policy-making algorithmic bias transparency and responsible AI practices.

items.title: Responsible AI Governance Programme
items.justification: The Responsible AI Governance Programme by the Internet Society Kyrgyz Chapter (a Kyrgyz CSO) began in 2023 as indicated by its AI-related activities on its website (https://web.archive.org/save/https://isoc.kg/news/page/5/) and remains ongoing in 2025. It promotes ethical and transparent AI development through a rights-based approach. It addresses Safety and Security through regular monitoring auditing and oversight to ensure AI reliability and prevent harm. Impact Assessments by promoting continuous evaluation of AI systems’ societal and ethical implications throughout their lifecycle. The initiative delivers capacity building through training programs on AI deployment and AI-related laws for civil servants judiciary members CSOs etc.

items.title: Workshop on ‘Responsible use of data and formation of a global legal framework for Artificial Intelligence’
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The workshop featured expert presentations on legal and ethical regulation of AI human rights protection and algorithmic accountability. On data protection and privacy: During the workshop participants explicitly discussed the risks of unauthorised access to and leakage of official or confidential information when AI systems are used by government officials highlighting the need for legal safeguards and appropriate regulation. On Safety and security: speakers also addressed the use of AI for fraud and other illegal activities as well as associated national security risks and emphasised the need for state oversight and balanced regulation to protect the population.

items.title: AI Digital Public Goods: Securing Responsible Digital Public Infrastructure Development (Explainer)
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The “AI Digital Public Goods: Securing Responsible Digital Public Infrastructure Development” research by KG Labs Public Foundation and ISOC Kyrgyz Chapter (see the research published here as well:https://web.archive.org/save/https://isoc.kg/news/ai-digital-public-goods-securing-responsible-digital-public-infrastructure-development-explainer/) promotes trust transparency and accountability in AI systems through open ethical and safe Digital Public Goods (DPGs). It highlights data protection privacy and security in AI-enabled public infrastructure and supports responsible governance aligned with the Digital Public Goods Alliance’s updated qualification standards for AI systems.

items.title: 'Transforming Youth and Adult Learning and Education in the Era of Digitalization Algorithms and Artificial Intelligence' Green Action through Media Mass Organization and Civil Society in Laos (GAMCIL) Project Training (Specifically the training sessions on 'using artificial intelligence (AI) in news production' for journalists) and Lao CSO Platform Free Online Courses.
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Lao CSO Platform Courses: Offers foundational learning to the public via free courses like 'Introduction to Artificial Intelligence' and 'ChatGPT for Beginners' (Source 3.1 in Q5). These initiatives aim to democratize basic AI understanding and concepts. https://laocso.org/lo/capacity_building/introduction-to-artificial-intelligence/; https://laocso.org/lo/capacity_building/https-www-mygreatlearning-com-academy-learn-for-free-courses-chatgpt-for-beginners/

items.title: PANEL DISCUSSION “SUSTAINABILITY AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: SYNERGY OR CHALLENGE?”
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The discussion called 'sustainability and AI: synergy or challenge' discussed the synergy between sustainable development and artificial intelligence (AI) as well as the potential impact of AI on environment. The Discussion was organized by Latvian Information and communications technology association (LIKTA). Representatives from the Latvian Association of Artificial Intelligence the Ministry of Climate and Energy the Latvian Association of Artificial Intelligence the Techritory ecosystem the Institute of Electronics and Computer Science the Smart Administration and the Ministry of Regional Development participated in the discussion.

items.title: Conference “Revolutionary Solutions in Occupational Safety – the Role of Artificial Intelligence and Digitalization in the Workplace”.
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Latvian Confederation of Free Trade Unions (LBAS) organised a conference dedicated to the International Day for Safety and Health at Work “Revolutionary Solutions in Occupational Safety – the Role of Artificial Intelligence and Digitalization in the Workplace”.

items.title: Conference “Revolutionary Solutions in Occupational Safety – the Role of Artificial Intelligence and Digitalization in the Workplace”.
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Latvian Confederation of Free Trade Unions (LBAS) organised a conference dedicated to the International Day for Safety and Health at Work “Revolutionary Solutions in Occupational Safety – the Role of Artificial Intelligence and Digitalization in the Workplace”. It focused on the use of artificial intelligence and digitalization in improving working conditions. Among the topics discussed was the impact of artificial intelligence and digitalisation from the perspective of the European trade union movement.

items.title: Training course on the ethics issues of Artificial Intelligence organised by the Association “Baltic Media Excellence Center”
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The association 'Baltic Media Excellence Center' organised training courses on the ethical and legal issues of Artificial Intelligence as a part of the project activities 'Latvian Media Industry Competence Center'. For example on August 15 2025 it organised training on the use of AI in the creation and detection of disinformation on August 22 2025 - training seminar on the ethical and legal aspects of AI.

items.title: Maharat Foundation – AI and Digital Rights Capacity Building Program
items.justification: Maharat Foundation’s AI and Digital Rights program promotes Fairness and Non-Discrimination by training journalists and civil society actors to identify and counter bias in automated decision-making and online moderation systems. It also advances Transparency and Explainability by emphasizing algorithmic accountability media responsibility and open communication about how AI systems influence access to information. Through ongoing workshops and collaborations with SMEX and UNESCO the initiative builds capacity for ethical and transparent AI use in Lebanon.

items.title: Bread&Net 2024 – Regional Digital Rights and AI Ethics Forum
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Bread&Net 2024 organized by SMEX served as a major regional platform for digital rights and AI ethics discussions. It included panels on algorithmic accountability bias in automated systems and AI-driven misinformation. The initiative promoted fairness transparency and accountability in AI and digital governance engaging activists policymakers and researchers from across Lebanon and the MENA region through open public dialogue and awareness events.

items.title: SMEX – From Sharing to Silence: Assessing Social Media Suppression in the WANA Region (2024)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This SMEX research report examines how automated content moderation and platform algorithms disproportionately suppress voices from the WANA region including Lebanon. It analyses algorithmic bias lack of transparency in moderation systems and unequal redress mechanisms. By documenting these systemic issues the initiative promotes fairness and accountability in AI-driven moderation and advocates for transparent human-rights-based digital governance.

items.title: “Use of Artificial Intelligence Applications in Differentiated Education” training course – The Social Association (Lebanon)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This training course specifically focuses on using AI applications in differentiated education contexts (i.e. for educators adapting to diverse learner needs) thereby increasing AI literacy among teaching professionals and reskilling/upskilling them in the practical deployment of AI tools.

items.title: United Nations Lebanon & Maharat Foundation - Campaign for Information Integrity
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: This national social media campaign equipped journalists media professionals and the public with tools to navigate AI-driven misinformation digital manipulation and data privacy risks. The campaign incorporated 20 short videos on topics including AI’s role in news content fact-checking and media bias thereby fostering public resilience to AI-facilitated disinformation. (p. 3)

items.title: Professional Internship Program - Libya Technological Foundation
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Internship Program of the Libyan Technology Foundation is an intensive summer program targeting recent graduates and soon-to-graduate students in the fields of Information Technology and Communications. The program aims to develop technical skills enhance professional and personal competencies and bridge academic learning with the requirements of the Libyan job market. It provided structured internship/training pipeline with explicit AI training aimed at employability and workforce readiness. More information on the program: https://technology.ly/en/ngo_projects/internship-program/

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Safety Violations
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The objective of this article by the Internet Society of Libya (ISOC) NGO is to raise public awareness about digital safety and privacy risks arising from the use of artificial intelligence applications particularly AI-powered image and photo-processing tools. It explains how such AI systems collect process and potentially retain sensitive personal and biometric data highlighting the lack of user awareness and informed consent as a key safety concern. This directly relates to the Trust and Safety indicator specifically Data Protection and Privacy and Safety and Security by demonstrating a civil society effort to inform users about AI-related risks and promote safer more responsible interaction with AI technologies.

items.title: AI Governance Forum Lithuania – Working Groups on Regulation/Compliance & Ethics/Public Trust (2024–2025)
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The AI Governance Forum convened government academia industry and civil society in 2024–2025 to co-develop Lithuania’s approach to the EU AI Act.  Cultural & linguistic diversity: p.7 (Section 6 “Data & Ethics” point 3 – prioritising high-quality Lithuanian-language datasets for language model training). Gender equality: not explicitly addressed in this document; the closest inclusion-related reference is p.7 (Section 6 “Data & Ethics” point 1 – encouraging participation of vulnerable society groups to ensure inclusivity)

items.title: AI Governance Forum Lithuania – 3rd Meeting: “Ethics & Data in AI Governance”
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The 3rd AI Governance Forum meeting brought government academia industry and civil society together for a public-facing event on Ethics & Data. The insights emphasize fairness/non-discrimination inclusion of vulnerable groups transparency and human oversight-raising public awareness and informing debate on risks such as gender bias and language/cultural harms in AI systems (see key takeaways/insights).

items.title: Lithuanian Trade Union Confederation (LPSK) – awareness-raising on AI/algorithmic management at work and workers’ rights
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The LPSK initiative addresses Labour Protections by highlighting how AI/algorithmic management can affect workers’ rights and the need for safeguards and social dialogue. It also describes how can trade unions fight against algorithmic discrimination throughout collective agreements strategies.

items.title: Transparency International Lithuania – AI transparency study and proposal for an “AI transparency standard”
items.justification: The initiative contributes to Impact Assessments and Privacy by documenting how AI/algorithmic tools are used in Lithuania and highlighting risks (e.g. lack of transparency insufficient testing/validation bias and data-related concerns). It calls for an “AI transparency standard” and clearer disclosure/accountability practices which support ex-ante risk identification and more informed DPIA/impact assessment practices when AI is deployed in the public sector

items.title: AI Training Program for Marketers and ICT Professionals; MHub Malawi Training
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: ICTAM and the Institute of Marketing in Malawi co-hosted an AI training program in June 2025 in Blantyre targeting marketers and ICT professionals. The initiative directly addressed reskilling and upskilling by equipping the existing workforce with AI capabilities needed in the evolving digital economy. There is also another initiative (MhUb Malawi) [https://mhubmw.com/] which provides AI literacy training for kids and young people. Example training could be found here - https://www.tiktok.com/@mhubmalawi/video/7372574127380532485?lang=fr

items.title: Digital Rights Asia-Pacific Assembly (DRAPAC25) Kuala Lumpur Malaysia
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The tentative in the assembly championing gender equality through feminist dialogues on AI-enabled online violence protecting children’s rights via age-gating and digital-safety consultations highlighting indigenous data sovereignty to uphold cultural and linguistic diversity and ensuring representation of under-represented communities.

items.title: Novel AI technologies and the future of work in Malaysia
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The initiative is a policy brief drafted by the CSO ISI Malaysia. In the section 1. Labour Protections: The document analyses AI-related labour-market risks and explicitly proposes strengthening social protection mechanisms (e.g. unemployment insurance safety nets) to mitigate AI-driven job displacement (p26–28).  2. Reskilling / upskilling initiatives: The document recommends reforms to education training and lifelong-learning systems including skills training platforms and workforce upskilling pathways in response to AI exposure (p27–29). 3. AI Literacy: The document explicitly calls for mainstreaming AI education and establishing a national AI literacy framework including curriculum integration and educator training (p29–30)

items.title: KRYSS Network – “Horror in Digital Spaces: AI-Generated Pornographic Images as a Form of Online Gender-Based Violence (OGBV)”
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
