items.justification: The initiative raises public awareness on AI-enabled online gender-based violence (OGBV) by explaining how generative AI is used to create non-consensual sexual imagery and it is complemented by the OGBV Kit which provides practical guidance definitions risk recognition and response options for survivors advocates and the public thereby strengthening trust and safety literacy and harm prevention. (Website source; OGBV Kit referenced on KRYSS Network platform)

items.title: Justice for IPN comrades. Call for collective action after ruling in favor of Diego N.
items.justification: In December 2024 the 'Frente Nacional para la Sororidad Defensoras Digitales del Movimiento Ley Olimpia and the Asamblea Justicia' Digital IPN organised collective actions in response to a judge's acquittal of a student found with 166000 AI-generated images and 20000 videos produced for the sexual exploitation of female IPN students. The organisations publicly demanded judicial accountability ethical limits on AI-generated content and full application of the 'Ley Olimpia' — raising public debate on human oversight and the ethical use of AI in criminal contexts.

items.title: UNESCO-ANIA AI Readiness Assessment for Mexico (RAM Report)
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: In July 2024 ANIA co-developed with UNESCO the 'Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) Report for Mexico' presented at the Senate of the Republic. The report produced through 18 multi-stakeholder roundtables with over 250 participants provides a comprehensive diagnosis of Mexico's preparedness for ethical AI governance across legal sociocultural scientific and economic dimensions. It addresses AI ethics and sustainability directly: it identifies governance gaps recommends an AI ethics-centred national strategy and proposes institutional design for responsible AI development aligned with UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of AI.

items.title: Justice for IPN comrades. Call for collective action after ruling in favor of Diego N.
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: In December 2024 the 'Frente Nacional para la Sororidad Defensoras Digitales del Movimiento Ley Olimpia' and the 'Asamblea Justicia' Digital IPN organised collective actions in response to a judge's acquittal of a student found with 166000 AI-generated images and 20000 videos produced for the sexual exploitation of female IPN students. The organisations publicly denounced the ruling as enabling impunity for AI-facilitated gender-based violence and demanded victim-centred judicial accountability and full application of the 'Ley Olimpia' to AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery.

items.title: Proposed National AI Agenda for Mexico 2024-2030
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: In May 2024 ANIA published the 'Propuesta de Agenda Nacional de IA para México 2024–2030' in collaboration with UNESCO and over 40 civil society organisations. Section 3.4 recommends training on bias detection gender perspective and human rights for all actors involved in the AI lifecycle; promotes STEM inclusion for women indigenous communities and rural populations to address structural inequalities; and calls for safeguarding the rights of vulnerable groups including children in the development and use of AI systems in both public and private sectors.

items.title: Proposed National AI Agenda for Mexico 2024-2030
items.justification: Bullet 3.4 Gender Inclusion and social responsibility. Promote the full exercise of human rights in the development acquisition and use of AI systems in the public and private sectors through guides protocols training and technical assistance. In sense to identify and mitigate algorithmic discrimination by providing training on bias gender perspective and human rights to all those involved in the different stages of AI cycle from data generation to system use. STEM for women indigenous communities and people in rural and semi-urban environments; Safeguard the country's multicultural and linguistic diversity

items.title: “Real voices for a humane future”; march for AI regulation
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: In July 2025 Mexican voice actors and dubbing artists organised public demonstrations in Mexico City under the slogan 'Real Voices for a Humane Future' demanding legislative protection against AI-driven voice cloning and job displacement. Demonstrators called for recognition of the voice as sensitive biometric data fair compensation when voices are used to train AI systems protection of deceased artists' rights and the creation of a 'Dubbing Made in Mexico' identity. The initiative directly addresses labour protections for workers in sectors affected by generative AI.

items.title: Proposed National AI Agenda for Mexico 2024-2030
items.justification: In May 2024 ANIA published the 'Propuesta de Agenda Nacional de IA para México 2024–2030' in collaboration with UNESCO and over 40 civil society organisations. Section 3.2 addresses the Labour and Skills dimension directly: Objective 3.2.1 covers education digital skills development and workforce preparation for AI-driven labour market transformation; Objective 3.2.2 explicitly addresses AI literacy through educational goals and public awareness; and the document incorporates ethical considerations and protections for workers in AI employment contexts. The agenda provides concrete policy recommendations across all three Labour and Skills indicators: labour protections reskilling and upskilling and AI literacy.

items.title: Proposed National AI Agenda for Mexico 2024-2030
items.justification: In May 2024 ANIA a non-profit multi-stakeholder think tank published the 'Propuesta de Agenda Nacional de IA para México 2024–2030' in collaboration with UNESCO and over 40 civil society organisations. The document addresses multiple Trust and Safety indicators: it recommends mechanisms for reporting abuses and complaint resolution (p. 19 23) mandates ethical impact assessments (p. 11) proposes algorithm audits and performance evaluations (p. 18 21 25) promotes cybersecurity and data protection (p. 18 23) and recommends tools to detect AI-generated disinformation and synthetic content (p. 26).

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Olympiad
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Mongolian Artificial Intelligence Olympiad Association (NGO) was successfully organized National Artificial Intelligence Olympiad with the aim of promoting Artificial Intelligence (AI) education nationwide and supporting  in collaboration with the School of Information Technology and Electronics National University in May 2-262025. The event received significant support from government bodies including the Ministry of Education and Science the Ministry of Digital Development Innovation and Communication as well as notable private sector organizations such as Buren score LLC SmartLogic LLC and Rookie System LLC.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Warfare: Evolution of Protection or Threat to Ethics?
items.justification: The article was published by the CSO Women4Cyber Montenegro. It discusses AI in warfare through an ethical lens stressing that autonomous systems must not operate without meaningful human control and accountability. It calls for transparency in the development and deployment of AI weapons clear responsibility for decisions made by autonomous systems and adherence to humanitarian law and moral principles linking AI use to the need for human oversight and ethical governance.

items.title: Advantages and Risks of Using Artificial Intelligence in the Media Sector
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: This study was conducted by the NGO Media Council for Self-Regulation. It requires transparency in AI use including informing users about algorithmic recommendations and AI-assisted content (page 12). It mandates clear labelling of AI-generated content and disclosure to audiences (pages 33 38–39). Platforms must ensure explainability transparency and accountability of personalization systems (page 19).Considering  human oversight and determination AI implementation is defined as an editorial decision requiring designated human accountability (page 16). All AI-assisted content must undergo human review and approval (pages 17 and 38). Journalists and editors retain full responsibility for published content (page 38).

items.title: Manual for Reporting on Artificial Intelligence (Media Council for Self-Regulation Montenegro)
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The manual “Reporting on Artificial Intelligence” published by the CSO Media Council for Self-Regulation embeds fairness transparency and human oversight throughout. It requires attention to dignity privacy equality and justice (page 11) and establishes “Requirement #5 Diversity non-discrimination and fairness” (page 55). It defines explainability through transparency and traceability (page 55) and calls for verifiability (page 11). It also sets “Requirement #1 Human agency and oversight” (page 55) and stresses that humans must ensure fairness accountability and ethics (page 116).

items.title: Women4Cyber Montenegro Welcomes First Intern through the CybHER Programme
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Women4Cyber Montenegro is NGO was founded with the aim of raising awareness towards a gender inclusive cybersecurity community. The CybHER Programme is designed to empower women and girls through skills development mentorship and training in cybersecurity and AI-related domains. From September to December 2025 Teodora Kovacevic a final-year student of Information Technology will be working as their first intern. Teodora will join team and gain hands-on experience in the multifaceted field of cybersecurity. Through mentorship collaboration and exposure to real-world challenges she will have the opportunity to strengthen her professional skills expand her network and contribute directly to the mission.

items.title: Tinkering with Tech - UNICEF Digital Education Initiative in Montenegro
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The UNICEF “Tinkering with Tech” initiative led by UNICEF Montenegro aims to enhance children’s digital skills creativity problem-solving abilities and understanding of emerging technologies through hands-on play-based learning. The initiative introduces students and teachers in Montenegro to coding design thinking and responsible technology use promoting curiosity collaboration and innovation. From 2025 AI literacy was added further strengthening the initiative’s contribution to digital transformation in education and preparing young people for the digital future. (https://web.archive.org/web/20251104161840/https://www.unicef.org/digitaleducation/tinkering-with-tech).

items.title: Applying artificial intelligence in education is a (impossible) mission: A huge task for professors and the system
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The article “The application of artificial intelligence in education is an impossible mission a huge task for teachers and the system” presents views from experts on the use of artificial intelligence in education in Montenegro. Milutin Pavicevic CEO of the Montenegrin AI Association (MAIA) spoke about the importance and challenges of applying AI in teaching and the need to prepare teachers and the education system for these changes. MAIA is a Non-Governmental organization founded in September 2022 with an ambition to bring together the Montenegrin AI community.

items.title: International Conference 'Law and Security in the Digital World - The Impact of Artificial Intelligence'
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The international conference “Law and Security in the Digital World – The Impact of Artificial Intelligence” organized by the NGO Association of Security Managers and the Faculty of Law of the University of Montenegro focused on the impact of artificial intelligence on law and security. The working panels brought together experts and leaders from the fields of law and security who through five discussions addressed issues of international and national legislation on AI application whether AI is an ally or a threat in protecting critical infrastructure and topics of modern forensics the challenges of the digital age cyberspace and security in the era of digitalization.

items.title: Legal Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in Cybersecurity – with a focus on copyright protection
items.justification: The article “Legal Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in Cybersecurity with a Focus on Copyright Protection” published by the NGO Women4Cyber Montenegro analyzes the use of artificial intelligence in cybersecurity and the challenges that arise in this area. It points out that AI brings numerous advantages but also serious risks in cybersecurity stressing the importance of ethical and responsible application. Special attention is given to copyright protection and questions of authorship of AI-generated works as well as the need to clearly define responsibility and ownership. The article underlines the importance of aligning national legislation with EU legal standards and practices.

items.title: Countering Disinformation while Protecting Freedom of Expression
items.justification: Analytical report “Countering Disinformation while Protecting Freedom of Expression” by NGO Center for Democratic Transition (CDT) examines how emerging technologies including AI contribute to the creation and dissemination of false or manipulative content. AI-generated disinformation is discussed in Chapter I (pages 9–11). The need for transparent regulation institutional safeguards and media literacy is elaborated in Chapter II (pages 12–16). Further guidance and steps for strengthening national responses to digital and AI-driven disinformation are outlined in Chapter V (pages 24–27). Recommendations related to alignment with EU standards and public education on digital and AI-enabled disinformation are outlined in Chapter VI(page 28).

items.title: Montenegro facing a challenge – How to protect yourself from AI-generated false information?
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: Montenegro Media Institute’s article “Montenegro facing a challenge – How to protect yourself from AI-generated false information?” explains how AI misuse already happens in Montenegro gives local examples of manipulated interviews and fake ads defines deepfake and notes EU measures (Digital Services Act AI Act). It stresses media literacy education and training and the need for mechanisms to prevent the spread of false information highlighting risks to public trust and cybercrime reporting.

items.title: Trusted Artificial Intelligence: A Lever for Change in Favor of Accelerated Development in Morocco
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: AI Movement a non-profit participated in a reflection session hosted by the Royal Institute for Strategic Studies (IRES) a public entity. The reflection session was titled 'Trustworthy AI: A level of change in favor of accelerated development in Morocco and aimed to develop recommendations for a National Strategy (pp. 5-6). One of the key recommendations supports the establishment of AI steering committees in the public and private sectors overseeing the integration of among other principles ethics and transparency (p. 29).

items.title: Cloud Crypto and Smart Contracts: What legal framework and what opportunities for Morocco?
items.justification: AUSIM publishes a series of magazines and reports. This edition featured a discussion with the Minister of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform who emphasized the need for a governance model for AI. This model should ensure equitable and inclusive access while addressing disparities to prevent bias and exclusion. Additionally models and algorithms must be designed to be useful inclusive cost-effective and safe. Collaboration among international stakeholders is essential to align AI research with ethical principles and ensure that governance promotes fairness and transparency. The governance of AI should also prioritize sustainability ensuring that the training processes do not have a negative impact on the environment. (p. 47)

items.title: Adopting AI in your company: a strategic plan
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: AUSIM released the 'Adopting AI in your company: a strategic plan' in partnership with AI Crafters. The report highlights best practices for integrating AI into companies. One of the first steps in automation is integrating AI models into existing information systems ensuring their transparent implementation.p. 45 The report recommends using the AI Transformation Framework to automate their processes while maintaining human control over critical decisions p.78 The reports also emphasise the need to establish an ethics Committee exemplified by Microsoft's committee established to oversee the development and use of its AI solutions particularly to avoid bias in algorithms and ensure that AI is deployed in a fair and transparent manner p.104

items.title: High-level Forum on Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The High-level Forum on AI was organised by Movement AI with participation from ministries public administrations international organisations researchers and private actors. This forum aimed to launch capacity building for among others women and girls addressing the empowerment of women and children in the context of AI. Additionally the forum convened dialogues on the governance of AI on key themes that concern African communities. These discussions addressed the necessity of endorsing cultural diversity in the context of AI particularly for Africans. By inviting high-level government entities and parliamentary members to the forum AI Movement raised awareness among decision-makers and tried to influence their AI policies.

items.title: African Women In Tech and AI Program
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: AI Movement organised the second cohort of the African Women in Tech & AI summer camp in collaboration with the UNESCO Priority Africa. This initiative empowered African women entrepreneurs in the fields of technology and artificial intelligence aiming to boost their career paths. Throughout this training 80 women participants from 28 African countries engaged in a program designed to foster innovation leadership and collaboration. Projects' themes include: inclusion agriculture health and education; topics emerging for local needs. This initiative addresses therefore gender equality by empowering African Women in the context of AI in addressing local needs.

items.title: Women's Entrepreneurship and AI: Redrawing the Boundaries of Possibility
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: This conference was organised by the Association of Women Entrepreneurs of Morocco (AFEM) in partnership with the German Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Morocco (AHK). The Minister of Higher Education Scientific Research and Innovation emphasised the importance of 'helping women and supporting our youth so that they adopt a proactive approach oriented towards innovative sectors.' The conference aimed at inspiring women towards new horizons and exchanging on the theme of AI several reflections were shared notably on the dynamic interaction between AI and women its societal and personal impact the challenges and opportunities it presents as well as the gender bias it generates.

items.title: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The 2nd Edition of the AI Summer School was organised in September 2025. It is a five-day program jointly organised by MoroccoAI (a non-profit) in cooperation with the Soft Centre among other partners. This training equipped participants with cutting-edge AI knowledge and skills. It was targeted at Master's and PhD Students Post-Docs Young researchers (academic & industrial) Senior researchers (academic & industrial) and academic/industrial professionals making it an AI literacy upskilling and reskilling initiative.

items.title: Public Seminar: Youth and Women in the Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem in Mozambique
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The seminar organized by the organization Mozambique Inclusion (Inclusão Moçambique) focused on promoting the participation of young people and women in Mozambique’s AI ecosystem. It created a platform for dialogue on opportunities challenges and gender inclusion in emerging technologies while also highlighting the role of youth in shaping equitable digital futures.

items.title: International Fact-Checking Day: Combating disinformation is everyone’s responsibility!
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The initiative addresses AI-facilitated misinformation and violence by raising public awareness of how emerging technologies including artificial intelligence can be misused to spread false or manipulated content. It emphasizes that AI tools while capable of supporting verification are increasingly used to amplify disinformation particularly during elections and calls for collective responsibility to counter these risks.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Could Be a Threat to Mozambique’s History
items.justification: The initiative contributes to addressing AI-facilitated misinformation by highlighting the risk of AI generating false historical narratives about Mozambique which can mislead the public especially younger generations.

items.title: Myanmar’s repressive use of AI to counter “terrorism”
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The initiative addresses Safety and Security Impact Assessments by examining how military weaponises AI under the guise of counter-terrorism to target civilians conduct surveillance and enable arbitrary arrests and torture. Sections on the AI-powered dictatorship and AI’s impact on digital rights (pp. 4–27) function as risk assessments linking AI systems to violations of life liberty and privacy. It also tackles AI-facilitated misinformation and violence (pp. 28–44) analysing how algorithmic platforms like Meta and Telegram amplify hate doxing and propaganda that fuel offline attacks and ethnic persecution.

items.title: Risks of creative AI in Myanmar
items.justification: The report highlights key trust and safety risks related to AI actors particularly in the chapter on Heightened Due Diligence (p. 4). It notes that Myanmar’s experience shows technology companies often fail to conduct adequate due diligence before deploying new digital applications especially in the Global South. It stresses that given the significant risks posed by creative AI companies should consult independent experts to assess potential human rights harms. The Recommendations chapter (p. 5) calls for heightened due diligence in conflict zones in line with the UNGPs and urges stronger international norms including binding AI impact assessments victim remedies and UN monitoring mechanisms.

items.title: Computer Association of Nepal (CAN) recommends changes to National AI Policy 2025
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Computer Association of Nepal (CAN) in the recommendation appealed for  need for a robust legal framework and strong data protection policies to safeguard AI-related data and set clear guidelines on data management including aspects such as data cleansing safety and privacy. The organization also proposed the development of a dictionary containing definitions of technical terms such as AI machine learning and data privacy ensuring clarity for policymakers and stakeholders which can be an approach towards sustainability.

items.title: UNESCO's Unveiling the Intricacies of AI Governance in Nepal
items.justification: The multistakeholder dialogue co-organized with Digital Rights Nepal addressed AI governance through discussions on equality non-discrimination transparency and accessibility. Panels on “AI Governance and Legal Framework” and “AI Regulation in Nepal” examined regulatory needs ethical safeguards and inclusion of marginalized communities and persons with disabilities. The event also reinforced UNESCO’s 2021 Recommendation on the Ethics of AI promoting fairness and responsible AI development in Nepal.

items.title: A Case for Nepal's Al Diplomacy: Artificial Intelligence and Diplomacy
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Extract from Page 36 (Drive full document) reads 'Addressing Bias and Fairness that includes promoting policies for the development and use of fair and unbiased AI systems—that incorporates addressing data bias algorithmic bias and ensuring that AI systems do not perpetuate or exacerbate existing inequalities.' Extract from page 48 reads 'By participating in the development of international AI protocols concerning data sharing privacy and transparency Nepal can help ensure that emerging norms are equitable and consider the interests of smaller nations'

items.title: Computer Association of Nepal (CAN) recommends changes to National AI Policy 2025
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The initiative contributes to Cultural and Linguistic Diversity by recommending that AI technologies be tailored to Nepal’s linguistic context. The concept paper calls for AI systems focused on Nepali and regional language models promoting inclusion of speakers of diverse local languages. By advocating AI solutions adapted to Nepal’s multilingual society the initiative seeks to reduce exclusion of non-English-speaking populations and ensure equitable access to AI benefits

items.title: Women In Data
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The panel discussion focused on the historical underrepresentation of women in STEM fields and how the growing popularity of Artificial intelligence exacerbates the issue. The discussions also spotlighted the intersectionality in fostering inclusion for women in the field.

items.title: Nepal National Summit on Artificial Intelligence 2024
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Summit Report: Nepal National Summit on Artificial Intelligence 2024 addresses Gender Equality and Cultural and Linguistic Diversity by explicitly tackling AI bias and inclusivity. On p.16 Ms. Aakriti Kharel stressed prioritizing women in science and computer education and embedding human rights in AI policy. On p.18 (Section 3: Bias and Inclusivity) the report calls for addressing AI bias promoting women’s inclusion and enhancing accessibility in public services including language recognition in government offices.

items.title: Safeguarding Futures: Exploring the Impacts of Generative AI onChild Online Protection in Nepal
items.justification: Safeguarding Futures: Exploring the Impacts of Generative AI on Child Online Protection in Nepal (ChildSafeNet Sept 2024) addresses Children’s Rights by analysing how Generative AI affects child safety online. Chapter 4 (pp.27–33) details risks such as cyberbullying CSAM/OCSEA privacy breaches biased content and psychological harm. Chapter 5 (pp.34–39) reviews gaps in national laws and policies and Chapter 6 (p.42) provides recommendations for child-centred AI regulation and safety-by-design measures.

items.title: AI Usage and Practice in Nepal
items.justification: Computer Association Nepal (CAN) is an established  autonomous body working on the development of ICT. Before the National AI Policy was approved by the government  CAN submitted  recommendations to the government to revise the policy. The key recommendation included revision on Data Management Policies where CAN said  development of policies should clearly outline data governance including data cleansing safety and privacy measures. It also suggested Legal Framework and Data Protection and cross border data sharing.

items.title: KTM Journathon: Tackle Misinformation and Disinformation Using AI
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Nepal Investigative Multimedia Journalism Network organized the KTM Journathon (Feb 18–22 2024) to develop AI-based solutions to combat misinformation and disinformation. The press release explicitly states the event aimed to “tackle misinformation and disinformation using AI” and supported the creation of tools such as Khoj AI (verification extension) and Khop Board (chatbot providing accurate vaccine information) directly addressing AI-facilitated information harms and digital safety.

items.title: Future of Work in Nepal: Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The sessions at the conference featured presentations from tech experts on combating misinformation and disinformation. At the conference the  Ministry of Education Science and Technology (MoEST) also emphasized on importance of ethical considerations and data privacy in the development and implementation of AI technologies.

items.title: A Comprehensive Study on Artificial Intelligence DigitalInfrastructure and Data Policies with Recommendations for Policy to Strengthen AI Ecosystem in Nepal
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The report recommends the government must take proactive measures to combat AI-generated misinformation by implementing stricter regulations and promoting public awareness. It suggests that Nepal should enhance its regulatory framework for AI to safeguard data security and privacy with particular attention to addressing challenges such as data bias and misuse. The report reads It is also crucial to update and strengthen data privacy laws and security measures to protect personal information. Facet Technology a research firm collaborated closely with Data for Development The Asia Foundation along with UKAID to prepare this report.

items.title: Response from Amnesty International and Bits of Freedom to the Call for input on AI systems for risk assessment of criminal offences
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: This input from Amnesty and Bits of Freedom addresses Fairness & Non-Discrimination as its core theme arguing that discriminatory 'criminal risk assessment' is a 'real problem' (p. 3)  not a hypothetical one. It cites numerous government scandals involving racial and socioeconomic bias (p. 3) and insists that any discriminatory system is prohibited and must be taken offline (p. 4) . On Transparency & Explainability the document focuses on governance criticising the lack of 'independent oversight' (p. 4) and legal clarity on which AI systems are covered by the law (p. 3). It explicitly demands that governments act 'carefully and transparently' (p. 5). It provides a strong critique of Human Oversight warning against its symbolic gesture.

items.title: ALLAI Academy
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: ALLAI is a Dutch non-profit foundation based in Amsterdam. It engages with a wide range of stakeholders including policymakers social partners consumers and both public and private sector actors. Among its various initiatives ALLAI has launched the ALLAI Academy which offers training and workshops on topics such as AI fairness trustworthy AI and the EU AI Act.

items.title: Algo-Lit project Waag Futurelab
items.justification: The project’s core mission as described on its webpage is to make “the use of algorithms more transparent to citizens.” It focuses on helping both professionals and citizens understand algorithmic decision-making processes and on strengthening citizens’ right to explanations about high-risk algorithms. It addresses transparency and explainability by co-creating methods and tools with practitioners developing a transparency toolkit that brings together existing explanation methods and clarifying citizens’ rights and possible actions when affected by algorithmic systems. In addition the project conducts surveys among digital inclusion workers generating empirical insights into knowledge gaps and practical challenges.

items.title: The 5-star model for transparent algorithms
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The project is a collaboration between the Open State Foundation and The Green Land who jointly received the grant to further develop the 5-star model. They are funded by a grant from the 'maatschappelijke coalitie Over Informatie Gesproken. The project's title is 'The 5-Star Model for Transparent Algorithms'. The whitepaper's summary explicitly introduces it as 'a framework for step-by-step realisation of transparency'. The model is designed to make transparency 'concrete manageable and secure' by offering five progressive levels from 'Published' to 'Open'.

items.title: Input for digital inclusion
items.justification: leder(in) is a national-level Dutch civil society organisation working on inclusion and diversity with a focus on disability rights and accessibility and actively participates in public policy processes. Ahead of a parliamentary debate on Digital Inclusion (January 23 2025) Ieder(in) representing the Digital Inclusion User Network- a coalition advocating for the rights of people with disabilities and other groups addresses disability inclusion in AI and digital accessibility. It urges Parliament to ensure that AI applications are inclusive accessible and developed with a “Design for All” approach that prevents exclusion of people with disabilities women people of colour and the elderly.(page 2)

items.title: Facebook algorithm engages in prohibited gender discrimination
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Following a joint investigation by Global Witness and Dutch women’s rights organisations Global Witness and Bureau Clara Wichmann filed a complaint against Meta for discriminatory practices in its job advertisements. The Netherlands Institute for Human Rights concluded that Meta’s job-ad delivery system amounted to prohibited gender discrimination. This marks the first time in Europe that an official human rights body has found a social media algorithm guilty of gender discrimination setting an important precedent for greater accountability inclusion and diversity in AI systems.

items.title: DIVERSIFAIR
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The DiversifAIR project tackles bias through an intersectional approach which inadvertently touches all four indicators. It examines how different forms of discrimination overlap affecting individuals in complex ways. The project contributes to gender equality by partnering with groups like Women in AI providing training to detect bias and influencing policy to prevent gender-based stereotyping in AI algorithms. It promotes cultural and linguistic diversity by advocating for changes in data practices and promoting the inclusion of diverse perspectives. While children rights and rights of persons with disabilities is not directly mentioned but the project focusses on marginalised voices.

items.title: DMIS - Shaping Ethical AI for Social Impact
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The summit advances inclusivity by encouraging discussions on ethical AI for marginalised groups. The resulting Haarlem Declaration commits to reducing bias and discrimination in AI systems. Across its various sessions the summit promotes cultural and linguistic diversity by encouraging the inclusion of Global South perspectives and underrepresented communities and languages in AI narratives and policymaking (pp. 8 9 24). It also references the MIT “Gender Shades” study as a key resource for advancing human-centred and ethical AI (p. 6).

items.title: Harmful Sexual Behaviour Research Report
items.justification: Gender equality is promoted by showing how harmful sexual behaviours are shaped by misogyny and hegemonic masculinity understood as norms of male dominance. It promotes gender-transformative consent-based education and intersectional approaches responsive to diverse identities including gender sexuality (SOGIESC) and ability (Section 5.1.2 “Gender” pp. 7 30; Section 5.3.4 pp. 8 42; Section 7.1.4 pp. 10 46).It advances children’s rights by framing HSBs as a child-rights and safety issue that harms children’s well-being and development and by prioritising child-focused non-judgemental and trauma-informed responses that protect children’s safety dignity and rights to age-appropriate sexual information (p 5-6 10 sec 7.1)

items.title: AI and work
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The SER  a statutory advisory body that brings together representatives of employers trade unions and independent experts to advise the Dutch government and parliament on social and economic policy was asked to provide guidance on the opportunities of artificial intelligence (AI) to increase labor productivity as well as the opportunities and risks for job quality and the potential impact on employment and income inequality. In response it drafted an advisory report 'AI and work' and presented the findings to the House of Representatives' Digital Affairs Committee. It emphasised the establishment of  'Decent Work' as a non-negotiable standard for AI policy.(p 105).

items.title: Facebook algorithm engages in prohibited gender discrimination
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The complaint filed by Bureau Clara Wichmann and Global Witness directly addresses labour protections by challenging Meta’s job-advertising algorithm which was found by the Netherlands Institute for Human Rights to produce prohibited indirect gender discrimination limiting equal access to employment opportunities. https://web.archive.org/web/20251216193830/https://clara-wichmann.nl/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Oordeel-180225-College-voor-de-Rechten-van-de-Mens-.pdf. The decision (2025-17 sections “Facts of the case” and “Assessment”) details how AI-driven ad personalisation reinforced stereotypes (e.g. mechanics primarily shown to men receptionists to women) illustrating a concrete breach of Dutch equal-treatment law.

items.title: CNV AI Academy
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: CNV the Dutch Trade Union Federation has the CNV AI Academy which is an online/blended training programme for (future) school-leaders in secondary education. It is meant for secondary school leaders offering three modules: AI Rising Star (foundational AI knowledge) AI Go-To Person (internal support and guidance) and The Right AI Moves (strategic AI adoption in schools). It addresses AI literacy by building participants’ understanding of AI concepts and applications and reskilling/upskilling by developing leadership and organisational capacity to implement AI safely

items.title: Reshaping Work 2024 conference
items.justification: The Reshaping Work 2024 programme centers on work-related impacts of AI with explicit sessions on “AI Skills and Labor Relations” (Forum 8) panels “AI in HR” and “AI in Digital Platforms” and multi-stakeholder “Think Like…” roundtables. These sessions directly address worker impacts collective bargaining and policy responses.

items.title: The impact of artificial intelligence (AI) in the workplace
items.justification: FNV is a federation that acts as an umbrella organisation for various sector-specific unions. In March 2024 it issued a public call for evidence and a summary of initial findings from sector members (Call Centers/Logistics). It functioned as a (Hotline) to gather the data needed for policy influence. The report summary discusses how the FNV identifies possible job cuts as an issue that directly threatens job security particularly in sectors like ICT and call centers where technology companies are already linking the reduction of positions to the introduction of AI. By documenting these developments the FNV justifies the need for labor protections that address the risk of algorithms taking over entire roles and functions.

items.title: Position paper Bits of Freedom
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The document is a 'Position paper' submitted by Bits of Freedom for a 'roundtable discussion' held by the Dutch Parliament's Digital Affairs Committee. Access to Remedy and Redress is the paper's primary focus. Bits of Freedom argues that the regulator (ACM) is failing to inform end users about their right to 'file a complaint'  calling this a 'crucial aspect of End-user protection'(p.1). The first principle stated is 'End users must be central' (p. 1 ). It criticises the regulator's website for being too 'focused on businesses' instead of the end users who should benefit. It addresses the core safety risks the law must solve including 'data hunger and tracking-based advertising' and 'sensationalist algorithms and manipulative design'.

items.title: Bits of Freedom vs Meta
items.justification: Bits of Freedom is suing Meta citing the Digital Services Act (DSA) to demand that users be allowed to set a non-profiling chronological feed as their default. This case addresses data privacy by challenging Meta's constant monitoring and profiling of user behavior seeks to enhance consumer protection by enforcing a user's right to genuinely control their own timeline instead of being forced into Meta's preferred algorithmic feed and tackles AI-related misinformation by aiming to limit the power of recommendation algorithms that can be 'misused to covertly influence voters.'

items.title: Incentive Scheme 2025: Media-wise use of AI
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: This initiative Netwerk Mediawijsheid’s Stimuleringsregeling 2025: Mediawijze inzet van AI is a grant scheme designed to support Dutch projects to make Netherlands media literate. Netwerk Mediawijsheid (Media Literacy Network) is the national expertise center in the Netherlands dedicated to helping everyone become 'media-wise.' It is a massive collaboration of over 1200 partners including libraries schools cultural institutions media etc. The programme aims to fund initiatives that explore or apply AI with attention to societal impact focusing on four major challenges. Out of these four the grant focuses on resilience against disinformation and reflection on social dimensions such as safety and autonomy when using AI.

items.title: Social Research Agenda on AI by Waag Futurelab
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Social Research Agenda on AI (2024) developed by Waag Futurelab and the Dutch AI Coalition addresses data protection privacy safety and security and AI-facilitated misinformation and violence through several themes and recommendations. This initiative surveyed the Dutch population on AI research priorities directly addressing key concerns. AI-facilitated misinformation emerged as the #1 priority with 58% citing 'Fake news fake photos and polarisation' (p. 2 27) due to worries about deep fakes (p. 3).  Data protection and privacy was the #3 priority (33%) via the theme 'Supervision of people and freedom' (p. 3 30) reflecting public concern over data control and misuse (p. 3 23).

items.title: Police use unlawful incorrect and outdated information on a large scale for investigations
items.justification: Follow the Money an investigative journalism platform published a report which raised concerns about the police’s reliance on automated data analysis which has led to the buildup of large databases containing reportedly unlawfully obtained and outdated information. The investigation reveals that the Dutch police extensively collect and analyse vast amounts of personal data using automated tools like AI. These analyses increasingly drive law enforcement and public order enforcement. Despite legal obligations to delete such data the police have failed to do so for years exposing citizens to potential misuse

items.title: EU Code of Conduct for Data Sharing in the Social Economy
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: This is a set of principles and practical guidelines co-created by Commons Network and Waag Futurelab to help social economy organizations (like cooperatives) share data in a way that aligns with their values. Data Sharing and Access is the document's central topic. It is a toolkit to help social economy organizations share data. Chapter 2 'Guidance on Data Management & Sharing' (p. 20) provides governance models (p. 26) and practical 'Data Sharing Agreement Checklists' (p. 30).The Code embeds privacy in its core values. The principle of 'Self-determination' (p. 15) states data subjects must have control and 'Data Sufficiency' (p. 18) acts as a data minimisation principle to 'avoid the unnecessary collection storage and processing'.

items.title: Explainable Al: building trust through understanding
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: AI Forum NZ (an NGO) published a whitepaper on AI explainability with a particular focus on machine learning (p. 8). The paper discusses the relationship between model performance and explainability and highlights key benefits of interpretability including improved error detection stronger user understanding (pp. 9–11) bias reduction and increased trust. It also provides guidance on transparency the role of human decision-making across the AI lifecycle and responsibility (p. 7) and outlines a developer- and user-oriented conception of fairness (pp. 3 7 18).

items.title: Guidelines for the best-practice use of generative artificial intelligence in research in Aotearoa New Zealand
items.justification: Royal Society Te Aparangi is an independent NGO serving NZ’s research sector. One of the Society’s parliamentary remits is to provide infrastructure and other support for the professional needs and development of science technology and humanities researchers including research practice guidance. This guidance released in June 2025 is to help researchers leverage GenAI’s innovative benefits while remaining aware of ethical risks; their guidelines advocate transparent disclosure of GenAI use and limitations (Pg 5) mandate active mitigation of bias to promote inclusion (Pg 5 Pg 7) and ensure full accountability and oversight rests with human researchers (Pg 5) not AI systems.

items.title: Netsafe submission to the Parliamentary Inquiry into the harm young New Zealanders encounter online and the roles that Government business and society should play in addressing those harms
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Netsafe is NZ’s independent non-profit online safety organisation focused on advancing digital safety protecting the rights of NZ’ers including children and young people and promoting responsible digital citizenship. In this submission Netsafe highlights the cases of AI-created deepfake imagery noting NZ’s laws do not adequately address synthetic sexual content and non-consensual use involving children. The submission urges platform accountability rejecting blanket bans and promoting risk-based rights-respecting approaches that consider children’s participation wellbeing and dignity online. (Pg 14).

items.title: AI with Eteroa
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: AI with Eteroa is a free online learning experience designed to empower Pacific communities with the skills knowledge and confidence to navigate the AI wave. The free course offers 4 modules; Understanding AI Machine Learning Understanding Data Prompting.

items.title: AI and Accessibility: Keeping it human
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Access Advisors is an independent nationwide pan-disability consultancy and a for purpose organisation. Their mission is to help  help Aotearoa New Zealand become more digitally inclusive. The blogs on their webpage reflects their thoughts and work. This blog by the org argues that while AI can help charities and organisations streamline work and improve accessibility it must remain a tool that supports rather than replaces human expertise and empathy. It stresses that AI cannot fully understand emotional or contextual nuance (for example in writing alt text) and highlights serious concerns around data sovereignty security and biased training data particularly for disabled people.

items.title: A.I For Good: 10 perspectives on artificial intelligence
items.justification: Public Service Association (PSA) NZ published 'AI for Good' (2025) with perspectives on labour protection and upskilling advocating for labour rights. One of the perspectives advocates for workers rights: 'involving the people affected the workers in determining the inputs at both the production and deployment stages will help to effect this shift to human centered AI (Not by Chance; but by Choice Pg 8-9). Also advocates for 'intentionally aimed at undermining organised labour and worker voice must be prohibited and both the producers and deployers of such products should be penalised' p.8-9. Another perspective calls for a Just Transition where upskilling should be a right and Maori data sovereignty must be respected (p25- 27).

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Workplace
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: NZ Council of Trade Union's report outlines practical strategies and principles for labour protection in the face of workplace AI adoption. It urges unions to leverage existing laws (like the Employment Relations Act Health and Safety at Work Act Privacy Act Human Rights Act) (Pg 8) and collective bargaining to protect workers. Key recommendations include worker voice in AI decisions impact assessments for AI tools (pg 10) robust health and safety protocols (pg 17) clear data privacy and protection guidelines (Pg 20) limits on surveillance (pg 4) and model clauses for collective agreements that ensure fair job quality (Pg 5) prevent job loss (pg 18) and uphold data sovereignty and the right to disconnect (pg 6).

items.title: Aotearoa AI Summit 2025
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Aotearoa AI Summit 2025 organised by AI Forum NZ and NZ Tech is a one-day national event uniting industry leaders researchers policymakers and innovators to discuss AI ethics responsible innovation and real-world applications across sectors like healthcare finance agriculture and government through keynotes panels and workshops. In the 2025 summit there were sessions on Maori data sovereignty data protection AI governance. The Summit aims to share space for cutting-edge research success stories and future trends shaping the AI landscape in Aotearoa.

items.title: How to improve the Aotearoa New Zealand Code of Practice forOnline Safety and Harms?
items.justification: The report presented by NZ Human Rights Commision presents findings from a three-month Independent Accountability Group that examined selected human rights and Te Tiriti o Waitangi issues arising from the Aotearoa New Zealand Code of Practice for Online Safety and Harms. (Pg 2) It uses concrete examples of online abuse including a detailed review of serious harm directed at former Prime Minister Dame Jacinda Ardern during the election campaign on X (Pg 3) and Facebook to inform its analysis of how the Code addresses online safety and harms in Aotearoa New Zealand. (Pg 9).

items.title: AI and Online Safety: Emerging Risks and Opportunities
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: Netsafe and AI Asia Pacific Institute published a paper to analyse & provide insights into the implications of AI on online safety. The paper identifies key trends challenges and strategies for addressing online harms including AI-facilitated issues. The objective is to offer insights and observations for policymakers industry stakeholders and educators to foster a safer digital environment. Online harms explored in this paper are limited to those affecting individuals and society from online content and digital comms in the following categories: child sexual exploitation and abuse violent and graphic content extremism harm to health and well-being indecent and obscene content hate & discrimination cyberbullying (Overview Pg 7).

items.title: a capacity building session dedicated to introducing members of the group to artificial intelligence (AI)
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: On Thursday August 21 2025 the GTH-OIREN Technical Communication Group (GtC) held a capacity building session dedicated to introducing members of the group to artificial intelligence (AI) in a collaborative and learning framework. It is an association of international NGOs working in the humanitarian field in Niger.

items.title: Fact-Checking & Artificial Intelligence (AI): Youth in Action
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The Tillabéri training (“Fact-checking & Artificial Intelligence: Youth in Action” 23–25 Sept 2025) addresses AI-facilitated misinformation and violence by equipping youth leaders with practical fact-checking skills (source verification rumour deconstruction critical analysis) and explaining how Artificial Intelligence tools can help detect fake news (methods limits opportunities). It emphasises combining critical thinking with technology to strengthen community resilience to conspiracy narratives and to protect public space from information manipulation.

items.title: AI Integration Training for Educators under the Nigeria AI Collective Portfolio
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The initiative addresses the selected areas by focusing on AI literacy and curriculum reform.Human Oversight and Determination: By training educators the initiative ensures future professionals (journalists communicators) have the critical skills to scrutinize AI recognize risks and maintain human control over content creation auditing and decision-making processes preventing blind reliance on automation.Transparency and Explainability: The workshop's content emphasizes teaching strategies for embedding algorithmic bias and data privacy into curricula. This directly builds the capacity of future workers to understand how AI makes decisions thereby demanding greater transparency and explainability from the systems they use.

items.title: Brain Builders Youth Development Initiative Champions AI Literacy with Nationwide Curriculum Review
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Brain Builders Youth Development Initiative (BBYDI) advances AI literacy by championing a nationwide review/validation of an AI literacy curriculum to improve what learners are taught about AI and how it is taught. It supports reskilling/upskilling by linking the curriculum update to implementation steps such as educator engagement and planned rollout helping build practical AI competencies among teachers and students for future work and learning in AI-enabled environments.

items.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Accountability in Nigeria: Insights and Learnings From Focused Group Discussion (Paradigm Leadership Support Initiative (PLSI)
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The initiative promotes data sharing and access by PLSI’s revamped civic technology platform Value for Money 3.0 platform to make public finance and service delivery information easily accessible to citizens enabling faster petition submission and engagement with anti-corruption agencies. It also addresses data protection and privacy by emphasising secure data handling compliance with privacy laws and the need for national AI governance and ethical standards discussed during the focused group session.

items.title: ALIGN LEGISLATION WITH THE DIGITAL SERVICES ACT INCLUDED IN THE 2025 GOVERNMENT WORK PROGRAMME
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Aligning the legislation with the Digital Services Act will support North Macedonia’s EU integration goals improve its digital regulatory framework and provide a safer and more predictable digital environment for citizens and the business community.

items.title: Surveillance Technologies at European Borders Assessment on NorthMacedonia
items.justification: Civil society organizations have been denouncing the dangers of the use of new technologies and Artificial Intelligence in the field of migration and border control including the deployment of intrusive surveillance technology and the collection of biometric data from people on the move. The lack of transparency and regulation surrounding these processes and their impact results in a lack of accountability on the part of the authorities tech companies as well as public research institutions as it poses severe difficulties in the monitoring of likely violations of human rights.

items.title: Human Rights Protection in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Overall objective of the project „Human Rights Protection in the Age of Artificial Intelligence“ is to shape AI policies and regulatory frameworks that uphold human rights online. Specific objectives: Raise public awareness of the challenges and risks imposed by adopting upcoming strategic framework and related legislation related to AI to human rights online. Support policy development in North Macedonia in the area of protection of online privacy and other human rights online. Target groups :Citizens including marginalized groups: Civil society organizations and Media

items.title: Analytical report on the Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI) in the Republic of North Macedonia
items.justification: The research report writes that there has been some disinformation based on generative AI circulating on Macedonian social media most of it consists of reshared or reposted content from foreign politicians or leaders.This is largely because AI-generated disinformation in North Macedonia has not yet reached the advanced stage seen in other countries. A significant barrier to this is that most sophisticated deepfake and AI-altered content is trained on vast datasets in native languages primarily English. In North Macedonia there has been virtually no targeting of politicians or public figures with this technology due to the lack of sufficient content required to produce realistic deepfakes that can pass the 'human-eye test.

items.title: Ethical standards for protecting human rights online in automated decision-making
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The initiative represents a research-based ethical standards to guide the creation implementation and use of AI systems. These standards emphasize balancing innovation with responsibility to safeguard human rights focusing on safety trustworthiness and accountability in automated processes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights: Finding the Right Balance between Innovation and Responsibility
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: Gender equality links to the focus on AI bias and discrimination and to Ethics by Design: Building Inclusive and Non-invasive Technological Solutions promoting non-discrimination and warning tech can deepen inequalities. Children’s rights link to Cyber Shake -Youth dialogues: Why study when there is Artificial Intelligence? on pupils/students' AI use misuse detecting model written texts consequences in education and regulation. Rights of persons with disabilities link to Ethics by Design meeting the diverse needs of citizens and aiming to empower and include rather than marginalize plus Lightning Talk-on transparency and equitable .Full agenda here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/116_xtfIeiOXjpdDrAi11MuW0gX1ViShO/view?usp=drive_link

items.title: Ethics and bias in artificial intelligence
items.justification: The Republic of North Macedonia and neighboring countries face the challenge of adapting to the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI). With ethical standards and the need to prevent bias global and European initiatives (such as the new EU Artificial Intelligence Act the AI-Act) are introducing strict rules for the responsible use of AI but there is mixed progress in the region. The document addresses and debates on several dimensions. On page 47 for example mentions that : 'Imported educational technologies often do not reflect the linguistic cultural and socio-economic realities of students in the region'

items.title: The Digital Transformation of the Parliament: Civil Society as a Key Partner in Building a Modern Parliament
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: University professors civil society experts and digitalization experts from European countries debated in the Parliament of the Republic of North Macedonia regarding the Digital Transformation Strategy of the Parliament. In a panel discussion titled: 'Parliament 2.0 - Change Leadership Capacity and Inclusion' the participants shared their thoughts on a more effective digital strategy towards the goal of a more modern Parliament and foreign experts encouraged use of AI in the Parliament.

items.title: Open your AIs: Responsible Use of AI Tools by Youth Organisations
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The study session pursues three key objectives: helping youth organisations remain vigilant and responsible when integrating AI into their work; supporting them to become vocal advocates for AI ethics within their structures and among their beneficiaries and building knowledge to navigate and contribute to key policy processes like the EU AI Act and the Council of Europe’s AI Convention especially considering growing concerns around AI-driven discrimination.

items.title: Inclusiveness in the process of creating support programs and partnership with the business sector in the Municipality of Centar
items.justification: Public consultations held to explore several aspect of the possibilities of cooperation with the business sector among companies in Municipality of Center including AI tools. The responses from the survey also provided information that in 2023 only one quarter used AI tools at work and 61% responded that they would like to attend a training on AI in 2024. The survey provides disaggregation by sector company size and so on (page 24-26). The public consultations served as an input for the Strategy for local economic development of the Municipality. https://www.centar.gov.mk/sites/default/files/alfa/doc/programi/strategija-ler-2024-2028.pdf

items.title: TRANSFORMATION OF EMPLOYMENT RELATIONS: ADDRESSING THE CHALLENGES OF AI AND DIGITAL PLATFORM WORKERS
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The publication of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation  jointly with the Institute for Democracy yielded a series of research papers that address the AI and the public administration. The minister for digital transformation also writes an article on: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCEAND THE EFFICIENCY OF THE MACEDONIAN PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION. Overall papers cover all three initiatives: Labour protection upskilling of the public administration and AI literacy.

items.title: AI guidelines for parliaments
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: This is a document prepared by the Westminster Foundation for Democracy (WFD) in July 2024 with contributions from international parliamentary experts and translated in Macedonian by their local office. It offers practical guidance for integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into parliamentary operations in North Macedonia with focus on ethical and human rights and capacity building like trainings on AI. (page 9-capacity building and education)page 72-provide instructions about trainings and education; page 75-Organize frequent artificial intelligence training programs for parliamentary officials and administrators.

items.title: Digitalization of public administration in the context of European integration - Benefits and challenges
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: (page 2 - Gdrive link) Related to the introduction of AI-based solutions in the delivery of public services Metamorphosis conducted research on the impact of AI on human rights analyzing European and international regulations and ethical standards. The participant   emphasized that before applying AI in the public sector it is necessary to establish clear strategies and policies that will ensure that the technology does not have a negative impact on human rights especially in automated decision-making.

items.title: Effective Justice to Protect the Fundamental Freedoms and Privacy of People in the On-line Space
items.justification: (page 1-GDrive link) North Macedonia is a signatory to the Convention for the Protection of Individuals with regard to Automatic Processing of Personal Data 108/81. The Law on Personal Data Protection was adopted in February 2020 to align the national legislation with the EU  (GDPR) as the highest legal standard for personal data. Although the Personal DataProtection Agency has a primary authority in this area to supervise the legality of the activities undertaken during the processing of personal data as well as the protection of the fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals regarding processing of their personal data judiciary and public prosecution have significant role in the protection of human rights in the online space.

items.title: From AI to Gamification: Transforming Education for the Digital Generation – Dig-Ed at REMA 2025
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Innovative program to create a workshop-based training methodology for primary and secondary schools integrating digital storytelling AI tools and game-based learning to make cybersecurity education dynamic and engaging. In late 2024 Dig-Ed developed supporting resources and issued an open call for teachers to participate in workshops.

items.title: Navigating AI’s Impact on Human Rights in a Digital Era at the 19th International e-Society.mk Conference
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The conference explores the artificial intelligence (AI) which opens unprecedented opportunities for innovation in various sectors while at the same time opening different questions on the protection of basic human rights. Achieving the right balance between innovation and accountability is essential to ensuring a digital landscape that includes addressing issues such as privacy bias discrimination and the ethical use of AI to protect human rights. The conference offered a possibility for networking with international experts.

items.title: Ethical standards for protecting human rights online in automated decision-making
items.justification: The document (in Macedonian) focuses on the areas selected. It emphasizes the importance of ensuring that AI systems are developed and used in ways that prioritize safety and do not compromise fundamental rights or public security (pages 13–14). Then it highlights the need for thorough impact assessments especially Data Protection Impact Assessments to evaluate how AI might affect privacy and human rights before these technologies are deployed (page 30). Also it mentions about the potential misuse of AI to spread misinformation or incite violence stressing the need for safeguards to prevent such outcomes (page 19).

items.title: Blocksi AI Web Filter - MKSafeNET
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: A consortium of Macedonian CSO's  partnered with the government on “MKSafeNet” a project to establish the first National Safer Internet Centre. Backed by an EU Digital Europe grant and the Ministry of Digital Transformation MKSafeNet is creating an awareness hub school programs a youth panel and a helpline for reporting online abuse including guidelines about AI tools filters and related resources.

items.title: Webinar: Is your business ready for artificial intelligence?
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: The workshop is created by the Confederation of Norwegian Enterprise (NHO) organization that operates as a non-profit. The webinar is meant for businesses and employers that want to adopt AI techniques responsibly with respect to their employees: p.2:'Build safe environments for experimentation' p.2 also mentions risks and compliance with laws and regulations. P.3 talks about transparency and trust labeling AI generated content and confidentiality. Another point addressed:'How do you avoid AI creating a sense of surveillance or loss of autonomy among employees? (impact on employees)'.P.4 brings up responsibility and consequences for AI mistakes and failures.

items.title: The  Consumer  Council's  input  to  the  Screen  Usage  Committee
items.type: Developing ethical guidelines principles or best practices.
items.justification: The activity is a policy submission to a governmental committee on children’s screen use led by the Norwegian Consumer Council a Norwegian CSO . It focuses on risks arising from AI-driven digital environments for minors including addictive design targeted advertising and AI-based “virtual companions.” The activity directly addresses Children’s Rights by advocating stronger protections precautionary approaches to AI in schools and regulatory safeguards against manipulation and exploitation (pp. 2-3).

items.title: Measuring prejudice in AI systems using Norwegian language and context
items.justification: Norwegian AI Ethics Association (NAIE) is advocating for developing Norway's own benchmark and guidelines for measuring and detecting biases in AI models. There has been multiple installments of an ongoing experiment where the group has been adapting some existing benchmarks to Norwegian language and realities p.4 (previously: https://naie.no/en/measuring-bias-in-ai-systems-using-norwegian-language-and-context-part-1/). They use indicators to measure LLM biasedness towards gender age religion etc. (p.7). The authors are hoping that this project can gain visibility and motivate further developments in AI bias diversity and inclusion guidelines and audits.

items.title: Measuring prejudice in AI systems using Norwegian language and context
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: Norwegian AI Ethics Association (NAIE) is advocating for developing Norway's own benchmark and guidelines for measuring and detecting biases in AI models. There has been multiple installments of an ongoing experiment where the group has been adapting some existing benchmarks to Norwegian language and realities p.4(previously: https://naie.no/en/measuring-bias-in-ai-systems-using-norwegian-language-and-context-part-1/). They use indicators to measure LLM biasedness towards gender age religion etc. (p.7). The authors are hoping that this project can gain visibility and motivate further developments in AI bias diversity and inclusion guidelines and audits.

items.title: NITO consultation submission  –  draft  new  law  on  artificial  intelligence  (AI  Act)
items.justification: The submission by the Norwegian CSO NITO – The Norwegian Association of Engineers and Technologists addresses Labour Protections by emphasizing employee rights in AI deployment including privacy co-determination and a safe working environment and by requiring involvement of shop stewards in AI-related workplace processes (pp. 1-2). It also addresses Reskilling / Upskilling initiatives by calling for strengthened support for continuing education long-term funding of industry programmes and a comprehensive competence boost to ensure workers can adapt to AI-driven changes in the workplace (pp. 1 3).

items.title: Artificial intelligence in the workplace: A survey of professional groups affiliated with Unio
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The report presents findings from a research project on how AI is used and experienced at work by employees in various professions affiliated with trade union Unio. Chapter 5 addresses mostly all three points of this indicator e.g. p63-64 point out the importance and current lack of AI skills and knowledge training need for overall AI expertise and literacy. In terms of labour protection members and union representatives report limited involvement in decisions about AI use(e.g. p67) suggesting a lack of structured worker protection mechanisms in how AI is introduced and governed at workplaces which is pointed out again in conclusions chapter 7.

items.title: NITO consultation submission  –  draft  new  law  on  artificial  intelligence  (AI  Act)
items.justification: The activity led by the Norwegian CSO NITO – The Norwegian Association of Engineers and Technologists is a consultation submission (30 September 2025) on Norway’s draft AI Act. It addresses Data Protection and Privacy by emphasizing employee privacy and safeguards in workplace AI use (p. 2) Data Sharing and Access through calls for clearer guidance on data use and transparency requirements (p. 3) and Impact Assessments by explicitly advocating fundamental rights impact assessments for high-risk AI systems including workplace-related impacts (pp 2 4).

items.title: Complains about Meta's use of personal content for AI training
items.justification: The litigation led by the Norwegian CSO Consumer Council in collaboration with NOYB challenges Meta’s use of user content to train AI models without a valid legal basis. Filed with the Norwegian Data Protection Authority and other EU regulators it addresses Data Protection and Privacy (unlawful processing of personal data) Data Sharing and Access (repurposing user-generated content for AI training) and Consumer Protection (manipulative opt-out mechanisms undermining informed consent).

items.title: Four proposals for new AI policy
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The report with proposals is written by Langsikt - an independent non-profit think tank for longer-term policy offering steps forward in AI regulations and developments.
