items.justification: The event provided an in-depth assessment of the current AI development landscape strategic direction and current status of AI applications in the public sector from there make policy recommendations to promote max potential of AI. Key Recommendations:1) Establish a clear legal framework and mechanism including regulations on accountability ethical standards risk management and data privacy protection. 2)Focus on AI ethics and risk management through monitoring systems impact assessments ensuring transparency fairness and privacy protection. IPS is an independent not-for-profit think tank: https://ips.org.vn/en/about-us.html. It is a member of the Vietnam Digital Communications Association a business association.

items.title: Seminar 'Developing and using trustworthy artificial intelligence'
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The roundtable was led by the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) Vietnam. It addressed Data Protection and Privacy by highlighting the need for responsible data governance frameworks to support trustworthy AI development. It addressed Data Sharing and Access through discussions on strengthening data infrastructure and regulatory conditions that enable AI innovation. It also addressed Safety and Security by emphasizing risk management and the importance of legal safeguards to prevent harmful AI uses. The discussion focused on policy-level governance rather than specific technical measures.

items.title: Workshop 'Digital Communications Code on Responsible Use of AI'
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The Code of Responsible AI Use in Digital Communication was issued by the Vietnam Digital Communications Association (CSO) and establishes multiple core principles and practices. It addresses Data Protection and Privacy by requiring lawful necessary and transparent handling of personal data in AI-supported digital content. It addresses Consumer Protection by promoting disclosure of AI-generated materials accountability in content production and safeguards against misleading or manipulative uses of AI in media. The Code establishes ethical principles to guide responsible AI deployment in digital communication focusing on transparency and user trust.

items.title: We Digit Training Programme
items.justification: The Women’s Entrepreneurship Access Centre (WEAC) is a Zambian women-led entrepreneurship support organisation and business incubator that helps women (and youth) move from the informal to the formal economy.The initiative promotes gender equality by intentionally partnering with the WEAC and prioritizing women’s participation. Out of the 175 youth participants nearly half were women as noted in the article reinforcing gender-inclusive leadership in tech education. In addition the training placed a strong emphasis on digital technologies including artificial intelligence equipping participants with practical hands-on skills. This focus supports inclusive AI literacy and empowers underrepresented groups especially women to access opportunities in the digital economy.

items.title: Survey Report by Internews Network Zambia on Artificial Intelligence Adoption by Civil Society Organizations in Zambia
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: A survey was conducted by Internews Network Zambia to report on Artificial Intelligence adoption by CSOs in Zambia. According to the survey findings on page two “Some CSOs cited that the AI tools they are utilizing do not have correct or ample information on Zambia and most of the AI tools are not tailored to suit the unique circumstances of their communities; ‘It’s not made for us’” says a participant from Livingstone. This entails that due to cultural diversity it is difficult for certain people to use AI. Linguistic diversity as cited on the same page equally makes it a challenge: “CSOs feel pressured to train AI chatbots to understand their local languages for free while most of these chatbots are for profit.”

items.title: Panos Institute Hosts Information Session on AI and Civic Participation
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The session highlighted CSOs’ central role in promoting responsible AI adoption through community awareness advocacy for inclusion and digital literacy initiatives. By engaging government media and business stakeholders it fosters collaboration to build an ethical and inclusive AI ecosystem. Participants also discussed AI’s potential to drive entrepreneurship and job creation for youth and women across sectors like agriculture healthcare fintech and e-commerce equipping communities with knowledge and skills to understand and engage with AI thus strengthening AI literacy.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Adoption by Civil Society Organizations (CSOs)  in Zambia A Survey Report
items.justification: The Internews Zambia survey report addresses AI literacy and reskilling/upskilling by analysing how Zambian CSOs use AI their knowledge gaps and capacity needs. The survey strengthens AI literacy and skills development by revealing how limited capacity affects CSO adoption of AI. The findings show that 54% of CSOs have not integrated AI and most lack training and resources. The Survey Overview emphasizes that “ethical considerations technical challenges and financial constraints pose significant barriers” highlighting the need for targeted skills support. It finds that only 18% of CSOs currently offer staff training on AI tools and explicitly identifies this as a major skills gap that must be addressed. It notes that many CSOs struggle with integration ethics data quality and bias; and frames these challenges as requiring additional support and capacity-building so organisations can responsibly adopt and manage AI.

items.title: Media Awareness and Advocacy Raising on Responsible AI
items.type: Public engagement & awareness: conferences public awareness events/campaigns public consultations.
items.justification: The initiative promotes responsible AI use by media and CSOs to inform communities and strengthen democratic processes enhancing data sharing and access for public good. It also emphasizes safety and security by cautioning against misuse that could distort public discourse. Moreover it addresses AI-facilitated misinformation and violence by urging ethical AI practices to prevent manipulation and protect human rights. This is highlighted in Mr. Sifile’s call for objective responsible AI use to protect democracy from Panos Institute Southern Zambia.

items.title: IndabaX 2024 Zimbabwe AI Symposium
items.type: Capacity building and collaboration: training courses workshops networks.
items.justification: Based on the conference's stated themes of Innovation Inclusion and Responsible AI the discussions provided clear evidence that Fairness and Discrimination were addressed. The outcomes directly noted a focus on building AI free from bias and discrimination and the inclusive multi-stakeholder nature of the event underscored this goal. Regarding Transparency and Explainability the program featured a dedicated practical session on Explainable AI (XAI). This hands-on workshop provided attendees with direct knowledge of methods to make AI decision-making processes understandable a core tenet of transparency framed within the broader push for responsible and accountable AI systems.

items.title: Al Report on Southern Africa
items.justification: On transparency the document discusses public disclosure of AI systems (pp. 71–72) and documents how biased data can foster discrimination against women and minorities (pp. 44–45).On human oversight it notes the need for independent regulators and redress mechanisms (pp. 59 71). On the environmental dimension citing sustainable data-centre plans alongside Africa's limited computing capacity (p. 45).

items.title: 6th Privacy Symposium Africa (PSA) Report - Key Policy-Recommendations-
items.type: Participation in public policy formulation implementation M&E: as part of advisory councils partnerships with state independent observers participating in parliamentary hearings.
items.justification: The Privacy Africa Symposium (PSA) and subsequently published report by CSO Unwanted Witness outlines several key policy recommendations to address the complexities of Artificial Intelligence (pp. 3 10 17). It explicitly explored AI in relation to data protection and privacy (p. 3); AI's unrestricted access to data (p. 18); Consumer trust and protection (pp. 6 15); combating misinformation (p.14); promote Collaboration for Data Security Innovation (p. 8); and note that new frameworks must incorporate ethical principles risk assessment mechanisms and provisions for algorithmic transparency and accountability (p. 10) and recommends to notify consumers about breaches and remediation steps (p.16) while noting current gaps for doing so (p.5)

items.title: Public consultation on the Draft Law on Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The public consultation platform of the Ministry of Telecommunications Information Technologies and Social Communication enabled CSO participation by providing an official channel for submitting feedback on the AI policy and other sectoral draft  policies. The consultation process is described as a mechanism for dialogue between public administration and society allowing communities and organised groups to contribute information and opinions to improve the documents under review. According to the consultation guidance the population including CSOs may comment on issues of collective interest and support government decision-making by expanding the discussion (Public Consultation Portal - “Consulta Pública” section).

items.title: National Plan of Artificial intelligence
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: Pages 50 and 234 of the plan document the working tables conducted with CSOs and other key actors to develop the strategy. Representatives from research centers universities private companies trade unions business chambers international organizations and third-party agencies participated in this multi-stakeholder process to define the National Artificial Intelligence Plan. The document does not provide the specific names of the CSO stakeholders involved

items.title: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.type: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.justification: The National Observatory on Artificial Intelligence is established as a body for permanent dialogue and collaboration among the public academic private and civil society sectors. Its role includes providing assistance and preparing recommendations for AI adoption within both the government and the private sector (P.193)

items.title: The establishment of a new Artificial Intelligence Expert Group
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: The Artificial Intelligence Expert Group provides advice to the Department of Industry Science and Resources on AI governance issues including transparency testing accountability and guardrails for high-risk AI systems. The group includes a representative from the Gradient Institute an independent non-profit research organisation focused on ethical and responsible AI. Through this membership the mechanism enables civil society participation by allowing a CSO-affiliated expert to contribute to government discussions and provide input into the development of Australia’s AI governance approaches.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Mission Austria 2030 (AIM AT 2030)
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The strategy enabled CSO participation by involving civil society actors in its development and implementation framework. The document states that more than 160 experts from diverse disciplines including civil society organisations were involved in drafting the strategy and that it is a participatory interdisciplinary process open to the involvement of civil society and citizens (pg. 3-4). This shows CSO involvement in shaping the AI policy.

items.title: AI Stakeholder Forum
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: The AI Stakeholder Forum enables CSO participation and oversight in Austria’s AI governance by serving as a formal multi-stakeholder body where civil society organisations sit alongside industry academia and social partners. Through regular consultations feedback rounds and structured dialogue with the federal government CSOs can review comment on and influence the implementation of national AI strategies and Austria’s approach to the EU AI Act. This gives civil society a direct channel to shape policy decisions raise risks or societal concerns and monitor how AI-related measures are carried out.

items.title: Public Council under the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: Public Council is a body under the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport consisting of the representatives of several CSOs. Ministry of Digital Development and Transport is the main authority implementing Azerbaijan's digitalization procedure including the AI strategy and as such Public Council also being involved in AI-related policy-making processes. In the official meeting with the Public Council the chairman of the Council addressed issues such as systematic implementation of artificial intelligence in public administration. It was emphasized that an open dialogue environment can contribute to the country’s digital development strategy and the importance of continuous cooperation with civil society was highlighted.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The National AI Policy draft clearly incorporates civil society into the institutional framework as mentioned on page 11 where the ICT Division collaborates with ministries industry academia and civil society. Additionally on page 16 under the policy review section the draft emphasizes continuous stakeholder engagement and public consultation. This cohesive collaborative approach aligns perfectly with the idea of a multi-stakeholder advisory council making it the most fitting choice.

items.title: Project Implementation and Execution
items.justification: GovTech(Ministry of Technology) partnership with Zindi to create an AI ecosystem in Barbados this will create opportunities for networking and creation of solutions based on a holistic stakeholder engagement on April 26 2025. This year long partnership entails AI challenges (e.g Hackathons) educational events community building activities with the aim of providing world class AI knowledge and skills. In addition this projects seeks to prepare Barbadian citizens for employment opportunities in particular areas such as data sciences and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The AI4Belgium coalition is explicitly included in the policy's governance structure for ongoing input and monitoring. The coalition is the primary multi-stakeholder body (p. 35-36 framework: National Plan).

items.title: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.type: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.justification: The Federal Data and AI Ethics Advisory Committee was established. The Plan also refers to the establishment of an AI Observatory to track implementation which is another type of monitoring mechanism that civil society can engage with (p. 35-36 framework: National Plan). Its composition explicitly includes two representatives of the National Labour Council which represents social partners (trade unions and employer organisations).

items.title: Steering Committee
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: To guide the implementation of this national plan a joint Steering Committee was created between FPS BOSA and FPS Economy composed of 12 members 6 French-speaking and 6 Dutch-speaking (p. 37). The Steering Committee will function as a single point of contact at the federal level for AI-related issues. If deemed necessary the Steering Committee may create a subgroup with a mixed composition (members of the political committee and external members). This information is in the main framework p.35-36.

items.title: Process of Developing National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence and Big Data (2023–2027)
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The Strategy states that it was developed by the Ministry of Digital Affairs and Digitalization using a “stakeholder-integrated approach” (Introduction p. 2). Within its Theory of Change it explicitly identifies “Civil Society Leaders” among the actors bearing governance and accountability responsibilities (p. 13). More specifically the development process of Benin’s National Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategy (SNIAM) is described as integrating stakeholders through a holistic approach centered on technological solutions tailored to the country’s specific needs. This is still continuing over the monitoring stage of the strategy.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The policy does not establish a formal “advisory council” “AI observatory/ethics committee” or audit/impact body with explicit CSO seats. Instead it foresees multi-stakeholder participation through the implementation mechanism: the coordinating body involves “all stakeholders” (Implementation Mechanism p.42) and “ecosystem stakeholders” are “involved in the implementation of the actions” and “express their needs and give their opinions” (Responsibilities of Actors p.43)

items.title: Minutes of the Ordinary Meeting of the National Council for Science and Technology - Proposal for the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: Ordinary Meeting of the National Council for Science and Technology – with a non-deliberative character whose agenda was the debate of the proposal for the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan. In addition to council members and government representatives representatives from entities such as producers and users of science and technology participated and the Brazilian Institute for Human Intelligent Creative and Sustainable Cities (https://www.ibrachics.org.br/). According to the Plan (p.5) more than 30 bilateral meetings were held with public and private institutions and 6 workshops as evidenced here.

items.title: Minister of Science Technology and Innovation representatives of Brazilian generative AI companies
items.type: Written submissions from CSOs officially acknowledged in policy documents
items.justification: The Minister of Science Technology and Innovation who coordinated the development of the plan met with representatives from Widelabs a company that develops generative AI solutions.The CEO of Widelabs presented the AmazonIA Brazilian Portuguese Language Model (LLM) developed in partnership with a Brazilian university and international companies which can be used in sectors such as education health and security. The minister stated that the initiative is welcome and that she has been listening to different sectors about Artificial Intelligence such as civil society researchers and large technology companies.

items.title: CSO membership in audit or impact assessment bodies
items.type: CSO membership in audit or impact assessment bodies
items.justification: The Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Observatory is part of Axis 5 of the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan (PBIA) focused on 'supporting the regulatory and governance process of AI' and is part of the strategic actions of the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Strategy.It works in conjunction with Cetic.brNIC.br and Ceptro.brNIC (entities that were the core management of the internet in Brazil) and has a network of partners such as C4AI CGEE and SEADE with a commitment to delivering solid and significant indicators. It is based on the principle of multi-sectoral cooperation between government academia the technical community the private sector civil society and international organizations.

items.title: Brazilian Observatory of Artificial Intelligence
items.justification: The Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Observatory is part of Axis 5 of the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan (PBIA) focused on 'supporting the regulatory and governance process of AI' and is part of the strategic actions of the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Strategy.It works in conjunction with Cetic.brNIC.br and Ceptro.brNIC (entities that were the core management of the internet in Brazil) and has a network of partners such as C4AI CGEE and SEADE with a commitment to delivering solid and significant indicators. It is based on the principle of multi-sectoral cooperation between government academia the technical community the private sector civil society and international organizations.

items.title: Public Consultation - Draft Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Bulgaria until 2030
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The draft concept was published on the official website of the Council of Ministers i.e. the Public Consultation Portal and one month was given to any CSO and any other interested parties to submit positions and papers. Few CSO submitted their positions that are visible at the bottom of the internet page and were also freely accessible by any visitors of the website. The contact details of the person responsible for this public consultation were provided as well as indication that the responsible institution is Ministry of Transport Information Technology and Communications and their contact details.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: It is proposed that an Interdepartmental Working Group which will include representatives of key state institutions district administrations academia business and professional associations and related NGOs (section 7.1 first paragraph). This working group should analyze the state of the sector map the expert units achievements and implemented innovations and prepare an operational National Plan / Roadmap for the implementation of the Concept which defines the specific measures deadlines responsible institutions and organizations expected results and indicators and sources of the necessary financial resources as well as organization for reporting on their implementation and their periodic updating.

items.title: National workshop on AI
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: On August 27th 2025 the digital economy ministry has organized a workshop for the National AI Action plan. This workshop brought together representatives from public institutions the private sector. universities research centres civil society as well as technical and financial partners. By this way CSO participate to AI policy in Burkina Faso.

items.title: Progress of Preparing and Opening Public Consultation on Draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The initiative supported CSO participation by openly inviting CSOs to review and comment on the draft National AI Strategy providing public access to the documents and a structured feedback form and holding a multi-stakeholder workshop that included CSOs. The ministry also committed to reviewing and integrating all submitted feedback into the final strategy ensuring CSOs had opportunities to influence the policy.

items.title: Other
items.justification: The draft Strategy outlines a 'National AI Observatory' (Strategic Priority 5 Flagship Activity 4) to monitor ethical and responsible AI adoption. Including CSO representation is justified because Strategic Priority 6 commits to a “multi-stakeholder approach” involving civil society in implementation (Section III p.16-17; Measures 6.2 and 6.6). Embedding CSOs in the Observatory or ethics bodies strengthens transparency aligns with the Strategy’s collaboration principles and ensures societal perspectives are reflected in monitoring.

items.title: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.type: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.justification: The Strategy repeatedly mandates a 'multi-stakeholder approach' making this mechanism well aligned with its design. Sec.III (Strategic Priority 6 p.16-17) requires creating an environment for collaboration among government private sector academia and 'civil society' (Measures 6.2 and 6.6). The Conclusion (p.18) further states that implementation depends on cooperation with CSOs. Using multi-stakeholder mechanisms therefore reflects the Strategy’s intent and ensures inclusive representative implementation.

items.title: The Fourth Cambodia ICT and Digital Forum: Dialogue on the Digital Development
items.justification: The Fourth CamIDF enables CSO participation in AI governance by providing a multi-stakeholder forum where civil society can engage directly with government private sector and technical experts. Through open discussions on AI ethics data protection and digital rights CSOs can raise concerns influence policy directions and strengthen oversight. The forum’s focus on knowledge-sharing and cooperation also builds CSO capacity to monitor and shape future AI governance.

items.title: AI Strategy Task Force
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: This task force consists of representatives from corporations universities and CSOs (one example is Centre for International GovernanceInnovation CIGI)  and serves as a way for such stakeholders to provide actionable insights and recommendations on Research and Talent; Adoption across industry and governments; Commercialization of AI; Scaling our champions and attracting investment; Building safe AI systems and public trust in AI; Education and Skills; Infrastructure; and Security. By informing the development of the new AI strategy they directly participate in AI Governance of Canada.

items.title: Public consultation on the National AI Policy - Results Report 2024
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The public consultation explicitly enabled CSO participation by inviting all citizens and organizations to submit feedback via an online form disseminated across social media (pp. 2–3). The results report details participation from over 150 organizations including NGOs academia and the private sector (p. 6) and shows how their input influenced updates to specific sub-axes. However the government’s report only describes how input was collected and general themes raised; the public consultation did not include any provision or mechanism to demonstrate how specific CSO feedback was formally incorporated into the final policy decisions.

items.title: Public Solicitation of Opinions on AI Governance Framework Draft for Comments
items.justification: Regulatory bodies sometimes release draft regulations for public comment. The public can send their opinions and feedback through email or mail to the bodies within one month after the notice is released. The archived webpage shows the Cybersecurity Administration of China issuing a notice of public solicitation of opinions for 'the Measures for the Labelling of Artificial Intelligence-Generated and Synthetic Content' released on Sep 14 2024 with the consultation deadline on Oct 14. The formal framework came out in March 2025.

country.name: China Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

items.title: Written Submissions
items.justification: CSO can send in submissions with existing consultation opportunities. There are currently no AI related consultations. The government held a consultation on copyright and artificial intelligence on 3 July 2024- 8 September 2024 regarding the enhancement of the Copyright Ordinance (Cap 528) on the protection of the copyright of works generated by generative AI copyright infringement liability of AI Possible introduction of specific copyright exception and other issues related to copyright and generative AI.The consultation received 60 submissions from the public enterprises and industry associations which are publicly available. Included the original link in the public evidence box as wayback machine returned an error.

items.title: Artificial intelligence as a key driver for Colombia's social and economic development (Public consultation on the National Artificial Intelligence Policy)
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The draft CONPES on AI was presented in August 2024 for public comment receiving more than 1000 contributions. In addition consultation sessions were held (17–18 September) with opportunities for open dialogue and active participation by civil society academia and the private sector which allowed proposals to be adjusted and the policy to be enriched.

items.title: Colombia: roundtables for formulation of CONPES 4144 2025
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: CONPES 4144 of 2025 the Roadmap for the Development and Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Colombia by MinCiencias and the Colombia PotencIA Digital strategy by MinTIC involved multiple stakeholders including civil society in working groups and regional dialogues. Specifically for the CONPES document 15 roundtables were held with 137 participants (public sector private sector academia and CSOs) and regional dialogues with more than 3000 people providing input for the National AI Policy (UNESCO pp. 15 58 and 59).

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2027
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The ENIA 2024-2027 states at p.3 that the strategy was jointly validated with the public sector civil society the private sector and academia aiming to align national efforts toward a long-term vision. At p.5 the document lists the specific actors involved in this process including named civil society organisations confirming CSO participation in the strategy's multi-stakeholder development and validation process.

items.title: The National AI Strategy of Côte d'Ivoire for Horizon 2030 (SNIA 2030).
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: Civil society organisations (CSOs) were extensively and formally consulted and involved in the development of the SNIA 2030. 312 CSOs contributed to the development of the SNIA with more than 70% of CSO proposals being adopted or partially adopted. All these elements were included in the official summary report of the SNIA national consultations (June 2025 – 120 pages) but unfortunately it is no longer available online. It was drafted by the SNIA Editorial Team.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: SNIA 2030 explicitly provides for a multi-stakeholder advisory board that clearly includes civil society organizations (CSOs) within the National Artificial Intelligence Council (CNIA). The CNIA is presented as a permanent advisory body attached to the National Artificial Intelligence Agency. It is responsible for ensuring inclusive and participatory governance. Specific references in the official document: Page 57 (section “Governance” / “Governance bodies”) (Page 58 (subsection “Composition of the CNIA”). The SNIA specifies that 20% of members must come from CSOs. These provisions aim to ensure inclusive governance that is representative of social diversity and attentive to ethical inclusion and equity issues.

items.title: CSO membership in audit or impact assessment bodies
items.type: CSO membership in audit or impact assessment bodies
items.justification: SNIA 2030 explicitly provides for the participation/involvement of CSOs in the bodies or mechanisms responsible for auditing and evaluating the impact of the AI strategy and projects. In fact CSOs must be part of the steering committee for each independent audit (minimum quota of 15-20%). They must participate in defining the terms of reference selecting the firm and validating the final report of the Independent Audits on AI technological solutions to be deployed and/or currently in use. Audéka it is also planned that any algorithmic impact assessment (AIA) or social impact assessment may include at least one CSO representing vulnerable groups in the panel of assessors.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Dominican Republic
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The Dominican Republic’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy was developed through a participatory process that included thematic working groups and an open public consultation with a public forum/space for citizens to submit comments and proposals bringing together hundreds of participants from government the private sector NGOs universities and individual citizens to foster inclusive dialogue and contribute analyses and proposals across areas such as ethics infrastructure education R&D financing and governance (p 15).

items.title: Multi-sectoral technical committee and deliberative consultation process for the development of the Organic Law on Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The draft Organic Law on Artificial Intelligence was developed through a multi-actor deliberative process that included civil society organizations indigenous peoples feminist groups consumer associations academia and the private sector. Page 6 of the Draft Law states that the regulatory vision resulted from an “intense deliberative process” involving civil society actors. Page 79 provides that a multi-sectoral technical committee including representatives of public institutions academia the private sector and civil society must participate in the preparation of the National AI Strategy. The framework also promotes ongoing multisectoral participation in governance and policy updates (Art.45).

items.title: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.type: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.justification: The draft law establishes formal mechanisms for civil society participation in AI governance and oversight. Art.49 creates the National Ethics Committee in Artificial Intelligence Research (CNEI-IA) composed of experts and representatives of civil society to review AI research with potential human rights impacts. Art.65 establishes a Citizen Observatory of AI and Justice including universities bar associations civil society organizations consumers and users of the justice system to monitor the use and impacts of AI in the justice sector. In addition Art.45 requires that updates to the National AI Strategy occur through a participatory multi-stakeholder process including civil society.

items.title: AI Readiness Assessment Methodology consultation
items.justification: The Egyptian Ministry of Communications and Information Technology in collaboration with the United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) has launched a consultation on Egypt’s Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) for artificial intelligence (AI). The consultation sessions focus on four key areas where AI plays a pivotal role: policies and legislation cultural and social domains scientific research and infrastructure and the economic sector. These sessions included participation from diverse stakeholders and experts including representatives from the public and private sectors academia civil society and young entrepreneurs. However it is an had oc mechanism rather than permanent.

items.title: Participation in committee on generative artificial intelligence
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The 'Generative AI Committee' was formally tasked by the Prime Minister to 'present concrete proposals' to 'adapt our national strategy' (p. 1). Its composition explicitly ensured multi-stakeholder participation by including civil society representatives like Franca Salis-Madinier (CFDT Cadres union p. 2) and Martin Tisné (Open Government Partnership p. 2). The committee functioned as a diverse working group to 'enlighten Government decisions' (p. 1)  ensuring that non-state perspectives on 'societal' and 'ethical' issues (p. 1)  directly shaped the strategic recommendations delivered to the government.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The Phase 3 National Strategy explicitly mandates the National Digital Council (CNNum) to lead ongoing civil society participation. On page 26 the strategy tasks this independent consultative commission with 'structuring a system of democratic debates' (Café IA) and 'bringing together stakeholders... to collectively build' AI awareness initiatives. Additionally the Prime Minister's editorial (p. 3) and the 'Empowering the Nation' section (p. 25) establish a formal 'social dialogue' mechanism involving 'professional trade unions' to co-develop regulations and oversee AI's impact on work ensuring a permanent channel for non-state actor inclusion in governance.

items.title: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.type: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.justification: The Phase 3 Strategy establishes two key oversight bodies: INESIA (National Institute for AI Assessment and Security p. 25) for technical evaluation and LaborIA (p. 36) a dedicated 'action-research laboratory' to 'analyze and experiment with the impacts of AI technologies on work' LaborIA is explicitly tasked with 'fostering public debate on the major social implications of AI.' Crucially the strategy mandates that these oversight mechanisms operate within a framework of 'social dialogue' that formally involves 'workers and unions' (CSOs) in 'developing regulations and disseminating use' (p. 3 36) ensuring civil society representation in monitoring AI's societal impact.

items.title: CSO membership in audit or impact assessment bodies
items.type: CSO membership in audit or impact assessment bodies
items.justification: The Phase 3 Strategy explicitly designates LaborIA (p. 36) as the national body responsible for 'analysing and experimenting with the impacts of AI technologies on work.' While LaborIA leads the technical assessment the strategy mandates that this oversight be conducted through a formal 'social dialogue' involving Trade Unions (CSOs). The Prime Minister’s editorial (p. 3) and the governance section (p. 25) state that 'Harnessing AI means involving all of society (workers and unions) in developing its regulations' thereby ensuring that civil society representatives are active participants in the bodies assessing AI's societal and labour impacts.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Council
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: The Council institutionalizes the participation of Civil Society Organizations by reserving eight of its 17 seats for 'qualified personalities' from the associative sector and civil society. It is statutorily mandated to consult civil society regularly to advise the government on the societal and economic impacts of Artificial Intelligence. This mechanism provides an independent permanent platform for non-state actors to formulate recommendations and oversee policy development to ensure technological progress aligns with the general interest.

items.title: Le LaborIA
items.justification: Le LaborIA is a research-action laboratory co-led by the Ministry of Labour and Inria. It facilitates Civil Society Organization participation through its Executive Committee (COMEX) which explicitly includes 'qualified personalities' recognized for their expertise in Artificial Intelligence and work-related issues. The mechanism supports participation by producing pedagogical tools and publications for 'organisations syndicales' (trade unions) and employee representatives. By integrating these stakeholders into research projects and public debates the initiative ensures that social partners and non-state actors can evaluate risks and influence the conditions for integrating Artificial Intelligence into professional environments to protect

items.title: Open Consultations and Public Comments on the AI Market Surveillance Act
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The AI Market Surveillance Act (KIMÜG) supported CSO participation through the formal association consultation (Länder- und Verbändeanhörung) initiated on September 12 2025. This process enabled CSOs to provide expert technical and legal feedback through a structured questionnaire and written submissions (https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/media/a8/2b/659360/Stellungnahme-Gutachten-SG2512170092.pdf). AlgorithmWatch is a notable German CSO that took part in the consultation: https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/media/f6/2d/628462/Lobbyregister-Regelungsvorhaben-Detailansicht-RV0004864-2025-10-13_12-24-40.pdf full statement: https://algorithmwatch.org/de/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/251009b-KI-MIG-Stellungnahme-AlgorithmWatch.pdf

items.title: EU AI Act Advisory Forum
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: Following the entry into force of the EU AI Act there was an open call for applications to the EU AI Act Advisory Forum. The Forum includes dedicated seats for civil society to advise the AI Office and the AI Board. The selected participants will be announced in early 2026. German CSOs such as AlgorithmWatch have been vocal about the being involved in shaping the Advisory Forum (https://politiscope.eu/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Politiscope_Open_Joint_Letter_against_the_Delaying_and_Reopening_of_the_AI_Act.pdf  p.3). Because the KI-MIG is a Regulation-implementation law Germany will have to follow any technical consensus from the Forum once established.

items.title: National AI Strategy Consultation
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: On page 13 it is stated that Ghana’s strategy explicitly used ~40 expert interviews and 4 high-level public-sector consultation workshops which included government academia private sector and civil-society actors. This created targeted spaces for CSOs to feed evidence raise rights/ethical concerns and shape sectoral use-cases and the action plan. Specific CSOs that participated in this exercise are however not mentioned

items.title: Other
items.justification: Page 25 the Responsible AI Office a mandate to “coordinate across institutions… involving government ministries and agencies the private sector academia and civil society.” This embeds CSOs directly into ongoing implementation coordination and review of the strategy. It therefore establishes a standing mechanism for continuous CSO participation rather than a one-off consultation.

items.title: A Blueprint for Greece's AI Transformation
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The Blueprint describes a structured stakeholder engagement process during its drafting (Section 2.3 p. 28-31) involving multi-stakeholder working groups and consultations with representatives from civil society academia the private sector and public institutions. The Guiding Principles (p. 12-13) emphasize participation and inclusiveness as core values of AI governance. CSO participation was enabled through involvement in consultations and expert discussions that informed the policy’s strategic priorities and recommendations.

items.title: National Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) Position Paper for Indonesia’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Roadmap 2025
items.justification: The National CSOs Position Paper for Indonesia’s AI Roadmap 2025 was officially launched during an in-person consolidation event at Kekini CoWorking Space in Jakarta on July 28 2025. The Position Paper is intended to serve as the official strategic recommendation from the CSO Network to the National AI Roadmap Working Group under the Ministry of Digital Communications (KOMDIGI).

items.title: Public consultation on the Development of a National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The Irish government opened public consultations online for the development of a National Strategy on Artificial intelligence.

items.title: The AI Advisory Council
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: The members of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Advisory Council represent a spectrum of experience and expertise from academia business law security social sciences economics and civil society. It is tasked with providing expert guidance insights and recommendations developing a workplan of advice to government on issues in artificial intelligence policy and engaging in public communication on AI.

items.title: National AI Leadership Forum unites sectors to secure Ireland’s AI future
items.justification: On 25 September 2025- The national AI leadership forum brought together senior representatives from Government academia industry regulators and civil society. The ongoing goal is to develop a shared roadmap for Ireland’s global leadership in the development and use of safe ethical and human-centric AI to build a successful AI future.The Forum is organised by the Research Ireland ADAPT Centre for AI-Driven Digital Content Technology in partnership with the Insight Centre for Data Analytics and William Fry.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Regulation and Ethics Policy Principles Document
items.type: Written submissions from CSOs officially acknowledged in policy documents
items.justification: The document states the process of writing and formulating the policy included consultation as stated:' In this context written responses were received from various entities in the broad public sector and from representatives of academia civil society organizations and industry.” A draft was circulated and fixed after some of the responses.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The document explicitly recommends establishing a Public Participation Forum that includes representatives from 'civil society organizations'. This forum is designed to be an ongoing mechanism to 'identify the main areas where there is a need to adapt the regulation or regulation policy' effectively serving as a review and monitoring channel.Additionally the Government Knowledge Center is formally tasked with establishing 'relevant forums for dialogue and knowledge sharing with... third sector [CSOs]'. This institutionalizes the mechanism for ongoing engagement rather than limiting it to a one-time consultation.

items.title: The National Forum of AI Experts
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: The task of the forum is exactly to escort oversee and advise. As stated in the white paper that led to its foundation.

items.title: Parliamentary hearings & stakeholder consultations during approval of Law 132/2025
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: During the review of the AI bill (A.S. 1146 / C. 2316) the relevant parliamentary committees (Trasporti & Attività produttive) held verbal hearings and public sessions with trade unions (CGIL CISL UIL UGL) the national journalists’ federation (FNSI) professional associations industry associations academic experts and other non-state stakeholders — enabling civil society and sectoral representation to voice concerns suggestions and critiques.

items.title: “Inclusion and Rights in Artificial Intelligence – Commitment IT0086 (Italy Open Government Action Plan 2024–2026)”
items.justification: Commitment IT0086 is implemented through a live process on the official government participation platform partecipa.gov.it (“Raccomandazioni IA”) which hosts documented activities stakeholder inputs and outputs. The process is coordinated by the OGP IT Community Participation Hub a network of ~100 organizations (around two-thirds CSOs) and includes scheduled meetings and co-design workshops on inclusive and fair AI for public administrations. Event from the network: https://eventipa-formez-it.translate.goog/eventi/c70f4aee-e75e-4b01-9ca8-8d42438ffb95?_x_tr_sl=auto&_x_tr_tl=it&_x_tr_hl=it - Program :https://partecipa-gov-it.translate.goog/processes/raccomandazioni-IA?_x_tr_sl=auto&_x_tr_tl=it&_x_tr_hl=it (not possible to translate)

items.title: Public Opinion Call on E-GOV Platform for the 'Draft AI Business Guidelines'
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The national Ministry of Economy Trade and Industry (METI) and the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) opened a public opinion call on the E-GOV platform for the “Draft AI Business Guidelines” in which 47 corporations and organisations submitted comments to inform the draft [p.1]. Several civil-society actors also participated. One example is (Creators AI Association for Thinking about the Future of Art) a volunteer-based CSO supporting creators in light of evolving AI technologies (see: https://support-creators.com/start_page) which suggested to mandate for AI training to use only licensed lawful well-sourced data and to allow individuals to opt out of data use [p.97].

items.title: First AI Business Guidelines Review Meeting - Committee Members List
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The Guidelines received a substantial update in Ver. 1.1 reflecting in part the opinions submitted by multiple stakeholders during the review meetings. The advisory committee list includes several external experts among them the CCFS (translation: Sustainability Consumer Council) which is a certified NPO (see: https://web.archive.org/web/20251121195712/https://cnrc.jp/members/members-635). Additionally the Guidelines themselves explicitly state that they were developed through input given by multiple stakeholders explicitly mentioning civil society [p.4].

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The Guidelines are explicitly meant to be updated as a 'living document' as needed including in response to international discussions and through continued multi-stakeholder engagement [p.3]. Ver. 1.1 was itself produced after review meetings where multiple stakeholders submitted opinions and the advisory committee list includes external experts such as the CCFS a certified NPO see https://web.archive.org/web/20250805150126/https://cnrc.jp/members/members-635/ . The Guidelines further state that they were developed through input from multiple stakeholders explicitly including civil society [p.4].

items.title: Ministry of Education Culture Sports Science and Technology (MEXT) Study Group on the Use of Generative AI in Primary and Secondary Education (Chair Yuta Tonegawa the Representative Director of Minna no Code)
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: The Ministry of Education Culture Sports Science and Technology  (MEXT) established a Study Group on the Use of Generative AI in Primary and Secondary Education to review monitor and update generative-AI guidelines for schools. One of the Chairs is Yuta Tonegawa the Representative Director of Minna no Code a certified NPO focused on children’s digital literacy (see https://code.or.jp/about). Through regular meetings (every month see: https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/shingi/chousa/shotou/193/giji_list/index.htm) she can express her expert opinion and give recommendations and thus participate in AI governance in the education sector.

items.title: National public-comment (E-GOV) Platform
items.justification: The E-GOV public comment platform gives CSOs a formal traceable channel to publicly influence national AI governance. The entry I listed under “Open public consultation”the 'Public Opinion Call on the Draft AI Business Guidelines' was actually carried out through this exact mechanism ensuring that civil society input is officially recorded and considered. Further AI-related consultations such as for example the call on the Guidelines for Procurement and Utilization of Generative AI (https://public-comment.e-gov.go.jp/pcm/1040CLASSNAME=PCM1040&Mode=1&id=290503241) demonstrate that CSOs can provide concerns suggestions and other feedback not only at the drafting stage but also during subsequent updates of AI guidelines.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The Policy establishes a permanent National Ministerial Committee for Artificial Intelligence that is responsible for implementation monitoring and review and it formally includes civil society organizations as members (Pillar One p. 5).This Committee oversees sectoral plans sets national priorities and evaluates progress. Since CSOs hold seats in this body they are part of the ongoing governance and review cycle defined in the Policy.

items.title: National AI Conference for an Active Civil Society in Jordan
items.justification: Although not a formal or recurring mechanism the National Conference on Artificial Intelligence for an Active Civil Society (RASED 2025) provided a temporary platform for CSO participation in AI governance. Held under the patronage of MoDEE it gathered ministries Parliament private sector academia and civil society to discuss ethical transparent and participatory AI governance. The event enabled CSOs to voice concerns share recommendations and engage directly with policymakers indicating emerging but not institutionalised CSO involvement.

items.title: Kenya: Ministry of Information Communications and Technology opened consultation on draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2030
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: On 14 January 2025 the Ministry of Information Communications and Technology opened a consultation that was set to close on 19 January 2025 on the draft of Kenya's National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy 2025-2030 which outlines a vision to position Kenya as an AI hub in Africa.This consultation involved various stakeholder including CSO's as outlined in the Strategy on Pg.7 and Pg.22.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The Strategy under the theme on Data [Pg.72] Sub-theme 2.1.3 calls for the establishment of an AI task force with representation from key actors including; MCDAs counties (CoG) private sector and civil society representatives. This taskforce is required for the creation of a robust and responsive data governance framework in the country. The Strategy further under sub-theme 2.2.2 [Pg.73] calls for the incentivisation of data sharing and collaboration among stakeholders including private sector research institutions government agencies and civil society organisations. The main objective behind this is the development and implementation of secure data sharing data access and data interoperability protocol in the country.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: on page 22 Kuwait National AI Strategy: From Vision to Execution  the table clearly mention ' Identifying and Engaging Key Stakeholders for AI Governance Fostering collaboration among key stakeholders across government entities the private sector academia and(( civil society ))to maximize the benefits of AI and address potential challenges' . the title is from vision to execution so most probably it refers to implementation and monitoring not writing the draft itself

items.title: National Council for AI Development
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: The Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic (January 22 2025) 'About the National Council for the Development of Artificial Intelligence' establishes the National Council on AI Development which includes CSO representatives as full Council members in its structure (Accelerate Prosperity PF Kyrgyz Eye Research Institute Association of Developers and Owners of AI Systems - AIDA). This creates a formal standing mechanism for civil society to advise the government on AI policy monitor implementation and participate in strategic decision-making.

items.title: Participation in the negotiation of the draft law 'Artificial IntelligenceCentre Law' and providing an opinion.
items.type: Written submissions from CSOs officially acknowledged in policy documents
items.justification: The Latvian Information and Communication Technology Association participated in the negotiation process and provided opinion. For example the opinion indicated that 'It would be desirable to amend(supplement) Section 3 Paragraph 1 of the Law on the National Artificial Intelligence Centre of Latvia stating as follows:(1) The aim of the Centre is to promote the competitiveness of the country by developing public-private partnerships in the field of artificial intelligence and to promote the implementation and development of responsible and reliable AI systems the improvement of AI skills in relation to the promotion of the capabilities of artificial intelligence systems the prevention of risks and the management of AI systems.'

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The Draft Artificial Intelligence Policy Implementation Plan (Version 0.1) (Government of Lesotho 2025) foresees the creation of a National Digital Council as a multi-stakeholder advisory body including civil society academia and private sector representatives (Section 5.6 pp. 14–15). It also proposes the establishment of an AI Ethics Oversight Committee under the Council to promote responsible AI practices and monitor compliance. However both mechanisms are draft provisions and not yet operational as of September 2025.

items.title: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.type: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.justification: The Draft Artificial Intelligence Policy Implementation Plan (Version 0.1) (Government of Lesotho 2025) foresees the creation of a National Digital Council as a multi-stakeholder advisory body including civil society academia and private sector representatives (Section 5.6 pp. 14–15). It also proposes the establishment of an AI Ethics Oversight Committee under the Council to promote responsible AI practices and monitor compliance. However both mechanisms are draft provisions and not yet operational as of September 2025.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The AI Act establishes an “Advisory Forum” to ensure the involvement of relevant stakeholders in the governance/implementation of the framework. The Advisory Forum advises the European Artificial Intelligence Board and the Commission/AI Office and is composed to reflect a broad multi-stakeholder representation (incl. civil society among “relevant stakeholders”). See Title VII Chapter 1 Art. 67 (Advisory Forum) (OJ L 12.7.2024 p. 78/144)

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The roadmap uses a Quadruple Helix model that includes community actors / CSOs alongside academia government and industry. CSOs can participate via alliances and consortia (e.g. MyAI-Alliance) and in national AI Use Case projects (p.24 69).

items.title: Representative of Non-Governmental Organizations in the Working Group for Drafting the Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Montenegro 2026–2030
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: The Government created a Working Group to draft the AI Strategy 2026–2030 and issued a public call for NGO participation (13 June 2025). The government document “List of Representatives of Non-Governmental Organizations for the Development of the Artificial Intelligence Strategy” (4 July 2025) confirms that the NGO Montenegrin AI Association (MAIA) submitted a complete and timely proposal and that its representative Miodrag Vujkovic was listed as the NGO candidate for the Working Group tasked with drafting the Strategy for Artificial Intelligence of Montenegro 2026-2030. This shows that civil society is formally included in the government’s working body responsible for shaping AI governance.

items.title: Pleio (generatieveai.pleio.nl)
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: Since May 2023 the government has developed an inclusive AI vision by testing outcomes across multiple sectors. Central to this was Pleio a secure open-source Dutch public sector collaboration tool which facilitated CSO and public participation via iterative insight sharing. This created a feedback loop where expert and public input from sessions was validated on the platform. To ensure diverse viewpoints a sounding board representing social perspectives and an intergovernmental working group were established. While the community link (generatieveai.pleio.nl) is now inactive its role in validating policy outcomes is confirmed in Appendix 1 (Page 50).

items.title: Sounding Board Group
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: There is no clear website or clear start/end date for the sounding board group which was created to provide direct feedback on policy drafts during 2023 (attached google drive doc)(Appendix 1 p. 50). It worked to ensure the vision has a broad societal basis by connecting stakeholders at all levels and balancing opportunities with risks regarding sustainability ethics and work. The sounding board group included representatives from CSOs like Bits of Freedom FNV(The Federation of Dutch Trade Union) and other bodies like CIO (Chief Information Officers)-Platform IPO(Interprovinciaal Overleg) NL-AIC(Nederlandse AI Coalitie) Politie The Social and Economic Council municipal association and employers organisation.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The vision uses an iterative 'learning approach' requiring 'continuously conducting a broad social dialogue' (Page 29). Active collaboration with civil society organizations is explicitly cited as essential for policy on Page 31. Under 'new actions' (Page 30) the government plans to extend dialogue with 'residents workers trade unions and entrepreneurs' and separately explores appointing a 'quartermaster' to coordinate social dialogue initiatives. CSOs also participated via a sounding board group and the Pleio community (generatieveai.pleio.nl) used to test outcomes and gather public input (Page 50).

items.title: Fine-tuning two LLMs
items.justification: This initiative establishes a project-based partnership where the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations (government) serves as the funder and provider of open data. The Open State Foundation (OSF) a civil society organisation acts as the developer tasked with building an open-source language model using Dutch government information.This mechanism enables limited CSO participation in AI governance through instrumental project-based involvement. This is aimed at exploring democratic opportunities and risks of generative AI.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy Workshop
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The initiative enabled CSO participation in developing the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025 (NAIS) through a deliberate multi-stakeholder design that co-created the strategy using a human-centred approach. The NAIS reinforces this: Page 2 acknowledges stakeholders who participated in workshops; Page 16 identifies non-profits/civil society groups as core ecosystem actors; and Section 1.8.2 (Stakeholder Consultation Process and Contributors) lists CSOs that contributed to the strategy including Data Science Nigeria (DSN) RISE Networks Nigeria Computer Society (NCS) Co-Creation Hub Africa (CcHUB) and the Global Center on AI Governance.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The strategy is built on a foundational 'Collaboration' principle and explicitly requires a multi-stakeholder approach for implementation including commitments from civil society (Page 5 29). This makes CSO involvement a continuous requirement for the implementation of the strategic pillars.

items.title: National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics (NCAIR) AI Collective
items.justification: Nigeria AI Collective is a government-initiated multi-stakeholder community of practice that convenes CSOs with policymakers to support responsible AI governance. The Ministry’s official “Week in Review” notes that the Minister formally launched the Nigeria AI Collective describing it as a community of practice to advance AI in Nigeria and support the safe and ethical use of AI. It enables CSO participation through structured engagement and capacity building (e.g. the six-month “AI for Civil Society Workshop”) helping CSOs build AI literacy develop advocacy strategies and implement accountability interventions/campaigns that feed into public engagement and policy dialogue on ethical inclusive AI.

items.title: Council for Cooperation between the Government and Civil Society
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: The government adopted the 'Strategy of the Government of the Republic of North Macedonia for Cooperation with and Development of Civil Society 2025–2028 '(June 2025) and an Action Plan which is general for all sectors. The Council for Cooperation with the CSO sector is a body that receives initiatives for the implementation and  cooperation with the CSO. The strategy has a mechanism to include CSOs in the consultation process and also AI initiatives can fit in.    One of the initiatives proposed by the CSO Metamorphosis  is the creation of National AI strategy (page 1): https://drive.google.com/file/d/15MeQfuwKqUJb9NoANv-grMwsbUc9w9wK/view?usp=drive_link

items.title: Received input on the AI ??strategy
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The ministry published written inputs received from civil society organisations and public-interest groups including the Consumer Council Seniornett the Norwegian Institution for Human Rights (NIM) Effective Altruism Norway and Circular Norway alongside contributions from academia industry associations companies and public institutions.

items.title: Consultation – draft new law on artificial intelligence – implementation of the EU regulation on artificial intelligence in Norwegian law
items.justification: Norwegian government is drafting a new national law on AI which would implement the EU AI Act into Norwegian legislation by summer 2026. In summer 2025 after the first hearing for the law the government has opened a request for public and private organizations and entities to submit their comments consultations and opinions on the first drafts and proposals. More than 20 independent organizations have submitted their written consultations to the government including trade unions interest groups etc.

items.title: Public Consultation for the National ArtificialIntelligence Policy
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The Ministry of Transport Communications and Information Technology launched a public consultation on the National AI Policy from August 2 to August 31 2024 with the aim of collecting opinions and feedback to draft a balanced and effective policy.A number of participants representing various segments of society took part in this consultation. See details of results: https://web.archive.org/web/20260605131416/https://prod.mtcit.gov.om/ITAPortal/Data/SiteImgGallery/202551385414309/Press%20Release%20on%20the%20Outcomes%20of%20the%20Public%20Consultation%20for%20the%20National%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Policy.pdf

items.title: Feedback on Draft National Artificial Intelligence Policy
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: In the Preamble on page 4 it does mention that the policy has been developed after extensive consultations with the stakeholders. On page 19 under the heading of 'Policy Implementation Mechanism' the policy promotes public and civil society participation through citizen engagement community discussions and public consultations so that AI policies are aligned with societal needs and ethical values.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: On page 19 of the National AI Policy under the heading of AI Council one of the member of the council will be from civil society.

items.title: Senacyt organized workshops for the formulation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
items.justification: The National Secretariat of Science Technology and Innovation (Senacyt) in partnership with Georgia Tech University and Georgia Tech Panama conducted multi-sector workshops as part of a participatory process for the formulation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy. This is an inclusive national strategy that seeks the participation of all sectors of Panamanian society (p.1). Recent dialogue offices will bring together representatives of government academia business associations and civil society with specialists from the AI Technology Center of Georgia Tech University (p.1). During the sessions participants are invited to respond to the National Research on Artificial Intelligence (2).

items.title: Submit contributions for the new Draft Regulations of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Law
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: In 2023 Peru became the first country in Latin America to pass a General Law on Artificial Intelligence. In Peru laws are usually implemented through regulations. The entity responsible for drafting the regulations for the AI Law conducted several rounds of public consultations and virtual sessions between 2023 and 2024 to gather feedback from all stakeholders including CSOs. The final consultation took place from November 25 to December 6 2024.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: Article 9 of the Framework indicates that the mechanism through which the participation of CSOs and other stakeholders will take place is through the 'High-Level Committee for a Digital Innovative and Competitive Peru.' This Committee is a mechanism that predates Peru's AI Law and has existed since 2018 to generate synergies among multiple stakeholders to promote government and digital transformation. From now on the Committee will include the implementation of the AI Law as one of its activities. The Committee has reserved seats for representatives of civil society. Link to the Committee's page: https://www.gob.pe/institucion/comiteperudigital/institucional

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: Sec. 2 provides that 'the State shall advance AI in a manner that is ethical inclusive transparent and accountable.' (p. 1) Sec. 7 creates the National AI Council which shall have (j) one (1) representative each from the following sectors to be appointed by the President of the Philippines for a term of three (3) years: i) The private technology sector with expertise in AI or data science; ii) The civil society sector with expertise in AI ethics human rights or digital governance. (p. 5) Sec. 18 (d) institutionalize a Tripartite AI and Labor Transition Council composed of representatives from the Department of Labor and Employment employers' organizations labor groups and civil society to recommend policy safeguards. (p. 11)

items.title: Public consultations
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The Ministry of Digital Affairs announced that the draft AI Act implementation law was submitted to konsultacje spoleczne (public consultations) to gather opinions from citizens NGOs companies and public institutions (16.10.2024). The draft also provides for a Rada Spoleczna (Social Council) composed of representatives of NGOs trade unions and entrepreneurs to co-shape AI policy demonstrating formal involvement of CSOs in the development and future governance framework.

items.title: Working Group on Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Participation in multi-stakeholder working groups or advisory committees
items.justification: The initiative enabled CSO participation through the Grupa Robocza ds. Sztucznej Inteligencji (GRAI) an open multi-stakeholder working group established by Decision 2/2024. NGOs are explicitly invited to join alongside academia business and public administration. GRAI works on AI regulation (including AI Act implementation) human rights public administration and policy updates allowing CSOs to contribute to recommendations regulatory proposals and educational initiatives shaping Poland’s AI policy.

items.title: Government Legislation Center
items.type: Written submissions from CSOs officially acknowledged in policy documents
items.justification: Government Legislation Center is a legal body that publishes all comments submitted to the public consultations and the replies from the gov site. Unfortunately web archive cannot archive this website. Here is the link with the legislation and consultation process on the Act on Artificial Intelligence Systems (EU AI Act implementation)

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: AI Analysis Center: The policy recommends establishing a 'dedicated AI analysis center funded by public money'.t specifies that the composition of this publicly funded entity should include 'non-governmental organizations including watch-dogs' alongside representatives of science government and business. This provides a state-resourced platform for CSOs to meaningfully participate in shaping policy regulations and ethical standards.

items.title: Working Group on Artificial Intelligence
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: CSO are invited to the working group that works on topics like: AI and legal regulations (including the implementation of the AI Act) AI human rights and democracy Regulatory sandboxes and supporting innovation (including the development of sustainable computing infrastructure) AI Policy update AI in public administration Data for AI Awareness competencies and digital hygiene International cooperation based on trustworthy Artificial Intelligence.The results of the group's work are available on the Artificial Intelligence Portal.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Agenda public consultation on Participa.gov.
items.justification: The Participa.gov entry describes a formal public consultation process for Portugal’s National AI Agenda where contributions from citizens experts organizations and CSOs are solicited and can influence the final policy document. This mechanism enables CSO participation by allowing organizations to submit structured proposals for the National Artificial Intelligence Agenda through Participa.gov. The “How to participate” section specifies that proposals must identify the relevant area describe the action and state its objectives. Submissions are analyzed for maturity and alignment with the National Digital Strategy and may be incorporated into the final Agenda giving CSOs a direct channel to influence AI governance.

items.title: CSO Meter Moldova: First policy framework document on Artificial Intelligence and Data Governance
items.type: Open public consultation (e.g. online comments public hearing)
items.justification: The online public consultation for the White Book on AI & Data Governance (21.02.2024–31.03.2024) on the particip.gov.md platform invited public input allowing CSOs to submit comments on the draft document.

items.title: Multi-stakeholder advisory council including CSOs
items.justification: The White Book explains that SCIA acts as a multi-stakeholder advisory mechanism that includes civil society. Its mandate explicitly states that it facilitates collaboration between stakeholders from the public private academic industry civil society and development partners sectors. It also works through transparency accountability and feedback mechanisms supporting CSO participation in ongoing AI policy implementation and oversight (p.51).

items.title: Sub-Council on AI and Data Governance
items.type: Oversight advisory policy monitoring and evaluation bodies where CSOs have a seat
items.justification: SCIA enables CSO participation by formally including civil society (CSOs Sigmoid and AI in Action) among its stakeholder groups and mandating collaboration across public private academic industry and CSO sectors (section “Membrii SCIA”). Its mission emphasizes transparency accountability feedback mechanisms and periodic reporting allowing CSOs to contribute to policy proposals oversight discussions and the development of responsible AI and data governance in Moldova (p.51 White Book on AI and Data Governance).

items.title: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.type: AI observatory or ethics committee with CSO representation
items.justification: Measure 6.1.1 of the National AI Strategy refers to creating an institutional framework for governing AI in line with the provisions of the EU AI Act.
